When this given name first came into use, it was usually given in honour of the medieval saint John of Nepomuk (c. 1345-1393). He was born and raised in the town of Pomuk, which is what Nepomuk refers to. The town was located in what was once Bohemia, but is now located (under the name Nepomuk) in the Plzeň region in the Czech Republic.Some sources claim that Nepomuk literally means "from Pomuk" or "born in Pomuk" in Czech, but this is probably incorrect, as "from" is z in Czech and "born" is narozený in Czech. Instead, Nepomuk probably literally means "not Pomuk" in Czech, derived from ne meaning "not" or "no" and Pomuk meaning "Pomuk". This unusual meaning is said to originate from the early history of the town, which is as follows: in the beginning, there were two towns in the area, namely Pomuk and Přesanice. Both were located in the near vicinity of the one Cistercian Monastery in the area. Apparently, the two towns were often confused with each other, because at some point, the need arose for people to differentiate the two towns from each other. People informally started calling Přesanice ne Pomuk meaning "not Pomuk", which set it apart from the town of Pomuk in no uncertain terms. Eventually, in 1413, the two towns and the monastery were merged into one town, which was henceforth known under the name Nepomuk.This early history surrounding the town of Pomuk is plausible by itself, but it seems a bit problematic when you try to relate it to saint John of Nepomuk. After all, he was born long before the merge of the two towns and the monastery. In his day, Pomuk was still a separate and independent town. In addition to that, Nepomuk was the nickname given to Přesanice at the time - it was never a nickname for Pomuk itself. As such, it does not make sense for a Pomuk native such as the saint to refer to themselves as "Nepomuk". The only way in which it would make sense for the saint to refer to himself as such, would be if he was actually born and raised in Přesanice instead of in Pomuk.All in all, there is some uncertainty and ambiguity surrounding the etymology of Nepomuk. The only thing that we can truly say for certain, is that the name is of Czech (and therefore Slavic) origin.Finally, a well-known bearer of this name was Johann Nepomuk Hummel, a 19th-century Austrian composer and virtuoso pianist.

Derived from the name of the Greek sea god Neptune, used by the Roman poet Catullus to refer to the nymph Thetis, because she was a granddaughter of Poseidon (Neptune).

A maidservant of Queen Amena of Korntin (Amene) in Wirnt von Grafenberg’s Wigalois.She traveled to Arthur’s court to find a champion when Korntin was invaded by King Roaz of Glois. When Arthur appointed Wigalois (Gawain’s son) to the task, Nereja was furious because she thought Wigalois too young and inexperienced.As she traveled with Wigalois, however, and watched him win a number of combats, she gradually developed respect for and confidence in him. By the time they reached Roimunt (Amena’s castle), Nereja was happy to present Wigalois as her champion.Her counterpart in Renaut de Bâgé’s Le Bel Inconnu is Helie.

In Mesopotamian mythology he is a deity of Akkad, Assyria, and Babylonia, with the main seat of his cult at Cutha, represented by the mound of Tell-Ibrahim. He is the son of Enlil and Ninlil, and is sometimes associated with Shamash. Nergal seems to represent the sun of noontime and of the summer solstice that brings destruction, high summer being the dead season in the Mesopotamian annual cycle, and was also the deity who presides over the netherworld, and who stands at the head of the special pantheon assigned to the government of the dead.Being a deity of the desert, god of fire, which is one of negative aspects of the sun, god of the underworld, and also being a god of one of the religions which rivaled Christianity and Judaism, Nergal was sometimes called a demon and even identified with Satan. According to Collin de Plancy and Johann Weyer, Nergal was depicted as the chief of Hell's 'secret police', and worked as an "'an honorary spy in the service of Beelzebub'.

From Lithuanian legends about Neringa and Naglis. The exact origin and meaning of the name are uncertain, however some scholars believe that it is derived from Old Prussian neria "to dive (like a swimmer)."In Lithuanian folklore, Neringa is a beautiful, gentle giantess who built a mound of sand to keep the stormy waves of the Baltic sea at bay and protect the village and the people who live in it. One day, she catches the eye of Naglis, a dragon (some legends call him a sea serpent) living nearby, who madly falls in love with her. When Naglis realizes that his love is unrequited, in his wrath and his grief, he starts eating the fishermen living in Neringa's village one by one. Neringa is greatly saddened by these occurences, and so she creates a strip of sand between the bay and the Baltic sea, which would seperate her and her subjects from the dragon forever.Its designated name day is August 20.

Means "sea snail" in Ancient Greek, possibly related to Nereus. In Greek mythology he was the only son of Nereus and Doris, with the fifty Nereids as his older sisters. In one legend, he rejected Aphrodite's invitation to Olympus, preferring his life at sea, resulting in him turning into a shellfish by a scorned Aphrodite. In other myths, he was a consort of Poseidon and was made his charioteer, but shortly afterwards was changed into a shellfish by Anteros.

An Oscan prenomen meaning "strong, vigorous" (related to the Latin prenomen Nero 1).It was also the name of a Roman gens.

Meaning unknown, possibly based on Merle. This is the name of a character in L. Frank Baum's novel ''The Enchanted Island of Yew'' (1903).

Neroli oil was named after the princess of Nerola, Anne Marie Orsini (1642-1722), who popularized the essence of bitter orange tree as a perfume, making it fashionable by the end of the 17th century. A known bearer of this name is Neroli Meadows (b. 1985 or 1986), an Australian sports journalist.

He guarded a bridge called the Bridge of Giants.Lancelot gave him the lands surrounding Pendragon Castle when he conquered the castle from Sir Brian of the Isles. In Egyptian mythology, Neseret is a minor but fierce snake (uraeus) goddess whose name translates to "the Fiery One" or "the Flame". She embodies the dangerous and protective fire of the sun, often called upon to scorch the enemies of the cosmic order or burn away the wicked in the underworld.The term neseret is used to describe the mystical, blazing breath or venom that the sacred cobra (uraeus) spits at the foes of the gods. Because Neseret is both a goddess in her own right and a descriptive title for a fiery serpent, she is deeply linked to other solar and protective deities.

Originally a diminutive of Agnes, used independently from at least the 18th century. It is now also used as a diminutive of Vanessa. Since the 1950s it has been used as a nickname for the legendary Loch Ness Monster.
Greek form of Nessus. Nessos of Chios was a pre-Socratic ancient Greek philosopher.

Possibly derived from Greek νῆσσα (nessa) meaning "duck (bird)". In Greek mythology, Nessus was a centaur who was killed by Heracles, and whose tainted blood in turn killed Heracles. He was the son of Centauros. He fought in the battle with the Lapiths and became a ferryman on the river Euenos. His name might refer to his role as a ferryman, carrying passengers across the river on his back.
Cremish Lombard short form of Ernestina.

The name is a Jamaican Patois form of Nestor.This name is best known for being the middle name (but originally the first name) of the Jamaican reggae singer Bob Marley (1945-1981), who also bestowed the name upon three of his sons.Another well-known bearer of the name is Zuma Rossdale (b. 2008), the second son of the singers Gavin Rossdale (b. 1965) and Gwen Stefani (b. 1969). He carries the name as a middle name, which was in all likelihood given to him in honour of Bob Marley.
Medieval variant of Nest and Nesta.
Possibly an Ubykh form of Nesrin.
Mycenaean Greek name meaning "who saves his men", derived from νέομαι (neomai) meaning "to return, come home, flow back" (see Nestor) and ἀνήρ (aner) meaning "man" (genitive ἀνδρός).
Derived from Romanian neştiut "unknown". This was an amuletic name.

An infant girl found by Arthur and Lancelot in an eagle’s nest. She had a ruby necklace around her neck. Arthur gave the baby to Guinevere to raise, but it died in infancy.Her necklace was later awarded to Tristan as a tournament prize.

Means "branch, shoot." Compare Nazareth, which stems from the same word. Netzar features in Sanhedrin 43a in the Talmud, during an apocryphal description of the death of Yeshua the Nazarene, as one of his five disciples. Netzar uses a pun with his name, alluding to Isaiah 11:1, saying, "And a branch {netzer} shall grow out of his roots," and the judges of the Sanhedrin respond with Isaiah 14:9 - "But you are cast out of your grave like an abhorred branch {netzer}," before giving him the death sentence.

The Armenian name "Nevart" is an anglicized form of Նվարդ (Nvard). The etymology of "Nvard" is subject to various interpretations:​(1) Derived from the Armenian words նոր (nor), meaning "new," and վարդ (vard), meaning "rose," thus translating to "new rose." ​(2) Originating from նուրբ (nurp), meaning "tender," combined with վարդ (vard), resulting in "tender rose." ​(3) Stemming from նվեր (nver), meaning "gift," indicating "a gift."The name "Nvard" has historical significance in Armenian culture and is associated with beauty and elegance. The anglicized form "Nevart" includes an 'e' to reflect the original Armenian pronunciation more accurately.

This was the name of a goddess in Elamite religion. The name Nibar is the surname Rabin, spelled backwards. Yitzhak Rabin was an Israeli politician, statesman and general. He was the fifth Prime Minister of Israel. It can be also a combination of the names Niv and Bar, or a combination of the names Nir and Bar.

According to Josephus' Antiquitates Judaicae XI 7:2 and 8:2, Nicaso was the name of a daughter of King Sanballat of Samaria who was given by Sanballat in a political marriage to Manasseh, brother of the high priest Jaddua. The elders of Jerusalem told him to either divorce Nicaso or revoke his priesthood, as a part of the mass divorce initiative of intermarried couples (Ezra 10:33).
Latinized form of Nikator. A notable bearer of this name was Seleucus I Nicator (c. 358 BC-281 BC), one of the generals of Alexander the Great. He later founded the Seleucid Empire.

Latinized form of Nike. In Italy it's also used as diminutive of names with the element nice (derived from nike) such as Berenice and Eunice. In Greek mythology, Nice was a Thespian princess as one of the fifty daughters of King Thespius, and mother of Nicodromus by the hero Heracles.

Saint Nicephorus I (c. 758 - 829) was a Greek Orthodox theologian, historian, and patriarch of Constantinople (806–815) whose chronicles of Byzantine history and writings in defense of Byzantine veneration of icons provide data otherwise unavailable on early Christian thought and practice.

Meaning unknown. This was the name of the father of Fanny Cochrane Smith (1834-1905), who was the last fluent speaker of a Tasmanian language.

She died in circa 345 BC, twenty days after giving birth to their daughter Thessalonike of Macedon. Nicesipolis was likely of noble Thessalian origin and may have been a niece of Jason of Pherae.

Nichette is the name of a character in Alexandre Dumas's (fils) 1848 novel and play named "Camille" (also known as "The Lady of the Camellias"). The name Nichette was also featured in the title of a movie short from 1911 named "The Heart of Nichette". It was also used for a character in the 1917 musical comedy play "Yes, Uncle!". Since Dumas fils is the earliest instance of the aforementioned sources, it is unclear whether Dumas fils independently made the name up, or whether he took it from the highly rare French surname Nichette (also compare the surnames Nichet, Niquet and Niquette) - which is probably a patronymic derived from the first name Nicolas.

There, it can be: a short form of Nicholas, a pet form of Nicholas' short form Nick and an anglicisation of the Scottish name Nichol. Very rarily will this name have been inspired by the coin or the metal, in which case nickel is ultimately derived from German nickel meaning "goblin, devil."The name Nickel is still in use in the English-speaking world, Germany and the Netherlands to this day, albeit (very) rarely.

The name Nidra is related to the concept of nidra, which is “one of the four states of consciousness in Hindu philosophy”. Nidra is the state of “deep sleep”, where the individual is “unaware of the external world and the inner self”. Nidra is also associated with the goddess Nidra, who is “the personification of sleep” and the consort of Vishnu, the “supreme god of Hinduism”. Nidra is sometimes depicted as a “beautiful woman holding a lotus flower and resting on a bed of snakes”. Nidra is also the name of a form of yoga that involves “guided meditation and relaxation”.The name Nidra comes from the Sanskrit word निद्रा (nidrā), which means “sleep”. It is a learned borrowing from Sanskrit into Hindi, and a doublet of the word नीद (nīd), which also means “sleep”. The concept of nidra as a state of consciousness is mentioned in the Upanishads and the Mahabharata, while the goddess Nidra appears in the Devīmāhātmya. Nidra is also linked to meditation in Shaiva and Buddhist tantras and is used as a synonym for samadhi, the state of intense concentration, in some medieval hatha yoga texts. The modern form of yoga nidra, which is a technique of guided relaxation, was popularized by Satyananda Saraswati in 1976.

In Dutch, Frisian and Limburgish, Nies is predominantly a masculine given name. For the Dutch, it is a variant form of Nijs (which has a different pronunciation), while for the Frisians, it is a variant spelling of Nys (which has the same pronunciation). As for the Limburgians: in their case, the name is a short form of Dionysius. In all three cases, the name Dionysius is ultimately at the root, so in the end, Nies (as a masculine name) has the same etymological origin in these three languages.With that said, Nies can also be a feminine given name in all three languages. In this case, the name is a short form of Angenies (Dutch and Limburgish) and Angenietsje (West Frisian). Both names are ultimately derived from the Greek feminine name Agnes, meaning that the two names have the same etymological origin and are therefore not all that different from each other.

Niggle is the main character in "Leaf by Niggle", a short story written by J.R.R. Tolkien, the author of "The Lord of the Rings", "The Hobbit", and many other stories. Niggle's story, however, has nothing to do with Middle Earth, the lands in which Tolkien's most famous works take place. Niggle is a simple man, who lives out in the country and enjoys painting. His central work is a massive painting of a tree, and the landscape around it. Unfortunately, he is never able to finish it. He eventually has to leave on a journey (which represents death), and when he arrives in heaven he finds that it is, for him, the landscape in his painting, and that the Tree is there, complete and living.

column12: This name can be used as 仁子, 仁湖, 仁胡, 二子, 二胡, 日子 or 日湖 with 仁 (jin, ni, non) meaning "benevolence, charity, humanity, kernel, man, virtue", 二 (ji, ni, futa, futata.bi, futa.tsu) meaning "two", 日 (jitsu, nichi, -ka, hi, -hi, ni) meaning "day, Japan, sun", 子 (shi, su, tsu, ko, -ko, -ne) meaning "child, sign of the rat (1st sign of the Chinese zodiac)", 湖 (ko, mizuumi) meaning "lake" and 胡 (u, ko, go, nanzo, ebisu, kuru) meaning "barbarian, foreign."

Derived from Greek νίκη (nike) meaning "victory" and πόλις (polis) meaning "city".

Derived from Latin Nicopolitanus meaning "Nicopolitan, Nicopolite", as in: a citizen of Nicopolis. Also compare the Greek word πολίτης (polites) meaning "citizen, freeman".Nicopolis was the capital city of the Roman province of Epirus Vetus, located in what is now western Greece. It was founded in 28 BC by the Roman emperor Augustus, who gave it the Greek name of Νικόπολις (Nikopolis), which meant "city of victory", derived from Greek νίκη (nike) meaning "victory" combined with Greek πόλις (polis) meaning "city".Nikopolitianos is the name of a 4th-century martyr and saint of Sebaste (which is now Sivas in Turkey), whose feast day is on November 3 (Julian) and 16 (Gregorian). He is better known under the name Nictopolion, which is a variant transcription of Niktopolion, the Russian form of his name. The Russian form is possibly derived from a Greek corruption of his name, which was probably Νυκτοπολιων (Nyktopolion) or something close to it. Because of this corruption, the saint's name is sometimes thought to mean "night wanderer", due to association with the Greek adjective νυκτιπόλος (nyktipolos) meaning "roaming by night". The meaning of "many nights" or "much of the night" has also been encountered, as some people thought that the name was derived from the Greek noun νύξ (nyx) meaning "night" (see Nyx) combined with the Greek adjective πολύς (polys) meaning "many" as well as "much".

Unknown meaning. Nikuyah Walker is the first Black female mayor of Charlottesville, Virginia.

A name for Ninella as "lady of the earth".Ninella, 'the pure Lady' The child of Enki and Ninella was the ancestor of mankind.The Sumerian account of Beginnings centres around the production by the gods of water, Enki and his consort Ninella, of a great number of canals bringing rain to the desolate fields of a dry continent. Other Assyriologists have asserted that Ninkarrak is more likely to be a deity from a culture that pre-dated the Sumerian and Akkadian cultures, who was assimilated into Sumerian religion, meaning that her name originates from a language that is thus far unknown. Ninkarrak was a healing goddess mainly worshipped in Sippar and Terqa.

Likely means "mistress of beer", derived from the Sumerian elements nin ("lady") and kaš ("beer, alcoholic beverage"). As a goddess of beer, Ninkasi was associated with the production and consumption of beer, and all of the positive and negative effects that came with it.

Means "mistress beloved by the prince", deriving from the Sumerian elements nin ("queen, mistress, lady"), ki-áĝ ("beloved"), and nun ("prince, noble"). Attested as another name for the goddess Sadarnunna.
Means "lady of gold", deriving from the Sumerian elements nin ("lady or mistress") and kù-sig ("gold"). Attested as a Sumerian name for the goddess Shalash.
From Thai นิล (ninla) meaning "jet, black, dark (precious stone)" and วรรณ (wan) meaning "colour, hue, complexion".

Means "great queen" in Sumerian. Another name of Ninhursag.In Babylonian legend she was given the name Ninmah by her son Ninurta in order to commemorate his creation of the mountains. Ninmah/Ninmenna may have originally been independent goddesses who were later identified as and merged with Ninhursag.

Means "lady of battle", deriving from the Sumerian elements nin ("queen, mistress, lady") and me (an archaic word for "battle"). This is attested as an epithet of Inanna, in her capacity as a war goddess. It is also suggested by some scholars that a form of this name may have been used to refer to Annunitum.
Diminutive of many names, such as Ingrid and Kristina.

The name of the Lady of the Lake in the Old French Vulgate Lancelot and the continuation to the Vulgate Merlin, known as the Suite du Merlin. (The earlier Vulgate Merlin uses the variant form Viviane.) 'She raised Lancelot and imprisoned Merlin. The Middle English Prose Merlin says that the name was Hebrew, meaning "I shall not lie". Arthour and Merlin, which gives the Lady of the Lake role to Morgan le Fay, names Ninniane as a town near Morgan's residence. Some scholars have favored a Celtic origin for Ninniane, finding it in the lady Rhiannon, wife of Lord Pwyll. Merlin calls her Nimue' (Christopher W. Bruce, 1999). This name is possibly of Celtic origin, perhaps related to Ninian; a derivation from Proto-Celtic *nino- "ash tree" has been proposed.
Diminutive of Ninian. This was the name of a 6th-century saint, one of the Twelve Apostles of Ireland.
This name was borne by a 5th-century Breton saint whose life is recorded in the Vita Sanctæ Ninnocæ. It has been speculated that she might be identical with Saint Candide.
Means "Little Boy" or "Christ Child" in Spanish.

column3: 二乃, 仁乃, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 二 (ni) meaning "two" or 仁 (ni) meaning "benevolence" combined with 乃 (no), a possessive particle. Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.
Meaning "one whose anger is new", from the elements nino ("young" or "new"), and gniew ("anger").

Variant transcription of Ninochka.It was used for the main character Nina Ivanovna "Ninotchka" Yakushova in the eponymous 1939 film, portrayed by Greta Garbo. One real life bearer of this name is Filipina feminist, author, journalist and human rights activist Ninotchka Rosca (1946-).
Diminutive of Catarino and Provençal form of Ninon.
Diminutive of Benigno.A famous bearer of this nickname was Benigno "Ninoy" Aquino Jr., a Filipino politician.

Means "Lady Chosen by (means of) the Heart (Omens)", deriving from the Sumerian elements nin ("queen, mistress") and saĝ ("to chose"). Name borne by a high-priestess of Meslamta-ea (fl. 18th century BCE), known for a letter she wrote to the king of Larsa, Rim-Sin I.

Possibly means "Lady of Subartu", deriving from Sumerian element nin, and shubur (Sumerian form of Subartu, a kingdom in Upper Mesopotamia referenced in three of the Amarna Letters). Ninshubur was a 'sukkal' (vizier) to the goddess Inanna.
Ancient Sumerian god or goddess of Venus. The name means "divine lady, illumination of heaven" or "divine lady of the redness of heaven".

Means "lady of the diadem of lapis lazuli", deriving from the Sumerian elements nin ("lady or mistress"), aga ("diadem, circlet, crown"), and naza-gìn ("lapis lazuli, precious stone"). This was one of the Sumerian names for the goddess Shalash, that was given in the Great God List.

Meaning uncertain. It may be a variant of Nienke or Nina 1.This name was first borne to Dutch singer Ninthe Kiemeneij (1985-), going only by her first name, who popularised the name in 2005 after she was featured on hip hop duo Lange Frans & Baas B's 2004 single 'Zinloos'.
Means "mistress who revives the dead". Nintinugga was a Mesopotamian medicine goddess, who was also associated with the underworld. Nintinugga was primarily worshipped in Nippur.
Means "lady of birth" in Sumerian. Another name of Ninhursag
The name of the Sumerian mother goddess, derived from nin meaning "lady, queen" and tur meaning "hut", with allusions to the word šà-tùr meaning "womb".
Medieval Italian diminutive form of Nina 1.

Means "lady who amazes the world", deriving from the Sumerian elements nin ("lady or mistress"), u-di ("admiration, amazement"), and šár ("all, totality, world"). Attested as a Sumerian name for the goddess Shalash.
Diminutive of Nino 2. Also compare Ninutsa, which is sometimes transcribed as Ninuca.
Probably a pet form of Nino 2.

Of uncertain etymology, likely deriving in part from the Sumerian element nin ("queen, mistress, lady"). Name borne by a tutelary goddess of Umma, who was considered to be the consort of the god Shara.
Means "Ninurta is giver of progeny". Name borne by a Babylonian king of the 2nd dynasty of Isin, who ruled c. 1127–1122 BC.
Means "she of Nineveh". This was an epithet of the Hurrian goddess Šauška that was also possibly used in reference to the goddess Ishtar.
From the modern Assyrian form of the name of the ancient Assyrian capital city of Nineveh.
Dena'ina Athabaskan meaning "Little Animal". English equivalent is "Fox".
Serbian, Bulgarian, Macedonian, Russian, Kazakh and Slovene form of Niobe.
French and Hungarian form of Niobe.
Possibly from the Irish name of the fifth letter of the Ogham alphabet, an Early Medieval alphabet used to write the early Irish language and later the Old Irish language.
Possibly a transferred use of the surname Nionne.
Alternate transcription of Persian نیوشا (see Niusha).
Alternate transcription of Thai นิภาพรรณ (see Niphaphan).
Alternate transcription of Thai นิภาภัทร (see Niphaphat).

Alternate transcription of Thai นิภาวรรณ (see Niphawan).
Alternate transcription of Thai นิภาวรรณ (see Niphawan).
Alternate transcription of Thai นิภาพรรณ (see Niphaphan).
Alternate transcription of Thai นิภาภัทร (see Niphaphat).
From Thai นิภา (nipha) meaning "equal, comparable, similar" and พรรณ (phan) meaning "kind, variety, type".
From Thai นิภา (nipha) meaning "equal, comparable, similar" and ภัทร (phat) meaning "magnificent, glorious, auspicious".
From Thai นิภา (nipha) meaning "equal, comparable, similar" and พร (phon) meaning "blessing".
From Lao ນິພາ (nipha) meaning "similar, equivalent" and ພອນ (phone) meaning "blessing".
Alternate transcription of Thai นิภาพร (see Niphaphon).
Alternate transcription of Thai นิภาพร (see Niphaphon).
From Thai นิภา (nipha) meaning "equal, comparable, similar" and รัตน์ (rat) meaning "gem, jewel".
From Thai นิภา (nipha) meaning "equal, comparable, similar" and วรรณ (wan) meaning "colour, tint".
Means "writing, composition, literary work" in Thai, ultimately from Sanskrit निबन्ध (nibandha).
Meaning unknown; possibly related to hnipinn ("drooping; downcast"). This is the name of a dwarf in Norse mythology.
Alternate transcription of Thai นิพนธ์ (see Niphon).
Skilled in all that he attempts
Means "full moon" in Tamil. From the Tamil நிறைகலை 'the full moon', from நிறை (niṟai) 'become full'.
Alternate transcription of Thai นิรมล (see Niramon).
Means "forever, eternally, always" in Thai, ultimately from Sanskrit निरन्तर (nirantara).

The name Nirani may have derived from the Sanskrit word nirāṇa, which means “free from bonds, liberated, pure, clear” or “a kind of precious stone”. Another possible origin is the Tamil word nīraṇi, which means “a river” or "a stream".

Means "unstained, untinged, pure, spotless" in Sanskrit. This is an epithet of the Hindu god Shiva, as well as a title of Krishna in the Hindu epic the Bhagavad Gita. This spelling also represents the modern feminine form of the name.
Variant or feminine form of Nirav.

column3: 仁礼, 仁嶺, 丹麗, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 仁 (ni) meaning "benevolence" combined with 嶺 (rei) meaning "peak; summit; ridge; top" or 礼 (rei) meaning "a bow, the gesture of bending at the waist". Other kanji combinations are possible.A famous male bearer is Nirei Fukuzumi, a Japanese racing driver.
Combination of the names Nir - means "plowed field" and El - means "God", the meaning is "Field of God".
Possilbly the name is derived from the Greek name Eirene meaning “peace”
Etymology unknown. In Greek mythology, Nireus was a king of Syme who fought with the Greeks in the Trojan War. Nireus was also the name of a son of Poseidon and the Thessalian princess Canace.
Norwegian variant of Neri. It is most prominent in Buskerud and Telemark, Norway.
In Japanese folklore, whenever Kirin lose their temper, they transform into beasts of fire and rage called Nirik.
Means "desired, wanted" in Malagasy, from the word irina meaning "to be desired".
From the Malagasy niri meaning "to desire" and soa meaning "good".
Hebrew name for Ridolfia segetum, a genus of plant similar to the dill.
MEANING - measure, value, equivalent, to build, fabricate, create,to make
Variant of Nir, known by the famous Israeli actor Niro Levi (born in 1968)
Alternate transcription of Thai นิรุตติ์ (see Nirut).
This name signifies a sense of purity, brightness, or new beginnings.
Means "absence of". Nirṛti is the Hindu goddess of deathly hidden realms, sorrows, death and corruption and one of the dikpāla (guardians of the directions), representing the southwest.
The name of the Hindu goddess of deathly hidden realms and sorrows as well as the southwest direction. Her name is derived from nirhti meaning "absence of".
From the Chinese 霓 (ní) meaning "rainbow" and 睿 (ruì) meaning "shrewd, astute, clever".
Alternate transcription of Thai นิรันดร์ (see Niran).
Means "language, speech" in Thai, ultimately from Sanskrit निरुक्ति (nirukti).
"A Soul that has reached the final goal of being free from the cycle of birth & death", "Reached state of Nirvana"
Ancient persian, comes from the name Nirvana, this presents the person who attains the state of absolute awareness and conciousness

Borrowed from Sanskrit निर्वाण (nirvana), meaning "blown out, extinguished" and referring to a state of paradise or heightened pleasure. Its use in the United States started sporadically in the 1970s and the rock band Nirvana (1987-1994) may have helped it to rise further in later years.
Derived from a Sanskrit word meaning 'Goddess of bliss'
Derived from Indonesian nirwana meaning "heaven" or "enlightenment, liberation", ultimately from Sanskrit निर्वाण (nirvana).
Means "heaven" or "enlightenment, liberation" in Indonesian, ultimately from Sanskrit निर्वाण (nirvana).
Derived from Javanese nirwana meaning "heaven" or "enlightenment, liberation", ultimately from Sanskrit निर्वाण (nirvana).

column3: นิสา(Thai)|新咲, 虹彩, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Thai นิศา (nisa) meaning "night", ultimately from Sanskrit निशा (niśā).
Derived from the Sumerian element 𒉀 naga, meaning "wheat". Nisaba was the Sumerian goddess of writing, learning, and the harvest. She was considered a patron goddess of scribes.
From Thai นิศา (nisa) meaning "night" and ชล (chon) meaning "water".
Etymology uncertain, although the first element may be related to the Adyghe нысэ (nyse) meaning "sister in law".
From Thai นิศา (nisa) meaning "night" and มณี (mani) meaning "precious stone, jewel".

Possibly derived from Guanche *(a)nəssamar meaning literally "man who invites, lets someone pass or grants passage to someone; man who presents or submits something". This was listed in a baptismal register from Seville dating to the 15th century; the sex and age of the bearer were not recorded. In modern times it has been used as a Canarian feminine name.
The first month name of the Babylonian calendar. It denotes the month of April in modern Turkish.
From Thai นิศา (nisa) meaning "night" and รัตน์ (rat) meaning "gem, jewel".
Perso-Arabic-origin multi-part name consisting of the elements Nisar and ḥaqq.
There is a state park in California named after Nisene Marks.See: https://www.parks.ca.gov/?page_id=666
Meaning "Night", or possibly from a Plant called Daruhldi.

column3: 錦(Japanese Kanji)|にしき(Japanese Hiragana)|ニシキ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name is used as 錦 (kin, nishiki) meaning "brocade," most likely deriving from 丹 (ni) meaning "red" and 頻 (shiki) meaning "repetition."It is rarely used.

column3: 仁志子, 西湖, 錦子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 仁 (ni) meaning "humaneness, benevolence, kindness", 志 (shi) meaning "purpose, will, determination, aspiration, ambition" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Japanese 西 (nishi) meaning "west" combined with 男 (o) meaning "male". Other kanji combinations are possible.

Name Nishith generally means Night, is of Indian origin, Name Nishith is a Masculine (or Boy) name. This name is shared across persons, who are either Jain or Hindu by religion. Name Nishith belongs to rashi Vrushik (Scorpio) with dominant planet Mars (Mangal).
Derived from nishon meaning "mark, sign" and bibi meaning "learned woman".
Derived from nishon meaning "mark, sign" and gul meaning "rose, flower".
Derived from nishon meaning "mark, sign" and oy meaning "moon".

The name Nishtha has its origins in the Sanskrit language, where it is derived from the word "निष्ठा" (Nishthā). It carries the meaning of "devotion" or "dedication," reflecting qualities of steadfastness and commitment. The name is often associated with a person who is reliable and earnest in their pursuits.Linguistic Origin:- Language: Sanskrit- Etymology: The name Nishtha comes from the Sanskrit term "निष्ठा" (Nishthā), which translates to "faithfulness" or "steadfastness."In Indian culture, the name Nishtha is valued for its deep and meaningful significance, embodying the virtues of loyalty and unwavering dedication.
From the Chinese characters 霓 (ní) meaning "rainbow; variegated, colored" and 霜 (shuāng) meaning "frost; crystallized".
From the Chinese 霓 (ní) meaning "rainbow" and 烁 (shuò) meaning "shine, glitter, sparkle".
suchira's boyfriend in a very ethnic world of life and love in the old Indian stories.
Truncated form of Anísia and Dionísia. Nísia Floresta, born Dionísia Gonçalves Pinto, (1810 - 1885) was a Brazilian educator, translator, writer, poet, philosopher, and feminist.
Nisien is a figure in Welsh mythology, the son of Penarddun and Euroswydd and twin brother of Efnysien.
Means "miracles" in Hebrew, the plural of נס (nes) meaning "miracle".
Alternate transcription of Arabic نسرين (see Nisrin).
Alternate transcription of Arabic نسرين (see Nisrin) chiefly used in North Africa.

The Assyrian god of agriculture, in whose temple king Sennacherib was worshiping when he was assassinated by his own sons in revenge for the destruction of Babylon (2 Kings 19:37; Isa. 37:38). Josephus calls him Dagon.
Alternate transcription of Arabic نسرين (see Nasrin), chifely used in Morocco.

The seventh month of the Hebrew calendar and the first month of the ancient Hebrew calendar. The month of Pesach. The name was brought from the Babylonian exile and originates from the Akkadian word "Nisanu", from the Hebrew word for flower bud Nitzan, which blossoms in spring.
Yiddish name. May be a pet form of Nessia, or a female form of Nissan or Nissim.

‘“Nis’ meaning ‘Sun or Moon’, and ‘shoku’ meaning “food” or “eclipse”My father gave me this name meaning solar eclipse, to always remind myself to never settle for living in someone else’s shadow, but to stand in front and steal the show. As far as I know, this name is unique in Japanese culture. (Other kanji may be used to form this name)
First used as a biblical term in Exodus. The full word being Jehovah-Nissi, and meaning "victorious" or "banner". Moses named the victory banner as such after defeating the Amalekites.
This name is showing up on other name sites with the same meaning. (They are not my entries.)
Alternate transcription of Hebrew נסים (see Nisim).
Alternate transcription of Arabic نسرين (see Nisrin) chiefly used in North Africa.
Alternate transcription of Arabic نسرين (see Nisrin) chiefly used in North Africa.
Likely a diminutive of Eunice or Genesis.

MEANING : free from desires, Satisfied. It is joining of निः / निस् + तृषा . Here निः means without + तृषा means desireUsage : Sanskrit, Indian, Tamil, Telugu, Nepali, Sinhalese, Hindi, Marathi, Gujarati, Assamese, Malayalam, Kannada, Bengali, Hinduism, Fijian, American
Ancient Egyptian masculine name meaning "He, who belongs to Heqet".
Derived from Sanskrit नीत (nīta) meaning "modest, correct, well-behaved" or "guided, led".
From Sanskrit नित्य (nitya) meaning "eternal". This was another name of 16th-century Bengali Hindu saint Nityananda.
Derived from Sanskrit nitara (नितर) "deeply fixed; standing firm; having deep roots".
Proto-Germanic nīþą "hate, envy, malice" + Old Saxon hard, Old High German hart "strong, hard".
MEANING - gained or obtained hope. Here नीत means gained + आशा means hope.
Alternate transcription of Hebrew ניתאי (see Nitai).This name first appeared in the Talmud Era. Nittai of Arbela was one of the Tannaim.
Alternate transcription of Thai นิตยา (see Nittaya).

Possibly means "God is extended", derived from Hebrew נִטָּה (nita) meaning "extended, stretched out" combined with אֵל (ʾel) meaning "God". This is the name of an angel belonging to the order of the Principalities. He is one of the 72 angels bearing the explicit name of God (the Shem HaMephorash), as interpreted by some Christian Kabbalists.
Derives from Old Norse elements niðr "ancestor, kinsman, relative" and bjǫrg "help, salvation".

Means "malice striker". In Norse mythology this is the name of the dragon who lives in the pool Hvergelmir and gnaws at the roots of Yggdrasil. He lives in Nástönd, a part of Niflheimr ("the dark home") or Helheimr ("Hel's home") and chews on the corpses of those guilty of murder, adultery and oath-breaking (which the Norsemen considered the worst possible crimes).
From Old Norse name meaning "dark one" from Old Norse nið meaning "new moon". This is also the name of a dwarf in Norse Mythology.

Old Norse byname, from Old Norse níðingr meaning "villain, nithing" or composed of Old Norse níð "contumely, derision" with an -ingr-ending (ingr-endings are quite common in Old Norse names. They indicate a patronymic form meaning 'son/descendant of ...' or just 'belonging to ...', 'coming from).

column3: นิธิพร(Thai)|นิธิพล(Thai)
column12: From Thai นิธิ (nithi) meaning "treasure" and พร (phon) meaning "blessing".
Means "ancestor, kinsman". In Norse mythology this is one of the sons of Jarl and Erna.
From Sanskrit नीति (nīti) meaning "guidance, moral conduct, behaviour". It is a feminine name in India while it is masculine in Thailand.
From the Chinese 旎 (nǐ) meaning "fluttering of flag; romantic" or 霓 (ní) meaning "rainbow" and 婷 (tíng) meaning "pretty, graceful".

Greek form of Egyptian nt-jqr.t meaning "Neith is excellent", derived from the name of the goddess Neith combined with jqr "excellent, worthy, reliable" and the suffix tj. This was the name of several prominent ancient Egyptian women, and may have been the nomen of pharaoh Netjerkare.
From the word nitro, referring to the system that adds nitrous oxide to a car engine to produce a boost. This is the name of a Marvel supervillain first appearing in 1974.
The part of the plant from which the flower and fruit grow.
Medieval Silesian German diminutive of Nikolaus.
Possibly a Romani form of Mitchell.

Means "eternal bliss" from Sanskrit नित्य (nitya) meaning "eternal" and आनन्द (ānanda) meaning "happiness, bliss". This was the name of a prominent 16th-century Bengali Hindu saint. He was a close friend and disciple of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, the founder of the Gaudiya Vaishnavi tradition.
Derived from the word נצחון (Nitzahon) meaning "Victory". This name appeared as a Hebrew translation of Victoria but was never used as an independent name, making it extremely rare.
From Chinese 妞 (niū) meaning "girl" or 牛 (niú) meaning "cattle, ox, cow", in addition to other hanzi that are pronounced similarly.
From the Chinese 妞 (niū) meaning "girl" and 宝 (bǎo) meaning "treasure, jewel, precious, rare".
From the Chinese 妞 (niū) meaning "girl" and 钏 (chuàn) meaning "bracelet".
From the Chinese 妞 (niū) meaning "girl" and 娥 (é) meaning "be beautiful, good".

Means "cowherd", from Chinese 牛 (niú) meaning "cow" and 郎 (láng) meaning "man, youth". In Chinese mythology, Niulang is the main character of The Cowherd and the Weaver Girl, who falls in love with the deity Zhinü. He is associated with the star Altair.
From the Chinese 妞 (niū) meaning "girl" and 妹 (mèi) meaning "younger sister".
From the Chinese 妞 (niū) meaning "girl" and 晴 (qíng) meaning "clear weather".
One of the Belarusian versions of the name Anna
Variant of Niurka, with the popular suffix -is.
Means "tearing apart coconut leaves" in Bellonese.
Meaning "Woman with a Pestle" in Ainu.
From the Chinese 妞 (niū) meaning "girl" and 珍 (zhēn) meaning "precious, valuable, rare".
Gothic niujis, Old High German niuwi, niwi "new" + Old Saxon hard, Old High German hart "strong, hard".

From the Roman name for the island of Tenerife (present-day Canary Islands, Spain), which was derived from Latin nivarius meaning "of snow, pertaining to snow" - itself from nix "snow" (genitive nivis, plural nives) - after the snow-covered peak of Mount Teide.

column3: นิวัฒน์, นิวัติ(Thai)
column12: Alternate transcription of Thai นิวัฒน์ or นิวัติ (see Niwat).

This name was originated in back 90's by a great leader Suresh bhai's daughter.They originally wanted Nivedita, but as of her uncle's blessings and very good education, he named her Nivatha instead of Nivedita in her Birth certificate.
Old (Kleinschmidt orthography) spelling of Nivi. This is borne by Greenlandic singer-songwriter and actress Nive Nielsen.
From Latin niveus meaning "snow-white" (itself from nivis, "of snow"). It was used by Isabel Allende for a character in her novel 'La casa de los espíritus' (1982).
Likely a variant of Nívea influenced by Nevaeh.
From Sanskrit निवेदित (nivedita) meaning "made known, announced, delivered, given".
Alternate transcription of Thai นิเวศ (see Niwet).
Alternate transcription of Thai นิเวศ (see Niwet).
Used by Bernardo Tasso for a character in his epic poem L'Amadigi. In the poem Nivetta, Carvilia and Morganetta are the three daughters of Morgan le Fay.
Derived from the Hebrew name Niv, meaning either "speech, expression" or "fang, tusk".
Possibly a variant of Nevaeh or Navia
Formed from Niviaq and the Inuit name suffix na, which indicates a personal name.
Derived from the Greenlandic word niviarsiaq "girl" (compare Niviarsiaq), possibly meaning "reincarnated as a girl".
Greenlandic name meaning "young woman or girl, maiden, girl of marriageable age", combined with Niviaĸ and -siaq "acquired as" or meaning "Rosebay Willowherb" (Name meanings depend per dialect).
Greenlandic name meaning "graceful, beautiful girl" with the combination of Niviaĸ and suffix -tsiaq "beautiful", "fair", "fairly good", "precious", "sweet", "fair-sized", "nice", "good", "handsome".
Greenlandic name meaning "dear, sweet girl". Combination of Niviaĸ and suffix -nnguaq "sweet, dear".
Hypocoristic of names beginning with Old High German word niwi meaning "new".
Combination of the names Niv and Or with the meaning of "bright dialect, bright speech".
Combination of nittaalaq meaning 'thick air with rain or snow' and -nnguaq. "sweet, dear".
The goddess of the road or spirit of the journey. She is also known as Olwen, the name under which she appears as the daughter of the giant Yspaddaden.

column3: นิวัฒน์, นิวัติ(Thai)
column12: Means "return" in Thai, ultimately from Sanskrit निवृत्ति (nivritti).
From the Shipibo niwe meaning "wind" and the genitive suffix -n.
Alternate transcription of Thai นิเวศ (see Niwet).

This is the name of feminine shapeshifting water spirits in Germanic mythology, who apparently derive their name from Proto-Germanic nikwus or nikwis(i) "wash". See also Nix for the male counterpart(s).

From the English word nixie meaning "water fairy, water sprite", which is related to German Nixe. Alternatively in some cases it could be an invented name using the sounds present in Dixie, Trixie and Pixie, or possibly an elaboration of Nix.
Of the Yaminawá language that belongs to the Panoan language family.
Created in the 1940s, probably modelled on Taíno names that contain the letter X such as Guarionex and Caguax.
Elaboration of Nixza using the popular name suffix liz (from Elizabeth or a related name).
A combination of Nixzaliz and Maria. A famous person with this name is Nixzmary Brown (1998-2006).
MEANING : path, access,coming or arrivalUsage : Sanskrit, Indian, Tamil, Telugu, Nepali, Sinhalese, Kannada, Marathi, Hindi, Sikh, Buddhist, Gujarati, Assamese, Oriya, Bengali
Possibly a variant of Niya or Aniyah.
From hindu, meaning, restraint of mind; ethical rules; Discipline activity in accordance in the rules
MEANING : a way, access, arrivalUsage : Sanskrit, Indian, Tamil, Telugu, Nepali, Sinhalese, Kannada, Marathi, Gujarati, Assamese, Indonesian, Fijian, Mauritian, Hindi

Combination of Niyaz with the Turkish military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".
From Persian نیاز (niyāz) meaning "need, necessity, want, supplication, wish, desire".

She is best known for 'Binti', 'Who Fears Death', 'Zahrah the Windseeker', 'Akata Witch', 'Africanfuturist 419' and 'Lagoon'. In 2015, Brittle Paper named her the African Literary Person of the Year.
Originated from the Hebrew given names Noah 1 and Noa 1. This name is mostly used among children from Christian families in Korea.

From the Hebrew name No'adhyah (also found spelled as Now'adyah) which meant "meeting with Yahweh". In the Bible, this was the name of a female prophet (mentioned in Neh. 6:14) as well as the name of a son of Binnui, a Levite (mentioned in Ezra 8:33).

column3: のあこ(Japanese Hiragana)|ノアコ(Japanese Katakana)|乃亜子, 望愛子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 望 (no) meaning "hope", 愛 (a) meaning "love, affection" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Combination of the names Noah 2 and Li 2 means "my motion" in Hebrew.
Icelandic and Faroese form of Noam.
From Japanese 望 (no) meaning "hope", 歩 (a) meaning "walk" combined with 実 (mi) meaning "reality, truth". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Variant of Oan by misinterpreting the Breton article an "the" as part of the name.
Could be a combination of Noa 1, Noah 1 or the prefix no- and Anna.It could also be a variant of Joanna, probably influenced by names that begin in no- or it could be an elaborated form of Noa 1.
French Polynesian name, derived from no meaning "from, of" or noa meaning "free, freely, solely" and arii meaning "chief".

Real name of Amon from Legend of Korra, an American animated television series that aired on the Nickelodeon television network from 2012 to 2014.Alaskan place CDP Noatak was established as a fishing and hunting camp in the 1800s. Two identifiable groups of Inupiat resided on the Noatak River. The Nautaagmiut (called "Noatagamut" in the 1880 census), Inupiaq for "inland river people", lived upriver, and the Napaaqtugmiut, meaning "people of the trees", lived downriver. By the early 20th century, the missionaries Robert and Carrie Samms settled in what they called "Noatak".

column3: のあと(Japanese Hiragana)|希亜斗, 希空斗, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 希 (no) meaning "hope, beg, request, rare", 亜 (a) meaning "second, Asia" or 空 (a) meaning "sky" combined with 斗 (to), which refers to a Chinese constellation. Other kanji combinations are possible.
The name of a J.R.R. Tolkien character.
Nobah, of the Tribe of Manasseh defeated the Amorites, took the villages of Kenath and renamed it Nobah according to Numbers 32:42.
Means "new spring" in Persian نو (now) meaning "new, fresh" combined with بهار (bahār) meaning "spring (season)".
From Japanese 野 (no) meaning "field, rough, natural" and 薔薇 (bara) meaning "rose". A fictional character with this name is Nobara Kugisaki from 'Jujutsu Kaisen' manga series.
A common nickname and short form of Norbert.Nobby Nobbs is a character in the series Discworld, which is written by Terry Pratchett. His real name is Cecil.
Transferred use of the surname Nobel.
Means "the one who writes" in Zulu.

column3: 進, 伸, 延(Japanese Kanji)|のびる(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: From 進 (nobiru) meaning "to advance, make progress, enter", 延 (nobiru) meaning "extend, prolong, lengthen, postpone", or 伸 (nobiru) meaning "lengthen". Other kanji or kanji combinations can be used.
The name of the main character in The Graveyard Book by Neil Gaiman. The novel is about a little boy, named Nobody Owens, who is raised in a graveyard by ghosts.
Alternate transcription of Thai นพพล (see Nopphon).

From Japanese 信 (nobu) meaning "trust", 延 (nobu) meaning "prolong, stretch", and 晶 (aki) meaning "clear, crystal", 明 (aki) meaning "bright, light, clear" or 秋 (aki) meaning "autumn". Other kanji combinations are also possible.
Means "grace" or "mother of grace" in Xhosa.

column3: ノブエ(Japanese Katakana)|のぶ え(Japanese Hiragana)|信絵, 延恵, 伸枝, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 伸 (nobu) meaning "open, stretch, extend" combined with 枝 (e) meaning "branch, limb, bough, twig". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Japanese 信 (nobu) meaning "trust" or 延 (nobu) meaning "prolong, stretch" combined with 二 (fu) meaning "two" and 三 (mi) meaning "three". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 信英, 信秀, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|ノブヒデ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 信 (Nobu) meaning "trust" and 英 (Hide) meaning "excellent, outstanding". Other combinations of kanji characters are possible. Oda Nobuhide was the father of Oda Nobunaga.

column3: 信彦, 伸彦, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 信 (nobu) meaning "faith, believe, trust" or 伸 (nobu) meaning "extend, stretch, open" combined with 彦 (hiko) meaning "boy, prince". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 伸大, 伸博, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 伸 (nobu) meaning "extend, stretch, open", 延 (nobu) meaning "prolong, stretch" or 信 (nobu) meaning "trust" combined with 大 (hiro) meaning "big, great" or 博 (hiro) meaning "command, esteem". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 伸尚, 伸久, 修央, 信久, 進久, 宣久, 展央, 靖久, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 伸 (nobu) meaning "lengthen" combined with 尚 (hisa) meaning "esteem". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 信人, 伸人, 宣仁, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|のぶひと(Japanese Hiragana)|ノブヒト(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Nobu combined with 人 (hito) meaning "person," also used as 仁 meaning "benevolence, compassion, humanity."

column3: のぶほ(Japanese Hiragana)|ノブホ(Japanese Katakana)|伸穂, 信帆, 信歩, 暢保(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 伸 (nobu) meaning "extend, stretch", 暢 (nobu) "stretch, relax" or 信 (nobu) meaning "trust" and 穂 (ho) meaning "grain", 帆 (ho) meaning "sail", 歩 (ho) meaning "walk" or 保 (ho) meaning "protect, maintain". Other kanji combinations can also form this name.

column3: 信一, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|のぶいち(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: From Japanese 信 (nobu) meaning "trust" and 一 (ichi) meaning "one", as well as other kanji combinations that can form this name.

column3: 信幾, 信郁, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 信 (nobu) meaning "trust" and 幾 (iku) meaning "how far/long/many/much". Other kanji characters can also form this name.

column3: 信治, 信次, 暢治, 延次, 展士, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|のぶじ(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: From Japanese 信 (nobu) meaning "trust", 暢 (nobu) meaning "stretch", 延 (nobu) meaning "prolong, stretch" or 展 (nobu) meaning "unfold, expand" combined with 治 (ji) meaning "govern, regulate, administer", 次 (ji) meaning "next" or 士 (ji) meaning "gentleman, scholar, samurai". Other kanji combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 信二郎, 延司郎, 伸次郎...(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 信 (nobu) meaning "trust" combined with 二 (ji) meaning "two" combined with 郎 (rou) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 信雄, 信和, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 信 (nobu) meaning "trust", 延 or 伸 (nobu) meaning "prolong, stretch, extend" combined with 克 (katsu) meaning "overcome", 勝 (katsu) meaning "victory, triumph", 和 (katsu, wa, kazu) meaning "harmony, peace" or 雄 (katsu, o) meaning "hero, manly". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 延和, 伸和, 延一, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 延 (nobu) meaning "prolong, stretch" or 伸 (nobu) meaning "extend, stretch, open" combined with 和 (kazu) meaning "harmony, peace". Other kanji combinations are also possible.

column3: ノブキ(Japanese Katakana)|信樹, 暢希, 信生, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 信 (nobu) meaning "trust, believe, faith" combined with 樹 (ki) meaning "tree". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 信昌, 延雅, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 信 (nobu) meaning "faith, trust, believe" and 昌 (masa) meaning "prosper". Other kanji combinations can spell this name.

column3: のぶみ(Japanese Hiragana)|伸海, 伸実, 伸美, 伸未, 身文, 薫海, 薫実, 薫美, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 伸 (nobu) meaning "extend, stretch", 身 (nobu) meaning "body, identity" or 薫 (nobu) meaning "fragrant" combined with 海 (mi) meaning "sea, ocean", 実 (mi) meaning "fruit, good result, truth", 美 (mi) meaning "beautiful", 未 (mi) referring to the Sheep, the eighth of the twelve Earthly Branches or 文 (mi) meaning "sentence". Other kanji combinations are also possible.
From 信 (nobu, shin) meaning "trust, faith, believe" and 光 (mitsu, hikari) meaning "light". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 宣長, 信長, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 宣 (nobu) meaning "declare, announce, proclaim" combined with 長 (naga) meaning "chief, head, leader". Other kanji combinations are possible.A famous bearer was Nobunaga Oda, a powerful Daimyō of Japan in the late 16th century who attempted to unify Japan during the late Sengoku period.
From 信 (nobu) meaning "trust" and 成 (nari) meaning "become". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 伸人, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|のぶんど(Japanese Hiragana)|ノブンド(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Shift from Nobuhito.This name is extremely rare.

column3: 伸敬, 伸規, 信徳, 信則, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 伸 (nobu) meaning "extend, stretch and 容 (nori) meaning "contain, permit, allow, appearance, shape" or 規 (nori) meaning "standard, regulation, rule". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 信夫, 信男, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 信 (nobu) meaning "trust" or 延 (nobu) meaning "prolong, stretch", combined with 男 (o) meaning "male", 夫 (o) meaning "man, husband", or 雄 (o) meaning "hero, manly". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 信貞, 信定, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|のぶさだ(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: From Japanese 信 (nobu) meaning "trust" and 貞 (sada) meaning "virtue, faithfulness, chastity" or 定 (sada) meaning "determine, establish, decide", as well as other kanji combinations that can form this name.

column3: 信重, 信繁, 信茂, 信成, 陳重, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|のぶしげ(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: From Japanese 信 (nobu) meaning "trust" or 陳 (nobu) meaning "display, exhibit" combined with 重 (shige) meaning "layers, folds", 繁 (shige) meaning "flourishing, luxuriant", 茂 (shige) meaning "lush, luxuriant" or 成 (shige) meaning "become, do". Other kanji combinations can form this name as well.

Nobusuke can derive from nobu 延 'extended, prolong' or 信 'trust, truth' and suke 助, 祐, 輔 all meaning 'help' or 介 'concerned with'. Nobusuke Tagomi is a character of Philip K. Dick novel The Man in the High Castle written in 1962. In its Tv series adaptation (2015- with the same title) Nobusuke Tagomi is player by Cary-Hiroyuki Tagawa.

column3: 信孝, 信隆, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|のぶたか(Japanese Hiragana)|ノブタカ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 信 (nobu) meaning "trust, believe" combined with 孝 (taka) meaning "filial piety, obedience" or 隆 (taka) meaning "noble, prosperous". Other combinations of kanji can form this name as well.

column3: 信輝, 伸晃, 信輝, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 信 (nobu) meaning "trust, faith, believe" and 晴 (teru) meaning "clear or fine weather". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: のぶとも(Japanese Hiragana)|ノブトモ(Japanese Katakana)|靖朝, 延知, 暢友, 陳供, 述侶, 伸朋, 展智, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 宣 (nobu) meaning "say, announce, proclaim" combined with 伴 (tomo) meaning "consort." Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 喜也, 喜弥, 修也, 伸伸, 伸矢, 信哉, 信彌, 宣哉, 暢允, 暢弥, 展也, 農夫也, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 喜 (nobu) meaning "rejoice" combined with 也 (ya) meaning "also". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 信泰, 信康, 延康, 伸泰, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 延/伸 (nobu) meaning "stretch, prolong, extend", or 信 (nobu) meaning "trust, faith, believe" combined with 康 (yasu) meaning "peaceful", 泰 (yasu) meaning "Thailand, peaceful", or 安 (yasu) meaning "relax, rested, cheap, low". Other kanji can be used as well.

column3: 信代, 伸代, 展代, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|のぶよ(Japanese Hiragana)|ノブヨ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 信 (nobu) meaning "trust, believe", 伸 (nobu) meaning "extend, stretch, open" or 展 (nobu) meaning "unfold, expand" combined with 代 (yo) meaning "generation, era". Other combinations of kanji can form this name as well.

column3: 信吉, 信芳, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 信 (nobu, shin) meaning "faith, believe, trust" or 伸 (nobu, noburu) meaning "extend, stretch, open" and 義 (yoshi) meaning "righteous", 芳 (yoshi) meaning "fragrant, virtuous, beautiful", or 吉 (yoshi, kichi) meaning "good luck". Other kanji combinations can also form this name.

Possibly derived from Nahuatl nochehuatl "prickly pear fruit rind/skin", implying persistence or tenacity. Alternately, may be a combination of nochtli "prickly pear fruit" and either huehue "elder, old man" or huehuetl "drum".
From the Garo word নো (no) meaning "younger sister" and চি (chi) meaning "water".
Noctante is a knight outside Malecasta's castle in Book 3, Canto 1 of "The Faerie Queene".

From Latin noctilūca meaning "something that shines by night" - thus also "moon" and "lantern" - from nox "night" and luceo "to shine". It may be an epithet of the Roman goddess Juno. It also occurs in John of Salisbury's 12th-century treatise the Policraticus as an alternative name for the goddess Herodias.
Derived from Latin noctis "of the night". This is the name of a character in Final Fantasy XIII Versus.

Derived from Latin nocturnus meaning "of or belonging to the night, nocturnal", from the Latin noctū "by night". This name appeared in the 1979 camp comedy-horror film Nocturna, also as the DC comics character Nocturna, a daughter of Dracula, created by writer Doug Moench and artist Gene Colan in 1983.
The name of a character in Wynken, Blynken, and Nod.
Form of Nodar with the nominative suffix, used when the name is written stand-alone.
Noddy is a popular children's character made by Enid Blyton.
Diminutive of Nodar. A known bearer of this name is the Georgian singer Nodar "Nodiko" Tatishvili (b. 1986).
Derived from nodir meaning "rare, precious, valuable" and bibi meaning "learned woman".
Combination of the name Nodira and the word xon, meaning "khan".
Tajik and Uzbek form of Nadirbek. A known bearer of this name is the Uzbek chess player Nodirbek Abdusattorov (b. 2004).
Derived from nodir meaning "rare, precious, valuable" and bonu meaning "lady (title)".
Derived from nodir meaning "rare, precious, valuable" and gul meaning "rose, flower".
Derived from nodir meaning "rare, precious, valuable" and toj meaning "crown".

column3: 和, 長閑, 和花, 和華, 和香, 和佳, 温花, 温華, 温香, 温佳, 悠花, 悠華, 悠香, 悠佳, 望花, 望華, 望香, 望佳(Japanese Kanji)|のどか(Japanese Hiragana)|ノドカ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name can be used as 和 (wa, o, ka, yawa.ragu/eru, nago.mu, nago.yaka, a.eru, nodoka) meaning "harmony, peace" or 長閑 (nodoka) meaning "tranquil, quiet, calm, peaceful," made up of 長 (chou, naga.i, osa) meaning "long" and 閑 (kan) meaning "leasure." The word is probably a result of a shift from earlier nodoke (和気).It can also be used to combine 和, 温 (on, atata.ka(i), atata.ma/eru, nuku, nodo) meaning "warm," 悠 (yuu, nodo) meaning "permanence, leisure" or 望 (bou, mou, nozo.mu, mochi, nodo) meaning "ambition, hope, desire" with 花 or 華 (ka, ke, hana), both meaning "flower," 香 (kou, kyou, ka, kao.ri/u) meaning "incense, smell, perfume" or 佳 (ka) meaning "beautiful, good, excellent​."Fictional (female) bearers of this name include Nodoka Saotome (早乙女 のどか) from 'Ranma ½' and Nodoka Manabe (真鍋 和) from 'K-On!'.

column3: 乃衛, 乃衣, 乃依, 暖愛, 伸恵, 希咲, 延笑, 乃会, 乃咲, 望笑, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|のえ(Japanese Hiragana)

Combination of Noel (or its derivations), the infix -el-, stemming from names like Elvia, and the suffix -is (or Elvis).

Dutch (usually informal rather than official) short form of names containing -nous- and -noes-, such as Anouschka (and its many variant spellings, such as Anoeska) and Manouschka (and its many variant spellings, such as Manoeska).
Feminine diminutive of Noé recorded in the 1600s. In some cases, however, it may also have been a feminine form of Noët.
Possibly derived as a diminutive of Noah 1 or Noe.

The conventional German form of Nefertiti.
Means "God’s view" or "beautiful view" from Hebrew name Noya ("God’s beauty") and the name Nof.
Probably derived from Mongolian нохой (nokhoi) meaning "dog".
Combination of the names Noga and Li 2 means "my brightness" in Hebrew.

I should also add that for this bearer, Noks is a (technically informal) short form of one of the official given names on her birth certificate (which in her case is Arnolda), since the name is not listed in the Corpus of First Names in The Netherlands, which is an on-line database that features all given names that have been recorded on Dutch birth certificates since 1880.With that said, you might also want to compare this name with the names Nolke and Cox (which is also found written as Coks and Koks).

Derived from номин (nomin) meaning "lapis lazuli, azure" and зол (zol) meaning "fortune, luck, blessing".

Most likely derived from Ancient Greek νόμος (nomos) meaning "usage, custom, law, ordinance". However, a derivation from νομός (nomos) meaning "place of pasturage" as well as "dwelling place" is also quite possible. The latter possibility is closely related to νομεύω (nomeuo) meaning "to put to graze, to drive afield" and νομεύς (nomeus) meaning "herdsman, shepherd". Also compare the English word nomad. In Greek mythology, Nomion was the name of several characters, one of them being a horned centaur.

Epithet of the Zulu goddess Mbaba Mwana Waresa, a shapeshifting fertility goddess who rules over rainbows, agriculture, harvests, rain, and beer and has power over water and earth. The name means "she who chooses the state of an animal" referring to the goddesses ability to shapeshift into an animal.
Frisian diminutive of names containing the name element nand "to dare".
From Japanese 野 (no) meaning "area, field" combined with 萌 (mo) meaning "sprout, bud". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 野茂子, 野萌子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 野 (no) meaning "area, field", 茂 (mo) meaning "overgrown; luxuriant, thickly growing, lush" or 萌 (mo) meaning "bud, sprout" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.

The name Nomsa is a traditional Zulu name from South Africa, meaning "grace," "mercy," or "kindness," and is also used in isiNdebele culture with meanings of "compassion" or "hallowed". It is predominantly a female name, reflecting positive attributes and deeply rooted in South African culture.Origin and MeaningZulu Origin: The name Nomsa comes from the Zulu language and is most popular in South Africa. English Meanings: It translates to "grace," "mercy," or "kindness," reflecting positive qualities. isiNdebele Context: In the isiNdebele language, it can mean "compassion" or "hallowed". Cultural Significance Positive Attributes:Like many African names, Nomsa often reflects positive traits or hopes for the child.Traditional Name:It stands on its own within its cultural context, rather than being derived from other names.Notable Individuals Nomsa Buthelezi: A well-known South African actress and television personality.Nomsa Manaka: A celebrated South African dancer and choreographer.

From the Xhosa ukuvuya meaning "be glad".
Means "of good name" or "famous" in Pashto.

Noreia used to be considered the epithet of an unidentified pre-Roman mother goddess who left her name in inscriptions throughout the Roman province Noricum (present-day Austria and Slovenia). Current theories suggest, however, that she might have been a Roman "creation" to gain the loyalty of the Norici (ever since Vespasian's time, she was associated with the goddess Isis and referred to as Isisi-Noreia). It has been claimed that she was a goddess of fate and fortune, life's happiness, fertility, mining and healing waters. The origin and meaning of her name are lost to time.

The etymological meaning of the name of all the villages is basically "town of the Normans", so when it comes to purely the meaning itself, it doesn't matter all that much which of the villages is the one that truly lies at the root of the surname. column3: 女魃, 女妭(Chinese, Japanese Kanji)
column12: From a combination of the characters 女 (nü, meaning “female, woman”) and 魃 (ba, meaning “drought spirit”). This is the name of a mythological figure mentioned in the Shanhaijing (山海经), or Classic of Mountains and Seas. She was the daughter of the Yellow Emperor who helped her father defeat Chiyou at the Battle of Zhuolu by stopping the storms caused by Chiyou’s retainers, Fengbo and Yushi. After the battle, she remained on earth, bringing drought wherever she went.She is first described as a woman in green, though later sources say she is topless, has a single eye at the top of her head and walks as fast as the wind.

Nuit is the Ancient Egyptian goddess of the heavens, with her name meaning "sky." Originally she was only the goddess of the night sky, but gradually she came to represent the sky in general. Nuit also protects people in the afterlife. Her many titles include "Coverer of the Sky," "Mistress of All," "She Who Protects," and "She Who Holds a Thousand Souls." Nuit is the daughter of Shu, the god of air, and Tefnut, the goddess of moisture. Her brother, who also became her husband, was named Geb. Geb and Nuit are a bit of an anomaly of mythology. Usually it's the male deity representing the sky while the female represents the earth. This is one of the few times in which it is the other way around. Most of the time, Nuit is depicted as a star-covered nude woman arching over Geb, the earth. It is believed that her hands and feet touch the four cardinal directions. She is also sometimes shown as a giant cow. She had at least four children: Isis, Osiris, Set, and Nephtys. In some variations of the mythology she is also the mother of Horus, but in most cases Horus is her grandson. The inside of tombs were often painted a deep blue with lots of stars to represent her, and her image was painted inside the sarcophagus. The story as to how she gave birth to her children is an interesting one. Ra, the sun god, was paranoid over others stealing his throne. So when it became known that Nuit was pregnant, he became furious and decreed that Nuit was not allowed to give birth on any day of the year. At this time there were only 360 days in a year. Nuit hatched a plan with Thoth, the god of wisdom. Thoth played gambling games with Khonshu, the god of the moon, and every time Khonshu lost he gave Thoth some moonlight. Eventually Thoth had enough moonlight to make five extra days. Since these were technically not a part of the year, Nuit could have her children. When Ra found out, he separated Nuit from Geb for all eternity, but she never regretted her actions. The reason Aleister Crowley gave this name to his child is because Nuit is an important goddess to the religion he founded, Thelema. Basically she represents the All, or the universe. It's interesting to note that Nuit is also French for "night."

Nundina presides over the dies lustricus, the purification day when the child was given a name (praenomen). This occurred on the eighth day for girls and the ninth day for boys, a difference Plutarch explains by noting that 'it is a fact that the female grows up, and attains maturity and perfection before the male.' Until the umbilical cord fell off, typically on the seventh day, the baby was regarded as 'more like a plant than an animal,' as Plutarch expresses it. The ceremony of the dies lustricus was thus postponed until the last tangible connection to the mother's body was dissolved, and the child was seen 'as no longer forming part of the mother, and in this way as possessing an independent existence which justified its receiving a name of its own and therefore a fate of its own.' The day was celebrated with a family feast.

West Frisian cognate of Nick (also compare Nyckele) as well as a Dutch and English variant spelling of the name. West Frisian form of Nicolaas, which originated in late medieval times (as is evident by the archaic -ck- spelling), but is still in use to this day - albeit rarely. The modern spelling of the name is Nykele.

Shorter form or variant of Nyckele, which originated in late medieval times (as is evident by the archaic -ck- spelling), but is still in use to this day - albeit rarely. The modern spelling of the name is Nykle. A known bearer of this given name was the Frisian author Nyckle Haisma (1907-1943).

Latinized form of Greek Νυκτηίς (Nykteis), a derivative of Greek νύξ (nyx) meaning "night" (compare the related names Nycteus and Nyx). In Greek mythology, this name was borne by the wife of King Polydorus of Thebes.
Latinized form of Greek Νυκτεύς (Nykteus), which was derived from Ancient Greek νύξ (nyx) meaning "night". In Greek mythology, Nycteus was the name of a king of Thebes.

Derived from Ancient Greek νύξ (nyx) meaning "night" and μένω (meno) "to last, stay, wait, withstand". In Greek mythology, this was the name of a princess of Lesbos who fled her father, Epopeus, after he raped her, hiding in the forest. Latinized form of Nyktimos. In Greek mythology, this is the name of the youngest of the fifty sons of king Lycaon of Arcadia.

This is the name of the goddess of the sea in Javanese and Sundanese mythology, more specifically the guardian of the Indian Ocean. The second element of her name, rara, was later changed to lara meaning "sick, suffering".

Means "of the night, nightly", derived from Ancient Greek νύξ (nyx) meaning "night". In Greek mythology, Nyktimos was the youngest son of King Lycaon. He was either killed by his father and then resurrected by Zeus, or saved from the lightning bolt that killed his father and brothers by Gaia, in either case inheriting the kingdom of Arcadia.

This name was used by American author Sherrilyn Kenyon. It is a hybryd character in her League Series who happens to be the only assassin to leave the League without being hunted down and killed. He is invincible, tough, strong, smart, a survivor, and falls in love at first sight. He becomes an emperor and is successful in whatever he does. This name means "victorious, knowledgeable king".
Variant of Nikita 1, which was possibly influenced by Mykyta.A notable bearer of this name was the Ukrainian Catholic saint Nykyta Budka (1877-1949).
Possibly a masculine form of Nyla, also used sometimes as feminine.
Meaning unknown, perhaps an invented name based on similar-sounding names such as Nyah, Aaliyah and Nyla.

Recorded in 1350 in Silesia and in the Rhineland region of what is today Germany, this name is basically a Latinization of the German word niemand "nobody".During the Middle Ages it was common practice to give orphans, especially orphaned infants, the name Nemo as either their given name or a byname, signifying that they "belonged to nobody". Nymandus could thus be considered a cognate of Nemo.

Of Australian Aboriginal origin (Ngarrindjeri, to be precise), the meaning of this name is not yet known to me at the moment. This was the name of the mother of David Unaipon (1872-1967), an Australian Aboriginal preacher, inventor and writer.

Perhaps a one-off variant of Numeria. This name was used several times in the book series A Song of Ice and Fire (published beginning 1996) by George R. R. Martin and the television adaptation Game of Thrones (2011-2019): Queen Nymeria of the Rhoynar was a great warrior; later Arya Stark names her direwolf Nymeria after Queen Nymeria; lastly, Nymeria Sand is a 'sand snake', one of the bastard daughters of Oberyn Martell, who is extremely skilled with blades.
Combination of the phonetic elements ny and meer.
Variant of Nymphodora used by J. K. Rowling in her 'Harry Potter' series of books, where it belongs to a minor character, a Metamorphmagus who despises her name.
Derived from Greek νύμφη (nymphe) "bride, nymph" and ἔρως (eros) "love".
Transferred use of the surname Nymphias.
From the Greek name Νυμφικός (Nymphikos), apparently a genitive form of Nymphe (see Nympha).

Feminine form of Nymphidios (see Nymphidius). A bearer of this name was the mother of Gaius Nymphidius Sabinus, a Prefect of the Roman Praetorian Guard from the 1st century AD. In literature, the poet Michael Drayton used the name for a fairy in his epic 'Nimphidia' (1627).

Originally a Late Roman cognomen, which was derived from the latinized Greek name Nymphidius. In turn, the Greeks translated this cognomen back into Greek as Nymphidianos (Νυμφιδιανός). A bearer of this name was Nymphidianus of Smyrna, a Graeco-Roman philosopher from the 4th century AD who was also the brother of fellow philosopher Maximus of Ephesus.

Latinized form of the Greek name Νυμφιδιος (Nymphidios), the genitive form of Nymphe (see Nympha). It was borne by Gaius Nymphidius Sabinus, a 1st-century Roman officer who was murdered after declaring himself emperor.
A masculine form of Nympha. Nymphis (fl. about 250 BC), the son of Xenagoras of Heraclea, wrote a work on Alexander the Great and his successors in 24 books.
Latinized form of the Greek name Νύμφιος (Nymphios), a masculine derivative of Nymphe (see Nympha). Nymphios (literally "bridegroom" in Greek) is also a title applied to Jesus by Orthodox Christians.
Latinized form of the Greek name Νυμφόδωρος (Nymphodoros), derived from νυμφη (nymphe) "bride, young wife" and δωρον (doron) "gift".
Derived from Ancient Greek νύμφη (nymphe) meaning "bride, nymph, young wife" and δοτός (dotos) meaning "given, granted".
Latinized form of the Greek name Νυμφοδοτος (Nymphodotos), derived from νύμφη (nymphe) "bride, nymph, young wife" and δοτός (dotos) "given, granted".
Variant of Nyneve used by Robert Jordan for a character in his 'Wheel of Time' series of fantasy novels.

From Egyptian nj-nṯr, possibly meaning "he is like (a) god" or "godlike", derived from Egyptian nj "of, belonging to, possessing" combined with nṯr "god". This was the Horus name of the third pharaoh of the Second Dynasty of Egypt during the Early Dynastic Period.

Form of Ninniane used by Thomas Malory for one of the Ladies of the Lake in his 15th-century compilation of Arthurian legends 'Le Morte d'Arthur' (as she is called Ninniane in Malory's source, the continuation to the Vulgate 'Merlin', known as the 'Suite du Merlin'). In Malory, Nyneve imprisons Merlin, twice rescues Arthur from the sorceress Morgan le Fay, and marries Sir Pelleas after punishing Ettarde for her mistreatment of him.

Of uncertain origin and meaning.Some derive this name from the Danish verb nynne "to hum; to croon", although it is certainly possible that Nynne might simply be a variant of Ninne.Nynne also coincides with an old term for "baby talk; childhood language".

The name of a character from two 15-part movie serials in the early 1940s: Jungle Girl (1941) and Perils of Nyoka (1942). The serials were based on the novel Jungle Girl (1932) by Edgar Rice Burroughs, in which the titular character was named Fou-tan. The meaning of the name is not uncertain, but it has been suggested that it was inspired by the word nyoka which means "snake" in multiple African languages including Swahili, Shona, Kikuyu and Tsonga.

In Greek mythology, Nysa was one of the Nysaids, a group of Oceanid nymphs tasked with raising the infant god Dionysos. In a different account, she was instead a daughter of the rural deity Aristaeus, and raised Dionysos on her own.

Probably means "of Nysa", the name of several ancient settlements in Greece and Turkey, as well as of a mountainous region in Greek mythology where the god Dionysus was raised. Nysaeus was a tyrant of Syracuse in the 4th century BCE.

Derived from obsidian, the English name for a specific type of volcanic glass. The name is ultimately derived from Latin obsidianus meaning "of Obsidius", after the Roman (also called Obsius in some instances) who supposedly was the first to discover this type of volcanic glass. The name Obsidius is possibly a corruption of Opsidius, which is apparently a very obscure Roman nomen gentile.** Etymologically, Opsidius may be a more elaborate form of Opsius. It could also be Oscan in origin, in which case it may have been derived from Oscan úpsed meaning "worked, laboured" (which would thus make the name related to Oppius). Last but not least, if the discoverer's name was Obsius rather than Obsidius, then his name was probably a corruption of Opsius. In either case the etymology is very similar. Finally, in popular culture, Obsidian is the name of a character in the "Transformers" franchise as well as a character in a comic published by DC Comics.** Please see page 638 of the book "The Italic Dialects" written by Robert Seymour Conway.

Od Ana is a sublime Turkic divine name, a majestic fusion of Od/Ot ("Fire") and Ana ("Mother"). She is the "Primordial Mother of the Flame," the cosmic hearth that anchors the soul of the home. In the ancient Altai cosmogony, she is not merely an elemental force but a radiant matron of the universe, emerging from the celestial sparks kindled by the creator god Ülgen to pierce the nine heavens.As a core pillar of Siberian and Central Asian animism, her lore defines her as the ultimate guardian of the lineage and the supreme cleanser of spiritual impurities. Cloaked in shimmering red silk, she represents warmth in the winter of history, the protective embrace that shields existence from the void. Her presence is the sacred bridge between the celestial fire and the domestic altar; she is tenderness absolute, yet wields the righteous fury of the wildfire to protect the sanctity of the family. To speak her name is to summon the eternal flame of the bloodline itself.Centuries of ancestral traditions are living testaments to her enduring legacy: the absolute reverence demanded before approaching a flame, where one must never defile the fire but instead approach it with a whispered plea for safe passage and protection, the bride’s ritual walk around the central hearth to seek the matriarchal blessing of the home, and the deep-seated dread of a "hearth being extinguished" (ocağı sönmek), which signifies the literal erasure of a lineage. She remains the immortal Mother of all Life-Giving Heat, whose cosmic radiance never wanes.

Oduduwa, Olofin Adimula, Emperor and First Suzerain of the Yoruba, was the Oba of Ile-Ife. His name is generally ascribed to the ancestral dynasty of Yorubaland due to the fact that he is held by the Yoruba to have been the ancestor of their numerous crowned kings. Following his post-humous deification, he was admitted to the Yoruba pantheon as an aspect of a primordial divinity of the same name.
