利世子, 里代子, 理代子, 利容子, 里栄子, 莉陽子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 里 (ri) meaning "village", 栄 (yo) meaning "honor, flourish, glory, prosper, splendor", and 子 (ko) meaning "child, sign of the rat, first sign of the Chinese zodiac". Other kanji combinations can be used.
From Japanese 梨 (ri) meaning "pear", 世 (yo) meaning "world" combined with 菜 (na) meaning "vegetables, greens". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: りゆ(Japanese Hiragana)|リユ(Japanese Katakana)|俐宥, 梨由, 理優, 凜憂 李夕, 莉結, 里悠, 璃友, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 莉 (ri) meaning "white jasmine" combined with 優 (yu) meaning "gentleness, superiority" or 結 (yu) meaning "tie, bind" or 夕 (yu) meaning "evening". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Ri can mean "jasmine" or "hamlet, village", yu can mean "truth, reason, cause", or "excellent", and ko means "child, sign of the rat".

column3: 隆太郎, 竜太郎, 龍太朗, 龍太郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column12: Short form of Rizwan or Rizwana.
Possibly a short form of Clarissa or derived from the surname Rizal.
Derived from Arabic رجال (rijāl) meaning "infantrymen, footsoldiers" or "men", the plural of راجل (rājil) meaning "footsoldier" or رجل (rajul) meaning "man".

Variant of Rizal Day, the Philippine national holiday (held on December 30th) commemorating the life and works of national hero José Rizal.This name is mainly given to children born on or around that holiday or Rizal's birth (June 19th).
Diminutive of the surname Rizal, given in honour of the Filipino nationalist José Rizal (1861-1896).
Combination of Riza or Rizal and the popular suffix -lyn.

column3: 麗世, 里瀬, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 麗 (ri) meaning "lovely, beautiful" combined with 世 (ze) meaning "world". Other kanji combinations are possible.
My husband has a forefather whose first name was Rizen. As I didn't see this in your list of virtue names, I'm adding it.

column5: RI-zee-ə(Biblical English, Biblical Hebrew)|REE-zee-ə(Biblical English, Biblical Hebrew)

column12: Meaning uncertain. It could derive from the Italian word riccio meaning "curly-haired" with the suffix -iero. Another etymology is from the French verb risier meaning "to laugh; to mock". It could also derive from the Germanic element ris meaning "voyage" or ric meaning "power" and hari meaning "army".
From Swahili riziki meaning "daily bread, subsistance" and by extension "divine blessing".
Alternate transcription of Arabic رزق (see Rizq).

column3: Ризо(Tajik, Uzbek Cyrillic)|理三, 里三, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: Tajik and Uzbek form of Ridha.
Derived from riso meaning "satisfaction" or "purification of the heart" and gul meaning "rose, flower".
Means "sustenance, boon, blessing" in Arabic. It is sometimes used as a feminine name in Indonesia and Malaysia.
Means "sustenance of Allah" from Arabic رزْق (rizq) meaning "sustenance, boon, blessing" combined with الله (Allah).
Means "they bestow" or "they are bestowed, blessed" in Arabic.
Derived from Arabic رزق (rizq) meaning "livelihood" combined with Ningsih.
Alternate transcription of Arabic رزق الله (see Rizq Allah), as well as the Indonesian form.

column3: りづ(Japanese Hiragana)|リズ(Japanese Katakana)|理珠, 莉鶴, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 理 (ri) meaning "logic, reason" and 鶴 (zu) meaning "crane (bird)". Other kanji combinations can be used as well.This name is a borrowing of the English name Liz.

column3: りずむ(Japanese Hiragana)|リズム(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name has, technically, no meaning since it is written in hiragana or katakana. However, Rizumu, as a word, is a loan word of English origin meaning "rhythm."
Chechen and Dagestani form of Ridwan.
From the given name Rizwan combined with Uyghur گۈل (gül) meaning "flower".
Transferred use of the surname Rizzo.
From Old Norse rjūpa meaning "snow grouse".
Old East Slavic form of Ryurik.
Alternate transcription of Arabic رقية (see Ruqayyah) chiefly used in Northern Africa.
Directly taken from Faroese ró "calm, tranquility; peace; quiet; rest".
From Sino-Vietnamese 鱸 (rô) meaning "sea bass, sea perch".
From a non-Sino-Vietnamese reading of Chinese 里 (rợ) meaning "wild".

column3: ろあ(Japanese Hiragana)|ロア(Japanese Katakana)|로아(Korean Hangul)|羅阿(Japanese Kanji, Korean Hanja, Chinese)|로아(Korean Hangul)

column12: From the Middle English word roam(er), to refer to someone who likes to move around and travel, especially without a clear idea of what they want to do or go.
It derives from the surname Ó Ruairc in Irish. Other variants of the surname include Rourke and O'Rourke, both common in Ireland. Possibly an Irish translation of the Germanic name Roderick
Hypochoristic form of names with the Germanic stem hruod "fame".

In Wirnt von Grafenberg's 'Wigalois', The pagan king of Glois, evil and villainous, who sold his soul to the Devil and was thus able to use sorcery to take over many lands, including the neighboring kingdom of Korntin. He killed King Lar of Korntin and drove Queen Amene to the border. After holding Korntin for ten years, he was killed in single combat by Wigalois, who had arrived as Amene’s champion. Roaz’s wife, Japhite, died from sorrow.
Alternate form of Roberta. Noted bearer is female country music pioneer Roba Stanley (1908-1986).
Alternate transcription of Persian ربابه (see Robabeh).
Possibly an invented name based on the phonetic spelling of the French pronunciation of Robert.
Italian form of Rotbald.Known bearers of this name include the Italian archbishop Robaldo di Milano (died in 1145) and the Italian architect Robaldo Morozzo della Rocca (1904-1993).
Variant of Rob, used in George R. R. Martin's 'A Song of Ice and Fire' and the corresponding TV series 'Game of Thrones'.
Probably a variant of Robin.It is the given name of the guitarist Robben Ford.
Variant of Robert probably via the surname Robbertt.
From Roberto combined with the suffix -cio, from names that end in that pattern, e.g. Maurício.
Variant of Rogério, influenced by Roberto.
Jèrriais. Languedocian, Provençal, Gascon, Gallo and Franco-Provençal form of Robert.
Variant of Roberta. A notable bearer was Robertha Watt (1899-1993), a second-class survivor of the Titanic disaster.

Medieval French diminutive of Robert. This given name is no longer in use in France (apart from the handful of bearers that were born in the 1960s), but it still survives there as a patronymic surname (albeit barely, as the surname is extremely rare there nowadays).
Medieval French diminutive of Roberte and feminine form of Robertin. This name was borne by Robertine Barry (1863-1910), a French Canadian journalist and publisher.
Transferred use of the surname Roberts.
Transferred use of the surname, Robertson.
Medieval Italian diminutive of Roberta, as -uccia is an Italian feminine diminutive suffix.
Medieval Italian diminutive of Roberto, as -uccio is an Italian masculine diminutive suffix.
From Roberto combined with the suffix -val, from names that either begin or end with this pattern like Valdecir and Durval.
Transferred use of the surname Robeson.
Transferred use of the surname Robespierre as a given name, used in reference to Maximilien Robespierre (1758-1794), who was one of the best-known leaders of the French Revolution.

Created by author George R. R. Martin for a character in his series 'A Song of Ice and Fire'. It is possibly derived from Robert. In the series, Robett Glover is the brother of Galbart and the heir to Deepwood Motte.
Swiss German diminutive of Robert and Robin.
Feminine form of Robert.A known bearer is actress Robia LaMorte, who was named after her father, Robert LaMorte.
Transferred use of the surname Robichaux, which in itself is an altered spelling of Robichon or Roubichou, pet forms of Robert.
Variant of Robine, with its spelling phonetical in nature.

Feminine form of Robigus. In Roman mythology Robigo and her male counterpart Robigus were minor deities summoned for protection of the crops against blight, i.e. agricultural diseases such as mold, mildew and rust. The festival Robigalia was held on April 25.

Derived from Latin robigo meaning "red blight, wheat rust", referring to a red fungus that could infest crops. This was the name of a minor god in Roman mythology, summoned for protection against agricultural diseases such as mold, mildew and rust. The festival Robigalia, where non-edible animals were sacrificed, was held on April 25. He also had a female counterpart named Robigo.
Dutch pet form of Robert, and a variant spelling of Robin.

column3: 로빈(Korean Hangul)|路彬, 老彬, etc.(Korean Hanja)

column12: Variant of Robina primarily used in Uganda. The current prime minister of Uganda (as of 2021) is named Robinah Nabbanja.

French feminine form of Robin, which originated in medieval times. For reasons unknown, it fell out of use after the Middle Ages, after which it continued to survive as a matronymic surname (mostly in the Normandy region of France). Robine began to be used as a given name again in the late 1980s, but it never regained the popularity that it once had and as such is now a very rare given name in France. Meanwhile, the name came into use in the Netherlands in the early 20th century, where the name is nowadays a bit more prevalent than in France.Also, you might want to compare the given name Robertine, which might perhaps make you want to entertain the possibility that Robine is (at least in some cases) a contracted form of this name.Lastly, a known bearer of this given name is the Dutch actress and model Robine van der Meer (b. 1971).

Strictly masculine diminutive of Robin (as -et is a French masculine diminutive suffix), which itself is a diminutive of Robert. This given name is no longer in use in France: it fell out of use after the Middle Ages, which was probably due to the growing association of the name with a faucet. In this day and age, robinet is now synonymous with a faucet and has thus become an everyday word in France. However, the given name still survives as a patronymic surname in the country, and it is a fairly common one there at that.A known bearer of this given name was the medieval French illuminator and painter Robinet Testard (active in his work from 1470 to 1531 or 1533; his birthdate and date of death are unknown).

Medieval French diminutive of Robine (as -ette is a French feminine diminutive suffix). In other words: you could say that this name is the feminine form of Robinet. This given name is extremely rare in France nowadays, as there are only a handful of bearers in the country today. It doesn't fare much better as a matronymic surname either, what with only 8 bearers of the Robinette surname having been born in France between 1966 and 1990.As a given name, Robinette is nowadays more used in English-speaking countries (primarily the United States), where its use is often inspired by the surname Robinette (as surnames are often used as given names in the English-speaking world), which is more prevalent there than in France.
Diminutive form of Roberto, Robson, etc.

Combination of Robin and Hood. Robin Hood was a legendary hero and archer of medieval England who stole from the rich to give to the poor.A notable bearer of this name is Robinhood Ferdinand "Robin" Cariño Padilla, a Filipino movie actor and director.
A feminine form of Robin or inspired by the botanical name Robinia "black locust, false acacia".
Spanish (Latin American) form of Robinson.Famous bearer of this name is Colombian football player Róbinson Zapata.

Form of Robinson in various languages. In some of them (such as Armenian and Georgian), the use of the name was inspired by the fictional character Robinson Crusoe from the eponymous book written by Daniel Defoe (c. 1660-1731).
Transferred use of the surname Robison.
Form of Robby or diminutive of Robert.
Variant of Rooble, used outside of Somalia.

Contraction of Russian родился быть ленинцем (rodilsya byt' lenintsem) and of родившйся быть ленинцем (rodivshiysya byt' lenintsem), which both mean "born to be a Leninist". This name was created by Communist parents who were eager to reject traditional names.
Meaning unknown, possibly an Americanized version of the Spanish "roble," meaning "oak."
Form of Rehoboam used in the Greek and Latin Old Testament.
Combination of robot and cop. This is the name of the main character and cyborg policeman in the science fiction film saga RoboCop.

The first element of this name is derived from Polish robota "work, labour, servitude", which is derived from Polish robić "to work, to labour". It is ultimately derived from Slavic orbota "hard work, slavery", which came from Proto-Slavic orbь "slave". The second element is derived from Slavic mil "gracious, dear". As such, this name roughly means "dear work".

The first element of this name is derived from Polish robota "work, labour, servitude", which is derived from Polish robić "to work, to labour". It is ultimately derived from Slavic orbota "hard work, slavery", which came from Proto-Slavic orbь "slave". The second element is derived from Slavic slav "glory". As such, this name roughly means "to work for glory" or "work is glory" or "glory is work".

From the patronymic of the Roman cognomen Rōbustus, meaning “oak, oaken, (figuratively) robust, strong, vigorous, resistant, son of Robust, a descendant of Robust.” St. Robustian was an early martyr who was put to death probably in Milan. The feast day is celebrated in Italy on May 24 in memory of St. Robustian.
Galician and Spanish form of Robustianus.
derive from the patronymic of the Roman cognomen robustus meaning "oak, oaken, (figuratively) robust, strong, vigorous, resistant, son of Robustus, a descendant of Robustus".
Dutch diminutive of Robert (for men) and Roberta and Robine (for women).
Galician feminine form of Rocco (compare Catalan Roc). This name coincides with Galician roca "rock".
Probably a blend of two names like Roco and Rafael.
Means "fortress, cliff" in Italian. It can also be used as a feminine form of Rocco.
English feminine form of Rocco, probably inspired by Rocchina
Variant of Rosaline/Roslyn influenced by the spelling of Jocelyn (See also Rosslyn/Joslyn).
"Shining "; "radiant" ;"one who lightens or makes bright "Origin - Sanskrit
Derived from Sanskrit रोच (rocá) meaning "shining, radiant".
From Sanskrit रोचनी (roćani) meaning “yellow, red arsenic”.
From Arabic رَشَدَ (rašada) meaning "to go the right way, to be well guided", etymologically related to Rashad and Rashid.
Fom the surname Rochester, which is derived from the places called Rochester.
This name is a nickname for the Hebrew name, Rochel.
Means "nag; old horse" in Spanish. This is the name of Don Quixote's horse.

English form of Rocco, traditionally used to refer to the 14th-century saint. Modern use of the name is probably influenced by the English surname Rock and may also be inspired by the English word rock. This was borne by the American actor Rock Hudson (1925-1985), whose stage name was allegedly taken from the Rock of Gibraltar, a promontory on the south of the Iberian Peninsula.
Transferred use of the surname Rockefeller. Used in honor of the Rockefeller business family.
Transferred use of the surname Rocker.

From the English word rocket. The word comes from Italian rocchetta, from Old Italian rochetto (“rocket”, literally “a bobbin”), diminutive of rocca (“a distaff”), from Lombardic rocko, rukka (“spinning wheel”), from Proto-Germanic *rukkô (“a distaff, a staff with flax fibres tied loosely to it, used in spinning thread”).
Transferred use of the surname Rockford.
The name of character Rockingham Napier in, “Excellent Women,” by Barbara Pym.
Transferred use of the surname Rockley.
Variant of Rocky, using the popular suffix lyn.
Transferred use of the surname Rockmond. A known bearer of this name is the American actor Rockmond Dunbar (b. 1973).
Transferred use of the surname Rockwell. A notable bearer of this name was American painter Rockwell Kent (1882-1971).
Hispanic variant of Roxy or Roxie. A known bearer is Raquel Roxanne 'Rocsi' Diaz (1983-), a Honduran-born American television host and radio personality.
Variant form of Rochus. A known Dutch bearer of this name was the composer and conductor Rocus van Yperen (1914-1994).
The given name of the Lebanese football player Roda Antar.

It is the name of a character from the Shahnama (شاهنامه). In the Shahnama, Rodaba is the daughter of Mehrab Kaboli (مهراب کابلی) and Sindokht (سیندخت). She marries Zal (زال), and together they have a son named Rostam (رستم).This is how the name is pronounced in the Kabuli form of Persian/Farsi (the main standard dialect of Persian/Farsi in Afghanistan), whereas this would be pronounced as Rudabeh in the Tehrani form of Persian/Farsi (the main standard dialect of Persian/Farsi in Iran).
Derived from Old Irish rod "strong, spirited, furious", itself related to rúad "red".

Georgian form of Rudabeh. This name was originally feminine in Georgia, but over time it has become a unisex name.Notable bearers of this name include the first wife of king Vakhtang V of Kartli (1618-1675) and the Bagratid princess Rodam of Kartli (died after 1716).
Transferred use of the surname Rodan.
Means "rolling" in Spanish. A bearer of this name is Rodante Marcoleta, a Filipino politician.
Derived from the Germanic elements hrôthi "fame" combined with hiltja "battle, fight".
Derived from the Germanic element hrôthi "fame" combined with Old High German lind or lindi "soft, tender."

Hungarian, Italian, Portuguese, Romanian and English form of Rodelind. Rodelinda (6th century) was a Lombard queen by marriage to king Audoin, and the mother of king Alboin. This name was also borne by Rodelinda (7th century), the wife of King Perctarit of Lombardy and title character of Händel's opera Rodelinda (1725).
German form of Rodelind. Rodelinde (6th-century), was a Lombard queen by marriage to king Audoin, and mother of king Alboin.
A more Latinate form of Rodelind. Rodelindis was the wife of Alduin, a 6th-century king of the Lombards.
A diminutive of names with the Germanic name element hroð "fame" such as Rodrigo.
Combination of Rodel and the popular suffix -lyn.
Italian, Spanish and Portuguese form of Roderic.
Variant of Rodrigo used in Shakespeare's tragedy Othello (1603).
Transferred use of the surname Rodgers.
Transferred use of the surname Rodham.
Variant transcription of Jediael, as used in 1 Chronicles 12:20.This transcription is used in English translations of the Septuagint Bible.

Originally a pet form of given names containing the Germanic element hrod "fame". Usage of this name nowadays is probably mainly inspired by the famous French sculptor Auguste Rodin (1840-1917), whose surname has the same etymological origin.
Bulgarian, Croatian and Serbian cognate of Rodosław.

A possible variation on Rod, Rodney, and other names starting with ROD-. Two well known bearers are Rodman Philbrick (1951-), who wrote the young adult novel "Freak the Mighty", and Rodman Edward "Rod" Serling (1924-1975), a television writer known for the classic "Twilight Zone" series.
Derived from the Germanic element hrôthi "fame" combined with Old High German mâri "famous."
Feminization of the name Rodney using the popular element sha.
Variant of Rodwald. Rodoald was the name of a 7th-century king of the Lombards.
Italian and Spanish form of Rodoald, which is a variant form of Rodwald.
Medieval Italian diminutive of Rodolfo, as -uccio is an Italian masculine diminutive suffix.
Latinized form of Rudolf. This was used for a character (the husband of Bellatrix Lestrange) in the 'Harry Potter' series.
Derived from Slavic rod "family, race, kind" combined with Slavic mil "gracious, dear".

The first element of this name is derived from Russian rod "family, kind, race, genus", which is ultimately derived from Proto-Slavic rodъ "family". The second element is derived from Slavic mir "peace".
Russian form of Rhodopianus via its hellenized form Rhodopianos.
Georgian form of Rhodopianus via its hellenized form Rhodopianos.
Spanish and Portuguese form of Rhodopianus.

The first element of this name is derived from Polish rodu "family", which is ultimately derived from Proto-Slavic rodъ "family". Also compare Polish rodzic "parent", Polish rodzina "family" and Polish rodny "fertile". The second element is derived from Slavic slav "glory". The name's meaning is thus roughly "family is glory". Also take a look at Rodzisław, which has virtually the same meaning.
Derived from Greek ῥόδον (rhodon) meaning "rose" combined with Greek σθενος (sthenos) meaning "vigour, strength".
Gascon form of Roderick as well as an English and Welsh variant of this name.
From a surname that was a variant of Roderick.
Transferred use of the surname Rodríguez.
Swedish form of Roderick. A notable bearer is Ser Rodrik Cassel from HBO's ever-popular TV show 'Game of Thrones'.
Variant of Rodrigo. A famous bearer is soccer player Rodygo Goes (1999-).
Medieval German form of Hrodulf, cognate to modern High German Rudolf.
Derived from the Germanic element hrôthi "fame" combined with Gothic valdan "to reign."
English variant of Roddy as well as a Dutch cognate of the name. However, in Dutch it is usually a diminutive of Roderick and Roderik - not typically of Rodney.

The first element of this name is derived from Polish rodzina "family", which is ultimately derived from Proto-Slavic rodъ "family". Also compare Polish rodzic "parent", Polish rodu "family" and Polish rodny "fertile". The second element is derived from Slavic slav "glory". The name's meaning is thus roughly "family is glory". Also take a look at Rodosław, which has virtually the same meaning.
Transferred use of the surname Roe.
As a Dutch name, Roebi is a variant of Ruby. As a Swiss name, however, it is exclusively masculine. In this case it is generally a short form of Robert.
Roee (רעי or רועי) means "my shepherd" in Hebrew. It is derived from the old testament where it appears 25 times. the most famous quote is " יְהוָה רֹעִי, לֹא אֶחְסָר" (Psalms 23:1).
Contracted form of Rudolf and/or Roelof. A well-known bearer of this name is the late Dutch actor Roef Ragas (1965-2007).
Bassa African pronunciation of the hebrew word "Rapha," meaning "heals." Native to Ghana and Monrovia Liberia.

Meaning uncertain. It could be a contraction of a diminutive like Roelke or even be a variant of Rochus. However, it is also possible that the name is derived from Dutch roek meaning "rook" (as in, the bird).
Variant of Ruqayya, mainly used in Dutch-influenced regions of the continent.
Contracted form of Rudolf and/or Roelof.
Variant of Roelfine, with its spelling phonetical in nature.
Feminine form of Roelf. Also compare Roelofke (see Roelofje).
Diminutive of given names starting with Roel-, such as Roeland and Roelof (for males) and Roelanda and Roelofje (for females).
Variant of Roeline, with its spelling phonetical in nature.

When borne by a female person, this name is a good example of how one can turn a very masculine name (Roel) into a feminine name by simply adding the Dutch diminutive suffix -ke to the original name. But when borne by a male person, this name is simply a pet form because of the diminutive suffix.

This name consists of the name Roel - which in itself is a short form of Roeland - with the Germanic element man "man" added to it, by way of pet form. This name and its variants are quite rare nowadays and they are far more often found as a surname than as a first name.

When borne by a female person, this name is a good example of how one can turn a very masculine name (Roelof) into a feminine name by simply adding the diminutive suffix -je to the original name. But when borne by a male person, this name is simply a pet form because of the diminutive suffix.

When borne by a female person, this name is a good example of how one can turn a very masculine name (Roel) into a feminine name by simply adding the diminutive suffix -tje to the original name. But when borne by a male person, this name is simply a pet form because of the diminutive suffix.
Georgian form of Rowena as well as an English variant of the name.

column3: เรืองเขตกัน(Thai)
column12: From Thai elements เรือง (rueang) meaning "bright, glowing", เขต (khaeht) meaning "area, territory", and กัน (gan) meaning "together".
Older spelling of Rusdi influenced by Dutch orthography.
Variant of Ruslan influenced by Dutch orthography.
Older spelling of Rustam based on Dutch orthography.
Means "we are given" or "we are blessed" in Tshivenda.
Variant of Roi 2 influenced by the spelling of the name Joey

Italian form of Rotfrid. Also compare the similar-looking name Goffredo.Known bearers of this name include the Italian abbot and cardinal Roffredo dell'Isola (died in 1210), the Italian jurist Roffredo Epifanio (13th century AD) and the Italian aristocrat and composer Roffredo Caetani (1871-1961).
Meaning uncertain. It may be from Icelandic röfn "broken, severed" or a feminine form of Hrafn.
Short form of Roger. Also compare Rodge. This was the pen name of the American science fiction writer Rog Phillips (1909-1966; real name Roger Phillip Graham).
Czech and Slovak form of Rogatianus.
Spanish and Portuguese form of Rogatiana.
Spanish and Portuguese form of Rogatianus. A notable bearer of this name was the Brazilian journalist and poet Rogaciano Bezerra Leite (1920-1969).
Croatian and Slovene form of Rogatianus.
Transferred use of the surname Rogan.
Catalan, French and Polish form of Rogatus.

column4: Late Roman|Italian (Archaic)|Polish (Rare, Archaic)|Portuguese (Brazilian, Rare)|Spanish (Latin American, Rare)
column12: Feminine form of Rogatus. This name was borne by several obscure martyrs and saints.
English form of Rogatianus.This name was borne by several saints, the best known of which is Rogatian of Nantes, who was martyred together with his brother Donatian around 290 AD.

Roman cognomen which was derived from Rogatus. This name was borne by a Roman senator who, under the influence of the philosopher Plotinus (3rd century AD), resigned from his job and abandoned all of his wealth in order to live a simple lifestyle as a philosopher.This was also the name of several martyrs and saints, three of whom were part of the group of 49 Christians that were martyred in the town of Abitinae (located in what is now northern Tunisia) in 304 AD.
Diminutive of Rogata and Rogatia, as it contains the Latin feminine diminutive suffix -illa.
Roman cognomen which was derived from Rogatus.
Derivative of Rogatus.This is the name of an obscure saint, who together with Aresius and several other companions was martyred somewhere in North Africa at an unknown date.
Italian, Spanish and Portuguese form of Rogatus.
Malaya and Indonesian form of Ruqayya.
Probably an earlier form of Hrodger (see Roger).
Perhaps a variant of Regine or a feminine form of Roger. It seems to have been created in Vermont during the early 19th century.

column3: 로건(Korean Hangul)|潞建, 路巾(Korean Hanja)
column12: Ro-geon may also be a form derived from the English name Logan.
Variant of Roderick influenced by Roger.
Transferred use of the surname Rogers.
Alternate transcription of Persian رقیه (see Roghayeh).
Derived from the Germanic name elements vróg "slander, strife" and hvatr "active, brisk, vigorous, manly".
Franco-Provençal form of Roger. This name is borne by Rogiér Virèt, an Arpitan writer and author.
Slavic variant of the Old Norse name Ragnhildr (see Ragnhild). It was borne by a wife of the 10th-century Kievan prince Vladimir the Great.
Icelandic form of the Old Norse name Rǫgnvaldr, a variant of Ragnvaldr.
From Breton rog (“haughty”) or Middle French rogue (“arrogant, haughty”), from Old Northern French rogre, Old Norse hrokr (“excess, exuberance”).
Derived from Kurdish ro meaning "sun" and gula meaning "rose".

According to one version, it comes from the Old Norse Rögnvaldr, making it a cognate of Ronald, Reinhold, Renault and Rinaldo.According to another version, it comes from the Slavic рог, which means "horn", or "power, strength", and волод, which means "to wield, hold".The name was given to three princes of Polotsk. There's also an erroneous form of the name, Rogvold. A famous bearer is Rogvold Sukhoverko (1941-2015), a soviet film director of Tatar descent. His parents wanted to call him Rogvolod, but the employees of the registry office made a mistake.
One of the angels of punishment.
Variant transcription of Rou.Famous bearer of this name is Japanese composer and writer Roh Ogura.
Means "short-tail stingray" in Maori and Maori form of Rose.
Notable bearer is musician Rohahes Iain Phillips.
Meaning uncertain, probably of Arabic origin.

column3: 蕗繁, 蕗伴, 芦判, 蕗判, 呂伴, 呂繁, 路繁, 露繁, 絽半, 絽繁, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: Jamaican Patois form and English variant of Rowan.
Means "spiritual" in Indonesian and Malay, derived from roh meaning "spirit, soul" (of Arabic origin).

English name of uncertain origin and meaning which seems to have first appeared in the 19th century.Current theories include an elaboration of Rohan (influenced by Hannah), a name which was occasionally bestowed in honor of the French noble house of Rohan, some of whose members were leading Huguenots.It might also be an adoption and adaption of the Indian name Rohana.
Derived from rohat meaning "pleasure" or "comfort, ease" and gul meaning "rose, flower".
Derived from rohat meaning "pleasure" or "comfort, ease" and oy meaning "moon".
Bengali and Indonesian form of Rahima.
Indonesian and Malay variant of Rahima.
From the Malagasy rohin meaning "cord for binding" and soa meaning "good".
Transferred use of the surname Rohme.
Alternate transcription of Persian روح‌الله (see Ruhollah).
Transferred use of the surname Rohr. This is used as a feminine name in Victoria Aveyard's Red Queen.

column3: 로이(Korean Hangul)|露利, 路利, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 露 (ro) meaning "dew" or 路 (ro) meaning "road, avenue" combined with 利 (i) meaning "advantage, benefit". Other Hanja combinations are possible.
Old Norse variant and Faroese form of Hrói.
Means "to fall (from a height)" in Vietnamese.

column3: 路伊, 路以, 路威, 路郁, 呂伊, 呂偉, 遼威(Japanese Kanji)|ろい(Japanese Hiragana)|ロイ(Japanese Katakana)|Ρόη(Greek)
column12: This name can be used as 路伊, 路以, 路威, 路郁, 呂伊 or 呂偉 with 路 (ro, ru, -ji, michi) meaning "path, route, road, distance", 呂 (ro, ryo, sebone) meaning "spine, backbone", 伊 (i, kare) meaning "Italy, that one", 以 (i, mo'.te) meaning "because, by means of, compared with, in view of", 威 (i, odo.kasu, odo.shi, odo.su) meaning "dignity, intimidate, majesty, menace, threaten", 郁 (iku, i) meaning "cultural progress, perfume" and 偉 (i, era.i) meaning "admirable, conceited, excellent, famous, greatness, remarkable."One bearer of this name is actor Roi Hayashi (林 遼威) (2001-). In his case, the kanji used for his name are 遼 (ryou) meaning "distant" and 威.This name is very rarely given to children, if given at all. In the case for boys, this name may be phonetically linked to the name Roy.
Meaning uncertain. The name may be an Old Irish diminutive of Roibeárd or a gaelicization of an Old English personal name.

column3: 郎一, 郎市, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 郎 (rō) meaning "son" combined with 一 (ichi) meaning "one". Other combinations of kanji characters are also possible.
From Toba Batak ro meaning "come, arrive" and ida meaning "see, look".
Similar to Earleen, Charleen, Rayleen, Ashleen, Joeleen.

Derived from the Middle Persian adjective rōyēn meaning "brazen", which is ultimately derived from the Middle Persian noun rōy meaning "brass, copper".Also compare the name Royintan from the Shahnameh, which might possibly have been the inspiration behind the use of Roin as a given name in Georgia.Known bearers of this name include the Georgian historian Roin Metreveli (b. 1939) and the Georgian soccer player Roin Kvaskhvadze (b. 1989).

From the name of a lake in Häme, Finland. There are theories on the origin of this name, it could've come from Germanic hreini meaning "clean, clear" or from Pre-Germanic/Baltic *kroinis meaning "clean". This name was originally intended for females but nowadays is used more often among males.
Roja is the the Tamil name for Rose. Tamil is one of the many languages spoken in India and is mostly spoken in the state of Tamilnadu.
Derived from Kurdish ro meaning "sun" and jana meaning "pain".
Rojanice, with Rod her male counterpart, presides over the destinies of Humans. She is the co-creator of the universe, during birth.
From the Kurdish roj meaning "sun" and welat meaning "native land".
From roj meaning "sun" and dar meaning "tree, wood".

From 路(ro) meaning "road" or 露(ro) meaning "dew" or 璐(ro) meaning "beautiful jade" combined with 濟(je) meaning "corss a river" or 齊(je) meaning "complete, orderly". Other hanja combinations can also form this name.Usage of this name is, most likely, influenced by Rose with German pronouncuation or Rosé with French pronouncuation.

Similar to Rojin, the name’s meaning can be “light” (the more metaphorical meaning), “daylight”, “glimmering”, “shining”, or all of those combined. The ‘J’ in the name is pronounced the way it is in Jacques.
Possibly from Polish rój "swarm" and mir "peace".

This name can be the Lithuanian form of Roy as well as be an independent, authentic Lithuanian name. In the case of the latter, the name is derived from the Lithuanian noun rojus meaning "heaven, paradise".

Meaning unknown. Rokapi was an evil spirit and the leader of the kudiani (a group of witches) in Georgian mythology. He was punished by Ghmerti and chained to a column underneath the earth, where he ate the hearts of humans that his kudianis would bring to him. He would try to escape his prison every year, but always failed.
Alternate transcription of Arabic رقية (see Ruqayyah).
Form of Ruqayyah used in parts of western Africa (particularly Senegal).
First part of compound Arabic names, that in itself means "mercy of the" (compare Rokhimah)
Alternate transcription of Persian رخساره (see Rokhsareh).
Diminutive of Rodoljub used by Bosnian Serb singer Roki Vulović.
An Old Norse byname, from Old Norse rœkja meaning 'to care, to mind, to worry, to revere, to be careful with, take care of, guard, protect'.
French and French African form of Ruqayya.
Probably a spelling variant of Rocchina.
Indonesian and Malay form of Ruqayyah.

column3: 六花, 六華(Japanese Kanji)|ろっか(Japanese Hiragana)|ロッカ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From 六花 (rokka), an alternative reading of rikka literally meaning "six flowers," used as a synonym for 雪 (see yuki).This name is rarely used.
From Japanese 六九 (rokku) meaning "sixty nine". Other kanji or kanji combinations can form this name as well.Usage of this name is, most likely, influenced by the word lock or rock.
Maybe the name is related to the Old Norse word røkkr meaning "twilight" or røkkva meaning "to grow dark". In Norse mythology, Rǫkkvi was the name of a sea king
From Japanese word 六 (roku) means "six"This name also using by a fictional character in seri Avatar the last airbender. Avatar Roku, one of Aang's previous life
From Japanese 六 (roku) meaning "six" combined with 六 (roku) meaning "six". Other combinations of kanji characters can be possible.

column3: 六郎太, 六朗太(Japanese Kanji)|ろくろうた(Japanese Hiragana)|ロクロウタ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name combines 六 (riku, roku, mu, mui, mu'.tsu, mu.tsu) meaning "six" & 郎 (ryou, rou, otoko) meaning "son" or 朗 (rou, aki.raka, hoga.raka) meaning "bright, cheerful, clear, melodious, serene" with 太 (ta, tai, futo.i, futo.ru) meaning "big around, plump, thick."One fictional bearer of this name is Rokurōta Sakuragi (桜木 六郎太), the main character in the manga and anime series Rainbow: Nisha Rokubō no Shichinin.This name is very rarely given to boys, if given at all.
Alternate transcription of Arabic رولا (see Rula).
Icelandic and Faroese form of Roland.
Form of Roland with the Georgian nominative suffix -ი (-i). It is only used in Georgian when the name is written stand-alone.
Medieval Italian diminutive of Rolando, as -ino is an Italian masculine diminutive suffix.
Medieval Italian diminutive of Rolando, as -uccio is an Italian masculine diminutive suffix.
Icelandic and Faroese variant of Róland.
Mostly in books. Originated in Medieval Italy. Mainly in Tuscany, Rome, Sicily. Read "A River in Time: Italy." By Lisa T. Bergren to really enjoy how this name is used.
Transferred use of the surname Rolfe.
Variant of Roelien, though with this spelling, it may also be a short form of Carolien.

Means "pulling the branch of a tree" in Xhosa, colloquially "stirring up trouble" or "troublemaker". This was the given name of Nelson Mandela (Rolihlahla Mandela) and is now typically attributed to him as a middle name.
Meaning unknown. Mostly used in Asturias and León (also, to some extent, Galicia) in the 19th century and the first half of the 20th century.

In The Netherlands, this name is a variant of Roeline - though with this spelling, it may also be a short form of Caroline. In France, it is a variant spelling of Rauline - but the name is so archaic there, that one is far more likely to encounter it as a surname rather than a first name.
Most likely a transferred use of the surname Roll or a short form / nickname for Rudolph, Roland, Rollo or Rolf.
Possibly a phonetic spelling of Rollo.
Variant of the name Rolan and Roland.Also a name of one of the main characters from the Scholastic book series: Spirit Animals.
A pet form of names containing the name element hrod, for example Rolf.
Transferred use of the surname Rollin.
Transferred use of the surname Rollins.
Norman and Medieval French form of Rollo.
Low German form of Rodolf, as well as a Dutch variant of Roelof and a Swedish adoption.
Variant of Rolanda. This is borne by the American talk show host Rolonda Watts (1959-).
Short form of Romana and Romualda, occasionally used as a given name in its own right.
Indonesian and Thai form of Ramadan.
Alternate transcription of Arabic رميصاء (see Rumaysa), as well as the Urdu form.
Alternate transcription of Arabic رميصاء (see Rumaysa) chiefly used in North Africa.
Alternate transcription of Rumaysa chiefly used in North Africa.
Aragonese feminine form of Romaldo and Lithuanian feminine form of Romaldas.
Possibly a variant of Romualdine. It is also possible that this name is a combination of Romaine or Romane with a French feminine given name that ends in -line, such as Aline, Coraline and Pauline.
Probably a combination of Romaine or Romana with the popular English name suffix -lyn.
Icelandic and Kashubian form of Roman.
Alternate transcription of Bengali রুমানা (see Rumana), as well as an Urdu form.

This is the full name of one of the fourth Doctor's companions from the British TV series "Doctor Who", generally known as Romana. Although the first part is a real name, the rest was probably invented by the series' writers.
Diminutive of Romana, used as a given name in its own right.
From the English word “romance” this was given to 9 baby boys in the USA in 2014.
Derived from the Romani word rom "man; Roma".The name is borne by the German Romany activist Romani Rose.

Feminine form of Romanius.In modern times, Romania is also the name of a country in Europe. Its name is etymologically related, as it is ultimately derived from the Latin noun Romanus meaning "citizen of Rome" (see Roman).

Roman cognomen which was derived from either Romanus or Romanius.This was the name of a wealthy citizen of Thagaste (now Souk Ahras in Algeria), who was a friend and benefactor of saint Augustine of Hippo (354-430).
Originated from the Despotate of Obscuria, led by Despot Romanicus.
Diminutive of Romana and Romania, as it contains the Latin feminine diminutive suffix -illa.
Italian and Spanish form of Romanius.
Possibly a combination of Roman and Monique. This is the middle name of Laphonza Butler (1979-).
Allegedly derived from Romanian romaniță "camomile, chamomile".

Roman nomen gentile which was derived from the Roman cognomen Romanus.This name is primarily known from inscriptions, as no bearers of the name have ever had a position of importance or historical significance in the Roman Empire.
Form of Romanoz with the Georgian nominative suffix -ი (-i). It is only used in Georgian when the name is written stand-alone.
Variant spelling of Romani, the name of a chiefly European nomadic group of people (where they are mostly known as 'gypsies'). They ultimately derive their name from Latin Romanus meaning "Roman".
The African American collage artist Romare Bearden is a famous person with this first name.

Derived from Old High German hrôm "fame, glory" combined with rîcja "powerful, strong, mighty." The second element is also closely related to Celtic rîg or rix and Gothic reiks, which all mean "king, ruler." This name was borne by a Frankish saint from the 8th century AD, from whom the French village Remiremont derives its name.
Diminutive of Romário, as it contains the Portuguese masculine diminutive suffix -inho.
From Batak roma meaning "come, arrive" and uli meaning "good, beautiful".
Alternate transcription of Arabic رميصاء (see Rumaysa).
Derived from Old High German hrôm "fame, glory" combined with Old High German bald "bold, brave."
Derived from Old High German hrôm "fame, glory" combined with Old High German beraht "bright."
Diminutive of Romana, not used as a given name in its own right.
Alternate transcription of Arabic رمضان (see Ramadan) chiefly used in Tunisia.
A type of aromatic flower that blooms at night, typically found around Angkor Wat.
Feminine form of Romed, Romedio, or Romedius.

Italian form of Romedius.Saint Romedius (died c. 4th century) was the son on Tyrolese count. After his parents died, he gave away all his possessions and established himself in the Val di Non in Trentino, Italy, where the Sanctuary of San Romedio still exists. The saint is often depicted alongside a bear.

The origins and meaning of this name are disputed.It has been suggested that this name might either derive from Latin remedium "remedy" or else from Latin remex "oarsman".It was borne by a 4th century saint from Tirol.
Variant of Romée. This name is borne by Dutch fashion model Romee Strijd.
Probably a simplified spelling of Rommel.
Greek form of Remaliah, as it first appeared in the Septuagint.
Possibly a feminine form of Romel.
Transferred use of the surname Romelo.

This name is best known for being the name of the Belgian professional soccer player Romelu Lukaku (b. 1993), who is the eldest son of the Congolese professional soccer player Roger Menama Lukaku (b. 1967). He was named after his father, as his name consists of the first two letters of each of his father's three names. As such, the name Romelu is a modern creation.
Either a variant of România or directly derived from Romênia, the Brazilian Portuguese name for the European country of Romania.
Icelandic and Hungarian form of Romeo.

From Japanese 朗 (ro) meaning "bright, clear", 明 (me) meaning "clear, bright" combined with 生 (o) meaning "raw, live". Other kanji combinations are possible.Usage of this name is, most likely, influenced by the name Romeo.
Variant of Rodmar coincidentally also the german word for roman.
Taken from the Spanish word romeral, meaning "valley of rosemaries".

Portuguese diminutive of Romero.This name saw a jump in usage to over 1,400 counts in the 1980s from over 50 in the 1970s, influenced by Paraguayan football player Julio César Romero Insfrán (1960-), nicknamed Romerito, who was playing for the Brazilian football club Fluminense from 1983 to 1988.

Means "rosemary" in Spanish and Portuguese. As a Brazilian masculine name, it may related to the word romero or to the surname Romero, with a different origin. As a Spanish feminine name, it is taken from the title of the Virgin Mary Nuestra Señora del Romero (meaning "Our Lady of the Rosemary") and venerated at the town of Cascante (Navarre, Spain).
Archaic Dutch spelling of Romein. A well-known bearer of this name was Romeyn de Hooghe, an important Dutch painter and sculptor.
Derived from Old High German hrôm "fame, glory" combined with Old High German fridu "peace."
Derived from Old High German hrôm "fame, glory" combined with Gothic hardus (hart in Old High German) "brave, hardy."
Derived from Old High German hrôm "fame, glory" combined with Old Norse hildr "battle." Also see Romilda.
Diminutive of Roman and Romana or Romina.
Provençal and Gascon form of Remigius.
Combination of the names Romi and El means "God is my exaltation" in Hebrew.
Languedocian and Gascon form of Romeo.
Armenian diminutive of Roman and Romeo.
French form and Italian variant of Romilda.
Italian and Spanish form of Romilius.

Tajik form of the Persian name Ramish, which is derived from Persian رامش (ramish) meaning "joy, happiness, cheerfulness, delight", itself ultimately derived from Middle Persian or Pahlavi rāmišn meaning "peace, ease, pleasure". Also compare the related names Raman 2 and Ramin.
Combination of the name Romi, means "my exaltation" and the letters ya (יה) (which are part of the name of God)
Diminutive of Romme (when the bearer is male) and feminine form of Romme.
Variant of Ramli also used in Thailand.
Variant of Ramli, also used in Thailand.
The name of a Dark Elf in the video game The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim.
Frisian short form of names that contain the Old High Germanic element hrôm, such as Rombert and Romuald.

Transferred from the German surname Rommel (notable bearers include the German field marshal Erwin Rommel and the city mayor of Stuttgart Manfred Rommel).Rommel is not admitted as a given name in Germany because of its surname character.
Transferred use of the surname Romney.
Combination of Nicholas and a name starting with Rom- such as Romeo or Román.
Eritrean name, which is possibly derived from the Arabic name Ramadan.
Variant of Ramona, probably influenced by the name Pomona.
Variant of Ramazon, which is the main Uzbek form of Ramazan (see Ramadan).

Rongomātāne is a god of agriculture and peace (after war) in Māori mythology. Rongomātāne derives from rongo "peace, news", mā "by way of", and tāne "man".

A variant of Rowena, the daughter of the Saxon leader Hengist, given in marriage to King Vortigern of Britain by Hengist in exchange for the country of Kent. She is first found in Nennius.Vortigern’s marriage to Rowena horrified many of Vortigern’s subjects – as well as the British clergy – because Rowena was a heathen and Vortigern was a Christian, and also because the union cemented an uncomfortable alliance between the British and the Saxons.When Vortigern’s son, Vortimer, took the throne from his father and defeated the Saxons, Rowena pretended that she wished to convert to Christianity. She was able to get close to Vortimer, and she then poisoned and killed him, allowing Vortigern to reclaim the throne and the Saxons to return. Her character is found in Godfrey of Viterbo’s Pantheon as Angria and in Baudin Butor’s romance as Sardoine.Rowena appears as the main character in Thelwall’s The Fairy of the Lake. A heathen sorceress, she falls in love with Arthur (here presented as the contemporary of Vortigern and Ambrosius) and embarks on an elaborate scheme to seduce him by magic, calling upon her supernatural allies such as Queen Hela of the Infernal Regions and the demon Incubus. Thwarted by the Lady of the Lake, Arthur’s guardian, she murders her husband Vortigern and offers Arthur the crown along with herself. Arthur, horrified at her crime, burns Rowena and her castle to the ground.

"Every day propound to yourself a rosary or chaplet of good works to present to God at night." (Jer. Taylor)4) A coin bearing the figure of a rose, fraudulently circulated in Ireland in the 13th century for a penny.
From Italian rosa meaning "rose" and spina "thorn, spine", used as a translation of German Dornröschen, the title character of a Brothers Grimm fairy tale (known as Briar Rose in English).
Possibly a variant of Rosula, or an extension of Rosa 1.
French form of Rosaura used in French-language translations of Pedro Calderón de la Barca's play Life Is a Dream (1635).
From Ukrainian роса (rosa), meaning "dew". See also Rosa 2.
Derived from Old Norse rós meaning "rose" and bjǫrg meaning "help, save, rescue".
Old Frankish diminutive of Old Saxon hrōth and Old High German hruod "fame".

German diminutive of Rosa 1 and other feminine names that start with Ros- (such as Rosalie), as it has the German diminutive suffix -chen. This diminutive, which is typically only used informally, is rather old-fashioned and is now rarely used.It should also be noted that Röschen is also a regular word in German: it literally means "little rose", as it is a diminutive of the German noun Rose meaning "rose".A known bearer of this name is the German politician Ursula von der Leyen (b. 1958), who has been known to her family as Röschen since childhood.
Derived from the Slavic name element rasti "to grow" and gnyevu "anger".
Roscillus was a chief of the Allobroges, who had served Julius Caesar with great fidelity in the Gallic Wars, and was treated by him with great distinction.

The first element of this name is derived from Polish rościć, which can mean "to claim, to lay claim to" as well as "to sprout". Also compare Polish rosnąć "to grow, to sprout, to increase", Croatian rasti "to grow, to increase" and Czech růst "to grow, to increase". The second element of this name is derived from Slavic mir "peace". In other words, this name is the Polish form of Rostimir.

From a Roman nomen gentile, which was derived from Latin ros "dew" via roscidus "dewy, wet". This name was borne by several ancient Romans, one of them being an ancient Roman actor named Quintus Roscius Gallus.
Variant of Roscoe. One bearer of this variant was Roscow Shedden (1882-1956), an Anglican bishop.
Probably a feminine elaboration of Rosdi.
Variant of Rosabel or a combination of Rose and Belle.
Name of Rosebud Denovo, street activist, and Rosebud the Basselope, a character in the comic strip Bloom County.

A variant of Rosendale . habitational name from Rosedale (North Yorkshire). The placename derives from Old Norse dalr ‘valley’ with an uncertain first element either hross ‘horse’ (genitive plural hrossa) or the Old Norse personal name Russi Ross
Derived from French rosée "dew", this name might have come into use as an equivalent of Rocío.

Derived from English rose gold, the name of a gold-copper alloy which is sometimes also used to describe a colour that is golden yet somewhat reddish.This name is the middle name of the British-Vincentian singer Marlon Roudette (b. 1983).
Southern German diminutive of Rose and names containing Rose like Rosemarie or Annerose.
Of debated origin and meaning. Theories include a variant of Roselène, a variant of Roseline and a contraction of Rose and Madelaine.
Either a form of Rose with -lee suffix, or a form of Rosalie.
Contraction of Rose and Hélène. In some cases it might also have been a variant of Roseline.
German contraction of Rose and Lene and Haitian form of Roselène.
A new invented name of the words Rose and lieb meaning lovely.

Possibly a combination of Danish rose meaning "rose" and lilje meaning "lily" or lille meaning "little". Roselil og hendes moder (Roselil and Her Mother) is a Danish song by Christian Knud Frederik Molbech (1821-1888). The Roselil series is a collection of children's fables written by Danish author Josefine Ottesen (1956-).
Directly taken from Catalan rosella "(red) poppy".
Brazilian variant of Roselle reflecting the Brazilian Portuguese pronunciation to the French version of Rosella.
Possibly a combination of Rose and Elma.
Contraction of Rose and Eleonore via the short form Lore 1.
A combination of Rose and Louise.
Meaning unknown, perhaps based on similar-sounding names such as Rosella and Zelpha.
Variant of Rosália and Rosalie using the suffix ely used in Spanish-speaking countries outside Spain and in Brazil.
Combination of Swedish ros "rose" and Maj 2 as well as a diminutive of Rosemarie.
Combination of Rose and May, possibly used as a diminutive of Rosemary or Rosemarie.

Combination of Rose and -mene, a feminine name suffix commonly used in Haiti. The second element might be taken from Philomène or from a name such as Chrismene, Dieumene, Jesumene or Viergemene in which it appears to originate from French mène meaning "leads" (i.e., the aforelisted names appear to be derived from French phrases with religious meanings - "Christ leads", "God leads", "Jesus leads" and "the Virgin (Mary) leads", respectively).
Combination of Rose and Merlande, a variation of Mirlande.
Contracted form of Rosemarie and Rosemaria.
A known bearer of this name is Rosemin Madhavji, a Canadian-born fashion entrepreneur of Indian descent.
Variant of Rosemont, Dutch form of Rosamund. Also a combination of the names Rose and Mint.
Derived from Cornish rosen, the collective form of ros "rose".
Anglicized form of the noble Danish surname Rosenkrantz. Shakespeare used this name for a childhood friend of Hamlet in his play The Tragedy of Hamlet, Prince of Denmark (1600).
Nordic form of the German surname Rosenkranz meaning "rosary".
Possibly a variant of Rosanna or Rosina.
Combination of Rosen and Cornish gwynn "fair, white, blessed". This is a modern Cornish name.

Derived from the Latin adjective roseus "pink, rosy, rose-coloured". A bearer of this name is RJ Rosales (a Filipino artist of Spanish descent). The name seems to originally come from Italy, though, since roseo is an existing adjective there for "pink, rosy" (as opposed to Spanish and Portuguese-speaking countries) and because sources list it as a legitimate Italian name.
From the biblical expression, which refers to an unknown flower. Often used as a name for the Hibiscus, as well as many other flowering plants.
Referring to the Petals of a rose.
Elaboration of Rose with the suffix -ra
English translation of German Rosenrot. This name was featured on the German fairy tale Snow-White and Rose-Red by Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm.

Austrian and Bavarian German diminutive of given names that start with Ros-, such as Rosa 1 and Roswitha. It is typically only used informally, meaning: it is hardly ever (if at all) used as an official name on birth certificates.
Provençal and Louisiana Spanish form of Rosette.
The name Rosewood is boy's name meaning "rose wood".
Probably an Anglicized form of Rhoswen.
Combination of the Old Norse name elements rós "rose" and ey "island; flat land along a coast" or ey "good fortune".
Diminutive of Rosa 1, Rose and of compound names that start with Ros-, such as Rosaline.For men, this name is typically a diminutive of Roosevelt.

Possibly derived from the Old English elements hroð "glory, fame" and friþ "peace, happiness". It was mentioned by the 12th-century English historian Reginald of Durham as belonging to a 7th-century Christian woman from Hawick who, with Seigiv, had worshiped at the lost chapel of Saint Cuthbert in the Slitrig Valley.James A. H. Murray, founder of the Oxford English Dictionary, gave this name to his fourth daughter in 1884.
Derived from Icelandic rós meaning "rose" (see Rós) and Old Norse fríðr meaning "beautiful, beloved". Also see Rosfrith.
Meaning "Head." Rosh is the seventh of the ten sons of Benjamin named in Genesis 46:21
Could be a combination of the prefix Ros- (from Rosalind, Rosamund, Rosanne etc.) and Shae.
Alternate transcription of Arabic رشدي (see Rushdi).
Alternate transcription of Arabic رشدي (see Rushdi).
meaning:"The Head"name is used by Bukharian Jewish community from Uzbekistan
Means light or candle, similar to Roshni. Roshni
Derived from Persian روشن (roshan) meaning "light, bright".
Potentially derived from ro'shnolik meaning "a happy and comfortable life".
Fijian, Samoan, broadly Polynesian and Melanesian form of Rosie.
Feminine form of Rosianus. A bearer of this name was Rosiana Coleners, a Belgian poet from the 16th century AD.
Portuguese form of Rosianus, though in some cases it can also be a blend of Rosa 1 with a name ending in -iano, such as Cristiano. This name is mainly found in Brazil.
Extended form of Rosius. A bearer of this name was Rosianus Geminus, who lived in the first century AD.
Possibly a blend of Rosa 1 and Cleide.
Indonesian and Malay variant of Rashida.
Combination of Rosie and the popular suffix -lyn.
Diminutive of Róis or the Irish word for rose
Estonian variant of Rosilde and Italian, Québécois and Walloon form of Roshilda.
Possibly a variant of Roselina. Rosilena ed Oronta (1728) is an opera by Antonio Vivaldi.
Possibly from Portuguese rosa "rose" and lírio "lily" (cf. Alíria).
German short form of Euphrosina, common in the 1700s and 1800s, then almost forgotten and now being revived in recent years.
Probably a blend of the names Rosa 1 and Inés. A known bearer of this name is Rosinés Chávez Rodríguez (b. 1997), daughter of Venezuelan president Hugo Chávez (b. 1954).
Tagalog diminutive of Rosa 1, Generosa or other names containing rosa.
Combination of Rós and the Old Norse suffix ingr meaning "son of, belonging to".
Allegedly means "tub of roses" in Icelandic, from rós "rose" and kar "tub".
Derived from Latin rosa "rose", though a connection with Latin ros "dew" may also be possible (see Roscius). The best known bearer of this name was the Roman consul Rosius Regulus.
Likely a combination of Rosi and Edvaldo.

In the case of Icelandic avant-garde artist Róska (1940-1996), it was a pseudonym apparently formed from R, the initial letter of her given name Ragnhildur, and Óska, the first four letters of her surname Óskarsdóttir - itself a derivative of the masculine given name Óskar.
Derived from rǫskr "brave". In Norse Mythology, Rǫskva and her brother Þjálfi are servants of Thor.
Diminutive of Rosa 1, recorded in medieval Frankfurt, Germany.
Derived from the place name Roslin belonging to a village in Scotland.
Combination of Roslina and the feminine suffix -wati or alternatively, Ros and Linawati.
Malay and Indonesian form of Rosalind.
Possibly a feminine elaboration of Rosli or a combination of Ros and Liza.
Malay form of Rusman as well as an Indonesian variant.
Used among some Amish and Mennonite communities a variant of the name Rosamund.
Combination of the name Rosma and the feminine suffix -niar.
Derived from the Old Norse elements rós "rose" and maðr "person, man" (genitive manns).
Variant of Roosmarijn. The name coincides with Dutch rosmarijn, an obsolete variant of rozemarijn "rosemary".
Combination of the name Rosma and the feminine suffix -wati.

Probably means "great provider" from Gaulish ro, an intensive prefix (hence "very, most, great"), combined with smert "purveyor, carer" and the feminine name suffix a. This was the name of an obscure Gallo-Roman goddess of fertility, abundance and prosperity. The author J. K. Rowling borrowed the name for a witch in her 'Harry Potter' series.
Latin American Spanish adoption of Rosemary.
Possibly a variant of Rosmunda or Romina. This name was used by Francesco Cavalli for a character in his opera Giasone (1649).
Rosmira (also known as Rosmira fedele, 1738) is an opera by Antonio Vivaldi.
Indonesian and Malay form of Roshna.
Combination of Rosna and the feminine suffix -wati.
Indonesian and Malay form of Roshni.

From Catalan rosor meaning "rosiness, pinkness". This is the title of a Catalan song about a woman named Rosó that premiered in 1922 and soon became a staple in the repertory of Catalan popular music. Sometimes it is considered a variant of Roser.
Variant of Rosó using the normative spelling of the word in Catalan.

It is used in Ireland in honour of the Fenian leader Jeremiah O'Donovan Rossa (1831-1915). He took the agnomen Rossa after the town Rossmore in Kilmeen which his family had held in the 17th Century, with Rossmore coming from the Irish an ros mór meaning "the great wooded height".
Alternate form of Rossana (Italian) or Rosania (Portuguese) as the name for Roxana.
Masculine form of Rossana. A famous bearer was the actor Rossano Brazzi (1916-1994).
This is the name of a thane in William Shakespeare's Macbeth (also spelled Ross).
Transferred use of the surname Rossi. As a feminine name, it could be a variant of Rosie.
A variant of the surname Rossi, a variant of Rosie or diminutive of Ross.
Unknown, possibly an Italian form of Russell.
Diminutive of Rossa. But it should be noted that there are also cases where this name is a variant of Rosina.
Variant of Rositsa used mainly outside of Bulgaria.
Means "Russia" in Russian. Used by patriotic parents.
German calque of Philipp as chosen by Philipp Wackernagel, derived from the Germanic name elements hros "horse" (with modernised spelling) and lieb "kind, dear".

Either a variant of Roslyn or, in more recent times, an adoption of the name of Rosslyn Chapel in the Scottish village of Roslin which became famous overnight thanks to the publication of Holy Blood, Holy Grail by Baigent, Leigh and Lincoln in 1982 (and again two decades later when it featured in Dan Brown's The Da Vinci Code (2003)).The chapel's name is a corruption of the village's name which in turn was first recorded as Roskelyn and is said to be derived from Scottish Gaelic ros "promontory" and cuileann "holly".
Italian form of Russus. A known bearer of this name was Rosso Fiorentino, an Italian painter from late medieval times.
Probably a reinterpretation of Roswitha analysed as hros "horse" and hwit "white". Roßweiße is the name of one of the valkyries in Richard Wagner's opera 'Die Walküre'.
Diminutive of Rosa 1 and Rosana. Rosa Elena García Echave (born 16 September 1964), better known as Rossy de Palma, is a Spanish actress, singer and model.

Rostagnus is a Latinization of a Germanic given name common in the Middle Ages, especially in Occitania. It derives from Proto-Germanic Hrōþi- "fame" and stainaz "stone". It is attested in the Old High German form Hruodstein.In vernacular documents in England and Romance-speaking areas, the name appears as Rostaing, Rostand, Rostan, Rustand, Rustant, Rustan, Rodstein, Rostein, Rostain, Rostang and Rostagne. The Occitan form is Rostanh and the Catalan is Rostany.
French form of Rostagnus, ultimately from the Germanic name Hruodstein.

Georgian sources state that this name is of Persian origin and means "straight, righteous" as well as "wise, sage" and "truthful". This should connect the name to Middle Persian rāst meaning "true, straight, direct" and rastīh meaning "truth", which have evolved into modern Persian as respectively راست (râst) and راستی (râsti).There might also be a connection with Middle Persian drust meaning "right, well, healthy" and drustīh meaning "righteous, health", of which the modern Persian equivalents are درست (dorost) and درستی (dorosti) respectively.In Georgian literature, Rostevan is the name of a king of Arabia in the 12th-century epic poem The Knight in the Panther's Skin written by the Georgian poet Shota Rustaveli. He is the father of the princess Tinatin, who inherits the throne from him because he has no sons and she is his only child.
Derived from Slavic rosts "usurp" combined with Slavic mir "peace".
Short form of Rostom and also of Rostevan in some cases.
Form of Rostom with the nominative suffix, used in Georgian when the name is written stand-alone.
Possibly derived from the Uzbek rost meaning "true, real".
Medieval Italian diminutive of Rosa 1, as -uccia is an Italian feminine diminutive suffix.
This name is either a diminutive of Rosa 1 or formed from Orsula by metathesis of the letter R.
This name, now extremely rare, comes from the German 'rosen weilt', signifying "wild rose".
Slovene and Romansh form of Roswitha.
From hros "horse" and weald "power, ruler", meaning "powerful horse".
Combination of the name elements Hros meaning "horse" and Wini meaning "friend".

Polish name for Rapunzel, which is taken from their word for corn salad, also known as the Valerianella plant. This is also how the original German Rapunzel is named. This isn't used as a given name in Poland.

Possibly derived from the Old Norse verb róta meaning "to stir, overturn, tear". In Norse mythology, Róta is a valkyrie. She is attested in the Prose Edda book Gylfaginning, where she is mentioned alongside the valkyries Gunnr and Skuld. The three are described as "always riding to choose who shall be slain and to govern the killings".
Directly taken from Latvian rota "jewel; ornament, adornment; singing for some early summer morning songs".
Derived from the Germanic element hrôthi "fame" combined with Old High German bald "bold, brave."
Derived from the Germanic element hrôthi "fame" combined with Proto-Germanic beran or bernu "bear" (bero and bern in Old High German).
Derived from the Germanic element hrôthi "fame" combined with Old Norse brand "sword."

The first element of this name is derived from the Germanic element hrôthi "fame." The second element is derived from Gothic bairgan (bergan in Old High German) "to keep, to save, to preserve", or from Old High German burg "fortress."
Derived from the Germanic element hrôthi "fame" combined with Old High German fridu "peace."
Derived from the Germanic element hrôthi "fame" combined with gang "path."

The first element of this name is derived from the Germanic element hrôthi "fame." The second element is derived from gardan "to hedge in, to enclose, to fence in" or from Gothic gards "house, garden, (court)yard."
Derived from the Germanic element hrôthi "fame" combined with Gothic gasts (gast in Old High German) "guest, stranger."
Derived from the Germanic element hrôthi "fame" combined with Gothic gild "sacrifice."

The first element of this Germanic name comes from hrôthi "fame." The meaning and origin of the second element is rather uncertain: we know that it comes from gis (the original form was possibly gîs), but we don't exactly know where gis itself comes from. But there are a few possibilities. It might come from Gallo-Celtic gaiso "spear" (see Gaiseric) or it might be a short form of gisel, which means "hostage" or "pledge" (see Giselle).
Derived from the Germanic element hrôthi "fame" combined with Old Norse grîma "mask."
Derived from the Germanic element hrôthi "fame" combined with Old High German hadu "battle."
Derived from the Germanic element hrôthi "fame" combined with Old High German hari "army." This name was borne by a 7th-century king of the Lombards.
Derived from the Germanic element hrôthi "fame" combined with Gothic hardus (hart in Old High German) "brave, hardy."
Variant of Rothar. This name was borne by a 7th-century Lombard king of the house of Arodus.
Derived from the Germanic element hrôthi "fame" combined with Old High German helm "helmet, protection".
Means "famous battle", derived from the Germanic element hrôthi "fame" combined with Old Norse hildr "battle."
Rothilde (871 – 928/929) was a daughter of the King of the Franks, Charles the Bald, son of Louis the Pious.
A pre-anglicised Irish version of Roland (and the other related names), specifically used in a patronym surname from the medieval ages directly meaning "Descendant of Roland".
Derived from Old Norse rǫðull meaning "glory, halo" (poetic for "sun"). This is also a poetic word for "sun" in Icelandic.
Means "stay with me" or "stand by me" in Yoruba. Sometimes used as a short form for Olurotimi or Oluwarotimi.
A common name used among the Jos Plateau people of Nigeria. Meaning of the name is "love has come"
Ancient Germanic, Languedocian, Provençal and Gascon form of Roland.
Derived from the Germanic element hrôthi "fame" combined with Old High German mund "protection."
Meaning unknown. The most famous bearer, either in reality or in media, is Rotor the Walrus, from the Sonic the Hedgehog comic series by Archie Comics.
Derived from the Germanic element hrôthi "fame" combined with Old High German rât "counsel."
Derived from the Germanic element hrôthi "fame" combined with hraban or hramn "raven."
Derived from the Germanic element hrôthi "fame" combined with þruþ "strength."
Variant spelling of Rotrud. Rotrude of Treves was the first wife of Charles Martel, a Frankish king from the Carolingian dynasty.
Means "we have been saved" in Tshivenda.
Derived from the Germanic element hrôthi "fame" combined with Old High German stain "stone."
From Batak ro meaning "come, arrive" and tua meaning "good luck, blessing".
Derived from the Germanic element hrôthi "fame" combined with Old High German wart "guard."
Derived from the Germanic element hrôthi "fame" combined with Old High German wîg "warrior."
Derived from the Germanic element hrôthi "fame" combined with Old High German wini "friend."
Alternate transcription of Persian رودابه (see Rudabeh).

Sudanese Arabic form of Ridwan. Derived from the Arabic رضوان (riḍwān) meaning “satisfaction”, “contentment”, or “divine pleasure”. In Islamic tradition, Ridwan is the name of the angel who guards Paradise.The spelling Roudwan reflects Sudanese and regional Arabic pronunciation patterns, where the vowel sound is often rendered as “ou”.
Meaning uncertain, but likely derived from the French surname Roué or even Rué.A notable bearer of this name is the Surinamese actor and comedian Roué Verveer (b. 1972).
Modern Greek spelling of Rouphinos, which is the ancient Greek form of Rufinus.
Modern Greek spelling of Rouphos, which is the ancient Greek form of Rufus.

column3: 朗風, 浪風, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 朗 (rou) meaning "bright, clear" or 浪 (rou) meaning "wave" combined with 風 (fuu) meaning "wind". Other combinations of kanji are possible.

The name of a werewolf-like creature in Laurentian French. It is derived from standard French loup garou "werewolf" (where loup means "wolf" and garou is a borrowed word from Germanic were-wolf via Frankish garulf).
Means "red" in French, though it can also refer to the type of make-up. A famous fictional bearer is Rouge the Bat, a character in the Sonic games.

In the case of Venezuelan baseball player Rougned Odor, his first name is a combination of his grandfather's name, Douglas, and his grandmother's name, Nedia; in keeping with the family custom of giving boys names that begin with the letter "R", the "D" in Douglas was changed to an "R", yielding Rougned.
Form of Ruqayya used in parts of French-influenced West Africa, particularly in Guinea.
From Japanese 朗 (rou) meaning "bright, clear" combined with 一 (ichi) meaning "one". Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.
Combination of Rouke (a variant spelling of Rauke) with Bert.
From Japanese 朗 (rou) meaning "bright, clear" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Alternate transcription of Arabic رولا (see Rula).
Diminutive of Argyro, via its diminutive Argyroula. See also Roula.
From Japanese 朗 (rou) meaning "bright, clear" combined with 茉 (ma) meaning "white jasmine". Other combinations of kanji characters are also possible.
Alternate transcription of Arabic رميصاء (see Rumaysa) chiefly used in North Africa.
Alternate transcription of Arabic رميصاء (see Rumaysa) chiefly used in North Africa.
Variant of Romania.It was the original English spelling of the European country, borrowed from the French Roumanie in the 19th century.
Alternate transcription of Arabic رميصاء (see Rumaysa) chiefly used in North Africa.
Alternate transcription of Arabic رميصاء (see Rumaysa) chiefly used in North Africa.
Alternate transcription of Arabic رميصاء (see Rumaysa) chiefly used in North Africa.
A water plant with a white or purplish flower.

This name can be used as 浪人 (rounin) meaning "drifter" or "wanderer", i.e. "he who drifts/wanders".It is built from the kanji 浪 (rou) meaning "wandering, waves, billows, reckless, unrestrained" combined with 人 (nin) meaning "person". Other kanji combinations are possible.During the feudal period of Japan, the word Rōnin (浪人) was used meaning a samurai without lord or master. A samurai became masterless from the death or fall of his master, or after the loss of his master's favor or privilege. Today the word is now used meaning a salaryman who is unemployed or a secondary school graduate who has not yet been admitted to university.This name is rarely given to boys, if given at all.
Alternate transcription of Armenian Ռուբեն (see Rupen).
French variant of Rupert. It has fallen out of use in France, but the name is still used in francophone Africa (albeit rarely).

column3: 朗羅, 楼良, 玲良, 桜良, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 朗 (rou) meaning "bright, clear" combined with 羅 (ra) meaning "lightweight fabric". Other kanji combinations are possible.Usage of this name is, most likely, influenced by the name Lola or Laura.
Transferred use of the surname Rourke.
From Japanese 朗 (rou) meaning "bright, clear" or 琅 (rou) meaning "pure" combined with 々, a phonetic character indicting a duplication of the beginning kanji. Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Japanese 浪 (rou) meaning "wave" duplicated and combined with 子 (shi) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.

Hellenized form of the Urartian name Rusa, which was borne by four kings of Urartu (primarily located in what is now Turkey, Armenia and Iran).A notable bearer of this name was the Armenian-American philosopher and theologian Rousas John "R. J." Rushdoony (1916-2001), whose native Armenian name was Rusa Hovhannes Rshtuni.
From Japanese 朗 (rou) meaning "bright, clear" combined with 史 (shi) meaning "history". Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.
Perhaps a diminutive of Ruzan or Roza 1.

Transferred use of the surname Rousseau notably borne by the 18th-century Swiss philosopher Jean-Jacques Rousseau. A given name bearer was Rousseau Owen Crump (1843-1901), a U.S. Representative from Michigan.
Transferred use of the surname Roussel.
Transferred use of the surname Rousso.
From Japanese 朗 (rou) meaning "bright, clear" combined with 太 (ta) meaning "thick, big". Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.
Greek form of Ruth 1, as it first appeared in the Septuagint.
Transferred use of the surname Roux.
Alternate transcription of Arabic رؤية (see Ruya).
From the Persian روز‎ (ruz) meaning “day” and #‎ به‎ (beh) meaning “better, good”, ultimately meaning "fortunate".
From Japanese 浪 (rou) meaning "wave" combined with 都 (zu) meaning "capital (city)". Other kanji combinations are possible.This name is influenced by the word and given name Rose.
From the Malagasy rova meaning "fortification" and dialectal form lala meaning "dear, beloved".
Albanian, Croatian, Lithuanian and Portuguese form of Rowena.
Form of Rövşən used outside of Azerbaijan.
Form of Rövşanə used outside of Azerbaijan.
Derived from Arabic روضة (rawḍa) meaning "garden, flower garden".
Diminutive of Rowan or Rowena, Irish, Scottish, Welsh"rowan tree, little redhead; white spear, famous friend"
Alternate transcription of Arabic رويدا (see Ruwayda).
A nickname with synonyms such as boisterous or rambunctious. Notable namesake is US Olympic swimmer Rowdy Gaines.
Diminutive of Rowan, Roland, or Rhoda.

A variant of Rowena, the daughter of the Saxon leader Hengist, given in marriage to King Vortigern of Britain by Hengist in exchange for the country of Kent. She is first found in Nennius.Vortigern’s marriage to Rowena horrified many of Vortigern’s subjects – as well as the British clergy – because Rowena was a heathen and Vortigern was a Christian, and also because the union cemented an uncomfortable alliance between the British and the Saxons.When Vortigern’s son, Vortimer, took the throne from his father and defeated the Saxons, Rowena pretended that she wished to convert to Christianity. She was able to get close to Vortimer, and she then poisoned and killed him, allowing Vortigern to reclaim the throne and the Saxons to return. Her character is found in Godfrey of Viterbo’s Pantheon as Angria and in Baudin Butor’s romance as Sardoine.Rowena appears as the main character in Thelwall’s The Fairy of the Lake. A heathen sorceress, she falls in love with Arthur (here presented as the contemporary of Vortigern and Ambrosius) and embarks on an elaborate scheme to seduce him by magic, calling upon her supernatural allies such as Queen Hela of the Infernal Regions and the demon Incubus. Thwarted by the Lady of the Lake, Arthur’s guardian, she murders her husband Vortigern and offers Arthur the crown along with herself. Arthur, horrified at her crime, burns Rowena and her castle to the ground.
Variant of Rowan with the suffix -etta
A short form of names such as Rowan, Rowena, or Rowanne
Dutch variant of Rowan. A known bearer of this name is the Dutch professional soccer player Rowin van Zaanen (b. 1984).
Rowlf is a Muppet character created by Jim Henson.
English cognate of Roxabel (in English-speaking countries) as well as a variant form of Roxabel (in Latin America).

A variant of Rowena, the daughter of the Saxon leader Hengist, given in marriage to King Vortigern of Britain by Hengist in exchange for the country of Kent. She is first found in Nennius.Vortigern’s marriage to Rowena horrified many of Vortigern’s subjects – as well as the British clergy – because Rowena was a heathen and Vortigern was a Christian, and also because the union cemented an uncomfortable alliance between the British and the Saxons.When Vortigern’s son, Vortimer, took the throne from his father and defeated the Saxons, Rowena pretended that she wished to convert to Christianity. She was able to get close to Vortimer, and she then poisoned and killed him, allowing Vortigern to reclaim the throne and the Saxons to return. Her character is found in Godfrey of Viterbo’s Pantheon as Angria and in Baudin Butor’s romance as Sardoine.Rowena appears as the main character in Thelwall’s The Fairy of the Lake. A heathen sorceress, she falls in love with Arthur (here presented as the contemporary of Vortigern and Ambrosius) and embarks on an elaborate scheme to seduce him by magic, calling upon her supernatural allies such as Queen Hela of the Infernal Regions and the demon Incubus. Thwarted by the Lady of the Lake, Arthur’s guardian, she murders her husband Vortigern and offers Arthur the crown along with herself. Arthur, horrified at her crime, burns Rowena and her castle to the ground.

From Swedish rullgardin meaning "roller blind, roll-down curtain". This is one of the middle names of Pippi Långstrump (English: Pippi Longstocking), full name Pippilotta Viktualia Rullgardina Krusmynta Efraimsdotter Långstrump, a character invented by Swedish author Astrid Lindgren.

From the Roman agnomen or cognomen Rullianus, which was derived from the nomen gentile Rullius.A known bearer of this name was Quintus Fabius Maximus Rullianus, a Roman consul from the 3rd century BC.
From the obscure Roman nomen gentile Rullius, which was ultimately derived from the cognomen Rullus.

From the Roman cognomen Rullus, which was derived from Latin rullus meaning "rustic" as well as "boorish, uncultured" and (in some cases) "beggar".A known bearer of this name was Publius Servilius Rullus, a Roman tribune of the people who lived in the 1st century BC.
Variant of Roelof. This name is slightly more common as a patronymic surname.

Etymology unknown. This was the birth name of Chukchi poet and writer Antonina Kymytval.

column3: 琉真, 瑠牧, 瑠真, 瑠麻, 留摩, 留萌, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|रूमा(Sanskrit)|রুমা(Bengali)|ৰুমা(Assamese)
