Other kanji combinations are possible.
Alternate transcription of Arabic رميصاء (see Rumaysa).
Alternate transcription of Arabic رميصاء (see Rumaysa).

A girl's name that was first seen in the U.S. baby name data in 2023, making it a debut name that year, with 88 baby girls receiving the name in the United States, possibly influenced by the Indian actress, Roomani Khare, or by the character Rumani from the South Korean video game "Goddess of Victory: Nikke!" Rumani can be an alternative spelling for the European county, Romania, or for the nomadic Romani people. It is the Hebrew variation for an area on the coast of Egypt, and it shares similar sounds and qualities to Indian names such as Ramana, Roomani, and Rukmini, to the Japanese name, Runami, and to the Bulgarian Rumiana and the Arabic name Rumaan.
Corsican and Sicilian form of Romanus.

Diminutive of Arabic رمص (ramaṣ) meaning "rheum, sleep in the eye", used as an Arabic name for the star Sirius. Al-Rumaysa bint Milhan, also known as Umm Sulaym, was a companion of the Prophet Muhammad.
Alternate transcription of Arabic رميصاء (see Rumaysa).
Of unknown meaning. This was the name of two Emirs of Mecca.

From rumble (v.). Slang noun meaning "gang fight" is from 1946. Meaning "backmost part of a carriage" is from 1808 (earlier rumbler, 1801), probably from the effect of sitting over the wheels; hence rumble seat (1828).

Means "bold fame" from the Germanic elements "hrom", meaning "fame" and "bald", meaning "bold". This is the name of a Hiberno-Scottish saint from around 8th century, though his nationality is unknown.

The name of two medieval German minstrels. It can be analysed as a dithematic name with the name elements hruom "fame" and lant "land".The name is sometimes interpreted as Räum das Land "Leave the land" alluding to touring lifestyle of a minstrel.
Transferred use of the surname Rumer.
Old Norse byname, from Old Norse rúmfari meaning "one who makes voyages to Rome".

Means "from Rūm" in Arabic. A toponymic surname of 13th-century Persian poet Jalāl al-Dīn Muḥammad Rūmī, simply known as Rūmī. Rumi Carter, Beyoncé Knowles' second-born daughter is said to be named after the poet.

Possibly derived from the name of the mountain Rumija in southern Montenegro, situated between the Adriatic and Lake Skadar. The "Cross of Jovan Vladimir" is carried every year during August on the Feast of Pentecost from the village of Velji Mikulići to the summit of Rumija.

The first element of this name is probably derived from the Serbo-Croatian noun Rus meaning "Russian". The Russians themselves derived their name from (Old) Russian rusij or rusiy, which refers to a light hair colour (often blonde; some sources also say light-brown) and could be understood to mean "fair-haired" or "fair-headed". There are sources that claim that rusiy means "red-headed" and is itself derived from Old Church Slavonic rudŭ "red", but it is doubtful how correct that is, since that meaning would imply that the Russians were mostly red-haired people, while red hair is mostly a Germanic trait and not a Slavic one: Slavic peoples were mostly fair-haired. Also, still other theories exist about the etymology of the name of the Russian people: a derivation from Finnish, Greek or Persian are also among the possibilities. I will not list them all here, but suffice it to say that the ultimate etymology of the ethnonym is uncertain and disputed. Lastly, the second element of this name is derived from either Slavic mir "peace" or Slavic mer "great, famous".

column12: From Japanese 良 (ryō) meaning "good" or 亮 (ryō) meaning "clear" combined with 貴 (taka) meaning "valuable" or 孝 (taka) meaning "filial piety". Other kanji combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 了衛, 了恵, 亮衛, 良衛, 良枝, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 了 (ryou) meaning "end" combined with 衛 (e) meaning "defense, protection". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 凌羽, 凌波, 陵羽, 蓼坡, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 凌 (ryou) meaning "ice" combined with 羽 (ha) meaning "feathers". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column12: From Japanese 涼 (ryou) meaning "cool breeze, cool air", 冷 (ryou) meaning "cool" or 良 (ryou) meaning "good, pleasing, skilled" combined with 美 (mi) meaning "beautiful" or 水 (mi) meaning "water". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 亮之助, 亮之輔, 鐐之助, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 亮 (ryou) meaning "cool, refreshing", 之 (no), a possessive marker, combined with 助 (suke) meaning "assistance". Other kanji combinations are also possible.

Other kanji combinations are possible.

Other kanji combinations are possible.

Likely a Yiddish variant of Grace.

竜大, 龍大, 隆大, 琉大, 瑠大, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 竜 or 龍 (ryu) meaning "dragon" and 大 (dai) meaning "big, large, great". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 柳波, 竜羽(Japanese Kanji)|りゅうは(Japanese Hiragana)|リュウハ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 柳 (ryū, yanagi) meaning "willow", 竜, 龍 (ryū) meaning "dragon", or 隆 (ryū) meaning "noble, prosperous" combined with 波 (ha, nami) meaning "wave" or 羽 (ha) meaning "feather". Other kanji or kanji combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 隆平, 竜平, 龍平, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|りゅうへい(Japanese Hiragana)|リュウウヘイ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 隆 (ryū) meaning "noble, prosperous" or 竜/龍 (ryū) meaning "dragon" combined with 平 (hei) meaning "level, even, peaceful". Other kanji combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 琉彦, 竜日子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: Ryuhiko is a compound of Japanese 竜 or 龍 (ryu) meaning "dragon" and combined with 彦 (hiko) meaning "boy, prince". Other kanji combinations can make up this name.

column3: 竜仁, 龍仁, 流仁, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 竜 or 龍 (ryū) meaning "imperial, dragon" combined with 仁 (hito) meaning "benevolence". Other combinations of characters can form this name.

column3: 隆一, 龍一, 竜一, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|りゅういち(Japanese Hiragana)|リュウイチ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 隆 (ryū) meaning "noble, prosperous" or 龍/竜 (ryū) meaning "dragon" combined with 一 (ichi) meaning "one". This name can be formed from other combinations of kanji as well.

column3: 隆一, 龍一, 竜一, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|りゅういち(Japanese Hiragana)|リュウイチ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Alternate transcription of Japanese Kanji 隆一 or 龍一 or 竜一 (see Ryūichi).
A famous bearier of this name Shin Ryujin from ITZY.

column3: 竜二郎, 龍司郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 隆 (ryū) meaning "noble, prosperous", 二 (ji) meaning "two" or 司 (ji) meaning "officer, boss", and 郎 (rō) meaning "son". This name can also be formed using other kanji combinations.
Ryuk is a fictional character in the manga series Death Note, created by Tsugumi Ohba and Takeshi Obata.

column3: 竜希, 龍希, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
龍子, 竜子, 流子, 柳子, 龍虎, 竜虎, 龍乎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|りゅう子(Kanji/Hiragana)|りゅうこ(Japanese Hiragana)|リュウコ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Ryū combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child." The combination 龍虎/竜虎, literally meaning "dragon and tiger" and extended to refer to two mighty rivals, is sometimes used (though exclusively for boys) as is the case for actor Ryūko Isogai (磯貝 龍乎) (1987-), who was born with the given name 龍虎.

column3: 龍光, 竜光, 榴岡, 柳虹(Japanese Kanji)|りゅうこう(Japanese Hiragana)|リュウコウ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name can be used as 龍光 or 竜光 with 龍 (ryuu, ryou, rou, tatsu) meaning "dragon, imperial," 竜 (ryuu, ryou, rou, ise, tatsu) with the same meaning as 龍 and 光 (kou, hikari, hika.ru) meaning "light, ray."Bearers of this name include Neo-Confucian scholar Hayashi Ryūkō (林 榴岡) (1681-1758), whose true name is Nobumitsu (信充), and poet & literary critic Ryūkō Kawaji (川路 柳虹) (1888-1959), used as the pen-name of Makoto Kawaji (川路 誠). In their cases, their kanji are, in order, 榴 (ryuu, ryou, ru, zakuro), an outdated kanji meaning "pomegranate," 岡 (kou, oka) meaning "hill, knoll, mount," 柳 (ryuu, yanagi) meaning "willow" and 虹 (kou, niji) meaning "rainbow."This name is rarely given to boys, if given at all.Ryūkō is also used as a surname.
From 류리 meaning "glass" in North Korea.

column3: 류상(Korean Hangul)|柳霜, 柳尚, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 柳 (ryu) meaning "willow" combined with 霜 (sang) meaning "frost" or 尚 (sang) meaning "still, yet". This name can be formed using other hanja combinations as well.This is the Korean reading of the Chinese name Liushuang/Liu-tsong. Liushuang/Liu-tsong was the Chinese given name of Chinese-American actress Anna May Wong, whose Chinese name was Wong Liu-tsong/Huang Liushuang (黄 柳霜, Huáng Liǔshuāng).

column3: 流星, 流成, 流生, 流聖, 琉成, 琉星, 琉生, 琉聖, 竜聖, 竜生, 竜星, 竜成, 隆星, 隆生, 隆聖, 隆成(Japanese Kanji)|りゅうせい(Japanese Hiragana)|リュウセイ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name combines 流 (ryuu, ru, naga.su, -naga.su, naga.re, naga.reru) meaning "a sink, current, flow, forfeit", 琉 (ryuu, ru) meaning "gem, lapis lazuli, precious stone", 竜 (ryuu, ryou, rou, ise, tatsu) meaning "dragon, imperial" or 隆 (ryuu) meaning "high, hump, noble, prosperity" with 星 (shou, sei, hoshi, -boshi) meaning "dot, mark, spot, star", 成 (jou, sei, na.su, -na.su, na.ru) meaning "become, elapse, get, grow, reach, turn into", 生 (shou, sei, i.kiru, u.mare, o.u, ki) meaning "birth, genuine, life" or 聖 (shou, sei, hijiri) meaning "holy, master, priest, sage, saint."As a word, Ryūsei (流星) is used to refer to a meteor or a falling star.

column3: 隆太, 竜太, 龍太, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 隆 (ryuu) meaning "noble, prosperous" and 太 (ta) meaning "thick, big".

リュウ タロウ(Japanese Katakana)|りゅうたろう(Japanese Hiragana)|龍太郎, 隆太郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 龍 (ryū) meaning "dragon", 太 (ta) meaning "big, thick" and 郎 (rō) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations can form this name.

column3: 流斗, 琉斗, 隆斗, 竜斗, 龍斗, 竜翔, 龍翔, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 流 (ryuu) meaning "style", 琉 (ryuu) meaning "lapis lazuli", 隆 (ryuu) meaning "noble, prosperous" or 竜, 龍 (ryuu) meaning "dragon" combined with 斗 (to), which refers to a Chinese constellation or 翔 (to) meaning "soar, fly". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: りゅつき(Japanese Hiragana)|琉月, 流月, 龍月, 竜月, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: Ryu means 竜 (ryu) meaning "dragon" and 月 (tsuki) meaning "moon, month". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column12: From Japanese 竜, 龍 (ryuu) meaning "dragon" combined with 真 (ma) meaning "real, genuine". column3: 竜介, 龍介, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 竜, 龍 (ryuu) meaning "dragon" combined with 介 (suke) meaning "forerunner, herald". Other kanji combinations are also possible.

Saba: While not a standalone dictionary word in Nepali, “Saba” appears frequently in feminine names and poetic expressions. It carries a soft, elegant tone and is used symbolically in name construction.Barna (वर्ण): Derived from Sanskrit and used in Nepali as well, "Barna" can mean form, essence, or identity. In name formation, it often symbolizes the nature or being of the individual.Oceanic reference: The interpretation “daughter of the ocean” emerges from traditional Nepali naming styles similar to names like Sagarika (सागरिका), which also symbolizes a feminine connection to water or the sea. Though “Sabarna” is not a literal translation, it follows this metaphorical tradition common in South Asian spiritual or poetic naming.

Hellenized form of the Hebrew noun shabbat, which is the name of the Hebrew day of rest. Shabbat (sabbath in English) means "rest" or "cessation", having ultimately been derived from the Hebrew verb shavat "to repose, to rest, to cease". Also, please do not confuse Sabbatios for being the hellenized form of the Hebrew name Shabbatai, because the proper hellenized form of that name is Sabbataios.

Latinized form of Sabbatios. This is the name of several saints, including Saint Sabbatius of Solovki (15th century AD). This was also one of the middle names of the Byzantine Emperor Justinian the Great (6th century AD).
Italian form of Sabbatios via Sabbatius.
Perhaps a feminine form of Sabbas. This was one of the three names of the Persian Sybil presiding over the Apollonian Oracle, also known as the Hebrew, Egyptian, and Babylonian Sybil.
filipino name desends from english name becky
Alternate transcription of Arabic سبيل (see Sabil).
Alternate transcription of Burmese စံပယ် (see Sabai).

Medieval English and Judeo-Anglo-Norman diminutive of Sabina as well as a Judeo-Anglo-Norman feminine form of Sabelin. The name also coincides with a medieval Latin word meaning "sable", derived from Latin sabellum.
Medieval Italian diminutive of Sabella, as -uccia is an Italian feminine diminutive suffix.This name can also be a short form of Isabelluccia in some cases.
From the English word saber (British English sabre), denoting a type of backsword with a curved blade. It is the name of a reoccurring character in the popular Fate visual novel and anime series.
Short form of Elisabeth. Max Frisch used this name on one of his characters in the novel "Homo Faber" (published in English in 1959).
Alternate transcription of Arabic صابر (see Sabir), chiefly used in Tunisia
"A West Connacht variant of Sadhbh." It was usually Anglicized as Sally.
Perhaps an Irish spelling variant of the name Savannah.
Diminutive of Sabina, Sabine and Sabrina.

Possibly an altered form of Sabina or a derivative of the Arabic name Sabiya.Notable bearers of this name include the medieval Georgian saint Sabiana of Samtskhe (10-11th century) and the Haitian judoka Sabiana Anestor (1994-), who competed in the 2020 Summer Olympics.

A maiden loved by Gerhart of Riviers.When her father, Tjofabier, refused to grant her to Gerhart, Gerhart launched a war, slaying Gilbert, the brother of Sabie. The war was ended by Arthur’s Sir Garel, who defeated Gerhart.
From the Arabic صَبِيحَة (ṣabīḥa) meaning "morning" or صَبِيح‎ (ṣabīḥ) meaning "handsome, beautiful, pretty".
Dutch form of both Sabinus and Sabina. However, in modern times, this name is found almost exclusively on females in The Netherlands. Usage of the name on males occurred mostly in archaic times.
Allegedly means "past" in Arabic. This is the name of the consort of Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifah, the king of Bahrain.
Alternate transcription of Arabic سبيلة (see Sabila), as well as an Indonesian variant.
Americanized variant of Sibylla or Sybilla.
A knight who performed well in a tournament thrown by King Brandegorre of Estrangorre, and he were the second of the twelve knights who swore fealty to Brandegorre’s daughter.
Icelandic and Slovak form of Sabina.
German diminutive of Sabine. Rarely, if ever, used as an official given name.It is the name of the tragic title hero of the German folk-like song 'Sabinchen war ein Frauenzimmer'.
Basque form of Sabina and Sabine.
Diminutive of Sabine, as it contains the Dutch diminutive suffix -ke.This name is almost exclusively used informally, meaning that it is extremely rare as an official name on birth certificates.
English and Polish form of Sabinianus. This name was borne by a pope and by a saint.
Galician, Italian, Spanish and Portuguese form of Sabinian.

Roman cognomen which was derived from Sabinus (see Sabina). This name was borne by several Romans, such as the Roman usurper Sabinianus (3rd century AD) and Flavius Sabinianus, a consul of the Eastern Roman Empire from the 6th century AD.
Feminine form of Sabinillus. Sabinilla was one of the Vestal Virgins.
From Bashkir сабыр (sabïr) meaning "patience, patient" and feminine name element бикә (bikä).
From Arabic صابرين (ṣābirīn), the plural of صابر (ṣābir) meaning "patient, steadfast, enduring".
Alternate transcription of Kazakh Сабыржан (see Sabyrzhan).
Arabic alternate transcription of Thabit as well as the form used in various languages.
Bengali, Odia, Assamese and Nepali form of Savita.
Means "beautiful sunshine" in many Indian languages.
Odia, Bengali, Assamese and Nepali form of Savitri.
Old Swedish variant form of Sæbiǫrn.
Sabline is the French name for a genus of flowering plants (Arenaria, sandwort).
Derived from Uzbek sabo meaning "morning breeze" and gul meaning "rose, flower".
Means "dawn, early morning" or "hope, bright spot" in Uzbek.
Means "patience of the religion" from Arabic صبر (ṣabr) meaning "patience, forbearance, perseverance" combined with دين (dīn) meaning "religion, faith".
Sabrael is a male angel of hebrew origin.

This name is the named of several Berethnet queens in Samantha Shannon's book ''The Priory of the Orange Tree'', most notably Sabran IX, one of the main characters of the book.According to Samantha Shannon, the name comes from a version of Saint George's legend, written by the Elizabethan writer Richard Johnson, in which the princess he saves is called Sabra. Where the author of that tale got the name from is unknown, though there is a theory that it comes from the Arabic word sabr (صبر), meaning ''endurance, patience''. In his version, Sabra is Egyptian, and she suffers quite a lot, so the meaning would make sense. Samantha Shannon, however, doubts this, saying that she doesn't ''believe for a minute he had the necessary awareness or sensitivity to choose an appropriate name in Arabic''.In the world of the Priory of the Orange Tree, Sabran Berethnet and her ancestors are named after the sabra flower, which is the most beautiful flower of the south. No one quite knows where that name came from.
African, Islamic name for boys meaning patient, sharp and enduring.
Means "patient", from Arabic صَبْر‎ (ṣabr) "patience; perseverance, endurance" (compare Sabri).
The name Sabria may be a simplification of the Arabic name Sabriyya "patient" of a short form of Sabrina.In German speaking countries it is pronounced with a /z/ initally.

There are multiple explanations for the etymology of this name. One is that it is a variant form of Sabrael. An other is that it is derived from Hebrew sabi "stop, rest" combined with el "God", thus meaning "(the) rest of God". Lastly, it could also have been derived from the name of the Sabra plant (a prickly pear) combined with el "God", making the meaning something like "cactus of God". The name of Sabriel was first used by author Garth Nix for the heroine of his fantasy novel 'Sabriel' (1995), and an important protagonist in the sequels 'Lirael' and 'Abhorsen'. It is uncertain where and how Garth Nix decided upon using the name Sabriel.
Means "patience" in Arabic, derived from Arabic صَبَرَ (ṣabara) meaning "to be patient, to have patience".
Alternate transcription of Arabic صبري (see Sabri).
Variant of Sabrina. This name is born by Sabrynaah Pope (1959-2005) a music vocalist.
Sabtah was a son of Cush according to Genesis 10:7, 1 Chronicles 1:9.
Sabtechah was a son of Cush according to Genesis 10:7, 1 Chronicles 1:9.
From Malay saptu meaning "Saturday", referring to someone that was born on Saturday.
From Arabic صبح (subh) meaning "morning, dawn". This was the pen name of Mirza Fatali Akhundov, a 19th-century Azerbaijani author and playwright.
Means "daughter of Shapur" in Middle Persian.
Diminutive of Saba 1, as it contains the Georgian diminutive suffix -უნა (-una).

column3: 三郎太, 三朗太(Japanese Kanji)|さぶろうた(Japanese Hiragana)|サブロウタ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name combines 三 (san, zou, mi, mi'.tsu, mi.tsu) meaning "three" & 郎 (ryou, rou, otoko) meaning "son" or 朗 (rou, aki.raka, hoga.raka) meaning "bright, cheerful, clear, melodious, serene" with 太 (ta, tai, futo.i, futo.ru) meaning "big around, plump, thick."This name is very rarely given to boys, if given at all.

Sabus is a character in the mythology of the Sabines of Italy, the son of the god Sancus (called by some Jupiter Fidius). According to Cato, writing in his work Origines, the Sabines took their name from his.
This name means “A lovely young lady”.
Bengali and Odia form of Savyasachi.
Kyrgyz and Kazakh form of Sabir.
Combination of Sabir and the Turkish military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".
From Kazakh сабыр (sabyr) meaning "patience, forbearance, endurance" (of Arabic origin) and жан (zhan) meaning "soul" (of Persian origin).
Derived from the Uzbek sabza meaning "green growth, verdant" and the given name Ali 1.
From Uzbek sabza meaning "verdant" and bahor meaning "spring".
Derived from Uzbek sabza meaning "verdant" and gul meaning "rose, flower".
Derived from Persian سبزی (sabzi) meaning "leafy, green vegetable".
From Sino-Vietnamese 色 (sắc) meaning "colour, tint, hue, beauty".
From the English word saccharine meaning "excessively sweet".
Roman cognomen which was derived from the Latin noun sacerdos meaning "priest, priestess, cleric".This name was borne by several early medieval saints.
In the Aeneid, Saces is a messenger who informs Turnus of the state of Latium.
From Sino-Vietnamese 索 (sách) meaning "rope" or "to search" or 策 (sách) meaning "plan, scheme, tactic".
Sanskrit MEANING - Worshipping, attached to, worshipperSource- Monier Williams Sanskrit-English dictionary Hindi MEANING - "Truth"

Derived from the Hebrew verb שָׂכַר (sakhar) meaning "to hire". Sachar or Sacar was the name of two individuals mentioned in the Old Testament.
Based on Latin sacharum "sugar". This name was invented by poet Edmund Waller (1606-1687), who used it as a nickname for Lady Dorothy Sidney, countess of Sunderland.
MEANING - beautiful, lovely, handsomeSource - Monier Williams Sanskrit -English dictionary
Means "jungle flower" in Quechua, from sacha, "jungle" and sisa, "flower".

In the case of the American actress and activist Sacheen Littlefeather (born Maria Louise Cruz; 1946-2022), who adopted it as her stage name, she claimed it means "little bear" in Navajo. The initial syllable resembles the Navajo word shash meaning "bear".
From Japanese kanji 幸 (sachi) meaning "happiness; good luck".

column3: 幸亜, 幸愛, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 幸 (sachi) meaning "happiness" combined with 亜 (a) meaning "second, Asia" or 愛 (a) meaning "love, affection". Other kanji combinations are possible.
A combination of the Japanese name Sachiko and the English name Ann.

column12: From 祥 (sachi) meaning means "happiness, fortune, good omen, auspiciousness" and 江 (e) meaning "bay, inlet". Other kanji combinations can be used.

From Japanese kanji 幸 (sachi) meaning "happiness; good luck", and "day's child".

column12: From 幸 (sachi) meaning "happiness, good luck" and 桜 (o) meaning "cherry (blossom) tree" or 雄 (o) meaning "male". This name can be formed with other kanji combinations as well.

column3: 倖月(Japanese Kanji)|さちし(Japanese Hiragana)|サチシ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 倖 (sachi) meaning "happiness, luck" combined with 月 (shi) meaning "moon"
From Sanskrit सत्य (satyá) meaning "real, true, honest" and चित्र (citrá) meaning "bright, visible, clear".

column3: さちと(Japanese Hiragana)|幸人, 祐人, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 幸 (sachi) meaning "happiness" combined with 人 (to) meaning "person". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Japanese 祥 (sachi) meaning "good luck, good omen, auspicious, propitious" combined with 知 (tomo) meaning "wisdom". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: さちよ(Japanese Hiragana)|サチ代(Kanji/Katakana)|祥美, 倖代, 幸世, 幸夜, 幸葉, 早千予, 佐智代, 沙智葉, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

Old High German cognate of Sasso and Saxi.
From the Turkmen saç meaning "hair", ultimately meaning "long haired, having lots of hair".
From the English word sacred, meaning "made holy" or "solemn in a religious way".

Created from the first syllables of the surnames Sacco and Vanzetti, after the wrongfully executed Italian-American anarchists Nicola Sacco and Bartolomeo Vanzetti. A notable namesake is the Canadian americanist Sacvan Bercovitch.

Means "fortune of the religion" from Arabic سعد (saʿd) meaning "fortune, good luck" combined with دين (dīn) meaning "religion, faith".

column3: 貞文, 定記, 禎史, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 禎 (sada) meaning "auspicious, divine grace, straight" or 定 (sada) meaning "determine, establish, decide" and 記 (fumi) meaning "statement, inscription, mention, describe, mark, Kojiki". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 貞治, 定治(Japanese Kanji)|さだはる(Japanese Hiragana)

column3: 貞彦, 定彦, 禎彦, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|さだひこ(Japanese Hiragana)|サダヒコ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 貞 (sada) meaning "virtuous, chaste, loyal", 定 (sada) meaning "determine, fix, establish, decide" or 禎 (sada) meaning "auspicious, blessed, good fortune, happiness" combined with 彦 (hiko) meaning "boy, prince". Other combinations of kanji can form this name as well.

column3: 定大, 定裕, 貞裕, 貞大, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 定 (sada) meaning "determine, establish, decide" or 貞 (sada) meaning "virtue, faithfulness, chastity" combined with 裕 (hiro) meaning "abundant", or 大 (hiro) meaning "big, great". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 貞次, 定次, 禎路, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 禎 (sada) meaning "auspicious, divine grace, straight" or 定 (sada) meaning "determine, establish, decide" and 二 (ji) meaning "two". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 定吉, 貞吉, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|さだきち(Japanese Hiragana)|サダキチ(Japanese Katakana)

column3: さだきよ(Japanese Hiragana)|サダキヨ(Japanese Katakana)|定清, 禎浄, 貞聖, 節淨, 憲潔, 質精, 清雪, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

Saint Sadalberga(c. 605 – c. 670) was the daughter of Gundoin, Duke of Alsace and his wife Saretrude. Sadalberga founded the Abbey of St John at Laon. She is the subject of a short hagiography, the Vita Sadalbergae.
Alternate transcription of Arabic سعد الدين (see Sa'd ad-Din).
A fashionable Knight of the Round Table slain during the Grail Quest.
Alternate transcription of Arabic/Urdu صدام (see Saddam), as well as the Indonesian form.

column12: From Japanese 定 (sada) meaning "determine, establish, decide" or 貞 (sada) meaning "virtue, faithfulness, chastity" combined with 信 (nobu) meaning "trust", 誠 (nobu) meaning "sincerity" or 延 (nobu) meaning "prolong, stretch". Other kanji combinations can form this name as well.

Of uncertain etymology, Sadarnunna was a minor Sumerian goddess, considered to be the wife of Nuska. Nuska was a "sukkal" (vizier deity) for the god Ea.

Means "ever-auspicious, always kind" in Sanskrit, from सदा (sadā) meaning "always, ever" combined with शिव (śiva) meaning "benign, kind, auspicious". This is another name of the Hindu god Shiva. In Shaiva Siddhanta tradition Sadashiva is considered Shiva's highest form.
Tamil and Malayalam form of Sadashiva.

column3: 節太, 定孝, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 節 (sada) meaning "season" and 太 (taka) meaning "big, great, thick". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column12: From 定 (sada) meaning "determine, fix, establish, decide" combined with 晃 (teru) meaning "clear". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column12: From 禎 (sada) meaning "auspicious, divine grace, straight" or 定 (sada) meaning "determine, establish, decide" and 次 (tsugu) meaning "second, next". Other kanji combinations can be used.
From the Hausa sā̀du meaning "get together”.

column3: さだやす(Japanese Hiragana)|サダヤス(Japanese Katakana)|定安, 禎靖, 貞裕, 節穏, 憲泰, 質安, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 質 (sada) meaning "characteristic, content, confirm" combined with 休 (yasu) meaning "vacation, rest". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column12: From 貞 (sada) meaning "chastity, righteousness, virtue, faithfulness" and 偉 (yori) meaning "admirable". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column12: From 貞 (sada) meaning "chastity, virtue" and 幸 (yuki) meaning "happiness, luck, favour". Other kanji combinations can be used.
Short form of Folasade. It was popularized in the mid-80s due to the Nigerian-born British singer Sade Adu (born Helen Folasade Adu, 1959-) and her eponymous smooth jazz band Sade.

Derived from the Arabic masculine name Sa'di and poshsha , an endearing term for a girl or woman.

Spanish, Italian and Catalan form of Zadok.
Cousin of Guinevere and brother of Guiomar.
Greek and Belarusian form of Zadok.

Sador is the Coptic Christian (Ge'ez) word for the piercing on Jesus' ribs by the lancet. Adding an "a" at the end feminizes it.It may also be a shortening of Isadora.
Alternate transcription of Arabic سعدون (see Sadun).
From arabic صَدْر (ṣadr), meaning "chest, front, leader". Sadr is also used as a title in Iran to refer to a notable person, such as a scholar.
Proto-Germanic sadaz "full, sated", related to Latin satis "sufficiently, adequately" + Old High German bald "bold".
Proto-Germanic sadaz "full, sated", related to Latin satis "sufficiently, adequately" + Old High German heri "host, army".
Means "front/leader of the religion" in Arabic.
Uzbek and Tajik form of Sadr al-Din.
Proto-Germanic sadaz "full, sated", related to Latin satis "sufficiently, adequately" + Old High German hiltja "battle".
Derived from the Arabic root "sadr" meaning "chest (of men)" or "leader". So the full meaning of this name, Ṣadr ud-Dīn, is "leader of the religion".
Derived from Arabic سَعَادَة (saʿāda) meaning "happiness, happy" and قَصَّاص (qaṣṣāṣ) "narrator, storyteller".
Means "happiness of Allah", from Arabic سَعِيد (saʿīd) "happy, cheerful, joyous" combined with Allah.
Alternate transcription of Arabic سعدون (see Sadun).
Means "happy, joyful, fortunate" in Arabic, from the word سعد (saʿd) meaning "fortune, good luck".
Variant form of Sadwrn. This name was borne by a Welsh saint from the 6th century AD.
Meaning unknown. Sadwes was the Ancient Persian goddess of rain, hail, thunder, lightning and storms.
Variant form of Sadwen. A known bearer of this name is Sadwyn Brophy (b. 1996), a New Zealand actor.
Derived from Arabic صَدْر (ṣadr) meaning "centre, front, head, leader". A notable bearer is Sadyr Japarov (1968-), the current president of Kyrgyzstan.

column3: 冴, 小恵, 小枝, 左恵, 佐栄, 紗英, 沙恵, 紗江, 三重, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|さえ, さゑ(Japanese Hiragana)|サエ, サヱ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From 冴え (sae) meaning "clarity; skilfulness," also written with a combination of a sa kanji, like 小 meaning "small," 左 meaning "left," 佐 meaning "help," 紗 meaning "gauze," 沙 meaning "sand" or 三 meaning "three," and an e kanji, like 恵 meaning "wisdom," 枝 meaning "branch, bough," 栄 meaning "glory, prosperity," 英 meaning "wisdom, brilliance," 江 meaning "inlet, bay" or 重 meaning "fold, layer."Female bearers of this name include actress Sae Isshiki (一色 紗英), born Sae Hatakeyama (畠山 紗英) (1977-), professional shōgi player Sae Itō (伊藤 沙恵) (1993-) and artistic gymnast Sae Miyakawa (宮川 紗江) (1999-).
It is a very feminine name associated with beauty and grace. It translates to "river" in Hebrew, and it is not commonly recognized today but it is a beautiful name.
Derived from the elements sæ "sea" and beorht "bright" meaning "bright sea". Used by the first Christian East Saxon king. Original form of Seabert.
From the elements sæ "sea" and beorn "bear, warrior" meaning "sea bear" or "sea warrior" cognate of Sǽbiǫrn. The surname Seaborn is derived from the name.

Saebie seems to appear in only a few old documents and census records from the 1800s and early 1900s, mainly in the US, some in Australia. Quite a few of those bearers had Dutch or Frisian last names and relatives with Dutch and Frisian given names.While I couldn't find Saebie as a Dutch or Frisian given name in its own right, there is an old (East) Frisian feminine name Saebina which was recorded in (East) Frisia in the 1800s.Saebina was coined as a feminine form of Saebe and Saeben, which themselves are variants of Sebe and Seben.
From Bit prefixed with determiner 새 (sae) meaning "new."
Ancient Scandinavian, Norwegian and Faroese combination of sær "sea" and bjǫrg "help, deliverance".
Norwegian and Faroese younger form of Sǽbiǫrn.
Means "bright sea", derived from the Old Norse elements sær meaning "sea" and bjǫrt meaning "bright, shining" (from bjartr).
From Bom prefixed with determiner 새 (sae) meaning "new."
Derived from the Old Norse elements sær "sea" and brá "eyelash".
From native Korean 새벽 (saebyeok) meaning "dawn, daybreak," from earlier 새배 (saebae).
Variant transcription of Saetbyeol or Saebyeol.
Earlier form of Saetbyeol, a combination of 새 (sae), a seaman's term for the east wind, and Byeol.
Alternate transcription of Arabic and Persian سعيد (see Said).

column3: 小枝(Japanese Kanji)|さえだ, さゑだ(Japanese Hiragana)|サエダ, サヱダ(Japanese Katakana)

column12: Icelandic name meaning "sea goddess", formed from the Old Norse elements sæ "sea" and dís "goddess". The suffix dís is fairly common in Icelandic names.
Faroese and Norwegian form of Sædís.
From 새 (sae) meaning "new," and 都 "elegant, refined".
Derived from the Old English elements sæ "sea, ocean" and faru "journey", making it an Old English cognate of Sǽfari.
Derived from Old Norse sær "sea" and finnr "Sámi, person from Finland".
Derived from the Old English elements sæ "sea" and flæd, possibly meaning "beauty".
Derived from the Old Norse elements sær "sea" and fríðr "beautiful, beloved".
Original form of Segar derived from the elements sæ "sea" and gar "spear" meaning "sea spear". The surname Sagar is derived from the name. Cognate of Sǽgæirr.
Means "sea gift", from the Old English elements sæ "sea" and giefu "gift".
Derived from the Old English elements sæ "sea" and guð "battle".
From Korean 새해 (saehae) meaning "new year," a combination of determiner 새 (sae) meaning "new" and 해 (hae) meaning "sun."
From Han-byeol prefixed with determiner 새 (sae) meaning "new."
From Sino-Korean 世 "generation; world; era" and 姬 "beauty" or 熙 "bright, splendid, glorious".
Derived from the Old English elements sæ "sea, lake" and hild "battle".
From Him prefixed with determiner 새 (sae) meaning "new."
From Japanese 沙 (sa) meaning "sand", 絵 (e) meaning "picture, painting, drawing, sketch" combined with 穂 (ho) meaning "ear of grain". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Meaning unknown. In Norse mythology this is the name of a boar which provides food for Valhalla.

column3: さえか(Japanese Hiragana)|サヱカ(Japanese Katakana)|さえ香(Kanji/Hiragana)|映香, 佐恵佳, 沙栄香, 沙英香, 沙恵香, 彩佳, 彩花, 冴可, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 映 (sae) meaning "a reflection; to reflect" combined with 香 (ka) meaning "fragrance". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 冴希, 彩樹, 彩木(Japanese Kanji)|さえき(Japanese Hiragana)|サエキ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name can be used as 冴希, 彩樹 or 彩木 with 冴 (go, ko, sa.eru, koo.ru, hi.eru) meaning "be clear, serene, cold, skilful", 彩 (sai, irodo.ru, sae) meaning "coloring, paint, makeup", 樹 (ju, ki) meaning "timber trees, wood" and 木 (boku, moku, ki, ko-) meaning "tree, wood."This name is rarely given to girls, if given at all.Saeki is also used as a surname and a place name.

column3: 彩子, 冴子, 紗子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: This name can be spelled with 冴 (go, ko, sa.eru, koo.ru, hi.eru) meaning "be clear, serene, cold, skillful" or 彩 (sai, irodo.ru, sae) meaning "coloring, paint" combined with 子 (ko, shi, ne) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations can be used.
A newly created name, formed from the first two letters of the names of the parents Sanne and Eljero.
Could be taken directly from the Icelandic word sæla, meaning "happiness, bliss", or be a short form of names such as Sælaug. Officially approved as a given name in 2015.
Derived from the Old Norse elements sær meaning "sea" and laug possibly meaning "vowed, promised, bound in oath".
From Korean 새(sae) meaning "new" and "bird" combined with hanja 隣(lin) meaning "neighbor" or 粼(lin) meaning "clear water".
Means "having a wise heart" from Sindarin sael "wise" and ind "inner thought, mind, meaning, heart". This was an epessë or epithet of Andreth in J. R. R. Tolkien's legendarium.
Derived from the Old English elements sæ "sea" and lufu "love" (related to leof).
From the Old English elements sæl 'happiness', and wig 'battle'.
Combination of the phonetic element sae with the popular name suffix lynn, likely inspired names like Jaelynn, Kaelynn or Raelynn.
From native Korean 샘 (saem) meaning "spring, fountain," also used to transliterate the name Sam 1.
Derived from the Old Norse elements sær "sea" and maðr "person, man" (genitive manns).
Derived from the Old Norse elements sær "sea" and mærr "famous, illustrious, known".

column3: さえみ(Japanese Hiragana)|さえ美, さえ実(Kanji/Hiragana)|佐英美, 佐英実, 佐江実, 左英見, 沙絵美, 彩笑, 皐笑, 紗恵美, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 佐 (sa) meaning "aid, help", 英 (e) meaning "English" combined with 美 (mi) meaning "beautiful". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Derived from Albanian sa "so; how (much)", the particle e and mirë "good".
From the native Korean 샘 (saem) meaning "spring, fountain" and Sino-Korean 那 (na) meaning "that", 奈 (na) meaning "how, why", or, 娜 (na) meaning "beautiful, graceful".

column3: 左衛門(Japanese Kanji)|左エ門, 左ヱ門(Kanji/Katakana)|さえもん(Japanese Hiragana)|サエモン(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Derived from 左衛門府 (Saemonfu), referring to a governmental department responsible for guarding, opening and closing the left gate to the royal palace. The name was classified as a hyakkanna (百官名), a court rank-style name that samurai used to announce oneself and give himself authority.
Norwegian and Old Swedish form of Sæmundr.
Derived from Old Norse sær "sea" and mundr "protection".

column3: 紗笑奈, 冴奈, 彩奈, 彩菜, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|さえな(Japanese Hiragana)|새나(Korean Hangul)
column12: From Japanese 紗 (sa) meaning "gauze, thin silk", 笑 (e) meaning "to laugh; laughter" combined with 奈 (na) meaning "apple tree". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From native Korean 새날 (saenal) meaning "new day; new age/era," a combination of determiner 새 (sae) meaning "new" and 날 (nal) meaning "day, time."
From Thai แสน (saen) meaning "very, extremely" and ชัย (chai) meaning "victory".
Combination of determiner 새 (sae) meaning "new" and adverb 늘 (neul) meaning "always, forever."
Means "light of dawn" in Thai, from แสง (saeng) meaning "light, ray, beam" and อรุณ (arun) meaning "dawn, daybreak".
From Thai แสง (saeng) meaning "light, ray, beam" and ชัย (chai) meaning "victory".
Means "moonlight" from Thai แสง (saeng) meaning "light, ray, beam" and จันทร์ (chan) meaning "moon".

column3: ແສງຈັນເພັງ(Lao)
column12: Means "light of the full moon" in Lao.
Means "starlight" from Thai แสง (saeng) meaning "light, ray, beam" and ดาว (dao) meaning "star".
Alternate transcription of Thai แสงเดือน (see Saengduean).
Means "moonlight, moonshine" from Thai แสง (saeng) meaning "light, ray, beam" and เดือน (duean) meaning "moon".
Alternate transcription of Thai แสงเดือน (see Saengduean).

แสงระวี, แสงรวี(Thai)
แสงระวี, แสงรวี(Thai)
column12: Means "sunlight" from Thai แสง (saeng) meaning "light" and รวี or ระวี (rawi) meaning "sun".
From Thai แสง (saeng) meaning "light, ray, beam" and สุรีย์ (suri) meaning "sun".
From Thai แสง (saeng) meaning "light, ray, beam" and เทียน (thian) meaning "candle".
From Thai แสง (saeng) meaning "light, ray, beam" and ทอง (thong) meaning "gold".
From Thai แสง (saeng) meaning "light" and วรรณ (wan) meaning "colour, tint".
Derived from the Old Norse elements sær "sea" and nýr "new".
Saer de Quincy, 1st earl of Winchester, a norman in Scotland and crusader

column3: さえら(Japanese Hiragana)|沙絵良, 佐依楽, 彩莉, 冴羅, 紗枝良, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|새라(Korean Hangul)

column12: Derived from the Old English elements sæ "sea" and ræd "advice, counsel, wisdom".
This is the name of the fictional character Saeran Choi (mostly known as unknown) from the hit Korean otome game Mystic Messenger.

column3: サエリ(Japanese Katakana)|さえり(Japanese Hiragana)|沙衿, 冴梨莉, 咲枝琳, 早咲里, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 冴 (sa) meaning "serene, skillful, cold, to be clear" combined with 映 (e) meaning "a reflection; to reflect" and 梨 (ri) meaning "pear". Other kanji combinations can be used.
Derived from the Old English elements sæ "sea" and ric "king, ruler".
From 새(sae) meaning "new" combined with 隣(rin) meaning "neighbor", 麟(rin) meaning "qilin", 璘(rin) meaning "luster of jade". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
Combination of adverb 새로 (saero) meaning "anew, newly," itself a combination of determiner 새 (sae) meaning "new" and adverbial particle 로 (ro) meaning "as," and the first syllable of Areum.

From adverb 새로이 (saero-i) meaning "renewedly," from the stem of adjective 새롭다 (saeropda) meaning "new" and the adverb-forming suffix 이 (i).Usage of this name increased in 2018, influenced by the webtoon 'Itaewon Class' which began to be serialised the previous year and adapted into a television series in 2020, the latter event bringing more attention to this name.
From adverb 새록새록 (saerok-saerok) which refers to a new thing popping up one after another.

Shortened from 새로움 (saeroum), the verbal noun of adjective 새롭다 (saeropda) meaning "new," a combination of determiner 새 (sae) meaning "new" and suffix —롭다 (-ropda), forming adjectives from abstract nouns (compare Saeron).
Variant of 새롬이 (saerom-i), from Saerom combined with the subject marking particle 이 (i).

Shortened from Saeroun (compare Saerom). It can also be written with hanja, combining a sae hanja, e.g. 賽 meaning "exorcism," with a ron hanja, e.g. 綸 meaning "fishing line."This name is popularised by actress Kim Sae-ron (2000-2025), better known mononymously as Saeron, whose career began in 2009 when she starred in the film 'A Brand New Life'.
From the stem of adjective 새롭다 (saeropda) meaning "new," a combination of determiner 새 (sae) meaning "new" and suffix —롭다 (-ropda), forming adjectives from abstract nouns.
Derived from Icelandic sær "sea" and rós "rose".
Saeros is one of J. R. R. Tolkien's characters.

From the present determiner form of adjective 새롭다 (saeropda) meaning "new," a combination of determiner 새 (sae) meaning "new" and suffix —롭다 (-ropda), forming adjectives from abstract nouns (compare Saerom).

column3: 冴, 冴栄留, 咲恵瑠, 早絵流, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 冴 (saeru) meaning "skillful, cold, severe". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Derived from the Old Norse elements sær "sea" and rún "secret lore, rune".

Uncertain etymology, possibly derived from Ancient Greek σαίρω (sairo) meaning either "to sweep" or "to grin". This was the name of a daughter of King Celeus of Eleusis in Greek mythology. An older name of Elefsis was Σαισάρια (Saesaria), supposedly in Saesara’s honour.
From Sol prefixed with determiner 새 (sae) meaning "new."
Derived from the Old Norse elements sær "sea" and sól "sun".
From native Korean 샛별 (saetbyeol) meaning "morning star; rising star," derived from earlier Saebyeol with the addition of the genitive infix ㅅ (-s-).

Variant of Sǣþrȳð. Saint Sæthryth (fl. 660s), was the stepdaughter of king Anna of East Anglia, who became a Benedictine nun at the abbey of Faremoutiers-en-Brie, Gaul under its foundress Saint Burgundofara, whom she succeeded as abbess. Saints Seaxburh, Ethelburga, Etheldreda and Withburga were half-sisters.
Derived from Old English sæ "sea" and þryþ "strength, power, force".
Derived from the Old Norse elements sær "sea", and unnr "wave".
Old Norse combination of sær "sea" and unnr "to wave, to billow" or unna "to love".
Old Norse combination of sær 'sea' and valdr 'ruler, mighty one, powerful one'.
Meaning "sea warrior", derived from the Old Norse elements sær "sea" and arr "warrior".
Old Swedish name derived from the adjectives siæver, sæver "calm, self-possessed, tranquil, gentle, leisurely".
Variant form of Sæwaru. This name was borne by the consort of Anna, king of East Anglia.
Derived from the Old English elements sæ "sea" and waru "guard, protection" or "care, watch" (compare weard and wær).
Derived from the Old English elements sæ "sea" and weald "powerful, mighty" or "authority, leader".
Derived from the Old English elements sæ "sea" and weard "guard, guardian".
Derived from the Old English elements sæ "sea" and wig "war, battle".
Derived from the Old English elements sæ "sea" and wulf "wolf".
Derived from Old English sæ "sea" and wynn "joy, delight".
This is the real name of the fictional character 707 (Luciel) from the Korean otome app "Mystic Messenger".
Variant transcription of Shiza.This transcription is used in English translations of the Septuagint Bible.
Derived from Persian شفا (šafâ) meaning "healing, cure, remedy".
Meaning unknown. This is the name of the Ossetian God of the hearth chain and the most important domestic deity to the Ossetian people.
Alternate transcription of Arabic صفاء (see Safaa') chiefly used in Morocco.
Arabic name, composed by "Safa", that means "purity" and "Faiza", that means "victorious".
Means "dawn, daybreak" in Turkish, ultimately from Arabic شفق (shafaq) meaning "twilight".
From Arabic صفا (safa) meaning "pure" and نور (nur) meaning "light".

From Arabic سفر (safar) meaning "journey, travel, voyage" or "campaign". It can also be derived from صفر (ṣafar) referring to the second month of the Islamic calendar, derived from the word صفر (ṣafr) meaning "empty, void" (so named because pagan Arabs looted houses empty during this month).
From Arabic صفر (safar) referring to the second of the twelve months of the Islamic lunar calendar combined with دين (dīn) meaning "religion, faith".
Derived from the Uzbek safar meaning "journey, trip" and the given name Ali 1.

Combination of Safar with the Turkish military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".A known bearer of this name was the Russian general Safarbek Malsagov (1868-1944), who was of Ingush descent and fought in the Russian Civil War (1917-1922).
Derived from the Uzbek safar meaning "journey, trip" and berdi meaning "gave".
Derived from safar, the name of the second month of the Islamic lunar calendar, and bibi meaning "learned woman".
From the Arabic سفر (safar) meaning "journey, travel, voyage", as well as the name of the second Islamic month, and Karachay-Balkar бий (biy) meaning "bey, prince".
Derived from the Uzbek safarboshi meaning "leader of a group of travellers".
Derived from safar, the name of the second month of the Islamic lunar calendar, and go'zal meaning "beautiful".
Derived from safar, the name of the second month of the Islamic lunar calendar, and gul meaning "rose, flower".

Means "journey" in Swahili, from Arabic سَفَر‎ (safar). It is commonly used by Eastern Bantus in Kenya, given to babies born when traveling or given in reference to a lot of traveling by a relative. However, this word is also used to market tourist sites and destinations in East Africa (Kenya), namely expeditions to observe or hunt animals in their natural habitat.Its use in the United States has been influenced by a brand of perfume called Safari, which was introduced by Ralph Lauren in 1990.
The name Safaria is the feminized version of the name Safari, meaning "journey" in Swahili
Derived from Uzbek safar, the name of the second month of the Islamic lunar calendar, and jamol meaning "beauty".
Derived from the Uzbek safar meaning "journey, trip" and juma meaning "Friday".
Derived from the Uzbek safar meaning "journey, trip" and the given name Muhammad.
Derived from the Uzbek safar meaning "journey, trip" and murod meaning "aim, wish, desire".
Derived from the Uzbek safar meaning "journey, trip" and niyoz meaning "entreaty, alms".
Derived from the Uzbek safar meaning "journey, trip" and omon meaning "safe, healthy" or "mercy".
Derived from the Uzbek safar meaning "journey, trip" and o'roz meaning "hope".
Derived from safar, the name of the second month of the Islamic lunar calendar, and oy meaning "moon".
Derived from the Uzbek safar meaning "journey, trip" and qilich meaning "sword".
Derived from safar, the name of the second month of the Islamic lunar calendar, and toj meaning "crown".
Alternate transcription of Arabic صفر الدين (see Safar ad-Din), as well as the Indonesian and Malay form.
Indonesian and Malay variant of Safar ad-Din.
Derived from the Uzbek safar meaning "journey, trip" and valiy meaning "saint, holy".
Derived from the Uzbek safar meaning "journey, trip" and xo'ja meaning "master".
Referring to being delivered from evil by God.
A name given to children when expected that they would die, in reference to being safe with God in heaven.
Often given to children expected to perish. References the safety of a child in Heaven versus earth.
A Knight of the Round Table.
Possibly from Arabic صفا (ṣafā), meaning "to be clear, to be pure".
Alternate transcription of Arabic صفية (see Safiyya).
A mountain mentioned in the Quran. Is now used as a name.
Derived from Arabic صفوة (ṣafwa) meaning "elite, best, prime, pure".

Derived from Dutch saffraan meaning "saffron". In other words, this name is the Dutch cognate of Saffron.This name is extremely rare in the Netherlands; even more so than its English counterpart Saffron, which is also extremely rare there.

Variant of Saffraan or (dutchization of) Saffron. It was probably created in an attempt to make either name more feminine and/or palatable to mainstream Dutch society, as the aforementioned two names are neither traditional nor obviously feminine by Dutch standards.Lastly, even though it is very unlikely to be related, you might want to compare the Dutch term saffrijn-slijpen, which refers to a specific technique of grinding glass. Here, saffrijn is a dutchization of French chanfrein meaning "chamfer, bevel" (obtuse-angled relief or cut at an edge). The term is typically only known by those who work with glass (either for a living or for a hobby), so it's not something that the general public is acquainted with. As such, the chances that parents were inspired by it are almost nil.
Variant spelling of Sophronia. It could also possibly be a more feminine and elaborate version of Saffron. This name is mentioned in the Nina Simone song, “Four Women”.

Diminutive of names beginning with a similar sound, such as Saffron (as used in the children's novel Saffy's Angel (2001) by Hilary McKay). It was also used as an Anglicized form of Sadbh in Ella Griffin's novel Postcards from the Heart (2011).
Malay and Indonesian form of Safiyya.
Means "pure of the religion" from صفي (safi) meaning "pure" combined with الدين (aldin) meaning "the religion"
Form of Safiyyah used in western Africa.
Variant of Safiye. This was the name of a Turkish merchant's daughter in the novel Frankenstein.
Means "pureness of Allah" from Arabic صفيّ (ṣafiyy) meaning "clean, pure" combined with الله (Allah).
From the given name Safiya meaning "pure" combined with the Uzbek word bonu meaning "lady".
Alternate transcription of Arabic صفية (see Safiyya), as well as the Malay form.
Chechen and Dagestani form of Safiyyah.
Derived from safo meaning "clear, limpid" or "enjoyment" and gul meaning "rose, flower".
Derived from the Uzbek safo meaning "clear, limpid" or "delight" and niyoz meaning "entreaty, alms".
Languedocian and Provençal form of Symphorianus.

Alternate transcription of Arabic صفوان (see Safwan) chiefly used in North Africa.

Occitan (Provençal, to be precise) form of Symphorianus.
Derived from Safra and the Turkic word hanım meaning "lady, mistress".
Derived from Uzbek safsar meaning "violet (colour)" and gul meaning "rose, flower".
Derived from Uzbek safsar meaning "violet (colour)" and jon meaning "spirit, soul".
Derived from Persian صافتر (sâftar) meaning "smooth, even", ultimately from صاف (sâf) meaning "flat, smooth, even".
Malay and Indonesian form of Safwan.
Variant transcription of Ṣaffūrah, the Arabic form of Zipporah. It is borne by Azerbaijani singer Safura Alizadeh (1992-).
Alternate transcription of Arabic صفوة (see Safwa), as well as the Malay form.
Means "stones, rocks" or "pure, clean" in Arabic, ultimately from the root صفا (ṣafā) meaning "to be clear, to be pure". This was the name of two companions of the Prophet Muhammad.
Alternate transcription of Arabic صفوان (see Safwan), chifely used in Morocco.
Means "best, finest" in Arabic, from the word صَفَا (safa) meaning "pure, clear".
Alternate transcription of Arabic صافي (see Safi).
One known bearer of the name is Naba Saga (king Saga) of Tenkodogo, who died in 2016.
A name that derives from the word sagal which means morning rays of the sun during the rainy season.
Derived from the word sagamore, which is an anglicization of a Native American word that means "chief".A notable bearer of this name is the French actor Sagamore Stévenin (b. 1974).

An Old French variant of the Old French sicamor meaning "sycamore", as in the tree.Sir Sagramore of Hungary (or Sagremor) is a Knight of the Round Table in the Arthurian legend. His characterization varies from story to story, though he is surprisingly prolific; he appears in a number of early stories, such as Chrétien de Troyes' works, and he turns up in all the cyclical versions. He gains a number of nicknames, including 'The Impetuous' and 'le Desirous'.In Alfred, Lord Tennyson's "Merlin and Vivien", one of the Idylls of the King, he makes an appearance. The knight appears in the musical Camelot, and was played by Peter Bromilow in the film version. Sagramore was portrayed by William Bendix in the 1949 film version of 'A Connecticut Yankee in King Arthur's Court'. In Bernard Cornwell's 'The Winter King', Sagramor is a fierce Numidian veteran of the old Roman army, and follows Arthur to Britain after the collapse of the Western Roman Empire.

In the Middle East, Saheed holds a special place within the region’s diverse cultural mosaic. It is embraced by countries such as Saudi Arabia, Iran, and Egypt, where it represents a deep connection to religious and spiritual beliefs. The name Saheed, derived from Arabic origins, carries the meaning of “witness” or “martyr” in Islamic culture. It symbolizes the importance of faith and sacrifice, evoking a sense of devotion and honor. The prevalence of the name Saheed in this region showcases its enduring popularity and significance in Middle Eastern societies.Furthermore, the name Saheed is often associated with historical figures and heroes who have made significant contributions to their communities. It is not uncommon to find individuals named Saheed being admired and respected for their courage, righteousness, and dedication to their beliefs. The name’s deep-rooted cultural and historical associations make it a cherished choice for Middle Eastern families seeking to honor their heritage and values.

column12: It means "saint", "master", or "lord" in Sindhi and Marathi, from the Dari Persian "sāyæ"Originally, سایه (sāyeh) was a poetic way to refer to Sufi mystics in Persian. It literally means "shade" with the connotation of "protective" and "influential." Sayeh in of itself is a name among Iranians. With the Mughal conquest of India, it was loaned into many languages. Sindhi Sufis added the suffix ین ईं -ī(n) to the root word to make it the adjective سائیں साईं sāī(n) an honorific meaning "saint", "master", or "lord." In fact, Modern South Asian Sufis often refer to God as "Allāh sāī(n)". In the 19th century, a Sufi ascetic in Shirdi, now located in Maharashtra, India, with no name came to prominence as a preacher of religious tolerance and unity and drew both Muslim and Hindu devotees to him. His devotees referred to him as سائیں بابا साईं बाबा "sāī(n) bābā". Over time, the word became standard Marathi but it was corrupted so that the homorganic nasal was deleted and it became साई "sāī". Today, the name Sai is given to both boys and girls in India in reference to Sai Baba of Shirdi, however it is still relatively rare. It is often followed by a middle name which changes the overall meaning and avoids confusion with other people with the same name. It is most common among the people of Maharashtra, Andhra, Karnataka, Gujarat, and Goa.

column12: As a unisex name, it can be used as 咲也, 咲哉, 咲弥, 朔夜 or 朔椰 with 咲 (shou, sa.ku, -zaki) meaning "bloom, blossom", 朔 (saku, tsuitachi) meaning "conjuction (astronomy), first day of the month", 也 (e, ya, ka, nari, mata) meaning "to be (archaic form)", 哉 (sai, kana, ya) meaning "alas, how, question mark, what", 弥 (bi, mi, amaneshi, iya, iyoiyo, tooi, hisashi, hisa.shii, ya, wata.ru) meaning "all the more, increasingly", 夜 (ya, yo, yoru) meaning "evening, night" and 椰 (ya, yashi) meaning "coconut tree."As a feminine name, it can be used as 咲耶 or 沙久椰 with 耶 (ja, ya, ka) meaning "question mark", 沙 (sa, sha, suna, yonageru) meaning "sand" and 久 (kyuu, ku, hisa.shii) meaning "long time, old story."As a masculine name, it can be used as 作哉, 朔也, 朔哉, 朔弥, 朔矢 or 佐玖哉 with 作 (sa, saku, tsuku.ri, tsuku.ru, -dzuku.ri) meaning "build, make, prepare, production", 矢 (shi, ya) meaning "arrow, dart" and 玖 (kyuu, ku) meaning "beautiful black jewel, nine (used in legal documents)."One bearer from Japanese mythology is Konohananosakuya-hime (このはなのさくやひめ), simply known as Sakuya-hime (さくやひめ), who is a blossom-princess and symbol of delicate earthly life. "Sakuya" in Sakuya-hime is popularly written as 咲耶 but it can also be written as 佐久夜 (with 佐 - sa - meaning "assistant, help"), as used in the Kojiki, or 開耶 (with 開 - kai, a.ku, a.keru, hira.ki, hira.ku, hira.keru, -bira.ki - meaning "open, unfold, unseal"), as used in the Nihon Shoki.

column12: From Japanese 朔 (saku) meaning "first day of lunar month", 夜 (ya) meaning "night" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 左京, 佐京(Japanese Kanji)|さきょう(Japanese Hiragana)|サキョウ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name combines 左 (sa, sha, hidari) meaning "left" or 佐 (sa) meaning "assistant, help" with 京 (kyou, kin, kei, miyako) meaning "capital."One bearer of this name was science fiction writer and screenwriter Sakyō Komatsu (小松 左京), born Minoru Komatsu (小松 実) (1931-2011).As a word, Sakyō (左京) means "the left side of the capital," referring to an area east of Suzaku Avenue, which is the central avenue leading to the Imperial Palace from the south in ancient capitals.

The name of the consort of Adad, often considered to be a minor goddess of non-Mesopotamian origin, potentially related to crop fertility. The etymology of her name is unknown, but may be from the Hurrian šāla meaning "daughter".
Possibly an alternative transcription of Salar.

The meaning and origin of the first element in this Germanic name is rather uncertain, and so there are various possibilities to the name's meaning. The most likely possibility is that the first element is derived from Old High German salo "black." Other possibilities are sal "house, living room" and Gothic sêls "kind, friendly." The second element is derived from Gothic bairgan (bergan in Old High German) "to keep, to save, to preserve", or from Old High German burg "fortress." Salaberga was the name of a 7th-century saint.

Galician and Italian form of Saladin.

Indonesian and Malay form of Salah ad-Din.
Means “engraved in the mind”, from สลัก (salak) meaning “carve, engrave, enscribe” combined with จิต (chit) meaning “heart, soul, mind”.
Alternate transcription of Thai สลักจิต (see Salakchit).
Means "waterfall" in Azerbaijani, ultimately from Arabic شلال (shallal).
Means "peace" in Arabic. It is a unisex name in most Arabic-speaking countries while it is solely masculine in Indonesia.
Alternate transcription of Arabic سلامة (see Salama), as well as a Malay and Indonesian variant.

The second element is derived from man "man."
Greek form of Shalmaneser, as it first appeared in the Septuagint.

Salamanca Tree Hiddle is the main character of the novel "Walk Two Moons". It was made up by her parents, who based it upon the word Seneca, as a refrence to the Native American tribe which her great-great grandmother belonged to.
Derived from Greek salamándra, which was in turn derived from Persian samandar meaning "fire from within" (from sām "fire" and andarūn "within").

The second element is derived from Old High German mâri "famous."
Name of a queen of Samoa. The name is held with respect there and is only meant for the royal family. It means "forever".
From of Salma used in Western Africa.

Greek and Latin form of the name of a Babylonian goddess of love, equivalent to Aphrodite or Venus. It may correspond to the once-attested Punic name šlmbʿl meaning "(the god) Dusk (is) (my?) Lord", in which the ending of the name comes from Ba'al, a title of various deities meaning "lord". This has also been used as an anglicized or simplified form of Salammbô in some English translations of the French historical novel Salammbô (1862) by Gustave Flaubert, in which the fictional title heroine is a virgin priestess of the goddess Tanith and the daughter of Hamilcar Barca.
From Uygur سالامەت meaning "healthy, safe", from Arabic سَلَامَة (salāma).
Belarusian form of Solomiya and Belarusianised form of Salomėja and Salomea.

Form of Shelumiel used in the English, Greek and Latin Old Testament.This is the name of an ancestor of Judith in the deuterocanonical Book of Judith. It is rendered as Salathiel and Samuel in many Bible translations.
Form of Shelumiel used in the Latin Old Testament. Also see Salamiel.

Hellenized form of the Hebrew name Shalom-zion "peace of Zion". The name "Shalom Zion" was used by the Judean royal family in the Roman period and is variously modified in rabbinical literature. (Cf. Salome, Shlomtzion.) According to the historian Josephus, Salampsio was the eldest daughter of Herod the Great.
A knight defeated in joust by Perceval.
Derived from sala meaning "sun" and neida meaning "daughter, girl". This is the name of the Sami solar goddess.
Possibly derived from sala meaning "path, road, climb" or "wrap, bundle" and nita meaning "obtain fire by friction", or Fijian translation of Sally Knight.

Variant transcription of Zillethai.This transcription is used in the Douay-Rheims Catholic Bible and English translations of the Septuagint Bible.
Portuguese and Spanish form of Salathiel.
From Arabic سلاطين (salāṭīn) meaning "sultans", the plural of سلطان (sulṭān).
A heathen king who joined King Ekunaver of Kanadic’s war against Arthur.He was slain in the battle of Kanadic by Duke Eskilabon of Belamunt.

Breton form of Solomon (via Old Breton Salamun and Middle Breton Salavun). Salaun (died 874), son of Riwallon and nephew of Nevenoe, was Count of Rennes and Nantes from 852 and Duke of Brittany from 857 until his death by assassination. He used the title "King of Brittany" intermittently after 868. Under his reign Brittany experienced its largest expansion. In popular tradition within Brittany he was canonised as "Sant Salaun" ("Saint Salomon") after his death and raised to the rank of martyr.
Derived from Arabic صَلَوَات (ṣalawāt) meaning "prayers", the plural of صَلَاة (ṣalāh) "prayer". A notable bearer was Salawat Yulayev (1754 - 1800), a Bashkir national hero.
Transferred use of the surname Salazar. It was used by J. K. Rowling in her 'Harry Potter' series of books, where it belongs to Salazar Slytherin, the eponymous founder of Hogwarts' Slytherin house.
Possibly from Arabic سَلْبِيَّة (salbiyya) meaning "negativity, passivity", referring to negative attributes (sifat) that cannot be found in Allah.
Derived from Arabic سَالَ (sāla) meaning "to flow, to run" (figuratively meaning "brook, stream, creek") combined with the Turkish military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".
Frisian short form of names that contain the Germanic elements salo or sal, such as Salabert and Salamar.

Malay and Indonesian form of Salah ad-Din.
Possibly an elaboration of Sally or altered form of Salena, influenced by Aleigha.It shares a suffix sound with names such as Kaliyah, Jaliyah, Maliyah and Taliyah.
Refers to one of the adityas, or deities, in Hinduism. Singer-songwriter and actress Saleka Shyamalan, known as Saleka, is a notable bearer of this name.
Most likely a variant of Selene.

Used by William Shakespeare in the play "The Merchant of Venice". Possibly derived from Saverio.

Variant of Saleta. However, the earliest usage of Saletta seems to predate the French Marian apparition. In these cases a transferred use of the surnames Salette and Saletta is more likely.

From the title of the Virgin Mary Our Lady of La Salette, which comes from the Germanic root sal meaning "house, hall" and the diminutive suffix -ette. A Marian apparition reported by two children is said to have occurred at La Salette-Fallavaux, France, in 1846.
From Lao ສະເຫຼີມ (saleum) meaning "eulogise, exalt, celebrate" and ໄຊ (xay) meaning "rank, power, authority".
Old Norse combination of sól 'sun' and garðr 'enclosure', 'protection'.
Salgra is the Sun God in Garo Mythology.
Means "Apricot" (a sweet orange fruit) in Korean.
Alternate transcription of Arabic صالحة (see Salha), as well as a Malay variant.
Alternate transcription of Arabic صلاح الدين (see Salah ad-Din) chiefly used in Algeria.
Albanian and Tausug form of Salih. A notable bearer is Albanian president Sali Berisha (1944-).

From a Spanish title of the Virgin Mary, Nuestra Señora del Saliente, meaning "Our Lady of El Saliente". The word saliente refers to the platform-like geological formation in which the Virgin's sanctuary is located, in the town of Albox in Almería, Spain.
Alternate transcription of Arabic صالحة (see Saliha), as well as the Malay form.

From Arabic صالحين (ṣāliḥīn‎), the plural of صالح (ṣāliḥ) meaning "virtuous".
Tatar and Bashkir form of Salih.
Bashkir form of Salim and masculine form of Sälimä.

Used by Australian author Alison Croggon in her 'Pellinor' series of fantasy novels, in which the character Saliman of Turbansk was a friend of Maerad, Hem/Cai and Cadvan. It may be a variant transcription of Suleiman.
Form of Salima used in parts of western Africa.

Derived from Italian salimmo meaning "we went up" combined with Italian bene meaning "good". Also compare Ognibene.There are also sources that believe that the name is entirely Hebrew in origin, and thus consider it to be a Jewish name. They derive the first element from either Hebrew שָׁלוֹם (shalom) meaning "peace" or Hebrew שולם (shulam) meaning "paid". Meaning uncertain, possibly of Arabic origin.

Meaning uncertain. The second element is likely derived from Italian guerra meaning "war".
Form of Salih used in parts of French-influenced western Africa.

Transferred use of the English surname Salisbury, recorded several times during the 17th century as a feminine name in Mann.

While he sells his skills to the highest bidder, he has some genuine loyalty to his friends and allies."You think I'm insulted? I am a pirate. I'm an excellent pirate."
Means "squirrel", from the Cherokee sa lo li 'squirrel'.
Means "born on a feast day" in Hausa.
Possibly from the Aymara salla meaning "sonorous".
From the Hausa sallā̀ meaning “prayer, religious holiday”.
Relatively modern name (late 19th century) created by combining Swedish säll meaning "blissful, happy" with frid meaning "peace, protection".
Feminine form of Sallustius. A well-known bearer of this name was Sallustia Orbiana, who had briefly been the wife of Roman Emperor Alexander Severus.
English form of Sallustianus. This was the name of a saint who was apparently especially venerated on the island of Sardinia.
Swedish name with the combination of sæll "blissful", "happy" and vé "home", "temple", "sanctuary".

Salma is a purely Turkic name originating from the verbal root sal- ("to swing, to release, to set free, to cast"). Symbolically, it embodies the spirit of "the one who moves freely" or "the unshackled." It is a structural sibling to Salkım.It must be distinguished from the Arabic Selma/Salima (root: s-l-m, "peace/safe"). The Turkic name derives from the active verb of motion, whereas the Arabic cognate is a passive/stative participle denoting the state of being safe. The phonological shift from Turkic Salma to Arabic-derived Selma is a common misidentification. Turkic Salma preserves the back-vowel harmony of the original verb, whereas the Arabic loanword Selma adopts the front-vowel adaptation typical of Semitic borrowings in Turkish.

Latinized form of Greek Σαλμακίς (Salmakis), possibly derived from Ancient Greek σαλμάκιον (salmakion), a type of poisonous reed that grew in marshy areas, perhaps related to σάμαξ (samax) "rush-mat, bed of reeds". This was the name of a fountain and nymph at Halicarnassus, featured in Ovid's Metamorphoses. The nymph Salmacis fell in love with Hermaphroditus. When he rejected her, she attempted to rape him and prayed to the gods to be bound with him forever. As a result their bodies fused together to create the Hermaphrodite. The fountain Salmacis was said to cause men who drank its waters to be weak and effeminate.
Form of Shalmai used in some versions of the Old Testament.
Salmakia is a character in Philip Pullman's His Dark Materials book series, first released in 1995.
Combination of the name Salma and the feminine suffix -niar.

Derived from Old Norse salr "hall, house" and maðr "person, man" (genitive manns). Alternatively this could be an Icelandic form of a German name in which the first element is derived from Old High German salo "dirty gray" (related to English sallow and Old Norse sölr "dirty yellow").However, in the case of Salmann Tamimi (1955-2020), a Palestinian immigrant to Iceland who founded the Association of Muslims in Iceland, this was adopted as an Icelandic form of Suleiman, his original name.
Combination of the name Salma and the feminine suffix -wati.
Variant of Salma. Sayyida Salme was a princess of Zanzibar and a writer. She changed her name to Emily Ruete after converting to Christianity and moving to Europe.
Medieval German form of Salome, used in what is today Germany and Austria from the 13th century onwards.
From Arabic سِلْمِيّ (salmiyy) meaning "peaceful, amicable, pacifistic".
Short form of Salmon and masculine form of Salme.
He is the son of Nahshon, and married Rahab, possibly she of Jericho, by whom he had Boaz. Thus, according to the Biblical genealogies, Salmon is the patrilineal great-great-grandfather of David.

Uncertain etymology. Salmoneus was the eponymous founder and king of Salmone in Greek mythology, and the brother of Sisyphus. He eventually demanded that his subjects worship him as the god Zeus, and so was struck down by lightning.
Either a medieval Scandinavian adoption of Salomon or a combination of Old Norse name elements salr "hall, house" and mundr "protection".

From the Lithuanian word Šalna meaning "frost."
Either derived from Latvian salna "fost, frostiness" or from Latvian salnis "roan (the color)".

Slovak, Croatian and Kashubian form of Salome.
Means "healthy and sound" in Uzbek, also an expression used to express gratitude.
Possibly a masculine form of Salome.
Variant of Salome. This was used for a character in the movie 'I Origins' in 2014.
Medieval Dutch form of Salomon, which was primarily used in the Jewish community.

Salonia Matidia was the daughter and only child of Ulpia Marciana and wealthy praetor Gaius Salonius Matidius Patruinus. Her maternal uncle was the Roman emperor Trajan. Trajan had no children and treated her like his daughter. Her father died in 78 and Matidia went with her mother to live with Trajan and his wife, Pompeia Plotina.
Spanish, Italian and Portuguese form of Saloninus.
Roman cognomen derived from Salona (a city name) with the suffix -inus , meaning "from Salona". This name was borne by a 3rd-century Roman emperor.
Fijian and Tongan form of Charlotte.

"Human is not God" denoting "man is not God"

Alternate transcription of Arabic سلسبيل (see Salsabil) chiefly used in Egypt.
From the name of a water spring in paradise mentioned in verse 76:18 of the Quran. The term itself is of uncertain meaning, possibly of Akkadian origin.
Alternate transcription of Arabic سلسبيلة (see Salsabila), as well as an Indonesian variant.
"Pure Water", "Clay"In Islam it refers to a well of water called salsal.
Transferred use of the occupational surname Salter.
Salu, of the house of Simeon, was the father of Zimri who was involved in the Heresy of Peor according to Numbers 25:14.
Old High German short form of names containing the element salo meaning "dark, dusky, dirty gray" (related to English sallow and Old Norse sölr "dirty yellow").
Possibly after the Saluda Mountains and Saluda River, both located along the border of North and South Carolina.
Derived from Spanish saludación meaning "greeting, salutation".
Means "health, safety" in Latin. This was the name of the Roman goddess of safety and well-being, sometimes equated to her Greek counterpart Hygieia.

A saint from Orberica.Salustes is described as a knight and a cousin of Joseph of Arimathea in some versions of the Arthurian legends. He is often depicted as one of the keepers or guardians of the Holy Grail. He is sometimes portrayed as a faithful and virtuous knight who remains dedicated to protecting the sacred relic.Joseph of Arimathea had him interred in Sarras, giving the newly-christened city a holy body. A church was founded in his name. His spirit appeared to assist King Mordrains of Sarras during his difficult adventure on the Rock of the Perilous Port.
Spanish and Polish form of Sallustia.
Spanish and Galician form of Sallustianus.

Portuguese cognate of Catalan Salut.According to IGBE Censo2010, 60 girls were named Salute in the 1940s and it's most prelevant in Santa Catarina with a total of 156 girls named Salute in that region.

this name was found in the Jewish catacombs of Rome, it appears to be used almost exclusively by Roman Jews except for one well-recorded casederived from salus meaning "health"

From the genus name of sage, an herb formerly used as medicine, which comes from Latin salvus "healthy, safe" (related to salvere "to save, to be saved"), referring to the plant's supposed healing properties. The Latin salvia was corrupted to sauja and sauge (the Old French form), which eventually became the modern English sage (see Sage).In the English-speaking world, this name has been occasionally used since the 19th century. As an Italian name, it can be regarded as a feminine form of Salvo.
English form of Salvianus. This was the name of a Christian writer from the 5th century AD.
Italian and Spanish form of Salvianus.
Roman cognomen which was derived from Salvius.
From the Latin salvus, meaning "salvation" (as in 'of the soul').
Diminutive of Salvius. This was the name of a Frankish saint from the 5th century AD.
After the island of Sálvora, in Galicia. It possibly comes from a Celtic word meaning "salt" or "turbulent waters".
Alternate transcription of Arabic سلوى (see Salwa), as well as the Indonesian form.
From the title of Mary Virgen del Salz ("Virgin of the Willow"). This Marian devotion belongs to the town of Zuera (Spain).
From Sino-Vietnamese 旵 (sảm) meaning "daylight, sunlight". This was the personal name of the eighth emperor of the Lý dynasty, Lý Hạo Sảm.

From the Sanskrit word समाधि (samādhi) meaning "placing together", from सम (sama) "together" combined with the prefix आ (ā) and धा (dhā) "to place". This word refers to the practice which produces complete meditation (though usage of the term varies among the Indian religious traditions, such as Hinduism and Buddhism). Bearers of this name include Sri Lankan actress Samadhi Arunachaya (1990-) and Mexican actress Samadhi Zendejas (1994-).

It's pronounced Sah-mee-rah. My dad read 'Conan the Barbarian' when my mom was pregnant with me. That's where he got my name.' It may have been inspired by the Irish river name Samair, Samhair, about which Adolphe Pictet (1799-1875) wrote: '...in the colloquial Irish of the people the old name Samhair was corrupted to Camhair; and as this word signifies the first appearance of daylight or the break of day, so they translated it into "Morning Star"'; or it may have been influenced by the fictional place name Cimmeria, the homeland of Conan the Barbarian in the works of Robert E. Howard.

Means "breeze, wind" in Kazakh, ultimately from Arabic شمال (shamāl) meaning "north, north wind".
From the Nyakyusa name for a type of bird.
Means "nosegay, collection of flowers" in Sanskrit.

According to the Prose Tristan, the large son of Duke Frollo of Germany who went on to become a knight of great renown.Although he was knighted by Galahad, he opposed Arthur’s knights for having defeated his father. During the Grail Quest, he fought and defeated Kay, Gaheris, and Griflet.

Germanic name meaning "same battle", derived from Gothic sama, Old High German samo "same" combined with Old High German hilt, Old Frankish hildi "battle".

column12: This name can be used as 左馬之介 or 左馬之助 with 左 (sa, sha, hidari) meaning "left", 馬 (ba, uma, uma-, ma) meaning "horse", 之 (shi, oite, kono, kore, no, yuku) meaning "of, this", 介 (kai, suke) meaning "concern oneself with, jammed in, mediate, shellfish" and 助 (jo, suke, su.keru, tasu.karu, tasu.keru) meaning "assist, help, rescue."In modern times, it is very rarely given to boys, if given at all.

Means "universal goodness" or "all-good" from Sanskrit समन्त (samanta) meaning "universal, entire" and भद्र (bhadra) meaning "worthy, good, virtuous". In Buddhist tradition this is the name of a bodhisattva associated with meditation and spiritual practice. This was also the name of two prominent Jain monks.
Means "whole, complete, entire" in Sinhalese, ultimately from Sanskrit समन्त (samanta). It is also sometimes associated with the name of the Buddhist deity Saman.

Samanthe and its variant spellings, including its most common variant Semanthe, are relatives and possibly predecessors of the name Samantha, which were at their peak use in the 1700s and 1800s in the United States, mainly in New England, though there is also some evidence of Semanthe being used in 1700s England.The usage of Samanthe, Semanthe, and the other variant spellings of this name before the popularity of Samantha lends credence to the theory that these names originate as an anglicization of the name Sijmentje, which is said to be the feminine Dutch form of the German name Sigimund.
Means "she who is unknown" in Chikaguru.
