column12: From Japanese 世 (se) meaning "world", 瀬 (se) meaning "rapids, current, torrent, shallows, shoal", 星 (se) meaning "star", 聖 (se) meaning "holy, saint, sage, master, priest" or 姫 (se) meaning "princess", 亜 (a) meaning "second, Asia" or 愛 (a) meaning "love, affection" combined with 羅 (ra) meaning "gauze, thin silk", 良 (ra) meaning "good, pleasing, skilled", 新 (ara) meaning "fresh, new", 来 (ra) meaning "come, due, next, cause, become", 空 (ara) meaning "sky", 愛 (ara) meaning "love, affection", 蘭 (ra) meaning "orchid" or 微 (ara) meaning "delicate, minuteness, insignificance". Other kanji combinations are possible.

The name Sharon is primarily a female name of Hebrew origin that means Of The Fertile Plain.While in Hebrew Sharon is a word for plain, it also specifically refers to the location between the Samarian Hills and the coast of Israel. In the King James Bible version of the Song of Solomon the phrase "I am the rose of Sharon" is used, which has led to various flowering plants being called the same name.Sharon was not commonly used as a given name until it entered the top 1000 for baby girls in the United States in 1925. One possible influence for its usage is the character from the 1925 novel The Skyrocket by Adela Rogers St. Johns which was made into a film the year after. The name reached its peak in the U.S. between 1943 and 1945 when it ranked 8. Sharon ranked for boys in the U.S. for a handful of years, predominantly in the 1940s, though never became popular.In most other English-speaking countries, the name was most popular in the 1950s and 1960s including England & Wales, Australia, and New Zealand. In Canada Sharon's popularity was contemporary with the United States and peaked at 5 in 1943 and 1944.
Referring to John 5:39, 'Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me.'
Respelling of Sergio. A famous bearer is Seargeoh Stallone.
Variant of Saorfhlaith. It means free princess or free noblewoman derived from Irish saor meaning "free" and Irish flaith meaning "princess, nobelwoman".
Scottish form of Charlotte (compare Séarlait), sometimes associated with the name Teàrlag (which was Anglicized as Charlotte).
Variant of Saorfhlaith. It means free princess or free noblewoman derived from Irish saor meaning "free" and Irish flaith meaning "princess, nobelwoman".
Gaelic form of Jessie 1. The name coincides with the future tense of the Scottish Gaelic verb seas "to stand".

From the English word "season", derived from Latin sationem "a sowing, planting" (nominative satio). It got a boost in popularity in the 1970s due to Season Hubley (1951-; birth name Susan Hubley), an American actress.
Means "bodyguard" from Irish seasuighim meaning "to resist, to defend".
Scottish Gaelic form of John via Old French Jehan.

Seattle is an anglicization of the modern Duwamish conventional spelling Si'ahl, equivalent to the modern Lushootseed (Chief Seattle's native language) publishing spelling Si'aɫ.A noted bearer is Chief Seattle (c.1780 - 1866) of the Duwamish. A widely publicized speech arguing in favor of ecological responsibility and respect of native Americans' land rights has been attributed to him, and the largest city in Washington state, Seattle, was named after him.
Transferred use of the surname Seaver.
Seawillow Margaret Ann Wells was named Seawillow after the unusual circumstances of her birth. The community Seawillow in Texas is named after her.

Derived from the Old English elements seax "knife" and burg "fortress". Saint Sexburga (7th century) was a daughter of King Anna of the East Angles and wife of King Eorcenberht of Kent. This name was also borne by a queen of the West Saxons (Wessex), who ruled the kingdom for one or two years after her husband Cenwealh's death in 672.
Old English name derived from seax "knife" and giefu "gift", an early form of a name recorded in 1185 in the genitive case Sexhiue (see Sexiva).
Derived from the Old English elements seax "knife" and helm "helmet, protection".

Old English cognate of Sahsnot, possibly consisting of Old English seax "knife, dagger" (related to seaxa "Saxon") and (ge-)nēat "companion, associate" or nēat# "help, need".Seaxnēat was the name of an Anglo-Saxon god from which the kings of Essex claimed descent.
Derived from the Old English elements seax "knife" (compare seaxa "Saxon") and ræd "advice, counsel, wisdom".
Derived from the Old English elements seax "knife" (compare seaxa "Saxon") and wine "friend".
Derived from the Old English elements seax "knife, dagger" (compare seaxa "Saxon") and wulf "wolf".

There's only one Seba in the Bible, and he's a son of Cush, son of Ham, son of Noah (Genesis 10:7).There seems to be something secretive about this name. Neither BDB Theological Dictionary nor NOBS Study Bible Name List dare to even hint at an interpretation. Jones' Dictionary of Old Testament Proper Names ignores any Hebrew words that may have to do with the name Seba and goes after an Arabic cognate and concludes Eminent.Perhaps that's what the name Seba meant to those who made it up, but to a Hebrew audience the name Seba sounded very clearly like it came from the verb Seba (saba), meaning to imbibe, even "heavy drinking" according to HAW Theological Wordbook of the Old Testament (Deuteronomy 21:20, Isaiah 56:12, Nahum 1:10).The two derivatives of this verb are Seba (sobe 1455a), meaning a drink (of an alcoholic beverage), and Seba (saba), meaning drunkard (Ezekiel 23:42). The King James Version actually invented a people here, the Sabeans, but later scholars assume that a meaning of drunkards is probably what was intended.The name Seba means He Drank Wine, according to Klein's Etymological Dictionary of the Hebrew Language.

Contraction of Siegbald. Saint Sebald was an Anglo-Saxon missionary to Germany in the 9th or 10th century. He settled down as a hermit in the Reichswald near Nuremberg, of which city he is the patron saint. According to legend Sebaldus was a hermit and a missionary.
Basque form of Sebastiana and Sébastienne.
Catalan and Cremish Lombard form of Sebastian.
Corsican, Sicilian and Sardinian form of Sebastian.

Derived from Σεβαστός (Sebastos), which is an Ancient Greek calque of the Roman title Augustus. Also compare the Greek noun Σεβάστιος (Sebastios) meaning "an oath by the genius of the Emperor". Both are ultimately derived from the Greek adjective σεβαστός (sebastos) meaning "venerable, reverend, august".
Modern Swedish diminutive of Sebastian and an Old Swedish diminutive of Sebjörn.
Old Norse and Old Danish diminutive of Sǽbiǫrn.
Diminutive of Sebastian or Sebastiane, usually not used as a given name in its own right.
Ancient Egyptian masculine name meaning "Sobek is in festival".
Possibly derived from Old English elements sǣ meaning "sea" and burg meaning "fortress". This name might also be an Anglicization of the Old Norse name Sæbjørg.

Variant of Severina. This name was borne by Seberina Candelaria, a young woman who lived in colonial Philippines in the early 19th century who in 1808, at age 22 years, was arraigned before an ecclesiastical court for 'associating with the devil'.
Konkani form of Sebastian, borrowed from Portuguese Sebastião. Used by Konkani Catholics.

Possibly derived from Ancient Greek, meaning "fast-flowing" or "to go with impetus". This was the name of a nymph in Greek mythology, a daughter of the eponymous god of the Sebeto river, mother of Oebalus, and wife of Telon.
Etymology unknown, perhaps related to Eusebius.
From the Arabic شَبيبَة (šabība) meaning "youth, youthfulness".
Variant of Sybil. In Arthurian legend and Italian folklore, Sebile is a queen or princess often portrayed as a fairy or enchantress.

A mythical medieval queen or princess who is frequently portrayed as a fairy or an enchantress in the Arthurian legend and Italian folklore. She appears in a variety of roles, from the most faithful and noble lady to a wicked seductress, often in relation with or substituting for the character of Morgan le Fay. Some tales feature her as a wife of either King Charlemagne or Prince Lancelot, and even as an ancestor of King Arthur.

Derived from Korean 세(se) meaning "three" or Korean Hanja 世(se) meaning "world, lineage, generation" combined with 彬(bin) meaning "bright, luminous" or 贇(bin) meaning "beautiful". Other combinations can also form this name.
Either a newer form of Sæbiǫrn (see Sǽbiǫrn) or a variant of Sigbjörn (uncertain).
Scottish Gaelic form of Zebulun used in the Bible.
From Japanese 世 (se) meaning "generations" combined with 聞 (bun) meaning "hear". Other kanji combinations are possible.Usage of this name is, most likely, influenced by the number seven.
The name is purely Malayalam in origin, a South Indian language spoken by the Malayalis.
The meaning is 'nation' as in 'our nation', 'the country we live in'.
Queen Sectonia is the primary antagonist of Kirby: Triple Deluxe and the penultimate boss of that game. She first appears in-game after Kirby beats Taranza, who was the queen's loyal servant.
Recorded in Montenegro in the early 1600s.

Man's defender; Warrior. A name made for a true champion, Secunder is a masculine name of Greek origin that means “man's defender” or “warrior.” It is the Persian interpretation of the name Alexander, hailing from when the Greek king Alexander the Great conquered Persia and took on the moniker Secunder.
Anglicized form of Secundianus. This was the name of several saints.
Roman cognomen which was derived from Secundus.This name was borne by several saints.
Diminutive of Secunda, as it contains the Latin feminine diminutive suffix -illa. This name was borne by a saint from the 4th century AD.

The infidel queen of Tribalibot, India, and its cities of Thabronit and Thasme.She was fascinated with stories of the Grail, and she sent two of her subjects – Cundrie the Sorceress and Malcreatiure – to Anfortas, the Grail King, as servants.Later, she fell in love with Feirefiz, Perceval’s half brother, and gave him her lands in exchange for his devoted service. He eventually cast off her love, however, in favor of the Grail Maiden, Repanse de Schoye, causing Secundille to die of heartbreak.

Diminutive of Secundus, as it contains the Latin masculine diminutive suffix -ulus.This is the name of a saint who was martyred together with Perpetua and Felicitas (also known as Felicity) in Carthage around 203 AD.
Means "security, safety" in Latin. Securitas was the goddess of security and stability in Roman mythology.

From the Turkish seda meaning "sound, voice" and gül meaning "rose".
From the Turkish seda meaning "sound, voice" and naz meaning "coy".

From the Turkish seda meaning "sound" and su meaning "water".

East Frisian short form of names containing the element side "custom, habit; manner". This name also saw some usage on the Faroe Islands.

The name of the wife of Shem in the Book of Jubilees.
Transferred use of the surname Sedgwick.

Of uncertain origin and meaning. One current theory, however, links this name to Latin sedile "seat; chair".
Means "Providence has favored me" in Ewe.
Varient of Sadiqullah, Siddiqullah, and Sidqullah.

Meaning unknown. A notable bearer was Saint Sedna, an early bishop of Ossory. This was also the name of the ancestor of the Brophy family, who also gave his name to the region of Magh Sedna (located within County Kilkenny).

Old Polish male name, of which the first element is derived from Polish sądzić "to judge" (also compare Croatian suditi and Czech soudit, both of which mean "to judge"). The second element is derived from Slavic mir "peace". This name is not to be confused with Čedomir.

In the United States, this name is usually given in honour of the city of Sedona in Arizona. The city itself had been named after Sedona Arabella Schnebly (née Miller), who was the wife of Theodore Carlton Schnebly, the city's first postmaster. Sedona herself is said to have gotten her name from her mother, who had allegedly thought up the name herself, thinking it sounded pretty. However, it could just as well be that her mother had taken the existing names Sidonia or Sidony and slightly altered them to her liking. She may even have been inspired by Cydonia to some degree, which is the Latin name of the quince plant.
Modern form of Sǽþórr or Sigþórr.

While the first name element is derived from Polish sądzić "to judge", the second element is of debated origin and meaning. The predominant theory considers it the Pomeranian equivalent of Polish wuj "uncle", which would make Sędowin the Pomeranian form of Sędziwuj.
Greek form of Shadrach, as it first appeared in the Septuagint.
Variant of Cedric. Known bearers of this name include the American basketball players Sedric Toney (b. 1962) and Sedric Webber (b. 1977).
Variant spelling of Cedric via Sedric. Also compare Cedrick. A known bearer of this name is the American retired football player Sedrick Ellis (b. 1985).
Catalan and Spanish form of Sæthryth.
Feminine form of Sedulius. Sedulia was the mother of Saint Maura of Troyes.
Italian and Spanish form of Sedulius.
Derived from Latin sedulus "zealous, diligent, industrious". This name was borne by Coelius Sedulius, a Christian poet of the first half of the 5th century.
Norwegian combination of siðr "custom", "habit", "manner" and vǫrðr "guard".
Derived from Haitian Creole se "that is; it is" and dye "god".
Derived from Polish sądzić "to judge" and sława "glory, fame".
Derived from Polish sądzić "to judge" and wuj "uncle".
From Japanese 星 (se) meaning "star", 月 (dzuki) meaning "moon" combined with 夜 (ya) meaning "night". Other kanji combinations are possible.

This name is more often seen on men than on women. For men, the name is a short form of Josephus and in some cases also of Severinus and its Dutch form Severijn. For women, this name is a short form of Josepha, Joséphine and in rare cases also of Severina and its French form Séverine. Also see Seefke.Lastly, this name is not to be confused with the Dutch word zeef meaning "sieve".
Diminutive of Seef. This name is predominantly feminine, but has occasionally informally been used on men (especially in Limburg, because diminutives ending in -ke are common for both sexes there).

Possibly means "summit of Yahweh", derived from Hebrew שִׂיא (si) meaning "peak, pinnacle, top, summit" combined with יָהּ (yah) referring to the Hebrew God. This is the name of an angel belonging to the order of the Dominions. He is one of the 72 angels bearing the explicit name of God (the Shem HaMephorash), as interpreted by some Christian Kabbalists.
Means "oriole (a type of bird)". Seelasat was the protector of virgins in Vainakh mythology.
Transferred use of the surname Seeley. Seeley Booth is a fictional character in the TV series 'Bones' (2005-2017).

Medieval nickname for a person with a cheerful disposition, from Middle English seely "happy, fortunate" (from Old English sæl "happiness, good fortune"). The word was also occasionally used as a female personal name during the Middle Ages. The word's considerable sense development moved from "blessed" to "pious", to "innocent" (c.1200), to "harmless", to "pitiable" (late 13c.), to "weak" (c.1300), to "feeble in mind, lacking in reason, foolish" (1570s); the sense "pitiable", which developed into modern English silly, is not attested before the 15th century.
Scots form of Simon 1. In some places it is also used as a Scots form of Sigmund or Simeon.

In the case of Danish-American silent film actress Seena Owen (1894-1966), it was an Anglicized form of Signe, her birth name. It could also be a short form of Thomasina and other names featuring this sound.
Diminutive of Serafiina.A famous bearer is Seere Salminen (1894–1977), Finnish author and playwright.

Member of Gadianton band, tenth known Nephite chief judge (c. 26 BC), eventually succeeded by Lachoneus. How and when he began his reign as chief judge is not known; his first appearance in the Book of Mormon is when Nephi, son of Helaman, prophesied his murder by the hand of his brother, Seantum. To give the wicked Nephites a sign that he, Nephi, was a prophet, he prophesied this murder to his people. Seezoram should not be confused with Cezoram, another Nephite chief judge who was assassinated earlier.
Means "God has comforted me" in Ewe.
Swedish, Afrikaans and Dutch form of Zephaniah.
Combination of the Old Norse name elements sær "sea" and fastr "strong, firm".
This is the birth name of Persian Japanese baseball player Yu Darvish.
Albanian, Bosnian and Turkish form of Safar.
Possibly from the Arabic سَفَرى (seferî) meaning “traveler”.
Diminutive of names ending in -sef or -zef.
Upper German diminutive of Josefine. This name is strictly a diminutive and not used as a given name in its own right.
Truncated form of Josefína and Josefina.
A Cretan dialectal form of Joseph.It is the name of a crocodile living in an artificial lake near Rethymno in summer 2014.
Italian and Polish form of Zipporah.
Gascon form of Symphorianus. This name is not to be confused with the similar-looking name Severianus.
Unknown meaning, possibly related to the Wolof word ségg ("tiger, leopard").
Archaic Italian form of Siegfried via its medieval Latin form Segafredus. This given name is no longer in use, but it still survives as a patronymic surname.
Possibly a Breton form of Severinus.
Means "that which draws water" in Setswana.
Medieval form of Sægar, an Old English name derived from the elements sæ "sea" and gar "spear".
Archaic North Swedish form of Sigurd. Means "victory" in modern Swedish.
Segeric was, according to Jordanes, the king who immediately followed Alaric I as ruler of the Visigoths. He ruled only a short time and then was killed by his soldiers.

Possibly from Egyptian sgr-snj, perhaps meaning "to silence the two of them", from Egyptian sgr "quiet, silence" combined with snj "the two of them". This was the name of an ancient Egyptian or Nubian chieftain of Nubia, likely reigning concurrently with the end of the 11th and beginning of the 12th Dynasty during the early Middle Kingdom.

column3: 世儀子, 瀬木子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 世 (se) meaning "world", 儀 (gi) meaning "ceremony" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Dialectal form of Sigurd found primarily in the Swedish province Västergötland.
Gascon and Polish cognate of Ségolène.

Celtic name, in which the first element is Proto-Celtic *sego- "force, victory" (also found in the Gaulish name Segomaros). The second element, *uako, possibly means "empty" or "curved". This was the name of a king of the Cantiaci in modern Kent at the time of Julius Caesar's second expedition to Britain ca. 54 BC. Segovax is also the name of a fictional character in Edward Rutherfurd's historical novel 'London' (1997).
King Anguish of Ireland’s astrologer.He interpreted Anguish’s dream portending the affair between Tristan and Isolde, Anguish’s daughter.
Segub, meaning “He has revealed Himself as exalted” or “He has protected.” He was the youngest son of King Ahab

Hebrew word name, it has several meanings.- "treasure"- "good omen"- "kabbalistic helper": for example, it is said that praying for someone else's well-being is a 'segula' for recovering quickly yourself.Typical of North African Jewry.
Segurant, the Knight of the Dragon is a character who first appeared in the Middle Ages on Armorials of the Round Table (a list of fictional knights attending King Arthur's court).
Segwarides is the son of the Saracen king Esclabor who becomes a liegeman of King Mark and a knight of the Round Table.

column3: 세하(Korean Hangul)|歲夏, 歲河, 世夏, 世河, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 歲 (se) meaning "year, age, harvest" or 世 (se) meaning "world, generation, lifetime" combined with 夏 (ha) meaning "summer, grand, great" or 河 (ha) meaning "river, stream". Other Hanja combinations are possible.
Alternate transcription of Korean Hangul 세희 (see Se-hui).
From the Arabic سَهْل (sehl) meaning "easy, gentle”.
Of uncertain meaning. Sehener was an Ancient Egyptian princess that lived during the Second Dynasty, although the specific reign under which she lived is unknown.
Croatian, Bosnian, Slovene and Serbian form of Shahrazad.
From the Turkish seher meaning "dawn" and soy meaning "family, descent, line".
Likely derives from Ottoman Turkish shehla meaning "bluish or light eyes".
Contracted form of Sheikh Musa who was an 11th century Muslim Saint of Mardin (Turkiye).
From Sino-Korean 世 "generation; world; era" and 鎬 "stove; bright".
Form of Sihon used in the Douay-Rheims Bible (1582-1610).

column3: 세훈(Korean Hangul)|世勳, 世勛, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Alternate transcription of Korean Hangul 세훈 (see Se-hun).
From the Persian شهربانو (şehr-bânû) meaning "state lady, queen".
From Sino-Korean 世 (se) meaning "world, era, generation" combined with 熙 (hui) meaning "bright, splendid, glorious". This name can be formed from other hanja combinations as well.

column3: 세훈(Korean Hangul)|世勳, 世勛, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 世 (se) meaning "world, era, generation" combined with 勳 (hun) or 勛 (hun) both meaning "meritorious deed, rank". Other combinations of hanja can form this name as well.

column3: 세현(Korean Hangul)|世賢, 世鉉, 洗賢, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 世 (se) meaning "world, era, generation" or 洗 (se) meaning "clean, purify" combined with 賢 (hyeon) meaning "virtuous, worthy, wise" or 鉉 (hyeon) referring to a device used to lift a tripod cauldron. Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 세현(Korean Hangul)|世賢, 世鉉, 洗賢, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Alternate transcription of Korean Hangul 세현 (see Se-hyeon).

column3: せい(Japanese Hiragana)|セイ(Japanese Katakana)|晴, 星, 成, 整, 聖, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|새이, 세이(Korean Hangul)
column12: From Japanese 晴 (sei) meaning "clear up, clear weather". Other kanji or kanji combinations can be used.

column3: せいあ(Japanese Hiragana)|井蛙, 成亜, 星亜, 星空, 星彩, 聖亜, 聖愛, 聖天, 青空, 彗亜, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 井 (sei) meaning "well, well crib, town, community", 成 (sei) meaning "turn into, become, get, grow, elapse, reach", 星 (sei) meaning "star", 聖 (sei) meaning "holy, saint, sage, master, priest", 青 (sei) meaning "blue, green" or 彗 (sei) meaning "comet" combined with 亜 (a) meaning "second, Asia", 空 (a) meaning "sky", 彩 (a) meaning "colour", 愛 (a) meaning "love, affection" or 天 (a) meaning "heavens, sky, imperial". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column5: sei ah ku mo ku mo
column12: Means "do not take me in a bad way" in Ijaw.

column3: セイバ(Japanese Katakana)|せいば(Japanese Hiragana)|星馬, 誠羽, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column12: Phonetic spelling of Sadie reflecting the English pronunciation.
Variant of Sadie, which reflects the Spanish pronunciation.

column3: 清円院(Japanese Kanji)|せいえんいん(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: Seienin (清円院) was a Japanese noble woman from the Nagao clan during the Sengoku period. She is best known as the formal second wife of Uesugi Kagetora, also referred to as Kakeiin, and as the niece of the famed Uesugi Kenshin. She was the daughter of Aya-Gozen and sister of Uesugi Kagekatsu.
Alternate transcription of Arabic سيف (see Saif).
Alternate transcription of Arabic سيف الله (see Sayfullah).
Arthur’s sister in Der Pleier’s Meleranz. She was the wife of King Lot and the mother of Gawain. Her sisters included Anthonje and Olimpia.Her name is probably a corruption of Wolfram’s Sangive.
Maghrebi transcription of Saif al-Din (chiefly Tunisian and Algerian).
Taken from the last name Seifer. Seifer Almasy (サイファー・アルマシー, Saifā Arumashī) is character from Final Fantasy 8.
Means "(he is) the sword" in Amharic
Alternate transcription of Arabic سيف الله (see Sayfullah).

column3: 星河, 清河, 清雅, 誠芽, 青我, 静芽, 菁莪, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 星 (sei) meaning "star, dot" combined with 河 (ga) meaning "stream, river". Other kanji combinations are possible.

Medieval form of Sægiefu. It was mentioned by the 12th-century historian Reginald of Durham as belonging to a 7th-century Christian woman from Hawick who, with Rosfrith, had worshipped at the lost chapel of St Cuthbert in the Slitrig valley.
Diminutive of one of the variants of Schneur.

column3: 誠吾, 星吾, 晴吾, 正吾, 清吾, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 誠 (sei) meaning "sincerity", 星 (sei) meaning "star", 晴 (sei) meaning "clear weather, fine weather", 正 (sei) meaning "justice, correct, right" or 清 (sei) meaning "pure" combined with 吾 (go) meaning "I, me". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Alternate transcription of Khmer សីហា (see Seyha).
The name Originates from Tiv and it means "Peaceful Bird" or "One of a kind"

column3: 星歩, 星帆, 星火, 栖圃, 正歩, 清秀, 盛保, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 星 (sei) meaning "star" combined with 歩 (ho) meaning "walk". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 誠一, 清一, 成一, 聖一, 精一, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|せいいち(Japanese Hiragana)|セイイチ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 誠 (sei) meaning "sincere, honest, true", 清 (sei) meaning "clear, pure, clean", 成 (sei) meaning "become", 聖 (sei) meaning "holy, sacred" or 精 (sei) meaning "pure, refined" combined with 一 (ichi) meaning "one". This name can be formed from other combinations of kanji as well.

column3: 勢一郎, 制市朗, 制壱朗, 制一朗, 省一郎, 歳一郎, 勢市郎, 成一郎, 整一郎, 星一郎, 晴委智郎, 晴市朗, 正壱郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 勢 (sei) meaning "forces, energy", 一 (ichi) meaning "one" combined with 郎 (rou) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations are possible.Famous bearers are Seiichirou Okuno, a former Japanese football player and Seiichirou Maki, a Japanese professional football player.

column3: せいいん(Japanese Hiragana)|清陰, 星陰, 世陰, 清院, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column12: This name is used as a short form of Germanic names that begin with the element sigu meaning "victory."

column3: 征二郎, 晴二郎, 盛二郎, 成二郎, 誠二郎, 清次郎, 清治郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|せいじろう(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: From Japanese 征 (sei) meaning "subjugate", 晴 (sei) meaning "clear up", 盛 (sei) meaning "boom, prosper", 成 (sei) meaning "turn into, become, grow", 誠 (sei) meaning "sincerity, truth, fidelity" or 清 (sei) meaning "clear, pure, clean" combined with 二 (ji) meaning "two", 次 (ji) meaning "next" or 治 (ji) meaning "reign, rule, calm, peace" and 郎 (rō) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 清十郎, 清重郎, 政十郎, 政重郎, 征十郎, 征重郎, 精十郎, 精重郎, 晴十郎, 晴重郎(Japanese Kanji)|せいじゅうろう(Japanese Hiragana)|セイジュウロウ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name combines 清 (shou, shin, sei, kiyo.i, kiyo.maru, kiyo.meru) meaning "cleanse, exorcise, Manchu dynasty, pure, purify," 政 (shou, sei, matsurigoto, man) meaning "government, politics," 征 (sei) meaning "attack the rebellious, collect taxes, subjugate," 精 (shiyau, shou, sei, kiyo) meaning "energy, excellence, fairy, ghost, purity, refined, skill, vitality" or 晴 (sei, ha.rasu, ha.re, ha.re-, ha.reru, -ba.re) meaning "clear up" with 十 (ji', juu, ju', to, too) meaning "ten" or 重 (juu, chou, e, omo, omo.i, omo.ri, kasa.naru, kasa.neru) meaning "-fold, heap up, heavy, pile of boxes, pile up" and 郎 (ryou, rou, otoko) meaning "son."One bearer of this name was politician and Minister of Transport Seijūrō Arafune (荒舩 清十郎) (1907-1980). Fictional bearers of this name include Seijūrō Akashi (赤司 征十郎), leader of the Rakuzan High basketball team in manga and anime series Kuroko's Basket/Kuroko no Basuke, and Seijūrō Nanami (七海 征十郎) from Hiiragi Academy in the manga and anime series Ultimate Otaku Teacher.This name is rarely given to boys, if given at all.

column3: 盛華, 聖加, 成化, 栖可, 数蔚香, 瀬道郁, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From the Japanese 盛 (sei) meaning "prosper" and 禾 (ka) meaning "cereal, grain, rice plant". Other kanji combinations are usable.
聖 Holy, Sacred. 堅 Strong, healthy.

column3: 星紀, 清記, 栖樹, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 誠 (sei) meaning "sincerity", 栖⁠ (sei) meaning “nest” or 星 (sei) meaning "star" and 記 (ki) meaning "inscription, Kojiki, describe, mention" or 紀 (ki) meaning "narrative, chronicle". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: せいきち(Japanese Hiragana)|栖⁠吉, 成吉, 誠吉, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 成 (sei) meaning "become" or 栖⁠ (sei) meaning “nest” combined with 吉 (kichi) meaning "good fortune". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: せいこう(Japanese Hiragana)|星貢, 聖幸, 成光, 清甲, 正孝, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 聖 (sei) meaning "sacred, holy" combined with 貢 (kou) meaning "support, tribute". Other kanji combinations can be used.
From Japanese 星空 (seikuu) meaning "starry sky", combined with 星 (sei) meaning "star" and 空 (kuu) meaning "sky". Other kanji or kanji combinations can form this name as well.
Meaning unknown. Seilatsatsi is a character in some Sotho tales.
A fairy name of the Aes Sídhe and pleasant people.

column3: 晴真, 星舞, 星磨, 世磨, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 晴 (sei) meaning "clear up", 星 (sei) meaning "star" or 世 (sei) meaning "generations" combined with 真 (ma) meaning "real, genuine", 舞 (ma) meaning "dance" or 磨 (ma) meaning "polish". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 清明, 政明, 晟明, 星明, 西明, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|せいめい(Japanese Hiragana)|セイメイ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Combination of a sei kanji, like 清 meaning "clean, pure, chaste," 政 meaning "rule, government," 晟 meaning "clear," 星 meaning "star" or 西 meaning "west," and a mei kanji, usually 明 meaning "brightness; clarity."This name is rarely used.
From Japanese 清 (sei) meaning "pure" combined with 美 (mi) meaning "beautiful". Other combinations of kanji characters are also possible.

column3: 星夢, 成夢, 晴夢, 清務, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|せいむ(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: From Japanese 星 (sei) meaning "star" combined with 夢 (mu) meaning "dream". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 세인(Korean Hangul)|世人, 世仁, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 世 (se) meaning "world, generation" combined with 人 (in) meaning "person, mankind, people" or 仁 (in) meaning "compassionate". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
A Lithuanian form of the Yiddish Shayna, a notable bearer was Polish-Lithuanian artist, Šeina Efron (1909-1983)

column3: セイナ(Japanese Katakana)|聖南, 聖奈, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 成 (sei) meaning "to become" or 栖 (sei) meaning "nest" combined with 奈 (na) meaning "what". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Alternate transcription of Burmese စိန် (see Sein).

column3: 星乃, 静乃, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 星 (sei) meaning "star" or 静 (sei) meaning "calm, quiet, silent" combined with 乃 (no), a possessive particle. Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.

column3: 誠之佑, 誠之介, 聖之助, 精之丞, 静之佑, 斉之助, 晴之佑, 星之祐, 星之丞, 成之介, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 誠 (sei) meaning "sincerity", 之 (no), a possessive marker combined with 佑 (suke) meaning "to help, rescue, save". Other kanji combinations are also possible.
The Japanese name of the Queen Mother of the West, or Xiwangmu.
Seir, meaning "Rough, hairy." It is sometimes used as an alternative term for a goat, as in Seir La'Azazel (שעיר לעזאזל - scapegoat).

column3: セイラ(Japanese Katakana)|せいら(Japanese Hiragana)|世楽, 瀬依良, 世依羅, 聖羅, 世良, 勢良, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 世 (sei) meaning "generation, world, society" or 勢 (sei) meaning "energy, power, force, vigour" combined with 楽 (ra) meaning "comfort, music" or 羅 (ra) meaning "thin silk, silk gauze, lightweight fabric or clothing, Latin". Other kanji combinations are possible.For females the usage of this name is most likely influenced by the name Sarah or Sara.

column3: 星蘭, 青蘭, 静蘭, 聖蘭, 晴瀾, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|Սեյրան(Armenian)|Сейран(Crimean Tatar)
column12: From Japanese 星 (sei) meaning "star" or 青 (sei) meaning "blue" combined with 蘭 (ran) meaning "orchid". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Derived from Welsh serennu meaning "sparkling (like stars)", compare Seren.
Possibly related to Welsh siriol meaning "joyful". This name was borne by an early 6th-century saint.

column3: 惺朗, 青朗, 聖朗, 清朗, 靖朗, 晴朗, 済朗, 勢朗, 正朗, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 惺 (sei) meaning "intelligent, clever, astute", 青 (sei) meaning "blue", 聖 (sei) meaning "holy, sacred", 清 (sei) meaning "pure", 靖 (sei) meaning "peaceful, calm, easygoing", 晴 (sei) meaning "clear up", 済 (sei) meaning "settle, finish, feel at ease", 勢 (sei) meaning "forces, energy, military strength" or 正 (sei) meaning "first (month of the lunar year)" combined with 朗 (rou) meaning "bright, clear". Other combinations of kanji characters are also possible.As a word, Seirou (晴朗) means "serenity, clarity (of the weather)".

column3: 青龍, 青竜, 青流, 清龍, 清竜, 清流, 聖龍, 聖竜, 聖流(Japanese Kanji)|せいりゅう(Japanese Hiragana)|セイリュウ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name combines 青 (shou, sei, ao, ao-, ao.i) meaning "blue, green," 清 (shou, shin, sei, kiyo.i, kiyo.maru, kiyo.meru) meaning "cleanse, exorcise, pure, purify, Manchu dynasty" or 聖 (shou, sei, hijiri) meaning "holy, master, priest, sage, saint" with 龍 (ryuu, ryou, rou, tatsu) meaning "dragon, imperial," 竜 (ryuu, ryou, rou, ise, tatsu) meaning "dragon, imperial" or 流 (ryuu, ru, naga.su, -naga.su, naga.re, naga.reru) meaning "a sink, current, flow, forfeit."This name coincides with the Blue/Azure Dragon (青竜/青龍) which is a god said to rule the eastern heavens and an auspicious creature in Chinese mythology. It also coincides with the word of the same name (清流) meaning "clear stream."

column3: 青咲, 誓作, 誠策, 聖作, 靖作, 清策, 正, 星作, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 青 (sei) meaning "blue" combined with 咲 (saku) meaning "blossom". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 勢至(Japanese Kanji)|せいし(Japanese Hiragana)|聖史, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 勢 (sei) meaning "force, strength" and 至 (shi) meaning "reach, arrive", a calque of Sanskrit महास्थामप्राप्त (mahāsthāmaprāpta). This is the Japanese name for the bodhisattva Mahasthamaprapta.

column3: 精七郎, 誠七郎, 清七郎, 正七郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 精 (sei) meaning "essence", 七 (shichi) meaning "seven" combined with 郎 (rou) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 誠士郎, 征四郎, 征士郎, 星史郎, 清史郎(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 誠 (sei) meaning "sincerity", 士 (shi) meaning "samurai, warrior" combined with 郎 (rou) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 星水, 正水, 清水, 西水, 静水, 靜水, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 星 (sei) meaning "star", 正 (sei) meaning "first (month of the lunar year)", 清 (sei) meaning "pure", 西 (sei) meaning "west" or 静, 靜 (sei) meaning "calm, quiet, silent" combined with 水 (sui) meaning "water". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Albanian, Kazakh, and Crimean Tatar form of Sayyid.

column3: せいた(Japanese Hiragana)|セイタ(Japanese Katakana)|済大, 惺多, 制多, 勢大, 請汰, 情堪, 凄太, 性太, 誓妥, 醒大, 製汰, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 歳 (sei) meaning "year", 省 (sei) meaning "Chinese province, government ministry", or 静 (sei) meaning "quiet, calm, silent" combined with 太 (ta) meaning "thick, big", 大 (ta) meaning "big, great" or 多 (ta) meaning "many, much". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 清太郎, 栖太郎, 整太郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 整 (sei) meaning "arrange, settle, organize", 太 (ta) meaning "thick, big, great" and 郎 (rō) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: せいじたろ(Japanese Hiragana)|セイタロタ(Japanese Katakana)|勢多朗, 省太郎, 性田朗, 制多郎, 盛太郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 誓 (sei) meaning "swear, vow, pledge", 多 (ta) meaning "many, much" combined with 朗 (rou) meaning "bright, clear". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Meaning unknown, though it may be related to Seit. In the Kyrgyz epic of Manas, Seitek is the grandson of the legedendary hero Manas and son of Semetey.
Etymology unknown.Seithenyn (sometimes spelt Seithennin), sometimes known as Seithenyn of the Feeble Mind, is a figure from Welsh legend, apparently contemporary with King Gwyddno Garanhir.
From Arabic سَيِّد (sayyid) meaning "lord, master" and نَبِيّ (nabiyy) meaning "prophet".

column3: 星斗, 聖斗, 星吐, 征登, 征世, 青杜, 誠人, 彗斗, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 星 (sei) meaning "star" combined with 斗 (to), which refers to a Chinese constellation. Other kanji combinations are also possible.

column3: せいや(Japanese Hiragana)|星夜, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 星 (sei) meaning "dot, star" combined with 夜 (ya) meaning "night". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 聖代, 青余, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 聖 (sei) meaning "holy, sacred" combined with 代 (yo) meaning "generation". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Japanese 正 (sei) meaning "first (month of the lunar year)" combined with 諭 (yu) meaning "proclaim, instruct". Other combinations of kanji characters are also possible.
From Japanese 靖 (sei) meaning "peaceful, calm, easygoing" combined with 雄 (yuu) meaning "hero, manly". Other combinations of kanji characters are also possible.

column3: せいぞう(Japanese Hiragana)|セイゾウ(Japanese Katakana)|晴三, 星造, 成蔵, 整三, 聖造, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 誠 (sei) meaning "sincere, honest, true" or 精 (sei) meaning "pure, refined" combined with 蔵 (zō) meaning "to hide". Other kanji combinations are possible.
The given name of the German-Australian musician Seja Vogel.
Lucius Aelius Sejanus (20 BC – 18 October AD 31), commonly known as Sejanus, was a Roman soldier, friend and confidant of the Roman Emperor Tiberius.
Combinations of the name Selena and Jayda.

Derived from Korean 세(se) meaning "three" or Korean Hanja 世(se) meaning "world, lineage, generation" combined with 眞(jin) meaning "genuine, true" or 珍(jin) meaning "precious, rare". Other hanja combinations can also form this name.
From Sino-Korean 世 (se) meaning "world" and 種 (jong) meaning "sort, type, kind".
Danish word meaning "victory". From Old Norse sigr.
Taken from the nickname, which originated as a pet form of the word sestra meaning ''sister''.

column3: せかい(Japanese Hiragana)|世快, 世界, 世楷, 聖海, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From the Japanese word 世界 (sekai) meaning "world". Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name, such as 世 (se) meaning "world" or 聖 (se) meaning "holy, saint, sage, master, priest" combined with 快 (kai) meaning "cheerful, pleasant, agreeable, comfortable", 界 (kai) meaning "boundary", 楷 (kai) meaning "square character style, correctness" or 海 (kai) meaning "sea, ocean".This is borne by Sekai Yamamoto (1991-), a Japanese dancer better known by his stage name Exile Sekai.
Means "be happy, boisterous" or "laugh" in Chewa and Tumbuka.

Sekendiz is an archaic, medieval Turkic astronomical name meaning "the Saturn planet." It is one of the oldest recorded names for the ringed planet within the early Turkic stellar mapping tradition, preserved in late Old Turkic and Middle Turkic manuscripts.Turkic lexicons, most notably highlighted by the 11th-century scholar Kaşgarlı Mahmud in the Divanü Lügati't-Türk, where it represents the furthest visible celestial boundary in medieval Turkic astronomy.For decades, Eurocentric philologists attempted to link Sekendiz to the Indo-European/Latin root Secundus (second), proposing it was a loanword representing a planetary order. However, modern Turkic historical linguistics has thoroughly disproven the Indo-European Secundus theory by offering irrefutable morphological proof rooted in native Turkic verb structures. The strongest evidence lies in the dual-layered combination of the numeral sekiz (eight) and the core Turkic verb sek- (to hop, leap, step over, or move in distinct intervals).Astronomically, to the naked eye of ancient steppe observers, Saturn's retrograde motion appears as though the planet is "stepping or skipping" (sek-mek) across the constellations. Furthermore, in early Turkic cosmology, Saturn was categorized as the "eighth station" or the regulator of the eighth cosmic sphere beyond the visible inner planets, tying it numerically to sekiz. The suffix -diz is a highly archaic nominalizer used specifically for celestial and atmospheric phenomena (cognate with yıldız - star, and gündüz - daytime). Thus, Sekendiz translates morphologically to "The skipping eighth celestial body."For parents, this rare and deeply academic name signifies structured wisdom, cosmic endurance, and a brilliant mind capable of making giant leaps in life while maintaining perfect alignment and inner discipline.

From Egyptian zkr, possibly derived from skr "to clean the mouth", in reference to a funerary ritual, or from sy-k-ri "hurry to me", a cry from Osiris to Isis. Another suggested meaning is "the adorned one". This was the name of an Egyptian underworld deity with the head of a hawk or falcon, also associated with agriculture and goldsmithing.
Name of a Berber King who rebelled against the Arabs
From the Turkish şeker “sugar” and naz meaning "coy".
From Ottoman Turkish Şekerpare or Şeker-pare meaning "a piece of sugar" (from words şeker - "sugar" and pare-"piece"), "like sugar", "very sweet".

From Egyptian sḫm-jb-pr.n-mꜣꜥt "the one daring of heart for whom Maat has come forth" or "the one daring of heart going forth for Maat", derived from the Egyptian sḫm "powerful", jb "heart, mind", either pr.n "has gone forth" or pr n "going forth for", and the Egyptian Goddess Maat from mꜣꜥt. This is the name of a 2nd-century early Egyptian pharaoh who was possibly the same person as Seth-Peribsen.
Ancient Egyptian masculine name meaning "Powerful is the ka of Re".

From Egyptian sḫm-ẖt, possibly meaning "(the one who is) powerful of torso", from Egyptian sḫm "powerful" and ẖt "torso". This was the name of an ancient Egyptian pharaoh of the 3rd Dynasty during the Old Kingdom.
Ancient Egyptian masculine name meaning "Mighty Re, he who protects the Two Lands"
Ancient Egyptian masculine name meaning "the Might of Re which rescues Thebes".

From Egyptian sḫm-pr.n-rꜥ, possibly meaning "(the one) daring forth to Ra", from Egyptian sḫm "powerful" combined with prj "to come forth" combined with the Egyptian God Ra. This was the name of an Egyptian pharaoh of the 14th Dynasty of Egypt during the Second Intermediate Period.
Derived from the Georgian noun სეხნია (sekhnia) meaning "namesake".
From the Buryat сэхэ (sekhe) meaning "directly, straight, frank, decisively" or "truth".
From 積 (Seki) meaning “Accumulated” and 怒 (Do) meaning “Anger”.This character is known from Demon Slayer most commonly.

column3: 雪花, 雪火, 雪佳, 石花, 関華, 雪舸, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 雪花 (sekka) meaning "snowflake". Other kanji or kanji combinations can form this name as well.
Ukrainian form of Syncletica. Sekleta Lymerykha is a character in comedy film "Chasing Two Hares" based on a play by Mykhailo Starytsky.

column12: From Japanese 聖 (se) meaning "holy, sacred", 香 (ko) meaning "fragrance" combined with 愛 (a) meaning "love, affection". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Fula form of the Arabic title Sheikh.
Hellenized form of Secundus. This name was borne by a Greek Cynic or Neopythagorean philosopher from the 2nd century AD.
From Thai เสก (sek) meaning "create, cause (through supernatural means)" and สันต์ (san) meaning "quiet, peaceful, calm".
Kashubian form of Sixtus via Polish Sykstus.
Meaning as of yet unknown. A notable bearer of this name was the Montenegrin nationalist and politician Sekula Drljević (1884-1945).
Bosnian and Croatian form of Secundus.
Possibly an elaborated form of Sekunda.
Etymology uncertain, possibly from the Awajún name for a species of vine or from the Awajún sekúut meaning "vanilla".
Greenlandic name meaning "egg yolk" or "egg still inside the bird which hasn't yet developed a hard shell".
from kasem language in northern part of Ghana that is upper east region of Ghana in the west africa
Meaning unknown. This was the name of the Vainakh god of stars, thunder, and lightning. He is usually portrayed as an evil and cruel god who lives on the peak of Mount Kazbek with his fire chariot.
Possibly from Indonesian and Malay selamat meaning "safe, healthy, secure" or perhaps a form of the name Salama.
Means "safe, healthy, secure" in Indonesian and Malay, ultimately from Arabic سلامات (salamat).

Variant of Shealtiel and Salathiel. This is the name of one of the seven Archangels of the Presence who is venerated in Eastern Orthodoxy and Eastern Catholicism. "Prayer of God" is an alternative translation of the name.

Means "light-bearing" in Ancient Greek, derived from σέλας (selas) meaning "light, brightness, shine" and φέρω (phero) meaning "to carry, to bear". This was an epithet of the Greek moon goddess Artemis.
Derived from Haitian Creole se "that is; it is" and lavi "life".
Variant of Selavi influenced by French vie "life".
Derived from sel meaning "downpour" and bibi meaning "learned woman".
English and German variant of Zelda 2, the short form of Griselda, as well as a variant of Zelda 1, the feminine form of Selig, occasionally found among Yiddish speakers in German-speaking areas.
Derived from Haitian Creole sèl "alone; only" combined with French dieu "god".
Means "from the house on the hill" or "from the willow valley".
Means "judge or plan carefully" in Ijaw.
Derived from the Old English elements sele "manor" and burg "fortress"(Compare Selwyn).
Means "sword hero" in Mongolian, from сэлэм (selem) meaning "sword, sabre" and баатар (baatar) meaning "hero".

Uncertain origin, perhaps related to Ancient Greek σέλας (selas) meaning "light, flame, shine". In Greek mythology, Selemnos was a mortal shepherd beloved by the nymph of a spring where he grazed his sheep, Argyra. When she abandoned him as he grew older and less beautiful, Selemnos wasted away from grief, and the goddess Aphrodite took pity on him by transforming him into a river. He still pined for Argyra, so Aphrodite erased his memories of her, and the Selemnos river became known as a place where people could attempt to wash away unwanted love and passion.
Possibly a variant of Selena or Celinda.

Derived from the Selenge (or Selenga) River, which runs through Mongolia and Russia. The name likely stems from the Mongolian verb сэлэх (seleh) meaning "to swim", though another theory suggests it originated with Evenki сэлэ (sele) "iron" and the possessive suffix -nge.
From the name of the Selenge River and the Mongolian word мөрөн (mörön) meaning "river".
From the name of the Selenge River and the Mongolian word сайхан (saikhan) meaning "nice, beautiful, handsome".
Hispanic variant of Selene. Also see Selenia, Selenis. This was used for the character Seleni Aristizábal on the Colombian television series La promesa (2013).
Elaboration of Selene. In Italy, this form is prevalent in the region of Lombardy.
Fictional inhabitant of the moon, from the story "The First Men in the Moon".

Derived from the Old English elements sele "hall, manor" and ræd "advice, counsel, wisdom". Alternatively, the first element could be from sæl "happiness, prosperity" or the related sel "good, noble". This was the name of an 8th century King of Essex.
Invented by Alexandra Christo for a witch in her book Princess of Souls, released in 2022.
Variant transcription of Zillethai.This transcription is used in the Douay-Rheims Catholic Bible.
Derived from the Old English element sele "manor" and þryð "strength" (Compare Selwyn).
Italian, Spanish and Portuguese form of Seleucus.
Bosnian and Croatian form of Seleucus.
Possibly an invented name inspired by Selena.
Derived from the Old English elements sele "hall, house, manor" (from saliz) and wine "friend". This name gave rise to both the given name and surname of Selwyn.
Variant of Zelfa, from Biblical name Zelpha, or variant of Selva meaning "forest, wood" in Spanish, Portuguese, and Italian.
Derived from Latvian selga "deep sea; open sea".
Segars = Selgas + Ars = Plower of the Sea

Names of Various Frankish Nobles like Seliger Relative of Rudolph III. of Burgundy or Seliger of GrenchenNames is used in close relation to the Rudolphian Dynasty.Probably a Kombination of Selig - blessed and Heri-army Could also be a Kombination of Sala Dark or Hall and ger meaning Speer
In Lithuanian mythology, this is the name of one of the daughters of Saulė.
Derived from the Slavic elements seliti, "to move, to migrate" and mir meaning "peace".The first known Selimir was a legendary 7th century Serbian ruler Selimir I (660 - 680).
Derived from Korean 세(se) meaning "three" or Korean Hanja 世(se) meaning "world, lineage, generation" combined with 粼(lin) meaning "clear water".

The name "Selinay" can be broken down into two parts:"Selin" which is derived from "Sel," meaning "stream" or "flood" in Turkish."Ay" means "moon" in Turkish. So, "Selinay" could be interpreted as "Moon of the Stream" or "Moon of the Flood."
This given name can be a Dutch variant of Sieglinde as well as be a combination of Selina with Linde.

Probably derived from the toponym Σελινούς (Selinous), itself meaning "full of celery" from Ancient Greek σέλινον (selinon) "celery". This was the name of a king of Aegalea (present-day Aigio) in Greek mythology, who resolved his war with Ion by offering him his only daughter Helice as wife.
Etymology uncertain, although it is likely a form of Salome. It is attested in 16th Century England.
Derived from the word seraph, ultimately from Hebrew שרפים‎ (serafim) (see Seraphina). It is the name of a character in the fantasy role-playing franchise 'Fire Emblem'.
From the Turkish sel meaning "flood" and ışıl ışıl meaning "sparkling, radiant".
From the Turkish sel meaning "flood" and ışın meaning "ray, beam, gleam".
Variant of Celia. It also means "elder (plant)" in Finnish.
From sel meaning "flood, stream" combined with jān meaning "soul, life"
Possibly a Polish Yiddish diminutive of Selda, found in documents from the early 1800s regarding contemporary Yiddish-speakers in Poland.

Possibly a Low German diminutive of names containing the Old High German element salo "dark-coloured, dirty gray" (related to Old Norse sölr "sun-coloured, dirty yellow, sallow"), but this is not known for certain.
A creature from Norse or Celtic mythology that is able to shapeshift between human and seal form. Origin as a name is unknown.
Variant of Sälla as well as a Norwegian diminutive of Cecilia.
Transferred use of the surname Sellers.

From ”sällt liv” meaning ”happy life”.This name was invented in 1815 by the father of Swedish painter Egron Sellif Lundgren, with both Egron and Sellif being based on the saying ”äg ron (och ett) sällt liv” meaning ”own the calm (and a) happy life”.
Means "crying" in Sesotho and Setswana. It is the masculine form of Selloane/Sellwane.
Means "crying" in Sesotho, from sellwana or selloana, the diminutive of sello, with the name suffix -e. It is the feminine form of Sello.
Medieval variant of Solomon. It was recorded in 16th-century Frankfurt, Germany.
Transferred use of the surname Selmer.
Elaborated form of Selma 1 as well as a feminine form of Selmer.
From the Turkish sel meaning "flood" and nur meaning "light".
Komi Sélom Klassou is Prime Minister of Togo.
A Western African name used for both genders.
Turkish form of Shlomtzion, used to refer to the historical Judaean queen commonly known as Salome Alexandra in English.
Derived from French selon "according to" and dieu "god".
Means "God loves me" or "divine love" in Ewe.
Alternate transcription of Arabic سلوى (see Salwa), chiefly used in Algeria and Morocco.
Diminutive of Zelpha. A notable character is Selphie Tilmitt from Final Fantasy VIII, and a side character from the Square Enix Disney game "Kingdom Hearts".
Alternate transcription of Arabic سلسبيل (see Salsabil) chiefly used in North Africa.
Name of brazilian actor Selton Mello (Passos, Minas Gerais, 30/12/1972). Selton played Dom Pedro II, Emperor of Brazil, in the soap novel Nos Tempos do Imperador.
Turkish spelling of the Arabic name Salwa. This name is popular in Arabic-speaking countries. It's uncommon in non-Arabic-speaking countries.
Derived from the words செல்வம் (celvam), meaning "wealth", and the Sanskrit term कुमार (kumāra), meaning "prince".

This is a typical Tamil name of persons, and is mostly masculine, rarely used also in the feminine. However, 'Selvan' would be only masculine; and 'Selvi' would be only feminine. 'Selvam' in poetic Tamil means, 'wealth', or 'something precious'. In Tamil literature, wealth is spoken of as being various types: material wealth, and wisdom and education. Persons can be named as 'Wealth of Wisdom', which would be: 'Gnanaselvam' -ஞானசெல்வம். The latter form could be used for boys and girls.
From Tamil செல்வம் (selvam) meaning "wealth, riches, prosperity". This is a Tamil name for the Hindu goddess Lakshmi.
Meaning uncertain, used especially in Central America.
Alternate transcription of Arabic سلوى (see Salwa).
Derived from Old English sælig "happy, blessed". (As a Jewish name it can be considered a Judeo-Anglo-Norman Contage of the Yiddish name Zelda 1).

Kazakh feminine given name of unknown meaning. It might possibly be an invented name, either from scratch or by combining two existing given names (in which case one of those names is probably Elvira).
Variant of Celidoine, king of Scotland, son of the first Nascien and Flegentine, and ancestor of Lancelot and Galahad.
Welsh form of Solomon via Old Welsh Seleu. Selyf ap Cynan, also known as Selyf Sarffgadau, (died 616) appears in Old Welsh genealogies as an early 7th-century King of Powys, the son of Cynan Garwyn.
Used in GRR. Martin's "A song of ice and fire". Selyse Baratheon, born Selyse Florent, is Stannis Baratheon's wife and she is the mother of Shireen. Her name may come from Elise and Selene.

Of Syriac Aramaic origin, the name Semaan belongs to the Semitic Aramaic dialect of northern Iraq and Syria of the second century C.E."Semaan" means "he who listens". Its equivalent in Hebrew is Shimeon.It is a very common name for Christians in the Middle East. It is still considered as one of the earliest names in Syriac Christendom.Simon Peter, also known as St. Peter, is known as Semaan Butrus to Mideastern Christian adherents.
From the Turkish sema meaning "sky" and can meaning "spirit, soul".
From the Turkish sema meaning "sky" and gül meaning "rose".
Portuguese and Spanish form of Shemaiah.
Unknown origin. Possibly an early version of Samantha. Semanthe is a character in 'Aglaura' (1637) a stage play written by Sir John Suckling.

Derived from the French noun sémaphore meaning "semaphore", which is a visual signalling system. The word is ultimately derived from the ancient Greek words σῆμα (sema) meaning "sign, mark, token" and φέρω (phero) meaning "to bear, to carry". As such, the original meaning of the word is roughly "the sign-bearer".In French literature, Sémaphore is the name of the owner of the corpulent talking dog Cubitus, who is the main character of the Franco-Belgian comic Cubitus, which was created in 1968 by the Belgian/Walloon cartoonist Dupa (1945-2000). In the Dutch-speaking part of Belgium, namely Flanders, Sémaphore is known as Semafoor.

Likely derived from Javanese samar meaning "vague, dim, obscure, mysterious". In Javanese mythology this is the name of a divine jester depicted as having a short stature and a large rear figure. He is prominently featured in traditional shadow puppet plays (wayang) and is considered the guardian spirit of the island of Java.
From Egyptian smꜣ.t meaning "the companion", derived from zmꜣ "to join, unite" and the suffix .t.
Variant transcription of Zillethai, as used in 1 Chronicles 12:20.This transcription is used in English translations of the Septuagint Bible.
Derived from Basque seme "son". It was recorded as a given name in the 13th and 14th centuries.
Means "while I was wishing" in Amharic.
One of Jesus' ancestors from Luke 3:26.
Russian variant transcription and Dutch form of Semyon.
Feminine form of both Seme and Semeno.
Possibly derived from Romanian semen "fellow human being" (compare Surata).
Of debated origin and meaning. While some modern-day academics consider this name a variant of Seme, other theorize a derivation from Simon 1 (compare Ximeno).
Variant of Semena, recorded in the 12th century.
ethiopian name. meaning Everything goes fine

From Egyptian smr-ẖt meaning "friend of the gods", from Egyptian smr “royal friend, courtier” and ẖt “group of gods”. This was the Horus name of an early Egyptian king who ruled during the First Dynasty.
From the name of the son of Manas in the epynominous Epic poem.
Bosnian form of Shamsuddin. A bearer of this name is the Bosnian writer Semezdin Mehmedinović.
From Sino-Korean 世 (se) meaning "world, era, generation" combined with 美 (mi) meaning "beautiful". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
Derived from a Guanche title meaning "honorable".
A rare medieval name of uncertain origin.
Derived from Korean 세(se) meaning "three" or Korean Hanja 世(se) meaning "world, generation" combined with 旻(min) meaning "sky, heaven" or 暋(min) meaning "strong".
Estonian and German transcription of Russian Семён (see Semyon).
Short form of Semme, where the diminutive suffix ke has been added to the name.
Means "bracelet" in Manchu. This was the personal name of Concubine Muktu, who was a consort of the Shunzhi Emperor, and the mother of his eighth son Yonggan.
Ukrainian diminutive or alternative form of Semen.
Derived from Ancient Greek σεμνός (semnos) meaning "revered, august, venerable, holy" or "solemn, grave, haughty".
Of unknown meaning. Possibly related to the Etruscan word 'semna' meaning "trace, track (way, passage)".
Possibly derived from the Ancient Greek name Σέμνη (Semne), from σεμνός (semnos) meaning "revered, august, venerable, holy" or "solemn, grave, haughty".
Derives from Simeon or Simas or Simão
Possibly a variant of Simon 2. Alternatively, perhaps derived from Ancient Greek σῆμα (sema) meaning "sign, mark, token".

In Roman mythology, Semonia was the goddess of sowing. She belonged to a group of agricultural deities which also comprised Setia (or Seja) and Segetia. Their names are derived from the same stem as the Latin verb sero "to sow".This ancient deity, associated with crops and sowing,is of possible Roman or Sabine origin and worship. She is usually attested with the epithet Salus Semonia.

Means "son of Semon", from the Ancient Greek name Σήμων (Semon) and the patronymic suffix ἴδης (ides). Semonides was the name of at least two Ancient Greek poets, both of whom may have also written their names as Σιμωνίδης (see Simonides).
Means "dark warrior, black warrior" in Mari.
Derived from Latin semper meaning "forever, always". It also coincides with the surname Semper. It has been occasionally used as a given name from the 18th century onwards.
Derived from Latin semper meaning "always" and from Latin bella meaning "beautiful, charming, pleasant".
Derived from Latin semper meaning "always" and Latin bona meaning "good, kind, right, pleasant; valid, useful, healthy".
Derivative of Sempronia. This was the name of an early martyr and saint.
Italian and Spanish form of Sempronius. This is the name of a character in the Spanish novel 'La Celestina' (1499).
Roman family name, possibly derived from Latin sempiternus meaning "eternal".

Variant transcription of Shimri, as used in 1 Chronicles 4:37 and 1 Chronicles 26:10.This transcription is used in the Douay-Rheims Catholic Bible and English translations of the Septuagint Bible (1 Chronicles 4:37 only).
Derived from the Turkish word şems meaning "sun", itself derived from the Arabic شمس (see Shams).
A common name used among the Jos Plateau people of Nigeria. Means "stay together".
Means "cheeks like the sun" in Ottoman Turkish.
From Arabic شمس (shams) meaning "sun" and Persian پری (pari) meaning "fairy".
Old Danish and modern form of Sæmundr and variant of Sigmund.

Uncertain etymology. This was the name of a nymph in Greek mythology, the eponym of the town Symestra in ancient Thrace. In some accounts she was the mother of king Byzas, though in others she was instead the foster-mother of Keroessa, who then had Byzas by the god Poseidon.
Means "a kind of tree (Madhuca pasquieri)" in Vietnamese.
Variant of Thịnh, from a Vietnamese transcription of the Teochew pronunciation of Chinese 盛 (sển).

column12: From Japanese 世 (se) meaning "world" or 聖 (se) meaning "holy, sacred", 和 (na) meaning "peace, harmony, Japan", 奈 (na) meaning "apple tree" or 那 (na) meaning "what" combined with 心 (ko) meaning "heart, mind, soul" or 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Meaning unknown. This was the name of the wife of Gruffudd ap Llywelyn, the firstborn son of Llywelyn the Great.
Means "happy, content, loved" in Indonesian or "easy" in Malay.

From the name of the patron saint of Zennor, a village in Cornwall, which is of obscure origin. Conceivably it may be derived from the Breton name Azenor or the old Celtic Senovara. According to local legend Saint Senara was originally Princess Azenor of Brest in Lower Brittany, the mother of Saint Budoc. She is also said to have been a mermaid before her conversion (though even after becoming a Christian, "she continued to pine for the sea"). This name was given to 52 girls born in England and Wales in the years 1916-2005.
Derived from someone serving in a senate (senatus) from Latin senex "old man". Used by a 4th century bishop of Milan.
Ancient Egyptian masculine name derived from the element snb meaning “to be healthy”.
Senbonzakura means 'One thousand cherry blossoms' or 'One thousand cherry trees'.Senbonzakura is the zanpaku-to of Byakuya Kuchiki, in the popular Anime/manga Bleach, by Tite Kubo.
Alternate transcription of Tamil செந்தில் (see Senthil).
Feminine form of Sender, possibly making it the Yiddish form of Sandra, Alexandra, or Aleksandra.
Ancient Egyptian feminine name meaning "Health is with her".
From Egyptian snb-n.j meaning "be healthy for me".
From Egyptian snb.tjsj, possibly meaning "she is healthy", derived from snb "health; to heal, be healthy" and a combination of tj "you; she, her, they" and sj "she, her, hers".

A Roman cognomen meaning "old man" in Latin, from Latin senex "old" and -io, a nickname-forming suffix. Herennius Senecio ( -93) was among the Stoic Opposition to the emperor Domitian, under whose rule he was executed.
Means "aged, very old" in Latin. In Roman mythology, Senectus was a god of old age and the Roman equivalent of Geras.
From Egyptian snd meaning "fear". This was the throne name of an early Egyptian pharaoh of the 2nd dynasty who was possibly the same person as Seth-Peribsen.
Possibly from Old Occitan sener "sir" and garda "to maintain".
Armenian form of Sennacherib. Senekerim-Hovhannes Artsruni (-1025/1027) was the sixth and last King of Vaspurakan, from the Artsruni dynasty.
Spanish, Asturian and Galician form of Sennen.
Ancient Egyptian masculine name meaning "mother's brother".
French and Guernésiais form of Seneca.

Means "moonlight" from Lao ແສງ (seng) meaning "light" and ເດືອນ (deuane) meaning "moon".
From Lao ແສງ (seng) meaning "light" and ແກ້ວ (keo) meaning "gem, jewel".

From Lao ແສງ (seng) meaning "light" and ມະນີ (many) meaning "gem, jewel".

Sengqu Seli (Šiñko Šäli Tutuñ) represents the pinnacle of the synthesis between the Turkic literary spirit and the Buddhist-Chinese administrative culture in the Kocho Uyghur Khanate. The name is a composite title: Sengqu is a phonetic adaptation of the Chinese Shèngguāng (勝光, "Superior Light"), while Seli is derived from the Sanskrit Ācārya (via Chinese shélí), signifying a religious master. Tutuñ is an administrative title for a high-ranking official or supervisor.As a translator and poet, he was the intellectual architect of the Altun Yaruk (Golden Light Sutra), transforming abstract Buddhist philosophy into a rhythmic, aesthetically rich Old Uyghur. His work in translating the Hsüan-tsang Biography provided not only religious guidance but also a historical map of 7th-century Turkic life. Rashid Rahmeti Arat identifies him as one of the first "Great Artist" figures of Turkic literature, noting that his prose displays a level of sophistication previously thought unattainable in the period. His legacy is the maturation of the Turkic language into a medium capable of expressing high philosophical, metaphysical, and historical concepts.
From Lao ແສງ (saeng) meaning "light" and ສະຫວັນ (savanh) meaning "heaven, paradise".
From Lao ແສງ (seng) meaning "light" and ທອງ (thong) meaning "gold".
