From 千 (sen) meaning "hundred" and 姫 (hime) or 妃 (hime) meaning "princess".
Variant and feminine form of Seneca.

column3: 仙一, 仙壱, 仙市, 千一, 千壱, 千市, 宣一, 宣壱, 宣市, 専一, 泉一, 泉壱, 泉市, 潜一, 銑一, 閃一, 鮮一, 仟一, 愃一, 沾一, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 仙 (sen) meaning "immortal, transcendent, celestial being, fairy", 千 (sen) meaning "thousand", 宣 (sen) meaning "proclaim, say, announce", 専 (sen) meaning "specialty, exclusive, mainly, solely", 泉 (sen) meaning "spring, fountain", 潜 (sen) meaning "submerge, conceal, hide, lower (voice), hush", 銑 (sen) meaning "pig iron", 仟 (sen) meaning "thousand", 愃 (sen) meaning "abundant, generous" or 沾 (sen) meaning "moisten, wet, soak, touch" combined with 一 (ichi) meaning "one", 壱 (ichi) meaning "one (in documents)" or 市 (ichi) meaning "market, city, town". Other kanji combinations are possible.A famous bearer is Senichi Hoshino, a former Japanese professional baseball player and current manager.
Possibly a rare feminine form of Seneca or a variant of Sinikka.
Means "Monday" in Indonesian and Malay, ultimately from Arabic الِاثْنَيْنِ (al-iṯnayn).
Means "evening" in Indonesian, from Sanskrit संध्या (saṃdhyā), meaning "evening, twilight".
From the Chinese 森 (sēn) meaning "forest" and 姣 (jiāo) meaning "beautiful, handsome".
From the Chinese 森 (sēn) meaning "forest" and 婧 (jìng) meaning "modest".

column3: 千珠, 千重, 千寿, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 千 (sen) meaning "thousand" and 珠 (ju) meaning "jewel, gem, pearl". Other kanji combinations can be used.
From the Chinese 森 (sēn) meaning "forest" and 娟 (juān) meaning "beautiful, graceful".

column3: 茜花, 茜香, 仙果, 仙華, 千架, 千花, 千賀, 千叶, 扇歌, 扇華, 扇香, 泉下, 泉華, 旋花, 仙花, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 茜 (sen) meaning "deep red, dye from the rubia plant", 仙 (sen) meaning "immortal, transcendent, celestial being, fairy", 千 (sen) meaning "thousand", 扇 (sen) meaning "fan, folding fan" or 泉 (sen) meaning "spring, fountain" combined with 花 (ka) or 華 (ka) both meaning "flower", 香 (ka) meaning "fragrance", 果 (ka) meaning "fruit, reward, carry out, achieve, complete, end, finish, succeed", 架 (ka) meaning "erect, frame, mount, support, shelf, construct", 賀 (ka) meaning "congratulations, joy", 叶 (ka) meaning "grant, answer", 歌 (ka) meaning "song, sing" or 下 (ka) meaning "below, down, descend, give, low, inferior". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 千姫, 仙姫, 千喜, 鮮姫, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 千 (sen) meaning "thousand" or 仙 (sen) meaning "immortal, transcendent, celestial being, fairy" combined with 姫 (ki) meaning "princess".

column3: 仙狐, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|せんこ(Japanese Hiragana)|セン コ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 仙 (sen) meaning "sage, hermit" and 狐 (ko) meaning "fox" (Kan-on reading).

column3: せんく(Japanese Hiragana)|センク(Japanese Katakana)|千庫, 茜空, 泉焚, 扇久, 仙招, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: Spelled with Japanese 旋 (sen) meaning "rotate, go round" and 庫 (ku) meaning "warehouse". Other kanji combinations are possible.A notable bearer is Senku Ishigami (石神 千空), the main protagonist from the popular 'Dr. Stone' manga series.
From the Chinese 森 (sēn) meaning "forest" and 兰 (lán) meaning "orchid".
From the Chinese 森 (sēn) meaning "forest" and 丽 (lì) meaning "beautiful".
From the Chinese 森 (sēn) meaning "forest" and 玲 (líng) meaning "tinkling of jade".

column3: 茜美, 千美, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 茜 (sen) meaning "deep red, dye from the rubia plant" or 千 (sen) meaning "thousand" combined with 美 (mi) meaning "beautiful". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: せんな(Japanese Hiragana)|センナ(Japanese Katakana)|川奏, 鮮夏, 仙梛, 宣農, 千凪, 撰摩, 泉納, 扇汝, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|森娜(Chinese)
column12: Derived from the plant named Senna. The name is a variant of the Arabic name Sana 1, which means "brilliance, radiance, splendour."In literature, this is the name of a female antagonist and witch from K.A. Applegate's series Everworld as well as a character in Stephenie Meyer's Twilight saga.
Greek form of Sennacherib, as it first appeared in the Septuagint.
The name of a mayor of Thebes during the reign of Amenhotep II in the 18th Dynasty. His tomb is known as the “Tomb of the Vineyards” due to its decoration.
Old High German sin "sense; meaning; opinion" + Old High German hiltja "battle".
This is the name of a Persian saint, martyred with St. Abdon.
From Japanese 仙人 (sennin) meaning "immortal mountain fairy or wizard".
From Turkish şen meaning "happy" combined with Arabic نور (nūr) meaning "light".
A name of unknown meaning used in Ancient Egyptian times.A notable Sennuy was a wife of Djefai-Hapi I, nomarch of Asyut and high priest of the nome's temples during the 1800s BCE.
From Javanese sena meaning "soldiers, troops, army", ultimately from Sanskrit सेना (senā).
Italian form of Xenokrates via Xenocrates.
Meaning unknown, possibly a corruption of Shenoywa. This was the name of a Native American chief in which the town of Senoia, Georgia is named after.
Of uncertain meaning, perhaps from Proto-Celtic *senos meaning "old". This was the name of a 10th-century Galician saint.

Romanized Celtic name, in which the first element is ultimately from the Indo-European root *sen meaning "old" (the second element, uaro, is uncertain, possibly meaning "war"). It was found scratched onto a metal "curse tablet" (c.2nd-century) at the temple of Sulis Minerva at Bath (Somerset, South West England). The masculine form Senovarus is also attested.

column3: 千里, 千理, 千利, 千莉, 千璃, 千梨, 千吏, 扇利, 扇里, 扇梨, 扇理, 泉里, 泉理, 泉理, 泉李(Japanese Kanji)|せんり(Japanese Hiragana)|センリ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: As a unisex name, this name combines 千 (sen, chi) meaning "thousand" with 里 (ri, sato) meaning "league, parent's home, ri (unit of distance - equal to 3.927 km), village", 理 (ri, kotowari) meaning "arrangement, justice, logic, reason, truth", 利 (ri, ki.ku) meaning "advantage, benefit, profit", 莉 (rai, ri, rei) meaning "jasmine" or 璃 (ri) meaning "glassy, lapis lazuli."As a feminine name, it can be used as 千梨, 千吏, 扇利, 扇里, 扇梨, 扇理, 泉里, 泉理, 泉理 or 泉李 with 扇 (sen, ougi) meaning "fan, folding fan", 泉 (sen, izumi) meaning "fountain, spring", 梨 (ri, nashi) meaning "pear tree", 吏 (ri) meaning "an official, officer" and 李 (ri, sumomo) meaning "plum."As a word, Senri (千里) means "1000 ri" (a ri is equivalent to 3.927 km or 2.44 miles) or, in other words, "a long distance."Senri is also used as a surname.
Medieval transliteration of Senchia or Sancho.
An anagram of the word suisen, meaning "daffodil"
This name is often a short form of Vincent. However, it is also a short form for names that contain the Gothic elements sanths (like Sandulf) or sinths (like Sindulf).

Variant of Saintanise. Ti Sentaniz ("Little Sentaniz") is a fictional character created by Maurice Sixto for his 1977 Volume III, a collection of lodyans (a Haitian literary genre akin to fairytales). Ti Sentaniz is a Cinderella like figure from a poor country family who is sent to live with rich relatives in the city who treat her like a slave.
From Old Germanic senþaz "path, journey; time, instance" and harjaz "army".
Possibly derived from Sanskrit सिन्दूर (sindūra) meaning "red, vermillion". This is another name of the Hindu god Murugan (Skanda).
Derived from the Proto-Germanic elements sinþaz "journey, way, path" and hildiz "battle, fight".
Combination of the name Senthil and Sanskrit कुमार (kumāra) meaning "boy, son, prince".

In Roman mythology, Sentia is the goddess of child development and the bringer of awareness into young children. The English word "sentient" meaning "able to perceive or feel things", is derived from her name.
God who gives sentience or the powers of sense perception (sensus). Augustine calls him the sensificator, "creator of sentience."
From Javanese sênthot meaning "going quickly, running, sprinting".
Gallo form of Sancta as well as a feminine form of Sènt.
Possibly the Uygur form of Sanubar.

A Celtic goddess worshipped in Roman Britain. Her name is possibly related to the Proto-Celtic 'seno' meaning "old". Some academics have associated the name to the ancient river Senua that was once located in southern Britain, which may have also been known as Alde, from the Anglo-Saxon 'ald' meaning old.Not much is known of Senuna though correlations have been drawn between her and Minerva due to the few representations of her iconography that exist. Some items have been found which portray classical images of Minerva with her sword, shield, and owl but which are inscribed with Senuna's name. From this we can deduce that she may have been a goddess of wisdom and defense.

From Egyptian z-n-wsrt meaning "man of Wosret", derived from z "man" combined with n(j) "of, belonging to" and the name of the goddess Wosret. This was the name of four Egyptian pharaohs and a vizier.
From the Chinese 森 (sēn) meaning "forest" and 婉 (wǎn) meaning "amiable, congenial".

column3: 千夜(Japanese Kanji)|せにゃ(Japanese Hiragana)|セニャ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Means "many nights" in Japanese. From 千 (sen) "one thousand" and 夜 (ya) "night, evening".

Filipinized form of the Spanish word señora meaning "lady." Senyora Santibañez is a snobbish and stereotypically arrogant plantation owner depicting the main antagonist in the Mexican telenovela Marimar and actor Chantal Andere.
From the Chinese 森 (sēn) meaning "forest" and 媛 (yuàn) meaning "beauty, beautiful woman".
Short form of Cresenza, traditionally found in the Surselva region.
Means "what did we do?" in Ndebele.

column3: 서빈(Korean Hangul)|瑞斌, 舒斌, 徐斌, 序斌, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 瑞 (seo) meaning "felicitous omen, auspicious" or 舒 (seo) meaning "open up, unfold, comfortable, easy" or 徐 (seo) meaning "slowly, calmly, composed, dignified" or 序 (seo) meaning "series, sequence" combined with 斌 (bin) meaning "refined". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
Directly taken from Irish seoda meaning "jewels". This is a modern Irish name.

From 曙(seo) meaning "dawn" or 書(seo) meaning "book, document" or 栖(seo) meaning "reside, stay" or 西(seo) meaning "west" combined with 恩(eun) meaning "kindness, mercy, charity" or 殷(eun) meaning "abundant, flourishing". Other hanja combinations are possible.
From Sino-Korean 石榴 (seog-lyu) meaning "pomegranate". This name can be formed using other hanja combinations as well.

column3: 서경(Korean Hangul)|西敬, 瑞敬, 西瓊, 瑞瓊(Korean Hanja)
column12: Feom Sino-Korean 西 (seo) meaning "west" or 瑞 (seo) meaning "auspicious, lucky" combined with 敬 (gyeong) meaning "respect" or 瓊 (gyeong) meaning "jade". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 서하(Korean Hangul)|瑞夏, 舒夏, 徐夏, 序夏, 瑞昰, 舒昰, 徐昰, 序昰, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 瑞 (seo) meaning "felicitous omen, auspicious" or 舒 (seo) meaning "open up, unfold, comfortable, easy" or 徐 (seo) meaning "slowly, calmly, composed, dignified" or 序 (seo) meaning "series, sequence" combined with 夏 (ha) meaning "summer, great, grand" or 昰 (ha) meaning "summer, name". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 서희(Korean Hangul)|瑞姬, 徐姬, 瑞熙, 徐熙, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Alternate transcription of Korean Hangul 서희 (see Seo-hui).

column3: 서호(Korean Hangul)|敍澔, 舒澔, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 敍 (seo) meaning "express, state, relate, narrate" or 舒 (seo) meaning "open up, unfold, comfortable, easy combined with 澔 (ho) meaning "radiance of gems". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
Alternative transliteration of the name Seo-hoo.

column3: 서희(Korean Hangul)|瑞姬, 徐姬, 瑞熙, 徐熙, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 瑞 (seo) meaning "felicitous omen, auspicious" or 徐 (seo) meaning "slowly, calmly, composed, dignified" combined with 姬 (hui) meaning "beauty" or 熙 (hui) meaning "bright, splendid, glorious". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

서향, means Daphne odora, is a species of flowering plant. The Latin specific epithet odora means "fragrant". In Korea, the plant is also poetically called "churihyang" - a thousand-mile scent - referring to the fragrance of the foliage. In Japan, the plant is more commonly known as "jinchoge".
From Sino-Korean 瑞 (seo) meaning "felicitous omen; auspicious" and 慧 (hye) meaning "bright, intelligent". Other hanja can be used.
From 瑞 (seo) meaning "felicitous omen, auspicious" combined with 賢 (hyeon) meaning "virtuous, worthy, able". Other combinations of hanja characters can form this name as well.

column3: 서형(Korean Hangul)|瑞亨, 書馨, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 瑞 (seo) meaning "felicitous omen, auspicious" or 書 (seo) meaning "book, letter, document" and 亨 (hyeong) meaning "prosperous" or 馨 (hyeong) meaning "fragrant". Other hanja combinations can also form this name.

column3: 서형(Korean Hangul)|瑞亨, 書馨, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Alternate transcription of Korean Hangul 서형 (see Seo-hyeong).

column3: 서이(Korean Hangul)|瑞利, 徐利, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Means "three" in Korean (Gyeongsang dialect). Alternatively, it coukd come from Sino-Korean 瑞 (seo) meaning "felicitous omen, auspicious" or 徐 (seo) meaning "slowly, calmly, composed, dignified" combined with 利 (i) meaning "benefit, advantage". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
From seoid meaning "jewel, gem" combined with the diminutive suffix -ín.

column3: 서인(Korean Hangul)|西人, 西寅, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 西 (seo) meaning “west” combined with 人 (in) meaning “man, person, mankind” or 寅 (in), meaning “revere, respect”, also referring the to third Earthly Branches (3AM to 5AM), itself associated with the tiger of the Chinese zodiac. Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 서정(Korean Hangul)|西情, 瑞情, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 西 (seo) meaning "west" or 瑞 (seo) meaning "auspicious, lucky", combined with 情 (jeong) meaning "feeling, emotion". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
From Sino-Korean 錫 "bestow, confer" and 範 "pattern, model, rule, law".
From Sino-Korean 碩 (seok) meaning "large, big, great", 錫 (seok) meaning "tin", or 石 (seok) meaning "stone, rock" and 卿 (gyeong) "noble", 敬 (gyeong) "respect, honor" or 耿 (gyeong) "bright, shining".

column3: 석호(Korean Hangul)|錫浩, 錫瑚, 錫鎬, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 錫 (seok) meaning "tin" combined with 浩 (ho) meaning "great, numerous, vast", 鎬 (ho) meaning "stove, bright" or 瑚 (ho) meaning "coral, person of virtue". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 석희(Korean Hangul)|石姬, 碩姬, 石嬉, 碩嬉, 石熙, 碩熙, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 石 (seok) meaning "stone" or 碩 (seok) meaning "large, great" combined with 姬 (hui) meaning "beauty" or 嬉 (hui) meaning "enjoy, play" or 熙 (hui) meaning "bright, splendid, glorious". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 석환(Korean Hangul)|石煥, 碩桓, 奭奐, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 石 (seok) meaning "stone", 碩 (seok) meaning "big, great" or 奭 (seok) meaning "red, anger" combined with 煥 (hwan) meaning "shining, brilliant, lustrous", 桓 (hwan) meaning "Chinese soapberry" or 奐 (hwan) meaning "numerous, brilliant". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 석현(Korean Hangul)|晳鉉, 錫炫, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 晳 (seok) meaning "fair, white, clear" or 錫 (seok) meaning "tin" combined with 鉉 (hyeon) referring to a device used to lift a ritual tripod cauldron. Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 석현(Korean Hangul)|晳鉉, 錫炫, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Alternate transcription of Korean Hangul 석현 (see Seok-hyeon).

column3: 석준(Korean Hangul)|錫俊, 錫駿, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Alternate transcription of Korean Hangul 석준 (see Seok-jun).

column3: 석준(Korean Hangul)|錫俊, 錫駿, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 錫 (seok) meaning "tin" combined with 俊 (jun) meaning "talented, handsome" or 駿 (jun) meaning "good horse". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
From Sino-Korean 錫 (seok) meaning "tin" combined with 悅 (yeol) meaning "joy, pleased". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
From Sino-Korean 石 (seok) meaning "stone" combined with 燕 (yeon) meaning "swallow (bird)". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 석영(Korean Hangul)|石英, 晳暎, 錫榮, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 石英 (seokyeong) meaning "quartz" or from 晳 (seok) meaning "fair, white, clear" or 錫 (seok) meaning "tin" combined with 暎 or 映 (yeong) meaning "reflected light" or 榮 (yeong) meaning "glory, honor, flourish, prosper". Other hanja combinations are possible.
Alternate transcription of Korean Hangul 석열 (see Seok-yeol).

column3: 서경(Korean Hangul)|西敬, 瑞敬, 西瓊, 瑞瓊(Korean Hanja)

column12: From Sino-Korean 雪 (seol) meaning "snow" combined with 娥 (a) meaning "beautiful". Other hanja combinations can also form this name.
From Korean 雪花(seolhwa) meaning "snow flower, snowdrop".

column3: 설현(Korean Hangul)|雪炫, 雪賢, 設賢, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Combination of a seol hanja, like 雪 meaning "snow" or 設 meaning "establish, set up," and a hyeon hanja, such as 炫 meaning "bright, brilliant; light, clear" or 賢 meaning "benevolent; wise, sensible."

column3: 설현(Korean Hangul)|雪炫, 雪賢, 設賢, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Variant transcription of Seol-hyeon.A famous bearer of this name is singer and actress Kim Seol-hyun (1995-), a member of the South Korean girl group AOA.

From Korean 서린(seorin) meaning "misted up, frosted up".From Hanja 書(seo) meaning "book, document" or 栖(seo) meaning "reside, stay" combined with 粼(lin) meaning "clear water" or 隣(lin) meaning "neighbor". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well
From Sino-Korean 雪 (seol) meaning "snow" combined with 乃 (nae) meaning "inside; mine". This name can be formed using other hanja combinations as well.
From 瑞 (seo) meaning "felicitous omen, auspicious" combined with 媺 (mi) or 美 (mi) both meaning "beautiful". Other combinations are possible.
From Sino-Korean岛"island" and 水" water"
From Sino-Korean 瑞 (seo) meaning "felicitous omen, auspicious" combined with 娜 (na) meaning "elegant, graceful, delicate". Other Hanja combinations are possible.
From Sino-Korean 宣 "declare, announce, proclaim" and 兒 "child". A famous bearer is South Korean actress Kim Sun-a (1975-).
The Irish form of the Scottish-Gaelic name Seònaid, in turn a translation of Joan 1.

The name of the Korean goddess of villages, boundaries and war. Her name is derived from the hanja 城 (seong) meaning "city wall, fort, defensive wall", 隍 (hwang) meaning "dry moat" or "god of a city" and 神 (sin) meaning "god".
Posthumous name of the queen regnant of Silla, one of the Three Kingdoms of Korea, from 632 to 647. She was Silla's twenty-seventh ruler, and its first reigning queen.
From Sino-Korean 成 (seong) meaning "completed, finished, succeeded", combined with Sino-Korean 愛 (ae) meaning "love, affection"
From 星 (seong) meaning "star, planet" or 性 (seong) meaning "sex, gender" and 彬 "cultivated, well-bred"
From 聖 "holy, sacred; sage" or 成 (seong) meaning "to succeed, to finish, to complete" or 城 (seong) meaning "fort, castle, cidatel" and 福 "happiness, good fortune, blessing".

From 成(seong) meaning "complete, achieve" or 盛(seong) meaning "abundant, flourishing" combined with 찬(chan) meaning "cold, filled" or 燦(chan) meaning "vivid, illuminating, bright". Other hanja combinations can also form this name.

column3: 성철(Korean Hangul)|成哲, 聖哲, 聖喆, 性徹, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 成 (seong) meaning "completed, finished, succeeded", 聖 (seong) meaning "holy, sacred" or 性 (seung) meaning "nature, character" combined with 哲/喆 (cheol) meaning "wise, sage" or 徹 (cheol) meaning "pierce, penetrate". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 성철(Korean Hangul)|成哲, 聖哲, 聖喆, 性徹, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Alternate transcription of Korean Hangul 성철 (see Seong-cheol).
From Sino-Korean 聖 "holy, sacred; sage" and 基 "foundation, base".
From Native Korean noun - "seonggonghada" (성공하다) which means "to be successful"
Meaning unknown. This was the personal name of Taejo of Joseon (1335-1408), founder and first king of the Joseon dynasty.

column3: 성한(Korean Hangul)|成漢, 星漢, 城漢, 聲翰, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 成 (seong) meaning "completed, finished, succeeded", 星 (seong) meaning "star, planet", 城 (seong) meaning "castle, city, town" or 聲 (seong) meaning "sound, voice, tone" combined with 漢 (han) meaning "Han people, man" or 翰 (han) meaning "writing, painting". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
From Sino-Korean 盛 "abundant, flourishing" and 希 "rare; hope, expect, strive for".
From Sino-Korean 城 "castle; city, town", 星 "a star, planet; any point of light" or 成 "completed, finished, fixed" (seong) and 煥 "shining, brilliant, lustrous" (hwan).

column3: 성혜(Korean Hangul)|成慧, 盛慧, 成惠, 盛惠, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 成 (seong) meaning "completed, finished, succeeded" or 盛 (seong) meaning "abundant, flourishing" combined with 慧 (hye) meaning "bright, intelligent" or 惠 (hye) meaning "favour, benefit". Other hanja combinations are possible

column3: 성혁(Korean Hangul)|盛爀, 星爀, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 盛 (seong) meaning "abundant, flourishing" or 星 (seong) meaning "star, planet" combined with 爀 (hyeok) meaning "red, bright red". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
From 星 (seong) meaning "star, planet" or 性 (seong) meaning "sex, gender" and 顯 "manifest, display; evident, clear".
From Sino-Korean 善 "good, virtuous, charitable, kind" and 吉 "lucky, propitious, good".

column3: 성일(Korean Hangul)|成一, 星一, 城一, 誠一, 盛一, 聖一, 晟一, 瑆一, 惺一(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Korean Hanja 成 (seong/sŏng) meaning "to succeed, to finish, to complete", 星 (seong/sŏng) meaning "star", 城 (seong/sŏng) meaning "city walls, city, town", 誠 (seong/sŏng) meaning "honest, sincere, true", 盛 (seong/sŏng) meaning "flourishing, vigorous, magnificent", 聖 (seong/sŏng) meaning "holy, sacred, saint", 晟 (seong/sŏng) meaning "splendor", 瑆 (seong/sŏng) meaning "jade-green, bright", 惺 (seong/sŏng) meaning "tranquil, understand" combined with 一 (il) meaning "one". Other character combinations are also possible.

column3: 성임(Korean Hangul)|成林, 盛林, 成任, 盛任, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 成 (seong) meaning "completed, finished, succeeded" or 盛 (seong) meaning "abundant, flourishing" combined with 林 (im) meaning "forest" or 任 (im) meaning "burden, responsibility, duty". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 成子, 聖子(Korean Hanja)|성자(Korean Hangul)
column12: From Sino-Korean 成 (seong) meaning "turn into, become, get, grow, elapse, reach" or 聖 (seong) meaning "holy, saint, sage, master, priest" combined with 子 (ja) meaning "child". Other hanja combinations are possible.Famous bearers are Shin Seong-ja, a South Korean fencer and Park Sung-ja, a Korean former judoka who competed in the 2000 Summer Olympics.

column3: 성재(Korean Hangul)|成宰, 誠宰, 星材, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 成 (seong) meaning "completed, finished, succeeded", 誠 (seong) meaning "sincere, honest, true" or 星 (seong) meaning "star, planet" combined with 宰 (jae) meaning "kill, rule" or 材 (jae) meaning "material, talent". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 성주(Korean Hangul)|成珠, 盛珠, 成周, 盛周, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Alternate transcription of Korean Hangeul 성주 (see Seong-ju).

column3: 성준(Korean Hangul)|成俊, 盛俊, 成准, 盛准, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Alternate transcription of Korean Hangeul 성준 (see Seong-jun).

column3: 성주(Korean Hangul)|成珠, 盛珠, 成周, 盛周, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 成 (seong) meaning "completed, finished, succeeded" or 盛 (seong) meaning "abundant, flourishing" combined with 珠 (ju) meaning "jewel, pearl" or 周 (ju) meaning "circumference". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 성준(Korean Hangul)|成俊, 盛俊, 成准, 盛准, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 成 (seong) meaning "completed, finished, succeeded" or 盛 (seong) meaning "abundant, flourishing" combined with 俊 (jun) meaning "beautiful, handsome" or 准 (jun) meaning "allow, permit". Other hanja combinations are possible.
From Sino-Korean 性 "nature, character" and 美 "beautiful, pretty; pleasing".
From Sino-Korean 城 (seong) meaning "castle, fortress" and 旿 (o) meaning "bright".

column3: 성옥(Korean Hangul)|成玉, 盛玉, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 成 (seong) meaning "completed, finished, succeeded" or 盛 (seong) meaning "abundant, flourishing" combined with 玉 (ok) meaning "jade". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 성수(Korean Hangul)|成洙, 聖洙, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Alternate transcription of Korean Hangeul 성수 (see Seong-su).

column3: 성우(Korean Hangul)|成雨, 星雨, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 成 (seong) meaning "completed, finished, succeeded" or 星 (seong) meaning "star, planet" combined with 雨 (u) meaning "rain". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 성욱(Korean Hangul)|成旭, 盛旭, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 成 (seong) meaning "completed, finished, succeeded" or 盛 (seong) meaning "abundant, flourishing" combined with 旭 (uk) meaning "rising sun". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 승욱(Korean Hangul)|成旭, 盛旭, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Alternate transcription of Korean Hangeul 승욱 (see Seong-uk).
From Sino-Korean 成 "completed, finished, fixed" and 妍 "beautiful, handsome; seductive".
From 聖 "holy, sacred; sage" or 成 (seong) meaning "to succeed, to finish, to complete" or 城 (seong) meaning "fort, castle, cidatel" and 允 "allow, consent" or 潤 "soft, sleek" (yun).
From Sino-Korean 先 "first, former, previous" and 皓 "bright, luminous; clear".
From Sino-Korean 仙 "transcendent, immortal" and 姫 "beauty".

column3: 선재(Korean Hangul)|先宰, 宣宰, 先才, 宣才, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 先 (seon) meaning "first" or 宣 (seon) meaning "declare, announce" combined with 宰 (jae) meaning "govern, rule", or 才 (jae). Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 선정(Korean Hangul)|善靜, 宣靜, 鮮靜, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 善 (seon) meaning "good, virtuous" or 宣 (seon) meaning "declare, announce" or 鮮 (seon) meaning "new, fresh" combined with 靜 (jeong) meaning "quiet, still, gentle" . Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
From Sino-Korean 宣 "declare, announce, proclaim" and 美 "beautiful, pretty; pleasing".

column3: 선녀(Korean Hangul)|善女, 宣女, 鮮女, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 善 (seon) meaning "good, virtuous" or 宣 (seon) meaning "declare, announce" or 鮮 (seon) meaning "new, fresh" combined with 女 (nyeo) meaning "woman". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 선웅(Korean Hangul)|善熊, 宣熊, 善雄, 宣雄, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 善 (seon) meaning "good, virtuous" or 宣 (seon) meaning "declare, announce" combined with 熊 (ung) meaning "bear" or 雄 (ung) meaning "male". Other Hanja combinations are possible.

column3: 선우(Korean Hangul)|善宇, 善佑, 宣佑, 宣宇, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Alternate transcription of Korean Hangul 선우 (see Seon-u).
From Sino-Korean 先 "first, former, previous" and 藝 "art; talent, ability; craft".

column3: 선유(Korean Hangul)|善有, 宣裕, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Combination of a seon hanja, like 善 meaning "good, nice" or 宣 meaning "giving; mercy, kindness," and a yu hanja, such as 有 meaning "stand; exist" or 裕 meaning "sufficient, ample; generous."

column3: 선율(Korean Hangul)|璇律, 仙律, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 璇 (seon) meaning "fine jade" or 仙 (seon) meaning "transcendant, immortal, extraordinary" combined with 律 (yul) meaning "law". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
Variation of Korean Sora and So-Ra.

From 曙(seo) meaning "dawn" or 書(seo) meaning "book, document" or 栖(seo) meaning "reside, stay" or 西(seo) meaning "west" combined with 來(rae) meaning "to come, to arrive". Other combinations can also form this name.

column3: 聖音鈴, 星織, 瀬織梨, 世織里, 世央莉, 茜緒鈴, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|서리(Korean Hangul)
column12: From Japanese 聖 (se) meaning "holy, sacred", 音 (o) meaning "sound" combined with 鈴 (ri) meaning "bell, chime". Other kanji combinations are possible.

From Korean 서린(seorin) meaning "misted up, frosted up".Also from 書(seo) meaning "book, document" or 栖(seo) meaning "reside, stay" combined with 粼(rin) meaning "clear water" or 隣(rin) meaning "neighbor". Other hanja combinations can form this name.

column3: 서우(Korean Hangul)|瑞雨, 栖瑀, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 瑞 (seo) meaning "felicitous omen, auspicious" or 栖 (seo) meaning "to perch, to roost" combined with 雨 (u) meaning "rain" or 瑀 (u) meaning "stone resembling jade, agate". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
Hellenized form of Severa. Also compare the names Silvanus and Silouanos, which show that the letter -v- was usually hellenized to -ou- by the ancient Greeks.
Hellenized form of Severianus. Also compare the names Silvanus and Silouanos, which show that the letter -v- was usually hellenized to -ou- by the ancient Greeks.
Hellenized form of Severinus. Also compare the names Silvanus and Silouanos, which show that the letter -v- was usually hellenized to -ou- by the ancient Greeks.
Hellenized form of Severus. Also compare the names Silvanus and Silouanos, which show that the letter -v- was usually hellenized to -ou- by the ancient Greeks.

column3: 성일(Korean Hangul)|成一, 星一, 城一, 誠一, 盛一, 聖一, 晟一, 瑆一, 惺一(Korean Hanja)

column12: From Sino-Korean 瑞 (seo) meaning "felicitous omen, auspicious" combined with 元 (won) meaning "first, origin". Other Hanja combinations are possible.

column3: 서우(Korean Hangul)|瑞雨, 栖瑀, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Alternate transcription of Korean Hangul 서우 (see Seo-u).

column3: 서영(Korean Hangul)|瑞英, 西瑛, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 瑞 (seo) meaning "felicitous omen, auspicious" or 西 (seo) meaning "west" combined with 英 (yeong) meaning "flower, petal, brave, hero" or 瑛 (yeong) meaning "jade". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
Alternate transcription of Korean Hangul 서윤 (see Seo-yun).

column3: 서영(Korean Hangul)|瑞英, 西瑛, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Alternate transcription of Korean Hangul 서영 (see Seo-yeong).

column3: 서율(Korean Hangul)|瑞律, 舒律, 徐律, 序律, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 瑞 (seo) meaning "felicitous omen, auspicious" or 舒 (seo) meaning "open up, unfold, comfortable, easy" or 徐 (seo) meaning "slowly, calmly, composed, dignified" or 序 (seo) meaning "series, sequence" combined with combined with 律 (yul) meaning "law". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
Short for Patisepa, Tongan form of Bathsheba.
Means "wild rue" (scientific name Peganum harmala) in Persian.

Means "sword of the state", derived from the Arabic noun سيف (sayf) meaning "sword" (see Saif) combined with the Arabic noun دولة (dawla) meaning "state".In Georgian literature, this is the name of a famed warrior from the 12th-century Georgian romance Amiran-Darejaniani written by Moses of Khoni.
From Uygur سەپەر meaning "journey, march, trip", from Arabic سَفَر (safar).
Diminutive of Joseph, Josepha, and other names containing -seph-.
Short form of Josepha and Josephina.

This name originally came into being as an erroneous spelling of Severinus (see Severino). But, when found spelled as Zepharinus, it can also be an erroneous spelling of Zephyrinus (see Zeferino). And last but not least, this name can also possibly be a metathesis of Seraphinus (see Seraphina).
Variant of Josephine influenced by names ending in een (an anglicisation of the Irish diminutive suffix ín).
Diminutive for Persephone and Josephine. This is the name of the heroine in the CrossGen comic series 'Meridian'.
Diminutive of Josephine and other names containing "sephine".

Derived from English sephiroth, the plural form of sephirah, itself derived from Hebrew סְפִירָה (s'fira) meaning "counting, enumeration". In the Kabbalah, this is one of the emanations through which God projects himself to the universe and man. This is the name of the main antagonist of the video game 'Final Fantasy VII' by Japanese artist Tetsuya Nomura, and the character that popularized the name.
Diminutive of Persephone. The main female character in the novel series 'Noughts and Crosses' has this name.
Alternate transcription of Persian سپیده (see Sepideh).
Derived from sipisttoo meaning "owl" and okós meaning "child" in the Kainaa dialect of Siksika.

The term sepoy is derived from the Persian word sepāhī (سپاهی) meaning the traditional "infantry soldier" in the Mughal Empire. Historically it has been used in Singapore as a given name largely by Indian Singaporeans.
Alsatian and Upper German short form of Joseph.
From the name of the month of September, usually used as a given name for someone born in September.
From the name of the month of September, usually used as a given name for someone born in September.
From the name of the month of September, usually used as a given name for a boy born in September.
From the name of the month of September, usually used as a given name for a girl born in September.
From the name of the month of September, usually used as a given name for a girl born in September.
From the name of the month of September, usually used as a given name for a girl born in September.
From the name of the month of September, usually used as a given name for a boy born in September.

Jeanne-Louise-Armande-Élisabeth-Sophie-Septimanie de Vignerot du Plessis (1740-1773), daughter of the 3rd Duke of Richelieu, was a salonnière of the French Ancien Régime. She was married to the Count of Egmont and also known as Septimanie d'Egmont.
French form of Septimus and Septimius, as well as the French feminine form of Septima.A known bearer is French painter Septime Émeric Marie Le Pippre (1833-1871).
Roman cognomen which was derived from Septimius. This name was borne by a Roman consul from the 2nd century AD.
Diminutive of Septimus. This name was borne by Lucius Fabius Cilo (it was one of his many names), a Roman senator from the 2nd century AD.
Spanish and Portuguese form of Septimius.
From the name of the 9th sunday before easter. The name of the sunday is derivded from the Latin word for "70th".
From the Armenian word սեպուհ (sepuh) meaning "sepuh" (a title of Armenian nobility).
Derived from the name of the Sepulveda valley in the mountains of Segovia. It is possibly derived from Spanish sepultar "to bury".
Latinized form of the Gaulish (Celtic) name Sicauna, which is argued to mean "sacred river" or "the fast flowing one". This was the name of the Gallo-Roman goddess of the River Seine.

The Celtic goddess of the river Seine. Water was venerated by the Celts as a source of the life-force, as well as for its cleansing and curative properties. The River Goddess Sequanna stands in her duck-prow vessel, welcoming pilgrims visiting her shrine to seek cures.
From the Korean phrase 굳세라 (gudsera) meaning "stay strong". Also from Sino-Korean 世 (se) meaning "world" combined with 羅 (ra) meaning "silk, display". Other Hanja combinations are possible.
Short form of Séraphin.A notable bearer of this name was the French athlete Séra Martin (1906-1993).

column3: 世良, 世麗, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column12: A king once defeated in combat by Perceval.

Means "abundance" in Hebrew. This was the name of the granddaughter of Jacob, and the daughter of Asher in the Torah, who is said to have lived past the era of Moses until she was taken to heaven (like Enoch and Elijah).
From 世(se) meaning "world, generation" or 세(se) meaning "three" combined with 來(rae) meaning "to come, to arrive".
Catalan form of Seraphinus. Serafí Pitarra was the pen name of Frederic Soler i Hubert (1839-1895), a Catalan poet and dramaturge.

Seraphiel meaning "Prince of the High Angelic Order" is the name of an angel in the apocryphal Book of Enoch. Protector of Metatron, Seraphiel holds the highest rank of the Seraphim with the following directly below him, Jehoel.Seraphiel is described as an enormous, brilliant angel as tall as the seven heavens with a face like the face of angels and a body like the body of eagles. He is beautiful, like lightning and the light of the morning star. As chief of the seraphim, he is committed to their care and teaches them songs to sing for the glorification of God. In magical lore, Seraphiel is one of the rulers of Tuesday and also the planet Mercury. He is invoked from the North.
Alternate transcription of Korean Hangul 세라 (se Se-ra).
From the Hebrew name שָֽׂרַח (Serach) meaning "abundance". In the Old Testament this is the name of Asher's daughter, Jacob's granddaughter.

One of the maidens of Viviane, the French Damsel of the Lake, Seraide seems to have held a high place in the Damsel’s service. her grasp of magic, while doubtless far short of Viviane’s, Nimue’s, or Morgan’s, was practical and useful.
Romansh form of Serena, traditionally found in the Engadine valley.
Alternate transcription of Arabic سراج (see Siraj).

From the English word seraph, singular form of the biblical word seraphim referring to an order of angels (see Seraphina, Seraphim). This was borne by Seraph Frissell (1840-1915), an American physician and medical writer who specialized in diseases of women and children.
Possibly a variant spelling of Séraphine.
Variant of Serapia. Saint Seraphia (or Serapia) was a 2nd-century Syrian martyr.

Means "seraph of God" in Hebrew, derived from שָׂרָף (saraf) referring to the angelic order known as the seraphim (meaning "burning ones" in Hebrew) and אֵל (ʾel) meaning "God". This is the name of an angel in the apocryphal Book of Enoch, described as the chief of the seraphim.

Directly from the biblical word seraphim which meant "fiery ones", from Hebrew שרף (saraf) meaning "to burn", referring to an order of angels described in the Book of Isaiah (see Seraphina). A famous bearer of the name was Saint Seraphim of Sarov, a 19th-century Russian mystic, in whose case his name was an anglicization of his actual name Serafim.
Feminine form of Seraphim, as well as an English strictly feminine variant. This is another name for Saint Serapia, a 2nd-century martyr from Antioch.
English and German form of Seraphinus (see Seraphina).

Variant of Seraphinus. Born at Montegranaro, Italy, in 1540, Seraphino worked as a shepherd in his youth and was reportedly much abused by his older brother. At the age of sixteen he entered the Capuchins as a lay brother at Ascoli Piceno, earning a reputation for his holiness. He was graced with considerable spiritual gifts and wisdom, as well as devotion to the Blessed Sacrament.

Séraphîta is possibly a variant of Seraphina. Séraphîta is the heroine of Honoré de Balzac's 1837 novel called 'Séraphîta', which explores themes of androgyny. In the novel Séraphîta is actually portrayed an androgyne known as Séraphitüs-Séraphîta, appearing as a woman to some people and a man to others.
Latin, Spanish and Galician form of Serapion.
From the Kurdish ser meaning "crest, crown, top" and av meaning "water".

Khazar, Karaite, Krymchak and Turkish form of Sergius. The name is known as ''Seraj'' in Polish and ''Seraja'' in Lithuanian.''Seraya Shapshal'' or His Excellency Hajji Seraya Khan Shapshal (Karaim: Серая Бен Мордехай Шапшал; Lithuanian: Seraja Šapšalas; Polish: Seraj Szapszał; Russian: Серге́й Маркович Шапшал) (1873–1961) was a hakham and leader of the Crimean and then the Polish and Lithuanian Crimean Karaites (Karaim) community.
Derived from Servus (via the form Șerb).
Means "officer" in Kurdish, possibly derived from Turkish subay.
Possibly from ser meaning "crest, crown, top" and çil meaning "forty".
Derived from Kurdish serfermandar meaning "army commander".
From the Kurdish şêr meaning "lion" and dil meaning "heart".
Sered was a son of Zebulun according to Genesis 46:14 and Numbers 26:26. He was one of the 70 souls to migrate to Egypt with Jacob.
From the Turkish şeref meaning "honour" and naz meaning "coy".
From the Turkish şeref meaning "honour" and nur meaning "light".
From the Buryat сэрэг (sereg) meaning "army" and the Mongolian feminine suffix -маа (-maa).
The Portuguese word for mermaid. Found in use in Brazil as a given name but also well represented as a nickname.
Variant of Seraina, traditionally found in the Surselva region.

column3: 芹礼奈, 星玲菜, 瀬怜那, 聖礼名, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 芹 (se) meaning "water dropwort (Oenanthe javanica)", 怜 (re) meaning "actor", and 菜 (na) meaning "vegetables, greens". Other kanji combinations are possible as well.
From the English word serendipity, coined in 1754 by English writer and politician Horace Walpole based on the Persian story of The Three Princes of Serendip.
From the English word "serene" or a variant of Serena.
Diminutive of Serena. It also coincides with one of the Italian words for "lilac".
Roman cognomen which was derived from Serenus.

Invented as a combination of Serena and Veronica for the game Dragon Quest XI: Echoes of an Elusive Age (2017), where the name is given to an ancestor of a pair of twins with the aforementioned names, who together are said to be her reincarnation.
Possibly a masculine variant of Serena.
Spanish, Portuguese and Italian forms of Serenus, and masculine form of Serena.
This was used as a Welsh translation of Stellaluna (for a 2000 Welsh adaptation of the children's book 'Stellaluna'). It is derived in part from Welsh seren "star" (cf. Seren).
Hellenized form of Serenus. A known bearer of this name was Serenos of Antinoöpolis (4th century AD), a Greek mathematician from Roman Egypt.
Roman cognomen which was derived from the Latin adjective serenus meaning "clear, tranquil, serene" (see Serena).In Roman mythology, Serenus was an epithet of the god Jupiter.
One of the elements of this name is the god Horus.

Means “the clay that binds" in Tswana.Seretse Khama (1921-1980) was the first President of Botswana, in office from 1966 to 1980. He was the son of Queen Tebogo and Sekgoma Khama II, the paramount chief of the Bamangwato people, and the grandson of Khama III, their king.
Means "freedom," "beauty, charm," "peace," or "power, authority" in Khmer.
Derived from Serey and Sophear, ultimately meaning "the splendor of beauty".

column3: សិរីវុឌ្ឍន៍(Khmer)
column12: From Khmer សិរិ (serəy) meaning "to combine, to add up" and វឌ្ឍន (vŏətthĕəʾnĕəʾ) meaning "progress, development, growth".
Limburgish short form of Servatius (see Servaas).
Derived from Old French serf "serf" and deu "god". This name was used as a secular form of Obediah.
From the name of a ritual pole or tree in Buryat and Yakut culture, used to indicate that a place has an owner, ultimately from the Buryat word for "pole".
Means "cheerful" or "lively, sharp, clever" in Mongolian.
Means "cheerful hero" in Mongolian, from сэргэлэн (sergelen) meaning "cheerful" or "lively, sharp, clever" and баатар (baatar) meaning "hero".
Means "cheerful celebration" in Mongolian, from сэргэлэн (sergelen) meaning "cheerful" or "lively, sharp, clever" and баяр (bayar) meaning "joy, celebration".
Feminine form of Serge. However, it could also be considered to be a diminutive of Sergine, as -ette is a French feminine diminutive suffix.
Languedocian, Gascon and Provençal form of Sergius.
Feminine form of Sergio and Sergiusz respectively.
Possibly a combination of Sergia and Ana or a Brazilian feminine form of Sérgio.
Serbian and Croatian form of Sergius.
Rare feminine form of Sergio and Serge.
Sergis is the knight who informs Artegall of Irena's impending death in Book 5, Canto 11 of "The Faerie Queene".
Derived from Kurdish seraza meaning "excellent" and gula meaning "rose".
Variant of Sergio and a Brazilian variant of Sérgio.
German and Polish transcription of Serhiy.

column3: 세리(Korean Hangul)|世理, 世理, 世里, 世裏(Korean Hanja)
column12: Derived from the Korean Hangul 세 (se) meaning "three" or Korean Hanja 世 (se) meaning "world, lineage, generation" combined with Korean Hangul 리 (ri) coming from Korean Hanja 理 (ri) meaning "reason, sense, logic" or 里 (ri) meaning "village; ri a unit of distance" or 裏 / 裡 (ri) meaning "inside, within, inner".Other characters combinations are also possible.

column3: 芹, 世莉, 世理, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|세리(Korean Hangul)

column12: The Sumerian name of the dawn goddess Aya. While the etymology is uncertain, one suggested root is the Akkadian šērtum, meaning "morning".
From Wolof sëriñ meaning "marabout (a Muslim holy man or a mystic)".

column3: せりか(Japanese Hiragana)|セリカ(Japanese Katakana)|芹伽, 芹佳, 芹夏, 芹架, 芹花, 芹華, 芹香, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 芹 (seri) meaning "water dropwort (Oenanthe javanica)" combined with 伽 (ka) meaning "nursing or taking care of a person", 佳 (ka) meaning "beautiful, good", 夏 (ka) meaning "summer" or 架 (ka) meaning "construct, build". Additionally, other kanji combinations can form this name.
Combination of the name Serik and Kazakh бай (bay) meaning "rich, wealthy".
From the given name Serik combined with the Turkish military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".
From Kazakh серік (serik) meaning “partner”, and болат (bolat) meaning “steel”.
Alternate transcription of Kazakh Серікжан (see Serikzhan).
From Kazakh серік (serik) meaning "support, companion, partner" and жан (zhan) meaning "soul".
Of uncertain origin and meaning; theories include a derivation from Sarahild. It was regionally popular in the Midwestern and Southern United States in the 19th century (see also Zerelda).
From Sino-Korean 世 (se) meaning “world, generation” combined with 璘 (rin) meaning “lustre of jade”. Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 星林, 星鈴, 星凛, 世林, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|세린(Korean Hangul)
column12: From Japanese 星 (se) meaning "star" combined with 林 (rin) meaning "woods; grove; forest; copse", 鈴 (rin) meaning "bell, chime" or 凛 (rin) meaning "dignified, severe, cold". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 芹奈, 芹那, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 芹 (seri) meaning "water dropwort, Oenanthe javanica" combined with 奈 (na) meaning "what?, Nara, apple tree". Other kanji combinations are possible.This name is most likely influenced by Serina.
Possibly a derivative of Old Armenian սէր (ser) meaning "love".
Means "cool rose, fresh rose" in Turkish.
Variant of Sirius, perhaps influenced by the English word "serious".
From the Arabic سرية seriye(t)) meaning “happy, blissful”.
Breton form and Ukrainian and Russian variant transliteration of Serge.
Yiddish girls name, could possibly be a diminutive of Sura (Yiddish for Sarah), combined with the Slavic suffix -ka.
Alternate transcription of Thai เสริมชัย (see Soemchai).
From Persian شرم (sharm) meaning "modesty, bashfulness, shame".
Languedocian and Gascon form of Saturninus.
Means "Lotus flower" in Malay and Indonesian.

column3: セロリ(Japanese Katakana)|せろり(Japanese Hiragana)|瀬蕗里, 瀬蕗里, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 瀬 (se) meaning "rapids", 蕗 (ro) meaning "butterbur" combined with 里 (ri) meaning "village". Other kanji combinations are possible.Usage of this name is influenced by the word celery.
Greek form of Serug, as it first appeared in the Septuagint.
Hellenized form of Servius. Also compare the names Silvanus and Silouanos, which show that the letter -v- was usually hellenized to -ou- by the ancient Greeks.
Means "sickle" (in refrence to "hammer and sickle"). Was often used as sibling to Molot.
From the English word "serpentine" or the place name Serpentine.
Means "hammer and sickle (communist symbol)" in Russian. Compare Serp and Molot.
A new world mythology name meaning traitor, deciever
Serro is a short form of the name Serapion.
Means "the main light, radiance". Sertab Erener is a famous singer with the name. Her name was chosen from a classical Turkish song called "Ey Şûh-i Sertab".
Terived from Turkish ser, an archaic word for "head" and taç meaning "crown".
Of uncertain etymology. Name borne by a daughter of the god of the sea Kiaše in Hurrian and Hittite mythology. She became the wife of the god Kumarbi.

Uncommon Roman praenomen of debated etymology. Some argue that it is derived from a shared root with Servius whilst others cite satio meaning "a planted field" or adsertor meaning "a person who asserts another's liberty".
Feminine version of the Roman praenomen Sertor.
Possibly from Akkadian šērtum, meaning "morning". Šerua was a minor Akkadian goddess sometimes seen as the wife or daughter of Ashur.

From Akkadian elements Šērū’a and ēṭirat, meaning "Šerua (a minor deity, possibly a consort of the god Ashur) is the one who saves". Name borne by a princess of the Sargonid dynasty, known from her letter (circa 670 BCE) to her sister-in-law Libbali-sharrat.

Means "branch" in Hebrew.Serug was the son of Reu and the father of Nahor, according to Genesis 11:20–23. He is also the great-grandfather of the prophet and patriarch Abraham, thus the ancestor of the Ishmaelites and the Israelites.
Derived from Mongolian сэрүүн (serüün) meaning "cool, chilly, fresh; awake, alert" and тунгалаг (tungalag) meaning "serenity, clarity" or "clear, unclouded, transparent".
Slovak and Czech form of Servatius.
Feminine form of Servais and variant of Servasie.
Directly taken from the name of the African cat species.
French and Breton form of Servanus.
French form of Servatius and rarer variant of Servais.
Possibly a contracted form of Servatius.
Flemish and Limburgish variant spelling of Servet, which is a diminutive of Servais, the French form of Servatius.
A derivative of Latin serviens "serving; servant".
Derived from Arabic سُرُور (surūr) meaning "joy, pleasure, satisfaction". It can also be taken from Persian سَروَر (sarvar) meaning "master".
Turkish and Albanian male name of Arabic derivation.People named Servet include:* Servet Çetin, Turkish footballer * Servet Pëllumbi, Albanian politician * Servet Tazegül, Turkish taekwondo athlete
Means "worthy of riches", from Ottoman Turkish ثروت (servet) meaning "riches, wealth" (of Arabic origin) and seza meaning "worthy" (of Persian origin).
Bulgarian, English and Ukrainian form of Servianus.
Feminine form of Servianus. A bearer of this name was Julia Serviana Paulina, the daughter of Roman politician Lucius Julius Ursus Servianus and his wife Aelia Domitia Paulina.
This Roman cognomen is an extended form of Servius. A bearer of this name was Lucius Julius Ursus Servianus, a Roman senator and consul from the 2nd century AD.
From the Turkish servi meaning "cypress" and gül meaning "rose".
Croatian and Serbian form of Servianus.
Bosnian, Croatian and Serbian form of Servius.
Feminine form of Servilius. A known bearer of this name was Servilia Caepionis (1st century BC), who was the mother of Caesar's assassin Marcus Junius Brutus the Younger.
Bulgarian, Russian and Ukrainian form of Servilianus.
Italian, Spanish and Portuguese form of Servilianus.
Extended form of Servilius. This name was borne by the Roman senator and consul Quintus Fabius Maximus Servilianus (2nd century BC).
French form of Servilianus. This name is mostly used in French-speaking parts of Africa. A known bearer of this name is Servilien Nzakamwita (b. 1943), bishop of the Rwandese city Byumba.
Croatian and Serbian form of Servilius.
Italian and Spanish form of Servilius.

Roman nomen gentile which was derived from the Latin adjective servilis meaning "of a slave, slavish, servile", which is ultimately derived from the Latin verb servio meaning "to serve, to be in service, to be a servant/slave". A known bearer of this name was Servilius Casca (1st century BC), who was one of the assassins of Julius Caesar.
Bulgarian, Russian and Ukrainian form of Servilius.
Bulgarian, Russian and Ukrainian form of Servilia.

Variant of Serviliano. This was borne by Servillano Aquino (1874-1959), a Filipino general during the Philippine Revolution against Spain. He was the great-grandfather of Benigno Aquino III, the 15th president of the Philippines, and grandfather-in-law to his mother, Corazon Aquino, the 11th president and first female president of the Philippines.
From the Turkish servi meaning "cypress" and naz meaning "coy".
From the Turkish servi meaning "cypress" and Arabic نساء (nisāʾ) meaning "women".
From the Turkish servi meaning "cypress" and nur meaning "light".
Galician, Italian and Spanish form of Servius.
Late Greek and modern Greek form of Serouios, which is the ancient Greek form of Servius.
From the Turkish servi meaning "cypress" and su meaning "water".
Bulgarian, Russian and Ukrainian form of Servius.
Name of a 9th century Spanish saint.
Means "servant, serf" in Latin. This is the name of an obscure Orthodox martyr who lived in northern Africa in the 5th century.
From Latin servus dei "servant of God".It is the name of two of the Martyrs_of_Córdoba.
From 세련(洗練, Seryeon) meaning "stylish, elegant".
Derived from Turkic ser meaning "head, top" and Persian جان (jān) meaning "soul".
Means "God has avenged me" in Yoruba.

Meaning unknown. Georgian sources state that the name is of Kartvelian origin. However, there might possibly be a chance that the name was originally a short form of Ioseb (compare its diminutive Soso), in which case it is technically of Hebrew origin. A derivation from Aleksandre might also be possible, as is indicated in the case of the Georgian actor Aleksandre "Sesika" Kuprashvili (1904-1979).
From the Mongolian Tsetseg combined with the Mongolian feminine suffix -маа (-maa).

Sesehang is Nepali name more specifically from a Limbu community derived from Limbu language meaning "bright king". Sesehang is combination of sese and hang. Sese means Bright more like bright thoughts and Hang means king. Its other meaning could be king of light as well which means Sese stands for light.
Etymology uncertain, possibly related to the Awajún sésa meaning "flower" or seséjut meaning "healing a wound".
Sesemi (real name Therese) Weichbrodt is a figure from the Buddenbrooks by Thomas Mann.

column3: せせら(Japanese Hiragana)|星々羅, 星々来, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 星 (se) meaning "star", 々, a phonetic character indicting a duplication of the beginning kanji combined with 来 (ra) meaning "to come". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: せせらぎ(Japanese Hiragana)|セセラギ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From せせらぎ (seseragi), referring to a small stream or brooklet, the meaning extended to a murmuring (as of a stream).This name is very rarely used.
In Hindu tradition, Sesha (also: Shesha, Sheshanaga) is the king of all Nagas (serpent deities).

Means "(she who) scrivens (who is the scribe)".In Egyptian mythology she was a goddess of wisdom, knowledge, and writing, seen as a scribe and record-keeper, and is credited with inventing writing. Eventually she came to be identified with architecture, astronomy, astrology, building, mathematics, and surveying as well. She was typically depicted as a woman holding a palm stem or other tools or sometimes a knotted cord used for surveying, and with a seven-pointed emblem above her, though it's unsure what this emblem represents. As the diving measurer and scribe, she was believed to assist the pharaoh in these tasks, and it was she who records, by notching her palm, the time allotted to the pharaoh for his stay on earth. As Thoth became more prominent and identified as the god of wisdom, Seshat became his daughter and, later his wife.
Ancient Egyptian feminine name meaning "(She) who led the Ka". Ka is the Ancient Egyptian concept of the vital essence, which distinguishes the living from the dead.
Possibly deriving from the name of the Egyptian goddess of wisdom and knowledge Seshat. Name borne by the mother of King Teti, who founded the Sixth Dynasty of Ancient Egypt
Diminutive of Sese. A known bearer of this name was the Georgian actor Aleksandre "Sesika" Kuprashvili (1904-1979).
From Sino-Korean 世 (se) meaning "world, generation" combined with 室 (sil) meaning "room, home, house". Other Hanja combinations are possible.
Bulgarian form of Cecilia, perhaps via its French form Cécile.A notable bearer of this name is the Bulgarian tennis player Sesil Karatantcheva (b. 1989).
Modern Georgian form of Cecilia. Other Georgian forms of the name are Sesilia and Tsetsilia, but these are older and rare.

Faroese and Fijian form of Cecilia as well as a Finnish variant of the name. In Georgia, it is a variant of Tsetsilia. A known bearer of this name was the Georgian actress Sesilia Taqaishvili (1906-1984).

Sesim is a modern, minimalist Turkish name formed from Ses ("voice") and the possessive suffix -im ("my"). Literally meaning "My Voice," it is a name of profound self-expression and identity. It signifies an individual who is heard, whose opinions matter, and who possesses the power of articulation. It is a powerful, contemporary choice for a child intended to grow up with agency, confidence, and a unique perspective to share with the world.
Short form of Sesili and Sesilia.

From Japanese 殺 (sechi) meaning "to kill", 生 (sho) meaning "life", and 丸 (maru) meaning "whole, round, circle". This is the name of Inuyasha's older half-brother in the manga and anime series 'Inuyasha'.
English cognate of Cécile, influenced by the botanical term sessile, meaning "a leaf issuing directly from the stem of the plant, rather than by a petiole."
Variant of Cecily, influenced by the botanical term sessile, meaning "a leaf issuing directly from the stem of the plant, rather than by a petiole."
Derived from Cissot, itself an archaic English diminutive of Cicely.
(雪洲, Sesshū), meaning "snowy field" (雪 means "snow" and 洲 means "north field")
Emilian-Romagnol feminine form of Sest and Italian feminine form of Sesto.
Italian form of Sextius or Sestius.
Variant of Estrid, predominantly used in Southern Sweden.
Czech and Slovak form of Seth 1.
Form of Seth 1 in various languages.
“Given name of the folk hero, Cúchulainn”. This birth name was imparted by the deity, Lug, prior to the conception of the demigod child by the mortal mother, Deichtine.
Means "praise, glory, worship, adoration" in Persian.
Seen in Shakespeare's play 'The Tempest' (1611), in which Setebos is the god worshipped by Caliban and Sycorax.

From the Spanish titles of the Virgin Mary, La Virgen de Setefilla and Nuestra Señora de Setefilla, meaning "The Virgin of Setefilla" and "Our Lady of Setefilla," venerated at the hermitage in Lora del Río in the Andalusian province of Seville. For this reason, usage of this name is particularly concentrated in that province.
From Egyptian stp-n-rꜥ meaning "chosen of Ra". This name was borne by the sixth and youngest daughter of the 14th-century BC Egyptian pharaoh Akhenaten.
Probably created as a feminine form of Seth 1, could also be a blend of Seth with either Stephanie or Bethanie.A famous bearer of this name is Sethanie Taing, a dancer, choreographer and model.
Form of Shethar used in the Vulgate (Latin Bible) as well as at least one English Bible: the Douay-Rheims Bible (1582-1610).

Created by Toni Morrison for her Pulitzer prize-winning novel "Beloved." Sethe is the mother of the title character, whom she murders out of an extreme act of love: she would rather kill her child than give it up to the hands of slavery.It was possibly used in the novel as a female version of Seth 1.
According to Gnosticism, Setheus is one of the great celestial powers dwelling in the Sixth Heaven.
Meaning as of yet unknown. This name is predominantly used in Ghana.

Etymology uncertain. Probably from Egyptian stẖ-prj-sn, perhaps meaning "the brother comes forth to Seth", from Egyptian prj "to come forth" combined with sn "brother" combined with the Egyptian God Seth 2. This was the serekh name of an early Egyptian pharaoh who ruled during the Second Dynasty of Egypt.
Name is originated from the word Rama Sethu , which is believed by the Hindu as the name of the bridge constructed by Lord Rama to reach Lanka to save his wife and Goddess Sita from Ravana.
Sethur, the son of Michael of the house of Asher, was a scout sent to Canaan prior to the crossing of the Jordan River according to Numbers 13:13.
Means "loyal, true, obedient, faithful" in Indonesian, ultimately from Sanskrit सत्य (satya).
Combination of Setia and Budi. A famous bearer is Indonesian nationalist Danoedirdja Setiaboedi (né Ernest Douwes Dekker).
From Indonesian setia meaning "loyal, obedient, faithful" combined with adi meaning "first" in Indonesian or "beautiful, good, valuable" in Javanese.
From Indonesian setia meaning "loyal, true" (of Sanskrit origin) combined with the feminine suffix -wati.
Of uncertain etymology, this was the name of an Ancient Egyptian noble woman who was likely the principal wife of the Pharoah Djedkare Isesi.
Used as a name for Khaemweset in Greco-Roman stories of ancient Egypt. Setna is a distortion of his title as setem-priest of Ptah; modern scholars call this character Prince Setna Khamwas.

A name assigned to Prince Khaemwaset of Egypt, son of Ramses the Great, in Greco-Roman times. The name is a distortion of his official title setem "priest of Ptah".Setne is a character in 'The Kane Chronicles', a series of novels by Rick Riordan.
variant of Seth which means "compensation"-------------------------------------From Japanese 瀬 (se) "torrent" and 人 (to) "person".

column3: 瀬戸香, 星秋華, 聖音花, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|せとか(Japanese Hiragana)|セトカ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: The name of a seedless and highly sweet Japanese tangor (written in hiragana), which was first registered in 1998.It can also be written in kanji, combining a se kanji like 瀬 meaning "shallows, rapids," 星 meaning "star" or 聖 meaning "sacred, holy," with a to kanji, such as 戸 meaning "door," 秋, from toki referring to an important time, or 音 meaning "sound," and a ka kanji like 香 meaning "fragrance" or 花/華 meaning "flower."This name is extremely rare.

column3: せつ(Japanese Hiragana)|セツ(Japanese Katakana)|せ津(Kanji/Hiragana)|節, 世津, 瀬津, 勢都, 拙, 摂節, 攝, 晢, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 節 (setsu) meaning "section, period, verse, melody", though it is often written せつ using the hiragana writing system. It can also come from せ (se) meaning "world" combined with 津 (tsu), a place name, such as Tsu city in Mie prefecture. Other kanji combinations are possible.A famous male bearer is Setsu Kobayashi, a professor of Keio university.

column3: セツカ(Japanese Katakana)|節加, 雪加, 節華, 雪華, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 節 (setsu) meaning "section, period, verse, melody" and 加 (ka) meaning "add, increase". Other kanji combinations can be used.
Setsu(説) means theory and Kei(敬) means respect. the name was Borne from Setsukei Makunokoji from an upcoming Danganronpa fangan, Danganronpa Twin fates

column3: 刹那, 雪菜(Japanese Kanji)|せつな(Japanese Hiragana)|セツナ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 刹那 (setsuna) meaning "a moment, an instant". It can also be given as a combination of 刹 (setsu) meaning "temple" or 雪 (setsu) meaning "snow" combined with Japanese 那 (na) a phonetic kanji or 菜 (na) meaning "vegetables, greens". 刹那 is by far the most popular spelling for boys, for girls the name is often written in hiragana. Other kanji combinations are possible. This name is extremely popular in Japanese manga and anime with many characters bearing the name.

column3: せつお(Japanese Hiragana)|セツオ(Japanese Katakana)|接央, 摂緒, 設生, 節緒, 刹朗, 説夫, 雪雄, 勢津郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 接 (setsu) meaning "touch" combined with 朗 (o) meaning "cheerful, sonorant, merry, clear, bright." Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 説矢, 雪伸, 雪耶, 雪矢, 晢也, 摂伸, 摂弥, 節允, 節也, 節耶, 説允, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 説 (setsu) meaning "theory" combined with 矢 (ya) meaning "arrow". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Possibly a variant of Seta, which is the Western Armenian transcription of Սեդա (see Seda).

Meaning uncertain. A famous bearer of this given name was Settela Steinbach (1934-1944), a Dutch Sinti girl who lost her life in the Auschwitz concentration camp during World War II. She posthumously became an icon of the Holocaust, due to her brief appearance in a video of the transit camp Westerbork, which had been made by fellow Holocaust victim Rudolf Breslauer (1903-1944 or 1945).
From Thai เศรษฐ (settha) meaning "excellent, best, supreme".
Former Faroese short form of Anicetus.
From Indonesian setia meaning "loyal, true" combined with the feminine suffix -ningsih (see Ningsih).
From Javanese sêtya meaning "loyal, faithful, obedient", ultimately from Sanskrit सत्य (satya).
From Javanese sêtya meaning "loyal, faithful, obedient" combined with either the masculine suffix -na or the word ana meaning "being, having, holding".
From Javanese sêtya meaning "loyal, faithful, obedient" combined with the feminine suffix -wati.
From 碩 "great, eminent; large, big" and 子 (ja) meaning "child".
From Sino-Korean 瑟 (seul) which refers to the se, an ancient Chinese bridge zither, or other hanja characters with the same pronunciation.
Transferred use of the name of the stratovolcano located at the northwestern tip of Sumatra, Seulawah Agam, itself of unknown etymology.
From Sino-Korean 瑟 (seul) meaning "se, zither" combined with native Korean 비 (bi) meaning "rain".
Feminine form of Seumas, anglicized as Jamesina.
From Sino-Korean 承 "inherit, receive; succeed" and 雅 "elegant, graceful, refined".
From the Sino-Korean seung meaning "rise, ascend" and Chinese an, meaning "peace, quiet". Other combinations are also possible.
From Sino-Korean 承 "inherit, receive; succeed" and 彬 "cultivated, well-bred".

column3: 승복(Korean Hangul)|昇福, 勝福, 承福, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 昇 (seung) meaning "rise, ascend", 勝 (seung) meaning "victory" or 承 (seung) meaning "inherit" combined with 福 (bok) meaning "fourtune, blessing, luck". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 승철(Korean Hangul)|承哲, 勝哲, 昇哲, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 承 (seung) meaning "inherit", 勝 (seung) meaning "victory, success" or 昇 (seung) meaning "rise, ascend" combined with 哲 (cheol) meaning "wise, sage". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 승철(Korean Hangul)|承哲, 勝哲, 昇哲, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Alternate transcription of Korean Hangul 승철 (see Seung-cheol).
From Sino-Korean 承 "inherit, receive; succeed" or 勝 "victory; excel, be better than" (seung) and 傑 "hero; outstanding, remarkable" (geol).

column3: 승희(Korean Hangul)|承熙, 承喜, 勝熙, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Alternate transcription of Korean Hangul 승희 (see Seung-hui).

Seung-heon, alternatively spelled Seung-hun, 承憲 in Hanja, is a male Korean given name.People with this name include:Lee Seung-heon (born 1950), pen name Lee Ilchi, South Korean self-help writerSong Seung-heon (born 1976), South Korean actorLee Seung-heon (born 2007), South Korean Singer and Idol.
From Sino-Korean 勝 (seung) "victory; excel, be better than" and 浩 (ho) "great, numerous, vast, abundant".

column3: 승호(Korean Hangul)|昇候, 昇厚, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino- Korean 昇 (seung) meaning "rise, ascend" combined with 候 (hu) meaning "expect, visit" or 厚 (hu) meaning "thick". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 승희(Korean Hangul)|承熙, 承喜, 勝熙, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 承 (seung) meaning "inherit" or 勝 (seung) meaning "victory, success" combined with 熙 (hui) meaning "bright, splendid, glorious" or 喜 (hui) meaning "like, love, enjoy". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
From Sino-Korean 承 "inherit, receive; succeed" and 勳 "meritorious deed".
From Sino-Korean 承 "inherit, receive; succeed" and 桓 "variety of tree (Chinese soapberry)".
From Sino-Korean 升 "arise, go up; advance" and 惠 "favor, benefit, confer kindness".

column3: 승혁(Korean Hangul)|昇爀, 勝爀, 承爀, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 昇 (seung) meaning "rise, ascend", 勝 (seung) meaning "victory" or 承 (seung) meaning "inherit" combined with 爀 (hyeok) meaning "red". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
From Sino-Korean 承 "inherit, receive; succeed" and 協 "be united; cooperate".
From 勝 "victory; excel, be better than",勝 meaning "victory", "win", "exellent", "good", "better" or 承 "inherit, receive; succeed" (seung) and 赫 "bright, radiant, glowing".

column3: 승일(Korean Hangul)|勝一, 勝日, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 勝 (seung) meaning "victory" combined with 一 (il) meaning "one" or 日 (il) meaning "day". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
From Sino-Korean 勝 "victory; excel, be better than" and 宰 "to slaughter; to rule".
From Sino-Korean 昇 "rise, ascent; peaceful; peace" and 辰 "early morning".

column3: 승주(Korean Hangul)|昇周, 勝周, 承周, 丞周, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 昇 (seung) meaning "rise, ascend" or 勝 (seung) meaning "victory" or 承 (seung) meaning "inherit" or 丞 (seung) meaning “assist, aid, rescue” combined with 周 (ju) meaning "circumference". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 승준(Korean Hangul)|承俊, 承埈, 勝俊, 勝準, 昇准, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 承 (seung) meaning "inherit", 勝 (seung) meaning "victory, success" or 昇 (seung) meaning "rise, ascend" combined with 俊 (jun) meaning "talented, handsome", 埈 (jun) meaning "high, steep, towering", 準 (jun) meaning "rule, guideline, standard" or 准 (jun) meaning "approve, permit". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 승관(Korean Hangul)|勝寬(Korean Hanja)|スングァン(Japanese Katakana)

column12: From Korean Hanja 勝 (seung) meaning "victory", "win", "exellent", "good", "better" and 奎 (kyu) meaning "star".Other Hanja combinations are possible.
From Sino-Korean 承 (seung) "inherit, receive; succeed" and 晩 (man) "night". A famous bearer is the first president of South Korea, Syngman Rhee (1875-1965).

column3: 승민(Korean Hangul)|承民, 承敏, 承旼, 昇敏, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 承 (seung) meaning "inherit" or 昇 (seung) meaning "rise, ascend" combined with 民 (min) meaning "people, citizens", 敏 (min) meaning "quick, clever, sharp" or 旼 (min) meaning "gentle, affable". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
From 勝 "victory; excel, be better than" or 承 "inherit, receive; succeed" (seung) and 묵 meaning neck.
From 勝 "victory; excel, be better than",勝 meaning "victory", "win", "exellent", "good", "better" or 承 "inherit, receive; succeed" (seung) and 泰 (tae) meaning "peaceful, calm, peace, easy."

Sevimbike is an elegant, historically monumental Turkic compound name formed by the fusion of two Old Turkic words: Sevim / Süyüm (beloved, darling, source of affection) and Bike / Begüm / Bige (noblewoman, princess, lady). The name translates directly to "The Beloved Princess" or "The Dear Noblewoman."The first element stems from the Proto-Turkic root sew- / süy- (to love, to cherish). In the Western Oghuz branch (Modern Turkish), this root stabilized as Sevim, while in the Kipchak branch (Tatar, Nogay, Bashkir), it retained its older vocalic form, Süyüm. The second element, Bike, is the ancient female counterpart to Beg / Bey, representing aristocratic status and leadership within the steppe hierarchy.Historical Attestation: The Queen of KazanThe name carries immense cultural, historical, and emotional weight across the Turkic world due to Süyümbike Hatun (1516–1554), the legendary ruler of the Kazan Khanate.Süyümbike was a Nogay princess by birth who became the regent queen of Kazan during the minority of her son, Utyamysh-Girey. She is immortalized in history, folklore, and poetry as a symbol of anti-imperial resistance, national dignity, and deep maternal devotion. When Kazan fell to Ivan the Terrible in 1552, she was captured and forcibly exiled. The famous Süyümbike Tower in the Kazan Kremlin stands to this day as a architectural monument to her legacy. Her tragic yet heroic life transformed Süyümbike / Sevimbike into an enduring emblem of freedom and patriotic love.Other Origins:Because of late medieval cross-cultural interactions, Sevimbike has frequently been subjected to overlapping folk etymologies, which must be clearly separated:The Arabic "Sawm" (صَوْم) Illusion: Folk etymologists sometimes attempt to link the Süyüm / Sevim prefix to the Arabic root S-W-M, specifically the word Sawm (fasting, abstinence), suggesting a religious connotation of spiritual purification. Linguistically, this is a complete coincidence; Sevimbike is entirely independent of Islamic religious terminology, tracking its roots straight back to pre-Islamic Turkic verbal morphology (sew-).The Pure Turkic "Sevim" Root: As an independent development in Oghuz Turkish, Sevim exists as a standalone name meaning "loveliness" and "charm." In the hybrid urban naming practices of the 19th and 20th centuries, this was combined smoothly with Bike to match the classical Kipchak Süyümbike, creating a phonetically modernized, unified Oghuz-Kipchak cognate.For parents, Sevimbike is a profound name that merges deep emotional warmth with royal, unyielding strength. It symbolizes a child who is universally cherished, yet possesses the dignity, resilience, and leadership qualities of an ancient queen. It is an honorary bridge between the heart's affection and history’s grandest legacies.

Sewinch Qaya represents the quintessential "union of the scholar and the statesman" during the Yuan dynasty. His name perfectly reflects this duality, blending the Old Turkic elements sevinç (joy, delight) and qaya (rock, stability). Born into a distinguished and highly influential Uyghur family in Gaochang, he was a pivotal intellectual figure whose life is verified by the Yuan Shi (History of Yuan) and his own surviving literary corpus, particularly his mastery of the sanqu poetic form.He belonged to the prominent Qaya Lineage, a family renowned for producing high-level governors, multi-lingual diplomats, and master calligraphers who served as the primary cultural conduits between the Uyghur steppe and the Chinese imperial administration.1. Father: He was the son of Xinxing Qaya (Shingşing Qaya), a high-ranking official who laid the foundation for the family's immense political and cultural capital in the Mongol court.2. Sister & Brother-in-law: His sister was married to the legendary Neo-Confucian statesman and vizier Lian Xixian (often dubbed the "Lian Mencius"). This marriage firmly entrenched Sewinch Qaya within the absolute intellectual and political elite of the empire.Contemporary accounts and his own poetry paint Sewinch Qaya as a deeply introspective, principled, and fiercely independent soul. Despite being born into immense privilege and possessing a brilliant mind suited for governance, he harbored a profound disdain for the superficiality and corruption of court politics. He was a man of quiet contemplation, characterized by a romantic longing for nature and spiritual autonomy. Displaying immense moral courage and a lack of worldly ambition, he famously abandoned his high-ranking political career at its peak. Choosing the "serenity of the eremitic life" over imperial luxury, he spent his remaining years embodying the classic ideal of the detached, nature-loving scholar-poet.

Shadoo is a surviving personal name in the Edisto language of South Carolina. This was the name of a captain or chief of the Edisto Nation encountered by Robert Sandford in 1666. The name is alternatively written in historical documents as Sheedou.The etymological meaning of this personal name has been lost to time, as the Edisto language, related to other Cusaboan languages, is largely unattested.Superficial comparisons can be drawn between the name "Shadoo" or "Sheedou" and other Cusaboan personal names, such as the preserved Escamacu personal name, Shemdadee. The Edisto prefix "Sha" or "Shee" may dialectically relate to preserved Cusaboan geographic names associated with bodies of water, like Shem Creek in Mount Pleasant, South Carolina, which was historically called Shamee, Shemee, Shembee, or Shimbee. However, the exact etymological meaning of this geographic name has also been lost due to the extinction of all members of the Cusabo language family.

Kazakh and Uzbek word for "chess". Derived from Persian shahamat, meaning "the shah (king) has been defeated".
Derived from شاه (shah) meaning "king" and نواز (navaz) meaning "chearish"
From Persian شاه (shah) meaning "king" and نواز (navaz) meaning "caress, cherish".
From Persian شاه (shāh) meaning "king" and Arabic نور (nūr) meaning "light".

The Native American name of the main protagonist in the Canadian animated TV series "Molly of Denali". The fictional girl is of Gwich'in, Koyukon, and Dena'ina Athabascan descent. In the Native names episode her Native name is "One who informs us."
Tajik and Uzbek form of Shihab.
Uzbek and Tajik form of Shihab ad-Din.

Derived from Arabic شَهَادَة (šahāda) meaning "testimony, witness", referring to the declaration of faith (Shahada) in Islamic tradition. It may also be considered of Persian origin, derived from شاه (šâh) meaning "king" and داد (dâd) meaning "justice, equality" or "gift".
It's mainly a Persian name since lots of words in Urdu come from Arabic/Persian words. It means "piece of royalty", Shah meaning king/royalty and Para meaning piece.
Nsme of a King of Adiabene orginating from Shah

Alternate transcription of Persian شهربانو (see Shahrbanoo).

A Middle Persian title meaning "the Boar of the Empire", from Middle Persian shahr "country" and warāz "boar", referencing the Zoroastrian deity Izad Vahram. This was the title of a shah (king) of the Sasanian Empire for approximately 40 days after being killed by Iranian nobles.
Possibly from Persian شاه‬ (shāh) meaning "king" combined with the name Rizal.
Malay, Tajik, and Uzbek form of Shahram. A notable bearer of this name is the Malaysian soccer player Shahrom Kalam (b. 1985).
Alternate transcription of Persian شهروز (see Shahrouz).
From Persian شاه (shāh) meaning "king" and روز (rūz) meaning "day".
First part of compound Arabic names beginning with شهر ال (Shahr al) meaning "month of the, moon of the".
Alternate transcription of Persian شهروز (see Shahrouz).

Means "royal horseman". From Persian شاه (shāh) meaning "king" and سوار (sawār) meaning "horseman, cavalryman, rider".
The Persian Ruler who lived in 625 bc.
From Persian شاه (shāh) meaning "king" and زیب (zib) meaning "embellishment, ornament, beauty".
From شاه (shāh) meaning "king" and زين (zayn) meaning "beauty" or "beautiful".
