Uzbek and Tajik form of Shahzad.
Derived from the given name Shahzod and the Turkish military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".

Means "(that which is) ordained". In the Ancient Egyptian mythology Shai was the deification of the concept of fate and determinate the span of men's lives as such would sometimes be considered female (in which case he would sometimes be called Shait).
A modern English feminine variant of the Hebrew masculine name Shai.
Combination of the name Shai and the letters יה (ya) which are part of the name of God.
A variant of Shade or a variant transcription of Shahid 1.
Hebrew combination of Shai - "gift" and El - "God". When combined, it takes up the meaning of "Gift of God" or "Gift from God". Alternate spelling of Shaiel. Typically a unisex name.
Combination of the name Shai "gift" and El "Lord"
Bengali and Malay variant of Saiful.

From the Arabic root ش-ي-خ (sh-y-kh), which means "female sheikh" or "matron." Aside from its use as a given name it is sometimes used as an honorific for respected women, such as daughters or wives of sheikhs, or women holding leadership or religious scholarly roles.
From the Arabic title شَيْخ (šayḵ) meaning "chief, chieftain, head" combined with the name of the religion Islam.
Meaning unknown. A known bearer was Shaikhzada Babich, a Bashkir writer and poet.
Spanish form of Shyla, reflecting the English pronunciation.

Means "daughter of the mountain" from Sanskrit शैल (śaila) meaning "mountain" combined with पुत्री (putrī) meaning "daughter". This is the name of a manifestation of the goddesses Parvati and Durga and the first Navadurga (nine forms of Durga).
A Hindi name meaning 'king of mountains'. One notable bearer is Shailen Bhatt, the administrator of the American Federal Highway Administration.
From Sanskrit शैल (shaila) meaning "mountain" combined with the name of the Hindu god Indra. This is an epithet of the god Shiva.
Combination of Shai and the popular suffix -lene. This name is borne by American actress Shailene Woodley.
Modern Hindi transcription of Sanskrit शैलेश (Shailesha) meaning "lord of the mountains", derived from शैल (śaila) meaning "mountain" and ईश (īśa) meaning "lord, ruler".
Variant of Shaylee. Sometimes used as a Diminutive of Shailene.
Combination of Shai and Li 2; means "gift for me" from Hebrew שַׁי (shai) meaning "gift" and לִי (li) meaning "to me, for me".
Possibly derived from the word shilhi which means "weapon, armor." This is the name of the female Chosen One in Robert Newcomb's Chronicles of Blood and Stone.
Variant of Shane or transferred use of surname Shain
Combination of the name Shai, means "gift". And the name Or, means "light".
Means "civilised, courteous, polite" in Urdu, ultimately from Persian شایسته‎ (shayesteh).
Alternate transcription of Urdu شائستہ (see Shaista).
The feminine form of Shai (the Egyptian god).
Variant of Shavonte. Shaivonte Aician Gilgeous-Alexander, also known as SGA, is a Canadian professional basketball player for the Oklahoma City Thunder in the National Basketball Association (NBA).
King of kings/ worshipper of Lord Shiva (Hindu god).
Alternate transcription of Kyrgyz Шайыр (see Shayyr).
Alternate transcription of Bengali সজল (see Sajal).
Means "trees, shrubs" or "origin, family" in Arabic.
Possibly from Arabic شَجَاعَة (šajāʿa) meaning "courage, bravery".
Combination of the prefix sha- combined with the name Juan 1 (See also Dajuan).
Combination of the prefix sha- with the name Juana thus strictly making it the feminine form of Shajuan (See also Dejuana)
Shak means "to see". It was most popular in the year 1996.

Means "bearing vegetables" from Sanskrit शाक (śāka) meaning "vegetable, greens" and भरि (bhari) meaning "bearing, possessing, bestowing, granting". This is the name of the Hindu goddess of nourishment identified with Durga.
Transferred use of the surname Shakamuri; of people belonging to kamma caste of category-1 (chowdary's).
From the Armenian word շաքար (šakʿar) meaning "sugar". In use since the 13th century.
Meaning uncertain, possibly an elaborated form of Zulu Shaka or Hebrew Shachar. This name was used by American football player Willie Gault for his daughter born 1986.
Derived from shakar meaning "sugar" and jon meaning "soul".
Derived from shakar meaning "sweet, sugar" and xo'ja meaning "master".
Combination of the phonetic elements sha, kay and la, likely influenced by Shakila. Also compare Jakayla, Nakayla, Lakayla.

This name is originaly Persian means : patience or tolerance,it used in Syria,Lebanon,Iraq. it can be used for females but with adding A,H in the end "Shakeebah" . Shakeeb Arsalan was very famous Arab writer ,this name has been getting old fashioned.The reference of the meaning of this name is The Arabic Persian Dictionary page number 376 ,it is translated in English "The Golden Dictionary" by Muhammad Al-Tunji
Alternate transcription of Arabic شكيلة (See Shakila).
"Cup bearer " metaphorically means "life","spiritual power" Aramaic,Armenian origin
Variant of Chekesha, or simply a combination of the popular phonetic prefix sha and the name Keisha.
Alternate transcription of Arabic شاكر (see Shakir).
Transferred use of the surname Shakespear.
Transferred use of the surname Shakespeare first borne as a forename of William Shakespeare’s grandson Shakespeare Quiney.
term used for naming the person who had been visited the mountains by feet and have desirability to see any high mountains.
Comes from شخصية (šaḵṣīyah), which means "personality", "rank, nobility", or "character (in a story)" in Arabic.
An invented name blending sha with Nakia.
Derived from Persian شکیب (šekib) meaning "patience, tolerance".
Malay and Indonesian form of Shakila.
Perhaps a variant of Shekinah, or possibly an invented name based on the sound of names such as Shakia, Shanika and Shakila.
Alternate transcription of Shakira as well as the Malay form.
Combination of Shakir with the Turkish military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".
Diminutive of Shakro and Shalva. In the case of the latter name, perhaps Shako first started out as a contraction of Shaliko.
Notable bearer is child actor Shakohahiiostha Jacobs.
Means "little six" in Dakota, from šákpe meaning "six". According to tribal histories, the first chief of this name was the sixth child of a set of sextuplets.
Means "powerful, mighty, strong" in Sanskrit. This is the Buddhist equivalent of the Hindu god Indra.

Diminutive of Zakaria (compare Zakro). However, it can also be an independent name in its own right, in which case it is derived from the Georgian noun შაქარი (shakari) meaning "sugar", which is ultimately of Persian origin.
From Sanskrit शक्ति (śakti) meaning "power" combined with पद (pada) meaning "foot".
Means "bird" in Sanskrit. In the Hindu epic the Mahabharata Shakuni is a prince of the Gandhara kingdom and the brother of Gandhari.
Combination of the prefix sha and Kyla.
Variant of Shakira or a combination of the prefix sha- with the name Kyra.According to the USA Social Security Administration, 73 girls were recorded with the name Shakyra in 2001.

The name of a Mesopotamian corn goddess who is also associated with war as well as the name of a Sumerian goddes of grain and the emotion of compassion.The name is said to be derived from either Akkadian šala'u "to shoot" or šalû "to submerge".

Alternate transcription of Arabic / Urdu شالامار باغ (see Shalimar). Though the name began to be used (in very small numbers) in America in the 1950s and 1960s, it gained some recognition there in 1980 following the release of the song 'Three for Love' by the R&B group of the same name.
Combination of the phonetic prefix sha and the name Lana, perhaps based on Shalonda or Shelena.

Etymology uncertain. Shalash was a goddess worshipped in the Hurrian, Eblaite, and Babylonian pantheons. She was considered to be the consort of the god Dagon. In the Hurrian tradition Ḫepat was their daughter, and Shalash was worshipped as a part of the Kaluti (or offering lists) of both Ḫepat and Šauška. Her Mesopotamian equivalent was Ninlil.
From the Hebrew name שָׁאוּל (Sha'ul) which meant "asked for" or "prayed for". This was the name of the first king of Israel who ruled just before King David, as told in the Old Testament.
Combination of the phonetic elements sha, lee and ya.
Combination of the phonetic prefix sha and the name Leesa, possibly modelled on Jaleesa and Shelena.
Could be from Manasseh, with an unknown prefix.
Combination of the phonetic elements sha and lene.
Meaning unknown, possibly of Mingrelian origin.
An invented name, blending the popular phonetic prefix sha and the name Alexus.
Means "flame" in Hebrew. This word appears briefly in the Old Testament books of Job and Ezekiel.
From a Hebrew term meaning "blaze; flame", derived from an unused root להב (lahab) meaning "gleam/blade (of a flame)“.
Variant of Shaila modeled after Shelia.
Variant of Shalia coinciding with the word shaliah, which in the context of Judaism means "emissary".
Of uncertain meaning, this was the personal name of Consort Gui of the Wanyan clan, who was a consort of the fourth Jin emperor Digunai.

From the name of the Shalamar Gardens near what is now Lahore, Pakistan, which were created in the mid-17th century by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan (who also built the Taj Mahal). It might be derived from Arabic shah al-‘imarat meaning "master of buildings". This spelling of the name is sometimes given in reference to the Guerlain perfume called Shalimar, which was first introduced in 1921 and was named after the famous Mughal gardens. This was also used for the titular Egyptian princess (played by actress Debra Paget) in the 1954 movie Princess of the Nile.
Of uncertain origin and meaning.Current theories range from a newly coined name combining the prefix Sha- with Line, a variant of Shelena, to a variant of Shalina.
From the Hindi adjective शालीन (śālīn) meaning "modest, ladylike", which comes from Sanskrit शालीन (śālīna).
Combination of the popular name elements sha, lee, and sha. Could possibly come from the Biblical village of Baal-Shalisha.
Of uncertain meaning. This was the name of a Jurchen noblewoman who led a militia to fight against a rebellion in Huanglong Superior Prefecture.
Of unknown origins and meaning. Shalla Nelprin is a character in the 'Star Wars: X-Wing' book series.
Variation of the phrase Inshallah meaning "god willing". Name is most famous for being Raekwon's aliases. Also common as a last name.
Possibly a blend of the popular phonetic prefix sha with Yolanda or Rolanda. Also compare Lashonda.

From Sanskrit शल्य (śalya) meaning "javelin, arrow, spear". This is the name of a major character in the Mahabharata and the ruler of the Madra kingdom, an ancient Indo-Aryan region in northwestern India.
This name either means silence or beautiful woman.
Likely from the Arabic word Sham meaning "candle". Could also be a variant of Shem.

This name comes from שמע (shama'), meaning "to hear".In the Bible, Shama is one of David's warriors. He is the son of Hotham and the brother of Jeiel. Shama is only mentioned once in the Bible, in 1 Chronicles 11:44.

The first element of this name is uncertain; it might possibly be derived from Persian شام (sham) meaning "dusk" as well as "evening". The second element is most likely derived from Arabic دولة (dawla) meaning "state" (see Sepedavle).
From the Tatar чшэмэ (sheme) meaning "question mark" and гол (gol) meaning "flower".

Modern Hebrew transcription of Shammai. Known bearers include Shamai Haber (1922-1995), a Polish-born sculptor who lived and worked in Paris, France; Shamai Leibowitz, an American linguist and whistleblower; and Israeli archer Shamai Yamrom (2005-).
Combination of the phonetic elements sha and mar, probably modelled on Lamar or Jamar.
Variant of Shamara.Also used as a variant of Shemariah in Young's Literal Translation of the Bible (2 Chronicles 11:19).

Feminine form of Shambhu. This is an epithet of the Hindu goddess Parvati.
Borne by Filipino beauty pageant titleholder Shamcey Supsup (1986-), who has said that her name was invented by her mother 'from her reading of Mills & Boon romance novels.'
Masculine form of Shamika, bearer: Shameik Moore an American actor.
Combination of prefix sha and Misha.
Means "the luscious one". Name borne by a prominent character in the Epic of Gilgamesh, responsible for bringing the wild man Enkidu to the city of Uruk.
Combination of the phonetic elements sha, mee and na.
Combination of the phonetic element sha with the name Miracle.
Assyrian and Armenian form of Semiramis.
Combination of the phonetic elements sha, mee and sha.
South Indian and Sinhalese form of Shamita.

Simple meaning: Helpful Healer.Derived from the old Persian Qajar aj Šâhanšâhiye Irân, name given to Ardabīl boys meaning the 'Kindhearted healer'. Despite the substantial scholarly efforts to uncover the etymology of the name, the name still poses an enigma. A village in Sajjadrud Rural District, Bandpey-ye Sharqi District, Babol County, Mazandaran Province, Iran; is named after 'Parminav Shamiun' Persian: پرميناو شميون‎, also Romanized as Parmīnāv Shamīūn, known to have healed hundreds of men from a widespread epidemic of plague that occurred in several outbreaks in 1526 - 1533. 'Savory; chpt: The Safavid empire at the height of its power under Shāh Abbas the Great (1588-1629)'.Additional Note:Name 'Shamiun' is hypothetically a derivation of the name Shimeun(شمعون) of Hebrew origin: Prophet Joseph's half-brother's name. Meaning "light of the world" from sham meaning "light" and jahon meaning "the world".
Either from Arabic شمس (shams) meaning "sun" or شمال (shamal) meaning "north" combined with the Turkic title khan meaning "leader, ruler".
From Arabic شَامِل (shamil) "to contain, to include" making it relative of Shamil.
Shammai was a Jewish scholar of the 1st century, and an important figure in Judaism's core work of rabbinic literature, the Mishnah.
Shammua, the son of Zaccur of the house of Reuben, was a scout sent to Canaan prior to the crossing of the Jordan River according to Numbers 13:4.
Derived from the Uzbek shamol meaning "wind" and boy meaning "rich, wealthy".

Means "dawn light". This was the Arabic name taken by a Christian concubine of Muhammad II al-Faqih, who was the mother of his son Nasr.
Means "sun of the age", from Arabic شَمْس (shams) meaning "sun" and زَمَن (zamān) meaning "time, age, era".

Means "solar" in Arabic, from شَمْس (šams) meaning "sun", also used as an alternate transcription of Azerbaijani Şəmsi. It is a solely feminine name in Iran and solely masculine in Azerbaijan.

Uzbek and Tajik form of Shams ad-Din.

From Hebrew שִׁמְשִׁיאֵל (Šīmšīʾēl) meaning "God is my sun", derived from שֶׁמֶשׁ (shemesh) meaning "sun" and אֵל (ʾel) meaning "God". The Book of Enoch names him as a fallen angel, one of the 200 Watchers who copulated with human women. Other sources describe him as a holy angel, with some holding him as the guardian of the Garden of Eden after Adam and Eve's expulsion.
Derived from Arabic شَمْس (šams) meaning "sun" combined with جَمَال (jamāl) meaning "beauty".
Derived from the Uzbek shams meaning "the sun" and nahor meaning "daytime".
Derived from the Uzbek shams meaning "the sun" and nazar meaning "look, glance".

Means "sun of the world" in Arabic.

Alternate transcription of Bengali শামসুজ্জামান (see Shamsuzzaman).
First part of compound Arabic names beginning with شمس ال (Shams al) meaning "sun of the" (such as Shams al-Din).
From Arabic شمس العالم (shams al-alam), meaning "sun of the world".

From the Arabic phrase شمس الزمان (shams az-zamān) meaning "sun of the era", derived from شمس (shams) meaning "sun" and زمان (zamān) meaning "time, age, era".
From monarchial title of Dagestani royalty шамхал (shamxal). It is unknown meaning.

An invented name, combining the phonetic elements sha, my and ya, and sharing a sound with other popular names such as Amaya and Shania. It is sometimes claimed to derive from Shemaiah, a masculine name in the Old Testament that is pronounced similarly. It can be spelled Shamya or with a capitalized third letter as ShaMya (or Sha'Mya).
Shan is an Indian name meaning "pride" or "prestige". It comes from the Sanskrit name Shaan.

column12: From Japanese 沙 (sha) meaning "sand" combined with 夏 (na) meaning "summer". Other kanji combinations are possible.

Irish word for "a skilled teller of tales or legends, especially Gaelic ones." From the Scots Gaelic word seanachaidh, from Old Irish senchaid, variant of senchae, meaning historian, derived from sen, meaning old.
Meaning uncertain. Name borne by a Nubian queen of Kush, who ruled from 170 to 150 BCE. She is the earliest known female ruler of Kush, and is said to have ruled without a king.
Etymology unknown. This was the name of a queen regnant of the Kingdom of Kush.
Likely an alternate spelling of Shannon, which may possibly have been influenced by the name Ann.
Of uncertain meaning, this was the personal name of a Beothuk woman, known for being the last known living member of the Beothuk people.

column12: From Chinese 善 (shàn) meaning "good, virtuous" combined with 导 (dǎo) meaning "to direct, to guide, to lead, to conduct". Other hanzi combinations are possible. 善导 was the Dharma name of Shandao (613–681), Chinese Buddhist scholar monk and influential figure of East Asian Pure Land Buddhism.

Probably a variant spelling of Shanae.

From the Chinese 上 (shàng) meaning "top, superior, highest" and 翠 (cuì) meaning "green, kingfisher".

Shangdi (Chinese: 上帝; pinyin: Shàngdì; Wade–Giles: Shang Ti), also written simply, "Emperor" (Chinese: 帝; pinyin: Dì), is the Chinese term for "Supreme Deity" or "Highest Deity" in the theology of the classical texts, especially deriving from Shang theology and finding an equivalent in the later Tian ("Heaven" or "Great Whole") of Zhou theology.
Combination of the prefix sh with Angela.
From Chinese 祥 (xiáng) meaning "good luck, good omen" and 芳 (fāng) meaning "fragrant, virtuous, beautiful".

From the Chinese 上 (shàng) meaning "top, superior, highest" and 珍 (zhēn) meaning "precious, valuable, rare". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

Combination of the phonetic element sha and the name suffix nique (from Monique or Dominique). Also compare Shaniqua.

column12: From the characters 少 (shào, meaning “young”) and 昊 (hào, meaning “vastness” or “heaven”). In Chinese mythology, Shaohao was one of the Five Emperors, sage-kings who ruled during the early days of Chinese civilization. He is commonly regarded as a son of the Yellow Emperor (Xuanyuan) and Leizu, though other accounts say that his mother was a heavenly fairy or a mortal woman impregnated upon sighting a comet. Shaohao is known for founding a kingdom of birds in the east, where he chose different bird species to handle different offices according to their temperament. He later moved to the west where he and his son, Rushou, were placed in charge of the setting sun. He later became deified as the White Emperor of the West.Shaohao is also known under the names Qingyang (青阳), Xuanxiao (玄嚣) and Zhi (挚). Emperor Shaohao, the ruler of the Pandaren race in World of Warcraft, is named after him.

She moves silently through the shadows, protecting those she loves with a fierce, almost sacred devotion. From the name of a private or secret language spoken by Irish Travellers (a group also known as the Pavee). It means "a voice that moves" in Shelta ("moves" in the sense of being emotional, endearing and affectionate) and some modern Celticists think it comes from the Irish Gaelic word siúlta which means "walking" (the "s" is pronounced "sh" and the diphthong is as much like a slurred schwa sound).The word Shelta was first recorded in 1876, by American "gypsiologist" Charles Leland. He was the first "country man" to come across the then generally unknown language of the Irish Travellers/Pavee, which its speakers have always called the Cant or Gammon, while he was doing field work on Gypsies in England and Wales.

Its name literally means "city" in Arabic, so the etymology remains the same.Georgian sources state that the name means "the conscience of faith", where the second element is clearly derived from the Arabic noun دين (dīn) meaning "religion, faith".In Georgian literature, Shermadin is the name of a character from the 12th-century epic poem The Knight in the Panther's Skin written by the Georgian poet Shota Rustaveli. Derived from the Uzbek sher meaning "lion" and toyloq meaning "young foal" or "dear, darling".

Sheshai was a clan of Anakim living in Hebron named for a son of Anak in the Holy Bible (Numbers 13:22). The clans were driven out of the city by Caleb (Joshua 15:14) and the Tribe of Judah (Judges 1:10).
InuYasha's half-brother, Shesshoumaru is a full dog demon in the manga/anime InuYasha. According to the character guide it means "Killing Perfection".

Bengali word for the plant Nyctanthes arbor-tristis, also known as "night-blooming jasmine". Ultimately from Sanskrit śephāla (शेफाल) via phāla (फल).A common feminine name in Bangladesh as well West Bengal, where it is the state flower. It has many spelling variations when converted into English, Sheuly being the most frequent.

This name is used by the fictional character in the Japanese video game series "Resident Evil".
From the Hebrew word שֶׁבַח (shévakh) "Praise; appreciation, raise in value".

The name of various characters in the Book of Mormon.

From Egyptian sšmw, derived from Egyptian sšmj "to lead, to guide" and -w, a masculine suffix. Shezmu is an ancient Egyptian deity with a contradictory character. He was worshiped from the early Old Kingdom period.

This was the name of a goddess in Elamite religion. It is uncertain what the meaning of her name was in the Elamite language. Not much is known about Shiashum, unfortunately. It is said that she, along with the goddesses Narundi and Niarzina, was a sister of the "great goddess", namely Kiririsha. She was entitled "keeper of the palace of the gods" in the late Elamite period, so perhaps she was a guardian of some sort.

column12: From Japanese 茂 (shige) meaning "lush, luxuriant" or 重 (shige) meaning "layers, folds" combined with 乃 (no), a possessive particle. Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.

column3: 薫信, 恵宣, 恵庸, 滋延, 滋信, 滋布, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 薫 (shige) meaning "fragrant, scented" combined with 信 (nobu) meaning "true; accurate; verifiable". Other kanji combinations are possible.A famous bearer was Shigenobu Ookuma, the founder of Waseda University.

column3: 成敬, 成孝, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 成 (shige) meaning "to become, to do something" combined with 孝 (nori) meaning "filial piety" or 敬 (nori) meaning "respect, honor, reverence". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 茂, 繁, 繁理, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|しげり(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: From 茂り/繁り (shigeri) meaning "to grow thick, to flourish".

column3: しげろう(Japanese Hiragana)|シゲロウ(Japanese Katakana)|慈郎, 滋郎, 重良, 重郎, 成郎, 繁郎, 茂朗, 茂郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 慈 (shige) meaning "mercy" combined with 郎 (rou) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 繁貴, 孝貴, 敬貴, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 茂 (shige) meaning "lush, luxuriant" or 重 (shige) meaning "layers, folds" combined with 隆 (taka) meaning "noble". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 繁斗, 重翔, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 成 (shige) meaning "to become" and 人 (to) meaning "person".

column3: しげとき(Japanese Hiragana)|シゲトキ(Japanese Katakana)|茂時, 重辰, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 重 (shige) meaning "layers, folds" and 時 (toki) meaning "time". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 重朝, 重友, 誠友, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 重 (shige) meaning "layers, fold" and 朝 (tomo) meaning "morning". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 茂寿, 恵敏, 滋世, 重敬, 成刀士, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 栄 (shige) meaning "glory, honor" combined with 智 (toshi) meaning "wisdom, intellect, knowledge". Other kanji combinations are possible.A famous bearer is Shigetoshi Hasegawa (1968-), a retired relief pitcher in Major League Baseball and best-selling author and Japanese television personality.

column3: 繁緒, 成緒, 茂緒, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 繁 (shige) meaning "flourishing, luxuriant" and 緒 (tsugu) meaning "beginning, mental or emotional state". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: しげよ(Japanese Hiragana)|シゲヨ(Japanese Katakana)|薫代, 成夜, 滋世, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 薫 (shige) meaning "scented, fragrant" combined with 代 (yo) meaning "world, society". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 重頼, 成頼, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 重 (shige) meaning "layers, folds" and 頼 (yori) meaning "to rely, to depend on". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 成美, 重儀, 樹美, 滋与史, 栄嘉, 重敬, 重吉, 重昌, 重徳, 重珍, 重令, 成元, 蒼芳, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 成 (shige) meaning "to become" combined with 美 (yoshi) meaning "beautiful". Other kanji combinations are possible.A famous bearer is Shigeyoshi Mochizuki, a former Japanese football player. He played for Japan national team. He was capped 14 times for the Japanese national team and scored the winning goal in Asian Cup 2000 Final, Japan vs Saudi Arabia.

column3: 栄侑, 栄征, 栄千, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 栄 (shige) meaning "honor, glory" combined with 侑 (yuki) meaning "help, recommend, reward, forgive". Other kanji combinations can be used.
Of uncertain meaning, this was the personal name of a consort of Digunai, who was the mother of his third son. She was the sister of Dingge and Puluhuzi.

column3: 志久真, 志俱馬, 志群磨, 詩空真, 矢功正, 信玖満, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|しぐま(Japanese Hiragana)|シグマ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Borrowed from Greek σίγμα (sigma), the name of the 18th letter of the Greek alphabet.It can be written with a variety of kanji, combining a shi kanji like 志 meaning "will, aim, goal," 詩 meaning "poem," 矢 meaning "arrow" or 信 meaning "honesty, sincerity," with one that can be read as gu, such as 俱, 久 meaning "long time," 群 meaning "group, bunch," 空 meaning "sky," 功 meaning "merit, success; achievement" or 玖, referring to the numeral nine in legal documents, and a ma kanji like 真 meaning "truth," 馬 meaning "horse," 磨 meaning "polish, shine," 正 meaning "exact, precise" or 満 meaning "full, whole."This name is very rarely used.

column3: 時雨(Japanese Kanji)|しぐれ(Japanese Hiragana)|シグレ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name is used as 時雨 with 時 (ji, toki, -doki) meaning "hour, time" and 雨 (u, ama-, ame, -same) meaning "rain."As a word, Shigure refers to a drizzle or a shower in late autumn/fall or early winter.This name is very rarely given to children, if given at all.

column3: 时, 实, 史, 石, etc.(Chinese)|時, 實, 史, 石, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: Alternate transcription of Shi (using the Wade-Giles romanization system).
Means "shooting star of the religion" from Arabic شهاب (shihāb) meaning "shooting star, meteor" combined with دين (dīn) meaning "religion, faith".
Alternate transcription of Arabic شهاب الدين (see Shihab ad-Din).
Alternate transcription of Arabic شهاب الدين (see Shihab ad-Din).
Indonesian and Malay form of Shihab ad-Din.

column3: 世豪, 士豪, 仕豪, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 世 (shì) meaning "world, generation, era", 士 (shì) meaning "officer, general" or 仕 (shì) meaning "scholar, official" combined with 豪 (háo) meaning "brave, heroic, chivalrous". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 诗嘉, etc.(Chinese)|詩嘉, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
世杰, 士杰, etc.(Chinese)|世傑, 士傑, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: Wade-Giles romanization of Shijie used in Taiwan.

column3: 識賢, 世賢, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: Wade-Giles romanisation of Shixian, used in Taiwan.

column3: 世华, 施嬅, etc.(Chinese)|世華, 施嬅, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: Wade-Giles romanization of Shihua used in Taiwan.

column3: 世英, 士英, 时英, 诗颖, 诗盈, etc.(Chinese)|時英, 詩穎, 詩盈, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: Varient transcription of Shiying (using Gwoyeu Romatzyh).

column3: 时敏, 诗敏, etc.(Chinese)|時敏, 詩敏, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: Wade-Giles romanization of Shimin used in Taiwan.

column3: 詩穂子, 志穂子, 紫穂子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 詩 (shi) meaning "poem, song", 穂 (ho) meaning "grain", and 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: しほり(Japanese Hiragana)|シホリ(Japanese Katakana)|糸秀莉, 知星吏, 紫穂利, 枝保凛, 始宝璃, 司秀理, 四甫利, 思法璃, 紙歩凛, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 姿 (shi) meaning "figure, shape" or 梓 (shi) meaning "catalpa, Japanese cherry birch", combined with 星 (ho) meaning "dot, star" or 歩 (ho) meaning "walk", and 吏 (ri) meaning "history" or 莉 (ri) meaning "white jasmine". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 世华, 施嬅, etc.(Chinese)|世華, 施嬅, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 世 (shì) meaning "life, age, generation, era" or 施 (shī) meaning "establish, render, put into effect" combined with 华 (huá) meaning "splendid, illustrious, Chinese" or 嬅 (huá) meaning "beautiful" (which is only feminine). Other character combinations can form this name as well.
Shihuh is an Arab tribal surname that means "nationality."
From the Chinese 诗 (shī) meaning "poetry, poem" and 慧 (huì) meaning "bright, intelligent".

column3: 时伟, 世伟, 实味, etc.(Chinese)|時偉, 世偉, 實味, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: Wade-Giles romanization of Shiwei used in Taiwan.

column3: 紫衣舞, 翔優, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 紫 (shi) meaning "purple; violet", 衣 (i) meaning "clothes" combined with 舞 (ma) meaning "dance". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: シイナ(Japanese Katakana)|しいな(Japanese Hiragana)|しい奈(Kanji/Hiragana)|椎名, 詩衣菜, 志衣菜, 詩衣菜, 惟七, 惟杏, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 椎 (shii) meaning "chinquapin, Castanopsis tree" combined with 七 (na) meaning "seven". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Chinese 世 (shì) meaning "world, generation, era" combined with 绩 (jì) "achievement, accomplishment". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From Chinese 诗 (shī) meaning "poetry" combined with 佳 (jiā) meaning "fine, beautiful". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 世杰, 士杰, etc.(Chinese)|世傑, 士傑, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 世 (shì) meaning "life, age, generation, era" or 士 (shì) meaning "officer, general, scholar, official" combined with 杰 (jié) meaning "heroic, outstanding". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 四島, 志島, 黙(Japanese Kanji)|しじま(Japanese Hiragana)|シジマ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Comes from ハオルチア・シジマ (Haoruchia-Shijima), the Japanese word for Haworthia, a large genus of small succulent plants native to Southern Africa. It can also come from Japanese 四 (shi) meaning "four" or 志 (shi) meaning "will, motive" combined with 島 (jima) meaning "island", or 黙 (shijima) meaning "silence". Other kanji combinations are possible.Cianwood City Gym Leader Chuck (who is also known as Shijima) in the Japanese version of Pokémon Gold, Silver, Crystal, Heartgold, and Soulsilver is a fictional bearer of this name.

column3: 诗瑾, 诗锦, 世金, 石进, etc.(Chinese)
column12: The name "SHIJIN" was orginated in China.
From the Chinese 诗 (shī) meaning "poetry, poem" and 晶 (jīng) meaning "crystal, clear, bright".
From Mongolian шижир (shijir) meaning "solid, noble, pure" and баатар (baatar) meaning "hero".
From Mongolian шижир (shijir) meaning "noble, pure" and бат (batu) meaning "strong, firm".
From the Chinese 诗 (shī) meaning "poetry, poem" and 娟 (juān) meaning "beautiful, graceful".

column3: 鹿, 史可, 志佳, 紫花, 詩夏(Japanese Kanji)
column12: This name can be used as 鹿, 史可, 志佳, 紫花 or 詩夏 with 鹿 (roku, shika, ka) meaning "deer," 史 (shi) meaning "chronicle, history," 志 (shi, kokorozashi, kokoroza.su, shiringu) meaning "aspire, hopes, intention, motive, plan, resolve, shilling," 紫 (shi, murasaki) meaning "purple, violet," 詩 (shi, uta) meaning "poem, poetry," 可 (ka, kou, -be.ki, -be.shi) meaning "can, do not, mustn't, passable, should not," 佳 (ka, kei) meaning "beautiful, excellent, good, pleasing, skilled," 花 (ka, ke, hana) meaning "flower" and 夏 (ka, ga, ge, natsu) meaning "summer."

From Chinese 世 (shì) meaning "world, generation, era" combined with 凯 (kǎi) meaning "triumph, victory, music of triumph", as well as other hanzi combinations. A notable bearer was the first official president of the Republic of China, Yuan Shikai (1859-1916).

column3: 鹿丸(Japanese Kanji)|しかまる(Japanese Hiragana)|シカマル(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name is used as 鹿丸 with 鹿 (roku, shika, ka) meaning "deer" and 丸 (gan, maru, maru.i, maru.meru) meaning "curl up, explain away, full, make round, month, perfection, pills, roll up, round, seduce."One fictional bearer of this name is Shikamaru Nara (奈良 シカマル), a character from the popular manga and anime series Naruto.This name is very rarely given to boys, if given at all.
Means "hunter" in Hindi, ultimately from Persian شکاری (shikārī).
Indepedent Lifestyle and Goddess of Love

column3: 思軒, 子顕, 史賢, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 思 (shi) meaning "think" combined with 軒 (ken) meaning "carriage". Other kanji combinations are possible.

Means "crested, pointed" or "fire" in Sanskrit, derived from शिखा (śikhā) meaning "crest, plume" or "flame". In Buddhist tradition this is the name of the 23rd of the 27 buddhas preceding Siddhartha Gautama, so named because he wore a turban that resembled a flame. In Pali he is known as Sikhī.

column3: 志樹, 志基, 志希, 志輝, 志騎, 志季, 志起, 詩希, 詩季, 詩稀(Japanese Kanji)|しき(Japanese Hiragana)|シキ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name can be used as 志樹, 志基, 志希, 志輝, 志騎, 志季, 詩希, 詩季, 詩稀 with 志 (shi, kokorozashi, kokoroza.su, shiringu) meaning "aspire, hopes, intention, motive, plan, resolve, shilling," 詩 (shi, uta) meaning "poem, poetry," 樹 (ju, ki) meaning "timber trees, wood," 基 (ki, moto, motoi) meaning "foundation, fundamentals," 希 (ki, ke, mare) meaning "beg, few, hope, phenomenal, pray, rare, request," 輝 (ki, kagaya.ku) meaning "gleam, radiance, shine, sparkle, twinkle," 騎 (ki) meaning "equestrian, riding on horses," 季 (ki) meaning "seasons," 起 (ki, o.kiru, o.kosu, oko.su, o.koru, ta.tsu) meaning "get/wake up, rouse" and 稀 (ki, ke, mabora, mare) meaning "phenomenal, rare."Except for 志季, 志起 and 詩稀, which is used for girls, all the other kanji combinations are given to boys.In the Edo period (1603-1868), this was a rare feminine name. Today, it's still rarely given, although it's now given to both girls and boys.
Derived from Hebrew שקמה (šiqmā́) "sycamore fig", a tree of the species Ficus sycomorus.

column3: שיקו(Hebrew)|しこ(Japanese Hiragana)|史子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: Shortened form of Moshiko which itself is a diminutive of Moshe.

column3: しこう(Japanese Hiragana)|梓虎, 四光, 士紅, 紫高, 志考, 旨倖, 次好, 枝宏, 史行, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 旨 (shi) meaning "clever, gist, meaning, delicious" or 梓 (shi) meaning "catalpa tree" combined with 好 (ko) meaning "fondness, like" or 鴻 (ko) meaning "wild goose".

column3: 诗昆, 昰昆, 十昆, 诗坤, 昰坤, 十坤, etc.(Chinese)|詩昆, 詩坤, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 詩 (shī) meaning "poem, verse, ode" or 昰 (shì) meaning "summer, name" or 十 (shí) meaning "ten" combined with 昆 (kūn) meaning "older brother" or 坤 (kūn) meaning "earth, female". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

From the word 士 meaning scholar, or 死 meaning death, or 資 meaning resources, and 今日 meaning today, or 距 meaning distance and 優 meaning excellent or from the word 司教 meaning bishop, or the word 死去 meaning death.
Acronym of a verse in Psalms that suggests a strong faith in God "שִׁוִּיתִי יְהוָה לְנֶגְדִּי תָמִיד" Psalm 16: 8.
Means "glass ornament, glass decoration" in Mongolian, from шилэн (shilen) meaning "(made of) glass" and чимэг (chimeg) meaning "ornament, decoration".

column3: 实里, 实理, 实立, 实黎, 实力, 实丽, 时里, 时理, 时立, 时黎, 时力, 时丽, 史里, 史理, 史立, 史黎, 史力, 史丽, 石里, 石理, 石立, 石黎, 石力, 石丽, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 实 (shí) meaning "real, honest", 时 (shí) meaning "time, era, season", 史 (shǐ) meaning "history" or 石 (shí) meaning "stone" combined with 里 (lǐ) meaning "inside, village", 理 (lǐ) meaning "reason, logic", 立 (lì) meaning "stand, establish", 黎 (lí) meaning "black, dawn", 力 (lì) meaning "power, capability, influence" (which is usually only masculine) or 丽 (lì) meaning "beautiful" (usually only feminine). Other characters can form this name as well.

column3: 时理安, 实黎安, etc.(Chinese)
column12: Combination of the names Shi, Li 1 and An 1
From the Chinese 诗 (shī) meaning "poetry, poem" and 泠 (líng) meaning "nice and cool".

column3: 石榴, 石流, 世刘, 视六, 仕六, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 石 (shí) meaning "stone", 世 (shì) meaning "world, generation, era", 视 (shì) meaning "watch, look at, observe" or 仕 (shì) meaning "official, scholar" combined with 榴 (liú) meaning "pomegranate", 流 (liú) meaning "flow, stream, current", 刘 (liú) meaning "kill, destroy" or 六 (liù) meaning "six". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
Shillem was a son of Naphtali according to Genesis 46:24 and Numbers 26:49. He was one of the 70 souls to migrate to Egypt with Jacob.
Joseph Smith said that this was a more correct name for Salem, the city that Melchizedek was king of. It means "righteousness" and "peace" in Hebrew.

column3: 诗龙, 师龙, 世龙, 仕龙, etc.(Chinese)|詩龍, 師龍, 世龍, 仕龍, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 诗 (shī) meaning "poetry, poem, verse", 师 (shí) meaning "teacher; to follow, to learn", 世 (shì) meaning "world, generation, era" or 仕 (shì) meaning "to hold an official post, to be an official" combined with 龙 (lóng) meaning "dragon". A notable bearer is Hong Kong martial artist, actor and filmmaker Fang Shilong (1954-), known professionally as Jackie Chan.
From Sanskrit शिल्प (śilpa) meaning "craft, art, skill".
Indian, Hindu, Meaning Best in Sculpture.

Derives from the Hebrew word שלש (shalosh), שָׁלַשׁ‎ (shalash), or שלש (shlsh) which means "three, triad, to do a third time". In the Bible, Shilshah is mentioned once, in 1 Chronicles 7:37, as one of the sons of Zophah, who was the son of Helem of Asher. He is thus a member of the tribe of Asher.
Meaning uncertain. This was the name of a chieftain of the Wanyan clan who was the father of Wugunai. He was later given the temple name Zhaozu.

column3: شیما(Persian)|Шима(Chechen)|しま(Japanese Hiragana)|シ マ(Japanese Katakana)|縞, 詩麻, 志馬, 詩摩, 志万, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|शिमा:(Newar Devanagari)

column12: Variant transcription of Devanagari शिमा: (see Shimah).

column3: しまこ(Japanese Hiragana)|縞子, 志麻子, 志摩子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 縞 (shima) meaning "stripe" or from 志 (shi) "purpose, will, determination, aspiration, ambition" and 麻 (ma) meaning "flax", that is then combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Chinese 诗 (shī) meaning "poetry, poem, verse" combined with 曼 (màn) meaning "graceful, soft and beautiful". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Means "flor de mayo, plumeria, frangipani" in Ashaninka.
Etymology uncertain, however the first part may be from the Ashaninka shimashiri meaning "flor de mayo, plumeria, fragipani".
From Japanese 島 (shima) meaning "island" combined with 人 (to) meaning "person". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 締, 七五三, 注連, 住連, 標, 志女, 四女, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|しめ(Japanese Hiragana)|シメ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From 締め/〆 (shime) meaning "bind, fastening, tightening​," extended to refer to a rope used to cordon off consecrated areas or as a talisman against evil​ (written as 注連, 標 or 七五三).It can also be written with a shi kanji, like 志 meaning "will, aim, goal" or 四 meaning "four," combined with 女 (me) meaning "woman."The name did see some usage before the late 20th century (used only on females before the Meiji Period (1868-1912), though nowadays, it's very rarely used.
Shimeah was a third son of Jesse, a brother of David (1 Samuel 16:9}, and the father of Jonadab (2 Samuel 13:3).

column3: 七五三八, 〆八, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|しめはち(Japanese Hiragana)|シメハチ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Combination of Shime and 八 (hachi) meaning "eight."It is very rarely used.

column3: 七五三一, 七五三市, 〆一, 注連一, 司馬一, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|しめいち(Japanese Hiragana)|シメイチ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Combination of Shime and 一 (ichi) meaning "one" or 市 (ichi) meaning "market, fair."This name is rarely used.

column3: 七五三二, 七五三治, 七五三次, 七五三司, 〆二, 標二, 注連二, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|しめじ(Japanese Hiragana)|シメジ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Combination of Shime and 二 (ji) meaning "two," 治 (ji) meaning "cure; management," 次 (ji) meaning "next" or 司 (ji) meaning "office."This name is rarely used.

column3: 七五三吉, 〆吉, 注連吉, 住連吉, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|しめきち(Japanese Hiragana)|シメキチ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Combination of Shime and 吉 (kichi) meaning "good fortune, good luck."

column3: 志女子, 〆子, 七五三子, 四女子, 締子, 司女子, 標子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|しめ子(Kanji/Hiragana)|シメ子(Kanji/Katakana)|しめこ(Japanese Hiragana)|シメコ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Combination of Shime and 子 (ko) meaning "child."

column3: 诗萌, 世蒙, etc.(Chinese)|詩萌, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 世 (shì) meaning "world, generation, era" or 诗 (shī) meaning "poetry, poem, verse" combined with 萌 (méng) meaning "bud, sprout" or 蒙 (méng) meaning variously "cover, suffer, ignorance". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 七五三之助, 〆之助, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|しめのすけ(Japanese Hiragana)|シメノスケ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Combination of Shime and 助 (suke) meaning "help" with the added genitive particle の (no), written as 之.This name is very rarely used.

column3: 七五三男, 七五三雄, 七五三夫, 〆男, 締男, 注連男, 住連男, 標雄, 〆緒, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|しめお(Japanese Hiragana)|シメオ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Combination of Shime and 男/雄/夫 (o) meaning "male" or 緒 (o) meaning "cord, strap" (the last one being used on females as well).

column3: 七五三太郎, 〆太郎, 標太郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|しめたろう(Japanese Hiragana)|シメタロウ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Combination of Shime and Tarō.This name is very rarely used.

column3: 七五三蔵, 七五三造, 七五三三, 〆蔵, 注連蔵, 志米蔵, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|しめぞう(Japanese Hiragana)|シメゾウ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Combination of Shime and 蔵 (zō) meaning "possession," 造 (zō) meaning "structure" or 三 (zō) meaning "three."
Shimi was a son of Gershon of the house of Levi according to Exodus 6:17. He was born in Egypt.
From the Chinese 诗 (shī) meaning "poetry, poem" and 妙 (miào) meaning "mysterious, subtle, exquisite".

column3: 时敏, 诗敏, etc.(Chinese)|時敏, 詩敏, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 时 (shí) meaning "time, era, season" or 诗 (shī) meaning "poem, verse, poetry" combined with 敏 (mǐn) meaning "quick, clever, sharp". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 世明, 市明, 世铭, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 世 (shì) meaning "world, generation, era" or 市 (shì) meaning "city, town, market" combined with 明 (míng) meaning "bright, light, clear" or 铭 (míng) meaning "inscribe, engrave". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 清水, 紫水, 施水, 寒水, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 清 (shi) meaning "clear, pure, clean", 紫 (shi) meaning "purple; violet", 施 (shi) meaning "grant, bestow" or 寒 (shi) meaning "cold" combined with 水 (mizu) meaning "water". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Derived from the English-speaking word ‘shimmer’, which is used to describe a bright or sparkling light or colour.

column3: 霜, 次茂(Japanese Kanji)|志も(Kanji/Hiragana)|しも(Japanese Hiragana)|シモ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name can be used as 霜 (sou, shimo) meaning "frost."It can also be used to combine 次 (shi, ji, tsugi, tsu.gu) meaning "next, order, sequence" with 茂 (mo, shige.ru) meaning "be luxuriant, grow thick, overgrown" or 志 (shi, kokorozashi, kokoroza.su, shiringu) meaning "aspire, hopes, intention, motive, plan, resolve, shilling" with the phonetic character も (mo).Shimo was used in the Edo Period (1603-1868) and though it was, at first, slightly uncommon, it became slightly common to common in the latter part of that period. It did slightly wane in popularity in the first half of the Meiji Period (1868-1912) but it was still (moderately) popular at that time before it dropped in popularity in the 1900s.
I was on Youtube shorts, and it showed me how my Japanese name is. So technically it's Roan but in Japanese.

column3: 志門, 士門, 志文, 士文, 詩文, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|しもん(Japanese Hiragana)|シモン(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 志 (shi) meaning "will, purpose, ambition", 士 (shi) meaning "gentleman, scholar, samurai, warrior" or 詩 (shi) meaning "poetry, poem, verse" combined with 門 (mon) meaning "gate, door" or 文 (mon) meaning "literature, culture, writing". Other kanji combinations can form this name as well.
Feminine form of Shimon, possibly making it the Hebrew form of Simeona, Simona, or Simone 1.

This name is comprised of two parts: שמר (shamar) meaning "to guard" and י (yod) which can make the word an adjective, make it possessive, or can be an abbreviation of Yahweh.There are 4 men named Shimri in the Bible. The first, in 1 Chronicles 4:37, is a descendent of Simeon. The second, in 1 Chronicles 11:45, is the father of Jediael, one of David's warriors. The third, in 1 Chronicles 26:10, is the first son of Hosah the Merarite. The fourth, in 2 Chronicles 29:13, is one of the Levites who worked to clean the temple.
From Hebrew שמר (shamar) meaning "to keep or guard". In the Bible, she is a Moabitess that can be found on 2 Chronicles 24:26.
Shimshai was a scribe who was represented the peoples listed in Ezra 4:9-10 in a letter to King Artaxerxes.

Means "fate".She was an Akkadian goddess of fate, tied to the West Semitic goddess Ashima. While a goddess in her own right, she was also part of a title for other goddess such as Ishtar, and Damkina, who was titled 'banat shimti' meaning 'creator of fate'.

column3: 思無邪, 思無哉, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|しむや(Japanese Hiragana)|シムヤ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Shift from 思無邪 (shimuja), a Sino-Japanese compound which refers to thinking no evil thoughts.The last kanji can be substituted with one that can be read as ya, e.g. 哉.This name is extremely rare.
Combinations of Kanji Character "椎" meaning "Castanopsis", and "菜" meaning "Vegetable Leaf". Other combinations possible.

column3: 心阿, 心開, 新亜, 新愛, 真愛, 進亜, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 心 (shin) meaning "heart, mind, soul", 新 (shin) meaning "fresh, new", 真 (shin) meaning "real, genuine" or 進 (shin) meaning "advance, make progress" combined with 阿 (a) meaning "mountain", 開 (a) meaning "open, unfold, unseal", 亜 (a) meaning "second, Asia" or 愛 (a) meaning "love, affection". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: しなこ(Japanese Hiragana)|標子, 志奈子, 詩菜子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 標 (shina) meaning "to guide, guidance" and 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 詩南, 蒔奈美, 之南, 品実, 品美, 梓菜美, 姿文, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 詩 (shi) meaning "poetry, poem" combined with 南 (nami) meaning "south". Other kanji combinations are possible.

In the Bible, a country on the lower courses of the Tigris and Euphrates rivers.Shinar (Hebrew שִׁנְעָר Šin`ar, Septuagint Σεννααρ Sennaar) is a broad designation applied to Mesopotamia, occurring eight times in the Hebrew Bible. Possible derivations from Semitic that have been suggested include Shene nahar "two rivers" and Shene or "two cities", but neither is certain.In the Book of Genesis 10:10, the beginning of Nimrod's kingdom is said to have been "Babel, and Uruk, and Akkad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar."
From Japanese 心 (shinba) meaning "heart" or from Japanese 真 (shin) meaning "real, genuine" combined with 羽 (ba) meaning "feathers". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: シンチロ(Japanese Katakana)|しんちろ(Japanese Hiragana)|新散侶, 慎地侶, 真致郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 真 (shin) meaning "genuine, real, truth", 致 (chi) meaning "to do", and 侶 (ro) meaning "follower, companion". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 心出莉楽, 心天稀, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 心 (shin) meaning "heart, mind, soul", 出 (de) meaning "coming out", 莉 (re) meaning "white jasmine" combined with 楽 (ra) meaning "comfort, music". Other kanji combinations are possible.Usage of this name is, most likely, influenced by the name Cinderella.

From Mongolian шинэ (shine) meaning "new" and баяр (bayar) meaning "celebration, joy".
From Mongolian шинэ (shine) meaning "new" and дэлгэр (delger) meaning "vast, wide" or "prosperous, abundant".

From Mongolian шинэ (shine) meaning "new" and хүүхэн (khüükhen) meaning "girl".

column3: 四猫, 梓猫(Japanese Kanji)|しねこ(Japanese Hiragana)|シネコ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 四 (shi) meaning "four" or 梓 (shi, azusa) meaning "catalpa, Japanese cherry birch" combined with 猫 (neko) meaning "cat". Other kanji or combinations of kanji can form this name as well.

From Japanese 真 (shin) meaning "real, genuine" combined with 我 (ga) meaning "I, me". Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.

column3: シンゲン(Japanese Katakana)|しんげん(Japanese Hiragana)|森玄, 信源, 心厳, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 森 (shin) meaning "forest, woods" and 厳 (gen) meaning "stern, strict". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 真一郎, 信一郎, 慎一郎, 伸一郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|しんいちろう(Japanese Hiragana)|シンイチロウ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 真 (shin) meaning "real, genuine, true", 信 (shin) meaning "trust, believe", 慎 (shin) meaning "prudent, careful" or 伸 (shin) meaning "extend, stretch, open" combined with 一 (ichi) meaning "one" and 郎 (rō) meaning "son". This name can be formed from other combinations of kanji as well.

column3: 真一郎, 信一郎, 慎一郎, 伸一郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|しんいちろう(Japanese Hiragana)|シンイチロウ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Alternate transcription of Japanese Kanji 真一郎 or 信一郎 or 慎一郎 or 伸一郎 (see Shin'ichirō).
Means "first day of the lunar month" in Mongolian, ultimately derived from шинэ (shine) meaning "new" and нэг (neg) meaning "one".

column3: 真二郎, 新次郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|しんじろう(Japanese Hiragana)|シンジロウ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Alternate transcription of Japanese Kanji 真二郎 or 新次郎 (see Shinjirō).

column3: 真二郎, 新次郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|しんじろう(Japanese Hiragana)|シンジロウ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 真 (shin) meaning "real, genuine, true" or 新 (shin) meaning "fresh, new" combined with 二 (ji) meaning "two" or 次 (ji) meaning "order, sequence, next" and 郎 (rō) meaning "son". This name can be formed from other combinations of kanji as well.

column3: 真二郎, 新次郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|しんじろう(Japanese Hiragana)|シンジロウ(Japanese Katakana)

column3: 伸吉, 信吉, 心吉, 慎吉, 新吉, 晋吉, 森吉, 申吉, 真吉, 秦吉, 紳吉, 親吉, 進吉, 槙吉, 愼吉, 瀋吉, 眞吉, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 伸 (shin) meaning "expand, stretch, extend, lengthen, increase", 信 (shin) meaning "faith, truth, fidelity, trust", 心 (shin) meaning "heart, mind, soul", 慎 (shin) meaning "humility, be careful, discreet, prudent", 新 (shin) meaning "fresh, new", 晋 (shin) meaning "advance", 森 (shin) meaning "forest, woods", 申 (shin) meaning "have the honor to, sign of the monkey", 真 (shin) meaning "true, reality", 秦 (shin) meaning "Manchu dynasty", 紳 (shin) meaning "sire, good belt, gentleman", 親 (shin) meaning "parent, intimacy, relative, familiarity, dealer (cards)", 進 (shin) meaning "advance, proceed, progress, promote", 槙 (shin) meaning "twig, ornamental evergreen", 愼 (shin) meaning "care, chastity", 瀋 (shin) meaning "juice, broth" or 眞 (shin) meaning "truth, reality" combined with 吉 (kichi) meaning "good luck". Other kanji combinations are possible.Famous bearers are Shinkichi Mitsumune, a Japanese composer who writes music primarily for anime (Japanese cartoons) and Shinkichi Kikuchi, a former Japanese football player. He played for Japan national team.

column3: 進子, 心子, 伸子, 晋子, 真子, 秦子, 臣子, 震子, 岑子, 津子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 進 (shin) meaning "advance, make progress", 心 (shin) meaning "heart, mind, soul", 伸 (shin) meaning "lengthen", 晋 (shin) meaning "to proceed", 真 (shin) meaning "real, genuine", 秦 (shin) meaning "Qin dynasty", 臣 (shin) meaning "one who serves a lord; a vassal, subject", 震 (shin) meaning "shake, quake, tremor, excite", 岑 (shin) meaning "steep, precipitous, peak" or 津 (shin) meaning "harbor" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 真紅, 真空, 眞紅, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 真 (shin) meaning "genuine, real, reality, truth" and 紅 (ku) meaning "crimson". Other kanji combinations can be used. As words, 真紅 (shinku) means "scarlet, crimson" and 真空 (shinku) means "space, gap, vacuum".
Third wife of Taejo, founder of Korea's Goryeo Dynasty.
From Japanese 真 (shin) meaning "real, genuine" combined with 奈 (na) meaning "apple tree". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 新之助, 新之介, 新之輔, 慎之助, 慎之介, 慎之輔, 心之助, 心之介, 心之輔, 伸之助, 伸之介, 伸之輔(Japanese Kanji)|しんのすけ(Japanese Hiragana)|シンノスケ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name combines 新 (shin, atara.shii, ara.ta, ara-, nii-) meaning "new", 慎 (shin, tsutsushi.mu, tsutsushi, tsutsushi.mi) meaning "humility, be careful, discreet, prudent", 心 (shin, kokoro, -gokoro) meaning "heart, mind, spirit" or 伸 (shin, no.biru, no.basu, no.beru, no.su) meaning "expand, stretch, extend, lengthen, increase" with 之 (shi, oite, kono, kore, no, yuku) meaning "of, this" & 助 (jo, suke, su.keru, tasu.karu, tasu.keru) meaning "assist, help, rescue", 介 (kai, suke) meaning "concern oneself with, jammed in, mediate, shellfish" or 輔 (fu, ho, tasu.keru, suke) meaning "help."Bearers of this name include voice actor Shinnosuke Tachibana (立花 慎之介) (1978-), professional baseball player Shinnosuke Abe (阿部 慎之助) (1979-) and singer, dancer and actor Shinnosuke Ikehata (池畑 慎之介), known as Peter when he appears in TV variety shows and musical revues (1952-).

column3: 篠, 志乃, 詩乃, 紫乃, 史乃, 信乃, 志野, 詩野, 紫野, 史野, 信野(Japanese Kanji)|志の, し乃, し之(Kanji/Hiragana)|しの(Japanese Hiragana)|シノ(Japanese Katakana)|شینو(Pashto)
column12: This name can be used as one kanji, 篠 (shou, zou, sasa, shino, suzu) meaning "bamboo grass," or it can be a combination of 志 (shi, kokorozashi, kokoroza.su, shiringu) meaning "aspire, hopes, intention, motive, plan, resolve, shilling," 詩 (shi, uta) meaning "poem, poetry," 紫 (shi, murasaki) meaning "purple, violet," 史 (shi) meaning "chronicle, history" or 信 (shin, shi) meaning "faith, fidelity, trust, truth" and 乃 (ai, dai, nai, no, sunawa.chi, nanji, no) meaning "accordingly, from, possessive particle, wherefore" or 野 (sho, ya, no, no-) meaning "civilian life, field, plains, rustic."As a word (篠), it refers to thin-culmed dwarf bamboo or a strand of loose fibers.In the Edo period (1603-1868), it was, at first, uncommon, but from the middle and latter part of that period, it became a slightly common feminine name before becoming uncommon to very uncommon again in the Meiji (1868-1912) and Taishō (1912-1926) periods. Today, it's still being used for girls, albeit with a bit more variety in kanji choices, and despite the name being given to a male character in Naruto, in reality, it's very rarely used on a boy.

column3: シノ子(Kanji/Katakana)|志乃子, 伎能子, 詩野子, 矢乃子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 志 (shi) meaning "purpose, will, determination, aspiration, ambition", 乃 (no), a possessive particle combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From 新 (arata, shin, nii) meaning "fresh, new" and 八 (hachi) meaning "eight". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 甚 八芦⁠, 甚 八麿, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 甚 (jin, somo, shin, nani, itaku) meaning “very, tremendously, great, greatly, exceedingly”, 晨⁠ (jin, ashita, toki, shin, asa) meaning “dawn, morning, early” or 賑⁠ (shin, nigi.wau, nigi.yaka) meaning “flourish, enliven, bustling, busy, crowded, noisy, lively, thriving, merry, cheerful, business, activity, crowd, turnout, prosperity" combined with 八 (hachi, ya) meaning "eight", and then combined with 櫓⁠ (yagura, ru, ro, odate) “turret, watchtower” or 麿⁠ (maro, ma, ro) “I, me” or 芦⁠ (ru, ashi, ro) “reed, bullrush”. Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 心平, 晋平, 新平, 伸平, 真平, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 心 (shin) meaning "spirit, soul, heart" or 真 (shin) meaning "true, sincere" combined with 平 (pei) meaning "peace, low, flat." Other kanji combinations are usable.
From Japanese 心 (shin) meaning "heart, mind, soul" combined with 羅 (ra) meaning "lightweight fabric or clothing; silk gauze; thin silk". Other kanji combinations are possible as well.

column3: 心利, 新理, 深李, 真履, 真理, 芯倫, 眞理, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 心 (shin) meaning "heart, mind, soul" combined with 利 (ri) meaning "profit, benefit". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 榛六, 真朗久, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 榛 (shin, haru) meaning "hazelnut, Asian hazel" and 六 (roku) meaning "six". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 心作, 新作, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 心 (shin) meaning "heart, mind, soul" combined with 作 (sa, saku, tsuku.ri, tsuku.ru, -dzuku.ri) meaning "build, make, prepare, production". Other kanji combinations can be used.

From Japanese 心 (shin) meaning "heart, mind, soul" (mostly feminine), 進 (shin) meaning "advance, make progress, enter" (mostly masculine), duplicated by 々, a ideographic iteration mark, indicating that the previous kanji should be repeated. Other kanji with the same pronunciations can also be used to form this name.

column3: 真太, 新太, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column3: 慎太郎, 新太郎, 信太郎, 晋太郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|しんたろう(Japanese Hiragana)|シンタロウ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Alternate transcription of Japanese Kanji 慎太郎 or 新太郎 or 信太郎 or 晋太郎 (see Shintarō).

column3: 心登, 信燈, 新藤, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column3: 史生, 紫緒, 師王(Japanese Kanji)|しお(Japanese Hiragana)|შიო(Georgian)

column3: 塩見, 汐見(Japanese Kanji)|しおみ(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: Derived from the Japanese kanji 塩 (shio) meaning "salt (a symbol of purification)" or 汐 (shio) meaning "eventide, salt water, opportunity" combined with 見 (mi) meaning "to see, the look or appearance of something".Other kanji combinations are also possible.Shiomi was used as a feminine given name in the Edo Period (1600-1868) but nowadays is more common as a surname or a fictional name.

column3: 汐音, 汐寧, 潮音, 潮寧, 詩央音, 詩緒音, 紫穂音(Japanese Kanji)|しおね(Japanese Hiragana)|シオネ(Japanese Katakana)

column3: 栞子, 汐里子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

From Chinese 淑 (shū) meaning "kind and gentle" or 姝 (shū) meaning "beautiful girl" combined with 杉 (shān) meaning "pine, fir".
From the Chinese 淑 (shū) meaning "kind and gentle" and 劭 (shào) meaning "encourage, excel, excellent" or 绍 (shào) meaning "continue, join".
From the Chinese 淑 (shū) meaning "kind and gentle" and 胜 (shèng) meaning "victory, excel" or 圣 (shèng) meaning "holy, sacred, sage".
From the Chinese 淑 (shū) meaning "kind and gentle" and 双 (shuāng) meaning "pair, couple".
From the Chinese 淑 (shū) meaning "kind and gentle" and 松 (sōng) meaning "fir, pine".

column3: 秋輔, 柊祐, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 秋 (shū) meaning "autumn" or 柊 (shū) meaning "holly osmanthus" combined with 輔 (suke) meaning "help" or 祐 (suke) meaning "divine intervention, protection". Other kanji combinations can also make up this name.
From the Chinese 淑 (shū) meaning "kind and gentle" and 泰 (tài) meaning "great, superior, exalted".
Shuthelah was a son of Ephraim according to Numbers 26:35 and 1 Chronicles 7:20.
From Chinese 书 (shū) meaning "book, letter, document" and 田 (tián) meaning "field".
From the Chinese 淑 (shū) meaning "kind and gentle" and 窕 (tiǎo) meaning "slender, quiet and modest, charming".

From Chinese 淑 (shū) meaning "good, pure, virtuous, charming" or 舒 (shū) meaning "open up, unfold, comfortable, easy" combined with 婷 (tíng) meaning "pretty, graceful". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 習人, 秋人, 柊人, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column12: From Japanese 秀 (shuu) meaning "excellent, outstanding" or 修 (shuu) meaning "discipline, study", as well as other kanji with the same pronunciation.
From Japanese 修 (shuu) meaning "discipline, study" and 一 (ichi) meaning "one". Other kanji combinations are also possible.

column3: 周子, 修子, 柊子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 萩⁠ (hagi, shu, ha) “Japanese clover, bush clover”, 洲⁠ (su, shu, shima) “state, continent” or 須⁠⁠ (su, shu, subeka-raku, mochi-iru, moto-meru, mochi, motomu, matsu) ”mandatory, necessary, moment, short while” combined with 子 (ko, ne, shi) meaning "child, sign of the rat". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 周真, 修真, 秀真, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 周 (shuu) meaning "circumference", 修 (shuu) meaning "discipline, study" or 秀 (shuu) meaning "beautiful; elegant; graceful" combined with 真 (ma) meaning "real, genuine". Other combinations of kanji can form this name as well.
Derived from Mongolian шуурга (shuurga) meaning "storm" and баатар (baatar) meaning "hero".

column3: 秀太, 洲太, 修太, 周太, 収太, 萩多, 柊汰, 脩太, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 秀 (shuu) meaning "excellent, outstanding" combined with 太 (ta) meaning "thick, big". Other kanji combinations are possible.A famous bearer is Shuta Tanaka, a retired Japanese professional Nippon Professional Baseball player and Shuta Tonosaki, a Japanese professional baseball infielder for the Saitama Seibu Lions in Japan's Nippon Professional Baseball.

column3: 修斗, 周大, 周人, 秀人, 秀斗, 柊人, 脩音, 脩斗, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 修 (shuu) meaning "discipline, study" combined with 斗 (to), which refers to a Chinese constellation. Other kanji combinations are also possible.

Via Sanskrit Śubha (शुभ), meaning "good" or "lucky". Ultimately from Sanskrit root śubh (शुभ्), meaning to embellish.Commonly used for both males and females in Bangladesh, especially in those from Hindu castes. It is also used as a Bengal-ised variant of Shubham in the West Bengal region of India.
From the Chinese 姝 (shū) meaning "beautiful girl" and 娃 (wá) meaning "doll, pretty girl".
From the Chinese 淑 (shū) meaning "kind and gentle" and 望 (wàng) meaning "look at, look forward to, hope, expect".

column3: 淑伟, 淑薇, 书伟, 姝威, etc.(Chinese)|淑偉, 淑薇, 書偉, 姝威, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: Wade-Giles romanization of Shuwei used in Taiwan.

column3: 淑伟, 淑薇, 书伟, 姝威, etc.(Chinese)|淑偉, 淑薇, 書偉, 姝威, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 淑 (shū) meaning "good, pure, virtuous, charming", 书 (shū) meaning "book" or 姝 (shū) meaning "beautiful woman, pretty" combined with 伟 (wěi) meaning "great, robust, extraordinary", 薇 (wēi) meaning "royal fern" or 威 (wēi) meaning "power, pomp". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 叔文, 书文, etc.(Chinese)|淑文, 書文, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 叔 (shū) meaning "clear, pure, good, virtuous" or 书 (shū) meaning "book" combined with 文 (wén) meaning "literature, culture, writing". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 淑霞, 淑侠, 舒霞, etc.(Chinese)|淑霞, 淑俠, 舒霞, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 淑 (shū) meaning "good, pure, virtuous, charming" or 舒 (shū) meaning "open up, unfold, comfortable, easy" combined with 霞 (xiá) meaning "rosy clouds, mist" or 侠 (xiá) meaning "chivalrous, gallant". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 淑贤, 淑娴, 舒贤, 树贤, 殊贤, 书贤, etc.(Chinese)|淑賢, 淑嫻, 舒賢, 樹賢, 殊賢, 書賢, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 淑 (shū) meaning "good, pure, virtuous, charming", 舒 (shū) meaning "open up, unfold, comfortable, easy", 树 (shù) meaning "tree, plant", 殊 (shū) meaning "outstanding, exceptional, excellent" or 书 (shū) meaning "book" combined with 贤 (xián) meaning "virtuous, worthy, wise" or 娴 (xián) meaning "elegant, gentle, skilled, adept". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
From the Chinese 淑 (shū) meaning "kind and gentle" and 祥 (xiáng) meaning "good luck, good omen, happiness" or 翔 (xiáng) meaning "circle in the air, soar, glide".
From the Chinese 淑 (shū) meaning "kind and gentle" and 新 (xīn) meaning "new, fresh" or 歆 (xīn) meaning "like, admire".
From the Chinese 淑 (shū) meaning "kind and gentle" and 星 (xīng) meaning "star, planet". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From the Chinese 淑 (shū) meaning "kind and gentle" and 雪 (xuě) meaning "snow".
From the Chinese 淑 (shū) meaning "kind and gentle" and 洵 (xún) meaning "true, real, truly".

column3: 秋也, 柊弥(Japanese Kanji)|しゅうや, しゅいや(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: From the Japanese kanji 秋 (shū) meaning "autumn" combined with 也 (ya) meaning "to be; also". Another combination could be 柊 (shū) meaning "holly osmanthus" and 弥 (ya) meaning "more".Other kanji combinations are possible.Shuya (秋也) Nanahara is the main character in the 1999 novel 'Battle Royale' written by author Koushun Takami.

column3: 淑嫣, 淑雁, 舒琰, 书燕(Chinese)
column12: From the Chinese 淑 (shū) meaning "kind and gentle", 舒 (shū) meaning "open up, unfold" or "comfortable, easy" or 书 (shū) meaning "book, letter" and 嫣 (yān) meaning "charming, fascinating", 雁 (yàn) meaning "wild goose", 琰 (yǎn) meaning "jewel, gem, glitter of gems" or 燕 (yàn) meaning "swallow (bird)".
From the Chinese 姝 (shū) meaning "beautiful girl" and 谣 (yáo) meaning "folksong, ballad".
From the Chinese 姝 (shū) meaning "beautiful girl" and 晔 (yè) meaning "bright, radiant, thriving". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 淑仪, etc.(Chinese)|淑儀, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 淑 (shū) meaning "good, pure, virtuous, charming" combined with 仪 (yí) meaning "ceremony, rites". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From the Chinese 淑 (shū) meaning "kind and gentle" or 姝 (shū) meaning "beautiful girl" and 银 (yín) meaning "silver, money, wealth" or 吟 (yín) meaning "sing, hum, a type of poetry".
From the Chinese 淑 (shū) meaning "kind and gentle" and 盈 (yíng) meaning "be full of, overflowing".
From the Chinese 淑 (shū) meaning "kind and gentle" and 勇 (yǒng) meaning "brave, courageous, valiant, fierce" or 雍 (yōng) meaning "harmony, union, harmonious".
From the Chinese 淑 (shū) meaning "kind and gentle" and 侑 (yòu) meaning "help, assist" or 友 (yǒu) meaning "friend, companion, friendly".
From the Chinese 舒 (shū) meaning "open up, unfold, comfortable, easy" combined with 予 (yǔ) meaning "to give, to praise". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 书苑, 淑苑, 淑园, 淑缘(Chinese)
column12: From the Chinese 书 (shū) meaning "book, letter, writings" or 淑 (shū) meaning "kind and gentle" and 苑 (yuàn) meaning "pasture, park, garden", 园 (yuán) meaning "garden, park, orchard" or 缘 (yuán) meaning "hem, margin; reason, cause; fate".
From the Chinese 淑 (shū) meaning "kind and gentle" and 增 (zēng) meaning "increase, add to".

column3: 淑贞, 淑珍, 淑真, etc.(Chinese)|淑貞, 淑珍, 淑真, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 淑 (shū) meaning "good, pure, virtuous, charming" combined with 贞 (zhēn) meaning "virtuous, chaste, loyal", 珍 (zhēn) meaning "precious, rare" or 真 (zhēn) meaning "real, genuine, true". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 树铮, 淑铮, etc.(Chinese)|樹錚, 淑錚, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 树 (shù) meaning "tree, plant" or 淑 (shū) meaning "good, pure, virtuous, charming" combined with 铮 (zhēng) referring to the clang of a metal object as well as an ancient percussion instrument (similar to a small gong). Other character combinations can form this name as well.
From the Chinese 淑 (shū) meaning "kind and gentle" and 智 (zhì) meaning "wisdom, intelligence, knowledge".

Means "the just hand of heaven", deriving from the Sumerian elements šu ("hand, portion, share"), an ("heaven, sky"), and the genetive suffix na. Name borne by a Mesopotamian goddess that was mainly worshipped in Nippur. She was thought of as a secondary spouse of the god Enlil, and also played a role in the myth of Enki and Ninmah, where she is one of the seven minor goddesses that helps to create mankind.

column3: 修蔵, 修三, 修造, 秋三, 秋蔵, 秋造, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|ぐぞ(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: This name is made of (Shu) 修 "Discipline, Mastering, Study", (Shu) 秀 "Excellent, Fine", (Zo) 三 "Three" often for a "Third Son", (Zo) 蔵 "Storehouse, Own, Possess", or (Zo) 造 meaning "Build, Create".
From the Chinese 淑 (shū) meaning "kind and gentle" and 佐 (zuǒ) meaning "assist, aid".
Means "white vehicle" or "white horse" from Sanskrit श्वेत (śveta) meaning "white" and वाहन (vāhana) meaning "vehicle, carriage, horse". This is an epithet of the hero Arjuna.
MEANING - white, brightnessOrigin - Sanskrit Usage : Sanskrit, Indian, Tamil, Telugu, Nepali, Sinhala, Hindi, Sikh, Buddhist

Name: Shvitraghni श्वित्रघ्नीMEANING - removing white leprosy, Plant(Tragia Involucrata). Here श्वित्र means leprosy +घ्नी means removingOrigin - Sanskrit, Indian Usage : Sanskrit, Indian, Tamil, Telugu, Nepali, Sinhala, Hindi, Sikh, Buddhist, Mauritian, Fijian
A Suquamish male name.A noted bearer is Chief (si'ab 'high status man') Shweabe of the Suquamish tribe, and father of Chief Seattle.
South Indian form of Shweta. It is often associated with the Hindu goddess Saraswati.
Variant of Chey. It can also be simply derived from the English word shy.
Alternate transcription of Bengali শ্যামল (see Shyamal).
Alternate transcription of Bengali শ্যামলী (see Shyamali).
Variant of Cheyenne. Also compare Shyann.
Possibly a combination of the phonetic elements shy, a and na or an elaboration of Shyanne.
Apparently a combination of the phonetic element shy (from names such as Shiloh and Shyanne) with the popular name suffix elle. It is also an anagram of Shelley.

Meaning uncertain, possibly an invented name blending the phonetic element shy with an Arabic name such as Raheem. Also compare Jaheim and Hashim. Usage of this name has been influenced by the American rapper Shyheim (1979-), who released his debut album AKA the Rugged Child at age 14 in 1994 - the first and only year that this name has appeared on the United States top 1000 list.

Combination of the popular phonetic elements shy and lee, possibly inspired by names such as Shiloh, Shyla, Shaylee, Kylie and Riley.In some cases it could be used as an alternate transcription of Hebrew שי-לי (see Shaili).
Alternate transcription of Hebrew שי-לי (see Shaili).
Invented name, based on Shyla and using the popular name suffix lyn.
Means "quiet", with -alche, a feminine diminutive suffix.
Combination of the phonetic elements shy and meer.
Combination of the phonetic prefix shy and Miracle. Also compare Amiracle.
Means "plane tree" in Kazakh (genus Platanus), derived from Persian چنار (chenar).
From the given name Shyngys combined with the Turkic title khan meaning "leader, ruler". It is most likely given in reference to the 12th-century Mongol leader Genghis Khan.
Derived from Kazakh шырайлы (shyrayly) meaning "glamourous" or шырай (shyray) meaning "look, appearance, face".
Means "juice, sap" in Kazakh, ultimately from Persian شیرین (shirin).
Likely inspired by Siobhán and Sylvana.
Variant of Shavonne, influenced by Yvonne.
Danish diminutive of Signy, Sigrid and other names beginning with the Old Norse element sigr meaning "victory", as well as Sofia, Cecilia and Lucia, or other names containing a similar sound.

column3: 시아(Korean Hangul)|始雅, 諟我, 是兒, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 始 (si) meaning "begin, start", 諟 (si) meaning "to examine, consider, honest", 是 (si) meaning "to be", or 詩 (si) meaning "poetry, poem, verse" combined with 雅 (a) meaning "elegant, graceful, refined", 我 (a) meaning "our, me, us", or 兒 (a) meaning "child". Other combinations of hanja characters can also form this name.
Short form of Nastasia and Nostasia.
Arabic feminine name of uncertain origin, purportedly meaning "help, support, aid".
Derived from Irish siadhail "sloth". Siadhail (d 813) was Abbot and possibly Bishop of Roscommon in the 9th century.
Italian and Spanish form of Syagrius.
Bulgarian and Russian form of Syagrius.

column3: 시아(Korean Hangul)|始雅, 諟我, 是兒, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Alternate transcription of Korean Hangul 시아 (see Si-a).
From the Chinese 丝 (sī) meaning "silk, fine thread" and 瑷 (ài) meaning "fine quality jade".
Siaka, meaning ''chief'', was the one who made the tribes in primarily West Africa. In old culture every family had to name at least one son Siaka.
From the word siale meaning "gardenia flower" in Tongan. And a diminutive of Salesi, as well as the Tongan form of Charlie. Siale is a cognate of Tahitian and Maori word Tiare.
Combination of Sialuk and suffix -nnguaq meaning "sweet, dear".
From Siam, a historical name for Thailand.
Greenlandic name meaning "bilge keel (on a kayak)".
From Chinese 翔 (xiáng) meaning "soar, glide", 祥 (xiáng) meaning "good luck, good omen", 香 (xiāng) meaning "fragrant".
From Lao ຊຽງ (siang) meaning "city, town", "prince" or "good, kind" and ພັນ (phan) meaning "thousand".
In Lady of Avalon by Marion Zimmer Bradley, Sianna was the daughter of the Faerie Queen.
Tongan and Samoan form of George.
Variant of Sierra or Ciara 2. 96 girls in the USA were named SIARA in 2005.
The Welsh version of Charlotte. Or feminine version of the Welsh name Siarl.
An alternate name for Sedna, and one of Saturn’s moons.
Short form of Josias. Known bearers of this name include the Dutch sculptor Sias Fanoembi (1949-2013) and the South African statesman Sias Hoffman (1807-1879).
Means "sweet foot" or "delicious paw", referring to a "bear's paw" in the Ho-Chunk (Winnebago) language.
From Sino-Korean 詩 (si) meaning "poem, poetry" and 白 (baek) meaning "white".
Means "let matters face you" in Nyakyusa.
Possibly means "bird-man" in Mongolian, from шувуу (šuvuu) (traditional Mongolian ᠰᠢᠪᠠᠭ (sibagu)) meaning "bird". Might refer to the job of a falconer.
Means "we have liberated them" in Ndebele.
From Bashkir сибәр (sibär) meaning "beautiful" and гөл (göl ) meaning "flower".
Means "bough, Cottage of spring" in Hebrew.
Frisian short form of masculine names that have sigu or sigis for a first element, and of which the second element starts with a "b." The names Sibald and Sibert are good examples of that.
Portuguese adaptation of Sibella and variant of Sibila. This name was used by portuguese poet Luís de Camões.
Variant of Sibyl, influenced by the spelling Sybella.
Frisian short form of Sibald or Sibert.
Sibeth Ndiaye was appointed as spokesman of the French government in 2019.
Means "colour of Allah", from Arabic صبغة (ṣibḡa) meaning "dye, colourant" combined with الله (Allah).
Diminutive of Srbislava, the feminine form of Srbislav. Srbislava was the birth name of Sibi Blažić (1970-), the Serbian-born wife of actor Christian Bale.
Bessarabian German and Italian form of Sibyllina.
From the Chinese 思 (sī) meaning "think, consider, ponder" and 冰 (bīng) meaning "ice".
Diminutive of Sibina, used as a given name in its own right.

From Guanche *sibissəy meaning "armhole (in clothing); cleavage, neckline; theft". This was recorded as the name of a 16-year-old Guanche girl from Tenerife who was sold at the slave market in Valencia in 1495.
Medieval vernacular form of Sibylla (see Sibyl).
Frisian form of Siegbod or a Frisian form of Siegbald.

Means "people of the precious stone" or "cave dweller" in Arawak, spoken in Cuba.It is an ethnic name as the Ciboney, or Siboney, were a Taíno people of Cuba, Jamaica and Hispaniola (Haiti and Dominican Republic).As given name is probably after Siboney a 1929 song written by Ernesto Lecuona, inspired by the village Siboney near Santiago de Cuba.
Meaning "(you), be thankful with us" in Zulu.
Derived from Albanian si "as, like" and borë "snow".
Dutch form of Sigibern or Sigebrand.
Sibú is a transforming folk hero from Bribri mythology. His name has an unknown meaning.
Dutch and Frisian form of Sigeburg.
Czech and Slovak form of Sibyl.

Derived from Latin sibyllinus, meaning "of or pertaining to sibyls". This name was borne by Blessed Sibyllina Biscossi (1287-1367), who became blind at the age of twelve and received a vision of Saint Dominic which prompted her to join the order. Sibyllina then lived as an anchorite for 65 years in a church in Pavia, Italy.
Most likely derived from σιβύνη (sibune) or (sibyne), the Greek name for a type of hunting spear. It is possible that the word is ultimately of Illyrian origin.
Latinized form of Sibyntios. This name was borne by a reader and a slave of the orator Theodectes of Phaselis, who died in the 4th century BC. He was the first slave who professed the art of oratory.
Probably derived from Σύβριτα (Sybrita) (also called Σίβυρτος (Sibyrtos), the name of an ancient Crete town of uncertain etymology.
Latinized form of Sibyrtios. This name was borne by an officer in the service of Alexander the Great (4th century BC), who was of Macedonian descent.
A famous bearer is Sicalo Dlamini (1987-) son of Mswati III, King of Eswatini and his first wife Queen laMatsebula.
Contracted form of Sigehard, as well as the Gascon and Lengadocian form. This was the name of a 9th-century prince of Benevento (Italy).
Means "born quickly" in Yavapai. Name borne by a prominent member of the Prescott Yavapai tribe, who was inducted into the Arizona Women's Hall of Fame in 2006.
Hypocoristic form of names containing the Germanic name element sigu "victory".Historically, this name could be latinised to Sixtus.
Possibly a latinised form of Sycharbus. Sychaeus, also called Acerbas and Zacherbas, was the uncle and husband of Queen Dido, and was murdered for his wealth by her younger brother Pygmalion.

From Sino-Korean 詩 meaning "Talented, Moral, Educated, Scholarly" or 時 meaning "Excellent, Great, Good, Best" and 燦 "vivid, illuminating; bright" or from the present determiner form of verb 차다 (chada) meaning "to fill".
From the Chinese 思 (sī) meaning "think, consider, ponder" and 嫦 (cháng), the name of a moon goddess.
Old High German sigu "victory" + Old High German hadu "battle".
Possibly derived from Old High German sigu "victory" and Langobardic gaida "sharp point (of a spear)". This was the name of a medieval duchess of Apulia (now part of Italy) and warrior.
Irish form of Sigfrøðr. Sichfrith mac Ímair (died 888), also known as Sigfred Ivarsson, was a ninth-century King of Dublin.
Possibly a variant of Cecilia or after the island of Sicily (Sicilia). If the latter case, it could be a reference to Saint Silvia of Sicily.
Derived from Sicily, the name of the Italian island.It is also possible that there are cases where this name is an alternate spelling of Cicily.
Name of a Spanish saint and martyr.

Diminutive of names containing the name element sig "victory".Sickan Carlsson (1915-2011) was a Swedish actress and singer. The fictional character Charles-Ingvar Jönsson from the popular Swedish movies about 'Jönssonligan' was called Sickan by his companions.
An elongation of Old High German sigu "victory" + Old High German bald "bold".
An elongation of Old High German sigu "victory" + Old High German beraht, Old Saxon berht "bright" from Proto-Germanic berhtaz.
Derived from a lengthened form of Old High German sigu "victory" combined with Old High German fridu or Old Saxon frithu "peace" (making it a variant of Sigifrid).
An elongation of Old High German sigu "victory" + Old Saxon hard, Old High German hart "strong, hard".
Derived from a lengthened form of Old High German sigu "victory" combined with hilt "battle" (making it a variant of Sigihild).
An elongation of Old High German sigu "victory" + Old High German hold "friendly, comely, graceful".
Derived from a lengthened form of Old High German sigu "victory" combined with Old High German or Old Saxon hram "raven". Also compare Sigiramnus.
An elongation of Old High German sigu "victory" + Proto-Germanic þrūþ "strength" or Proto-Germanic trut "maiden".
Variant spelling of Siko, which itself is a variant form of Sike. Out of these names, Sico is currently the most prevalent. Also compare Sikko.
Name of the first prince of Salerno, the brother of Sicard, prince of Benevento (832–839), who was assassinated by Radelchis.
Possibly a Judeo-Italian cognate of Ceti via the Judeo-Spanish variant Çida.
