From Egyptian zꜢt-jmn meaning "daughter of Amon", derived from zꜣt meaning "daughter" combined with the name of the god Amon. This name was borne by several Egyptian royals, including a daughter of Amenhotep III and one of Rameses II.

Means "white umbrella" from Sanskrit सित (sita) meaning "white" and आतपत्र (ātapatra) meaning "umbrella, parasol". In Mahayana and Vajrayana Buddhist tradition this is the name of a bodhisattva who protects against supernatural danger.
Possibly from the Kurdish sîtavk meaning "umbrella".
Of uncertain origin and meaning. It might be a borrowing of Síða or a truncated form of Ositha.
Means "we are very happy" in Ndebele.
Means "we love our country" in Ndebele.
An elaboration of Sitha, or a corrupted form of Catherine. One bearer of this name was Englishwoman Sitharina Shawe, who married Henry Hill in 1567 in Derbyshire, England.
Ancient Egyptian feminine name meaning “daughter of Hathor of Dendera". Dendera is a small, historic town in Egypt known to the Ancient Egyptians as Iunet.
Derived from Middle Gaelic sidhach "wolf", this name is now extinct but was "common in the 17th century".
Alternate transcription of Thai สิทธิชัย (see Sitthichai).

column3: សិទ្ធិស័ក្តិ(Khmer)

column12: Unknown etymology. This was the name of a king of Thrace in Greek mythology, considered the eponym of the peninsula Sithonia and the tribe Sithones. He was the father of two daughters, Rhoeteia and Pallene.
Variant of Sihtric. This was used by S. Fowler Wright in his historical novel Elfwin (1930).
From an honorific title derived from Burmese စည် (si) meaning "prosperous" and the third-person pronoun သူ (thu).
Sithum is of Sinhala linguistic origin (Sri Lanka) in S. Asia.
Alternate transcription of Thai สิทธิชัย (see Sitthichai).
Means "Honesty" in Turkish. From Arabic ṣıdqî
From the Arabic صِدْقِيّة (ṣıdqîye(t)) meaning "honest, loyal".
Possibly a Norwegian form of Sidonia.

column3: 思彤, 思同, 嗣同, etc.(Chinese)
column12: Derived from Chinese Si and Tong.
From Egyptian sꜣt-rꜥ meaning "daughter of Re", derived from zꜣt "daughter" combined with the name of the god Ra.
From Tagalog sitrina meaning "citrine", a type of quartz crystal.

Diminutive of various Greek names such as Isaia, as -ίτσα (-itsa) is a Greek feminine diminutive suffix. This was borne by Sitsa Karaiskaki (1897-1987), a Greek propagandist for women of the 4th of August (or Metaxas) regime.
Means, “place of refuge" from the Ewe elements “Sitso” means "refuge," "peace," or "comfort." and “Fe” (or “pe” in some dialects) means "place," "home," or "foundation."
From Arabic ست (sitt) "woman, lady" or "grandmother, madam". One notable bearer was Sit al-Berain, mother of Anwar Sadat, 3rd President of Egypt. The name is also used as an honorific.
Obsolete German and East Prussian German short form of Sidonia.

column3: สิทธัตถะ(Thai)|ສິດທັດຖະ(Lao)
column12: Thai and Lao form of Siddhattha (see Siddhartha), referring to the Buddha.
From Thai สิทธิ (sitthi) meaning "right, privilege" and ชัย (chai) meaning "victory".
From Thai สิทธิ (sitthi) meaning "rights, legitimate authority" and เดช (det) meaning "power, might, influence".

column3: สิทธิพร, สิทธิพล(Thai)
column12: From Thai สิทธิ (sitthi) meaning "entitlement, right, privilege" and พร (phon) meaning "blessing" or พล (phon) meaning "force, strength, power".

column3: สิทธิพงศ์, สิทธิพงษ์(Thai)
column12: From Thai สิทธิ (sitthi) meaning "entitlement, right, privilege" and พงศ์ or พงษ์ (phong) meaning "lineage, family".

column3: สิทธิศักดิ์(Thai)
column12: From Thai สิทธิ (sitthi) meaning "entitlement, right, privilege" and ศักดิ์ (sak) meaning "power, honour".
The name is derived from the High German word Sitte "custom, manners, morals".Sittich is also a modern German word meaning "parakeet".
Alternate transcription of Thai สิทธิชัย (see Sitthichai).
Maranao and Maguindanao form of Siti.
Possibly from Arabic ست (sitt) meaning "woman, lady" and Persian شاه (shāh) meaning "king". Sittişah Hatun was a Turkish princess and wife of Ottoman sultan Mehmed II.

column3: สิทธิศักดิ์(Thai)

column12: Latin form of Ziva, as found in the Mater Verborum.
Siuan Sanche is a character of the Wheel of Time fantasy series by Robert Jordan
Scottish Gaelic cognate of Siobhán. This name used to be Anglicized as the etymologically unrelated Judith.
Cantonese romanisation of Zhaohui or Shaohui.
Variant of Sjul. Mostly used between the 17th and early 19th century. It is now obsolete.

column3: 紹堅, 兆健, 兆堅, etc.(Chinese)
column12: Cantonese romanisation of Shaojin or Zhaojian.
Probably after the Siula Grande a 6,344 meters mountain of the Huayhuash mountain range in the Peruvian Andes.

column3: 兆倫, 小倫, 兆麟, etc.(Chinese)
column12: Cantonese romanisation of Zhaolun, Xiaolun or Xiaolin.
From si'u meaning "cultivate" or "corner, end" and malae meaning "field" in Samoan.

column3: 兆銘, 少明, 小明, etc.(Chinese)
column12: Cantonese romanisation of Zhaoming or Shaoming.
Rare Irish form of Susan, possibly a variant of Siobhán. Used as the name of the title character in the traditional song Siún Ní Dhuibhir ("Susan O'Dwyer").
Old Swedish short form of Sighurdh.
Scottish Gaelic form of Susan and Susannah.
Alternate name of Živa in Slovak (compare Šiwa).
Combination of the names Siva and Kumar.
Malayalam and Tamil form of Shiva 1.
The patron goddess of illusion magic, tricksters, and those who keep secrets.
Icelandic and Faroese variant of Sigvar.
Dialectal variant of Sigvard. Sivar Arnér (1909-1997) was a Swedish writer.
The meaning of this word is "Lord Shiva, Lord Ram" or "auspicious fortune".
Combination of Siva, Sankar, and Narayana.
Swedish name with the combination of Siv and bjarga "to help, save, rescue".
From the Turkish şive meaning "accent, speech" and can meaning "spirit, soul".
Finnish form of Siv and diminutive of Siviä and Sivia.
Modern coinage taken from the word siviä, a dialectal form of siveä, meaning "chaste".
Rare variant of Sevilya caused by Russian language similarities in better sounds е (ye) and и (i).
Greenlandic name meaning "dear/sweet little flower", with the combination of Sivkerneĸ and -nnguaq meaning "sweet, dear".
Greenlandic name meaning 'bud', 'sprout', 'blossom', 'the blossoming one' or 'the one in bloom' or Greenlandic name meaning 'burst out laughing'. Depends per regional use.
Greenlandic name meaning "the one who comes in your stead, i.e. the substitute"
This is basically the name you get when you spell Tony Stark's "Jarvis" backwards. Also the suffix "raj" means king in hindi
From Sino-Korean 始 (si) meaning "begin, start" and 完 (wan) meaning "complete, whole". Other hanja character combinations are also possible.

column3: 思维, etc.(Chinese)|思維, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 思维 (sīwéi), an academic term meaning "thought, thinking" in philosophy. Other homophonic character combinations can be used to infuse the name with extra meaning.
From the Chinese 鸶 (sī) meaning "eastern egret" and 雯 (wén) meaning "cloud patterns".

From Sino-Korean 時 (si) meaning "time," 始 (si) meaning "beginning, start" or 是 (si) meaning "right, proper" and 源 (won) meaning "root, source, origin; spring," 元 (won) meaning "foundation, basis" or 媛 (won) meaning "beautiful, elegant woman," among other hanja combinations.
Variant of Sixt which likely came about due to sloppy pronunciation.
From Arabic شيخ (shaykh) meaning "sheikh, chief" and Əli.
From the Chinese 思 (sī) meaning "think, consider, ponder" and 霞 (xiá) meaning "rosy clouds".
From the Chinese 思 (sī) meaning "think, consider, ponder" and 潇 (xiāo) meaning "sound of beating wind and rain".
Medieval German, Medieval Italian and Old Swedish vernacular form of Sixtus as well as the Languedocian form of this name.
Diminutive of Sixtus. A known bearer of this name was the Dutch Reformed theologian and orientalist Sixtinus Amama (1593-1629).
As an English feminine name, it is likely a modern respelling of Sia.In South Africa, however, this name seems to be exclusively masculine.
From Siyaj Kʼakʼ, a prominent warlord mentioned in the glyphs of Mayan civilisation monuments.
Means "fasting, abstaining" in Arabic, from the root صام (ṣāma) meaning "to fast".
Alternate transcription of Persian سیامک (see Siamak).
From the Chinese 丝 (sī) meaning "silk, fine thread" and 嫣 (yān) meaning "charming, fascinating".

column3: 巳洋, 司洋, 思洋, 巳阳, 司阳, 思阳, etc.(Chinese)|巳洋, 司洋, 思洋, 巳陽, 司陽, 思陽, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From 巳 (sì) meaning "snake of the Chinese zodiac" or 司 (sī) meaning "manage, control, officer" or 思 (sī) meaning "to think", combined with 洋 (yáng) meaning "ocean" or 陽 (yáng) meaning "light, sun, male". Other character combinations can form this name aswell.
From Chinese 思 (sī) meaning "think, consider" and 窈 (yǎo) meaning "obscure, secluded, refined".
From the Arabic سياسة (siyâse(t) meaning “(country) governance” and originally meaning "horse training".
Alternate transcription of Persian سیاوش (see Siavash).
Azerbaijani and Ottoman Turkish form of Siavash.

column3: 시연(Korean Hangul)|始姸, 時姸, 詩姸, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 始 (si) meaning "begin, start", 時 (si) meaning "time, era, season" or 詩 (si) meaning "poetry, poem, verse" combined with 姸 (yeon) meaning "beautiful". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 시영(Korean Hangul)|始英, 始榮, 始永, 始瑛, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 始 (si) meaning "begin, start" combined with 英 (yeong) meaning "flower, petal, brave, hero" or 榮 (yeong) meaning "glory, honour, flourish, prosper" or 永 (yeong), meaning "perpetual, eternal" or 瑛 (yeong) meaning "jade". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
From the Chinese 思 (sī) meaning "think, consider, ponder" and 怡 (yí) meaning "happy, joyful, harmony".

column3: 似莺, 思英, 嗣瀛, etc.(Chinese)|似鶯, 思英, 嗣瀛, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 似 (sì) meaning "like, similar to, resembling", 思 (sī) meaning "think, consider, yearn for, hope, wish" or 嗣 (sì) meaning "inherit, continue, succeed" combined with 莺 (yīng) meaning "oriole", 英 (yīng) meaning "flower, petal, brave, hero" or 瀛 (yíng) meaning "ocean, sea". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
From сыйлы (sıylı) meaning "honourable, respected" and къыз (qız) meaning "girl".

column3: 시윤(Korean Hangul)|始潤, 始允, 始昀, 始尹, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Alternate transcription of Korean Hangeul 시윤 (see Si-yun).

column3: 시영(Korean Hangul)|始英, 始榮, 始永, 始瑛, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Alternate transcription of Korean Hangeul 시영 (see Si-yeong).

column3: 思雨, 思宇, 思羽, 思玉, 思瑜, 嗣禹, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 思 (sī) meaning "think, consider" or 嗣 (sì) meaning "inherit, continue, succeed" combined with 雨 (yǔ) meaning "rain", 宇 (yǔ) meaning "house, eaves, universe", 羽 (yǔ) meaning "feather", 玉 (yù) meaning "jade, precious stone, gem", 瑜 (yú) meaning "fine jade, lustre of gems" or 禹 (yǔ) referring to the legendary king Yu the Great. Other character combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 思源, 思远, 嗣源, etc.(Chinese)|思源, 思遠, 嗣源, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 思 (sī) meaning "think, consider" or 嗣 (sì) meaning "inherit, continue, succeed" combined with 源 (yuán) meaning "source, origin" or 远 (yuǎn) meaning "distant, remote, far". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
From the Chinese 思 (sī) meaning "think, consider" and 樾 (yuè) meaning "the shade of trees".
Variant transcription of Shiza.This transcription is used in the Douay-Rheims Catholic Bible.
Means "be helped, be assisted" in Zulu.
Derived from 四 (si) meaning "four" or 思 (sī) meaning "think, consider, ponder" and 貞 (zhen) meaning "loyal, virtuous, chaste" or 真 (zhēn) meaning "clearly, really" or "real, true".
From the Chinese 思 (sī) meaning "think, consider, ponder" and 妆 (zhuāng) meaning "adorn oneself, make up".

From Chinese 思 (sī) meaning "think, hope" combined with 追 (zhuī) meaning "to chase, to pursue". Other hanzi combinations are posisble. A famous fictional bearer is Lan Sizhui from Chinese danmei novel Mo Dao Zu Shi.
Bulgarian, Croatian, Russian, Serbian and Ukrainian form of Sisyphus.
Diminutive of names containing the name element sigu "victory" with the suffix -zo
Short form of Johanna (feminine), or a short form of Christianus or Sebastianus (masculine).
Possibly derived from Old Norse sjafni "love" or the name Sjǫfn combined with Old Norse herr "army, warrior".
Older spelling of Syaiful influenced by Dutch orthography.
Variant of Sjaak, of which the pronunciation was influenced by the French name Jacques.Also compare Jac, Jack and Jacq, which can be pronounced in the same way, but are generally more common.
Strictly feminine form of Sjamme, where the diminutive suffix ke has been added to the name.
West Frisian form of Sihalm or Sihelm, which are short forms of Sigihelm.
Older spelling of Syamsul influenced by Dutch orthography.
Dutchization of either the English name Janet or the French name Jeannette. Also compare the related name Sjaan.
Dutch and Limburgian form of Charlotte.

Short form of Angelica and its variant Angelika. It can also be a short form of Angela, but only when it is spelled as Angéla, as otherwise the pronunciation does not match.A known bearer of this name is the retired Dutch singer Angéla "Sjeel" Kramers (b. 1960). She was a member of the girl band Dolly Dots, which was quite successful throughout the 1980s.

Short form of Michel and also its variant spelling Misjel. Also compare the related name Chiel.A known bearer of this name was the Dutch-Australian soccer player Michel "Sjel" de Bruyckere (1928-2011).
Variant of Sjinke, a Frisian name. Notable bearer is Dutch speed skater Sjinkie Knegt, although Sjinkie Knegt is named after his grandfather Sjing Ting.

Diminutive of Sjoerd (masculine) and Sjoerdje (feminine). Also compare the related name Sieuwke, not least because there are bearers of that name who have gone by Sjoeke in daily life.A known bearer of this name is the German professional soccer player Sjoeke Nüsken (b. 2001).

Name of a minor Norse goddess, one of Frigg's handmaidens, said (by the Icelandic chieftain and poet Snorri Sturluson, d. 1241) to be related to Old Icelandic sjafni "love". Modern-day academics, however, argue that it might rather be related to Old Norse sefi meaning "sense" as well as "relation".
Dutch form of John, completely phonetical in its spelling (which reflects only the pronunciation of John as it is done in English).
This name is a combination of the name Sjouwe (which is a variant form of Sieuwe) with the diminutive suffix -ke.
Limburgian form of the French name Gérard.
Dialectal form of Sigurd, mostly used in Norrland.
From Old Norse sjaundi meaning "the seventh". Number seven was considered to be a holy number.
Faroese modern form of Sigurði, the dative form of Sigurðr.

Dutch short form of the French names Jules 1, Julie and Juliette.In Limburgish, the source name doesn't necessarily have to be French: people will also use this French-based short form for Julius, Julia and Juliana.This name is not to be confused with the similar-looking name Sjul.
Latvian and Estonian borrowing of Syuzanna.
A new short form of Franziska.The German politician Ska Keller (Alliance90/The Greens) goes by this name.
The name of a character in the movie and television series 'Stargate'.
The Haida word for a type of mollusk that is also used as a given name.
Old Norse byname, from Old Norse sker meaning "rock in the sea", "skerry". As a modern Icelandic name, it could instead derive from skær "bright, radiant, clear".
From Old Norse skæringr meaning "man from Skára".
Feminine form of Skagi. This is the name of a Valkyrie.
Old Danish and Old Swedish form of Skagi.
Derived from Latvian skaidrs "clear, bright; pure".
Lithuanian feminine name meaning "clear, serene, pure".

The name was popularized by Lithuanian tv show host Skaiva Jasevičiūtė (b. 1982). Her birth name was Kristina. She took the stage name Skaiva and claims to have been inspired by the English word sky. It also shares a similar sonority to such names as Skaidrė and Vaiva.
From Kurdish سکاڵا meaning "complaint" or "request", likely in reference to a plea to God in times of difficulty.
Combination of Skalli and the Germanic name element grímr "person wearing a face mask".
Old Norse name and byname, from Old Norse skalli meaning "bald head".
Means "battle". This is the name of a Valkyrie.
Archaic North Frisian form of Charlotte, recorded on the isle of Föhr in the 1700s and early 1800s.
Russian and Ukrainian form of Skamandros.

Perhaps a combination of the river name Skamandros and the noun ὄνυμα (onyma) "name". According to some writers, the father of the poet Sappho bore this name (according to others, he was named Skamandros).

The meaning of this name is uncertain. The second element looks like it is derived from Greek ανδρος (andros) meaning "of a man", but there are sources who doubt this. The first element is more difficult to pinpoint: it could be derived from Greek σκάζω (skazo) "to limp, to stumble (over an obstacle)" or from Greek σκαιός (skaios) meaning "left(-handed)" or "awkward". The meaning of the name might then perhaps be "limping man" or "awkward man".
Short form of Iskandar. A well-known bearer of this name is the British actor Skandar Keynes.
Combination of Skandar with the Turkish military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".
Alternate transcription of Arabic إسكندر (see Iskandar) chiefly used in North Africa.
MEANING : princess, learned lady, effusing, spurting, jumping. It is feminine of name SkandOrigin : Sanskrit, Hindi Usage : Sanskrit, Indian, Tamil, Telugu, Nepali, Sinhala, Hindi, Sikh, Buddhist
Derived from Old Norse skapt "stick, shaft, missile".
Derived from Slavic skarbi "to be sad about, to grieve over, to worry" combined with Slavic mir "peace".
Derived from Slavic skarbi "to be sad about, to grieve over, to worry" combined with Slavic slav "glory".
Old Norse byname, from Old Norse skári meaning 'young sea-mew'.
Alternate transcription of Malayalam സ്കറിയ (see Scaria).
Alternate transcription of Malayalam സ്കറിയ (see Scaria).

Hellenized form of Scarlat. This name is very rare in modern Greece; one is much more likely to encounter it as a surname instead.Notable bearers of this name include the Greek politician and minister Skarlatos Soutsos (1806-1887) and the Greek philologist Skarlatos Byzantios or Vyzantios (1798-1878). Both were born in places that are located in what is nowadays Romania.
Latvian and Slovak form of Scarlett.
This name is used for one of the narrow gauge engines in the Railway Series and Thomas the Tank Engine. It means "lake in the Woods" in the fictional Sudric language.
Old Norse variant and Old Danish and Old Swedish form of Skarpi.
Possibly derived from the Old Norse elements skarpr "barren, skinny, sharp" and heiðr "bright, clear, cloudless" or heiðr "honour, worth". Compare Skarphéðinn.
Old Norse combination of skarpr "barren, skinny, sharp" and heðinn "jacket of fur or skin".
Old Norse byname, From Old Norse skarpr meaning "barren, skinny, sharp".
Originally a byname derived from Old Norse skarð "notch, gap, indentation".
Anglicised variant of Skaði, the name of one of Saturn’s moons.
Means "good tree" or "slanting tree". This is the name of a dwarf.
Perhaps from the Old Norse "Skotja" Meaning- "To shoot" Also believed to mean "Swift" from English.
Nickname derived from a slang or humorous term for "mosquito." A famous bearer is female singer-songwriter Skeeter Davis (1931-2004).
Derived from Old Norse skegg meaning "beard". It occurs in 'Grettis saga' belonging to Grettir's first victim.
Derived from skeggja ("battle-axe") and ǫld ("age"). This is the name of a Valkyrie.
Transferred use of a surname Skelton.
Tahltan name for the Raven, a common spirit found throughout Pacific Northwest Coast indigenous cultures.
Derived from the Georgian noun სხივი (skhivi) meaning "beam, ray (of light)".
Bulgarian, Russian and Ukrainian form of Scholasticus (see Scholastica).

Ukrainian form of Scholastica. It is also the Ukrainian everyday word for "scholastic, academic" or "scholasticism" (esp. within the context of Christian scholasticism) - the given name and the vocabulary word being closely related etymologically.The Eastern Orthodox Church celebrates the virgin-nun Skholastyka's life on February 10, the same day as the Catholic Church and the Anglican Communion also venerates her.
Means "reminder, remembrance" in Zulu and Xhosa.
From the hypothetical Anglo-Scandinavian name *Skjaldfríðr, derived from the Old Norse elements skjǫldr meaning "shield" (genitive skjaldar) and fríðr meaning "beautiful, beloved".
Derived from Albanian skifter "falcon" and, figuratively, "courageous and fierce fighter".
Variant spelling of Skylar.A notable bearer is Skilyr Hicks. She was a singer and songwriter.
It is the name of a principal cat in Andrew Lloyd Webber's Cats. He is the Railway Cat.
Latinised form of Scyld, used by Saxo Grammaticus to refer to Scyld Sceafing in his Gesta Danorum.
Derived from Middle Dutch schipper "boatman, bargeman", which referred to the master of a small ship or boat (like a fishing boat).
Transferred use of the surname Skipton.
Transferred use of the surname Skipwith.A notable bearer of this name is the American poet Skipwith Cannell (1887-1957).
Possibly derived from skirfill ("shard, cut piece"). This is the name of a dwarf.

The first element of this name is derived from the Lithuanian verb skirti, which usually means "to give, to devote, to dedicate" but has also been found to mean "to divide, to separate" as well as "to determine, to establish, to identify". The second element is derived from old Lithuanian gailas, which usually means "strong, potent" but has also been found to mean "sharp, jagged" as well as "angry, fierce, violent" and "miserable, sorrowful, remorseful". Also compare the modern Lithuanian noun galia meaning "power, might, force".This name was borne by a 14th-century regent of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, who was the son of Grand Duke Algirdas and his second wife Uliana of Tver.

The first element of this name is derived from the Lithuanian verb skirti, which usually means "to give, to devote, to dedicate" but has also been found to mean "to divide, to separate" as well as "to determine, to establish, to identify". The second element is either derived from the Lithuanian verb gaudyti meaning "to take" as well as "to catch, to hunt" or from the Lithuanian adjective gaudus meaning "sonorous, resonant, ringing, loud, echoing".

The first element of this name is derived from the Lithuanian verb skirti, which usually means "to give, to devote, to dedicate" but has also been found to mean "to divide, to separate" as well as "to determine, to establish, to identify". The second element is either derived from Lithuanian mantus meaning "intelligent" (see Daumantas) or from Lithuanian manta meaning "property, estate" as well as "wealth, riches, fortune".
Probably derived from Old Norse skírr meaning "clear, bright, pure". In Norse mythology Skírnir is a servant of the god Freyr.

The first element of this name is derived from the Lithuanian verb skirti, which usually means "to give, to devote, to dedicate" but has also been found to mean "to divide, to separate" as well as "to determine, to establish, to identify". The second element is derived from Baltic tauta meaning "people, nation" (see Vytautas).

The first element of this name is derived from the Lithuanian verb skirti, which usually means "to give, to devote, to dedicate" but has also been found to mean "to divide, to separate" as well as "to determine, to establish, to identify". The second element is derived from the old Lithuanian noun vaina meaning "cause, reason" as well as "fault".

The first element of this name is derived from the Lithuanian verb skirti, which usually means "to give, to devote, to dedicate" but has also been found to mean "to divide, to separate" as well as "to determine, to establish, to identify". The second element is derived from Baltic vyd meaning "to see" (see Vytautas). Also compare other names that end in -vydas, such as Alvydas and Tautvydas.
Derived from the Germanic name elements skjǫldr "shield" and bjǫrn "bear".
Derived from the Germanic name elements skjǫldr "shield" and garðr "enclosure", "protection".
Variant of Skjǫlf. In Norse mythology, Skjalf is the daughter of a Finnish king. She marries Agni and strangles him with his necklace.
Old Norse name and nick name, from Old Norse skjálgr "squinting".
Danish and Norwegian younger form of Skjǫldr.
From Old Norse skjǫldr meaning "shield". In Norse mythology this is one of Odin's sons, the husband of Gefjon.
Old Norse combination of skjǫldr "shield" and ulfr "wolf".
Derived from Old Norse skjalfa, meaning "to shake, shiver or quiver". Skjǫlf is another name of Freyja mentioned in the Heimskringla.
Norwegian variant of Skjøller and Skjalde.
Derived from Breton sklaer "clear, bright", this name is used as an equivalent of Claire.
Means "battle". This is the name of a Valkyrie in Norse mythology.
Means "mockery". In Norse mythology Skǫll is the wolf that pursues the sun. He is the son of Fenrir and the brother of Hati.
Derived from the Germanic name elements skor "precipice", "rift in a rock", "score", "notch", "incision" and geirr "spears".

From Swedish skrålla "to be noisy, to make unpleasant noise", a transformation of skråla "noisy singing (usually while drunk)". The name was invented by Swedish author Astrid Lindgren for a character introduced in the film 'Tjorven och Skrållan' (1965), a spin off of the TV-series 'Vi på Saltkråkan' (English: 'Life on Seacrow Island') from 1964.

German form of Skrållan, used in the German translation of the Swedish series 'Vi på Saltkråkan' by Astrid Lindgren (published in English as 'Seacrow Island'). Skrollan has been occasionally used in Germany since the 1970s.
Means "humble glory", derived from Polish skromny "modest, humble" combined with Slavic slav "glory".
The name of a giant from Norse Mythology, also known as Útgarða-Loki. A moon of Saturn was named after him.
A combination of Old Norse elements skuld, meaning "blame, future", and fríðr, meaning "beautiful, beloved, good, peaceful, safe".
Derived from Old Norse skýla "to protect, shelter, cover".
From Old Norse skúmr meaning "louring man, scary man".
Possibly means "excellent one, outstanding one", related to Ossetian sk’unxt "excellent" and sk’uänxun "distinguishes oneself". This is rendered as skₒyxyn (скойхйн) in the Digor dialect of Ossetian.

Name of a repeat character in Herge's comics TinTin. A blond Estonian pilot with an eye-patch, who shoots at TinTin and Haddock on orders but is later rescued by them and refuses to betray them. Friendly and honest, he provides assistance in further adventures.Although his full name is given as Piotr Skut, Skut is used as his name throughout the series. Skut is not an Estonian name but was given to facilitate a misunderstanding. In the English version, Haddock thinks he's being told to 'Scoot' instead of being introduced.Also related to the name of a bully, Scut Farkus, in the comedy 'A Christmas Story' (1983).
Variant of Skyler influenced by Schuyler.

Combination of Sky and the -den suffix used in names such as Jaden and Aidan.According to the U.S. Social Security Administration, 7 boys were born with the name Skyden in 2018 and another 5 were born with this given name in 2020.
Variant of Skylar by adding Skye.
Elaboration of Skye using the popular name suffix lyn.
Variant of Skylynn influenced by the spelling of Skye.

column4: English (Australian, Modern, Rare)|English (New Zealand, Modern, Rare)|English (American, Modern, Rare)

column12: An invented name blending Sky with Kailani, probably influenced by names such as Skylynn, Skyla and Skylee.
A variant of Skylynn using the suffix ann.

From the English word for the type of songbird, i.e., the common European lark (Alauda arvensis; which is "famed for its melodious song"). Use of the name is probably inspired by the similar name Skylar; it could also be viewed as a combination of Sky and Lark.This name has been in occasional use since the late 20th century.

From the Danish word skyldfri meaning "innocent, guiltless", derived from skyld "guilt" (cf. Old Norse Skuld, name of one of the Norns, possibly meaning "debt") and fri "free". This was formerly given to foundlings and girls born out of wedlock.
Combination of Sky and Lee. This name was used by the band Blink-182 for their unreleased song Skylee's With Me.
Combination of Sky and the popular name suffix -leen in the style of Kayleen. In other words a variant of Skylene.
Variant of Skylee, or a combination of Sky and the popular name suffix leigh.
From the English word sky combined with the popular name suffix lene.
Elaboration of Skyla or combination of Sky and Lia.

Variant of Skylyn. In 2011, this variant was given to 31 girls born in the United States (in addition, 101 were given the name Skylynn, 38 Skylyn, 22 Skylan, 11 Skyelynn, 10 Skylinn, 7 Skyelyn, and 5 were named Skylynne).
Variant of Skyra, a contraction of Sky and Kyra. In 2011, the name Skyra was given to 7 girls born in the United States.
Derived from (Serbo-)Croatian sladak "sweet" combined with Slavic mir "peace".
Old Norse combination of sær "sea" and leifr "heir", "descendant".
Maghrebi transcription of Salah al-Din used in Tunisian Arabic.
Rare variant of Sulaiman, used mostly in Lebanon.
Derived from Old Irish slán "healthy, safe" and oll "great, vast, ample". In Irish legend, this was the name of a High King of Ireland.
Transferred use of the surname Slater.
Derived from the Slavic elements 'slava' meaning "glory" and 'mirŭ' meaning "peace, world".
The name is divided into 2 parts in Russian: (slu-veet) that means "praise", and Yana. The whole meaning is "praise Yana". It's a long name for Yana.
A diminutive of Vyacheslav and other names containing the element Слава (slava) meaning "glory"
Either variant of Slaven or from слава (slava) "glory".
Derived from Slavic elements slava "glory" and gost "guest" (see Gostislav).
Derived from the Slavic elements slava "glory" and voji "soldier".A famous bearer of the name is the Slovenian philosopher Slavoj Žižek.
Derived from the Slavic elements slava meaning "glory" and milŭ meaning "gracious, dear".
From Polish sława "glory" and bój "battle" roughly translating to "battle for glory", "glorious in battle", "glorious fighter".
Derived from Slavic slav "glory" combined with Slavic tech "solace, comfort, joy".
Means "dear glory", derived from Slavic slav "glory" combined with Slavic mil "gracious, dear".
The first element of this name is derived from Slavic slav "glory". The second element is derived from Polish myśl "thought", which is ultimately derived from Proto-Slavic mysliti "to think".
Originally a diminutive of names beginning with the Slavic element slava meaning "glory" (compare Miloš).

Said to be the 2nd ruler of Essex and son of Æscwine, the founding ruler but it's disputed whether or not that Sledd was the first to found the kingdom instead of his father, He reigned from 587 to 604.
Derived from Old Norse sleipr "slippery" (in relation to "bog, marsh"). In Norse mythology, Loki's son Sleipnir was Odin's eight-legged horse.
Transferred use of the surname Slevin. The author Anne Tyler used this name in her novel 'Dinner at the Homesick Restaurant' (1982); it was also used in the movie 'Lucky Number Slevin' (2006).
Possibly a Spanish form of Slater.
From the English word slick. This is most common as a nickname.

From Miskito slilma meaning "star." It is heavily concentrated in Nicaragua, mostly in the North Caribbean Coast Autonomous Region, and has been in use since at least the early 1970s (as a first name; when considering middle name usage, it would have been in use since at least the mid-1940s).
Alternate transcription of Arabic سليمان (see Sulayman) chiefly used in North Africa.
One of the Yiddish forms of Solomon.
Yiddish exclusively feminine form of Slava
a Judeo-German variant of Slove (see Slava)
Smadi is a nickname for Smadar.
Derived from either Latvian smaids "a smile" or smaidīt "to smile".
Derived from either Latvian smaids "a smile" or Latvian smaidīt "to smile".
Variant of Isma'il chiefly used in Northern Africa.
Maghrebi Arabic alternate transcription of Smaïl as well as the Bosnian form of Isma'il (see Ishmael).
Albanian and Bosnian form of Ishmael.

Russian form of Smaragdos. In the Netherlands, the name is a very rare feminine name. It is derived from the Dutch noun smaragd meaning "emerald", which as you can see has the same etymology as Smaragdos.
French form of Smaragdos via its latinized form Smaragdus.
Modern Greek diminutive or variant of Smaragda.
Italian form of Smaragdos via its latinized form Smaragdus.

Latinized form of Smaragdos. This name was borne by at least two saints. One was a companion of saint Cyriacus (died c. 303 AD), who was buried together with him near the Via Ostiensis. The other was one of the forty martyrs of Sebaste (which is nowadays Sivas in Turkey), who died in 320 AD.
Ukrainian form of Smaragda. This name was borne by the Ukrainian saint Iulianiya Avramivna Onyshchenko (1858-1945), who was known as Reverend Smarahda.

Derived from Romanian smarand meaning "emerald". Smaranda Brăescu (1897 – 1948) was a Romanian parachuting and aviation pioneer, former multiple world record holder. Her achievements earned her the nickname "Queen of the Heights".
Princess Smartypants is the title of a children's book by Babette Cole. The book won the British Library Association award.
From the Armenian given name Smbat and անուշ (anush) meaning "sweet".
Derived from Old English smēah "sagacious, acute, subtle" combined with wine "friend".
Transferred use of the surname Smedley.
Means "loving"; derived from Nivkh ezmud meaning "love".
The name of a character occurring together with Mundungus in 'A sentimental journey' by Laurence Sterne.The name was later used as a pseudonym by Thomas Carlyle and by Patrick Proctor Alexander.
Derived from Albanian smerald and Italian smeraldo "emerald", making it a cognate of Esmeralda. This name was borne by the mother of Botticelli.
Fata Morgana's black slave in "L'amour des trois oranges" by Prokofiev.

The first element of this name is derived from Polish śmiały "bold, daring", which is ultimately derived from Polish śmieć "to dare" (which in turn is derived from Proto-Slavic sъměti "to dare, to venture"). Also compare Croatian smjeti "to dare". The second element of this name is derived from Slavic mir "peace".
Derived from Polish smierć "death". Alternate name for Marzanna 2.
From the English word smile combined with Sanskrit प्रीति (prīti) meaning "pleasure, joy, love".

A nickname for a person of happy disposition known for smiling or a nickname whose meaning is particular to the bearer. A notable namesake is comedic actor and country singer Smiley Burnette (1911-1967) who was born Lester Alvin Burnett. Burnette played the sidekick to Gene Autry and Roy Rogers among others. He took the name from the character Jim Smiley in Mark Twain's short story 'The Celebrated Jumping Frog of Calaveras County.'
Derived from Ancient Greek σμίλη (smile) meaning "tool for cutting or carving; knife, chisel". This was the name of a legendary Ancient Greek sculptor, a contemporary of Daedalus.
Diminutive of Smilja, occasionally used as a given name in its own right.
Invented combination of the Greenlandic name Millaaraq and the Danish words mild meaning "mild" and smile meaning "to smile".
Old Norse combination of smiðr "smith, craftsman, artisan" and ketill "cauldron hat, helmet".
Old Norse name and byname, from Old Norse smiðr meaning "smith, craftsman, artisan".
Transferred use of the surname Smithson.
A nickname for someone with the surname Smith.

From the English word smokey meaning "full of smoke" or "smoke colored". Mainly used as a nickname for someone with smoke colored features. This is the name of Smokey Bear, the mascot of an American fire prevention campaign.
Variant of Smokey. A famous bearer of this form is Major League Baseball pitcher, Smoky Joe Wood (1889–1985).
MEANING- remembered, recollected, thought of, mentioned
Malayalam and Tamil form of Smriti.
From Sanskrit स्मृति (smṛti) meaning "remembrance, memory, reminiscence".
Czech and Slovak form of Śmiertka (alternate name of Morana).

Means "myrrh" in Ancient Greek. In Greek mythology, Smyrna was an Amazon warrior who founded the ancient city Smyrna (now Izmir, Turkey). This is also an alternative name for Myrrha, mother of Adonis.
Means "of Smyrna, Smyrnaean" in Ancient Greek.
Transferred use of the surname Smyth.
Means "bright snow", derived from the Old Norse elements snær "snow" and bjǫrt "bright, shining" (from bjartr).
From the Old Norse elements snær "snow" and brá "eyelash".
Derived from the Old Norse elements snær meaning "snow" and fríðr meaning "beautiful, fair". According to medieval tradition, this was the name of a wife of the Norwegian king Harald Fairhair.
Derived from Old Norse snær "snow" and holmr "islet in a bay, small island", perhaps a transferred use of a surname.
Derives from Old Norse element snær "snow".
Derived from the Old Norse elements snær "snow" and rós "rose".
Derived from the Old Norse elements snær "snow" and rún "secret lore, rune". This name was coined in the 1920s.
Derived from the Old Norse elements snær "snow" combined with the name of the Norse god Þórr (see Thor).
Ancient Scandinavian masculine name with the combination of snær "snow" and ulfr "wolf".
Combination of Old Norse snær "snow" and either varr "attentive, aware, cautious" or herr "army, warrior".

From Proto-Germanic *snakon, source also of Old Norse snakr "snake," Swedish snok, German Schnake "ring snake"), from PIE root *sneg- "to crawl, creeping thing" (source also of Old Irish snaighim "to creep," Old High German snahhan "to creep").
Means "to jingle, ring", from Lakota snásna.
This was the name of a 4th century Persian saint who helped Christians who were in prison for their faith.
From Old Norse snarr "quick, swift, sharp".
Transferred use of the surname Sneed. This name is borne by Sneed B. Collard III, an American children's author.
Dutch calque of Schneewittchen. It consists of the Dutch words sneeuw meaning "snow" and wit meaning "white" combined with the Dutch diminutive suffix -je.
Original Low German form of Schneewittchen.

From Egyptian snfr-kꜣ, possibly meaning "(his) soul is beautiful", from Egyptian snfr "to make beautiful" combined with kꜣ "soul". This was the throne name of an early Egyptian king who may have ruled at the end of the 1st Dynasty.

Possibly from Egyptian snfr-rꜥ, perhaps meaning "Ra has made me beautiful", from Egyptian snfr "to make beautiful", a derivative of nfr "beautiful, good" combined with the Egyptian God Ra. This was one of the throne name of Piye, the founder of the 25th Dynasty of Egypt
This is the name of the popular Russian fairy tale character Snegurochka "The Snow Maiden". The name comes from Russian снег (sneg) which means "snow".
Diminutive of Snegurka.This is the name of a popular Russian fairy tale character Snegurochka "The Snow Maiden". The name comes from Russian снег (sneg) meaning "snow".
Means "love vine" in Chhattisgarhi, language spoken in India.
Czech form of Snow White, from Czech sněh "snow".
Derived from Old High German snel "fast, strong" combined with Old High German bald "bold, brave."
Derived from Old High German snel "fast, strong" combined with Old High German beraht "bright."

The first element of this name is derived from Old High German snel "fast, strong." The second element is derived from Gothic bairgan (bergan in Old High German) "to keep, to save, to preserve", or from Old High German burg "fortress."
Derived from Old High German snel "fast, strong" combined with Gothic hardus (hart in Old High German) "brave, hardy."
Derived from Old High German snel "fast, strong" combined with man "man."

Derived from Old High German snel "fast, strong" combined with Old High German râd "counsel."
Derived from the Old High German elements snel, meaning "quick, fast" and hruod, meaning "fame, glory".
Short form of Snežana, ulitmately derived from Macedonian снеже (sneže), itself a diminutive of снег (sneg) “snow”.
Diminutive of Snežana, occasionally used as a given name in its own right.
Derived from Serbian and Slovene снежна (snežna), meaning "snowy".

Either directly taken from Latvian sniedze "snow bunting (bird)" or derived from Latvian sniegs "snow". This name was used by Latvian playwright Anna Brigadere in her play Princese Gundega un karalis Brusubārda.
Derived from the Lithuanian noun sniegas meaning "snow". In some cases, this name can also be a short form of Snieguolė.
Derived from the Lithuanian noun sniegas meaning "snow". In some cases, this name can also be a short form of Snieguolė.
Means "snowball" in Polish. It is the Polish name for Snow White as well.
From Sanskrit स्निग्ध (snigdha) meaning "loving, affectionate, tender, charming".

The Hasbani River, also known as Snir Stream (Hebrew: נחל שניר‎‎ / Nahal Snir), is the major tributary of the Jordan River. The Hasbani River derives most of its discharge from two springs in Lebanon. The Hasbani forms the border between Lebanon and the Golan Heights.
Diminutive form of names containing the Old Norse element snjór "snow" (a variant of snær), such as Snjólfur.
Derived from the Old Norse elements snjór meaning "snow" (an alternative form of snær) and laug possibly meaning "vowed, promised, bound in oath".
Combination of Swedish snö "snow" and blomma "flower".
Swedish form of Snæfríðr. Snöfrid (1890) is a poem by the Swedish author Viktor Rydberg.
Variant of Snow.Made popular by the singer Snoh Aalegra (stage name).
In the case of American rapper and actor Snoop Dogg born Calvin Broadus Jr. (b. 1971-) he was given the name by his mom who thought he looked like Snoopy from the Charlie Brown cartoons.
In PEANUTS, Snoopy is the beagle. He is one of the major characters.

A nickname for someone who is arrogant or conceited. Famous bearers of this nickname include Lord Snooty, the fictional character in the British comic The Beano (1938), a manatee named Snooty (1948-2017), and American rapper Snooty Wild (1985-2022), real name LaPreston Porter.
Means "string". Snør is the wife of Karl in the Rígsþula (Lay of Rígr), part of the Poetic Edda.
Means "woman; gentlewoman". In Norse mythology this is the name of one of Karl and Snør's daughters.

An Old English personal name, deriving from Old English snotor "wise, prudent". A notable bearer of this name includes an Anglo-Saxon leader who led a tribe known as the Snotingas, who gave their name to the settlements of Nottingham, once known as "Snotengaham", meaning followers of Snot.

Derived from Old Norse snotr "clever; smart". In Norse mythology, Snotra is a goddess associated with wisdom. Snotra is solely attested in the Prose Edda, written in the 13th century by Snorri Sturluson and may be an invention of Snorri's. Simek writes that the goddesses Snotra, Sága, Hlín, Sjöfn, Vár, and Vör should be considered vaguely defined figures who "should be seen as female protective goddesses" that are all responsible for "specific areas of the private sphere, and yet clear differences were made between them so that they are in many ways similar to matrons."
Used as a Swedish translation of the name of the fairy tale character Snow White (Schneewittchen), from Swedish snö "snow" and vit "white".
Transferred use of the surname Snowden.
Possibly derived from a surname. This was used by Eudora Welty in her short story collection The Golden Apples (1949) for a central character, Snowdie MacLain.
The name of the flower used as a first name, mainly between the 1890s and 1920s, but never one of the more popular names of this kind.
Variant of Snow as well as a transferred use of the surname Snowe.

From the English word meaning "particle of snow crystal". It is commonly given to pets that have a white coloration. A famous bearer of the name was Snowflake the gorilla (1964-2003), known for being the world's only known albino gorilla.
From the English word snowman. Known bearers of this name include the supervillain Snowman in the DC Comics, and a horse named Snowman (1948-1974).
From the English word "snowy" meaning "covered with Snow; resembling snow; or when snow is falling".
Derived from the Germanic name elements snær "snow" and bjǫrn "bear".
A famous fictional character of this name is the Muppet character Mr. Snuffleupagus in the American educational children's television series Sesame Street (1969), who is known simply as Snuffy.
From the English word "snug" meaning "cozy, comfortable, or neat".
Transferred use of the surname Snyder.
Short form of Sophie, Sofia, Sophia, Soren, Solomon and other names beginning with So.

Diminutive of Soaz, itself a short form of Frañsoazig, a "Bretonized" form of Françoise.

The name of Sobe first appears in writings of about the 7th century by Hippolytus of Thebes.Sobe, also known as Sovin, is a biblical character said to be one of the daughters of Matthan the priest, sister of Saint Anne (Jesus' grandmother), and grandmother to John the Baptist. This is according to medieval Byzantine sources.According to St. Hippolytus of Rome, Sobe was the daughter of High Priest Phanuel and his wife Mary, and the eldest sister of St. Anne.

From Egyptian sbk-m-sꜢ.f meaning "Sobek protects him", derived from the name of the god Sobek combined with m "is; in the role of", zꜢ "protection", and the suffix .f "he, him, his". Although it is grammatically masculine name, there is evidence of it also being given to women.

Means "makes glory", a short form of Oluwasogo.

Meaning uncertain. According to one Russian source, the name is an Armenian form of Socrates. The flower's nature was to reveal your true intentions. If you went to ask it in false, you'd smell the sweet dew and get poison and become part of the mountain. Solkan is a rare, powerful name derived from the ancient Turkic elements sol, which in historical military and state contexts represented the highly prestigious left wing (the tactical flank that traditionally symbolized defense, protection, and the solid backbone of the army/state), and kan meaning "leader", "ruler", "sovereign", or "noble bloodline". It translates to "The Ruler of the Left Wing" or "The Sovereign Guardian".Solkan is a fiercely independent and noble name that carries a deep sense of strategic authority and unique leadership. It praises an individual who is not afraid to forge their own distinct path, standing strong as a protective shield and an independent thinker. Symbolically, it represents a leader who balances raw, sovereign power with calculated intelligence, acting as an unyielding pillar of defense for their people. It carries a sharp, modern phonetic punch while remaining deeply tied to old military honors, making it the ultimate praise for a courageous, reliable person destined to lead with honor, protect with loyalty, and carve a unique, unforgettable legacy in the world.

The name Somay is a feminine Turkish name formed from the combination of the elements som and ay. It is traditionally found in urban centers such as Istanbul, Bursa, Izmir, and Mersin.The first element, som, carries three distinct nuances in Turkic linguistics:In modern Turkish (as noted by scholars like Atalay and Kabalcı), it means "pure, unadulterated".It is the root of the word somut, meaning "concrete" or "tangible."According to the Dīwān Lughāt al-Turk by Kaşgari, it means "one-piece, solid" (referring to solid metal or ice), as seen in the phrase "som altun" ("solid gold").The second element is Ay, a common Turkish name element meaning "moon".For parents, the name symbolizes a child who carries a soul as "pure and unbreakable as solid gold," standing firm in their word and wisdom while possessing the "luminous, guiding light of the moon" to lead others through the dark. It suggests a personality that is both intellectually grounded (solid), like the roots of an ancient folk tale, and spiritually radiant (luminous), like a melody that echoes across the steppes.

Taken from the city of Sonoma in California. The name of the city comes from Wintun Sono (after Wintun local chief, literally meaning "nose") and ma meaning "land", but it is often given the popular meaning "valley of the Moon" through conflation with the Wintun word sano ("Moon").

column3: 園芽, 園女, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

Means "seven" in Ijaw. It is typically given to a seventh child, or a child born prematurely in the seventh month.
From Japanese 園 (sono) meaning "garden" combined with 乃 (no), a possessive particle. Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.

Of uncertain origin and meaning. It might be inspired by the name of the north-western Mexican state Sonora or possibly be derived from Latin sonorus "resounding; sonorous".

Means "weapon of Rama" from Thai ศร (son) meaning "weapon, bow, arrow" combined with the name of the Hindu god Rama 1.
Means "smile" in Spanish. It is not commonly used as a name in the Spanish-speaking world.

Name that was given during the Hēan Period, to an Empress Consort, "藤原 尊子" FUJIWARANOSONSHI, married to "一条天皇" ICHIJŌ the Japanese Emperor Ichijō. The Kanji Character "尊" meaning "Honor" with the Kanji Character "子" meaning "Child". It could also be called "Takako". See also Shōshi, Kenshi, Ishi, Kishi.

Spanish variant of Sons-ee-ah-ray, which was used for a young Apache girl in the American Western film Broken Arrow (first released in the United States in 1950). This name is mainly used in Venezuela.
Alternate transcription of Thai สนธยา (see Sonthaya).
Means "twilight" in Thai, ultimately from Sanskrit संध्या (saṃdhyā).
Means "combining, connecting, joining" in Thai, ultimately from Sanskrit सन्धि (sandhi).
From Thai สนธิ (sonthi) meaning "combining, connecting, joining" and ชัย (chai) meaning "victory".

From Sino-Vietnamese 山 (sơn) meaning "mountain" and 精 (tinh) meaning "spirit". This is a mountain god and one of the Four Immortals in Vietnamese mythology, governing the Ba Vì mountain range. He is also said to be one of the sons of Lạc Long Quân and Âu Cơ.
Means "camellia", especially Camellia sasanqua, from Sino-Vietnamese 山 (sơn) meaning "mountain" and 茶 (trà) meaning "camellia".
Derived from the word sohna, the Punjabi word for "handsome" or "beautiful".
Means "we are content" or "we are happy" in Xhosa.
Means "the end of summer" from Turkish son meaning "last, the end" and yaz meaning "summer".
Referring to the Chinese Song dynasty.

Modern name formed from the characters su (秀) meaning "luxuriant, beautiful, elegant, outstanding" combined with ri (裡) "admist by, surrounded in" when read in hanja. Can also take on the meaning "eagle" when written in hangeul or interpreted as one (鳥).

Derived from Kyrgyz соорон (sooron) meaning "soothing, comforting, consolation" combined either with бай (bay) meaning "rich, wealthy" or the Turkish military title beg meaning "chieftain, master". A notable bearer is Sooronbay Jeenbekov (1958-), the fifth president of Kyrgyzstan who served from 2017 to 2020.

Derived from σόος (soos), which is the Epic and Ionic Greek form of the adjective σῶς (sos) meaning "safe, whole, unwounded".This was the name of a semi-mythological king of Sparta, who is thought to have lived in the 9th century BC.
Tamil form of Joseph, used by Christians.
Alternate transcription of Persian سوسن (see Sousan).

column3: 수연(Korean Hangul)|秀妍, 受延, 水連, etc.(Korean Hanja)

From 秀 (su) meaning "luxuriant, beautiful, elegant, outstanding", 受 (su) meaning "receive, accept" or 水 (su) meaning "water" combined with 妍 (yeon) meaning "beautiful", 延 (yeon) meaning "stretch, prolong" or 連 (yeon) meaning "join, connect". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

Latinized form of Sopatros. A notable bearer of this name is Sopater of Apamea, a Greek philosopher from the 4th century AD.This name also occurs briefly in Acts in the New Testament, where it belongs to a Christian from the city of Berea in Roman Macedonia.
Contracted form of Sosipatra. This name was borne by a saint from the 7th century AD, whose name is frequently misspelled as Soprata.

Contracted form of Sosipatros. This name was borne by a Greek man from the New Testament as well as by a Greek philosopher from the 4th century AD. Both men are better known under the latinized form of their name, which is Sopater.
Alternate transcription of Khmer សុភាព (see Sopheap).

From a Spanish title of the Virgin Mary, Nuestra Señora de Sopetrán, meaning "Our Lady of Sopetrán", chiefly venerated in the town Jarandilla de la Vega in Spain. According to a local legend, the word Sopetrán comes from the name of a Moorish prince of Toledo who changed his name to Petrán after a Marian apparition, thus the Virgin was so Petrán ("under Petrán").
Derived from Greek σοφός (sophos) meaning "skilled, clever" and αἰνετός (ainetos) meaning "praiseworthy".
Means "well-born, well-grown" in Khmer, of Sanskrit origin.

column3: សុភក្ត្រ, សុភ័ក្រ្ត(Khmer)
column12: Means "good face" from Khmer សុ (so) meaning "good" and ភក្ត្រ or ភ័ក្រ្ត (pheak) meaning "face".
Variant of Sophie and diminutive of Sophia.
Alternate transcription of Arabic سفيان (see Sufyan) chiefly used in North Africa, as well as the Indonesian and Malay form.
Alternate transcription of Arabic سفيان (see Sufyan) chiefly used in North Africa.
Pet form of Sophie, but it is also a diminutive form of the name because it has the diminutive suffix -ke at the end.
Elaborated form of Sophie or Sophia.

Derived from the Greek adjective σῶς (sos) meaning "safe, whole, unwounded" (see Sosigenes) combined with the Greek noun φίλος (philos) meaning "friend, lover".This name was borne by an Attic potter and vase painter from the 6th century BC.
A blend of Sophie and Antoinette.
Sophitia Alexandra, better known simply as Sophitia, is a fictional character in the Soulcalibur series of video games.
Latinized form of Sophios, which is the masculine form of Sophia.
Derived from Greek σοφός (sophos) meaning "skilled, clever".
French form of Sophonias. It was originally strictly a masculine name, but it has been used on females since the late 1980s, which is probably due to the name's strong resemblance to Sophie.

French form of Sophonisba. Sophonisbe has been the subject of several tragedies, among others La Sophonisbe by Jean Mairet (1634), Sophonisbe by Pierre Corneille (1663) and Sophonisbe by Voltaire (1770).

column12: Alternate transcription of Sophon (see second user-submitted name).
French form of Sophronios via Sophronius.

Derived from Greek σωφροσύνη (sôphrosynê) meaning "prudence, self-control, temperance". Also compare Sophron. This was the name of the spirit or personification of moderation, self-control, temperance, restraint, and discretion in Greek mythology. In some tales Sophrosyne was one of the good spirits released from Pandora's box, but fled to Olympus and away from humankind.
Indonesian and Malay form of Safiyyah.
Diminutive of Sopio. A notable bearer of this name was the Georgian actress Sopiko Chiaureli (1937-2008).
Alternate transcription of Sophon (see second user-submitted name).
Alternate transcription of Thai โสภณ (see Sophon).
Corruption or misspelling of Sopatra, which is usually encountered in connection to the 7th-century saint Sopatra.
Georgian form of Sophron or a variant form of Soproni.
Meaning unknown; the second element is from the Turkish military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".
Name of a son of the "black sachem" Tuspaquin.

Indigenous Korean name, a single two-syllable word meaning "conch shell". It is one of a number of such native names (called 고유어 이름) that have become more popular in South Korea in recent decades. In some cases, however, parents also choose to register hanja to represent the name, picking them solely for their pronunciation (for example, 曙羅, with hanja meaning "sunlight" and "net", respectively). There are 45 hanja with the reading "so" and 14 hanja with the reading "ra" on the South Korean government's official list of hanja which may used in given names.
Archaic Anglicized form of Sorcha. Soraca Jonin, a member of the Mac Jonin (Jennings) family of Tuam, fl. 1678, was a religious patron.

column3: 空知, 空智, 天智, 宗良治, 颯良智, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|そらち(Japanese Hiragana)|ソラチ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From the name of a river in western Hokkaido (空知), derived from Ainu ソラㇷ゚チペッ (Sorapchipet), combined from ソ (so) meaning "waterfall" and ラㇷ゚ (rap) meaning "to descend" with the plural suffix チ (chi) and ペッ (pet) meaning "river."The second kanji can be substituted with a chi kanji, like 智 with the same meaning ("wisdom") as 知 or 治 meaning "cure; management." The first kanji can be substituted with a kanji that has the same or similar meaning to 空 ("sky, heaven"), like 天, or it can be split into two kanji with a so(u) kanji, e.g. 宗 meaning "principle, aim, pillar" or 颯 meaning "quick, sudden," and a ra kanji, e.g. 良 meaning "good, excellent."This name is rarely used.

column3: 昊葉, 空羽, 宙晴, 天葉, 穹羽, 宇晴, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 昊 or 空 (sora) meaning "sky" or 宙 (sora) meaning "space, mid-air" combined with 羽 (ha) meaning "feather, plume", 葉 (ha) meaning "needle, blade, leaf" or 晴 (ha) meaning "clear weather, clear up". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Japanese 空 (sora) meaning "sky" combined with 陽 (hi) meaning "light, sun, male". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 空彦, 宇彦, 宙彦, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 空 (sora) meaning "sky", 宇 (sora) meaning "house, building, structure, eaves" or 宙 (sora) meaning "mid-air" combined with 彦 (hiko) meaning "boy, prince". Other kanji combinations are also possible.
Bosnian, Croatian and Serbian form of Thurayya.

column12: From Japanese 空 (sora) meaning "sky", 宙 (sora) meaning "space, mid-air" or 天 (sora) meaning "heavens, sky" combined with 歌 (ka) meaning "song, poetry", 叶 (ka) meaning "fulfill, come true", 風 (ka) meaning "wind" or 遥 (ka) meaning "distant, remote". Other kanji combinations are also possible.

column3: 空輝, 宙輝, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 空 (sora) meaning "sky" combined with 輝 (ki) meaning "bright". Other kanji combinations are possible.

From Ángel or (sometimes) Orángel prefixed with Sor-, likely taken from names beginning with this pattern, e.g. Soraida.This name belongs to the main character of the eponymous 1982 Venezuelan telenovela.

column3: そらの(Japanese Hiragana)|空乃, 天乃, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 空 (sora) meaning "sky" or 天 (sora) meaning "heavens, sky" combined with 乃 (no), a possessive particle. Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.

column3: 宙生, 空夫, 空男, 空緒, 空雄, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 宙 (sora) meaning "mid-air" or 空 (sora) meaning "sky" combined with 生 (o) meaning "life, genuine, birth", 夫 (o) meaning "man, husband", 男 (o) meaning "male", 緒 (o) meaning "thread" or 雄 (o) meaning "hero, manly". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Variant of Seraphine influenced by the name Sora.
From Japanese 空 (sora) meaning "sky" combined with 々, a phonetic character indicting a duplication of the beginning kanji. Other kanji combinations are possible.

Other combinations of kanji characters are possible.
From Japanese 空 (sora) meaning "sky" combined with 太 (ta) meaning "thick, big". Other combinations of kanji are possible.

column12: From Japanese 空 (sora) meaning "sky" combined with 都 (to) meaning "capital (city)". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 空也, 天陽, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 空 (sora) meaning "sky" or 天 (sora) meaning "heavens, sky" combined with 也 (ya) meaning "also" or 陽 (ya) meaning "light, sun, male". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Perhaps from Soraye Takahashi, who was a fourth-grade girl in SRES.
From Japanese 空 (sora) meaning "sky" combined with 夜 (yo) meaning "night". Other kanji combinations are possible.

Meaning unknown.Chrétien de Troyes used it in his Arthurian romance poet Cligès, which is written around 1176. In the story, Soredamors was the lover of Alexander, a King Arthur's knight.
Transferred use of the surname Sorell. A famous namesake is biologist Sir Julian Sorell Huxley, the brother of Aldous Huxley.

Derived from Kurdish sor meaning "red" and gula meaning "rose".

A fictional character created by J.R.R. Tolkien. Soronto was a Númenorean nobleman of the royal lineage of Númenor or House of Elros, the grandson of Tar-Meneldur and son of Ailinel, sister of Tar-Aldarion. He lived in the later years of the first millennium of the Second Age. His father was Orchaldor, a descendant of the House of Hador.

Means "fortune, fate" in Latin. In Roman mythology, Sors was a god of luck and the supposed son of Fortuna.

The name of a character in Ron Howard's movie "Willow" (1988). In it, she is a princess, the daughter of the evil Queen Bavmorda. She ends up betraying her mother to serve the cause of good. George Lucas, who wrote the story for the movie, may have based Sorsha's name on either Sorcha or Saoirse.
Means "sweet, friendly, courteous, polite" in Batak.

Tongan form of Josiah. Alternative spelling of Siosaia. Often shortened to Saia.
Form of Susanna used by Malayalam-speaking Syriac Christians in the Indian state of Kerala.

Feminine form of Sosandros. This is an alleged epithet of a Greek goddess known from a statue erected on the Akropolis. It has been suggested that Sosandra may have been an epithet of Aphrodite, Hera, Hestia or Demeter.
Derived from Ancient Greek σῶς (sos) meaning "safe, whole, unwounded" combined with ἀνδρός (andros) meaning "of a man".
Dutch and German variant of Shosha.

Derived from Greek σως (sos) meaning "safe, whole, unwounded". In Greek mythology this was the name of a prophetic Oreiad or Naiad nymph of Arcadia (a southern region of Greece). According to one account she was the mother of the god Pan by Hermes.
Tongan and Chuukese form of Josephine.

column12: Old Church Slavic form of Sosthenes.

Derived from the Greek adjective σῶς (sos) meaning "safe, whole, unwounded" (see Sosigenes) combined with the Greek noun βίος (bios) meaning "life".
Latinized form of Sosikrates. A known bearer of this name is the Greek historian Sosicrates of Rhodes (2nd century BC).

Meaning uncertain. Actors Kevin Bacon and Kyra Sedgwick used it for their daughter Sosie Bacon (1992-). It was perhaps inspired by French sosie "lookalike", derived from Latin Sosia, the name of a character in Plautus' play 'Amphitryon', itself from Greek Σωσίας (Sosias) meaning "savior" from σως (sos) "safe, whole, unwounded" (compare Sostrate, Sose). Alternatively it may be a variant of Susie.
Derived from the Greek adjective σῶς (sos) meaning "safe, whole, unwounded" (see Sosigenes) combined with the Greek noun κλέος (kleos) meaning "glory".

Derived from the Greek adjective σῶς (sos) meaning "safe, whole, unwounded" (see Sosigenes) combined with the Greek noun κράτος (kratos) meaning "power".This is the name of a Greek historian from the 2nd century BC, who is better known under the latinized form of his name, which is Sosicrates.
Latinized form of Sosipatros. This is the name of a Greek man from the New Testament.
Russian form of Sosipatros, possibly via its latinized form Sosipater.
Feminine form of Sosipatros. This name was borne by the Greek philosopher Sosipatra of Ephesus (4th century AD).
Georgian form of Sosipatros. A known bearer of this name was the Georgian politician and diplomat Sosipatre Asatiani (1872-1971).

Derived from the Greek adjective σῶς (sos) meaning "safe, whole, unwounded" (see Sosigenes) combined with either the Greek adjective πατρός (patros) meaning "of the father" or the Greek noun πατρίς (patris) meaning "of one's fathers" as well as "fatherland".This is the name of a Greek man from the New Testament, who is better known under the latinized form of his name, which is Sosipater.

Derived from the Greek adjective σῶς (sos) meaning "safe, whole, unwounded" (see Sosigenes) combined with Greek φανής (phanes) meaning "appearing" (see Theophanes).A known bearer of this name is the Greek tragic poet Sosiphanes of Syracuse (3rd century BC).

Derived from the Greek adjective σῶς (sos) meaning "safe, whole, unwounded" (see Sosigenes) combined with either the Greek noun φρόνις (phronis) meaning "prudence, wisdom" or the Greek verb φρονέω (phroneo) meaning "to think" as well as "to be minded". Both words are ultimately derived from the Greek noun φρήν (phren) meaning "midriff" as well as "mind, intellect, wits".

Means "city saviour" in Ancient Greek, derived from σῴζω (sozo) meaning "to save, keep, preserve" (from sos "safe, whole") and πόλις (polis) meaning "city". This was the name of a son of the goddess Eileithyia worshipped in Elis, said to have gained his name as a child when he saved the city by turning into a serpent to frighten away an invading army. Means "subterranean" in Spanish, taken from the titles of the Virgin Mary La Virgen de la Soterraña and Nuestra Señora de la Soterraña, meaning "The Virgin of the Subterranean" and "Our Lady of the Subterranean" respectively. It refers to a statue of the Virgin Mary that was found buried underground in a cave or hill in Segovia‎, Spain, at the end of the 14th century. Our Lady of Soterraña is venerated at the church and monastery located in Santa María la Real de Nieva in the central northern province of Segovia, hence the name's high concentration there. She is also venerated at the basilica of San Vicente in Ávila and the church of San Miguel in Olmedo in the north-western province of Valladolid.

Presumably a variant or misreading of the surname Soulouque.Faustin-Élie Soulouque (15 August 1782 – 6 August 1867) was proclaimed Emperor of Haïti under the name Faustin I in 1849. He soon purged the army of the ruling elite, installed black-skinned loyalists in administrative positions, and created a secret police and a personal army. In 1849 he created a black nobility in the country. However, his unsuccessful attempts to reconquer the neighbouring Dominican Republic undermined his control and a conspiracy led by General Fabre Nicolas Geffrard forced him to abdicate in 1859.

Meaning uncertain. This name should be a compound name, of which the first element might be the Greek noun σοῦς (sous) meaning "upward motion" or the Greek noun σοῦσον (souson) meaning "lily". Even Σοῦσα (Sousa) is technically a possibility, which is a hellenization of the native Elamite name for the capital city of Elam. This city is best known to us as Susa, which is the latinized form of the aforementioned hellenization.The second element of this name could possibly consist of the Greek diminutive suffix -άριον (-arion), though the name should probably have been written as Σουσάριον instead of as Σουσαρίων then. One literary source theorizes that the second element might consist of the Greek name Arion, in reference to the Greek kitharode of that name, who was credited with inventing the dithyramb.Sousarion was the name (possibly pseudonym) of a Greek comic poet from Megara, who lived in the 6th century BC. He is better known under the latinized form of his name, which is Susarion.
