However, it would only apply when the name is written as ტალიკო, since Natalia is written as ნატალია in Georgian.
A very rare male name whose pronunciation is unknown.
Variant of Talilia or a diminutive of Talía
Means sharp or blade in tagalog. In Soulcalibur II, III, & IV there is a character named Talim.
Diminutive of Nutal, traditionally found in the Lower Engadine.
Diminutive of Nutala, the Romansh form of Natalia.
East Frisian diminutive and elaboration of Tale.
Diminutive of Catalina, Natalia, and other names containing -tal-.
This is the name of a character in the games 'Middle-earth: Shadow of Mordor' and 'Middle-earth: Shadow of War'.
From Tamil தளிர் (taḷir) meaning "sprout; shoot; tender leaf".
Originally a short form of Tālivaldis, now used as a given name in its own right.
Possibly an Estonian borrowing of Tālis.
From the name of the genus of flowering plants in the soapberry family.

The name Taliska has two primary origins: as an early language in J.R.R. Tolkien's writings and as a name derived from the Scottish Gaelic word for "sloping rock". In Tolkien's work, Taliska was an archaic language of the Edain (Men), which was later refined into different linguistic families. The name "Talisker," on the other hand, refers to an old Norse term for a place and is the name of a famous Scotch whisky and a location on the Isle of Skye.
Means "little girl arise" in Aramaic, from the phrase spoken by Jesus in Mark 5:41 in order to restore a young girl to life (see also Talitha, Cumi).

Derived from Latvian tāls "far; far away" and valdīt "to rule; to reign". Tālivaldis was a Latgalian elder, the ruler of Tālava, whose support for Albert of Riga and the German crusaders brought about his death at the hands of the native Baltic peoples.
An invented name combining the phonetic elements ta, lee and ya, based on the sound of Aaliyah. (Compare Kaliyah, Jaliyah, Maliyah.) It is probably also viewed as a variant of Thalía or Talía.
A character in the novel, "The Pilgrim's Progress."
Transferred use of the surname Tallan.
Dutch given name of unknown meaning. In 2010, there were less than 5 bearers (of all ages) in all of The Netherlands.
Variant of Talarico, a short form of Atalarico.

In Claris et Laris the King of Denmark and son of King Saladin.He besieged King Urien because he wanted to marry Marine, Urien’s daughter. Arthur’s knights, led by Claris and Laris, lifted the siege, and Arthur killed Tallas.
Means "dewy", deriving from the Ugaritic element ṭl ("dew"), combined with the feminine suffix y. Name borne by a weather goddess, considered to be a daughter of the god Baal.
Norwegian dialectal variant form of Torleiv.
Transferred use of the surname Talley
Variant of Tally, a diminutive of Natalie.-------------------------------------Diminutive of names such as Talbot or Talmadge or others beginning with Tal-.
Transferred use of the surname Tallis, which comes from the Old French taillis, referring to a clearing of woodland.
Derived from the Anglo-French surname of Tallon.A notable bearer of this name is the Dutch tennis player Tallon Griekspoor (b. 1996).
Diminutive of Tallulah, Talia 1 and other names that begin with or contain the element "Tal-".
Variant form of the English Talisa.Also a variant form of the name Tallis.Can be a combination of namesCan be shortened to Lyssi (LIS-ee)
Transferred use of the surname Talmadge.
Transferred use of the surname Talmon.
Combination of the names Tal and Mor means "dew of myrrh" in Hebrew.
Combination of the word "טל" (Tal), "dew", and the word אור (Or), "light", also used as a variant of Taylor.

In Greek mythology, Talos, also called Talon, was a bronze man given to Europa for protection in Crete from pirates and invaders. In some accounts he is an automaton made by Hephaestus, in others he is the last of a race of bronze men. Another account has him instead as the father of Hephaestus.
Means "little maiden", derived from ⲁⲗⲟⲩ (alou) "youth, maiden" combined with ϣⲏⲙ (šem) "small, little".
Derived from Latvian tāls "far away, distant" and rīts "morning".

column1: Talula Does the Hula from Hawaii
column12: 'Talula Does the Hula from Hawaii' was a name given to a New Zealand girl in 1999. In 2008, her parents lost custody of her, as her name was deemed child abuse, and the girl's name was changed.
Variant of Tallulah. A known bearer is Talulah Riley (1985-), an English actress who was formerly married to business magnate Elon Musk.
Variant of Tallulah, influenced by the similar Irish name Talulla.

Meaning uncertain, said to be derived from Arabic طويل (ṭawīl) meaning "tall" and chosen to rhyme with جالوت (jālūt) meaning "Goliath". This is the name of a king mentioned in the Quran who is usually identified as Saul, the first king of Israel.
Variant of Talvi. The name coincides with the genitive case of talv "winter".
Derived from Cornish tal "brow; forehead; temple" and gwynn "fair; white; blessed". This is a modern Cornish name.
From a non-Sino-Vietnamese reading of Chinese 糝 (tấm) meaning "broken rice". This is the name of the main character in Tấm Cám, an ancient Vietnamese folk tale similar to Cinderella.
From Sino-Vietnamese 尋 (tầm) meaning "range, high level, to seek".
Diminutive of Tamara as well as other names beginning with tam-.
Short form of Tamara.This name is extremely rare as an official name on birth certificates; it is almost exclusively used informally.
Variant of Temaeva. A famous bearer of this name is Tamaeva IV, queen of the Polynesian island of Rimatara.
Found in the bible (King James Version) in the old testament
Means "beloved child", from Tahitian tamariʻi meaning "child" and here "love".
Variant of Tōmairangi, meaning "dew", or as compound name Tama-i-rangi meaning "son in heaven". This was the name of a 19th-century Maori tribal leader and poet.

column3: タマカ(Japanese Katakana)|たまか(Japanese Hiragana)|玉花, 瑞夏, 珠香, 球, 多, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 瑞 (tama) meaning "congratulations" or 玉 (tama) meaning "jewel, gem, ball, sphere" and 花 (ka) meaning "flower". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: たまき(Japanese Hiragana)|タマキ(Japanese Katakana)|環, 圭既, 玲騎, 環機, 霊希, 玉葵, 珠季, 魂妃, 球綺, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: Māori name for the Auckland area of New Zealand. The word tāmaki means "omen".

column3: 玉子, 珠子, 球子, 多満子, 多摩子, 多磨子, 多真子(Japanese Kanji)|たま子(Kanji/Hiragana)|たまこ(Japanese Hiragana)|タマコ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name can be used to combine 玉 (gyoku, tama, tama-, -dama) meaning "gem, jewel," 珠 (shu, tama) with, pretty much, the same meanings as 玉 or 球 (kyu, tama) meaning "ball" with 子 (shi, su, tsu, ko, -ko, -ne) meaning "child."Other ways to write 'Tama' include using phonetic characters or using 2 kanji, like 多 (ta, oo.i, masa.ni, masa.ru) meaning "frequent, many, much" and 満 (ban, man, mi.tasu, mi.chiru, mi.tsu, ma) meaning "full, fulfill, satisfy," 摩 (ma, sa.suru, su.ru, ma.suru) meaning "chafe, grind, polish, rub," 磨 (ma, su.ru, miga.ku) meaning "brush, grind, improve, polish," or 真 (shin, ma, ma-, makoto) meaning "real, true."

From tama kō roro meaning "boy at the front of the meeting house". This was the name of a Moriori man who was killed in 1791 after a misunderstanding over a fishing net with the first outsiders who came to what is now the Chatham Islands.

column3: たまみ(Japanese Hiragana)|たま美(Kanji/Hiragana)|環実, 球実, 球微, 玉海, 球美, 玉実, 玉味, 玖美, 圭見, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 球 (tama, gu, kyuu, ku) meaning "sphere; globe; orb, (baseball) pitch", 玉 (tama, goku (non-Jōyō reading), gyoku) meaning "ball, (a Japanese) coin, precious stone, a chicken’s egg (to be eaten), geisha" or 環 (tama, tamaki, yubimaki, kwan, gwen, gen (non-Jōyō reading, historical) kan (historical)), combined with 美 (mi, bi, utsukushii, yoi, homaru) meaning "beauty; beautiful", 実 (shitsu, jitsu, minoru, mi, makoto, makotoni, mino, michiru, gumi, sane) meaning "reality, truth, fruit, seed; fruit; nut, kindness", 海 (kai, umi, wata, wada, a, ama, una, un, e, ka, ta, hiro, hiroshi, bu, machi, mama, mi, me, wataru) meaning "sea, ocean" or 微 (mi, bi, chiisai, kasuka, wazuka) meaning "delicate". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Perhaps derived from the Chuvash tǎmana meaning "owl" or tǎman meaning "snowstorm".
Berber name for the constallation Orion.
Variant of Tamann and diminutive of Tammana
Means "praise" or "to God be the glory" in Chewa.
Tamania is a genus of butterflies. Possibly a variant of Chewa name Tamani, or Arabic names Tamanya or Tamanna.
Alternate transcription of Hindi तमन्ना (see Tamanna).
Alternate transcription of Thai ธรรมนูญ (see Thammanun).
Combination of the popular name element Tam (see Tammy) and Samantha (see also Tamela).
Means "how can we know the future?" in Tumbuka.

column3: 玉男, 玉夫, 玉雄, 珠男, 珠夫, 珠雄, 玉尾, 玉緒, 玉青, 珠緒, 珠央(Japanese Kanji)|たまお(Japanese Hiragana)|タマオ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name can be used to combine 玉 (gyoku, tama(-), -dama) or 珠 (shu, tama), both meaning "gem, jewel," with 男 (dan, nan, otoko, o), 夫 (fu, fuu, bu, otto, sore, o) or 雄 (yuu, o-, osu, on), all meaning "man." For females, it can be used as 玉尾, 玉緒, 玉青, 珠緒 or 珠央 with 尾 (bi, o) meaning "tail (end)," 緒 (sho, cho, o, itoguchi) meaning "cord, strap, thong," 青 (sei, shou, ao(-), ao.i) meaning "blue" and 央 (ou, o) meaning "middle, centre."Bearers of this name include (female) actress Tamao Nakamura (中村 玉緒) (1939-), (female) actress and voice actress Tamao Satō (さとう 珠緒), born (佐藤 珠緒) (1973-) and (male) puppeteer Tamao Yoshida (吉田 玉男) (1919-2006).
Meaning unknown. Tamar was the Georgian goddess of the sky who was portrayed as riding on a snake. She is identified with the goddess Lamara.

column3: 貴麻, 多麻良, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: In Cornish folklore, Tamara is a nymph who lived in the underworld and wanted to wander freely in the mortal world, against the advice of her parents. When she falls in love with the giant Tawradge, she refuses to return to the underworld with her father. He becomes enraged and casts a spell on Tamara, turning her into a bubbling spring, which produced the Tamar river (Dowr Tamar in Cornish), that forms most of the border between Devon and Cornwall.
Variant of Tamara. Tamarah was a character played by actress Fern Andra in the film Lotus Lady (1930).
Means "there's none like God" in Ijaw.
Combination of the popular prefix ta with the name Marcus.
From the name of the tropical tree (species Tamarindus indica) or its fruit, ultimately derived from Arabic تَمْر هِنْدِيّ (tamr hindiyy) meaning "Indian date".
From the name of the flowering tamarisk plant.
Means "second child," from tama meaning "child" and rua meaning "two."
Means "hold on, hold fast" in Arabic.
Hindu name meaning "one who has darkness inside"
Means "subdued" in Māori, and variant of Tamati.

Means "the Moon, on the 8th night of a lunar month, first quarter lunar phase" in Maori. Tamatea Arikinui or Tamatea Mai-Tawhiti was a legendary Maori chieftain who captained the Tākitimu on its journey from the legendary place Hawaiki to New Zealand.
Variant of Tamatea, or from tama meaning "boy" and tia meaning "servant".

column3: 珠代, 圭代, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|たまよ(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: From Japanese 珠 (tama) meaning "pearl, gem, jewel" or 圭 (tama) meaning "gemstone" combined with 代 (yo) meaning "generation, era". Other kanji combinations can form this name as well.
Means "united" or "total, sum, result" in Malagasy.

Coined by Eduard Bornhöhe for a character in his novel 'Tasuja' (1880). The exact origin and meaning of this name are uncertain, it has, however, been speculated that it might be a contraction of Estonian tammepuust "of oak wood".

Derived from там (tam) meaning "whole, entire" combined with би (bi) meaning "ruler". The latter element is ultimately derived from the Turkic military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".In the Middle East (particularly Jordan and Syria), the name is most prevalent among the Circassian diaspora.
Transferred use of the surname Tamblyn.
Altered form of Tamra, perhaps influenced by Debra.
Diminutive of Tamar, Tamta and Tamuna.
From Sino-Vietnamese 三綱 (tam cương) referring to the three fundamental bonds in Confucian philosophy: ruler and subject, father and son, and husband and wife.
Alternate transcription of Tibetan རྟ་མགྲིན (see Damdrin).
Alternate transcription of Tibetan རྟ་མགྲིན (see Damdrin).
Alternate transcription of Tibetan རྟ་མགྲིན (see Damdrin).
Frisian short form of names that have thanc for a first element, and of which the second element starts with an "m." The name Dankmar is a good example of that.

column3: ためあき(Japanese Hiragana)|タメアキ(Japanese Katakana)|為昭, 為明, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 為 (tame) meaning "carry out, perform, do" combined with 明 (aki) meaning "bright". Fujiwara no Tameaki (1198-1275) was a Japanese poet.
Alternate transcription of Arabic تميم and Bengali তামিম (see Tamim).
From 為 (tame) meaning "to do, carry out, perform, benefit, advantage" and 清 (kiyo) meaning "clear, pure, clean".

the name itself means ‘first born’.Berbers often named children based on their order of birth, such as "first born", "their oldest", "their youngest" "that who has a brother" "that who has a sister"Because of the cases existing in the Berber language these names that would end up long sentences end up being one word.
Means "competent soldier" or "mannish, man of good qualities" in Turkish.
Probably created from Cameron by replacing the initial C with a T or an elaboration of Tamara.
Elaborated form of Tamesa and variant of Tamesis, the two names of the river Thames in Roman times.
The Celtic goddess of fresh waters. Her name survives in the English River Thames and in Tamise, a French name for the Schelde (Scheldt).
Diminutive of Tamara or Tamina. Means "chipmunk" in French. Also in the case of French composer Tamia Valmont (1947-).
Apparently means "perfection of God" in Hebrew. This is the name of one of the fallen angels listed in the Book of Enoch.

column3: タミカ(Japanese Katakana)|多実果, 多美佳, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 多 (ta) meaning "many, much", 実 (mi) meaning "reality, truth, fruit" combined with 果 (ka) meaning "fruit". Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.
Means "daughter of Mother Tamil" from Tamil தமிழ் (tamiḻ) referring to the Tamil language (and its personification, Mother Tamil) and செல்வி (celvi) meaning "daughter, girl".
Combination of Tami and the popular name suffix lyn.
Feminine form of Tamino. Tamina is a character in Milan Kundera's 'The Book of Laughter and Forgetting' (1979).
Descends from the Greek word tamias which means "lord" or "master". There is a Tamino in Mozart's "The Magic Flute".

column3: 民夫, 民生, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|たみお(Japanese Hiragana)|タミオ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 民 (tami) meaning "citizen" combined with 夫 (o) meaning "man, husband" or 生 (o) meaning "living, fresh". Other kanji combinations can form this name as well.
Means "date merchant, possessor of dates" in Arabic.
This is the Persian Form of the Name Tomyris
From tāmi "smother, quashing" and rangi "sky", or a variant of Tamairangi.
Dagestani and Kyrgyz form of Tamerlane.
Tamisa is the Latinized name the Romans gave to the river Thames in England. The ancient Brittons named Thames after the Celtic goddess of dark water, Tamesis.
Variant of Thomasin. Tamisen Brike was the wife of John Mayo, a Puritan minister in pre-revolutionary Boston, Massachusetts and the first minister of Old North Church.
Combination of the phonetic elements ta, mee and sha. Also compare Tamika and Tanisha.
Means "she-cat" in Ancient Egyptian. This was the name of Prince Thutmose's cat, best remembered for being buried in her own sarcophagus.

column3: 民代, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|たみよ(Japanese Hiragana)|タミヨ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 民 (tami) meaning "people, citizens" combined with 代 (yo) meaning "generation, era". Other kanji combinations can form this name as well.
Uzbek feminine name derived from tamiz meaning "intelligence, intellect, quick witted".
From the name of the Tamil people, which is of uncertain meaning.

Diminutive of Tam 1. Tam Lin was the subject of an Anglo-Scottish border ballad (first recorded in 'The Complaynt of Scotland', 1549), a man abducted by the Queen of the Fairies and rescued at long last by his true love.
Transferred use of the surname Tamlyn.
Alternate transcription of Thai ธรรมนูญ (see Thammanun).
Italian feminine form of Thancmar via the Latinization Tammarus.
Alternate transcription of Thai ธรรมรักษ์ (see Thammarak).
Alternate transcription of Thai ธรรมรัตน์ (see Thammarat).
Alternate transcription of Thai ธรรมรักษ์ (see Thammarak).
From Sino-Vietnamese 三昧 (tam muội), borrowed from Sanskrit समाधि (samādhi), referring to the Buddhist concept of the highest state of meditation before spiritual liberation (nirvana).
Means "he who lights up the valleys" in Meitei.
Means "he who rules the valleys" in Meitei.

column3: 多門, 多聞, 太門, 汰門, 田門(Japanese Kanji)|たもん(Japanese Hiragana)|タモン(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name can be used as 多門, 多聞, 太門, 汰門 or 田門 with 多 (ta, oo.i, masa.ni, masa.ru) meaning "frequent, many, much", 太 (ta, tai, futo.i, futo.ru) meaning "big around, plump, thick", 汰 (ta, tai, ogo.ru, nigo.ru, yona.geru) meaning "luxury, select", 田 (den, ta) meaning "rice field/paddy", 門 (mon, kado, to) meaning "gate" and 聞 (bun, mon, ki.ku, ki.koeru) meaning "ask, hear, listen."In modern times, it's rarely given to boys, if given at all.Tamon is also used as a surname.
From Guanche *tamannant, meaning "woman who knows to read" (literally "she who spells"). Tamonante was the daughter of Tibiabin, a priestess.
Alternate transcription of Urdu تیمور (see Taimur).

This name was used by Shakespeare for the evil queen of the Goths in his tragedy Titus Andronicus (1593). Shakespeare's source for the play is unknown, but he may have based the name on Tomyris. A known bearer is American fantasy writer Tamora Pierce (1954-), in whose case it originated as a misspelling of Tamara.
Etymology unknown. This was the name of an Egyptian mercenary admiral from Memphis who was hired by Cyrus the Younger during the 4th century BC.

column3: 保, 維, 太持(Japanese Kanji)|たもつ(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: Derived from the Japanese kanji 保 (tamotsu) meaning "protection" or 維 (tamotsu) meaning "keep; mantain" as well as the combination of two or more characters for example 太 (ta) meaning "big; great" combined with 持 (motsu) meaning "hold; have".Other characters combinations are also possible.
Derived from the Meitei tampha meaning "jewel" and sana meaning "gold, precious".

A Roman cognomen possibly from Ancient Greek ταμίας (tamíās) "steward, dispenser", from τέμνω (témnō) "to cut, hew", combined with φίλος (philos) "friend, lover". One bearer of this name was the name of a consul of the Roman Republic in 181 BC along with Publius Cornelius Cethegus.
From Sino-Vietnamese 三光 (tam quang) meaning "the sun, moon, and stars", composed of 三 (tam) meaning "three" and 光 (quang) meaning "light".
Means "practice, habituation, accustoming" in Arabic, from the root مَرَّنَ (marrana) meaning "to practise, to exercise".
Short form of Tamar and perhaps also of its diminutive Tamriko.
Variant of Tamsin as well as a short form of Thomasina.
Origin of the name is Turkish and it has been popular in western Georgia, specifically in Abkhazia, from somewhere XVI-XVII centuries.
From Bashkir тамсы (tamsï) meaning "drip, drop" and гөл (göl ) meaning "flower".

Derived from Persian tahamta or thamtha meaning "strong, brave", itself ultimately from Pahlavi تهم‎ (tahm) or (taham) meaning "brave". Also compare Avestan takhma meaning "strong, brave, valiant" (see Tahmina).
From Sino-Vietnamese 三才 (tam tài) meaning "three talents," referring to someone with the virtues and knowledge of heaven, earth, and man.

This name is often a pet form of Tamar, but it can also be a name in its own right. In that case, it is derived from Arabic تأمين (ta'min) meaning "insurance", which itself is ultimately derived from Arabic أمن (amn) meaning "security, peace". Also compare Arabic ضامن (daamin) meaning "guarantor, guarantee" (see Daamin) as well as Azerbaijani təmin "guarantee, security" and Turkish emin "sure, certain, secure, confident" (see Emin). The Arabic name Iman is probably also etymologically related, as to be faithful requires a certain kind of confidence or certainty.Last but not least: also compare the Persian name Tahmina, which is very similar in appearance. Given the fact that many given names are of Persian origin in Georgia, it is within the realm of possibility that Tamuna as an independent name comes from that name.
Means "wisdom of God" in Kalabari, spoken in Nigeria.
Means "God's will" or "God's favour" in Ijaw.
Belarusian and Georgian form of Tamusya.
Means "the one not housing the person" in Ganda.
Possibly means "hot, warm" in Hebrew. This is the tenth month in the jewish calendar.
Means "dog rose", from Sino-Vietnamese 尋 (tầm) meaning "to seek" and 春 (xuân) meaning "spring".
From Sino-Vietnamese 三春 (tam xuân) literally meaning "three springs", referring to the three months of spring, three years, or the last month of spring.

An invented name, combining the phonetic elements ta, my and ya, and based on the sounds of names such as Tamia and Amaya. It can be spelled Tamya or with a capitalized third letter as TaMya (or Ta'Mya).
Means "rain flower" in Quechua, from tamya, "rain" and sisa, "flower".
From Sino-Vietnamese 贊 (tán) meaning "to help, support".
From Sino-Vietnamese 晉 (tấn) meaning "advance, increase, promote".
From Sino-Vietnamese 秦 (tần) referring to the ancient state of Qin.

column3: 坦, 倓, etc.(Chinese)|坦, 旦, 淡, 潭, 澹, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|ต้าน(Thai)
column12: From Chinese 坦 (tǎn) meaning "smooth, flat, broad and level", in addition to other hanzi that are pronounced similarly.
Tanabata is the name of many japanese people & a festival.

A necromancer who lived in Britain some time between the time of Joseph of Arimathea and Uther Pendragon. He was hailed as the greatest magician ever to reside on the island, save Merlin.To keep a knight from reaching his unfaithful wife, who lived at Corbenic (Carbonek), Tanabos enchanted the Grail Castle in such a way that it could only be found by accident. The enchantment lasted until the time of Charlemagne, who razed Corbenic.

Uncertain etymology. This was the name of a naiad and namesake of the ancient town of Tanagra in Greek mythology, a daughter of either Aeolus or the river god Asopos. In some accounts the gods Hermes and Ares fought a boxing match over her, with Hermes being victorious and carrying her off; in others, she marries Poemander, who founds and names Tanagra after her. She was also called Γραῖα (Graia) "the grey one" in her later years.
Possibly a modern French variant of Tania based on Anaïs and Thaïs.
Means "we are good, we are blessed" in Shona.
Means "we have been blessed" in Shona.
Alternate transcription of Thai ธนกิจ (see Thanakit).
Alternate transcription of Thai ธนากร (see Thanakon).
Alternate transcription of Thai ธนากร (see Thanakon).
Alternate transcription of Thai ธนกฤต (see Thanakrit).

Variant of Tanimara. Taken from the 1970 American Western film Chisum, starring John Wayne as John Chisum. Some sources claim this name means 'lonely north wind' in Comanche or Cherokee, though no evidence supporting this meaning can be found.
Means "rays of the sun" in Malagasy.

Transferred use of the name of the Tanami Desert, a desert in northern Australia, situated in the Northern Territory and Western Australia. The name itself is an Anglicized form of Warlpiri Chanamee "never die", referring to certain rock holes in the desert which were said never to run dry.
Means "pearlaceous, pearly" in Mongolian, derived from тана (tana) meaning "mother-of-pearl, nacre".

Tanandra was apparently invented and has no meaning. It may be a junction names such as Tanya + Sandra, or a composition from the parent's name, for example, Tancred + Leandra. It can be inspired by other names with Andra, as Cassandra for example. Anyway, there are many girls born possibly in the 80 bearing that name, such as Tanandra Assmann (Candelaria, RS), which was one of the candidates finalists in the Miss Rio Grande do Sul in 2012.
Alternate transcription of Thai ธนภพ (see Thanaphop).
Alternate transcription of Thai ธนภพ (see Thanaphop).
Alternate transcription of Thai ธนภพ (see Thanaphop).

Latinized form of the Etruscan name Thanchvil which meant "gift of Thana 1", composed of the name of the goddess Thana and cvil meaning "gift". This was the name of the wife of Lucius Tarquinius Priscus, the fifth king of Rome in the 7th century BC. In modern times it was borne by prima ballerina Tanaquil Le Clercq (1929-2000).
Variant of Tanaquil used in Edmund Spenser's poem The Faerie Queene (1590), where it belongs to a daughter of Oberon who becomes the fairy queen Gloriana.
Combination of the phonetic elements ta, nay and sha in a similar vein to Tanisha.
Combination of ta, nay and Asia 1, similarly to Anasia.
From Kazakh таң (tan) meaning "dawn, daybreak" and ат (at) meaning "horse".

Tanausis was a legendary king of the Goths, according to Jordanes's Getica (5.47). The 19th-century scholar Alfred von Gutschmid assigned his reign to 1323 BC - 1290 BC. According to the Getica, he was the Gothic king who halted the advance of the Egyptian armies of the Egyptian king Sesostris (whom Jordanes calls Vesosis). At a battle on the banks of the river Phasis, Tanausis routed the Egyptian king who had already conquered the Ethiopians and the Scythians. The Getica states that Tanausis then pursued the Egyptians all the way back to the banks of the Nile, where the mighty river and the fortifications dissuaded him from slaying Sesotris "in his own land". The territory Tanausis had conquered in Asia was then bestowed upon his close friend Sornus, king of the Medes. Some of Tanausis' followers remained in the conquered lands, and Jordanes cites Pompeius Trogus as saying these were the origin of the Parthians, stating that in the Scythian language "Parthi" means "deserter" (5.48).Following his death, Jordanes writes that the Goths worshipped Tanausis as a god.

An ancient Turkish name derived from the Old Turkic root taŋ meaning "astonishment, wonder, miracle" and the old adjectival suffix +sUḳ. Rather than meaning "dawn water," Tansuğ directly translates to "you are a miracle, a supernatural beauty." It symbolizes rare excellence and an extraordinary gift that leaves onlookers speechless with admiration.The name is iconically embodied by Sabiha Tansuğ (1933–2023), the monumental Turkish ethnologist, art historian, and collector. She dedicated her life to preserving Anatolian cultural heritage and traditional costumes. Her international acclaim was so profound that her portrait in traditional headdress was minted onto the official Turkish 50 Kuruş coin in 1971, cementing her as the first non-political woman to achieve such an honor in the history of the Republic, standing alongside writer Fatma Aliye Hanım who appears on the 50 Lira banknote.

Transferred use of the surname Tapley, which was derived from the name of Tapeley, a place in Devon, England; according to the toponymist Eilert Ekwall, the place name means "wood where pegs are obtained" from Old English tæppa "peg" and leah "wood, clearing".
Derived from the Georgian noun თაფლი (tapli) meaning "honey".
Alternate transcription of Bengali তপন (see Tapan).
Alternate transcription of Bengali তাপসী (see Tapasi).
Alternate transcription of Bengali তাপসী (see Tapasi).

column12: From 竜 (tap) meaning "dragon" combined with 兵 (pei) meaning "war machine, soldier". Other kanji combinations are permissible.
Means "her daughter" in Hattian. The Hattian name for the minor Hittite goddess Mezulla.
Tapputi, or Tapputi-Butt, is the earliest known chemist. She distilled and mixed perfumes and was overseer of the royal palacein Babylonian Mesopotamia ca. 1200 BCE.

Ultimately from Egyptian ta-pȝ-šȝy meaning "she of Shai", in Coptic derived from the possessive feminine article ⲧⲁ- (ta-) combined with the name of the god Shai. Alternatively, the second element could derive directly from the word ϣⲁⲓ (šai) meaning "fate, destiny". This was also the name of an Egyptian goddess worshipped in Kellis, a village in ancient Upper Egypt. She may have been a local woman deified after death.
Alternate transcription of Thai ทับทิม (see Thapthim).
Derived from tapu meaning "sacred" and ari'i meaning "king".
Means "very sacred" in Tahitian. Combination of Tahitian tapu "forbidden" and nui "big".
Means "pious of the religion" from تقي (taqi) meaning "devout, pious" and دين (dīn) meaning "religion"
Alternate transcription of Arabic تقية (see Taqiya), as well as the Indonesian form.
Alternate transcription of Arabic تقية (see Taqiya), as well as the Indonesian form.

Combination of the phonetic elements ta and quan.
Combination of the phonetic element ta and the name Quasha. It can be spelled TaQuasha, Ta'Quasha or Taquasha.
From Old Norse *táR meaning "tough, resistant, enduring".
Feminine form of Taracius. Taracia was one of the Vestal Virgins.
Tahitian form of Catherine, and its diminutive Trina, or derived from tara meaning "thorn, peak" or "enchantment", and ina meaning "sharp" in Tahitian.
French form of Tarasios via Tarasius.

Means "hope" in Swahili. It is a verb, not a noun, and means "to hope, to wish for". It is not used as a name in Africa but was part of the Afrocentric African American naming culture of the 70s that borrowed from various African words.
" Star; pupil of eye; meteor; asterisk; rescuing; protector; Name of wife of lord Brihaspati "
Meaning Honey bee or liquid; famous bearer of this name is Taral Hicks.
Samoan form of Carolina and Catalina.
An elaboration of Tara 1 using the popular name suffix lyn. Taralyn was a minor character on the TV show "Legend of the Seeker."

This name is from a character by J. R. R. Tolkien, present in the book The Fall of Númenor: And Other Tales from the Second Age of Middle-Earth (2022) edited by Brian Sibley. Tar-Amandil is the third king of Númenor, from the line of Blessed Eärendel. The name Tar-Amandil comes from the Quenya words Tar ("high", used in the names of kings), Aman (the Quenya name of the Blessed Realm) and -dil ("friend, lover"). The name has the meaning of "king devoted to the Blessed Realm", or "lover of the Blessed Realm".
Given for females who are born during the day.
From Sanskrit तरण (taraṇa) meaning "crossing over, passing, overcoming" combined with दीप (dīpa) meaning "lamp, light".
Alternate transcription of Persian ترانه (see Taraneh).
From Sanskrit तरण (taraṇa) meaning "crossing over, passing, overcoming" and जिति (jiti) meaning "victory, conquering".
Alternate transcription of Punjabi Gurmukhi ਤਰਨਜੀਤ (see Taranjeet).
From Sanskrit तरण (taraṇa) meaning "crossing over, passing, overcoming" combined with ज्योतिस् (jyotis) meaning "light, brightness".
The meaning of "tarannom" is "melodey" in persian.
From Sanskrit तरण (taraṇa) meaning "crossing over, passing, overcoming" combined with प्रीति (prīti) meaning "pleasure, joy, love".
From the name of the island in the Outer Hebrides of Scotland. The name of the island is derived from Old Norse meaning "Taran's island" (see Ternan.)
Taranza is an antagonist first appearing in Kirby: Triple Deluxe. He serves as second-in-command to Queen Sectonia, the main villain of Kirby: Triple Deluxe.
Means "lord of stars" or "husband of Tara 2", derived from Sanskrit तारा (tara) meaning "star" and पति (pati) meaning "lord, husband".
Khanty and Mansi form of Proskovya.
Georgian form of Tarasios (see Taras). As for Russia, Tarasi is a variant transcription of Tarasiy there.
Portuguese form of Tarasios via Tarasius.
Italian and Spanish form of Tarasios via Tarasius.
Latinized form of Tarasios. Saint Tarasius (c. 730 – 25 February 806) was the Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 25 December 784 until his death on 25 February 806.
Russian and Ukrainian form of Tarasios.
Belarusian and Russian feminine form of Taras.
Alternate transcription of ธาราทิพย์ (see Tharathip).
Means "beam of light" or "reflection" in Malagasy.
Means "burning peak" in Māori. Mount Tarawera is a volcano in New Zealand. Tarawera also refers a type of fern known as Pellaea rotundifolia.
taraz said as trz in punjabi means music composition .
Meaning unknown. Notable bearer of this name is St Tarbula. She was martyred when King Shapur II of Persia accused her of practicing witchcraft, that caused the queen to fall ill.
In Etruscan mythology, Tarchon and his brother, Tyrrhenus, were cultural heroes who founded the Etruscan League of twelve cities, the Dodecapoli.
Means "a light coming from darkness" in Turkish.
A fictional character created by J.R.R. Tolkien.

The name Tarfa has a primary meaning related to a specific type of tree(Tamarisk tree), often associated with beauty and growth.Secondary MeaningThe root of the name also carries a related, abstract meaning:Rarity/Novelty: In some contexts, the root tarf can relate to something rare, novel, or excellent, though the most common and direct association is the Tamarisk tree.Historically it was originally a male name, with a slightly different Arabic spelling. However, it shifted into a female name.
Hellenized form of the name Targī̆tavah, meaning "possessing the strength of Tarkā". This name is borne by a prominent figure in Scythian mythology, whom the Greeks equated with Herakles.
Meaning unknown. This has been the first name of several notable Filipino figures, such as Princess Tarhata Kiram and Princess Tarhata Alonto-Lucman
Combination of the prefix Ta with the name Rhonda.
Means "worshipper of Tarhunz" in Luwian. This was the name of a 14th-century king of Arzawa who penetrated the Hittite empire, then weakened by invasions of the Kaška peoples.

Means "ask for or seek love" in Ijaw.

Meaning as of yet unknown. This name is not to be confused with the similar-looking name Darejan, which is not only feminine, but was also invented in the 12th century.A notable bearer of this name was saint Tarichan of Georgia († 693).
Form of Tariel with the nominative suffix, used in Georgian when the name is written stand-alone.
Diminutive of Tariel and its short form Taro.
Alternate transcription of Thai ธาริณี (see Tharini).
Invented name inspired by rhyming names like Marion and Larion.
Means "love has been given to me" in Ijaw.
Meaning “look; behold” or “look forth”, names with similar meanings include Onai and Ringai.

Tariso is similar to the name Tariro in that it has the same meaning..."hope"shona has many dialects and some when saying that they anticipate something they say"takataririra" whilst others say"takatarisira"so the difference is an s or an ra few tariso's can be found on facebook but the meaning has never been defined.it probably came about as a result of families trying to find a unique name apart from tariro which is a very common name..the name tariso is used as a surname in other countries as well not in africa..
A blend of the name Tara 1 with a name that ends in -issa, such as Clarissa and Marissa. Also, in some cases, this name is a modern variant of Theresa.

From Tarita tumi, Tahitian translation of biblical phrase 'Talitha cumi', meaning "little girl, arise" in Aramaic. This name was borne by Tahitian actress Tarita Teriipaia, born Tarita Tumi Teri'ipaia, who became the third wife of Marlon Brando. Tarita portrayed the character of Maimiti in the film Mutiny on the Bounty (1962).
Invented name, likely based on the phonetic element ta and the giben name Darius.
Modern coinage combining the phonetic elements ta, ry and ya, possibly based on Tara 1 and the popular -iyah suffix sound (found in names such as Mariah, Sariyah, Nariyah and Taniya 1).
Dialectal variant of Torgeir found in Telemark and Aust-Agder.
Short form of Tarquin used in Rin Chupeco's young adult novel 'The Girl from the Well' and its sequel, 'The Suffering'.

Name of the title character in Henry Williamson's novel 'Tarka the Otter' (1927) and the subsequent movie adaptation (1979). In the book the (male) character's name is said to mean "wandering as water"; perhaps the author based it on Welsh dwrgi "otter", literally "water dog", or on its Cornish cognate dowrgi.This is occasionally used as a masculine and feminine given name, and was most notably borne by Tarka Cordell (1966-2008), a British musician, writer, record producer, and sometime model. This also coincides with a Sanskrit word meaning "reasoning, logic".
Possibly deriving from the Iranic element tark ("to turn"). This was the name of a Scythian goddess who was worshipped at a shrine on the Tarkhankut peninsula.
Means "deck strap (for a kayak)" in Greenlandic.

In the case of the Turkish popstar Tarkan, this name comes from a Turkish comic book character in the 1960's, which in turn comes from the name of an ancient Khazar king. Also, it was the title of a high-ranking military rank.The meaning is "bold and strong"
From an ancient military title used by Mongol, Turkic and Iranian leaders, which is of uncertain origin. In the Mongol Empire this title granted exemption from taxation.
Derived from tālei meaning "wonderful, valuable" in Fijian, or possibly derived from Indo-Fijian name Tarla.
From Sanskrit तर (tara) meaning "crossing, passing over" combined with लोक (loka) meaning "world, realm, earth".
Tar'mach was a Khazar general, active in the Arab–Khazar Wars of the 720s and 730s CE.
From the Arabic surname الترمذي (at-Tirmidhī) borne by 9th-century Sunni scholar Muhammad ibn Isa al-Tirmidhi. The name indicates that he came from the city of Termez in present-day Uzbekistan.
Middle English (originally northern English dialect) from Old Norse tjǫrn.An infrequent modern English word meaning a small mountain lake.

Name of a fictional male character by Dutch author Tonke Dragt. Prince Tarne is the main protagonist of a children's story titled "Het was maar een droom - De geschiedenis van prins Tarne" ("It was just a dream - The history of prince Tarne"), which is one of several short stories in the book "Het gevaarlijke venster en andere verhalen" (Tonke Dragt, 1979)
Means "surf, wave, breaker" in Kaurna. The original form of Tahnee.
Derives from Australian Aboriginal name Tarni. It could also be a diminutive of the Tania or Tara 1, or possibly a variation of Marnie.
Alternate transcription of Punjabi Gurmukhi ਤਰਨਜੀਤ (see Tarnjeet).

column3: 太郎太, 田郎太, 太朗太, 田朗太(Japanese Kanji)|たろうた(Japanese Hiragana)|タロウタ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name combines 太 (ta, tai, futo.i, futo.ru) meaning "big around, plump, thick" or 田 (den, ta) meaning "rice field/paddy" & 郎 (ryou, rou, otoko) meaning "son" or 朗 (rou, aki.raka, hoga.raka) meaning "bright, cheerful, clear, melodious, serene" with 太.This name is very rarely given to boys, if given at all.

column3: タロウイチ(Japanese Katakana)|たろういち(Japanese Hiragana)|太郎一, 太朗一, 太郎市, 太朗市, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 太 (ta) meaning "thick, big", 郎 (rou) meaning "son" combined with 一 (ichi) meaning "one". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 太朗子, 太郎子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 太 (ta) meaning "thick, big", 朗 (rou) meaning "bright, clear" or 郎 (rou) meaning "son" combined with 子 (shi) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.

In Roman mythology, Tarpeia, daughter of the Roman commander Spurius Tarpeius, was a Vestal Virgin who betrayed the city of Rome to the Sabines at the time of their women's abduction for what she thought would be a reward of jewelry. She was instead crushed to death by Sabine shields and her body cast from the southern cliff of Rome's Capitoline Hill, thereafter called after her the Tarpeian Rock (Rupes Tarpeia).

MEANING : to satisfy oneself, be satiated, pleasure, satisfaction Usage : Sanskrit, Indian, Tamil, Telugu, Nepali, Sinhalese, Hindi, Sikh, Punjabi, Kannada, Marathi, Gujarati, Assamese, Kannada, malayalam, Bengali, Fijian, Hinduism
Alternate spelling of Tarĸik, an Inuit god of the moon. A moon of Saturn was named after him.
Italian, Galician and Spanish form of Tarquin.
From Old Norse tár meaning "tear, tear-drop".
From Old Norse *tarr, found in Old Norse svíntarr meaning "boar".
Elaboration of Rhonda using the prefix Ta-.
A character from the American TV show "Legend of Korra" bears this name.
Meaning "worshipper of Ahura Mazda" in Persian.

Brother of King Bagdemagus of Gorre and nephew of King Urien.Tarsan joined Arthur’s war against King Meliadus of Lyonesse. He engaged in combat with Melian, Meliadus’s nephew, and the two knights killed each other.
Means "got after a long desire" in Punjabi.
The wife of Licorant and mother of Enide.She lived with her husband in the town of Laluth until Erec married Enide and gave them two castles.
Probably an invented name inspired by Marsha.
Feminine form of Tarsicius. This name was borne by a saint from the 7th century AD.
Italian, Galician and Spanish form of Tarsicius.

This name entered the Latin language via Greek Tarsisi. Tarsisi is what the ancient Greek city of Tarsos was called at times; the city's name was the hellenized form of Tarsa, which is what the city's first settlers - the Hittites - called it. The original Hittite meaning is uncertain, though it may have been named after their god Tarku. Additionally, it should be noted that the ancient Greeks also used Tarsisi for an other city. In that case, it was the hellenized form of Semetic Tarshish, which was a city in southern Spain that the Greeks also called Tartessos. A known bearer of the name Tarsicius was Saint Tarsicius, who lived in the 3rd century AD.
Variant of Trasilla. A known bearer is Brazilian painter Tarsila do Amaral (1886-1973).
Of uncertain origin and meaning; theories include a derivation from the same root as Tarsicius.
Of uncertain origin and meaning; theories include a derivation from the same root as Tarsicius. This name was borne by an aunt of Pope Gregory I, who herself is venerated as a saint.
German form and Latin variant of Tarsicius.
From Basque tartaroa "Tatar". Tartalo is a one-eyed giant very similar to the Greek Cyclops that Odysseus faced in Homer's Odyssey.
Probably a feminine form of Tartaros, may have been an epithet of Gaia.

Latinized form of Greek Τάρταρος (Tartaros), of uncertain etymology. In Greek mythology, Tartarus was the name of both a primordial deity and the cosmic pit beneath the earth he embodied where threats to the gods were confined, later being considered an extension of the realm of the dead where condemned souls were sent to.
A great giant slain by Morholt. Morholt took his sword, which he later gave to Tristan.
Means "luck, blessing, good fortune" in Batak.
From Javanese taruna meaning "young, youth, boy", ultimately from Sanskrit तरुण (taruṇa).
Taruto (aka Tart) is the name of a major character in Tokyo Mew Mew (masculine use), and the titular character of Magical Nyan Nyan Taruto (feminine use).
Taruu Masing is the name of the ancestor of the Tranan Atayal tribe
The name of a Gaulish god depicted as a bull with three cranes on his back.
Means "constellation" in Burmese, ultimately from Sanskrit तारक (taraka).
Variant of Terrell or Darryl. This name was used by American musician Toriano Adaryll 'Tito' Jackson, a member of the Jackson 5, for his son born 1975.
Spanish and Greek form of Tarzan.
Means "love" when used as a name. Literally means "liver," the organ thought to be the seat of emotions, much like the heart's role in Western cultures.
From the Hausa ta meaning “of” and sallā̀ meaning "prayer, religious holiday”.
Means "be tolerant, show goodwill" in Arabic.
Alternate transcription of Thai ทัศนัย (see Thatsanai).
Alternate transcription of Thai ทัศนีย์ (see Thatsani).
Possibly means "evening" in Romani, deriving from the Wallachian word searla. Alternatively it is a variant of Tasorlo.
Means "imagination", from the Arabic تصور (taṣawwara) meaning "to imagine".
It probably derives from the hebrew "tach", meaning "crown".
From the Turkish taş meaning "rock, gem" and Azerbaijani dəmir meaning "iron".

Most likely a combination of words taş (from Old Turkic taş and Proto-Turkic *tāş) meaning "stone, rock, gem" and Demir, which is also used as a name, (from Old Turkic témir and Proto-Turkic *tämür) meaning "iron."This name is rarely given to boys, if given at all.

Taseen is a Quranic name for boys. Chapter 27 of the Quran (known as Surat an-Naml) begins with Taseen, just like Chapter 36 begins with Yaseen and chapter 20 starts with Taha. The meaning of these words are not known, but since they are in the Quran in the beginning of Quranic chapters, people use them as names.
Possibly from the Turkic word for stone, tash. This was the name of a demon in The Chronicles of Narnia. He is the chief god of the Calormenes.
Exact meaning unknown. Some sources claim it is derived from the Hindi word taashan "style".
Combination of prefix Ta- with Shane.
Perhaps a blend of the phonetic element ta with Rashad.
Combination of the popular prefix ta with the name Shawn.
From Kyrgyz таш (tash) meaning "stone, rock" and болот (bolot) meaning “steel”.
Likely an invented name, possibly an elaboration of Tasha influenced by Tamika.
Sinhala variation of Tashan (तशन) which is of Hindi origin meaning style, flair, attitude, or swagger.
Altered form of Tatiana, influenced by Tasha.
Meaning “we have been brave or resilient”.
Meaning "what has made us be resilient", a shorter form of the name is Takashinga.
This was a name given to a cross between a demon, Tash and a god, Aslan to trick citizens into thinking they were one, in the novel the Last Battle, by C.S. Lewis.
Variant form of Tašmetu, also translated as "the lady who listens".
Means, "Tashmetu is queen", from Tashmetum (an Akkadian goddess) and šarrat, meaning "queen"
From таш (tash) meaning "rock, gem" combined with the given name Mokhammat
Combination of the popular prefix ta with the name Shonda. It can be spelled TaShonda or Tashonda.
Alternate transcription of Bengali তাশরিক (see Tashrique).
the name "Tashvi" means calm and collected. In modern hindhi, it can also mean fat and irrigational.
Derived from татуси (tatusi) meaning "to keep deer".
Feminine given name for a royal Princess of a King or Queen.Also means flawless beauty and patience in life.
Means "handle (of a kayak paddle)" in Greenlandic.
Diminutive of Anastasia and its short form Taso.
this word is a Arabic word which in the religious book of Islam. The word meaning is unpredictable .

Transferred use of the surname Tasker. It could also be from the word itself. Famous bearers of the name were American officer Tasker H. Bliss (1853-1930) and Welsh Lord Justice of Appeal Sir Tasker Watkins (1918-2007).
Derived from Uzbek taslim meaning "surrender" and oy meaning "moon".
From the place name Tasmania. The name was first used as the pen name of Australian novelist, journalist and feminist Jessie Couvreur (1848-1897), who was raised and educated in Tasmania.

Transferred use of the surname Tasman. Used in honour of the 17th century Dutch explorer Abel Tasman, who claimed the island now known as Tasmania in 1642. Many places in Australia and New Zealand are named after him, most notably the Tasman Sea which lies between the two countries.
Ancient Mesopotamian goddess of wisdom and sexual attractiveness.
Ancient Mesopotamian feminine given name meaning "Tašmetu is queen". This was the name of a wife of the ancient Assyrian king Sennacherib.
Possibly means "Tashmetu is our comrade", deriving from the goddess Tashmetum, and the Akkadian elements tappa-um ("comrade") and ni ("our").
Likely a variant of Tamsin inspired by the sound of Jasmine.
Means "gift from God" or "little flower" in Arabic and Persian contexts.
Short form of Anastasia, which tends to be used as an independent name rather than as an unofficial nickname.
Variant of Tayson, possibly inspired by names like Mason and Cason.
Means "my sister", derived from the possessive feminine article ⲧⲁ- (ta-) combined with ⲥⲱⲛⲓ (soni) "sister".
From Arabic سعد (sa'd) meaning "fortune, good luck" combined with the Tamazight feminine prefix ⵜⴰ (ta) and suffix ⵜ (t).
Alternate transcription of Thai ทัศนัย (see Thatsanai).
Alternate transcription of Thai ทัศนีย์ (see Thatsani).

Diminutive of Anastasia. This name belonged to an 8th-century Lombard queen, the Roman wife of Ratchis.'Commonly found in Greece. It is the main nickname deriving from Anastasia. Today, most women prefer to keep their full name, but in the past, most women named Anastasia would choose to be called Tassia.'

Diminutive of Tasso. The Blessed Tassilo III (c. 741 – c. 796) was duke of Bavaria from 748 to 788, the last of the house of the Agilolfings. Modern-day bearers include Tassilo Thierbach (1956-), a German former pair skater, and Prince Tassilo Preslavski of Bulgaria (2002-).

column3: 太助, 太介, 多助, 助, 祐, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|たすけ(Japanese Hiragana)|タスケ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Combination of a ta kanji, like 太 meaning "plump, thick" or 多 meaning "many, much," and 助け (suke) meaning "help," the element also written as 介, 祐, and so on. The second kanji can also be used on its own, from 助け (tasuke), extended from suke with 手 (ta), the combining form of te meaning "hand," now the usual form.One fictional bearer of this name is Isshin Tasuke (一心 太助), considered the epitome of the Edokko (child of Edo), making appearances in novels, plays, film, television and other media.

column3: 助, 佑, 祐, 佐, 輔, 丞, 匡, 侑, 資, 右, 翼, 亮, 佑来, 翼空, 侑久, 祐玖, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|たすく(Japanese Hiragana)|タスク(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From the verb 助く (tasuku) meaning "to help, save, rescue," from earlier suku with prefixation of 手 (ta), the combining form of te meaning "hand." It can also be combined with a ku kanji, like 来 meaning "arrival," 空 meaning "sky," 久 meaning "long time" or 玖, referring to the numeral nine in legal documents.Bearers of this name include physician-scientist and immunologist Tasuku Honjo (本庶 佑) (1942-), the 2018 Nobel Prize winner in Physiology or Medicine, and actor Tasuku Emoto (柄本 佑) (1986-).
Diminutive of Anastasia and its short form Taso.
From Lakota Tȟašúŋke meaning "his horse". This is found in Tȟašúŋke Witkó, the original Lakota name of the Oglala leader known to the English-speaking world as Crazy Horse (c.1842-1877).
Hokkien Chinese form and Cantonese Chinese variant transcription of 達 (see Da and Daat).Other characters combinations are also possible.
Means "what wrong have we done?" in Shona.
Son of Pharien and brother of Anguin. He was raised by the Lady of the Lake and knighted by Sir Lionel.
Diminutive of Tata 2, which is a short form of several names.

Of Australian Aboriginal origin (Pintupi, to be precise), the meaning of this name is not yet known to me at the moment. A known bearer of this name was Tatali Nangala (b. between circa 1925 to 1928, d. 1999 or 2000), an Australian Aboriginal painter.
Means "it is full" or "the belly" in Inuktikut. Name borne by an Inuit interpreter that worked with John Franklin on two of his Arctic expeditions.
Perhaps a variant of Tatiana or a combination of the name prefix Ta- and Tanya.

the traditional Japanese furnace used for smelting iron and steel. The word later also came to mean the entire building housing the furnace.Notable bearers of the name include Tatara from the shoujo manga Basara, as well as Tatara from the anime and manga Tokyo ghoul.This name is rarely given to girls, if given at all.
Variant of the Georgian name Dadash.

Derived from the Old English elements tāt "glad, cheerful" and beorht "bright". This was the name of an 8th century Anglo-Saxon saint, abbot and contemporary of Bede, who was appointed the second Abbot of Ripon by his relative Wilfrid.

When written as ტატე, this name is a short form of Estate. It is now also used as an independent name.When written as თათე, Tate is a short form of Tadeoz. A known bearer is the Assyrian monastic missionary and saint Tadeoz Stepantsmindeli (6th century AD), who was also known as Tate Mamebeli in Georgian. He was one of the Thirteen Assyrian Fathers and was originally from Antioch on the Orontes. Eventually he travelled to Caucasian Iberia, where he spent the remainder of his life. He founded the Stepantsminda Monastery near what is now the town of Kaspi in the Georgian region of Shida Kartli.

column3: 建昭, 建章, 建明, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 建 (tate) meaning "build, establish, erect, found" combined with 昭 (aki) meaning "shining", 章 (aki) meaning "chapter; section" or 明 (aki) meaning "bright". Other combinations of kanji characters are also possible.

column3: 健彦, 建彦, 楯彦, 盾彦, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 健 (tate) meaning "healthy, strong", 建 (tate) meaning "build, establish, erect, found", 楯 (tate) meaning "shield" or 盾 (tate) meaning "shield, escutcheon" combined with 彦 (hiko) meaning "boy, prince". Other kanji combinations are also possible.
Means "Every Wind" or "Reaches for the Wind" in Dakota. This was the name adopted by Ellen Simmons, the mother of Dakota musician, activist and writer Zitkála-Šá (legal name Gertrude Simmons Bonnin).
Blend of Taylor and Katelyn, or a combination of Tate and the popular name suffix lyn. Also compare Taelyn.

Means "risen land" or "exalted earth", and also refers to the silt of the Nile River.In Egyptian mythology he was the primordial mound, and as a primeval chthonic deity he was associated with creation. He was viewed as the source of food and viands, divine offers, all good things", as his realms deep beneath the earth were "from which everything emerges". His father was the creator god Khnum who fashioned him on a potter's wheel using Nile mud, granting him the titles "creator and mother who gave birth to all gods" and "father of all the gods". Eventually he became an aspect of Geb.
One of the many names of LORD GAUTAM BUDDHA.

The meaning is unfortunately unknown to me. This was the name of a Welsh saint from the 5th century AD; sources conflict over whether the saint was a male or a female. In the case of the latter, the saint was thought to be a daughter of a King of Gwent.
Meaning uncertain. It is (was?) borne by Tathi bint Mishan al Faisal al Jarbah, one of the 30 or so wives of King Abdullah of Saudi Arabia (1924-2015).

Diminutive or short form of Tatiana, Tatiane, Tatjana and Tatyana. For Georgian, this only applies when the name is written as ტატი.When Tati is written as თათი in Georgian, it is a diminutive or short form of the common feminine names Tamar, Tamta, Tatia and Tatuli.Also compare the related names Tata 2 and Tato.
Feminine form of Tatius. A bearer of this name was the wife of Numa Pompilius, a king of Rome from the 7th century BC.
English and Friulian form of Tatianus. This name was borne by a Christian writer and theologian from the 2nd century AD.
Derived from Attic Greek τάττω (tatto) meaning "to place in order, to arrange, to form". This name is not to be confused with the Latin name Tatiana.
Possibly a combination of Tatiana and a name ending in -ele, such as Luciele or Gabriele 2.
Diminutive of Tata 2, Tate 1, Tati and Tato, which are all short forms of various names.This name is more often used on women than on men.
From Thai ตติย (tatiya) meaning "third" and อนุช (anuch) meaning "younger sister".
Bulgarian/Estonian/Albanian version of Tatyana or Tanja. In Switzerland the name spread thanks to its popularity in Germany.
From the name of the fairy companion character from the video game The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask.
From Bashkir татлы (tatlï) meaning "sweet" and банат (banat) meaning "girl".
From Bashkir татлы (tatlï) meaning "sweet" and Persian بانو (banu) meaning "lady".
From Sino-Vietnamese 必然 (tất nhiên) meaning "inevitable, certain".
Derived from the Old English elements tāt "glad, cheerful" and noð "boldness, daring". This was the name of a 9th century Bishop of Rochester.

When written as ტატო, this name is a short form of Anton, Estate and Tatash (masculine) and Tatiana (feminine).But when written as თათო, Tato is a short form of the rare masculine name Tadeoz and the common feminine names Tamar, Tamta, Tatia and Tatuli.Also compare the related names Tata 3 and Tate 1.
Derived from Slavic tata "father" combined with Slavic mir "peace". A known bearer of this name was Tatomir Anđelić (1903-1993), a Serbian mathematician and expert in mechanics.
Means "large deer" in Lakota. From the Lakota tȟáȟča 'deer' and tȟáŋka (ton'-kah) 'to be large, big, great'.
Possibly means "he passes by" or "is removed". Name of a Wampanoag chief during King Philip's War.
Alternate transcription of Thai ธาตรี (see Thatri).
Alternate transcription of Thai ธาตรี (see Thatri).
Alternate transcription of Thai ทัศนัย (see Thatsanai).
Alternate transcription of Thai ทัศนีย์ (see Thatsani).
Alternate transcription of Thai ทัศนีย์ (see Thatsani).
From the Awajún name for a kind of parrot.

column3: たつ(Japanese Hiragana)|タツ(Japanese Katakana)|起, 健, 建, 多津, 達, 辰, 立, 竜, 龍, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 起 (tatsu) meaning "rouse, wake up, get up", 健 (tatsu) meaning "healthy, strong", 建 (tatsu) meaning "build", 多 (ta) meaning "many, much", 達 (tatsu) meaning "accomplished, reach, arrive, attain", 辰 (tatsu) meaning "sign of the dragon", 立 (tatsu) meaning "stand up, rise, set up, erect" or 竜 (tatsu) and 龍 (tatsu) both meaning "dragon" combined with 津 (tsu) meaning "haven, port, harbor, ferry". Other kanji or kanji combinations can form this name as well.It was primarily used as a feminine name before the Second World War (usually written phonetically). Nowadays, it's mainly used as a nickname for male names beginning with Tatsu-.

column3: 達明, 達昭, 達章, 達朗, 達昌, 達秋, 辰明, 龍明, 竜明, 立明, 建明, 樹明, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|たつあき(Japanese Hiragana)|タツアキ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From 達 (tatsu) meaning "reach, arrive, attain," 辰/龍/竜 (tatsu) meaning "dragon" (辰 referring to the fifth sign of the Chinese zodiac), 立 (tatsu) meaning "to stand, rise," cognate to 建 (tatsu) meaning "to build, erect," or 樹 (tatsu) meaning "tree" (in this case, related to 立 and 建), combined with あき (aki), related to brightness or opening with kanji including 明, 昭, 章, 朗 or 昌, or 秋 (aki) meaning "autumn."

column3: 竜朗, 龍彬, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|たつあきら(Japanese Hiragana)|タツアキラ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From 竜/龍 (tatsu) meaning "dragon" combined with Akira.This name is extremely rare.
From Japanese 辰(tatsu) meaning "dragon" combined with 赤(aka, ako) meaning "red". Other kanji combinations can form this name as well.

column3: タツエ(Japanese Katakana)|たつえ, たつへ(Japanese Hiragana)|たつ恵, たつ枝(Kanji/Hiragana)|竜依, 建愛 建衣, 多津英, 達恵, 辰江, 龍栄, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 竜 (tatsu) meaning "dragon" combined with 絵 (e) meaning "picture, painting, drawing, sketch". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 辰右衛門(Japanese Kanji)|たつえもん(Japanese Hiragana)|タツエモン(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From the Japanese kanji 辰 (tatsu) meaning "Dragon (zodiac sign)" combined with 右 (u) meaning "right", 衛 (e) meaning "defend, guard" and 門 (mon) meaning "gate".Other kanji combinations are possible.
Tatsugo means "dragon", "reach, arrive, attain, achieve, accomplish" and "five" in Japanese.A known bearer was the Japanese swimmer Tatsugo Kawaishi (1911-1945).

column3: 達 秀, 達英, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 達 (tatsu) meaning "achieve" combined with 秀 (hide) meaning "ear/head (of plant); point, tip" or 英 (hide) meaning "wisdom, brilliance." Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 竜彦, 龍彦, 建彦, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 竜, 龍 (tatsu) meaning "dragon" or 建 (tatsu) meaning "build, establish, erect, found" combined with 彦 (hiko) meaning "boy, prince". Other kanji combinations are also possible.Famous bearers of this name are Japanese professional baseball player of Korean descent Tatsuhiko Kinjō and former Japanese football player Tatsuhiko Kubo.

column3: たつひろ(Japanese Hiragana)|辰寛, 達弘, 立裕, 竜洋, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 達 (tatsu) meaning "achieve" combined with 大 (hiro) meaning "big, large, great". Other kanji combintions are usable.

column3: 龍久, 竜尚, 竜久, 振寿, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 龍 (tatsu) meaning "dragon" combined with 久 (hisa) meaning "long time". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 辰人, 龍一, 立等, 竜壱, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 達 (tatsu) meaning "achieve" combined with 侍 (hito) meaning "serve, wait upon, warrior samurai". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 達一, 辰一, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 達 (tatsu) meaning "plural marker" or 辰 (tatsu), referring to the Dragon, the fifth of the twelve Earthly Branches combined with 一 (ichi) meaning "one". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 太月, 汰月, 竜貴, 龍樹, 龍生, 龍輝, 立樹, 立生, 立輝, 竜樹, 竜生, 竜輝, 建樹, 建生, 建輝, 樹生, 樹輝(Japanese Kanji)|たつき(Japanese Hiragana)|タツキ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: As a unisex name, this name can be used as 太月, 汰月 or 竜貴 with 太 (ta, tai, futo.i, futo.ru) meaning "big around, plump, thick", 汰 (ta, tai, ogo.ru, nigo.ru, yona.geru) meaning "luxury, select", 月 (gatsu, getsu, tsuki) meaning "month, moon", 竜 (ryuu, ryou, rou, ise, tatsu) meaning "dragon, imperial" and 貴 (ki, tatto.i, tatto.bu, touto.i, touto.bu) meaning "esteem, honour, precious, prize, value."As a masculine name, it combines 龍 (ryuu, ryou, rou, tatsu) meaning "dragon, imperial", 立 (rittoru, ritsu, ryou, ta.chi-, ta.tsu, -ta.tsu, ta.te-, tate-, -ta.te, ta.teru, -ta.teru, -da.te, -da.teru) meaning "erect, rise, set up, stand up", 竜 or 建 (ken, kon, ta.tsu, ta.te, ta.teru, -da.te) meaning "build" with 樹 (ju, ki, tatsu) meaning "timber trees, wood", 生 (shou, sei, i.kiru, i.keru, -u, u.mare, o.u, ki, na.ru, ha.eru) meaning "birth, genuine, life" or 輝 (ki, kagaya.ku) meaning "gleam, radiance, shine, sparkle, twinkle."It can also combine 樹 with 生輝.Bearers of this name include actor Tatsuki Yoshioka (吉岡 竜輝) (2000-) and Takarazuka actress Tatsuki Kōju (香寿 たつき), born Takako Tomizaki (富崎 貴子) (1965-).One fictional (female) bearer of this name is Tatsuki Arisawa (有沢 竜貴), one of the characters in the popular manga and anime Bleach.

column3: 龍清, 竜清, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 竜/龍 (tatsu) meaning "dragon" and 清 (kiyo) meaning "pure". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: タツコ(Japanese Katakana)|たつ子(Kanji/Hiragana)|立子, 辰子, 起子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 立 (tatsu) meaning "stand, establish, set" or 龍/竜 (tatsu) meaning "dragon, imperial" and 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 達磨, 竜馬, 立真, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|たつま(Japanese Hiragana)|タツマ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 達 (tatsu) meaning "achieve, arrive at", 竜 (tatsu) meaning "dragon" or 立 (tatsu) meaning "stand up, rise, erect" combined with 磨 (ma) meaning "polish, grind", 馬 (ma) meaning "horse" or 真 (ma) meaning "real, genuine, true". Other combinations of kanji can form this name as well.

column3: 辰巳, 龍美, 巽, 龍実, 龍己, 龍巳, 龍海, 辰己, 辰美, 辰実, 立己, 竜己, 竜巳, 竜美, 達己, 達巳, 達海, 達見(Japanese Kanji)|たつみ(Japanese Hiragana)|タツミ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: As a unisex name, it can be used as either 辰巳 or 龍美 with 辰 (shin, jin, tatsu) meaning "sign of the dragon (5th sign of Chinese zodiac)", 巳 (shi, mi) meaning "sign of the snake/serpent (6th sign of Chinese zodiac)", 龍 (ryuu, ryou, rou, tatsu) meaning "dragon, imperial" and 美 (bi, mi, utsuku.shii) meaning "beauty, beautiful."As a masculine name, it can be used as 巽 (son, tatsumi) which means "southeast." It can also be used with combinations shown after 巽. The kanji used include 立 (rittoru, ritsu, ryuu, ta.tsu, ta.teru) meaning "erect, rise, set up, stand up", 竜 (ryuu, ryou, rou, ise, tatsu) meaning "dragon, imperial", 達 (tatsu, da, -tachi) meaning "accomplished, arrive, attain, reach", 実 (shitsu, jitsu, makotoni, mi, michi.ru, mino, mino.ru) meaning "reality, truth", 己 (ki, ko, onore, tsuchinoto, na, mi) meaning "self, serpent, snake", 海 (kai, umi, mi) meaning "ocean, sea" and 見 (ken, mi.eru, mi.seru, mi.ru) meaning "chances, hopes, idea, look at, opinion, see, visible."Bearers of this name include Japanese choreographer Tatsumi Hijikata (土方 巽) (1928-1986) and film director Tatsumi Kumashiro (神代 辰巳) (1927-1995).Tatsumi is also used as a surname.

column3: 立道, 龍道(Japanese Kanji)|たつみち(Japanese Hiragana)|タツミチ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From the Japanese kanji 立 (tatsu) meaning "rise; stand up" or 龍 (tatsu) meaning "dragon" combined with 道 (michi) meaning "way; road; path".Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 辰巳, 龍美, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 辰 (tatsu) meaning "sign of the dragon (5th sign of Chinese zodiac)", 巳 (mi) meaning "sign of the snake/serpent (6th sign of Chinese zodiac)", and 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 立順, 建由, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 立 (tatsu) meaning "erect, rise, set up, stand up" or 建 (tatsu) meaning "build" combined with 由 (nao) meaning "reason, cause, purpose, logic", 順 (nao) meaning "obedience, order, sequence" or 直 (nao) meaning "straight, direct". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 達成, 樹成, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 達 (tatsu) meaning "achieve" or 樹 (tatsu) meaning "timber trees, wood" combined with 成 (nari) meaning "to become". Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.

column3: 達朗, 達郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 達 (tatsu) meaning "plural marker" combined with 朗 (rou) meaning "bright, clear" or 郎 (rou) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations are possible.Famous bearer of this name is Japanese singer-songwriter and record producer Tatsuro Yamashita.

column3: 建, 立, 樹, 達, 竜, 龍, 健, 立琉, 竜流, 辰瑠, 辰留, 多鶴, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|たつる(Japanese Hiragana)|タツル(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From verbs 建つ (tatsu) meaning "to be erected/built​" or 立つ (tatsu) meaning "to stand, rise, stand up" or from 竜/龍 (tatsu) meaning "dragon" (likely cognate with 立つ), modelled to look like it came from a verb ending in -ru.Other kanji related to the verbs include 樹 meaning "tree" and 健 meaning "health," also including 達, with the on'yomi reading of tatsu meaning "reach, arrive, attain." They can also be suffixed with a ru kanji, like 瑠/琉, part of 瑠璃/琉璃 (ruri) meaning “lapis lazuli,” 流 meaning "current, flow" or 留 meaning "stop."For females, it is mainly written phonetically but it can also be written with a ta kanji, like 多 meaning "many, much," combined with 鶴 (tsuru), referring to the crane.

column3: 達憲, 竜憲, 龍憲, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 達 (tatsu) meaning "acheive" and 憲 (sada) meaning "basic law, constitution". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 達介, 竜介, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 達 (tatsu) meaning "achieve" combined with 介 (suke) meaning "help, assist". This name can also be formed from other combinations of kanji characters.

column3: たつと(Japanese Hiragana)|タツト(Japanese Katakana)|樹都, 建仁, 達渡, 龍斗, 立登, 辰翔, 竜豊, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 龍 (tastu) meaning "dragon" combined with 人 (to) meaning "person" combined with 斗 (to), which refers to a Chinese constellation. Other kanji combinations are also possible.

column3: 達俊, 辰俊, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 達 (tatsu) meaning "achieve" combined with 俊 (toshi) meaning "genius, excellence". Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.

column3: 達之, 達行, 龍雪, 龍之, 立之, 建之, 辰之, 竜之, 龍幸, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 達 (tatsu) meaning "reach, arrive, attain", 龍 or 竜 (tatsu) meaning "dragon", 立 (tatsu) meaning "stand up, rise", 建 (tatsu) meaning "build", or 辰 (tatsu) referring to the fifth sign of the Chinese zodiac combined with 之 (yuki), a possessive marker, 行 (yuki) meaning "row, line", 雪 (yuki) meaning "snow", or 幸 (yuki) meaning "happiness, good luck". Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.

column3: たつぞ(Japanese Hiragana)|辰蔵, 达三, 龍造, 立三, 达蔵, 竜造, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 竜 or 龍 (tatsu) meaning "dragon, imperial" and 蔵 (zo) meaning "storehouse, own, possess". Other kanji combinations can be used.
The nickname of the main girl (real name not known) in the fairy tale 'Tattercoats'.
Derived from Kyrgyz таттуу (tattuu) meaning "sweet, delicious" and Persian بی‌بی‌ (bibi) meaning "madam, lady, matron".
It is said to be the name of Good Witch of the North which was featured in the book of The Giant Horse of Oz by L. Frank Baum (1928).
Derived from Nivkh t'atn meaning "morning", used to indicate girls born in the morning.
Diminutive of Tata 2, Tati 1 and Tato, which are all short forms of various names.
From the Old Armenian word թաթուլ (tʿatʿul) meaning "paw". It has been in use since the 5th century.
Derivative of the Georgian given name Tatia. Due to close resemblance with Tata, the name is also often used as a nickname for women named Tamar.
Variant of Tatum, the spelling influenced by that of Autumn.
Diminutive of Tata 2, Tate 1, Tati and Tato, as it contains the Georgian diminutive suffix -უნა (-una).This name is more often used on women than on men.
Diminutive of Tata 2, Tati and Tato, as it contains the Georgian diminutive suffix -უშა (-usha).
Derived from the Old English elements tāt "glad, cheerful" and wine "friend".
Magyarised form of Tatyana. This is used exclusively as a spelling from Russian, and is not the form Hungarians use. For the Hungarian form of Tatyana, see Tatjána.
From Sino-Vietnamese 輳 (tấu) meaning "hubs of wheel, to converge around".
From Sino-Vietnamese 走 (tẩu) meaning "to run, flee" or 嫂 (tẩu) meaning "sister-in-law".
Allegedly a masculine form of Tauane.
King of the Tartars who served Emperor Filimenis of Constantinople. He joined Filimenis in a brief war against Arthur.
German-Yiddish form of Toiba. The name coincides with German Taube "dove".
From the Karachay-Balkar тау (tau) meaning "mountain" and the Turkish military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".
From the Karachay-Balkar тау (tau) meaning "mountain" and бий (biy) meaning "bey, prince".
From the Karachay-Balkar тау (tau) meaning "mountain" and Turkic can meaning "soul".
Belarusian name for Tautvilas of Polotsk and Lithuania.
Tongan given name and surname meaning "warrior" and "storm". Taufa is also a god in Tongan mythology.

Derived from the Tongan god of the land and sea, Taufa, and the Tongan town of ʻĀhau. This is the name of two Tongan royals, most notably Tāufaʻāhau Tupou IV who was given the name after Tāufa allegedly healed him of a childhood sickness.
Indonesian, Malay and Bengali form of Tawfiq.
Derived from Arabic توفيق الرحمن (tawfīq al-raḥmān) meaning "success of the merciful", from توفيق (tawfīq) meaning "success, good fortune" and رحمن (raḥman) meaning "merciful".
From taa meaning "we, us, our, together" and -ggu/-ka a suffix or verb indicating that the action is completed, or from togo?o meaning "maternal grandfather" in Paiute.
Alternate transcription of Bengali তাওহিদ (see Tawhid), as well as the Indonesian form.
Alternate transcription of Bengali তৌহিদা (see Tawhida).
From the Karachay-Balkar тау (tau) meaning "mountain" and улан (ulan) meaning "son".

Derived from Taulantii, which is the latinized form of Ταυλάντιοι (Taulantioi), the Greek name for a cluster of Illyrian tribes that lived on the Adriatic coast of Illyria (modern Albania). Their name is thought to be connected to the modern Albanian noun dallëndyshe (also tallandushe) meaning "swallow". However, according to ancient Greek mythology, these tribes derived their name from their eponymous ancestor Taulas.A notable bearer of this name is the Albanian professional soccer player Taulant Xhaka (b. 1991).
Precise meaning unknown. In Greek mythology, Taulas was one of the six sons of Illyrios.
Means "bracelet, wristband" in Samoan. The word taulima refers a style of native Samoan tattoo, this type of tattoo is situated on the arm or wrist.
A knight who is said to be one of those who started in the first and second quests of Lancelot.
Means "of the mountain" or "man from the mountains" in Karachay-Balkar.
Means "to bend down, settle" in Māori.
From taupea meaning "fight, war" in Tongan.
From the Karachay-Balkar тау (tau) meaning "mountain" and the Turkic title khan meaning "king, ruler". This was the name of a mythological musician, son of Apsat.
Alternate transcription of Urdu توقیر (see Tauqir).
Derived from Arabic توقير (tawqīr) meaning "respect, honour, esteem".
Feminine form of Taurus or variant of Tara 1.
Means "rope, cord (attached to a blade)", "settle", and "many ridges" in Maori.
Means "speak out, speak up!" in Shona.

From the English word that means "person born under the astrological sign Taurus" (see Taurus). Use of the name has been inspired by the American actor Taurean Blacque (1941-2022), known for his role on the police drama television series Hill Street Blues (1981-1987), who was born Herbert Middleton, Jr. and chose his stage name because his astrological sign was Taurus.
Means "enslaved" in Māori. A notable bearer of this name is the Maori politician Taurekareka Hēnare (1878-1940) from New Zealand.
Variant of Taurean, perhaps influenced by Lauren. Also see Torin.
20th-century coinage of uncertain origin and meaning. Theories include a derivation from Kauri or from Tarvo.
Brother of Arthur’s Sir Dodinel the Wild. He was a friend of Perceval’s hermit uncle, Trevrizent. Perceval came across one of his lances, abandoned near Treverizent’s abode, and took it.
Means "young woman of the forest" in Sindarin, from taur "forest" and riel "maiden". It was created by Peter Jackson for the last two films of 'The Hobbit' trilogy, for the name of an elf.
Diminutive of Taurus. This was the name of a Roman usurper from the 3rd century AD, and of a Frankish saint from the 5th century AD.

Derived from Ancient Greek ταῦρος (tauros) meaning "bull" combined with σθένος (sthenos) meaning "vigour, strength". This name was borne by a Greek tyrant from the 4th century BC, who ruled over Chalcis together with his brother Callias.
Indian and Bengali transcription of Tawsif.
Tautalus was a chieftain of the Lusitanians, a proto-Celtic tribe from western Hispania. He succeeded Viriathus in the final year of the Lusitanian War.

Means "(a) strong people", derived from Baltic tauta meaning "people, nation" (see Vytautas) combined with old Lithuanian gailas, which usually means "strong, potent" but has also been found to mean "sharp, jagged" as well as "angry, fierce, violent" and "miserable, sorrowful, remorseful". Also compare the modern Lithuanian noun galia meaning "power, might, force".
Means "to defend the people", derived from Baltic tauta meaning "people, nation" (see Vytautas) combined with Lithuanian ginti meaning "to defend, to protect".

Basically has the (more or less) figurative meaning of "hear the people" or "the people hear (everything)", derived from Baltic tauta meaning "people, nation" (see Vytautas) combined with the Lithuanian noun girdas meaning "rumour", which is ultimately derived from the Lithuanian verb girdėti meaning "to hear". Also compare the related Lithuanian noun gandas meaning "rumour, hearsay".

The first element of this name is derived from Baltic tauta meaning "people, nation" (see Vytautas). The second element is derived from the Lithuanian verb minėti meaning "to celebrate" as well as "to remember, to commemorate".

Derived from Baltic tauta meaning "people, nation" (see Vytautas) combined with the Lithuanian verb rimti meaning "to calm down, to quieten". It is related to the Lithuanian adjective ramus meaning "calm, quiet, peaceful" (see Ramūnas) and the Lithuanian noun ramybė meaning "tranquility, peace, quiet". As such, the meaning of this name is basically "(a) people of peace" and thus likely refers to a peaceful nation that has not seen war in a (very) long time.In other words: this given name is basically the same as Rimtautas, but with the name elements in different places.

The first element of this name is derived from Baltic tauta meaning "people, nation" (see Vytautas). The second element is either derived from the Lithuanian verb vaišinti meaning "to entertain, to treat" or from the related Lithuanian noun vaišės meaning "feast, party, celebration" as well as "entertainment".In other words: this given name is basically the same as Vaištautas, but with the name elements in different places.
Means "(the) people's rule", derived from Baltic tauta meaning "people, nation" (see Vytautas) combined with Baltic vald meaning "rule" (see Visvaldas).

Means "(the) people's hope", derived from Baltic tauta meaning "people, nation" (see Vytautas) combined with Baltic vil meaning "hope" (see Viltautas). In other words: this given name is basically the same as Viltautas, but with the name elements in different places.
Name of unknown meaning. A notable bearer is actress Tauvia Dawn.
Derived from the Samoan tava'e meaning "tropical bird" and sina meaning "white, grey, silver".
Means "resignation to God's will" in Uzbek.
Derived from Uzbek tavakkal meaning "resignation to God's will".

From the Portuguese surname Tavares. This name entered the American top 1000 rankings in the mid-1970s due to the R&B and soul musical group Tavares, a family musical group composed of five brothers surnamed Tavares, whose parents were of Cape Verdean descent.
Perhaps an altered form of Tavares.

Tavaziva means "We know them". This name is given in a feuding situation to say we know who the enemy is.
Short form of Gustav.Täve Schur is a cyclist from East Germany.

Means "whirlwind, twisting air" in Māori. Tāwhirimātea (tāwhiri-ma-te-a-rangi "whirling wind from the sky") is the god of storms.
Alternate transcription of Thai ทวีชัย (see Thawichai).

Means "otter tooth" in Mohawk.Ta'wineonawira is used for a fictional character in the fourth season of the TV series 'Outlander'. He is played by Trevor Carroll.

Uncertain etymology. In the case of the Pontic general Taxiles, it’s likely a hellenised form of an unknown name; in the case of the ruler of Takshasila (modern Taxila), a contemporary of Alexander the Great, it’s a Greek appellation derived from the name of the city he ruled over.
Derived from Proto-Celtic taxsi "soft" combined with Celtic magalo "prince."
Latinized form of Taximagulos. This name was borne by one of the four kings of Kent in 54 BC.

Modern Greek transcription of Late or Medieval Greek Ταξιώτης (Taxiotes). It is derived from ταξιώτης (taxiotes), a variant of ταξεώτης (taxeotes) meaning "officer of a magistrate, sergeant" i.e. some type of government official with police duties. In turn, the word likely consists of Greek τάξις (taxis) meaning "arrangement, ordering" and the Greek suffix -ιώτης (-iotes), which denotes origin as well as property. Also compare names like Panagiotes.In the Eastern Orthodox tradition, Taxiotis was a soldier from Carthage who lived in either the 5th century or the 9th century (probably the former, as Carthage was destroyed in 698 AD). He led a sinful life, but changed it for the better after having a near-death experience (NDE). Taxiotis is remembered on March 28th, though not necessarily as a saint (at least not in all branches of the Eastern Orthodox Church).
Old Persian form of the Old Median name Taxmaspāδa, meaning "(belonging to/possessing) a brave army", equivalent to Old Persian tahma "valiant, brave" and 𐎿𐎱𐎠𐎭 (spādaʰ) "army".
Diminutive of Taisiya and Thaïs influenced by the spelling of the name Tai.
Meaning "small little man" related to Tayaĝux̂ and Tayaĝuudax̂.
Combination of the popular elements tay and den.
From a place name in the island of Gran Canaria, located in the Canary Islands. Of uncertain origin, it is said to mean "pine tree"; presumably derived from Tayda.
Possibly means "having a foal tail", deriving from the Turkic element tay ("colt"). Name borne by a queen consort of the Mongol Horde.
