Possibly a modern form of the ancient Persian name Tahmasp (also see its Georgian form Tamaz). Alternatively, this name may be a contracted form of Taymuraz, which ultimately comes from the ancient Persian name Tahmuras.It should also be noted that there are several sources that state that this name is actually of Turkic origin, in which case it either means "firm, established" or "child whose life will not end" (i.e. a strong and healthy child). Also compare the Turkish noun tay meaning "colt, foal".

Tayran is the name of a champion fictional racehorse who won almost all races ran. His name is really Tayran Blow Away, but everyone calls him Tayran. He has gone through many things, such as he was stolen, he was marked to be stolen after the robbery, and he went through many life-threatening situations due to an evil horse robber, Sectir, and his friend, Claudia. To learn more about this courageous horse, read Forge A Champion, which may or may not be already published, by Arwen D. Ramsay.

Alternate transcription of Arabic تيسير (see Taysir). It is used as a feminine name in Sudan while it is typically masculine elsewhere. A literary bearer was the Jordanian writer and poet Tayseer Sboul (1939-1973).
Combination of the prefix tay and Shaun.
Either a transferred use of the surname Tayson or a combination of the phonetic elements tay and son.
Unisex variant of Tate. Also used as a diminutive of Tatum.

column12: Combination of a ta kanji, like 太 meaning "plump, thick," 多 meaning "many, much," 大 meaning "large, big" or 手, the bound form of te meaning "hand," and a yu kanji, such as 結 meaning "tie, bond" or 優 meaning "gentle, elegant."This name is rarely used.
Tayuya is a fictional character from the 'Naruto' manga series. It is spelled with Japanese 多 (ta) meaning "many", 由 (yu) meaning "cause, reason", and 也 (ya) meaning "also".

This very rare name is an exception to the rule that numerals are normally not allowed as part of the spelling of names in the United States. It's a creative rebus-like spelling of a slang intensive term for "tiny" found in the Southwestern United States. Most Americans would be familiar with terms like "teeny-tiny", "teensy-weensy", etc. "Teeninecy" is a rare variation of these that's found in the Deep South, and as a rare slang term it doesn't have a set spelling, with teeninesy, teeninetsy, teaninesea, and many others being found. Though a couple of other spellings have been used as names, T9C seems to be the most common in that role. It probably began in Texas in the 19th century as the earliest examples found so far are from that state.
From Tcham N'Toya-Zoa (born 3 November 1983 in Kinshasa, DR Congo),a French-Congolese footballer.
Tchelio is a magician and the king's (and prince's) protector in "L'amour des trois oranges", a 1921 satirical French-language opera by Sergei Prokofiev.
Means "helper" in Fe'Fe', spoken in Cameroon.

A cultural founder hero of the Bushmen. Tchue's deeds and transformations were 'many, many and not one'. He was a genius of fruit; also was he at different times a bird, an elephant, a fly, a lizard and even a water hole. He also brought the gift of fire to the people.
Meaning unknown. Tcliblento is a character from the Choptank tribe in the novel 'Chesapeake' by James A. Michener.

Extremely rare combination of Teal and the popular name suffix lyn, based on similar-sounding names such as Keelin and Teagan.

From from te meaning "the" and ānau meaning "restless, crooked" in Māori. A notable bearer of this name is the Maori politician Teanau Tuiono (b. 1972) from New Zealand.
According to the Book of Mormon, Teancum was a Nephite military leader.
Diminutive of Dorotea, Matea, and other names with a similar sound.
Means "the cold" in Māori from te meaning "the" and anu meaning "cold". Cognate of Hawaiian Keanu.

Means "the world, the day, the cloud" in Māori.

Russian, doukhobor-traditional.Anglicized phonetic version of traditional doukhobor name. Meaning Held firmly in YAHWEH'S grip. origonal form pronounced Tzee-rah. Doukhobor meaning spirit wrestlers, Tradionally nameing all thier children meanings about hebrew god YAHWEH. The Doukhobors or Dukhobors (Russian: Духоборы, Dukhobory), earlier Dukhobortsy (Russian: Духоборцы) (literally - Spirit-Wrestlers) are a Christian group of Russian origin. The Doukhobors were one of the sects - later defined as a religious philosophy, ethnic group, social movement, or simply a "way of life".
Possibly from te ārani meaning "the orange" (referring to the fruit, not the colour).

Polynesian and Tahitian name, meaning "great and white" or "great light".
Means "the love" in Maori (te, "the" and aroha, "love"). A variant of Aroha.

Means "the morning" in Māori. Stage name of Mary Frances Thompson (1895 - 1995), best known as Te Ata or Te Ata Fisher after her marriage. Te Ata is said to mean "bearer of the morning" in the Chickasaw language even though te ata is not a known word or phrase in the Chickasaw language. Some Chickasaw speakers say her native name Itti' hata' was anglicized to Te Ata. Te Ata was an actress and member of the Chickasaw Nation known for telling Native American stories. She performed as a representative of Native Americans at state dinners before President Franklin D. Roosevelt in the 1930s. She was inducted into the Oklahoma Hall of Fame in 1957, and named Oklahoma's first State Treasurer in 1987. Notable Māori bearer Dame Te Atairangikaahu (born Pikimene Korokī Mahuta, 1931 - 2006), known as Queen Te Ata, was the longest reigning Māori monarch.
Means "the bright bay" from te meaning "the", ava meaning "bay" and ura meaning "bright, red" in Tahitian.
From te ave meaning "the tail of a meteor" in Tahitian.
Means "the bright comet tail" from te meaning "the", ave meaning "comet tail" and ura meaning "bright, red" in Tahitian.
Serbian and Croatian form of Thebe.
Means "slaughter" in Hebrew, from the verb טָבַח (tabach) "to slaughter, butcher, slay". In the Bible, Tebah was the firstborn son of Nahor by his concubine Reumah (Gen. 22:24).
Variant form of Teobaldo. A known bearer of this name is the Italian former soccer player Tebaldo Bigliardi (b. 1963).
Medieval Italian diminutive of Tebaldo, as -uccio is an Italian masculine diminutive suffix.

Georgian name sources state that this name is of Greek origin, but that the meaning is unknown.At the same time, Tebronia is the name used to refer to saint Febronia of Nisibis (284-304) on the Georgian Wikipedia. Confusingly, religious Georgian sources use the name ფებრონია (Pebronia) to refer to saint Febronia of Syria (8th century). The latter form makes the most sense though, since Latin -f- and Greek φ (ph) usually become ფ (p) in Georgian.

Means "words do not shatter" in Ganda.
Meaning uncertain, possibly derived from a place name.
Meaning uncertain. May derive from Nahuatl teca "to lie down" and the locative suffix -pan, or be related to tecampaxolitzli "the act of biting".
Meaning uncertain, possibly related to Nahuatl teca yehuani "berserk, dangerous, attacking".

Means "person from Tecciztlann" in Nahuatl, a place name derived from Nahuatl tēcciztli "conch" and tlācatl "person, human being". In Aztec mythology, Tecciztecatl was a lunar deity, representing the "Man in the Moon". In many cultures, several pareidolic images of a human face, head, or body are recognized in the disc of the full moon; they are generally known as the Man in the Moon.
Means "dwelling place, someone’s house" in Nahuatl, from the possessive prefix te- and chantli "house". Alternately, the first element may derive from tetl "stone".
Jewish name of unknown meaning. This name Germanized is Therese.
A dithematic name formed with the second name element hild "battle" and an unidentified first part.
Hebrew for "rebirth". It is a modern Israeli name, often connected to the rebirth of the state of Israel. It can also be an amuletic name.
Derived from Ancient Greek τέχνη (techne) meaning "art, skill, craft, cunning" combined with ἀνδρός (andros) meaning "of a man".
Derived from Slavic tech "solace, comfort, joy" combined with Slavic mir "peace".
Derived from Slavic tech "solace, comfort, joy" combined with Slavic slav "glory".

Possibly an English form of Thekla.

Possibly derived from Ancient Greek τέκμαρ (tekmar) meaning "fixed mark; end, goal, token, pledge". In Greek Mythology, this was the name of a princess of Phrygia (or sometimes Teuthrania) who was taken as a concubine by Ajax, as well as of an Amazon warrior killed by Hercules.

Means "owl" or "great horned owl" in Nahuatl.

Possibly means "mischievous person" or "someone bold, shameless, insolent" in Nahuatl, from cuecuech "mischievous, shameless, insolent" and the prefix te-.
From Nahuatl tecuecuextli, a kind of braided leather anklet decorated with golden bells.

Means "he throws like a lizard", from Nahuatl tecue "a kind of venomous lizard" and tlaza "to throw".
Meaning uncertain. Possibly derived from Nahuatl tecuhtli "lord" and xōchitl "flower". Alternatively, the first element could be tecue "venomous lizard".
Possibly a variant form of Tecuichpoch.

Probably means "old lord", derived from Nahuatl tecuhtli "lord" and -zolli "old, worn out". Alternately, the second element could be from zolin, "quail".

This was the name of a 3rd-century Christian martyr from Ancyra, the capital of the Roman province of Galatia. She was the eldest of seven holy virgins who were drowned in a lake during the persecutions of the Roman emperor Diocletian. The following night she appeared to her nephew, Saint Theodotus, in a dream.
Derived from Welsh teg "beautiful; fair" and gwyn "white; fair; blessed". Saint Tecwyn is the patron saint and founder of Llandecwyn in the Welsh county of Gwynedd.
Variant form of Teodaldo. A known bearer of this name was the Italian count and margrave Tedaldo of Canossa (died in 1012 AD).
Unknown meaning. This is tye name of African American hip-hop musician Tedashii Lavoy Anderson.

Derived from Proto-Germanic þiudiskaz "of the people, popular, vernacular". It coincides with the modern Italian adjective tedesco "German".

Rare name used in English speaking countries. Possibly borrowed from the surname Tedford.Tedford Cann was an American Naval Reserve officer in World War I who fixed an underwater leak on the USS May and saved his ship from sinking, thus earning him the Medal of Honor. He went on to become an Olympic athlete.

Cornish form of Tedda. This name was borne by a 5th-century virgin and saint in Wales and Cornwall. Early Latin records, however, mention the saint by the name Tecla (itself a form of the name Thecla borne by the first female martyr in Christianity) and consider her a companion of Breaca, while in Cornish sources, she was listed among the daughters of Brychan, king of Brycheiniog in Wales. She is sometimes conflated with Saint Tegla.
Variant of Teddy.A notable male name bearer is an American screenwriter: Tedi Sarafian

Phonetic spelling of the initials TJ. It has been used sometimes as a standalone name.

Meaning uncertain. Name borne by a queen regnant of the nomadic tribes of Qedar circa 690 BCE.

Originally a diminutive of names ending in -tin/-teen/-tine, or from hushteen/hastiin meaning "man" in Navajo. Alfred "Teen" Blackburn (1842 – 1951) was one of the last surviving people with a clear recollection of being enslaved as an adult.

Variant transcription of Devanagari तिसा (see Tisa).

It is from Thailand it means 'Nipple' or 'Ginger'. It is pronounced Looeedally as of the origin of the meaning. It comes from the food called 'Tim yang goon' which is a tasty treat the Thai have for Breakfast.
Likely from Dakota ti taƞka meaning "large home".
Meaning uncertain, though the second element of this name certainly consists of the diminutive suffix -ke. The name is possibly Frisian in origin.
Modern Greek transcription of Teukros. This name is rare and used mostly in Cyprus.
TEFNUT is a goddess of moisture, moist air, dew and rain in Ancient Egyptian religion. She is the sister and consort of the air god Shu, and the mother of Geb and Nut.

column3: てふ子(Kanji/Hiragana)|てふこ(Japanese Hiragana)|テフコ(Japanese Katakana)

column12: Borne by a Guanche boy christened in Seville, Spain.
Means "inhabitant of Tegea" in Ancient Greek. In Greek mythology, this is the name of a son of King Lycaon and the legendary eponymous founder of Tegea, an ancient settlement in Arcadia.
Means "orchid" in Welsh, composed of Welsh teg "fair, beautiful" and eirian "bright, brilliant, fair".
Derived from Cornish tegen "pretty thing, jewel, ornament".
A famous bearer is Tegla Chepkite Loroupe (born 1973) a Kenyan long-distance track and road runner. She is also a global spokeswoman for peace, women's rights and education.
Older spelling of Teguh influenced by Dutch orthography.
Possibly a short form of Teudegrimo, the Italian form of a Germanic name derived from the elements þeud "people" and grim "mask".
From Mongolian тэгш (tegsh) meaning "equal, even, flat, smooth" and баатар (baatar) meaning "hero".
From Mongolian тэгш (tegsh) meaning "equal, even, flat, smooth" and бадрах (badrakh) meaning "thrive, grow" or "blaze, shine".
From Mongolian тэгш (tegsh) meaning "equal, even, flat, smooth" and баян (bayan) meaning "rich, wealthy".
From Mongolian тэгш (tegsh) meaning "equal, even, flat, smooth" and баяр (bayar) meaning "celebration, joy".
From Mongolian тэгш (tegsh) meaning "equal, even, flat, smooth" and буян (buyan) meaning "good deed, virtue, charity" or "fortune, blessing".
From Mongolian тэгш (tegsh) meaning "equal, even, flat, smooth" and дэлгэр (delger) meaning "vast, wide" or "prosperous, abundant".
From Mongolian тэгш (tegsh) meaning "equal, even, flat, smooth" and гэрэл (gerel) meaning "light".
From Mongolian тэгш (tegsh) meaning "equal, even, flat, smooth" and мөрөн (mörön) meaning "river, large river".
From Mongolian тэгш (tegsh) meaning "equal, even, flat, smooth" and оюун (oyuun) meaning "cleverness, wisdom, intellect".
From Mongolian тэгш (tegsh) meaning "equal, even, flat, smooth" and сайхан (saikhan) meaning "nice, beautiful, handsome".
From Mongolian тэгш (tegsh) meaning "equal, even, flat, smooth" and ерөөлт (yeröölt) meaning "fated, blessed".
From Mongolian тэгш (tegsh) meaning "equal, even, flat, smooth" and жаргал (jargal) meaning "happiness, blessing".
Name borne by a Guanche prince, who was the son of the mencey (leader) Tegueste.

Possibly from Thagaste, the name of a historic Roman-Berber city in present-day Algeria, presumably derived from a word meaning "humid" in Berber (*tegăsət in Guanche). It was borne by two menceyes (leaders) of the menceycato (kingdom) of the same name.
Means "firm, strong, unwavering" in Indonesian and Javanese.

Meaning uncertain. Theories include a derivation from Berber t-eguize-t, meaning "careful female guardian"; from the ancient place name Thiges, in Tunisia, allegedly meaning "terrain elevation"; or from Tuareg tégezé, meaning "feminine lineage". This name now survives as a place name in the island of Lanzarote, Canary Islands.
Name of a 3rd century Christian saint.
Presumably it is a combination of teg "fair" and gwared "deliverance." The eldest natural son of Llywelyn the Great was named Tegwared, born c. 1210.
An Igbo name from the YouTube channel House of Ajebo.

Derived from Tahitian te meaning "the" and hani meaning "darling". This was used for a character in the novel Mutiny on the Bounty (1932) by Charles Nordhoff and James Norman Hall. It has been used occasionally in the English-speaking world due to the influence of the novel, as well as its 1935 film adaptation.
meaning unknown but is possibly derived from the root חתן (hatan) meaning "to get married", this name could mean "(you will get her) married"
Variant of names with the name element diota such as Diether.
From tehei meaning "the crown, the garland", or teihea meaning "where" in Tahitian.
Derived from Tahitian te hei 'ura literally meaning "the red crown".
Variant of Tehila. Tehilla Blad is a Swedish actress.
Means "the grey; the grey-haired" in Māori and Tahitian. Hina is the female personification of the moon in Tahitian and Māori mythology, also known as Mahina in Hawai'i.
Taken from the city of Tehran
Derived from Теҳрон (Tehron), which is the Tajik and Uzbek name for Tehran, the capital city of Iran.
Alternate transcription of Urdu تحسین (see Tehsin).
Means "he has someone" or "with another" in Nahuatl.
Meaning "brave", "indomitable" in mapudungun the language of the Mapuche people. Used in Argentina and Chile.
Notable bearer was Joseph Tehwehron David (1957–2004), a Mohawk artist who became known for his role as a warrior during the Oka Crisis in 1990.

Probably an invented name based on similar-sounding names such as Taya. Though many questionable websites claim this is a Native American name meaning "precious", there is as yet no evidence that it is an authentic name or word in any Native American language.

column12: Pet form of Teibe/Teiba, a variant of Toiba.
Possibly a variant form of Teicuh.
Means "younger sibling of a male, younger brother" in Nahuatl.
Allegedly a wife of Finn MacCúmhaill.Her name is said to be derived from either Irish téide "wantonness" or Old Irish tét "cord; cable".
From the name of a river in Wales.

Possibly an elaborated form of Teifi, the name of a river in Ceredigion, Wales, using the suffix on (found in names of Welsh rivers dedicated to gods, such as Aeron, as well as some early Welsh saints' names, such as Mabon).
Anglicized form of Tadhg used by Douglas Hyde in his translation of the Irish folktale 'Teig O'Kane (Tadhg O Cáthán) and the Corpse'.
Transferred from the surname Teigen or a variant of Tegan/Teagan.

column3: ていじ(Japanese Hiragana)|テイジ(Japanese Katakana)|訂滋, 態, 堤, 廷, 低, 第, 帝, 邸, 底, 艇, 定, 庭, 締, 鄭, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 亭 (tei) meaning "pavilion, arbor" or 体 (tei) meaning "form, body, shape" combined with 治 (ji) meaning "govern, regulate, administer". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: テイ子(Kanji/Katakana)|貞子, 禎子, 汀子, 綴子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 禎 (tei) meaning "auspicious, divine grace, straight", 汀 (tei) meaning "water's edge, shore, beach" or 貞 (tei) meaning "chastity, upright, faithfulness, virtue" and 子 (ko) meaning "child, first sign of the Chinese zodiac sign, sign of the rat". Other kanji combinations can be used.
Directly taken from Latvian teiksma "story; legend, fable".
Derived from Gothic dails (tail in Old High German) "part" combined with Gothic hardus (hart in Old High German) "brave, hardy."

From Teilio, which was originally a diminutive of Eiludd, composed of the Welsh pronoun ty meaning "thy, your" prefixed to a diminutive of Eiludd. This name was borne by a legendary or semi-legendary Welsh saint of the 6th century and occurs in Llandeilo meaning literally "church of Teilo", the name of 15 places in Wales (so called either currently or in former times). Saint Teilo appears in the Life of Saint Cadoc (late 11th century) in which he joins Saints David (Dewi) and Cadoc in mediating a dispute between King Arthur and Ligessauc, a chief of the Britons. According to the 12th-century chronicler Geoffrey of Monmouth, Teilo was a priest from Llandaff whom Arthur appointed as the archbishop of Dol, replacing Saint Samson, the previous archbishop.
Alternate transcription of Persian تیمور (see Teymour).
Alternate transcription of Persian تیمور (see Teymour).
Means "younger brother, sibling" in Māori and Tahitian.
Means "sibling's descendant; nephew, niece" in Tahitian from teina meaning "sibling" and uri meaning "descendant".
Notable bearer is actress Teioshontathe McGregor.

Possibly derived from Greek τεῖρος (teiros) "constellations, heavenly signs" and εἴδω (eidô) "to see". This was the name of a blind seer who appears in many Greek myths. Due to objecting the goddess Hera in a debate with her husband Zeus, he lost his eyesight, but was given the ability to see into the future by Zeus. His most noteworthy appearances were in Homer's 'Odyssey', several of Sophokles' opus as well as Ovid's 'Metamorphoses'.

Likely a variant of Teyrnon. This name appears in the Welsh tale Culhwch and Olwen belonging to Teirnon Twrfliant, an Arthurian warrior who ruled Gwent Ys Coed. He is probably the same character as Teyrnon Twryf Bliant, the man who found the infant Pryderi.

column3: 停留(Japanese Kanji)|ていりゅう(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: The name Teiryu (停留) uses the Kanji 停/Tei - "to stop" and 留/Ryū - "detain, halt". The name roughly means "halt, stoppage" in Japanese.
Variant of Theis. It was brought to Norway from the Netherlands in the 1700's.
Latinized form of Teisandros. Or, in other words, this name is a variant form of Tisander.
Derived from the Lithuanian adjective teisus meaning "righteous, just".

Latinized form of Τεΐσπης (Teḯspēs), a Hellenized form of Old Persian Čišpiš⁠, of uncertain meaning. This was the name of the second ruler of the Teispid Kingdom, who ruled from 705 BC up until 559 BC.

column3: 禎介, 楨助, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|ていすけ(Japanese Hiragana)|テイスケ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 禎 (tei) meaning "divine grace, auspicious, straight, unwarped" combined with 介 (suke) meaning "help, assist" or 助 (suke) meaning "assistance". Other kanji combinations can form this name as well.
Diminutive of the rare name Teisė, since this name contains the feminine diminutive suffix -utė. In other words, you could say that this name is the feminine equivalent of Teisutis.
Diminutive of Teisius, since this name contains the masculine diminutive suffix -utis.A known bearer of this name was the Lithuanian-Australian sculptor Teisutis "Joe" Zikaras (1922-1991).
Derived from Old Norse teitr "glad, cheerful, merry" (also compare Teitr) and nýr "new".
From Old Norse teitr meaning "glad, cheerful, merry'".
Faroese combination of teitr "glad, cheerful, merry" and rún "secret".
Variant of Tatum. This name is borne by American football player, Teitum Tuioti.
Icelandic and Faroese form of Teitr.
Variant of Tobias. Means “God is good.”
Means "a belittler, someone who is disrespectful and inattentive" in Nahuatl, literally "one who goes to someone’s face".
Possibly related to Nahuatl teiztlacahui "deceiver, one who tells lies".
Probably derived from Nahuatl itztlacoa "to look cautiously, to examine, to spy (on someone)".
From Sanskrit तेजस् (tejas) meaning "brilliance, splendour". As a Punjabi (Sikh) name it is sometimes feminine.
Means "afterglow, reddish or yellowish ray observed during sunset" in Indonesian, ultimately from Sanskrit तेजस् (tejas).
Alternate transcription of Telugu తేజస్వి or Marathi तेजस्वी (see Tejaswi).
Alternate transcription of Marathi तेजस्विनी or Telugu తేజస్వినీ (see Tejaswini).
From Sanskrit तेजस्विन् (tejasvin) meaning "brilliant, splendid, bright".
Derived from Sanskrit तेजस्विन् (tejasvin) meaning "brilliant, splendid, bright".
From Sanskrit तेजस् (tejas) meaning "brilliance, splendour" combined with दीप (dīpa) meaning "lamp, light".
From Sanskrit तेजस् (tejas) meaning "brilliance, splendour" combined with the name of the Hindu god Indra.
From Tejinder combined with Sanskrit प्रीति (prīti) meaning "love, joy".
From Sanskrit तेजस् (tejas) meaning "brilliance, splendour" combined with पाल (pāla) meaning "guard, protector".
From Sanskrit तेजस् (tejas) meaning "brilliance, splendour" combined with प्रीति (prīti) meaning "pleasure, joy, love".

This name means "radiance of Rama," "soul of Rama" or "majesty of Rama", which is derived from a combination of Sanskrit तेज (tēja) meaning "radiance, soul, majesty, lustre, energy, splendour, magnificence" and the name of the god Rama 1.
Means "focus on life, the world" in Yoruba.
Means "one who looks forward to better days" or "stare at wealth" in Yoruba, derived from tẹ meaning "press", ojú meaning "eyes, face", mọ́ meaning "onto" and ọlá meaning "wealth".

Means "the burning, the blaze" in Māori. The alter ego of fictional goddess Te Fiti (phonetic form of Māori te whiti meaning "the shining one") after her heart had been stolen by Maui in the Disney movie, Moana.
Means "Double life". This is the Mohawk name of Canadian writer and performer Pauline Johnson (1861-1913).
Means "harrier hawk" in Māori. Transliteration of "hawk".
Means "split in the sky" in Mohawk.
From Japanese 適 (teki) meaning "suitable, appropriate, fit" or other kanji which are pronounced the same way.
Derives from kiato which are wooden god sticks that are placed around gardens to keep the crops safe. The word kiato also means "compact".
From Japanese 迪 (teki) meaning "enlighten, advance" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Japanese 適 (teki) meaning "suitable, appropiate, fit" combine with 奈 (na) meaning "apple tree". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Means "the large feather of the wing (the flight feather)" and "the keel (of a boat)" in Māori.
The name of one of the most important hunting gods in the Inuit pantheon. Tekkeitsertok is a god of hunting and the master of caribou.
Georgian form of Thekla. A notable bearer of this name was the Georgian princess and poet Tekle of Georgia (1776-1846).
Diminutive of Tekla and Tekle, as it contains the Georgian diminutive suffix -უშა (-usha).
Georgian diminutive of Tekla and Tekle.
Derived from tekoa meaning "rocky, stony" in Māori, or te koa meaning "the happy" in Māori. Mount Tekoa is a mountain range in South New Zealand.
Means "her voice travels through the wind" in Mohawk.
Diminutive of Teko, which itself is a diminutive of Tekla and Tekle.In other words: this name is a double diminutive of Tekla and Tekle.
The name was used by Jean-Phillippe Rameau in his 1737 opera 'Castor et Pollux'. It is used as the name of a Greek princess whom both Castor and Pollux are in love with.
From Bashkir теләк (teläk) meaning "wish, desire", and feminine name element бикә (bikä).
Either a variant of Teleri or a transferred use of the Italian surname Telari.
Possibly a Spanish form of Thelbert.
From the Arabic ثَلْج (ṯalj) meaning "snow, ice".

A fictional character created by J.R.R. Tolkien. Telchar was one of the greatest smiths of the First Age of Middle-earth, having learned from Gamil Zirak the old.1 Telchar was commonly regarded amongst the greatest smiths of all time, save only Fëanor and Celebrimbor. Among his works were the knife Angrist, the sword Narsil (later reforged as Andúril), and the Dragon-helm of Dor-lómin, worn eventually by Túrin Turambar.
Semi-latinized form of Greek Τηλέκλεια (Telekleia), the feminine form of Telekles. This was the name of a Trojan princess in Greek mythology.
Latinized form of Telekles. This name was borne by two eponymous archons of Athens, the earliest of which lived in the 6th century BC.

Derived from Ancient Greek τηλέγονος (telegonos) meaning "born far from one’s father or homeland", composed of τῆλε (tele) "far, from afar, far off" and γονή (gone) "birth, offspring". This was the name of a daughter of Pharis and the Danaid Philodameia in Greek mythology.
Derived from Ancient Greek τηλέγονος (telegonos) meaning "born far from one’s father or homeland", composed of τῆλε (tele) "far, from afar, far off" and γονή (gone) "birth, offspring".
Means "son of Telekles" in Greek, derived from the name Telekles combined with the patronymic suffix ἴδης (ides).

Probably derived from Ancient Greek τῆλε (tele) meaning "far, from afar, far off" and κλέος (kleos) meaning "glory". Alternatively, the first element could instead derive from τέλος (telos), which can mean "purpose, goal, aim" as well as "fulfillment, completion".
Derived from Erzya телень (telenʹ) meaning "of winter", itself a derivative of теле (tele) "winter".
Means "follow success, nobility, wealth" in Yoruba.
Derived from Ancient Greek τελέω (teleo) meaning "to bring about, complete, fulfill" (see telos).

An ancient Greek epithet for the moon, meaning "far-shining", derived from τῆλε (tele) "far-off, afar" and a derivative of φάος (phaos) meaning "light". This was also another name for the queen of Tyre, Argiope, nymph and mother of Europa.
Means "far-shining", derived from Greek τῆλε (tele) meaning "afar, far off" and φάος (phaos) meaning "light".
Contraction of Welsh ty meaning "thy, your" and Eleri. This name is mentioned in Culhwch and Olwen as one of the maidens of King Arthur's court.
Meaning unknown. This was the name of a Bulgarian khan (ruler) from the 8th century AD.
Derived from Greek τέλος (telos) meaning "purpose, goal, aim" as well as "fulfillment, completion", or perhaps τῆλε (tele) "far, from afar, far off", combined with ἀνδρός (andros) meaning "of a man".
Bulgarian, Croatian, Polish, Russian, Serbian and Ukrainian form of Telesphoros (see Télesphore).
Galician and Portuguese form of Telesphoros (see Télesphore).

Derived from Greek τέλος (telos) meaning "purpose, result, completion", or the noun τέλεσις (telesis) "event, fulfillment". Telesilla (fl. 510 BC) was an ancient Greek poet, native of Argos. She was a distinguished woman who was especially renowned for her poetry and for her leadership of Argos through a political and military crisis and subsequent re-building. Antipater of Thessalonica included her in his canon of nine female poets.
Bessarabian German form of Telesphoros (see Télesphore).

Derived from the Greek noun τελεστής (telestes) meaning "(religious) initiator" as well as "priest" and "initiated person".Telestes was the name of the last king of Corinth. It is not quite clear whether he is a historical person, or whether he is a mythological character.

Means "fulfilled, perfected", derived from Ancient Greek τελέω (teleo) meaning "to bring about, complete, fulfill" as well as "to consecrate, initiate", ultimately from τέλος (telos) "purpose, result, completion". This was the name of an Oceanid in Greek mythology, one of the daughters of Oceanus and Tethys. A moon of Saturn was named after her.

Means "ritual, initiation rite, consecration" or "festival (at which rites are held)", ultimately derived from Greek τέλος (telos) meaning "purpose, result, completion". This was the name of a goddess or spirit associated with nighttime festivities and ritual dances in honour of Dionysos, her father.

Latinized form of Greek Τελέθουσα (Telethousa), which is possibly derived from Ancient Greek τελέθω (telethô) meaning "to come into being, arise". This name belonged to the mother of Iphis in Greek mythology, disguising her child as a boy to save her from being left to die.

Uncertain etymology, possibly derived from Ancient Greek τέλειος (teleios) meaning "perfect" or τελέω (teleo) meaning "to fulfill, accomplish, execute, perform", both of which derive from τέλος (telos) "purpose, result, completion", or perhaps from τῆλε (tele) meaning "far, from afar, far off". In Greek mythology, Teleus was a man from Argos, the father of Clymenus.
Derived from Greek τελευτάω (teleutao) meaning "to bring to pass, to accomplish" or "to end, finish; to die".
Derived from Ancient Greek τελευτή (teleute) meaning "completion, accomplishment, end" (compare telos).
Short form of Ottilia, traditionally found in the Surselva region and in central Grisons.
Means "girl who has a brother" in Tamazight.
Variant of Talisha, possibly influenced by the spelling of Felicia.
Of unknown origin, but is speculated to derive from Philomena via a Belarusian form.
Diminutive of Otelie or Otelia. It may also be used as a diminutive of Tellervo.
Transferred use of the surname Teller.
Norwegian dialectal pet form of Torleiv---------------------Variant form of Tella.
Means "the earth, globe" in Latin. In Roman mythology Tellus was the mother goddess who personified the earth, equivalent to the Greek goddess Gaia.

A diminutive of several names, such as Aristotelis, Donatella, Estella, Theodore and more. This name spiked in popularity after the 1973 premiere of the American television series Kojak, a crime drama starring Greek-American actor and singer Aristotelis 'Telly' Savalas (1922-1994) in the title role.
Derived from Nahuatl telpochtli "young man, youth, young warrior; son".
Means "young man" in Nahuatl, another name for Tezcatlipoca.

Originally a Low German diminutive of Elisabeth, which may have arisen from the contraction of either Sünt Else meaning "Saint Else", perhaps applied affectionately or ironically to an individual named Else (or else referring to the biblical character; see Elizabeth) or dat Else, an affectionate phrase meaning "the Else".
Means "last Finwë". In Tolkien's Legendarium this is the father-name of Amras.
A nymph of Diana in 'Gallathea", an Elizabethan era stage play, a comedy by John Lyly.
Probably a spin-off of the name Tevin influenced by names like Calvin and Kelvin, popularised through the R&B singer Tevin Campbell.
Means "the welcomed" from te meaning "the" and Maeva meaning "welcome" in Tahitian.

column3: 天毬, 天鞠, 手毬, 手鞠(Japanese Kanji)|てまり(Japanese Hiragana)|テマリ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name can be used to combine 天 (ten, amatsu, ame, ama-, te) meaning "sky, heaven" or 手 (shu, zu, (-)te(-), ta-) meaning "hand" with 毬 (kyuu, iga, mari) or 鞠 (kiku, kyuu, mari), both meaning "ball."Temari (天毬) is also used as a word to refer to handmade balls made from embroidery which may be used in handball games, hence the kanji make-up (though it's more often written as 手まり).One fictional bearer of this name is Temari (テマリ) from the popular manga and anime series Naruto.This name is rarely used.
Caló form of Mary, used in reference to the Virgin Mary.
Meaning uncertain, possibly means "someone’s hand", derived from Nahuatl maitl "hand" and the prefix te-. May alternately refer to a kind of cape.

Possibly derived from Nahuatl tematlahuia "to use a rock-hurling sling on something", or from a combination of tematlatl "rock-throwing sling" and either elehuia "to wish, to desire" or ilihuiz "thoughtlessly".
From te mauri meaning "the life force" in Maori and Tahitian, and "the spirit; the soul" in Cook Islands Maori.
Derived from Nahuatl temāzcalli meaning "steam bath" and tecitl "grandmother". This was the name of an Aztec goddess of steam baths.
Means "song, poetry" in Indonesian, of Javanese origin.
Meaning uncertain, but the -ko at the end indicates that it might possibly be a diminutive.

Temeluchus (probably a transliteration of the Greek Telémakhos; literally, "far-away fighter") is the leader of the tartaruchi, the chief angel of torment (and possibly Satan himself), according to the extracanonical Apocalypse of Paul.

Possibly from Mycenaean Greek qe-ja-me-no (kʷeiamenos) meaning "paid, compensated; revenged, avenged". Coincides with Ancient Greek τήμενος (temenos), a type of clothing. This was the name of several figures in Greek mythology.
(Polish?) Yiddish diminutive of Tema. Found in Polish documents from the early 1800s.
Means "you be praised" or "august" in Amharic.
Temetrius is a variant spelling of Demetrius.
This is a named from Ancient Egypt meaning "Atum is satisfied".
Means "my story has become one of joy".
This Nigerian name means "Mine has turned to blessings" in Yoruba.
Probably from Nahuatl temilotli, a kind of hairstyle or headdress.
Derived from the Uzbek temir meaning "iron" and the given name Ali 1.
From the names Temir and Ali 1.
From the given name Temir combined with the Turkish military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".
Derived from the Uzbek temir meaning "iron" and berdi meaning "gave".
From the Karachay-Balkar темир (temir) meaning "iron" and Persian جان (jan) meaning "soul".
Derived from Uzbek temir meaning "iron" and gul meaning "rose, flower".
Alternate transcription of Kazakh Теміржан (see Temirzhan).
Combination of the given name Temir and the Turkic title khan meaning "leader, ruler".
Kazakh and Kyrgyz form of Tamerlane. It could also be formed from Kazakh темір (temir) or Kyrgyz темир (temir) meaning "iron" and Turkic arslan meaning "lion".
Derived from the Uzbek temir meaning "iron" and malik meaning "king, lord".

Possibly from Kipchak تمور (temür) "iron" (see Timur) and Mirza. This was the name of a Tatar champion who fought Alexander Peresvet at the opening of the Battle of Kulikovo, known in Russian sources as Chelubey
Derived from the Uzbek temir meaning "iron" and niyoz meaning "offering".
Derived from the Uzbek temir meaning "iron" and po'lat meaning "steel, sword".
Derived from the Uzbek temir meaning "iron" and qo'zi meaning "lamb".
Derived from the Uzbek temir meaning "iron" and qutlug' meaning "blessed".
Derived from the Uzbek temir meaning "iron" and toy meaning "colt".
Combination of the given name Temir and Kazakh жан (zhan) meaning "soul" (of Persian origin).
Means "expose me to goodness" in Yoruba.
Croatian form of Themistios via Themistius.
Portuguese form of Themistios via Themistius.
Italian and Spanish form of Themistios via Themistius.
Portuguese and Spanish form of Themistocles (see Themistokles).
Means "mine is worthy of joy" in Yoruba.

Meaning uncertain, but it is likely a diminutive of a masculine given name that starts with Tem-, such as Temelko.A notable bearer of this name was the Macedonian political activist Temko Popov (1855-1929).
Means "she/he descended", derived from Nahuatl temo "to go down, to descend; to let fall".
Alternate transcription of Urdu تیمور (see Taimur).
Alternate transcription of Tibetan བསྟན་པ (see Tenpa).

Likely transferred use of the surname Tempany. Usage of this name rose in the United Kingdom after Australian actress Tempany Deckert (1978-) joined the cast of the Australian soap opera Home and Away in 1994.
From the Vale of Tempe, a gorge in Thessaly (located south of Mount Olympus) which was celebrated by the ancient Greeks for its beauty. This name can also be a diminutive of Temperance.
Derived from Latin temperantia "moderation, sobriety, temperance, self control".
Means "storm, tempest, (bad) weather" in Latin. This was the name of the Roman goddess of storms and sudden weather.
Variant of Tempest. A famous bearer is the actress Tempestt Bledsoe, who played Vanessa Huxtable on 'The Cosby Show.'
Diminutive of names beginning with Temp- such as Temperance, Tempest or Temple.
From Old French templier, from medieval Latin templarius, from Latin templum.
Transferred use of the surname Templeton.
Means "pointy tip of a spear or arrow" in Turkish.
Variant of Remuera, Māori form of Lemuel. Possibly derived from te muera meaning "the mule" in Māori, muera is a loan word from English mule.
Ffrom the Turkic word temür meaning "iron" combined with the Mongolian suffix -ge used for personal names. This was the name of the youngest brother of Genghis Khan.
From the stem "temü", meaning "iron", and "lun", a feminine name suffix. Temülün was the sister of Genghis Khan, or Temüjin.
Means "fully decorated, full dress uniform". From Thai เต็ม (tem) meaning "full, complete" and ยศ (yot) meaning "rank, title, merit".

column3: てん(Japanese Hiragana)|テン(Japanese Katakana)|殿, 天, 槇, 槙, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: Derived from Japanese 天 (ten), meaning "sky, heaven". Other kanji are possible.
Possibly from Ethiopian ጠና (t'ena) meaning "become strong" or "older".
Means "just stay at a place" in Akan.
An invented name that sounds like Renae, but then with a 't' instead.

Possibly derived from Ancient Greek τέναγος (tenagos) meaning "shoal water, shallows, lagoon". Tenages was a son of Helios and Rhodos in Greek mythology, murdered by his brothers due to their jealousy over his skill at science.
Name of a Roman governor, Tenagino Probus, who lived in the 3rd century.
Means "with someone, someone’s partner" in Nahuatl.
A famous bearer was the Telugu jester-poet Tenali Ramakrishna, whose cleverness was the subject of many Indian folk-tales.

Means "one’s mother" in Nahuatl. May alternately derive from tenantli "wall, rampart", tenani "moaner, one who complains", or a combination of tetl "stone" and nantli "mother", the latter being used in the sense of "protector".

From Ursula K. Le Guin's Earthsea Cycle, specifically 'The Tombs of Atuan', 'Tehanu', and 'The Other Wind'.Tenar is the true name of the character kept secret except for very close persons; she is called Arha and Goha publically.
Borne by a Guanche man who was christened in Seville.

This has been in rare use as a feminine given name in the United States since the 1970s. It is possibly taken from the name of a lake in Yosemite, California, which was itself named for a 19th-century chief of the Ahwahnechee (a Miwok people of the Yosemite Valley), whose name may be derived from Central Sierra Miwok taná·ya- meaning "evening star".

Transferred use of the surname Tenbroeck.The surname has never been in use as a given name in the Netherlands, as Dutch law has always expressly forbidden the use of surnames as given names. It is only found as a given name in countries where there are no such naming laws and where large portions of the population descend from immigrants, such as the United States. People in these countries will sometimes use surnames as given names, in order to honour their distant ancestors. As such, people with Dutch ancestry will sometimes choose to use Dutch surnames from their family tree for their offspring. In other words: the use of surnames like Tenbroeck as a given name is not a Dutch phenomenon, but a foreign one.
Means "desired, dear, coveted, yearned for" in Armenian.

column3: 天地, 天智, 天知(Japanese Kanji)|てんち(Japanese Hiragana)|テンチ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name combines 天 (ten, ama-, amatsu, ame) meaning "heavens, imperial, sky" with 地 (ji, chi) meaning "earth, ground", 智 (chi) meaning "intellect, reason, wisdom" or 知 (chi, shi.raseru, shi.ru) meaning "know, wisdom."One fictional bearer of this name is Tenchi Masaki (柾木 天地), the main protagonist of the Tenchi Muyo! (天地無用!) metaseries.This name began to be used in the early 1990s and it peaked in 1995 (25 boys), just after the first Tenchi Muyo! manga series came out. This name can be used for girls as well, but it's much rarer to encounter a girl named Tenchi than a boy with that same name.

column3: 天地金乃神(Japanese Kanji)|てんちかねのかみ(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: Means "Golden Kami of the Heavens and Earth" or "Golden Kami of the Universe" (as 天地 can also mean 'universe'). This is the name of the primary kami in Konkokyo sect Shinto.
Means "obstinate" or "loud-mouthed" in Nahuatl, literally "wooden lip", from tentli "lip, mouth; voice, word" and cuahuitl "tree, wood".
Means "foul-mouthed man" or "mischievous, unrestrained" in Nahuatl, from tentli "lip, mouth; voice, word" and cuecuenotl "proud, arrogant, insolent".
Meaning “be faithful; be true”, a longer form of the name is Tendekamunashe.
Means "what should we walk for?" in Tumbuka.
Can mean "faith" or some may use it as meaning something used to give thanks

column3: でんど(Japanese Hiragana)|テンド(Japanese Katakana)|店通, 天童, 展堂, 典同, 転道, 点胴, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 天 (ten) meaning "heaven, sky, imperial, celestial" combined with 童 (do) meaning "child, juvenile, young person." Other kanji combinations can be used.-------------------------------------Means "way of heaven" or "heavenly child" in Japanese.
Latin meaning "dark,blind"Was used in Harry Potter.
From Guanche *tenăfirah, meaning "huffs". This was the name of a woman who was baptized in Seville around 1427.

In Egyptian mythology she was a goddess of childbirth and beer. She was typically depicted as a woman wearing a cow uterus on her head like another Egyptian childbirth goddess, Meskhenet. She was considered a protector of the uterus for pregnant women. She was a consort of the war-god Montu. Eventually she was merged with Raet, Isis, and Iunit.

Probably from Nahuatl tene "lip-possessor; one who speaks well or vigorously", itself derived from tentli "lip, mouth; voice, word" and the possessive suffix -e, combined with the suffix -pal "through, by means of". This may have derived from a transliteration of la lengua, a Spanish sobriquet of the famous translator Malinche meaning "the interpreter; the tongue".
From Guanche *tennerist, meaning "she rests". This was the name of a woman who was baptized in Seville around 1427.
Etymology unknown. This was the name of a Theban hero and prophet in Greek mythology, a son of Apollo and Melia.

Uncertain etymology. In Greek mythology, Tenes was the son of either Apollo or of King Cycnus, and the eponymous hero of the island of Tenedos, having washed ashore there along with his sister Hemithea after being falsely accused of rape by their stepmother and cast into the ocean.

Of Guanche origin, meaning "you precede (others)", "lead the way" or "you stay ahead". This was the name of an Aboriginal chieftain from Gran Canaria who converted to Christianism and allied with the Spaniards, aiding them in the conquest of the Canary Islands. He was baptised as Fernando Guanarteme.

Of Guanche origin, possibly from *tenəsuy(ăh) meaning "she who dives" or "this one is submerged". This was borne by a niece of Tenesor, the last guanarteme or king of Gáldar on the island of Gran Canaria.

Teneu is a legendary Christian saint who was venerated in medieval Glasgow, Scotland. Traditionally she was a sixth-century Brittonic princess of the ancient kingdom of Gododdin and the mother of Saint Kentigern, apostle to the Britons of Strathclyde and founder of the city of Glasgow. Saint Teneu has been described as "Scotland's first recorded rape victim, battered woman and unmarried mother". Her son was conceived when the Welsh prince Owain mab Urien raped her. Upon discovering her pregnancy, her angry father King Lleuddun sentenced her to death and she was hurled from Traprain Law. Miraculously she survived the fall; when discovered alive at the foot of the cliff, Teneu was set adrift in a coracle and travelled across the Firth of Forth to Culross, where she was given shelter at the community of Saint Serf.
From Chinese 腾 (téng) meaning "to gallop; to rise, to soar", in addition to other hanzi that are pronounced similarly.
Means "the hundred flying fish" in Bellonese.
From the Garo word তেঁ (teng) meaning "shining" and চি (chi) meaning "water".
Means "equal" or "of the same age" in Uzbek.

There is no concrete meaning or origin for the name TengHouy. However, people with the name TengHouy are resilient, kind, and steadfast but at times could also be indecisive and stubborn. Although these people may not have a well-known meaning attached to their name they show meaning to everyone around them. People with the name TengHouy can see the positive in every situation and naturally help those around them see that perspective as well. It is not common to come across someone who has the name TengHouy but that shows the uniqueness of the person.
From Old Norse þengill meaning "prince, king". Tengil is the main antagonist in Swedish author Astrid Lindgren's novel 'The Brothers Lionheart' from 1973.
Form of Tengiz with the nominative suffix, used in Georgian when the name is written stand-alone.
From a hereditary title used by Malay men and women of royal descent, typically placed before the given name.

Means "sky, heaven, god" in Old Turkic, itself probably of Yeniseian origin. This is the name of the supreme god of the sky in the traditional Turkic and Mongolic religion (Tengrism). He is regarded as the creator and sustainer of the universe.
Of uncertain origin and meaning; theories include a short form of Antónia and a short form of names ending in -ténia.
Meaning uncertain, probably contains the element huehue meaning "an elder, an old man; old" in Nahuatl.
Means "roll out the carpet to receive joy" in Yoruba.
Means "roll out the carpet to receive wealth" in Yoruba.
Means "roll out the carpet for life" in Yoruba.
Variant of Tennille. Known bearers include Canadian country singers Tenille Townes (1994-) and Tenille Arts (1994-).
Means "I belong to the great one" in Yoruba.
Means "roll out the mat of honour" in Yoruba.
Means "roll out the carpet for God" in Yoruba.
Means "I belong to God" in Yoruba.
Meaning unknown, possibly a variant of Tanisha.

column3: 典子, 天子, 展子, 天恋, 天鼓(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 典 (ten) meaning "ceremony, rule", 天 (ten) meaning "heavens, sky" or 展 (ten) meaning "exhibition" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child", 恋 (ko) meaning "love" (for females) or 鼓 (ko) meaning "drum" (for males). Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 典真, 典磨, 天真, 天誠, 天麻, 天眞, 天茉, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 典 (ten) meaning "ceremony, rule" combined with 真 (ma) meaning "true, reality". Other kanji combinations are possible.

From the name of the state located in the Southeastern region of the United States, possibly derived from Cherokee ᏔᎾᏏ (tanasi), believed to mean "winding river", which was originally the name of a village in present-day Monroe County, Tennessee. Alternatively, it could be derived from Yuchi Tana-tsee-dgee, meaning "place of brother waters" or "where the waters meet".

Transferred use of the surname Tennille. This is the surname of American singer Cathryn Antoinette 'Toni' Tennille (1940-) who gained fame in the 1970s singing duo Captain & Tennille. Use of the name may be due to a misconception that Tennille was the singer's given name, rather than her surname.
This name was given to five baby boys in 1915.

Anglicized form of both Teunisje and the Dutch patronymic Teunis(s)e(n), which means "son of Teunis". In some cases, this name can also be a modern variant spelling of the name Denise, via its variant spelling Dennise.According to the website of The Corpus of First Names in The Netherlands, this name has never been in use in the Netherlands, which was to be expected, since this name is an anglicization and therefore originated in English-speaking countries.An example of a bearer of this name is the American author Tennise Broeck Morse (born ca. 1946), who is of Dutch descent.
Variant of Tennison, which is taken from the surname.

Possibly a combination of Nahuatl te- "stone" and nochtli "prickly-pear cactus fruit". This was the name of a possibly-legendary Aztec ruler, who is said to have led his people southward to found the city of Tenochtitlan.
Likely from the name of the voice type between countertenor and baritone.

column3: 天梨, 天里, 天理(Japanese Kanji)|てんり(Japanese Hiragana)|テンリ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name combines 天 (ten, ama-, amatsu, ame) meaning "heavens, imperial, sky" with 梨 (ri, nashi) meaning "pear tree", 里 (ri, sato) meaning "league, parent's home, ri (unit of distance - equal to 3.927 km), village" or 理 (ri, kotowari) meaning "arrangement, justice, logic, reason, truth."As a word, Tenri (天理) means "natural laws, rule of heaven."This name is very rarely given to girls, if given at all.Tenri (天理) is also used a place name.

column3: 天理王命(Japanese Kanji)|てんりおうのみこと(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: Means "absolute ruler of divine reason". 天 refers to heaven or divinity, and 理 refers to reason or knowledge, so 天理 can be said to refer to divine or heavenly knowledge, and is also used to refer to natural law. This is the more formal name of the creator god of Tenrikyo, formerly considered a type of sect Shinto but now considered its own religion.

column3: 天心, 典慎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 天 (ten) meaning "heaven" or 典 (ten) meaning "ceremony, rule, rite" combined with 慎 (shin) meaning "prudent, careful" or 心 (shin) meaning "heart, soul, spirit". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Possibly a blend of Tenley and Tinsley.
From Guanche *te-n-tagayəst, meaning "great bustard". This was recorded as the name of a 20-year-old Guanche woman who was sold at the slave market in Valencia in 1494.
Possibly from Nahuatl tentli "lip, mouth; voice, word" and tepiton "a little bit, something small".
Possibly meaning "she from the land of the Hittites". This name was borne by the Great Royal Wife of Amasis II.

column3: 展哉, 天也, 典矢, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|Теня(Russian)
column12: From Japanese 展 (ten) meaning "expand, unfold" combined with 哉 (ya), an exclamation. Other kanji combinations are possible.
Turkish form of Tanzila. A notable bearer was Tenzile Erdoğan (1924-2011), the mother of Turkish president Recep Tayyip Erdoğan.

column3: 天麻, 泰吾, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 天 (te) meaning "heavens, sky" combined with 麻 (o) meaning "hemp, flax, linen". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Cognate of Theo, meaning "gift of God".
Polish, Croatian and Gascon form of Theobald.
Spanish and Portuguese form of Theocritus.
Romanian form of Theoktistos via Theoctistus.
Romanian form of Theoktiste via Theoctista.
Italian form of Theoktistos via Theoctistus.
Norwegian and Polish form of Theodahad.
Swedish, Catalan, and Polish form of Theudehard via Latinized form Theodardus.
Italian, and Spanish form of Theudehard via Latinized form Theodardus.
Italian, Spanish and Portuguese form of Theodahad.
Galician, Italian, Spanish and Portuguese form of Theudebald.
Galician, Italian, Spanish and Portuguese form of Theodebert.
Galician, Spanish and Portuguese form of Theodemund.
Danish, Finnish and Norwegian form of Theodoric.
Languedocian and Provençal form of Theodore.

Medieval Georgian form of Theodoros (see Theodore), which is still in use today, but rarely so. It has largely been replaced by the newer form Tedore, which is now quite common in Georgia.This name was borne by three Catholicos(-Patriarchs) of Georgia: the first lived in the 7th century, the last in the 15th century.
Italian, Portuguese, Galician and Spanish form of Theodoric.
Rare feminine form of Teodor, variant of Teodora.
Georgian form of Theodoretos via its modern Greek form Theodoritos.
Sicilian, Corsican and Sardinian form of Theodore.
Georgian and Romansh form of Theodosios (see Theodosius).
Form of Theodosia in various languages.
Bulgarian form of Theodosius. Its usage has declined since the late 19th century.
Italian and Polish feminine form of Greek Theodotos.
Portuguese and Spanish form of Theodotos (see Theodotus).
Bosnian and Croatian form of Theodosius.
Serbian, Polish and Romanian form of Theodulus.
Spanish and Italian form of Theudulf.
Italian and Venetian form of Theodulus.
Diminutive of Teodoro, Teodulo, and other beginning with Teod-. A bearer of this name was Teody Belarmino, a Filipino actor.
Form of Theophanes used in various languages.
Spanish and Portuguese form of Theophanes.
Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, and Polish form of Theophania.
Galician and Spanish form of Theophylaktos.
Italian feminine form of Greek Theophylaktos.
Lithuanian form of Theophilos via its latinized form Theophilus.
Variant of Teopisto. A bearer of this name is Teofisto Guingona Jr., the 11th Vice President of the Philippines.
Catalan and Polish form of Theophrastus.
Italian, Portuguese and Spanish form of Theophrastus.
Portuguese and Spanish form of Theogenes.
Name of Greek origin, which means "coming from God", from the elements theo and genes. This was the name of a Greek saint who died in 320.
Georgian form of Theogenes via its modern Greek transcription Theogenis.
Means "high priest" in Nahuatl, literally "possessor of divinity" from teotl "deity, god; divine force" and the possessive prefix -hua.
Polish and Ukrainian form of Theoktistos (see Theoctistus).
Polish form of Theoleptos via Theoleptus.

Modern Turkish and Bosnian form of the Mongol name Tümen via its Chinese form Touman.Notable bearers of this name include the Turkish rock singer Teoman (b. 1967), the Bosnian-Slovenian former basketball player Teoman Alibegović (b. 1967) and Teoman Kumbaracıbaşı (b. 1971), an Argentinian actor of Turkish descent.
Combination of Teo and the popular element -mar (cf. Leomar).
Macedonian, Polish and Romanian form of Theona.
Italian and Polish form of Theonilla.
Spanish, Italian, and Portuguese form of Theopistus.
Means "the life" in Māori, Cook Islands Māori, and Tahitian.
Means "the bad weather" from te meaning "the" and ori meaning "bad weather" or "move about, sway" in Māori.
Teos was the name of Pharaon Teos of the Thirtieth Dynasty of Egypt (380-343 BC).
Combination of Teodoro and Óscar.An early bearer of this name was Theóscar Sanoja, a Venezuelan physician of the mid twentieth century.
Georgian form of Theosteriktos via its modern Greek transcription Theostiriktos.
Unaccented form of Teótimo primarily used in the Philippines.
Khanty and Mansi form of Stepan.
Māori form of Zephaniah. As a feminine name, Te Pania refers to the legend of Pania, a Māori sea maiden.
Means "mountain leader", derived from Nahuatl yacatl "mountain" and yacana "to lead, to guide".
Possibly a diminutive form of Patape. Alternatively, could derive from Egyptian tpj "being on top of, standing atop", figuratively "first, main, best".
Means "something small, small amount" in Nahuatl. Alternately, may be used as a diminutive form of Tepi.

Means "the fox" in Māori from te pōkiha. 'Poki' also refers to land used for cultivating. So another possible meaning of this name could be "to clear the garden." This was the name of a Senior Ngāti Mutunga chief.
Means "he slanders", or perhaps "he is slandered", derived from Nahuatl tepotzitoa "to slander, to denigrate someone", literally "behind-talk".
Means "iron bolt, crossbow bolt" in Nahuatl, literally "metal arrow", from tepoztli "metal" and mitl "arrow, dart".
Probably a misspelling of Teppo, the Finnish form of Stephen. Occurs once in a tax record from 1582.

column3: 哲平, 哲兵, 鉄平, 鉄兵, 徹平, 徹兵(Japanese Kanji)|てっぺい(Japanese Hiragana)|テッペイ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name combines 哲 (tetsu, aki.raka, satoi, saba.ku, shi.ru, te') meaning "clear, philosophy", 鉄 (tetsu, kurogane, te') meaning "iron" or 徹 (tetsu, te') meaning "clear, penetrate, pierce, sit up (all night), strike home" with 平 (hyou, byou, hei, tai.ra, -daira, hira, hira-) meaning "even, flat, peace" or 兵 (hyou, hei, tsuwamono, he) meaning "army, private, soldier, strategy, tactics, troops, warfare."As a word, Teppei (撤兵) refers to a withdrawal of troops, although this is only a word and isn't used as a name.Bearers of this name include actor and singer Teppei Koike (小池 徹平) (1986-) and professional baseball infielder Teppei Tsuchiya (土谷 鉄平) (1982-).Note that the p̚ is an unreleased stop.
From te pua meaning "the flower" in Maori and Cook Islands Maori.
Means "patience" in Mwanga, a language spoken in Zambia and Tanzania.
Variant of Taquan, a combination of the popular phonetic elements ta and quan.
Means "war captain, seasoned warrior" in Nahuatl, a title given to a warrior who had captured four prisoners in battle.
Combination of the phonetic elements tay, kee and la modeled after the word tequila for the alcoholic drink. It comes ultimately from the name of a town in Mexico where the drink was made.
Diminutive of Theresa, Terri, and sometimes Terence.
Variant of Tara 1, possibly intended as an anagram of the English word Earth.

Likely derived from Teramo, the name of a city in the Abruzzo region of Italy. Its name comes from the first part of its ancient Roman name, which was Interamnia Praetutiorum. It essentially means "between the two rivers of the Praetutii" in Latin, derived from the Latin words inter meaning "between" and amnis meaning "river, stream" combined with Praetutii, the name of an Italic tribe. This refers to the fact that the city was originally the capital city of the Praetutii and that it was built at the confluence of two rivers, which are now known as the Tordino and the Vezzola.Notable Italian bearers of this name include the Genovese painter Teramo Piaggio (died before 1562), the Genovese merchant Teramo Canevari (1511-1592) and the Genovese missionary Teramo Castelli (1597-1659).
Variant of Eramu derived from an erroneous truncation of Sant'Eramu.
Polish and Serbian forms of Therapon.

column3: 照, 照司, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|てらし(Japanese Hiragana)|テラシ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From 照らし (terashi) meaning "illumination, shining" (compare Terasu).It can also be suffixed with a shi kanji, e.g. 司 meaning "office."This name is rarely used.

column3: 照, 曜(Japanese Kanji)|てらす(Japanese Hiragana)|テラス(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From the verb 照らす (terasu) meaning "to shine on, illuminate" (compare Terashi).It can also be written as 曜, normally used for the days of the week.This name is rarely used.

From te ra ura meaning "the red sun", or from te raura meaning "the thief" in Tahitian. Teraura was the name of a Tahitian woman that, along with the Bounty mutineers, co-founded the settlement on Pitcairn Island.
From the Tahitian te meaning "the" and rava meaning "dark, brownish".
Means "not that one" in Mongolian, from тэр (ter) meaning "that; he, she, it" and биш (bish) meaning "not, isn’t" or "other, different".
Of debated origin and meaning. Theories include a variant of Tersa and a derivation from Middle English tercel and Middle French terçuel "hawk; falcon.
Diminutive form of Teréz or Terézia.

column3: เทิดศักดิ์(Thai)
column12: Alternate transcription of Thai เทิดศักดิ์ (see Thoetsak).
Possibly an Appalachian form of Theresa.
From an Appalachian pronunciation of Tereatha.
Used by French politician Cécile Duflot for her daughter born in 2008.
Means "Terebinth tree" in Latin. This was the name of a purported pupil of Scythianus during the 1st to 2nd century AD.

Derived from the feminine form of Ancient Greek τέρην (teren) meaning "soft, delicate, gentle". This was the name of a Naiad daughter of the river Strymon in Greek mythology, mother of Thrassa by the god Ares.
Catalan, Languedocian and Gascon form of Terentius.
Spanish and Portuguese form of Terentianus.
Spanish and Galician form of Terence.
English form of Terentianus. This name was borne by a saint from the 2nd century AD.
Extended form of Terentius (see Terence). This name was borne by a Latin grammarian from the 2nd century AD.
Italian and Spanish form of Tereus.
Ukrainian diminutive or folk form of Terentiy.
Diminutive of Teresa. This name is borne by Argentine senator Teresina Luna.
Diminutive of Teresa, Teresita, and other related names.
Phonetic respelling of Theresa, trying to capture several European pronuncations of this name, for example the Italian pronunciation.
Catalan and Portuguese form of Tereus.

Probably derived from Greek τηρέω (tereo), which can mean "to guard" as well as "to obey, to observe, to attend to carefully". However, it is also possible that it is derived from Greek τερέω (tereo) meaning "to bore through, to pierce". In Greek mythology, Tereus was a Thracian king who was the son of the war god Ares and the naiad Bistonis.
Polynesian origin name, based on "reva", meaning "to rise" and "ura", meaning "red" or "brightness"; hence the meaning can be interpreted as "raising to the brightness", "raising to the light".
Russian and Ukrainian form of Tereus.
Banatswabian form of Teréz and Theres.
Kashubian form of Theresa and Hungarian variant of Terézia.

In medieval German literature, Terramer is the name of a heathen king from the epic poem Willehalm (13th century) written by the German poet Wolfram von Eschenbach (died around 1220). He was based on Desramé, a Saracen king from the French epic poem Aliscans (12th century), which was the main source of inspiration for Willehalm.The author likely altered the name in order to make it more palatable for a German audience, as the original name might have reminded them of medieval German des rame(n) meaning "of the frame". At the same time, he must have wanted to remain faithful to the source material and preserve the original meaning of the name, because it is probably no coincidence that Terramer closely resembles the Old French verb deramer meaning "to debranch, to prune, to trim (off)" as well as "to shed (off)". Also compare modern Spanish derramar or derramare (also derramaré) meaning "to spill, to leak" as well as "to shed".However, it must be said that we cannot rule out the possibility that the author decided to make up a brand new name for the king instead: completely unrelated, but yet somewhat resemblant of the original name. In that case, Terramer might possibly be a combination of Latin terra meaning "earth" and Middle French mer meaning "sea".

Fire worship, rock or water, not to the taste of the emerging Christian church.Needless to say, it was a typical manifestation of the Celtic pagan religion that keep with us for the common people until the late Middle Ages. Derived from Proto-Celtic teutā- meaning "people" or "tribe", likely inferring he was a protector of a people or tribe.In Celtic mythology he was a god worshipped in ancient Gaul and Britain. Today, he is best known under the name Toutatis, through the Gaulish oath/catchphrase 'By Toutatis!', invented for the Asterix comics by Goscinny and Uderzo. The spelling Toutatis, however, is authentic and attested by about ten ancient inscriptions. Teutates was one of three Celtic gods mentioned by the Roman poet Lucan in the 1st century AD. Some scholars attest he was a cognate of Mercury, while others say that each tribe had its own toutatis.

Teutberga (died 11 November 875) was a queen of Lotharingia by marriage to Lothair II. She was a daughter of Bosonid Boso the Elder and sister of Hucbert, the lay-abbot of St. Maurice's Abbey. In 855 she was married to the Carolingian Lothair II, the second son of Emperor Lothair I. Lothar II, at the time of marriage, already had a mistress named Waldrada. Teutberga was not capable of bearing children and Lothair's reign was chiefly occupied by his efforts to obtain an annulment of their marriage, prompted also by his affection for Waldrada.In 857, Lothair imprisoned Teutberga, accusing her of incest with her brother Hucbert before their marriage. Hucbert took up arms on her behalf, and after she had submitted successfully to the ordeal of boiling water, Lothair was compelled to restore her in 858. Lothair won the support of his brother, Emperor Louis II, by a cession of lands and obtained the consent of the local clergy to the annulment and to his marriage with Waldrada, which took place in 862. Teutberga escaped and took refuge in the court of Charles the Bald. She appealed to Pope Nicholas I who voided the decision of the synod and Lothair's marriage to Waldrada. An attack on Rome by the emperor was without result, and in 865 Lothair was threatened with excommunication and was convinced that Louis and Charles at their recent meeting had discussed the partition of his kingdom. Lothair accepted the pope's ruling and again took Teutberga back.Teutberga, however, either from inclination or compulsion, now expressed her desire for an annulment, and Lothair went to Italy to obtain the assent of the new pope, Adrian II. Placing a favorable interpretation upon the words of the pope, he set out on the return journey, when he was seized with fever and died at Piacenza on 8 August 869. Teutberga then retired to the abbey of St. Glossinde of Metz until her death on 11 November 875. The illegitimate status of Lothair II's only son, Hugo, by Waldrada, was not rectified before Lothair's death, and Lothair's kingdom was divided between his uncles Charles the Bald and Louis the German by the Treaty of Meerssen.

This was the name of a king of the Teutones who lived in 2nd-century BC Europe. The historical tribe the Teutones (or Teutoni) are generally classified as Germanic, though some ancient writers called them Celts. This name may be a variant of Theudebod, the first element presumably derived from Gaulish teuta or touta "people, tribe" (a cognate of *þeudō). It has also been suggested that the second element could be from Celtic boduus or boduo(s) "crow".

Rather than relating directly to this tribe, the broad term, Teutonic peoples or Teuton in particular, is used now to identify members of a people speaking languages of the Germanic branch of the language family generally, and especially, of people speaking German.

Harper led a corp of frontier rangers and Oneida scouts during the early years of the Revolutions New York border war. He also purchased a 230,000-ac tract of land from the Onoquaga Oneida in 1768, now part of Delaware County.

He represents sensation, and his female counterpart is Enion, who represents sexual urges. He is connected to the God the Father aspect of the Christian Trinity and is the begetter of Los.
