column12: From the Chinese 彤 (tóng) meaning "red, vermilion" and 晶 (jīng) meaning "crystal, clear, bright", 静 (jìng) meaning "quiet, still, gentle" or 净 (jìng) meaning "clear, pure".
From the Chinese 彤 (tóng) meaning "red, vermilion" and 珏 (jué) meaning "two pieces of jade joined together".
From the Chinese 彤 (tóng) meaning "red, vermilion" and 恋 (liàn) meaning "love, yearn for".
From the Chinese 彤 (tóng) meaning "red, vermilion" and 玲 (líng) meaning "tinkling of jade".
From the Chinese 彤 (tóng) meaning "red, vermilion" or 瞳 (tóng) meaning "pupil of the eye" and 美 (měi) meaning "beauty, beautiful".
From the Chinese 彤 (tóng) meaning "red, vermilion" and 梦 (mèng) meaning "dream" or 萌 (méng) meaning "bud, sprout".
From the Chinese 彤 (tóng) meaning "red, vermilion" and 女 (nǚ) meaning "woman, girl".
Derived from the Uzbek tong meaning "dawn" and nur meaning "ray, beam, light".
Derived from the Uzbek tong meaning "dawn" and po'lat meaning "steel, sword".
From the Chinese 彤 (tóng) meaning "red, vermilion" and 茜 (qiàn) meaning "madder" or "reeds".
From the Chinese 彤 (tóng) meaning "red, vermilion" and 晴 (qíng) meaning "fine weather".
From the Chinese 彤 (tóng) meaning "red, vermilion" and 蕊 (ruǐ) meaning "unopened flowers, flower buds".
From the Chinese 彤 (tóng) meaning "red, vermilion" and 烁 (shuò) meaning "shine, glitter, sparkle".
From the Chinese 彤 (tóng) meaning "red, vermilion" and 恬 (tián) meaning "calm, quiet, tranquil".
Xianbei name of Emperor Ming of Northern Zhou, Yuwen Yu.
From the Chinese 彤 (tóng) meaning "red, vermilion" and 霞 (xiá) meaning "rosy clouds".
From the Chinese 彤 (tóng) meaning "red, vermilion" and 晓 (xiǎo) meaning "dawn, daybreak".
From the Chinese 彤 (tóng) meaning "red, vermilion" and 馨 (xīn) meaning "fragrant, aromatic" or "distant fragrance" or 欣 (xīn) meaning "happy, joyous".
From the Chinese 彤 (tóng) meaning "red, vermilion" or 瞳 (tóng) meaning "pupil of the eye" and 璇 (xuán) meaning "beautiful jade" or "star".
From the Chinese 彤 (tóng) meaning "red, vermilion" and 雁 (yàn) meaning "wild goose" or 彦 (yàn) meaning "elegant".
From the Chinese 彤 (tóng) meaning "red, vermilion" and 瑶 (yáo) meaning "precious jade".
From the Chinese 彤 (tóng) meaning "red, vermilion" and 晔 (yè) meaning "bright, radiant, thriving".
From the Chinese 彤 (tóng) meaning "red, vermilion" and 怡 (yí) meaning "happy, joyful, harmony".
From the Chinese 彤 (tóng) meaning "red, vermilion" or 同 (tóng) meaning "same, similar" and 璎 (yīng) meaning "necklace of precious stones" or 莹 (yíng) meaning "luster of gems, bright, lustrous".

column3: 彤妤, 潼羽, 潼雨(Chinese)
column12: From the Chinese 彤 (tóng) meaning "red, vermilion" or 潼 (tóng) meaning "high, lofty" and 妤 (yú) meaning "beautiful, fair", 羽 (yǔ) meaning "feather", or 雨 (yǔ) meaning "rain".

column3: 彤云, 彤昀, 彤芸(Chinese)
column12: From the Chinese 彤 (tóng) meaning "red, vermilion" and 云 (yún) meaning "clouds", 昀 (yún) meaning "sunlight" or 芸 (yún) meaning "rue" or "art, talent, ability".
From the Chinese 彤 (tóng) meaning "red, vermilion" and 珍 (zhēn) meaning "precious, valuable, rare" or 真 (zhēn) meaning "clearly, really" or "real, true".
From the Chinese 彤 (tóng) meaning "red, vermilion" and 峥 (zhēng) meaning "high, lofty, noble".
From the Chinese 彤 (tóng) meaning "red, vermilion" and 芷 (zhǐ) meaning "angelica, iris".
From the Chinese 彤 (tóng) meaning "red, vermilion" and 梓 (zǐ) meaning "catalpa".
Short form of Antoni, traditionally found in the Engadine valley.
From Japanese 桃 (to) meaning "peach" combined with 仁 (ni) meaning "humaneness, benevolence, kindness". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Combination of the names Toni 2 and Ann.
Derived from the name of former British Prime Minister Tony Blair.
Diminutive of Antonija, occasionally used as a given name in its own right.
Variant of Tanisha. In the case of the Portuguese singer Tonicha (1946-), born Antónia de Jesus Montes Tonicha, it is apparently from her surname.
Diminutive of Antonie 1, occasionally used as a given name in its own right.
Diminutive of Antonija, occasionally used as a given name in its own right.

The first element of this name is possibly derived from Russian tónkij or tónkiy "thin, slim, slender", which is ultimately derived from Proto-Slavic tьnъkъ "thin". The second element is derived from Slavic mir "peace". As such, the name probably signifies something along the lines of "fragile peace".
Diminutive of Antonio, Antonina, and other names containing -ton-.
Greek short form of Antonios and Antonis and medieval Latvian short form of Antonijs.
Combination of the popular name element Ton (from names such as Antonia) and the common name suffix sha.

The first element of this name is possibly derived from Russian tónkij or tónkiy "thin, slim, slender", which is ultimately derived from Proto-Slavic tьnъkъ "thin". The second element is derived from Slavic slav "glory". As such, the name probably signifies something along the lines of "fragile glory". A bearer of this name is Tonislav Hristov (b. 1978), a Bulgarian film director.
Slovene short form of Antonija and Scandinavian short form of Antonia as well as a variant of Tonje.
A Dutch hypochoristic form of Antonia or Antonius.Tonke Dragt is a Dutch writer and illustrator of children's literature.
Diminutive of Antoni. Tońko was a character in Batyar Polish radio show Szczepko i Tońko, played by Henryk Vogelfänger.
Croatian and Slovene diminutive of Anton or Antonio.
Alternate transcription of Bengali তন্ময় (see Tanmay).
Originally a short form of Tõnis, now used as a given name in its own right.
Originally a German variant of Tönius, a diminutive of Antonius.
Diminutive form of Ton and pet form of Antonia, depending on the sex of the bearer.
Short form of Antonius, which was possibly inspired by the more popular Teunis. As a medieval Latvian name, it is a variant of Tonis.
Variant form of Tonnis. A known bearer of this name is the Dutch writer and poet Tonnus Oosterhoff (b. 1953).

Variant of Toni 1 and Toni 2, which are short forms of Anton and Antonia respectively. (As a Scandinavian feminine name, Toni could also be a variant of Tone 2.) Notable bearers of this name include Angolan-Dutch soccer player Tonny Vilhena (1995-) and Danish entrepreneur Tonny Sorenson (1964-). A fictional bearer is the title character of the 1962 Norwegian film Tonny.
Means either "a tiny man" or a "spirit" or "ghost". Name of Korra's father from Legend of Korra.
From the Thai ต้นตะวัน meaning 'early sun'.
From Spanish tonto (“fool”), from Western Apache kounʼnde (“wild rough people”).

Means "white wave" in Welsh. Tonwen (or simply Gwen) was the mother of Saint Cybi and sister of Non (herself mother of Wales' patron saint, David). It was used by John Cowper Powys for a character in his novel 'Porius' (1951).
Meaning "scout woman" from Lakota toƞweya meaning "scout" and win meaning "woman".
The main character, a virtuous young nobleman, in the Breton Legend 'The Three Wayfarers.'
Urdu form of Tuba, as well as an alternate Arabic transcription of the name.
The name of a 19th century Nez Perce leader. His name is a Nez Perce term, meaning "the sound made when striking any vibrant timber or metal with a hard substance".
Means "mountain uncle" or "mountain elder brother" in Kyrgyz.
Diminutive of Antonia, occasionally used as a given name in its own right.
Alternate transcription of Persian تورج (see Turaj).
Alternate transcription of Pashto تورپيکۍ/تورپېکۍ/تورپیکۍ (see Torpekai).
Alternate transcription of Pashto تورپيکۍ/تورپېکۍ/تورپیکۍ (see Torpekai).
Alternate transcription of Pashto تورپيکۍ/تورپېکۍ/تورپیکۍ (see Torpekai).

Short form of Antonia, Catharina and Cato 2. The -s might possibly indicate that the name originated from a diminutive of these names, such as Teunisje for Antonia (variants include Tonisje, Toonisje and Toonsje) and the extremely rare Catoosje for Cato (see Catootje, which is much more common).
Diminutive of Toos, as it contains the Dutch diminutive suffix -ke.A notable bearer of this name is the Dutch television presenter Tooske Ragas (b. 1974).
In Inuit mythology the goddess Tootega is a wizened old woman who lives in a stone hut and walks on water.
Means "zinc oxide". It is also Persian for a genus of sea urchins.
This is a female name used in the Medieval era. Probably a variant of Topazia, Topaz.
Spanish form of Topaz.While it is predominantly feminine in Latin American countries, in the Philippines, it is predominantly masculine.
Means "typhoon" in Indonesian, ultimately from Arabic طوفان (ṭūfān).

Place name of an area in western Los Angeles County, California. The area was originally named by the Tongva people and may mean "a place above."In the American television show 'Boy Meets World' (1993-2000), one of the protagonists is named Topanga.
Derived from the Lithuanian noun topazas meaning "topaz" (as in, the gemstone).
Elaborated from the Italian word topazio meaning "topaz".A notable bearer was Italian painter Topazia Alliata (1913-2015).
Diminutive of the composed name António Pedro.

From the name of the capital city of the US state of Kansas (see Topeka).This was also borne by a Mohave (Native American) woman who took in Olive Oatman (1837-1903) and her sister Mary Ann after the girls were abducted and traded to the Mohave tribe by another group of south-western Native Americans.
"Flaming sword" believed to be used by the kings
Alternate transcription of Tibetan སྟོབས་རྒྱས (see Tobgay).

Toph is the name of a character in Avatar: The Last Airbender (Avatar: The Legend of Aang in some regions), an American animated television series that aired on Nickelodeon from 2005 to 2008. Toph was written as 北方拓芙, giving her name the meaning "expanding lotus". The name itself is not a genuine Chinese name, and may have been intended as a pun on the English word "tough".

A toponym literally meaning "warm river" (from the Slavic element topao, toplo ''warm''). Toplica is a river in southern Serbia which gave its name to Toplica District with the administrative center in the city of Prokuplje. The name is primarily associated with Toplica Milan (Milan from Toplica), a Serbian knight who died during the Battle of Kosovo in 1389.
Alternate transcription of Bengali তপন (see Tapan).
Anglicized form of Topʉsana. It was borne by Topsannah (1858-1863), the short-lived daughter of Peta Nocona and Naduah (Cynthia Ann Parker), and younger sister of Quanah Parker.
Diminuitive of Topias, Tobias. Would be used for a baby or toddler.
Derived from the Uzbek to'q meaning "full, satiated, comfortable, prosperous" and boy meaning "rich, wealthy".
Derived from the Uzbek to'q meaning "full, satiated, comfortable, prosperous" and berdi meaning "gave".
Derived from the Uzbek to'q meaning "full, satiated, comfortable, prosperous" and jon meaning "spirit, soul".
Derived from the Uzbek to'q meaning "full, satiated, comfortable, prosperous" and the given name Muhammad.
Derived from to'q meaning "prosperous" and potentially in this context too "dark coloured" and oyim, an obsolete term for aristocratic women.
Derived from the Uzbek to'q meaning "full, satiated, comfortable, prosperous" and said meaning "fortunate".
Derived from the Uzbek to'q meaning "full, satiated, comfortable, prosperous" and sari meaning "yellow" or "fine, best".
Means "ninety" or "the ninety days of winter" in Uzbek.
Derived from the Uzbek to'qson meaning "ninety" or "the ninety days of winter" and sharif meaning "sacred, holy".
Derived from to'qson, refering to "the ninety days of winter" and sulu(v) meaning "beautiful".
Derived from the Uzbek to'q meaning "full, satiated, comfortable, prosperous" and temir meaning "iron".
Means "stability" or "stopping, holding, settling" in Mongolian.
From тоқ (toq) meaning "full" combined with жан (zhan) meaning "soul, life"
Old Norse variant and Faroese form of Þóra.

Means "tiger" in Japanese.In WWII, it was used as a codeword to indicated that a complete surprise has been achieved, as an acronym for totsugeki raigeki (突撃雷撃) meaning "lightning attack". It was referenced in 'Tora! Tora! Tora!', the 1970 American-Japanese war film that dramatized the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor
Derived from the Uzbek to'ra meaning "lord" and the given name Ali 1.
Derived from the Uzbek to'ra meaning "lord" and beg meaning "chieftan, master"
Derived from the Uzbek to'ra meaning "lord" and berdi meaning "gave".
Derived from to'ra meaning "nobleman" (and perhaps by extension "noble") and bibi meaning "learned woman".
Derived from the Uzbek to'ra meaning "lord" and bo'l meaning "to be".
Derived from to'ra meaning "nobleman" (and perhaps by extension "noble") and gul meaning "rose, flower".

column3: 虎彦, 寅彦, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 虎 (tora) meaning "tiger" combined with 彦 (hiko) meaning "boy, prince". Other kanji combinations are also possible.
Tora means "tiger" and Ichi means "one." Ichi usually refers to a person if it's at the end of the name, such as, "the powerful one."
Variation of Taraki, used in reference to Nur Muhammad Taraki.

column3: トラコ(Japanese Katakana)|とら子(Kanji/Hiragana)|トラ子(Kanji/Katakana)|虎子, 登羅子, 寅子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 虎 (tora) meaning "tiger" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.

From Japanese 寅 (tora) meaning "tiger" combined with 楠 (kusu) meaning "camphor tree". Other kanji combinations are possible.Notable bearer of this name is: Torakusu Yamaha (Japanese entrepreneur who was the founder of the Yamaha Corporation).
Derived from Japanese name Tora meaning "tiger" and Hawaiian Lei 1 meaning "garland, child". A notable character is Toralei Stripe from the Monster High franchise.
Derived from the Uzbek to'ra meaning "lord" and the give name Muhammad.
Derived from the Uzbek to'ra meaning "lord" and murod meaning "aim, wish, desire".
Formed from a diminutive of tor ‘lord’, ‘hero’, ‘champion’.
Derived from the Uzbek to'ra meaning "lord" and nazar meaning "look, glance".
Derived from the Uzbek to'ra meaning "lord" and niyoz meaning "entreaty, alms".

column3: 寅之助, 虎之介(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From the Japanese kanji 寅 (tora) meaning "Tiger (zodiac sign)" or 虎 (tora) meaning "tiger" combined with 之 (no), a possessive, and 助 (suke) meaning "assistente" or 介 (suke) meaning "concern oneself with; mediate".Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: トラオ(Japanese Katakana)|虎雄, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 虎 (tora) meaning "tiger" and 雄 (o) meaning "hero, manly". Other kanji combinations can be used.
Derived from to'ra meaning "nobleman" (and perhaps by extension "noble") and poshsha, , an endearing term for a girl or woman.
Derived from the Uzbek to'ra meaning "lord" and qobil meaning "capable, gifted" or "obediant".
Derived from the Uzbek to'ra meaning "lord" and qo'zi meaning "lamb".

column3: 寅, 寅史, 寅司, 寅嗣, 寅士, 寅志, 寅至, 虎, 虎史, 虎司, 虎嗣, 虎士, 虎志, 虎至, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 寅 (torashi, tora) meaning "sign of the tiger" or 虎 (torashi, tora) meaning "tiger, drunkard" combined with 史 (shi) meaning "history, chronicle", 司 (shi) meaning "director, official, govt office, rule, administer", 嗣 (shi) meaning "heir, succeed", 士 (shi) meaning "gentleman, scholar, samurai", 志 (shi) meaning "intention, plan, resolve, aspire, motive, hopes, shilling" or 至 (shi) meaning "climax, arrive, proceed, reach, attain, result in". Other kanji or kanji combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 寅輔, 寅助, 虎介, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 寅 (tora) meaning "the Tiger, the third of the twelve Earthly Branches" combined with 輔 (suke) meaning "help". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 寅斗, 寅翔, 寅都, 虎斗, 虎翔, 虎都, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 虎 (tora) meaning "tiger" or 寅 (tora) meaning "sign of the tiger" combined with 斗 (to), which refers to a Chinese constellation, 翔 (to) meaning "soar, fly" or 都 (to) meaning "metropolis, capital, all, everything". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Mongolian төр (tör) meaning "state, government" or "power, authority" and баатар (baatar) meaning "hero".
From Mongolian төр (tör) meaning "state, government" or "power, authority" and бадрах (badrakh) meaning "thrive, grow" or "blaze, shine".
From Mongolian төр (tör) meaning "state, government" or "power, authority" and баяр (bayar) meaning "joy, celebration".
Norwegian and Swedish form of Þórbergr.
Faroese combination of þórr "thunder" and bjartr "light", "shining".
From Mongolian төр (tör) meaning "state, government" or "power, authority" and болд (bold) meaning "steel".
Galician form of Torquatus and variant of Trocado.
Portuguese form of Torquatus and variant of Torquato.
Either a variant form of Tord, a combination of Þórðr, Tord and herr "army" or þórr "thunder" and sufix -dar/-ðar.
Danish and Norwegian form of Þórður and Tórður.
This name means oystercatcher. This was the name of a Owenga Moriori Chief named Torea Takarehe (d. 1876) who was the teacher of Moriori elder Hirawanu Tapu.
Meaning uncertain. This is the name of the hero in a 13th-century Dutch romance by Jacob van Maerlant; for the love of a maiden, Sir Torec defeats all the Knights of the Round Table except Arthur.
From төре (töre) meaning "morals" and combined with гелди (geldi) meaning "came, arrived"
Töregene Khatun (1242–1246) was the Great Khatun and regent of the Mongol Empire.
Means "What shall we say?". This is a name of exclamation or questioning given by a parent who is a lost for words regards the situation they are in
Possibly formed from Torfi or Old Norse torf "turf, sod" combined with heiðr "bright, clear; honour" or heiðr "heath". Also compare Heiður.

From Torfi or Old Norse torf "turf, sod" combined with hildr "battle". This was borne by the Icelandic author Torfhildur Þorsteinsdóttir Hólm (1845-1918), who is frequently referred to as the first Icelandic woman novelist.
Variant of Þórviðr and Tiǫrvi. May also be derived directly from Old Norse torf "turf".

Torgaut was the name of a Torgaut Jonson who was assumed to be the son of knight Jon Ragnvaldson who was the founder of the Smør house around the mid 13th century for being lord of Blindheim at the time, the Smør house was one of the few remaining original Norwegian houses that survived from being wiped out by the Black Plague.The name Torgaut seems to be an Early Medieval diversion of Þórgautr
Meaning unknown. In Georgian folklore, this is the name of a Khevsur hero from the village of Mutso in the historical Georgian province of Khevsureti.
Derived from the Old English elements torht "bright, shiny" and helm "helmet".
Derived from the Old English elements torht "bright, shiny" and here "army". This was the name of an 8th century Bishop of Hereford.
Derived from the Old English elements torht "bright, shiny" and ræd "advice, counsel, wisdom". This was the name of Torthred of Thorney, a saint and hermit of the 9th century.

column3: 桃李, 冬里, 桃里, 桃梨, 桃理, 冬莉, 東李, 東里, 桐璃(Japanese Kanji)|とうり(Japanese Hiragana)|トウリ(Japanese Katakana)

column3: 利, 敏, 俊, 慧, 淑, 年, 歳, 才, 寿, 登志, 登士, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|とし(Japanese Hiragana)|トシ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Either from classical adjectives 利し (toshi) meaning "sharp" and 敏し (toshi) meaning "keen, clever" (where 俊 shares a similar meaning) or noun 年/歳/才 (toshi) meaning "year; age." Other kanji in relation to these derivations include, from the adjectives, 慧 meaning "wisdom," 淑 meaning "graceful, ladylike, modest, well-mannered" or, from the noun, 寿 meaning "congratulations; longevity," among others. 2-kanji combinations are possible, combining a to kanji, e.g. 登 meaning "ascent," with a shi kanji, like 志 meaning "will, aim, goal" or 士 meaning "warrior; samurai."In use as a (rare) feminine name before the Meiji Period (1868-1912), Toshi saw increase of its usage for both genders (though still mainly feminine) in that period. Nowadays, it is mainly used as a (largely male) nickname for names like Toshihiro or Toshiyuki.

column3: 利江, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|としえ(Japanese Hiragana)|トシエ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 利 (toshi) meaning "benefit, advantage" combined with 江 (e) meaning "bay, inlet". This name can be formed from other combinations of kanji as well.

column3: 雋文, 雋史, 利文, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 雋 (toshi) meaning "to excel" combined with 文 (fumi) meaning "writing" or 史 (fumi) meaning "history". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 俊春, 敏春, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column3: 俊日出, 利秀, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 俊 (toshi) meaning "talented, handsome" or 利 (toshi) meaning "benefit, advantage" combined with 秀 (hide) meaning "excellent, outstanding". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 敏彦, 俊彦, 利彦, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|としひこ(Japanese Hiragana)|トシヒコ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 敏 (toshi) meaning "quick, clever, sharp", 俊 (toshi) meaning "talented, handsome" or 利 (toshi) meaning "benefit, advantage" combined with 彦 (hiko) meaning "boy, prince". Other combinations of kanji can form this name as well.

column3: 敏弘, 敏宏, 敏浩, 敏博, 俊弘, 俊裕, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|としひろ(Japanese Hiragana)|トシヒロ(Japanese Katakana)

This name can be formed from other combinations of kanji as well.

column3: 稔永, 歳剛, 登志久, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 歳 (toshi) meaning "year" or 稔 (toshi) meaning "to ripen" combined with 剛 (hisa) meaning "sturdy" or 永 (hisa) meaning "eternity, long, lengthy". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: トシヒト(Japanese Katakana)|としひと(Japanese Hiragana)|敏士, 年一, 利仁, 歳等, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 敏 (toshi) meaning "quick, sharp" or 年 (toshi) meaning "year, counter for years" combined with 人 (hito) meaning "person". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 寿一郎, 俊一郎, 敏一郎, 利一郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 寿 (toshi) meaning "longevity, long life", 一 (ichi) meaning "one" combined with 郎 (rou) meaning "son". Other combinations of kanji characters are also possible.

column3: 利家, 俊家, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 利 (toshi) meaning "advantage, profit, benefit" and 家 (ie) meaning "family, house(hold)". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 歳二, 疾士, 寿次, 鋭治, 鋭次, 鋭至, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 歳 (toshi) meaning "a year (or years) of age" combined with 二 (ji) meaning "two". Other kanji combinations can also form this name.

column3: 敏雄, 敏克, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 敏 (toshi) meaning "quick, clever, sharp" and 雄 (katsu) meaning "male, manly". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 俊和, 俊一, 利和, 利一, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 俊 (toshi) meaning "talented, handsome" or 利 (toshi) meaning "benefit, advantage" combined with 和 (kazu) meaning "harmony, peace" or 一 (kazu) meaning "one". Other kanji cominations are possible.

column3: 俊樹, 敏喜, 俊輝, 寿樹, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 俊 (toshi) meaning "sagacious, genius, excellence" and 樹 (ki) meaning "timber tress, wood". This name can also be formed of other kanji combinations.

column3: トシマサ(Japanese Katakana)|としまさ(Japanese Hiragana)|紀正, 歳正, 年正, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

Other kanji combinations are possible.A famous bearer of this name is former Japanese football player Toshimasa Toba (1975-).

column3: 冬四郎, 冬史郎, 冬獅郎, 東四郎, 東史郎, 十四郎(Japanese Kanji)|とうしろう(Japanese Hiragana)|トウシロウ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name combines 冬 (tou, fuyu) meaning "winter" or 東 (tou, higashi) meaning "east" with 四郎 (shirou) meaning "fourth son", from 四 (shi, yo, yo'.tsu, yo.tsu, yon) meaning "four" and 郎 (ryou, rou, otoko) meaning "son", or 史郎 (shirou), from 史 (shi) meaning "chronicle, history" and 郎.It can also be used as 十四郎 (which can also be romanised as Jūshirō) which means "14th son", from 十 (ji', juu, ju', to, too) meaning "ten", 四 and 郎.One bearer of this name is Tōshirō Hitsugaya (日番谷 冬獅郎), a character from manga and anime, Bleach, who is, at one point, voted the most popular character. Truncated form of Antouanètt and Entouanètt.
From Japanese 桃園 (touen) meaning "peach orchard".
Vernacular form of Antoine used in several regions of France, including the Poitou and the Bourbonnais. This is not commonly used as an official given name.

Bengali transcription of Arabic توفيق (see Tawfiq), as well as an alternate transcription chiefly used in Northern Africa.
From Japanese 東 (tou) meaning "east" combined with 吾 (go) meaning "I, me". Other kanji combinations are possible.Famous bearer of this name is Japanese architect Togo Murano.
Alternate transcription of Urdu توحید or Bengali তাওহিদ (see Tawhid).
Alternate transcription of Bengali তাওহিদ (see Tawhid).

From Japanese 冬至 (touji) meaning "winter solstice".

column3: 藤二郎, 藤次郎, 藤詞郎, 東治郎, 東次郎, 十二郎, 稲二郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 藤 (tou) meaning "wisteria", 二 (ji) meaning "two" combined with 郎 (rou) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Means "good perfume" from Kanji 董 (tou) meaning "correct" and 香 (ka) meaning "incense, perfume".A famous bearer is character Touka (surname Kirishima) in 'Tokyo Ghoul'.

column3: 東権, 桐軒, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
冬季, 唐貴, 斗紀, 東禧, 桃李, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 冬季 (touki) meaning "winter" or from Japanese 唐 (tou), referring to the Tang Dynasty, which ruled China from 618 to 907, 斗 (tou), which refers to a Chinese constellation, 東 (tou) meaning "east" or 桃 (tou) meaning "peach" combined with 貴 (ki) meaning "expensive, worthful, precious", 紀 (ki) meaning "chronicle", 禧 (ki) meaning "happiness, congratulations" or 李 (ki) meaning "plum". Other kanji combinations are possible.

A fictional bearer is Toulane Thomas from the American Girl novel "McKenna" and the film adaptation "An American Girl: McKenna Shoots for the Stars". It is occasionally used as a given name in various countries.
Means "dawning" in Arabic. Derived from Arabic word "tulin", and possibly a variant of Tuleen.
Transferred from the surname Toulouse, meaning "place of the fertile land". A notable bearer was Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec, the French painter (1864-1901).

column3: 鉄, 顛, 屠, 當真, 東馬, 桃真, 藤馬, 騰舞, 瞳真, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 鉄 (touma) meaning "iron", 顛 (touma) meaning "overturn, summit, origin", 屠 (touma) meaning "slaughter, butcher, slay", 東 (tou) meaning "east", 桃 (tou) meaning "peach", 藤 (tou) meaning "wisteria", 騰 (tou) meaning "leaping up, jumping up, rising, advancing, going", 瞳 (tou) meaning "pupil (of eye)" or 當 (tou) meaning "bear, accept, undertake, just" combined with 真 (ma) meaning "true, reality", 馬 (ma) meaning "horse", or 舞 (ma) meaning "dance". Other kanji or kanji combinations can form this name as well.

A name used in Africa, usually in the Dazaga language, meaning "hope of life". Typically given to infants born around the dry season, with the hope that the child will survive. Notably, the name was given to Sahelanthropus tchadensis - the skull of a likely human ancestor that, at the time, was found the farthest West any human ancestor had been found.
Walloon, Guernésiais and Provençal form of Thomas.
Alternate transcription of Persian تورج (see Turaj).
Modern Persian form or variant transcription of Turan.
From the surname Touré, possibly a French form of Soninke tùùré "elephant".

From the name of a type of crystal.This crystal's English name is derived from Sinhalese tòramalli, via French tourmaline. The meaning of this word seems to be not entirely certain, although one theory suggests that it simply means "cornelian".As a name, Tourmaline has been in use since the late 20th century.

From the name of a mythical herb that is supposed to cause people to repeatedly run around in circles if stepped on (the name of the herb is derived from the French tourment meaning "torture"). This is the name of the wicked ogress who raises Aimée in Madame d'Aulnoy's fairy tale The Bee and the Orange Tree (1697).
Contraction of Saint Ours recorded in French-speaking Switzerland up until the 19th century.
Late medieval variant of Toussainte recorded up until the 17th century.

column3: 兜太, 通太, 登太, 東太, 桃太, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 兜 (tou) meaning "helmet", 通 (tou) meaning "pass through", 登 (tou) meaning "rise, ascend", 東 (tou) meaning "east" or 桃 (tou) meaning "peach" combined with 太 (ta) meaning "thick, big". Other kanji combinations are possible.

Means "all-fair" in French. This is the name of the princess in Madame d'Aulnoy's fairy tale ''The Yellow Dwarf'' (1697). Toutebelle is a beautiful but vain princess who is promised to an ugly dwarf, but decides to marry a king instead. She is later kidnapped by the dwarf. When the king goes to save her, the dwarf murders him leading Toutebelle to die of grief.

column3: 冬羽, 藤和, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 冬 (tou) meaning "winter" or 藤 (tou) meaning "wisteria" combined with 羽 (wa) meaning "feathers" or 和 (wa) meaning "peace, harmony". Other kanji combinations are also possible.

This name is derived from Tovar, a village that was adopted as the surname of a Castilian noble house that received lordship of the village from King Fernando III. The surname was first found in Asturias, a notable Christian kingdom in medieval Spain.Toval Randonneur, known as Zero Artisan Toval, is a B-Rank Bracer that is affiliated with the Erebonian branch of the Bracer Guild in the Trails series. He first appears in the Ring of Judgement manga, followed by Trails of Cold Steel I, Trails of Cold Steel II and Trails of Cold Steel III.Sources:https://www.houseofnames.com/tovar-family-cresthttps://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tovar_(surname)https://kiseki.fandom.com/wiki/Toval_Randonneur
Modernized spelling of Touilt, itself a Middle English form of the hypothetical Old Norse name Tófa-Hildr.
Meaning unknown. This is the name of Indian Malayalam actor Tovino Thomas.
Russian form of Toviyyah (see Tobiah) via its Biblical Greek form Tobias.
Russian name for Tautvilas of Polotsk and Lithuania.
Ukrainian name for Tautvilas of Polotsk and Lithuania.
Means "peacock" in Azerbaijani, ultimately from Arabic طاووس (ṭāwūs).

Originates in Puerto Rico from the word "tougue"

Means "beauty" or "beautiful". Traditionally the name was given to a child born after death(s) of a preceding sibling. The belief was that this new born is beautiful for death or beautiful for the soil.

Alternate transcription of Bengali তৌসিফ (see Tawsif).
Means "that which I love" in Yoruba.
Catalan and Portuguese form of Toxeus.

Transferred use of the surname Toxey.A known bearer of this name is the American entrepreneur and conservationist Toxey Haas (b. 1960).

Variant spelling of Toya.Though this name is rarely used in the United States, it received a slight boost in popularity in Britain (mostly in England) in 1981 and again in 1998, first as a result of the release of the album Anthem by English singer and actress Toyah Willcox (1958-) (often referred to by her first name) and then, most likely, as a result of the appearance of Toyah Battersby, played by Georgia Taylor, in the popular soap opera Coronation Street.
Diminutive of Antonia, Victoria and similar names.

column12: From 豊 (toyo) meaning "luxuriant, lush, bountiful" combined with 昭 (aki) meaning "bright, luminous" or 秋 (aki) meaning "autumn" . Other kanji combinations are possible.

From 豊 (toyo) meaning "luxuriant, lush, bountiful" combined with 絵 (e) meaning "painting, drawing, sketch, etch, picture" or 恵 (e, megu, megumi) meaning "favour, benefit, blessing". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column12: From Japanese 豊 (toyo) meaning "luxuriant, lush, bountiful" combined with 彦 (hiko) meaning "boy, prince". Other Kanji combinations can form this name as well.

column12: From Japanese 豊 (toyo) meaning "luxurious, lush, bountiful" combined with 和 (kazu) meaning "harmony, peace", 一 (kazu) meaning "one", 数 (kazu) meaning "number, amount", 千 (kazu) meaning "thousand" or 策 (kazu) meaning "scheme, plan, means". Other kanji combinations can also form this name.
Derived from the Uzbek toy meaning "colt" and o'roz meaning "hope".

column12: From 豊 (toyo) meaning "bountiful, abundant" and 信 (shige) meaning "faith, trust, believe". Other kanji combinations are usable.
Means "something to rejoice about" in Yoruba, also used as a short form for other names ending in -toyosi including Olutoyosi or Oluwatoyosi.

From the name of the Japanese car company (See Mercedes, Ferrari and Porsche).From Japanese トヨタ (Toyota), from the name of the Toyoda family. The spelling was changed to Toyota because of a belief that it sounded better, or because トヨタ takes eight strokes to write, and 8 is considered lucky.Toyota Motor Corporation (Japanese: トヨタ自動車株式会社, Hepburn: Toyota Jidōsha KK) is a Japanese multinational automotive manufacturer headquartered in Toyota, Aichi, Japan. In 2017, Toyota's corporate structure consisted of 364,445 employees worldwide and, as of December 2019, was the tenth-largest company in the world by revenue. Toyota is the largest automobile manufacturer in Japan, and the second-largest in the world behind Volkswagen, based on 2018 unit sales.

column3: 豊堂, 豊貴, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 豊 (toyo) meaning "luxuriant, lush, bountiful" and 堂 (taka) meaning "temple, shrine, hall". Other kanji combinations can be used.

From Japanese 豊 (toyo) meaning "abundant, lush", 玉 (tama) meaning "jewel, gem, ball" and 姫 (hime) meaning "princess". This is the name of a Japanese goddess who appears in the Kojiki in the episode of the 'Luck of the Sea and the Luck of the Mountain'. She is the paternal grandmother of Emperor Jimmu, the legendary first emperor of Japan.
Masculine Japanese name derived from 豊 (toyo) meaning "abundent, lush" and 年 (toshi) meaning "new, new year".

Portuguese short form of the double first name António José.
Possibly means "yellow parrot bracelet", from Nahuatl toztli "yellow-headed amazon (bird)" and macuextli "bracelet".
Means "someone with a voice" or "he who can sing" in Nahuatl, from tozquitl "voice" and the possessive suffix -hua.
Perhaps from Sino-Vietnamese 詐 (trá) meaning "cunning, deceitful".
From Sino-Vietnamese 卓 (trác) meaning "tall, elevated, oustanding".
From Sino-Vietnamese 濯 (trạc) meaning "to wash, cleanse" or 擢 (trạc) meaning "to select, promote".
Means "rosewood" in Vietnamese, or from Sino-Vietnamese 側 (trắc) meaning "side, slant". This was the name of the elder of the Trưng sisters, Vietnamese cultural heroes.
Combination of Trace and the popular name suffix lyn.
From Sino-Vietnamese 澤 (trạch) meaning "pool, pond, brilliance, favor" or 宅 (trạch) meaning "residence, dwelling, house".
Possibly derived from Greek τραχύς (trachys) meaning "rough, rugged, harsh".
From Middle English trak, tracke, from Old French trac, from a Germanic source akin to Old Norse traðk (“a track; path; trodden spot”).
Derived from the English word tracker meaning "one who tracks".
An earl who was the father of Elena, the brother of King Odus, and the uncle of Enide, Erec’s wife.
Combination of Tracy and the popular suffix lyn.
A Knight of the Round Table defeated in a tournament against the Queen’s Knights.
From the place name Cape Trafalgar in Spain, location of a sea battle in 1805 won by the British fleet under the command of Admiral Nelson.
The name of a legendary Cherokee princess.
From Sino-Vietnamese 廌 (trãi) referring to a kind of mythological deer. This was the name of the Confucian scholar and strategist Nguyễn Trãi (1380–1442).
Sicilian and Sardinian form of Traianus (see Trajan 1).
Either a transferred use of the surname Trail or simply from the English word trail.
Feminine version of the name Tremaine or Traimian.
Transferee use of the surname Trainor.

Means "three gems, three jewels" from Thai ไตร (trai) meaning "three" and รัตน์ (rat) meaning "gem, jewel". This is the Thai name for the Three Jewels (the Buddha, the Dharma and the Sangha) in Buddhist philosophy.
Means "tricolour" from Thai ไตร (trai) meaning "three" and รงค์ (rong) meaning "colour".
From Serbian трајати (trajati) meaning "to last", "to endure".
Spanish and Portuguese form of Trajan 1.

Derived from Latin traiectum "crossing (of a river)". It was the name of two Dutch cities, Utrecht and Maastricht (Mosa Traiectum).Borne as a second given name by Anna Trajectina von Brederode († 23. Februar 1672).
Derived from the Russian noun трактор (traktor) meaning "tractor" (as in, the agricultural vehicle). This name was used by Communist parents who were eager to reject traditional names.

Derived from the Russian noun трактор (traktor) meaning "tractor" (as in, the agricultural vehicle) combined with the Russian possessive suffix -ин (-in). This name was created by Communist parents who were eager to reject traditional names.
Feminine form of Traktorin. This name was used by Communist parents who were eager to reject traditional names.
Means "plants of genus Canarium (an olive-like plant)" in Vietnamese (cf. Cà Na).
Means "melaleuca (plants in the myrtle family)" in Vietnamese.
From Sino-Vietnamese 簪 (trâm) meaning "hairpin". It can also refer to someone noble and wealthy (see Trâm Anh).
From Sino-Vietnamese 湛 (trạm) meaning "deep, profound, clear".
From Sino-Vietnamese 沉 (trầm) meaning "to sink", referring to agarwood (see Trầm Hương).
From Sino-Vietnamese 簪 (trâm) meaning "hairpin" and 纓 (anh) meaning "a decorative band worn on a hat", referring to nobility and landed gentry.
Means "agarwood", from Sino-Vietnamese 沉 (trầm) meaning "to sink" and 香 (hương) meaning "fragrant".
From Sino-Vietnamese 茶眉 (trà my) meaning "camellia".
From Sino-Vietnamese 鎮 (trấn) meaning "to suppress, to guard, town".

From Sino-Vietnamese 壯士 (tráng sỹ) meaning "warrior, person with strong health and willpower".
Means "to avoid, to refrain from" in Vietnamese.
Means "to sway, lose balance" in Vietnamese.
From a non-Sino-Vietnamese reading of Chinese 幀 (tranh) meaning "painting, picture" or from Sino-Vietnamese 爭 (tranh) meaning "to compete, fight for".
In the case of Argentinian pilot Traniela Campolieto (1976-), it is possibly a combination of the Latin word trans "across, beyond", found in the word transgender, and Daniela.
Bosnian and Croatian form of Tranquillus.
Likely from the English word tranquil.

Spanish form of Tranquillinus. Notable bearers of this name include Tranquilino Luna, a 19th-century American politician, and Saint Tranquilino Ubiarco Robles (1899-1928), a Mexican priest who was martyred during the persecutions of the Mexican Revolution and canonized in 2000.
Feminine form of Tranquillinus. This was the name of the wife of Emperor Gordian III.
Diminutive of Tranquillus, as is evidenced by the suffix -inus. This was the name of a saint from the 3rd century AD.
From Latin tranquilitas which means "tranquility, serenity, calm".Tranquilitas was an ancient Roman goddess and personification of tranquility, security, calmness, peace.
Derived from Latin tranquillus "quiet, calm, still". A known bearer of this name was Gaius Suetonius Tranquillus, a Roman historian from the 2nd century AD.
Spanish and Portuguese form of Tranquillus.
Lombardic form of Thrasamund. This was the name of several rulers in Medieval Italy.
A niece of Arthur and Morgan who appears in the romance Huon de Bordeaux.
Derived from Spanish transfiguración meaning "transfiguration," referring to an event where Jesus is transfigured and becomes radiant in glory upon a mountain.
From Latin trans "across, over, beyond; on the other side" combined with Latin mundus "world". This phrase, more often used as a byname, was also rarely used as a given name.

From a non-Sino-Vietnamese reading of Chinese 真 (trấn) meaning "true" and 武 (vũ) meaning "military, martial". This is another name of Huyền Vũ (see Xuanwu), referring specifically to the Taoist god of the north. In Vietnamese mythology, he helped An Dương Vương fight demons while building the citadel of Cổ Loa.
From a non-Sino-Vietnamese reading of Chinese 潮 (trào) meaning "tide" or "to overflow" (compare Triều).

Derived from Greek τραπεζεύς (trapezeus) meaning "of a table, at a table", which is ultimately derived from Greek τράπεζα (trapeza) meaning "table". Also compare the modern English word trapeze, which is etymologically related. In Greek mythology, Trapezeus was one of the sons of the Arcadian king Lycaon.
Possibly a transferred use of the surname Trapp.
I was unable to find a meaning but it has been used to name a tropical cyclone
Alternate transcription of Tibetan བཀྲ་ཤིས (see Tashi).
Spanish and Portuguese form of Thrasybulus.
Italian and Spanish form of Thrasydaeus.
Variant of Tarsilla. This name was borne by an aunt of Pope Gregory I, who herself is venerated as a saint.
Galician, Spanish and Portuguese form of Thrasymachus.
Unknown origin, possibly related to the Germanic roots traustaz ("reliable, firm") and mers ("famous") (cf. Teodomiro).
From Sino-Vietnamese 𣉙 (trát) meaning "bright, sunrise, dawn". This was the personal name of the seventh emperor of the Lý dynasty, Lý Long Trát.
Vietnamese form of Sajai, referring to a king of Champa who died in 1474.
Vietnamese form of Sajan, referring to a king of Champa, Maha Sajan, who died in 1471.
From Old Norse traustr meaning "trusty, firm, strong".

Travalaha was a Germanic goddess known from an inscription found in Cologne, Germany. The origin and meaning of her name are uncertain, however one theory suggests a derivation from Proto-Norse þrāwō "to long for". Her functions have been lost to time.
Transferred from the surname Travanti due to the popularity of the actor Daniel J. Travanti.
Possibly transferred use of the surname Traver.
Transferred usage of the surname Traverse or from the English word "traverse".
From Ukrainian трава (trava), meaning "grass". Extremely rare.
From Ukrainian трава (trava), meaning "grass". Possibly influenced by Zhaneta. Extremely rare.
Likely an invented name made to sound like other popular names like Braxton or Jaxton.
Invented name created using the suffix aden. First used in 2002.
Transferred use of the surname Traylor.

Meaning unknown. It might possibly be an alteration (through metathesis) of Tarzana, which is said to mean "strange woman" in Bantu. Also compare Tarzan.A notable bearer of this name is the African-American actress Trazana Beverley (b. 1945).
Armenian form of Tiridata, which was also used in Georgia in older times.
From Middle English (in the senses ‘negotiate’ and ‘discuss a subject’) from Old French traitier, from Latin tractare ‘handle’, frequentative of trahere ‘draw, pull’.
Bert spelled backwards, or a short form of Trebor.
The name of a Lusitanian deity, most likely a goddess.

Lusitanian name believed to be the name of a goddess, which appears in a single inscription: the Cabeço das Fraguas inscription from present-day Portugal. It is likely derived from Celtic *trebo- meaning "house, dwelling place" and an uncertain second element, potentially the Lepontic and Ligurian word pala probably meaning "sacred stone", or the second element might mean "flat land" or "protector". In the inscription, Trebopala is recorded as receiving a single sheep (oilam).

Transferred use of the surname Tregory.The meaning of the name Tregurtha is not wholly certain: one source states that it is derived from Cornish tre-gorha meaning "the town for hay" or "the hay town", while an other source states that it is derived from Cornish tre-kerghan meaning "homestead of oats". Yet another source states that it is either derived from Cornish tre-c(g)ar(dh)then meaning "homestead with a thicket" or from Cornish tre-gerthan meaning "rowan-tree farm". All etymologies are different from each other, but have one thing in common with each other: all use the Cornish word tre meaning "homestead, dwelling" as well as "settlement, village". As such, it seems that at least the first element of the name is reasonably certain (or at least more so than the second element). Also compare other surnames of Cornish origin, such as Trevelyan.There are no well-known bearers of Tregory as a surname and as a given name, which is not very surprising, considering that the surname was already quite rare to begin with (and so the frequency of the name as a given name is even lower). But you can find a few living bearers if you carefully look through Google and Facebook. A fair number of the (often American) men who have this name for a given name, tend to be nicknamed Treg. In the meantime, it might perhaps be worth noting that there is at least one well-known bearer of the surname Tregury, which has the same etymological origin (as I mentioned earlier). This is Michael Tregury (1399-1471), a distinguished medieval archbishop and scholar of Cornish origin.

Possibly from Latin tristis meaning "sad, morose". This name was used by Jacob van Maerlant in his Arthurian romance Torec (c. 1280), where it belongs to the mother of the title character, a princess born posthumously to King Briant of the Red Island and Mariole. Tristouse's mother owned a magic golden circlet and, when it was stolen, Mariole fell into poverty and despair. She cast Tristouse into the sea. Tristouse washed up in the kingdom of King Ydor, whom she married when she came of age. Tristouse and Ydor had a son named Torec, and at his birth she laughed for the first time. Sir Torec eventually reclaimed the stolen circlet. Tristouse died shortly after Torec's marriage to Miraude, the most beautiful maiden in the world, who had agreed to marry Torec if he could defeat all the Knights of the Round Table.

This given name is best known for being the name of the 7th-century saint Trofimena, who was born and raised on the island of Sicily. During her lifetime, Sicily was a province of the Byzantine Empire, where Greek was the primary language. As such, the original form of her name must have been Trophimena (alternatively Trophimene), especially if you take into account the fact that the Italian language did not yet exist in the 7th century. It only began to develop in the 12th century, which means that we should conclude that Trofimena is a later form and therefore the Italian form of Trophimena.With that said, the name is clearly of Greek origin. It is most likely a compound name that consists of the Greek noun τροφή (trophe) meaning "nourishment, food" combined with either the Greek noun μένος (menos) meaning "mind, strength, force" (see Philomena) or the Greek verb μένω (meno) meaning "to stay, to remain" as well as "to last, to withstand" (see Menelaus). As such, the meaning of the name is either "nourishment of the mind" or "to stay nourished".Alternatively, the name is a variant of Trophimina, a Latin diminutive of Trophima. This seems a bit less likely however, given the strong presence of the Greek language on Sicily both at the time and when it was still part of the Roman Empire (from the 3rd century BC to the 5th century AD). Sicilians were culturally and linguistically Greek and remained so during Roman rule and subsequently Germanic rule and Byzantine rule, which probably means that they (or at least those who did not belong to the Sicilian elite) had little contact with the Romans and their native language (Latin). As a result, they had little need to latinize their native Greek names or to re-hellenize Greek names that were latinized (as essentially would have been the case if Trophimena came from Trophimina).

Transferred use of the surname Trott.One is that it is a medieval English surname, in which case it can be an occupational surname that refers to a messenger, either derived from Middle English trot(ten) meaning "to walk fast" or Old French troter, which also means "to walk fast". However, it can also be a descriptive surname, meaning that it is derived from a nickname. In that case it is derived from Old English trothe meaning "loyalty", in reference to the loyal and trustworthy nature of the original bearer of the nickname. And lastly, it can also be a matronymic surname, which means that it is derived from the given name of a female ancestor. This name was Troit, Troyt or Trote, which are variants of Trude, which is a short form of Gertrude, Hiltrude and other names that end in -trude. Also compare the German equivalent Traud (also spelled Traut), which is a short form of Gertraud, Hiltraud, Waltraud and other names that end in -traud.Another possibility is that it is a (sometimes anglicized) medieval German surname, in which case it can be an occupational surname that refers to a grape-treader, derived from Middle High German trot(t)e meaning "winepress". However, the surname can also be a descriptive surname that (mockingly) refers to a slow person, in which case it is derived from Middle High German trotten meaning "to trot".

Derived from the Georgian noun ცისკარი (tsiskari) meaning "sunrise, dawn, daybreak". It is a compound word that consists of Georgian ცის (tsis) meaning "of the sky" and Georgian კარი (kari) meaning "door". As such, a more literal meaning of the word would be "door of the sky" or "opening of the sky".ცისკარა (tsiskara) is also the Georgian name for the perennial herb lovage (Levisticum officinale). Obviously, the plant's name ultimately has the same etymology as the Georgian word for "dawn".

Derived from Georgian ცისმარა (tsismara) or ცისმარე (tsismare) meaning "long, lifelong". Also compare the related Georgian adjective ცისამარა (tsisamara), which roughly means "single day, whole day".All of the words mentioned above are compound words, of which the first element consists of Georgian ცის (tsis) meaning "of the sky". The second element appears to be derived from (or related to) the Georgian adverb მარად (marad) meaning "always, eternally, forever". Also compare the Georgian adjective მარადიული (maradiuli) meaning "eternal, everlasting" and the archaic Georgian adverb მარადღე (maradghe) meaning "every day".In summary, one could say that a more literal meaning of these words (and by extension this name) is perhaps "infinity of the sky".

Either derived from Georgian ცოტა (tsota) meaning "a little, few" or from Georgian მცოდნე (mtsodne) meaning "able, adept".This name is best known for being the name of Tsotne Dadiani, a 13th-century Georgian nobleman who participated in an attempt of the Georgian nobility to overthrow the Mongol rule of Georgia. This ultimately failed and most of the noblemen involved were arrested by the Mongols. Dadiani was one of the few who were not arrested, but he insisted upon sharing the fate of his kinsmen, after learning that the Mongols were torturing them. The Mongols were so impressed with his sacrifice that they ultimately set him and the other noblemen free. This act of selflessness made him one of the most popular historical figures of Georgia, which ultimately led to his canonization by the Georgian Orthodox Church in 1999.

column3: 円, 円良, 都夫良, 都布良, 豆布良(Japanese Kanji)|つぶら(Japanese Hiragana)|ツブラ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name can be used as 円 (en, mado, mado.ka, maru, maru.i, maro.yaka, tsubura) meaning "circle, round" or it can be combined with 良 (ryou, i.i, yo.i, ra) meaning "good." As a word, it (円ら) refers to something round and cute, especially the eyes.It was first recorded in the Kofun period (250–538), belonging to Katsuragi no Tsubura (葛城円), whose daughter was one of Emperor Yūryaku's wifes. In the Nara period (710–794), it was recorded as a female name, suffixed by -me (売), with phonetic kanji including 都夫良, 都布良 and 豆布良 (都 (tsu, to, miyako) meaning "capital," 夫 (fu, fuu, bu, otto, sore, o) meaning "husband, man," 布 (fu, nuno) meaning "cloth" and 豆 (zu, tou, mame, mame-) meaning "(soy)bean").The name decreased in usage after this period and it wasn't revived until the 20th century. Even so, the usage at this moment in time is rare.

column3: 鼓, 鼓美, 鼓実, 鼓海, 都々美, 都々実, 津々美, 津々実(Japanese Kanji)|つづみ(Japanese Hiragana)|ツヅミ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name can be used as 鼓 (ko, tsudzumi) meaning "beat, drum, muster, rouse" or it can be combined with 美 (bi, mi, utsuku.shii) meaning "beautiful, beauty", 実 (shitsu, jitsu, makoto, makotoni, mi) meaning "reality, truth" and 海 (kai, umi, mi) meaning "ocean, sea."This name can also be used as 都々美, 都々実, 津々美 or 津々実 with 都 (tsu, to, miyako) meaning "capital, metropolis" and 津 (shin, tsu) meaning "ferry, harbour, haven, port."々 (のま/おなじ) is used as a kanji repeater, duplicating the sound of the preceding kanji.As a word, Tsudzumi/Tsuzumi (鼓) refers to a particular hand drum of Chinese/Indian origin.Tsudzumi/Tsuzumi is also used as a surname.

column3: 綴, 綴莉, 津々理, 津々莉, 都々里, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|つづり(Japanese Hiragana)|ツヅリ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From 綴り (tsudzuri) meaning "spelling; patching, binding."It can also be suffixed with a ri kanji, like 理 meaning "reason, logic," 莉, part of 茉莉 (matsuri), referring to the Arabian jasmine, or 里 meaning "village." 綴 can also be substituted with 2 kanji, using a tsu kanji and repeating it with 々, like 津 meaning "harbour, haven" or 都 meaning "metropolis."This name is rarely given to girls, if given at all. It is also in use as a surname.
