column12: From 次 (tsugu) meaning "second, next" or 継 (tsugu) meaning "to succeed someone, inherit" combined with 正 (masa) meaning "correct, proper" or 雅 (masa) meaning "elegant". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 亜美, 亜実, 亜弥, 亜海, 次美, 次実, 次弥, 次海, 都久美, 都玖未(Japanese Kanji)|つぐ美, つぐ実(Kanji/Hiragana)|つぐみ(Japanese Hiragana)|ツグミ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name combines 亜 (a, tsu.gu) meaning "Asia, come after, rank next" or 次 (shi, ji, tsugi, tsu.gu) meaning "next, order, sequence" with 美 (bi, mi, utsuku.shii) meaning "beautiful, beauty", 実 (shitsu, jitsu, makoto, makotoni, mi) meaning "reality, truth", 弥 (bi, mi, amaneshi, iya, iyoiyo, tooi, hisashi, hisa.shii, ya, wata.ru) meaning "all the more, increasingly" or 海 (kai, umi, mi) meaning "ocean, sea."Rare examples of Tsugumi with 3 kanji include 都久美 and 都玖未 with 都 (tsu, to, miyako) meaning "capital, metropolis", 久 (kyuu, ku, hisa.shii) meaning "long time, old story", 玖 (kyuu, ku) meaning "beautiful black jewel, nine (used in legal documents)" and 未 (bi, mi, ima.da, hitsuji, ma.da) meaning "even now, hitherto, not yet, still, sign of the ram (8th sign of Chinese zodiac)."This name also combines つぐ, the 2 phonetic characters that make up Tsugu with either 美 or 実.Bearers of this name include actress and model Tsugumi (つぐみ), born Tsuzumi Ōtake (大竹 都々美) (1976-) and voice actress Tsugumi Higasayama (日笠山 亜美) (1978-).

column3: 次随, 嗣路, 承通, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 次 (tsugu) meaning "second, next" combined with 通 (michi) meaning "to pass through" or 随 (michi) meaning "follow, obey, comply". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 次宗, 嗣崇, 亜旨, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 次 (tsugu, ji) meaning "next, order, sequence, below" combined with 旨 (delicious, appetizing, clever, principle, aim, gist, purpose, meaning", 崇 (mune) meaning "to adore, worship, revere, lofty or 宗 (shuu, sou, mune) meaning "origin, religion, sect."

column3: 承野, 嗣乃, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 承 (tsugu) meaning "acquiescent", 嗣 (tsuguru, tsugu) meaning "descendants, heirs" combined with 野 (sho, ya, no, no-) meaning "civilian life, field, plains, rustic" or 乃 (ai, dai, nai, no, sunawa.chi, nanji, no) meaning "accordingly, from, possessive particle, whereupon". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 禎儀, 亜儀, 次紀, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 禎 (tsugu) meaning "divine grace, auspicious, straightforward", meaning 亜 (a, tsugu) meaning “second, Asia, sub-”, or 次 (ji, tsugu) meaning "next" combined with 儀 (nori) meaning "ceremony, rites", or 紀 (nori, ki) meaning "chronicle". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 次男, 嗣生, 次雄, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: Japanese masculine name derived from 次 (tsugu) meaning "second, next" and 男 (o) meaning "male" or 雄 (o) meaning "hero, manly". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: ツグル(Japanese Katakana)|つぐる(Japanese Hiragana)|継, 嗣, 告, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 継 (tsuguru) meaning "follow in someone's position or footsteps, acquire by birthright", or 告 (tsuguru) meaning "revelation, tell, inform", 嗣 (tsuguru) meaning "to inherent, descendant, heir". Other kanji or kanji combinations can be used.

column3: ツグシゲ(Japanese Katakana)|つぐしげ(Japanese Hiragana)|貢滋, 伝重, 継繁, 続成, 襲茂, 著栄, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 緒 (tsugu) meaning "beginning, cord, strap" combined with 重 (shige) meaning "layers, folds". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 注崇, 注隆, 注貴, 嗣崇, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 注 (tsugu) meaning "to pour, annotation, note" combined with 崇 (taka) meaning "to adore, worship, revere". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 承太郎, 嗣太郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 承 (tsugu, sho) meaning "acquiesce, consent" combined with 太 (ta) meaning "thick, big, great" and 郎 (rō) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 亜人, 胤人, 嗣人, 次人, 二人, 亞人, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 亜 (tsugu) meaning "second, Asia", 胤 (tsugu) meaning "paternal blood, offspring", 嗣 (tsugu) meaning "to connect, inherit", 次 (tsugu) meaning "next, secondary", 二 (tsugu) meaning "two" or 亞 (tsugu) meaning "rank" combined with 人 (to) meaning "person". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 嗣也, 継也, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 継 (tsugu) meaning "successor" and 也 (ya) meaning "also". Other kanji combinations can spell this name.

column3: 禎裕, 禎靖, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 禎 (tsugu) meaning "divine grace, auspicious, straightforward" combined with 靖 (yasu) meaning "peaceful, calm, easygoing" or 裕 (yasu) meaning "abundant". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 次代, 承陽, 禎洋, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 次 (tsugu, ji) meaning "next, order, sequence, below" or 継 (tsugu) meaning "to succeed someone, inherit" combined with 代 (yo) "world, generation". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 継尚, 嗣尚, 次尚, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 継 (tsugu) meaning "successor" and 尚 (yori) meaning "furthermore, in addition." Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 亜孝, 嗣敬, 次成, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 承 (tsugu) meaning "acquiescent", 胤 (tsugu) meaning "paternal blood, offspring", or 禎 (tsugu) meaning "divine grace, auspicious, straightforward", combined with 成 (yoshi) meaning "become", 敬 (yoshi) meaning "respect, honor, reverence", or 孝 (yoshi) meaning "filial piety".

column3: 詔之, 次幸, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 詔 (tsugu) meaning "imperial decree, edict" and 幸 (yuki) meaning "happiness, good fortune". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 祖贤, etc.(Chinese)|祖賢, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: Varient transcription of Zuxian (using Wade-Giles romanisation).
The Khoikhoi god of rain and thunder.

column3: 摘花, 都花, 都香, 津花, 津加, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|ツカ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 摘 (tsu) meaning "to pluck; to pick" combined with 花 (ka) meaning "flower". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 津香子, 津加子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 津 (tsu) meaning "port, harbor", 香 (ka) meaning "fragrance" or 加 (ka) meaning "increase, add" with 子 (ko, shi) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 束(Japanese Kanji)|つかね(Japanese Hiragana)|ツカネ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name is used as 束 (soku, taba, taba.neru, tsuka, tsuka.neru, tsukane) meaning "bundle."Throughout the late 19th century and first half of the 20th century, it was mainly (uncommonly) used on males. Nowadays, it is mainly given to girls, though it is now rarely given.

column3: 司(Japanese Kanji)|つかし(Japanese Hiragana)|ツカシ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From 司 (tsukasa) meaning "office," modelled on other names ending with -shi, like Hiroshi, Kiyoshi and Takashi.This name is extremely rare.

column3: ツキ(Japanese Katakana)|つき(Japanese Hiragana)|月, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 月 (tsuki) meaning "moon, month". Other spellings are possible.
From Japanese 月 (tsuki) meaning "moon" combined with 愛 (a) meaning "love, affection". Other kanji combinations can also form this name.
From Japanese 月 (tsuki) "moon", 地 (chi) meaning "earth; ground" combined with 陽 (yo) meaning "the sun". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 月恵, 月絵, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 月 (tsuki, getsu) meaning "moon, month" and 恵 (e, megumi) meaning "favour, benefit" or 絵 (e) meaning "picture, painting". Other combinations of kanji are possible.

column3: 月日, 月陽, 月姫, 月柊, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|つきひ(Japanese Hiragana)|ツキヒ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From 月日 (tsukihi), literally meaning "moon and sun," though it can also refer to time, years or days.Other kanji that can be (partially) read as hi include 陽, having the same meaning as 日 "day, sun," 姫 (hime) meaning "princess" and 柊 (hiiragi), referring to the flowering plant known variously as 'holly osmanthus', 'holly olive', or 'false holly'.This name is rarely used.

column3: 月彦, 槻彦, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 月 (tsuki) meaning "moon" or 槻 (tsuki) meaning "zelkova tree" combined with 彦 (hiko) meaning "boy, prince". Other kanji combinations are also possible.

column3: つきか(Japanese Hiragana)|月佳, 月嘉, 月夏, 月花, 月圭, 月樺, 月姫花, 津季香, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 月 (tsuki) meaning "moon" combined with 樺 (ka) meaning "birch, reddish yellow" or 嘉 (ka) meaning "praise, auspicious". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 月女, 月姫, 月明, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 月 (tsuki) meaning "moon" combined with 女 (me) meaning "woman", 姫 (me) meaning "princess" or 明 (me) meaning "bright, clear, tomorrow". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Japanese 月 (tsuki) meaning "moon" combined with 美 (mi) meaning "beautiful". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: つきな(Japanese Hiragana)|ツキナ(Japanese Katakana)|槻七, 月薙, 槻那, 槻名, 都稀鳴, 亜生来, 津利梛, 子祈雫, 都姫成, 月黄凪, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 月 (tsuki) meaning "month, moon" combined with 菜 (na) meaning "vegetables, greens" or 薙 (na) meaning "to mow down". Other kanji combinations are permissible.

column3: 月音, 及己, 月寧, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 月 (tsuki) meaning "moon" combined with 音 (ne) meaning "sound". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: ツキノ(Japanese Katakana)|月乃, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 月 (tsuki) meaning "moon, month" and 乃 (no), which is a possessive article. Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 月男, 月乙, 月夫, 月雄, 槻雄, 槻郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 月 (tsuki) meaning "moon" combined with 男 (o) meaning "male". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 月郎, 槻郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 月 (tsuki) meaning "moon" combined with 郎 (rou) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations are possible.
This name has no meaning since it is written only in hiragana.

column3: 月白, 月代, 月魄, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 月 (tsuki) meaning "moon" combined with 白 (shiro) meaning "white". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Alternate transcription of Hebrew צוקית (see Tzukit).
From Japanese 月 (tsuki) meaning "moon", 太 (ta) meaning "thick, big" and 郎 (rou) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 月人, 月兎, 月都, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 月 (tsuki) meaning "moon" combined with 人 (to) meaning "person". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 月夜, 築哉, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 月 (tsuki) meaning "moon" combined with 夜 (ya) meaning "night". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: ツキヨ(Japanese Katakana)|月世, 月輝夜, 月夜, 都喜代, 附代, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 月 (tsuki) meaning "moon" combined with 世 (yo) meaning "world" or from 月夜 (tsukiyo) meaning "moonlit night". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: ツコ(Japanese Katakana)|つこ(Japanese Hiragana)|つ子(Kanji/Hiragana)|津子, 土子, 都子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 津 (tsu) meaning "ferry, haven, port, harbor" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Japanese 津 (tsu), referring to Tsu city in Mie prefecture, 古 (ko) meaning "the past" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: つくみ(Japanese Hiragana)|繕美, 築美, 津久実, 都久実, 都久美, 月光, 菜美, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 繕 (tsuku) meaning "repair, mend" combined with 美 (mi) meaning "beautiful". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Tsukune is a character from Naruto Shippuden.Tsukune Aono is the only citable girl who has this name in real life.Its probably rare because the vocabulary word tsukune refers to a meatball dish.

column3: 創, 作, 造, 耕(Japanese Kanji)|つくる(Japanese Hiragana)|ツクル(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From verb 作る/造る/創る (tsukuru) meaning "to make, build, construct; to raise, cultivate; to till, etc."One other kanji used in relation to the verb is 耕 (kou, tagaya.su) meaning "to till, plough, cultivate."

Means "horsetail (plant)" in Japanese from 土筆 (tsukushi). Other kanji combinations are possible.It was used in 1992 for the main character Tsukushi (つくし) Makino in the manga 'Boys Over Flowers' that later had many screen adaptations through Japan, South Korea and China.
Means "kingfisher". Name borne by the husband of Nanyehi.
Means "rein, bridle, rope for leading a horse" in Mongolian.
Alternate transcription of Tibetan ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས (see Tshultrim).
Alternate transcription of Tibetan ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས (see Tshultrim).

column3: つま(Japanese Hiragana)|ツマ(Japanese Katakana)|妻, 津摩, 都万, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 妻 (tsuma) meaning "wife", 津 (tsu) meaning "haven, port, harbor, ferry" or 都 (tsu) meaning "capital (city)" combined with 摩 (ma) meaning "chafe, rub, polish, grind, scrape" or 万 (ma) meaning "very many". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 爪(Japanese Kanji)|つめ(Japanese Hiragana)|ツメ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Means "claw" in Japanese.One fictional bearer of this name is Tsume (ツメ) from the manga and anime franchise 'Wolf's Rain'.There has been evidence that it was (uncommonly) used as a feminine name as far back as the mid 19th century, but it's far unlikely that they were given the name because of the meaning since most of them would have their names written in kana. Nowadays, it's very rarely given to girls, if given at all, and it is not given to boys as of yet.

column3: ツミキ(Japanese Katakana)|つみき(Japanese Hiragana)|積妃, 柘騎, 摘紀, 津美祇, 都魅技, 豆農綺, 詰澪季, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 摘 (tsumi) meaning "pick, pluck" and 葵 (ki) meaning "hollyhock" or 柘 (tsumi) meaning "Japanese box plant, littleleaf box" combined with 祇 (ki) meaning "local or national god, good, peaceful". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: ツミコ(Japanese Katakana)|つみこ(Japanese Hiragana)|摘子, 通美子, 継未子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 摘 (tsumi) meaning "pick, pluck" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Most commonly spelled as 紬 (tsumugu) meaning "pongee", a knotted silk cloth. It can also be spelled as 績 (tsumugu) or 紡 (tsumugu) meaning "to spin". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Cantonese romanized of Jun 1 or Wade-Giles romanization of Zun.

column3: つな(Japanese Hiragana)|ツナ(Japanese Katakana)|絆, 繫, 維, 都那, 津那, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 絆 (tsuna) meaning "tether, tie, link, bond, fetter, connection" or 繫 (tsuna) meaning "connect, attach". Other kanji or kanji combinations are possible.

This is the name of Jiraiya's wife from the Japanese folktale 'Jiraiya Gōketsu Monogatari'. The character from 'Naruto' is named after her. The word 綱手 (tsunade) means "mooring rope"; it comes from 綱 (tsuna) meaning "cable, rope, genus, class" and 手 (de) meaning "hand".

column3: ツナコ(Japanese Katakana)|つなこ(Japanese Hiragana)|都菜子, 鶴名子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 鶴 (tsu) meaning "crane (bird)", 菜 (na) meaning "vegetable, greens", and 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: つなみ(Japanese Hiragana)|維美, 紀三, 純美, 津波, 純魅, 津奈美, 津那実, 津名魅, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 津波 (tsunami) meaning "a tsunami, a tidal wave", which is a compound 津 (tsu) meaning "harbor" and 波 (nami) meaning "wave". Other kanji or kanji combinations can form this name as well.

column3: つなお(Japanese Hiragana)|ツナオ(Japanese Katakana)|津南雄, 尋奈紘, 繫夫, 維男, 綱生, 繫郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 維 (tsuna) meaning "fiber, rope" or 綱 (tsuna) meaning "rope, cable" combined with 夫 (o) meaning "husband" or 男 (o) meaning "male, man". Other kanji combinations can also form this name.
Means "effort, zeal, perseverance, diligence" in Tibetan.
From Japanese 常 (tsune) meaning "continuation, eternal, unchanging" and 羽 (ha) meaning "feather, plume".

column3: 雅彦, 恒彦, 恆彦, 法彦, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 恒 (tsune) meaning "constant, persistent" or 雅 (tsune) meaning "refined, elegant, graceful", combined with 彦 (hiko) meaning "boy, prince". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 恒数, 恒和, 恆数, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 恒 (tsune) meaning "constant, persistent", 常 (tsune) meaning "always, consistently, constantly", 庸 (tsune) meaning "ordinary, commonplace", 恆 (tsune) meaning "constant", or 毎 (tsune) meaning "every" combined with 和 (kazu, wa) meaning "harmony, peace" or 一 (kazu, ichi) meaning "one", or 数 (saku, shu, su, suu, soku, kazu, kazo.eru, shibashiba, se.meru, wazurawa.shii) meaning "figure, number, count". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 恒貴, 恒樹, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 恒 (tsune) meaning "constant, persistent" combined with 貴 (ki) meaning "valuable" or 樹 (ki, itsuki, ju) meaning "tree". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 雅吉, 常吉, 恒吉, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 雅 (tsune) meaning "elegant" combined with 吉 (kichi) meaning "good luck". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 恒子, 雅子, 常子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: Japanese feminine name derived from the kanji 恒 (tsune) meaning "constant, persistent" or 雅 (tsune) meaning "gracious, refined, elegant, graceful" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child".

column3: 常正, 経幹, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 常 (tsune) meaning "usual" and 正 (masa) meaning "right, correct, proper, justice". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 雅己, 恒実, 恒三, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 恒 (tsune) meaning "constant, persistent" and 実 (mi) meaning "fruit, good result, truth". Other kanji combinations can also form this name.

column3: 常三朗, 恒珊郎, 恆三郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 恆 or 恒 (tsune) meaning "constant, persistent" or 常 (tsune, hisa, jo, tsura) meaning "eternal, unchanging, ordinary, usual" combined with 珊 (sabu) meaning "coral", and 朗 (rou, aki.raka, hoga.raka) meaning "bright, cheerful, clear, melodious, serene."

column3: 常民, 恒民, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 常 (tsune) meaning "continuation, eternity" and 民 (tami) meaning "people". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: つねゆき(Japanese Hiragana)|ツネユキ(Japanese Katakana)|恒行, 経之, 庸征, 常恭, 恒往, 経維, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 経 (tsune) meaning "elapse, usual, ordinary" and 征 (yuki) meaning "to go, head towards, past, previous". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 宗翰, 聰翰, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: Varient of Zonghan or Conghan (using Wade-Giles transcription).

column3: 宗怡, 宗义, 宗颐, 宗懿, etc.(Chinese)|宗怡, 宗義, 宗頤, 宗懿, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: Wade-Giles romanization of Zongyi used in Taiwan.
From Japanese 津 (tsu) meaning "harbor, port, haven" combined with 進 (nobu) meaning "to make progress, advance, enter". Other kanji combinations can be used.
Alternate transcription of Hebrew צוּר (see Tzur).

column3: 鶴千代, 鶴千世, 鶴知代, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 鶴 (tsuru) meaning "crane", 千 (chi) meaning "thousand" combined with 代 (yo) meaning "generation". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: つるゑ(Japanese Hiragana)|つる江(Kanji/Hiragana)|鶴枝, 津留江, 弦江, 弦影, 都留江, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 鶴 (tsuru) meaning "crane" combined with 枝 (e) meaning "bough, twig, branch, limbs". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: つるぎ(Japanese Hiragana)|ツルギ(Japanese Katakana)|剣, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 剣 (tsurugi) meaning "sword" in Japanese.

column3: 鶴一, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|つるいち(Japanese Hiragana)|ツルイチ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 鶴 (tsuru) meaning "crane" combined with 一 (ichi) meaning "one". Other kanji combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 鶴生, 鶴希, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 鶴 (tsuru) meaning "crane (bird)" and 生 (ki) meaning "living", as well as other kanji combinations with the same pronunciation.

column3: つるこ(Japanese Hiragana)|ツルコ(Japanese Katakana)|絃子, 鶴子, 津留子, 都流子, 都瑠子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 絃 (tsuru) meaning "string, cord", 鶴 (tsuru) meaning "crane, stork" or 都 (tsu) meaning "metropolis, capital, all, everything" combined with 留 (ru) meaning "detain, fasten, halt, stop" or 瑠 (ru) meaning "lapis lazuli" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.A famous bearer was Tsuruko Haraguchi (1886-1915), a psychologist and the first Japanese woman to receive a Doctor of Philosophy.

column3: 鶴駒, 弦駒, 蔓駒(Japanese Kanji)|つる駒(Kanji/Hiragana)|つるこま(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: Derived from the Japanese kanji 鶴 (tsuru) meaning "crane" or 弦 (tsuru) meaning “bowstring; musical instrument string" or 蔓 (tsuru) meaning "connections; contacts; influence" combined with 駒 (koma) meaning "foal, young horse". All these kanji have these pronounciations using the Kun Reading.Other kanji combinations are also possible.

column3: 鶴美, 鶴実, 蔓美, 蔓実, 鶴見, 蔓見(Japanese Kanji)|つるみ(Japanese Hiragana)|ツルミ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 鶴 (tsuru) meaning "crane" or 蔓 (tsuru) meaning "vine" combined with 美 (mi) meaning "beauty", 実 (mi) meaning "berry, fruit, nut, real", or 見 (mi) meaning "to see". Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.

column3: 鶴乃, 弦乃, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|つるか(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: From Japanese 鶴 (tsuru) meaning "crane (bird)" or 弦 (tsuru) meaning "string, chord." combined with 乃 (no), a possessive particle. Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 鶴雄, 鶴悟, 鶴男, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: Japanese masculine name derived from 鶴 (tsuru) meaning "crane" and 雄 (o) meaning "man, manly". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 鶴代, 蔓代(Japanese Kanji)|つるよ(Japanese Hiragana)|ツルヨ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 鶴 (tsuru) meaning "crane" or 蔓 (tsuru) meaning "vine" combined with 代 (yo) meaning "generation". Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.
From つ (tsu), “two”, る (ru), a possessive particle, and ぞ (zo), a sound that is used to make a statement more serious. Other kanji combinations are also possible.
Derived from Mongolian цус (tsus or cus) "blood".

column3: 蔦, 伝, 傳, 津多, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|つた(Japanese Hiragana)|ツタ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From either 蔦 (tsuta), referring to the Boston ivy, or the stem of verb 伝う/傳う (tsutau) meaning "to go/walk along, to follow​," the former likely related to that verb. It can also be written with a combination of a tsu kanji, e.g. 津 meaning "harbour, haven," and a ta kanji, e.g. 多 meaning "many."As a feminine name, it was most commonly used before the 20th century, though not nearly as common as the top female names of the late Edo period (1603-1868), e.g. Kiku. Nowadays, it is extremely rare.

column3: 蔦子, 伝子, 津多子, 津太子, 都多子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|つた子(Kanji/Hiragana)|つたこ(Japanese Hiragana)|ツタコ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Tsuta combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child."

column3: 伝, 傳(Japanese Kanji)|つたう(Japanese Hiragana)|ツタウ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From classical verb 伝う/傳う (tsutau), modern tsutaeru, meaning "to go/walk along."
This is the name of one of the characters that is featured in the Avatar franchise.

column3: 伝, 傳(Japanese Kanji)|つとう(Japanese Hiragana)|ツトウ(Japanese Katakana)
伝, 傳(Japanese Kanji)|つとう(Japanese Hiragana)|ツトウ(Japanese Katakana)

column12: From Japanese 躑躅 meaning "azalea", the name of the flower.

column3: つつみ(Japanese Hiragana)|ツツミ(Japanese Katakana)|つつ美(Kanji/Hiragana)|包美, 包未, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column12: From Japanese 艶 (tsuya) meaning "luster" or from Japanese 月 (tsu) meaning "moon" combined with 夜 (ya) meaning "night". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: つや子(Kanji/Hiragana)|沢子, 艶子, 彩子, 津夜子, 鶴矢子, 都哉子, 都耶子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: This name combines 沢 (tsuya) meaning "swamp, marsh, brilliance, grace", 彩 (tsuya) meaning "colour" or 艶 (tsuya) meaning "gloss, luster, beautiful, charming" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child, the rat, first sign of the Chinese zodiac". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: ツヨ(Japanese Katakana)|津代, 都代, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 津 (tsu) meaning "haven, port, harbor, ferry" or 都 (tsu) meaning "capital (city)" combined with 代 (yo) meaning "generation". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: ツヨイ(Japanese Katakana)|強, 剛, 豪, 毅, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 強 (tsuyoi) meaning "powerful, strong, intense". Other kanji or kanji combinations can be used.

column3: つよと(Japanese Hiragana)|ツヨト(Japanese Katakana)|剛人, 強陶, 侃斗, 毅翔, 豪都, 勁 透, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 剛 (tsuyo) meaning "firm; strong; sturdy" combined with 人 (to) meaning "person". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 梅雨, 露(Japanese Kanji)|つゆ(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: From Japanese kanji 梅雨 (tsuyu) meaning "East Asian rainy season" or 露 (tsuyu) meaning "dew; dewdrop".Other kanji or kanji combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 梅雨恵, 露絵, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: 梅雨 (tsuyu) meaning "East Asian rainy season" or 露 (tsuyu) meaning "dew; dewdrop" combined with 恵 (e, kei, megu.mi, megu.mu) meaning "blessing, favour, grace, kindness", 絵 (e, kai) meaning "drawing, picture, painting, sketch", 江 (kou, e) meaning "bay, creek, inlet" or 栄 (ei, you, e, saka.eru, ha.e, ha.eru, -ba.e) meaning "flourish, glory, honour, prosperity, splendour". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: つゆほ(Japanese Hiragana)|ツユホ(Japanese Katakana)|梅雨帆, 露帆, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese kanji 梅雨 (tsuyu) meaning "East Asian rainy season" or 露 (tsuyu) meaning "dew; dewdrop" combined with 帆 (ho) meaning "sail". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 津幸, 津雪, 都幸, 透由, 陽雪, 露葵, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 津 (tsu) meaning "harbour, port" combined with 幸 (yuki) meaning "happiness". Other kanji combinations can also form this name.

column3: つゆこ(Japanese Hiragana)|ツユコ(Japanese Katakana)|つゆ子(Kanji/Hiragana)|梅雨子, 露子, 都夕子, 津夕子, 津佑子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 梅雨 (tsuyu) meaning "East Asian rainy season" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 梅雨実, 露美, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: 梅雨 (tsuyu) meaning "East Asian rainy season" or 露 (tsuyu) meaning "dew; dewdrop" combined with 実 (mi, minoru) meaning "to bear fruit" or 美 (mi, bi, utsukushi) meaning "beautiful". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From 露 (tsuyu) meaning "dew, dewdrops" and 乃 (no), a possessive particle.

column3: 梅雨夫, 梅雨男, 梅雨雄, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese kanji 梅雨 (tsuyu) meaning "East Asian rainy season" or 露 (tsuyu) meaning "dew; dewdrop" combined with 夫 (o) meaning "man, husband", 男 (o) meaning "male, man" or 雄 (o) meaning "hero, manly". Other kanji combinations are also possible.
From Japanese 津 (tsu) meaning "haven, port, harbor, ferry" combined with 住 (zumi) meaning "dwelling; living". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 鼓音, 綴音, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 鼓 (tsuzu, ko) meaning "hand drum" and 音 (ne) meaning "sound, noise". Other character combinations can spell this name.

column3: 綴, 津々理, 津々莉, 都々里(Japanese Kanji)|つづり(Japanese Hiragana)|ツヅリ(Japanese Katakana)

column12: Slavicised form of Bluma, compare Russian цвето́к (cvetók) "flower" and Bulgarian Tsvetan.

The first element of this name is either derived from Bulgarian tsvete "flower" or from Bulgarian tsvyat "color". The second element is derived from Slavic mir "peace". As such, the meaning of this name is either "flower of peace" or "color of peace". Known bearers of this name include Bulgarian soccer player Tsvetomir Panov (b. 1989) and Bulgarian soccer goalkeeper Tsvetomir Tsankov (b. 1984).
Alternate transcription of Hebrew צְבִי (see Tzvi).
Derived from Bulgarian цвят (cvjat) "colour (usually vivid); (of a plant) blossom, flower; (figurative) elite, the best of the bunch".
Derived from Bulgarian цвят (tsvyat) meaning "color" as well as "blossom, flower".
Russified form of the Buryat name Цэбэг (Tsebeg) or Сэбэг (Sebeg) meaning "eternal, immortal, undying", ultimately from Tibetan ཚེ་དཔག (tshe-dpag).
Buryat form of Tshering, commonly used as an element in compound names.
Derived from Tibetan ཚེ་རིང (tshe ring) meaning “long life, longevity” combined with རྡོ་རྗེ (rdo rje) meaning “diamond”.
From Tibetan ཚེ་རིང (tshe ring) meaning "long life, longevity" (see Tshering) combined with Dulma.

column3: 子, 梓, 紫, 芷, etc.(Chinese)
column12: Cantonese romanization of Zi or Zhi.

column3: 芷晴, 芷菁, 梓晴, 紫澄, etc.(Chinese)
column12: Cantonese romanisation of Zhiqing, Zhijing, Ziqing, or Zicheng.

column3: 子聰, 梓冲, 梓聰, etc.(Chinese)
column12: Cantonese romanisation of Zicong or Zichong.

column3: 芷筠, 芷君, 子均, 子君, etc.(Chinese)
column12: Cantonese romanisation of Zijun or Zhijun.
Cantonese romanisation of Ziyan or Ziran.
From native Korean 뜰 (tteul) meaning "garden, court."

From Sino-Vietnamese 思 (tư) meaning "think, yearn for, hope, wish". It also means "four, fourth", from a non-Sino-Vietnamese reading of Chinese 四 (tư). In Southern Vietnam this refers to the thirdborn child.
From Sino-Vietnamese 賜 (tứ) meaning "bestow, confer, grant".
From Sino-Vietnamese 詞 (từ) meaning "word, term", 慈 (từ) meaning "kind, charitable, merciful", or 徐 (từ) meaning "quiet, composed".
From Sino-Vietnamese 嗣 (tự) meaning "to inherit, continue, heir", 緒 (tự) meaning "beginning", or 自 (tự) meaning "self, oneself".
From Sino-Vietnamese 子 (tử) meaning "child, son, small thing".
Vietnamese form of an unknown Hmong name.

Origin uncertain, possibly a variant of Tova 2, a feminine form of Tue or a short form of Perpetua. Alternatively it may be derived from Latin tua "yours" or Danish tue "small hill" (from Old Norse þúfa "mound, knoll", which coincides with the name Þúfa). In Sweden its earliest document use is 1835.
Means "luck, fortune, advantage" in Malay and Indonesian. It was borne by the legendary 15th-century Malay warrior Hang Tuah.
Means "pathway" from tu meaning "stand" and ala "path".
From Sino-Vietnamese 旬 (tuần) meaning "week" or 巡 (tuần) meaning "to patrol".
From Sino-Vietnamese 殉 (tuẫn) meaning "to die for a cause".

column3: 湍, 抟, etc.(Chinese)|摶, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 湍 (tuān) meaning "rushing water", 抟 (tuán) meaning "to roll something into a ball", in addition to other characters that are pronounced similarly.
Possibly a combination of tu ("you") and Ana.
From tu meaning "stand", aniga meaning "to be echoed", manuolepola meaning "singing bird".
Greenlandic name meaning from the baby language endearment term (aat)tuaruna! aarsuaruna! meaning "how ugly you are!"
Means "chief of high standing" from tū "stand" and ariki "chief" in Maori. A notable bearer of this name is Tuariki Delamere (b. 1951), a Maori politician and athlete from New Zealand.
From Sino-Vietnamese 戌 (tuất) referring to the eleventh Earthly Branch (7 PM to 9 PM), which is itself associated with the dog of the Chinese zodiac.
Means "princess of the people" from Irish tuath meaning "people, land" combined with flaith "princess".
Means "thou shalt be brought" in Hebrew. In the Old Testament, Tubal-Cain was the son of Lamech and Zillah, and brother to Naamah. He was the first blacksmith.

Means "offspring of Cain, smith of Cain" from the Hebrew root י-ב-ל (y-b-l) which means "to bring, to carry, to flow" combined with Cain meaning "smith," "metalworker," or originally "acquired, spear". Tubal-Cain was mentioned in Genesis 4:22 and he is the son of Lamech and Zillah, the brother of Naamah, and the descendant of Cain.
Lamanite king (c. 51 BC), son of Ammoron, the previous king. He appointed Coriantumr, a mighty man and Nephite dissenter, to lead his armies.
Means "lover of bees; friend of all" in Luhya.

Meaning: Tubeec is associated with "melodious" or "musical", reflecting a connection to singing or music.Origin: The name is notably linked to Hassan Aden Samatar, a renowned Somali singer known as Tubeec. His stage name symbolized his musical talent and influence in Somali music. The name has cultural significance in the context of Somali music and performing arts.

Means "student, learner", from the Hmong kawm which means "study, learn" and tub which can mean "son", but in this instance is likely a linguistic device preceding a word to designate someone who is engaged in an action.
Means "continue to move, expand" in Yoruba.
Alternate transcription of Thai ทับทิม (see Thapthim).

Means "one who completes", from the Hmong tub which can mean "son", but in this instance is likely a linguistic device preceding a word to designate someone who is engaged in an action, and tsheej meaning "complete".
Means "they have moved northward" in Ijaw.
From Sino-Vietnamese 肅 (túc) meaning "respectful, solemn" or 足 (túc) meaning "sufficient".
From Sino-Vietnamese 續 (tục) meaning "to continue, carry on, succeed".
From Sino-Vietnamese 息 (tức) meaning "interest, profit, news".
Tucana is one of the southern constellations created by Dutch explorers in the late 16th century. It was named after the toucan, a type of bird found in South America.
From Sino-Vietnamese 繡球 (tú cầu) meaning "hydrangea", composed of 繡 (tú) meaning "to embroider" and 球 (cầu) meaning "ball, sphere", literally "embroidered ball".
Feminine form of Tuccius, a name of Oscan derivation. This was the name of one of the Vestal Virgins.
Short form of Albertuccio, Donatuccio, Renatuccio, Vituccio and other pet forms that end in -tuccio.

Means "attainment of great power" from Tibetan མཐུ (mthu) meaning "power, force, strength", ཆེན (chen) meaning "great" and ཐོབ (thob) meaning "to attain, to achieve". This is the Tibetan name for the bodhisattva Mahasthamaprapta, used as a calque of Sanskrit महास्थामप्राप्त (mahāsthāmaprāpta).
Of uncertain etymology, although possibly of Anatolian origin. This name was borne by several Hittite kings, and was possibly given in honour of a deified mountain of the same name.
Possibly a combination of Welsh tut "people" and -no "knowing"
From Sino-Vietnamese 自由 (tự do) meaning "freedom, liberty", composed of 自 (tự) meaning "self" and 由 (do) meaning "to follow".
Romanian form of Theodorakis. This name has fallen out of use and now only survives as a patronymic surname.
Diminutive of Tudora, occasionally used as a given name in its own right.

Tudrus was a ruler of the Quadi, a Germanic tribe, in the 1st century AD. He was a contemporary of Maroboduus of the Marcomanni. Like Maroboduus, Tudrus established a dynasty which ruled his people for many years after his death.
Variant of Tugdual. A known bearer of this name is the Breton poet Tudual Huon (b. 1953).

From Sino-Vietnamese 嗣 (tự) meaning "to inherit" and 德 (đức) meaning "virtue". This was the era name of Nguyễn Phúc Hồng Nhậm (1829-1883), the fourth emperor of the Nguyễn dynasty, who reigned from 1847-1883.
Meaning as of yet unknown. This name was notably borne by a Breton saint from the 5th or 6th century AD.
From Sino-Vietnamese 歲 (tuế) meaning "year of age".
Means "memorable, recognisable" or "remind, call to mind" in Thai.
The name of a Nez Perce leader, commonly called "Old Chief Joseph".
Alternate transcription of Arabic طفيل (see Tufayl), as well as the Urdu form.
Means "heavy rain, flood, deluge" in Turkish, ultimately from Arabic طوفان (ṭūfān).
Means "more beautiful than the moon" in Tamazight.

Tuff (Bun in the original Japanese version) is one of the main characters in the anime, Kirby: Right Back at Ya! (Hoshi no Kaabii in the original japanese, which translates to Kirby of the Stars). Tuff is an ally of Kirby and often plays a large role. Tiff (Fumu in the original Japanese version) is his older sisterIt is probably a pet form of Tufford or a transferred use of surname Tuff
Means "more beautiful than the stars" in Tamazight.
Means "more beautiful than a star" in Tamazight.

From the naval expression. Famous bearers include: Tug Dumbly (1965-), the pseudonym of Australian performance poet and musician Geoff Forrester and Tug McGraw (1944-2004), a Major League Baseball pitcher.

Means "sadness" in Croatian. According to a folk tradition, she and her sister Buga, together with their five brothers Klukas, Lobel, Kosenc, Muhlo and Hrvat, led the Croats into the ancient Roman province of Dalmatia in the 7th century.
Derived from the Uzbek tugal meaning "complete, whole" and murod meaning "aim, wish, desire".
From Bashkir ай (ay) meaning "moon", with a first element of unknown etymology.
Means "flag hero" in Mongolian, from туг (tug) meaning "flag, banner, tuft" and баатар (baatar) meaning "hero".
Derived from the Uzbek tug', an obsolete word meaning "banner, flag" and boy meaning "rich, wealthy".
Derived from Breton tut "people" and uual "brave; bold; noble; exalted" or tad "father".

From the Tugela river in South Africa, first used as an English girl's name in 1900 to commemorate the battle of Tugela Heights in the Boer War. 36 girls were given the name in the UK in 1900, but it became extremely rare after then.
Directly taken from German Tugend "virtue". This is one of the so-called pietistic names coined in the 18th century.
Directly taken from German tugendreich "full of virtue". This is one of the so-called pietistic names coined in the 18th century.
Derived from the German adjective tugendsam meaning "virtuous". This is one of the so-called Pietistic given names that were coined in Germany from the late 17th century onwards.
Possibly a short form of Tuguslar.
Means "rising flag" in Mongolian, from туг (tug) meaning "flag, banner, tuft" and мандах (mandakh) meaning "ascent, rising".
Derived from tugma meaning "button" and oy meaning "moon".
From the Slavic elements togo "strong, mighty, potent" and milu meaning "gracious, dear".

Croatian and Slovenian form of the Old Slavic name Togomir, which is derived from Slavic togo "strong, mighty, potent" combined with Slavic mir "peace". Known bearers of this name were Croatian poet and storyteller Tugomir Alaupović (1870-1958) and Tugomir Franc (1932-1983), a Croatian opera singer.
Possibly related to Mongolian тоглох (toglokh) meaning "to play".
Meaning unknown. A known bearer was Tuguzhuko Kyzbech (1777-1840), a Circassian nobleman and leader during the Russian-Circassian War.
From Sino-Vietnamese 自豪 (tự hào) meaning "proud", composed of 自 (tự) meaning "self" and 豪 (hào) meaning "brave, heroic".
From Sanskrit तुहिन (tuhina), meaning "frost, mist, dew" or "moonlight".
Alternate transcription of Yakut Туйаара (see Tuyaara).
Name of an Irish saint. She was one of the abbesses of St. Brigid's convent at Kildare. Her two sisters Muadhnait and Osnait are also saints.
Derived from the archaic Finnish word tuiretuinen, which means both "unwise, uncomprehending" and "darling".

In Irish mythology, Tuireann is a tragic figure and father to three powerful sons, Brian, Iuchar, and Iucharba, who were members of the supernatural Tuatha Dé Danann. He is best known for his central role in one of Ireland's "Three Sorrows of Storytelling", where his sons' blood-price brings about their downfall and his own death from grief.
Meaning unknown. Tuiren was a character in The Birth of Bran, a story in the book Irish Fairy Tales, written by James Stephens. A star has been named after her.
King of Finland (Mythologia Fennica, 1789)Youngest son of Noah, ruler of North Europe (Chronicle of Finland, 1636).
The name of a Germanic Earth god mentioned once in the work of Tacitus. One manuscript of Tacitus provides the alternate name form Tuisco.
Derived from Breton tut "people" and gen "birth".
MEANING - a boy, swiftOrigin - Sanskrit Usage : Sanskrit, Indian, Tamil, Telugu, Nepali, Sinhala, Bengali, hindi, Sikh, Buddhist

Meaning: Tukaale generally means "noble" or "honorable."Origin: It is derived from the Somali language, where names often reflect virtues and esteemed qualities. Tukaale conveys a sense of dignity and respect.
Variant of Tucker as well as the Dutch form.
Means "shimmering of the atmosphere" and "wandering position" in Māori.
From Javanese thukul meaning "grow, sprout, develop".
Greenlandic name meaning "quick", "eager", "active", "cheerful", "vigorous", "is prompt to act" with the connotation "is busy".
Greenlandic name with the combination of Tukúmeĸ and suffix -nnguaq meaning "sweet, dear".
Derived from Greenlandic tukumavoq meaning "quick, alert, generous”.
Means "bush used for firewood" in Aymara.
Means "holy basil" in Sanskrit. In Hindu tradition this is the name of the personification of this plant, often considered a manifestation of the goddess Lakshmi.
Modern form of Tóli or a variant of Thule.
Possibly an Arabic form of Tülin. This was one of the most popular girls' names in Jordan in 2020.
Maybe from Gothic tulgus "firm, steady, solid".
Spanish feminine form of Tulio and Polish feminine form Tuliusz.
Means "rib". Used for a character in the Canadian Inuktitut-language film 'Atanarjuat: The Fast Runner' (2001).

According to some sources, this name means "to prevail over peace" or "to reign over peace", with the second element derived from Slavic mir "peace". Well, they are definitely correct about the second element, but I am uncertain or doubtful that the first element means "to prevail over, to reign". Perhaps it is more likely that the first element is derived from the Polish verb tulić (się) "to hug, to cuddle", which is possibly derived from Proto-Slavic toliti "to calm, to soothe, to silence".
Means "the halo around the moon" in Turkish.
From the name of the flower. Ultimately from Persian dulband, "turban", from the shape of the opened flower.As a given name, it has been occasionally used from the 19th century onwards.

Tulippa is a name worn by a minor character in the Moomin series. It was created by Tove Jansson and probably is derived from tulippaani, "tulip" in Finnish. She was a girl who lived in a tulip flower before she joined Moomintroll and Moominmamma on their journey to find Moominpappa.
Maybe an Old Danish form of Tólir.

Usage of this name is most likely adapted from British singer-songwriter Tula Paulinea Contostavlos (1988), who performs under the mononym Tulisa and has Greek ancestry. It is likely Tulisa is an elaboration or diminutive of her given name, Tula, a variant transcription of Toula.
Of uncertain etymology, this was the name of a Manchu official who wrote a famous travelogue while working as a representative of the Kangxi Emperor's government at the Kalmyk Khanate.
Tulkas had the most valor of the Valar(: in J.R.R. Tolkien's, The Silmarillion.
Derived from the Uzbek tulki meaning "fox" and boy meaning "rich, wealthy".
From Swedish tulta and Norwegian tulle, both meaning "little girl".
Feminine form of Tullius; in former times, it was occasionally used as a Latinization of Tolla.

Roman cognomen which was derived from Tullius (see Tullio).A notable bearer of this name was the 4th-century Roman consul Marcus Aurelius Valerius Tullianus Symmachus Phosphorius, who is better known as Aurelius Valerius Tullianus Symmachus.
Diminutive of Tullia. Cicero used this nickname for his beloved daughter Tullia.
Possible variant of the Irish last name Tully.

Transferred use of the surname Tulliver.Tulliver is the name of a young rabbit in author Diana Reynolds Roome's children's book 'Tulliver's Tunnel'. It is the protagonist's surname in 'The Mill on the Floss' by English novelist Mary Ann Evans under the pseudonym George Eliot.
From the Yakut word туллук (tulluk) meaning "snow bunting".
From the name of the city and county in the US state of Oklahoma which comes from Tallasi, meaning "old town" in the Creek.
Derived from Sanskrit तुलसी (tulasi) meaning "holy basil" (a type of plant; see Tulsi) combined with Sanskrit दास (dasa) meaning "servant".
In Inuit mythology, Tulugaak was the creator of light.
Sicilian form of Ptolemaios via Ptolemaeus.
The name of a god in Inuit Mythology.
Combination of Tuluy and the Turkic title khan meaning "leader, ruler".

Armenian, Kazakh, Kyrgyz and Uzbek form of the Mongol name Tümen, probably via its Old Turkic form Tümän. Also compare the Kazakh, Kyrgyz and Uzbek word tuman meaning "fog", which is ultimately derived from Proto-Turkic *tuman meaning "mist, fog".Notable bearers of this name include a 16th-century sultan of Egypt and the Armenian revolutionary Tuman Tumanian (1879-1906).
Derived from Uzbek tuman meaning "mist, haze" and oy meaning "moon".
Derived from the Kazakh and Kyrgyz noun tumar meaning "amulet". This name is unisex in both countries, but more often given to females than to males.
Maltese and Icelandic form of Thomas.
Romansh form of Thomas, traditionally found in the Engadine valley and in central Grisons.
Presumably from the English word "tumbleweed" which is a plant that breaks away from its roots and forms into a ball through being blown around by the wind.
Means "let us love Him" in Nyakyusa.

Means "ten thousand, multitude, myriad" or "people, nation" in Mongolian and Yakut, the attributive form of Mongolian түм (tüm). Among the Mongol and Turkic peoples, a tümen (tumen in English) was historically also a social and military unit of 10,000 households and soldiers.A notable bearer of this name was the Mongolian khagan (emperor) Tümen Zasagt Khan (1539-1592).
From Mongolian түмэн (tümen) meaning "ten thousand, multitude, myriad" or "people, nation" and амгалан (amgalan) meaning "peace, calm".
From Mongolian түмэн (tümen) meaning "ten thousand, multitude, myriad" or "people, nation" and баатар (baatar) meaning "hero".
From Mongolian түмэн (tümen) meaning "ten thousand, multitude, myriad" or "people, nation" and баяр (bayar) meaning "celebration, joy".
From Mongolian түмэн (tümen) "ten thousand, multitude, myriad" or "people, nation" and билэг (bileg) meaning "gift, talent, aptitude".
From Mongolian түмэн (tümen) meaning "ten thousand, multitude, myriad" or "people, nation" and дэмбэрэл (demberel) meaning "herald, (good) omen".

Tuonetar is the Queen of the Underworld in Finnish mythology. She is the wife of Tuoni, with whom she rules over the Underworld Tuonela.

A royal title from Tonga, means "bowing the head (as in bowing to a royal)" or "king". Tupou is the name of the royal family of Tonga, after King George Tupou I adopted the name.

Variant of Thabthim. This is the name of a concubine in the novel Anna and the King of Siam (1944) and the movie adaptation(s) The King and I (1956 and 1999).

Means "very well made painting, fabric" in Aymara.
Possibly deriving from the Akkadian element tuqūnu ("good order , security , safety").

Noted bearer is American actress Tura Satana (1938-2011), born Suvaki to a Japanese-Filipino father and Cheyenne-Scots-Irish mother. She said of her names: 'Suvaki means "white chameleon" or "white flower" in Japanese, but in Cheyenne it's Tura'. There is actually no such Cheyenne name as Tura and the words in the language that correspond to the meaning bear no similarity. The true origin and meaning of Tura is unknown.
Name given to a girl born on a Tuesday.
Variant of Tur, the meaning of which is uncertain.

Turan was the Etruscan goddess of love, fertility and vitality and patroness of the city of Velch. She was commonly associated with birds such as the dove, goose and above all the swan. Her name is the pre-Hellenic root of Turannos (absolute ruler, see tyrant), so Turan can be viewed as “Mistress".

Means "daughter of Turan", composed of Persian توران (Tūrān), a region of Central Asia that was part of the Persian Empire, allegedly meaning "land of Tur" (said to have been named for the legendary Persian prince Tur, a son of King Fereydoun who reigned around 750 BC), and دخت (dokht) "daughter".This is the original Persian form of Turandot. The opera by Puccini is ultimately based on a tale from the 12th-century Persian poet Nizami Ganjavi's epic the 'Haft Peykar' ('Seven Beauties'). The cruel princess is unnamed in Nizami's version, but known as Turāndoḵt in François Pétis de la Croix's translation of a later retelling; the story is included in Pétis de la Croix's collection 'Les Mille et un jours' (1710-1712), which in turn inspired Carlo Gozzi's play 'Turandot' (1762).

Derived from the Persian name Turandokht, meaning "daughter of Turan" (Turan being a region in Central Asia). This is the name of the title character in an opera by Giacomo Puccini. Turandot is a princess who gives would-be suitors three riddles to solve if they wish to marry her.
Means "will live", derived from Kazakh тірі (tiri) meaning "survive" or "alive, lively". This name was traditionally given when a child (usually a son) was not expected to live.
From the English word turbo meaning "Fast".
Derived from Arabic طرفة (turfah) meaning "novelty, rarity".

Portuguese form of Turibius (see Toribio). A known bearer of this name is the Brazilian classical guitarist and composer Turíbio Santos (b. 1943).

A prince and vassal of Queen Herzeloyde of Wales (Herselojde).Turkentals was killed when the bold Lähelin invaded and conquered Herzeloyde’s lands.

This name was used by American singer Mary Wilson of the Supremes for her daughter born 1975.

This Roman cognomen is an extended form of Turpilius. A bearer of this name was Publius Petronius Turpilianus, a Roman politician, general and consul from the 1st century AD.
Italian and Spanish form of Turpilius.

Probably derived from the Latin adjective turpis meaning "ugly, filthy, disgraceful", which itself derives from the Latin verb turpo "to make ugly, to defile, to disgrace". This name was borne by a Roman comic poet from the 2nd century BC.
From the opaque blue-green mineral whose name is derived from French pierre turquois "Turkish stone".In the English-speaking world, it was occasionally used from the late 19th century onwards.

Norman form of Þórsteinn. Turstin fitz Rou (known as Turstin FitzRolf in English) played a prominent role in the Norman conquest of England and is regarded as one of the few proven companions of William the Conqueror at the Battle of Hastings in 1066.
It means "Being Alive" or "Stay", from the Uyghur language.

A beautiful, traditional name combining the Turkic verb Tur- (meaning "to stay," "to exist," "to remain") with the honorific suffix -sun (a wish for longevity or preservation) and the celestial noun ay ("moon"). It translates to "May She Remain Like the Moon" or "The Everlasting Moon." This name is an exquisite prayer for longevity, constancy, and radiant, unchanging beauty. Symbolically, it praises a person who is a permanent, guiding light in the lives of those she loves, representing a soul that remains steady, bright, and beautiful regardless of the shifting tides of life.
Literally means "stay flower" in Uyghur. The name is often given when parents don't want their daughter to leave, in some cases it would replace their birth name.

Meaning uncertain; contains the Quenya word káno, meaning "commander". In The Silmarillion by J. R. R. Tolkien, this is the original name of King Turgon of Gondolin. He was the son of Fingolfin and the father of Idril. He died when his nephew Maeglin betrayed Gondolin to Morgoth.

This was the name of a 16th-century Mississippian chief who in 1540 led the Battle of Mabila against Spanish conquistador Hernando de Soto. The city of Tuscaloosa in the U.S. state of Alabama is named for him.
Alternate transcription of Sinhala තුෂාර (see Thushara).

Meaning unknown, possibly means "hoopoe" in Ingush (referring to a type of bird). In Vainakh mythology, Tusholi was the goddess of spring and fertility, protector of mankind, and daughter of the supreme god Dela. She was revered by the Vainakh people and considered to be the most important deity before the Islamization of the Caucasus. In Ingushetia, a spring festival is held in her honour, and the month of April in the Ingush calendar is named after her.
Means "teller of tales" in Samoan. This name was adopted by the writer Robert Louis Stevenson when he lived on the island.

Means "black warrior", from the western Muskogean language elements taska and losa.Tuskaloosa (died c. 1540) was a paramount chief of a Mississippian chiefdom in what is now the U.S. state of Alabama. His people were possibly ancestors to the several southern Native American confederacies (the Choctaw and Creek peoples) who later emerged in the region. Tuskaloosa is notable for leading the Battle of Mabila at his fortified village against the Spanish conquistador Hernando de Soto. After being taken hostage by the Spanish as they passed through his territory, Tuskaloosa organized a surprise attack on his captors at Mabila, but was ultimately defeated. The modern city of Tuscaloosa, Alabama is named for him.
Either from тускул (tuskul) meaning "future" or means "doing good" in Yakut.

Taken from the word Twig. Used 5 times for boys in 1955.
From the English word twig. Usage might be related to similar surnames.

From the English word referring to the time of day when the sun is just below the horizon. Ultimately from Old English twi- "half" + līht "light".As a given name, it has been in rare use from the early 20th century onwards.
From the English word "twinkle", ultimately from Old English twincan, "to blink".
Twintelle is a fictional character in the 2017 Nintendo Switch video game ARMS.
Means "to create peace", derived from Polish tworzyć "to create, to make" (which is ultimately derived from Proto-Slavic tvoriti "to make, to create") combined with Slavic mir "peace".
Derived from Polish tworzyć "to create, to make" (which is ultimately derived from Proto-Slavic tvoriti "to make, to create") combined with Slavic slav "glory".
Transferred use of the surname Twyford.
Diminutive of Txabier and variant of Xabi.
Basque adaptation of Charlie used as a diminutive of Karlos and Carlos.
Means "ballad, story song" in Hmong Daw.
Means "money, wealth" or "valuable" in Hmong Daw.
Pseudonym for José Luis Álvarez Enparantza (1929-2012), a Basque linguist, politician, and writer.
One of the personifications of lightning in Basque folklore.
From Hmong txiv "husband, father" and yawg "grandfather", meaning "father-in-law". This is the Hmong name of Chiyou, considered the ancestor of the Hmong people.
Derived directly from txori, the Basque word for "bird", and the name of a Marian statue in Gares / Puente la Reina.
Short from and diminutive of Txunamy
Variant of Tsunami borne by Txunamy Ortiz (2009-), an American YouTube personality who appears on the channel Familia Diamond.
From Sino-Vietnamese 子 (tí) referring to the first Earthly Branch (11 PM–1 AM), which is itself associated with the Rat of the Chinese zodiac. Compare Tí and Tử, also from 子.
From Sino-Vietnamese 巳 (tị) meaning "snake of the Chinese zodiac", also referring to the sixth Earthly Branch (9 AM to 11 AM).
Variant of Tyesha composed of Aisha with the popular prefix Ty-.
Combination of the popular phonetic elements ty, ya and na, probably modelled on Ayanna and influenced by Tiana.
Diminutive of Graciano, Luciano, Sebastián and similar names.
Combination of the popular phonetic prefix ty and Asia 1. Also compare Tyesha and Tasia.
Allegedly from the name of an island off the Georgia (U.S. state) coast, which is said to mean "salt" in Yuchi.
This was the name of an obscure Welsh saint of the 5th century, supposedly a daughter of Brychan Brycheiniog. A church in Dyfed, Wales was named after her.
Feminine form of Tyburcjusz and Tyburcy.
Probably derived from Greek τύχη (tyche) meaning "fortune, chance, fate" combined with γενής (genes) meaning "born".
Meaning uncertain; the first element is almost certainly derived from Greek τύχη (tyche) meaning "fortune, chance, fate".
Latinized form of Tychandros. This name was borne by an eponymous archon of Athens, who lived in the 2nd century BC.
Derived from Ancient Greek τύχη (tyche) meaning "fortune, chance, luck" (see Tyche) combined with ἀνδρός (andros) meaning "of a man". Also compare the Greek name Tychanor.

Derived from the Greek noun τύχη (tyche) meaning "fortune, chance" (see Tyche) combined with the Greek noun ἀνήρ (aner) meaning "man".Also compare the Greek name Tychandros, which is closely related and essentially means the same.
Probably derived from Greek τύχη (tyche) meaning "fortune, chance, fate" and ἀρετή (arete) meaning "goodness, excellence" as well as "virtue, skill".
Blending of the phonetic element ty and Michelle.
Latinized form of Tychikos. In the New Testament, this name belongs to a friend of Paul.
Derived from the Greek adjective τυχικός (tychikos) meaning "casual, fortuitous".
Combination of the phonetic element ty and the given name China.
Probably derived from Greek τύχη (tyche) meaning "fortune, chance, fate" and ἵππος (hippos) meaning "horse".
Combination of the popular elements ty and den.
Combination of the popular phonetic element ty and the name Derreon.

Uncertain etymology, possibly derived from Proto-Indo-European *(s)tewd- meaning "to push, hit", or perhaps τυτθός (tytthos) meaning "small, little". In Greek mythology, Tydeus was the name of an Aeolian hero, who was one of the Seven Against Thebes. He was mortally wounded by Melanippus in battle, and the goddess Athena considered making him immortal; however, she saw Tydeus smash open the head of his killer and eat his brain, causing her to let him die instead.

The Queen of Karmerie (Kamerie) who married Meleranz, Arthur’s nephew. The two met and fell in love when Meleranz was on his way to Arthur’s court. When he had been knighted, she sent him tokens of a belt, a wreath and a clasp.Meleranz eventually rescued her from a forced marriage to King Libers of Lorgan. Her uncle Malloas, who had supported the marriage to Libers, plotted to strip her of her lands, but he relented when he learned of Meleranz’s pedigree.Tydomie and Meleranz ruled Karmerie and Terrandes, and had a daughter, Olimpia, and two sons, Lazeliez and Medanz. Tydomie’s parents were named Garsidis and Lambore.
Combination of the popular name prefix ty and Donna.
A knight who fought on the side of the King with a Hundred Knights during King Mark’s tournament at Lancien.
Combination of the popular phonetic element ty and the name East.
Variant of Tyler. Tyeler was given to 5 girls and 10 boys in 2005 according to the SSA.
Means "hasty riser" in Quenya. In Tolkien's Legendarium this is the mother-name of Celegorm, the third son of Fëanor and Nerdanel.

Tyene Sand is a fictional character in the book series 'A song of Ice and Fire' by George R R Martin. Tyene is a 'sand snake', one of the eight bastard daughters of Prince Oberyn Martell. Tyene comes across as very sweet and innocent, but however she is very deadly, taking poisons as her weapon of choice.
Variant of Tienna. This is the name of the main character of a Through My Eyes novel.
An invented name, blending the popular phonetic prefix ty and the name Iesha.
From the Egyptian Demotic tꜥ-ꜣs.t meaning "She of Isis".

Variant of Tiger. This is the stage name of American rapper Micheal Ray Stevenson (1989-). He alledges to have been nicknamed Tyga after golf player Tiger Woods, although later reanalyzed the name as the acronym Thank You God Always. The name was brought to limited public attention after the rappers fame in 2013.
Older form of Tiger, used by William Blake in his poem 'The Tyger' (1794).
Transferred use of the surname Tyghe.
Means "Antigonon (a kind of flowering vine)" in Vietnamese.
Means "after" in Chukchi. This name was given to children as a reference the spirits or souls of deceased ancestors or family members.
From the name of Тыгын Дархан (Tygyn Darkhan) a legendary Yakut leader from the 17th century.
Possibly a combination of the popular element ty and the given name Tahir.
Modern name, possibly based on Thais or Tyrese.
Combination of the phonetic elements ty and jay. It can be spelled Tyjae or with a capitalized third letter as TyJae.

Apparently means "smart" in one of the languages on the African continent. However, the name can also be derived from the name abbreviation (or initials) T.J., which is typically pronounced as "tee-jay" and its pronunciation henceforth developed into a first name of its own right (Teejay).
Variant of Tywan, or a combination of the popular phonetic prefix ty and Juan 1.
Blend of the popular phonetic prefix ty and Toccara.
From the Old Norse name Týki, a diminutive of Þórketill (making it a variant of Tóki; see Toki). It was sometimes latinized as Tycho.
Combination of the popular phonetic prefix ty with the name Kisha.
Combination of the popular element ty and the given name Dylan.

Created by author George R. R. Martin for his series "A Song of Ice and Fire" and the upcoming television adaptation "House of the Dragon". In the series, Tyland Lannister is a politician of Westeros and the identical twin brother of Jason Lannister, the Lord of Casterly Rock.
Czech and Polish form of Tilda influenced by Czech and Polish Matylda
Combination of the phonetic elements ty and lee.
Feminization of Tyler using the popular name suffix -lene. It can also be seen as a combination of the phonetic elements ty and lene.
From Turkmen tylla meaning "golden, gold" combined with gözel meaning "beautiful, lovely".

Possibly from Ancient Greek τύλος (tylos) meaning "callus" or "knob, knot". Tylos is a mythological character in Nonnus' epic poem Dionysiaca, where he accidentally touches a serpent which attacks and suffocates him. His sister, the nymph Moria, watches helplessly until the giant Damasen arrives and kills the serpent with a tree trunk. The serpent's mate then revives it using a magical herb and Moria uses the same herb to bring Tylos back to life.
Meaning unknown. This is the name of a character from the 1908 play 'The Blue Bird' (French: 'L'Oiseau bleu') by Belgian playwright and poet Maurice Maeterlinck.
Combination of the phonetic elements ty and lyn.
Combination of the phonetic elements ty and mar.
Elaborated form of Tymar, sharing a sound with names such as Amari and Kamari.
Combination of the popular phonetic prefix ty and Marion 2. It can also be seen as an elaboration of Tymar.
Combination of the phonetic elements ty and meer.

Ukrainian diminutive or folk form of Tymofiy. Tymish Khmelnytskyi was hetman Bohdan Khmelnytskyi's eldest son and projected successor, who was killed at the age of 20 in one of his Moldovan campaigns.
Diminutive of Tymona as well as a quasi-feminine form of Tymoteusz.
Polish transcription of Тимофій (see Tymofiy). b
Variation of the transferred use of the surname Tuíneán.
From Kyrgyz тынчтык (tynchtyk) meaning "peace, quiet" combined with the Turkic military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".
Uncertain etymology, possibly related to Proto-Indo-European *(s)tewd- meaning "to push, to hit" (compare Tydeus). In Greek mythology, Tyndareus was a king of Sparta.

Most likely a diminutive form of Tyndareos (see Tyndareus), since this name contains the Greek diminutive suffix -ιων (-ion). Tyndarion was the name of a tyrant of Tauromenion (which is nowadays Taormina in Sicily), who lived in the 3rd century BC.
Transferred use of the surname Tyne.
Traditional masculine Chukchi name with an unknown meaning.
Traditional feminine Chukchi name with an unknown meaning.
Transferred use of the surname Tyner.
Combination of the popular prefix Ty- and Netta 1.
Variant of Tanika except with the ty- prefix.
Combination of the phonetic elements ty and nees.
From Nivkh tynad meaning "to be exact, correct".
From Kazakh тыныш (tynysh) meaning "quiet, calm, peaceful" and бай (bay) meaning "rich, wealthy".
Khanty and Mansi form of Timothy.
Means "two kettles together" in Oneida. Notable bearer of this name is Tyonajanegen, an Oneida woman who fought in the Battle of Oriskany during the American Revolutionary War.
Possibly from the Ashaninka toniro meaning "moriche palm" and the diminutive suffix -sho.
From the Ashaninka name for a species of yucca, or tyonki meaning "thin bone" and the feminine suffix -ro.
Genus of the cattail plant. Derived from Greek typhos, meaning "marsh".
Variant of Tiphaine. This name is borne by French actress Typhaine Duch (b. 1986).
Medieval diminutive of Tiphaine, recorded in the 1292 census of Paris.
Feminine form of Tyquan, or a combination of the popular phonetic prefix ty and Quanna.
An invented name, probably based on the sounds found in names such as Tyasia, Tyquan and Takisha.
Invented name, probably based on Tyquan and Octavius.
Icelandic and Faroese form of Tyra.

Created by video game developer Blizzard Entertainment for a character in the "Warcraft" video game series. In the series, Tyrande Whisperwind is the High Priestess of Elune and the leader of the night elves.

Derived from Ancient Greek τύραννος (tyrannos) meaning "absolute ruler, tyrant". A known bearer of this name was Tyrannion of Amisus, a Greek grammarian from the 1st century BC. In the case of two early 4th century bishops called Tyrannion, their names derived from the city of Tyre in modern-day Lebanon.
Derived from the Greek noun τύραννος (tyrannos) meaning "absolute ruler" as well as "tyrant, dictator, despot".
From the English word tyranny, ultimately from Ancient Greek túrannos (τύραννος) meaning "lord, master".
The name is a derivative of Tiras who was one of Noah’s grandsons. Specifically Japheth’s son.
Modern form of Þórví traditionally found in Scania.
Variant of Tyrese, influenced by Reece.
Hellenized form of Teti. Sekhemkhet is also known as this name from his later traditioned birth name Djoser-tety.
The name of a disciple of Augustine of Hippo.
Combination of the names Tyr and Grim.

Derived from Latin Tyrianus "of Tyre", an ancient city which is located in modern-day Lebanon. The name of the city itself is said to be derived from a Semitic word meaning "rock".In ancient times, the city was famous for the purple-red dye named Tyrian purple (also known as "royal purple", "imperial purple" or "imperial dye").

Variant of Tyrian.Tyrion is the father of the green dragon Tabaluga in the musical by Peter Maffay. Tyrion Lannister is one of the main protagonists in 'A Song of Ice and Fire' by George R. R. Martin.
Possibly a variant of Tyrus or Tyrese.
Combination of the phonetic elements ty, ree and sha.
Derived from Ancient Greek τυρός (tyros) meaning "cheese".
An invented name, blending the popular phonetic prefix ty and the name Darius (or blending Tyree with Darius).

Possibly derived from Greek τυρός (tyrôs) meaning "cheese". In Greek myth she was a Thessalian princess, daughter of Salmoneus and Alcidice, whose name was allegedly given in reference to her complexion, which was "as fair as white goat's cheese". She was the mother of Pelias and Neleus by the god Poseidon.
A variant of Tyrone likely influenced by Jerome.
Perhaps intended to be a feminine form of Tyrone, combining the popular phonetic prefix ty with the name Rhonda. Also compare Sharonda.
An invented name, blending the popular phonetic prefix ty and the name Veronica.
One of the nine sisters of Morgan Le Fay in Geoffrey’s Vita Merlini.
In the Aeneid, Tyrrheus was a shepherd who's stag was killed by Ascanius, starting a war between the Trojans and the Latins.
Latinized form of Tyrtaios. This name was borne by a Greek poet who lived in the 7th century BC.
Uncertain etymology. This was the name of an ancient Greek elegiac poet from the 7th century BC.
German form of Tyrtaios via Tyrtaeus.
French form of Tyrtaios via Tyrtaeus.

Transferred use of the surname Tyrus, or modern blend of Tyrone and Cyrus.From the city of Tyre in Lebanon, from a word meaning "rock". This is the most common origin in the USA before the middle of the 20th century. Tyrus is the form of "Tyre" used in the King James Version of the Bible in several places in the prophetic books of the Old Testament. There were 97 men listed as Tyrus in the 1850 United States census. It may have been seen as appropriate for a boys' name because it rhymed with Cyrus. It was the given name of the famous baseball player Ty Cobb, who was born in the state of Georgia in 1886. The two years Tyrus crept into the Social Security top 1000 names (1912 and 1916) were during the time when Cobb was an active famous outfielder. He was the holder of many records in the sport of baseball.Perhaps a topographic name from Middle English tye "common pasture".
Either derived from the name of the Norse god Týr (see Tyr) or from Old Norse tyrfi meaning "resinous fir-tree, fatwood".
Dutch variant spelling of Thijs, probably via its other variant spelling Tijs or even the medieval Thys.In West Frisian, this name is a short form of Matthys as well as the original form of Ties.
Combination of the popular phonetic elements ty and sha, possibly modelled on Tasha. Also compare Tyesha.
Combination of the popular phonetic elements ty and shay.
Variant of Tyshae or sometimes Tyshia.
Variant of Tashia using the popular prefix Ty-.
Diminutive of Tykhon. Also means "little quiet one".
Variant of Tashonda using the phonetic element ty.
Saint Tysilio (died 640) was a Welsh bishop, prince and scholar, son of the reigning King of Powys, Brochwel Ysgithrog.
Ukrainian and Belarusian form of Titus.
A shepherd in 'Gallathea", an Elizabethan era stage play, a comedy by John Lyly.
An invented name, blending the popular phonetic prefix ty and the name Tatiana.
Variant of Tytiana. Tytianna was given to 7 girls in 2018 according to the SSA.

Created by author George R. R. Martin for a character in his series 'A Song of Ice and Fire'. In the series, Tytos Lannister is the patriarch of House Lannister during the later years of the Targaryen dynasty and the father of Tywin and Kevan.
Monothematic name derived from Old English element þēod "nation, language" (from þeudō). This name gave rise to the village of Tiddington, a village in Tiddington-with-Albury parish, in Oxfordshire.
Means "tulip". Maybe influenced by Tulipán or Tyulpana.
Combination of the phonetic elements ty and von.
Combination of the prefix ty (as in Tyrone) and the phonetic element wan (as in Twan 3 (a short form of Antwan), Juwan and DeJuan).Also compare Taiwan and Tyjuan.
An invented name, blending the popular phonetic prefix ty and the name Dewayne.
The name of a character in George R. R. Martin's A Song of Ice and Fire series of fantasy novels. He is the patriarch of House Lannister, and father of Jaime, Cersei, and Tyrion.
It is from a great story of Haa
A rarer variant on Tyyne, means "calm". Nameday on September 18th.
Means "righteous, saintly, pious" in Hebrew. Tzadik is also name of צ, letter 18 of Hebrew alphabet.

Etymology uncertain. A possible meaning is "the successor, the counted one", deriving from the Classic Maya element tz’akbuj (counted, successor). Name borne by Lady Tz'akbu Ajaw, who was the mother of K'inich K'an Joy Chitam II of Palenque.
Probably related to Nahuatl tzalantic, "clear water".
Means "elite, top, high level" in Hebrew.
Derived from the notable wife of the Tzar and popularized in the newer 21st century due to it's exotic pronunciation. It means "wife of the great Tzar"
Means "to shout, to yell, to vocalize" in Nahuatl.
Meaning unknown, possibly of Albanian origin. The best known bearer of this name is the Greek actor Tzavalas Karousos (1904-1969).
Hebrew name meaning "justice, justness, fairness, righteous, merit, good deed, mercy, charity".
Variation of the name Tzephanya or Tzephanyahu. Means (Hebrew): 'Secret of God'.
Greek form of the Turkish name Cemile.
Greek form of Jenny, used as a diminutive of Evgenia.
Means "long Life," most likely from Tibetan ཚེ (tshe) meaning "life."
Tzeril is the Yiddish diminutive form of Sarah meaning 'princess'. When an 'e' is added to the end of the name, it adds the meaning 'little', which is an endearment.
Logudorese and Nuorese form of Caesar.

Meaning uncertain. In local legend, a Purépecha princess (sometimes identified as Tzetzangari) wept so bitterly that her tears flooded her village, forming Lake Zirahuén in Michoacán, Mexico. She is one of the three legendary Purépecha women represented in the 'Fuente de las Tarascas' monument in Morelia, Michoacán. (The current bronze sculpture, installed in 1984, depicts three kneeling, bare-chested women holding a large basket of fruit and is widely believed to represent the three Purépecha princesses Atzimba, Eréndira and Tzetzangari. This replaced the original 1931 concrete fountain, whose figures were merely referred to as 'Las Indias' (The Indian Women) without specific names.)
From Nahuatl tzihuactli, a kind of small agave with a spiny flower stalk.
Means "agave arrow" in Nahuatl, an arrow (mitl) made from the stalk of the tzihuactli plant, a kind of small agave.

Meaning uncertain. Possibly derived from Nahuatl tzihuactlah "place of prickly shrubs" (from tzicuactli, a kind of agave plant) and tonalli "day, sun, heat" or "soul, animating force", combined with the diminutive or reverential suffix -tzin.
Means "young prickly corn cob" or "edible part of the tzihuactli cactus" in Nahuatl, from tzihuactli, a kind of small agave, and xilotl "green ear of maize, young corncob".
Means "agave flower" in Nahuatl, from tzihuactli, a kind of small agave plant, and xōchitl "flower".

Variant of Tzihuacxochitl, with the diminutive or reverential suffix "-tzin", a suffix that was often used in Aztec royal families. This name was borne by a queen consort of Tezozomoc, the Tlatoani (ruler) of the city-state of Azcapotzalco.
Diminutive of Tzvi, or sometimes Tzvia. Also compare Tzvika, another diminutive of Tzvi.

Name of an old Otomi warrior ally of Tenochtitlan-Tlatelolco, who stood out during the conquest of Anahuac. According to the chronicles, Tzilacatzin was the only warrior to face Pedro de Alvarado when he arrived with the Spanish in Tlatelolco.
Variant transcription of Zillethai.This transcription is used in the Hebrew Names Version of the Bible.
Variant transcription of Zillethai.This transcription is used in The Complete Jewish Bible and Orthodox Jewish Bible.
Diminutive of Giorgia, possibly influenced by Gina.
Translates to "pulp, flesh", as in the covering on a fruit. Also possibly a short form of Tzipora.
Diminutive form of Tzipporah. A notable bearer is Israeli politician Tzipi Livni, whose full name is Tziporah Malka Livni (1958-).
Alternate transcription of Hebrew צִפּוֹרָה (see Tzipora).
Means "bird" in the Tzeltal and Quiche-Kaqchikel languages. Also the 15th day in the Tzental and Quiche-Cakchiquel calendars in ancient Maya.
Etymology uncertain; the second element is probably mitl, meaning "arrow" in Nahuatl. In Aztec mythology, this was the name of a number of skeletal deities linked to stars, eclipses, and fertility.
Probably derived from Nahuatl tziuhtli "turquoise-browed motmot (bird)" and cōātl "snake, serpent; twin".
Probably derived from tziuhtli "turquoise-browed motmot", a kind of bird.
Variant of the name Tslil which means "sound; voice" in Hebrew.
Modern Hebrew form of Zuph, or directly from Hebrew צוף (tsuf) meaning "nectar, honeydew".
Wade-Giles romanization of Zihan used in Taiwan.

Feminine form of Tzuk. This is also the Hebrew word for a type of bird, the rock thrush (genus Monticola).
Variant of Zuri or Zurie influenced by the Hebrew name Tzuri'el
Yiddish צערטל or צאַרטל from German Zart meaning tender or gentle.

Combination of the name Tzvi and the word עַד (ʿaḏ) "an eternity". The illustration of the gazelle, along with the value of eternity, creates a meaning that represents the beauty and existence of the Land of Israel. Used also as a surname.
Combination of the names Tzvi and El means "Gazelle of God" in Hebrew.
Combination of the names Tzvi and Or meaning "gazelle of light" or "bright gazelle" in Hebrew.

From Thai อวย (uai) meaning "grant, give" and ชัย (chai) meaning "victory".
Means "rain from heaven" or "heavenly rain" in Hawaiian.
Russian form of Valentinus via its hellenized (ancient Greek) form Oualentinos. Also compare the Russian name Valentin, which is directly derived from Valentinus.
Russian form of Valerianus via its hellenized (ancient Greek) form Oualerianos. Also compare the Russian name Valerian, which is directly derived from Valerianus.
Russian form of Valerius via its hellenized (ancient Greek) form Oualerios. Also compare the Russian name Valeriy, which is directly derived from Valerius.
Derived from Old Irish úall "vanity, pride" and garg "fierce, rough".
From Arabic ولِي (walī) meaning "guardian, friend" combined with the Turkic title khan meaning "leader, ruler".
Derived from Irish uall meaning "pride". Uallach ingen Muinechain (died 934) was an Irish woman poet and Chief Ollam of Ireland.
Derived from Old Irish úallach "proud, arrogant" combined with a diminutive suffix.
Of uncertain etymology, name borne by a king of Mannae.
From Sino-Vietnamese 蘊 (uẩn) meaning "to accumulate, to contain, profoundness".
Means "younger brother or sister, beloved" in Lao. If written ອ້ວນ (uan) it means "stout, fat, large".

Means "like a wolf" in Ossetian, derived from Scythian varka "wolf". His name comes from the fact that wolves were seen as a totemic symbol to the Ossetian people. This is the name of the ancestor of the Narts in the Ossetian Nart epic. He is the father of twins Akhsar and Akhsartag. Uarkhag can be compared to the Roman gods Romulus and Remus and Greek Castor and Pollux.
Anglicised as the etymologically unrelated given name Kennedy, The name is said to have been borne by various families of the surname Kennedy.

From an Ossetian form of the name George. In Ossetian mythology, this is the name of a patron god and the father of Satanaya. He is considered the patron of the present-day North Ossetia-Alania. He is still worshipped today in Uatsdin, the Scythian pagan religion practised by the modern-day Ossetians.
From Irish úathach meaning "terrible, dreadful". In Irish legend she was the daughter of Scáthach and fellow teacher at her school for warriors.
Samoan form of Walter. Also the word for "watch" in Samoan.

From the name of Saint Elijah of the Bible. Uatsilla was the God of rain, lightning, and thunder, and the protector of the harvest. If one was struck by lightning, they were considered to be chosen by this God, and if they survived, they would receive a sheep sacrifice in their honor. There is a festival celebrated in the summer in his honor.

Meaning unknown. A famous bearer of this name is Uatu a.k.a. The Watcher from a series of Marvel comic books, movies, TV shows etc. (beginning 1963). He is the narrator of the Disney+ series "What if...?".
Short form of Ubbe.Ub Iwerks, born Ubbe Ert Iwwerks, was an American animator, cartoonist and character designer known best for the design of Mickey Mouse.
Means "he who serves god" in Arabic.
Alternate transcription of Arabic عبيد (see Ubayd), as well as the usual Urdu form.
Alternate transcription of Arabic عبيد الله (see Ubayd Allah), as well as an Urdu variant.
English and Polish form of Hugbald and French variant of Ubalde.
French form of Hugbald via it's Latinized form Ubaldus.

Feminine form of Ubaldo. Saint Ubaldesca Taccini (1136–1205) was an Italian Roman Catholic nun and member of the Order of Saint John. Among the miracles attributed to her the most famous is the ability to turn water from the water well in the Church of the Santo Sepolcro in Pisa into wine. Her feast day is celebrated on 28 May.
Spanish, Galician, Portuguese, and Italian diminutive of Ubalda.
Medieval Italian diminutive of Ubaldo, as -uccio is an Italian masculine diminutive suffix.

Of uncertain etymology, possibly derived from the Sumerian element tum, meaning "wind; cardinal point" or "to bring; to carry away; to obtain". Ubartum was a female physician of the Neo-Sumerian Empire, who lived in Garšana.
From the Serbian feminine form of убав (ubav) meaning "beautiful, gorgeous, delightful".

The latter is known for having been expelled from Nepal and lost the throne to his younger brother, although his son later retook the Nepalese throne. There were also three Sri Lankan kings named Udaya: Udaya I, Udaya II and Udaya III, rulers of Anuradhapura.
