Derived from the Old English elements wulf "wolf" and weald "powerful, mighty" which in turn means "powerful wolf, mighty wolf". Old English cognate of Wulfoald and Wulfald.
Derived from the Old English elements wulf "wolf" and weard "guard, guardian".
Derived from the Old English elements wulf "wolf" and wig "war, battle".
Derived from the Old English elements wulf "wolf" and wine "friend".

A Benedictine abbott born near Boulogne, Picardy, France, he was actually married but was separated from his wife and entered the Benedictines as a lay brother at Haumont, in Hainault. He was eventually ordained and was the founder of the rnonastery of Samer near Boulogne, which he served as abbot. The abbey was named Saint-Vulmaire in his honor.

The name of a Benedictine bishop and monk also called Ultius. A disciple of St. Dunstan, he was named by the saint to serve as superior over the restored community of Westminster, England, circa 960, and eventually became abbot in 980. In 993 he was named bishop of Sherborne, although he remained abbot of Westminster.
Modern and Middle English form of Wulfstan and variant of Wolstan, and Wolfstan.
Of uncertain meaning, this was the personal name of Aguda's eldest daughter.
A boatman who ferries the souls of the dead to Purelko, the afterlife in Australian Aboriginal mythology.

column3: Умар, Омар, Омэр(Western Circassian, Eastern Circassian, Circassian)

column12: From the Chinese 妩 (wǔ) meaning "charming, enchanting" and 媚 (mèi) meaning "charming, attractive".
From Chinese 武 (wǔ) meaning "military, martial" combined with 梦 (mèng) meaning "dream" or 萌 (méng) meaning "bud, sprout", or other characters that are pronounced similarly

Either derived from Old High German wunna "bliss, delight, pleasure" or from Old English wuna "habit, custom; practice, rite". Saint Wuna of Wessex was a 7th and 8th-century Anglo-Saxon noblewoman and Christian saint.
Means "it is God who gives" in Dagbani.
Derived from Old High German wunna "bliss, delight, pleasure" combined with Old High German bald "bold, brave."
Means "God has given me" in Dagbani.
West Frisian variant spelling of Wubke and Low German variant spelling of Wübke via Wüpke.
Means "gold of wealth" or "shining treasure of wealth" in Yoruba.
it's a name given to a surviving child
Archaic Sorbian form of Ursula, recorded in the 17th century.
The name of a Hattian goddess whose name may potentially mean "Mother of the land".

From the characters 寤 (wù, meaning “to wake” or alternatively “difficult”) and 生 (shēng, meaning “born”). This was the personal name of Duke Zhuang of Zheng (郑庄公), the third ruler of the state of Zheng during the Chinese Spring and Autumn Period (770 - 473 BCE). According to historical records, he was named because of the difficult manner of his birth (interpreted either as birth in his mother’s sleep or a breech birth).
From Thai วุฒิ (wutthi) meaning "knowledge" and ชัย (chai) meaning "victory".
Alternate transcription of Burmese ဝတ်ရည် (see Wutyi).
Alternate transcription of Burmese ဝတ်ရည် (see Wutyi).
Alternate transcription of Burmese ဝတ်ရည် (see Wutyi).
From the Chinese 妩 (wǔ) meaning "charming, enchanting" and 玟 (wén) meaning "streaks in jade, gem".

column3: 无羡, 武贤, etc.(Chinese)|無羨, 武賢, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 武 (wǔ) meaning "military, martial" or 无 (wú) meaning "nothing, without" combined with 贤 (xián) meaning "virtuous, worthy, wise" or 羡 (xiàn) "to admire, to envy, to covet". Other hanzi combinations are possible. A famous fictional bearer is Wei Wuxian, protagonist of danmei novel Mo Dao Zu Shi.

A combination of the characters 无 (wú, meaning "no, without") and 艳 (yàn, meaning "color, vibrancy, beauty"). This was one of the names attributed to Zhongli Chun (钟离春), a woman who lived in the state of Qi during the Chinese Warring States period (475 - 221 BCE). According to legend, she was extremely ugly yet also clever and wise. She successfully convinced King Xuan of Qi to solve four latent risks present in his kingdom, after which she was made his queen and advisor.

From Chinese 舞 (wǔ) meaning "dance" combined with 瑶 (yáo) meaning "precious jade" or 曜 (yào) meaning "bright, brilliant, glorious; one of the seven planets of premodern astronomy." Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Of uncertain meaning, this was the name of the eldest brother of Aguda. He was given the temple name Kangzong by his descendant Emperor Xizong of the Jin dynasty.
From the Chinese 舞 (wǔ) meaning "dance" and 瑛 (yīng) meaning "luster of gems, crystal".

column3: 五月, 武跃, 吴越, 舞月, 武岳, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 五 (wǔ) meaning "five", 武 (wǔ) meaning "military, martial", 吴 (wú) referring to the ancient state of Wu or 舞 (wǔ) meaning "dance" combined with 月 (yuè) meaning "moon", 跃 (yuè) meaning "jump, leap", 越 (yuè) referring to the Yue people who inhabited southern China and northern Vietnam or 岳 (yuè) meaning "tall mountain". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
Of uncertain meaning. This was the personal name of a secondary consort of Hong Taiji. She was from the Yehe-Nara clan.
Name of a son of Wyandanch.
Name of a Montaukett sachem who helped to form an alliance between the English settlers and his tribe.
From Old English Wigbeorn, derived from Old English elements wig meaning “battle” and beorn meaning “warrior, man".
Middle English form of the Old English name Wigburg.
Transferred use of the surname Wyclef. A known bearer of this name is the Haitian-American artist Wyclef Jean.
Transferred use of the surname Wyeth.
Variant or feminine form of Wyatt or variant of Wyette and Wyetta.
Perhaps a feminine variant of Wiley or an invented name based on the sound of Twyla.
A character in the Protector of the Small book series (author Tamora Pierce). Presumably it is a variant of Weldon.
Wyldstyle is the female protagonist in "The LEGO movie". The name is derived from "wild style" with literal meaning.
Sorbian form of Wilhelm. Wylem Šybaŕ (German: Wilhelm Schieber), born 1887, was a Sorbian artist.
Transferred use of the surname Wyler.
From a surname that was either a variant of Wiley or a distinct surname derived from a Scots diminutive of the given name William.
Short form of the archaic name Wylliam. In other words, you could say that this name is an older form of Will.

In the United States, this name is a variant spelling of the feminine name Willa.In Brazil, this name is a unisex name that is most likely a short form of given names starting with Wil-, Wyl- and perhaps even Guil- (such as Guilherme).
An old English derivative of the word will. Meaning Wish/Will
Medieval Low German form of William, found in 15th-century Estonia and 16th-century Latvia.

In the English-speaking world, this is an archaic spelling of William, which is sometimes understandably perceived as a modern spelling of the name, due to the current trend of spelling traditional names differently.In Brazil, this is a variant spelling of William, which you could perceive to be modern in this case, as this spelling only emerged in Brazil in the last decades (at least as early as the late 1970s).A known bearer of this name was Wylliam Martin, a 16th-century mayor of the city of Galway in Ireland.
The name of a 6th Century Cornish saint.
Transferred use of the surname Wyman.
Anglicized form of the Old Breton name Wiuhomarch, which is made up of the elements wiu "worthy, noble" and march "horse".

column5: WIE-nahnt(Medieval Dutch, Dutch)|VIE-nahnt(Medieval Dutch, Dutch)|WEE-nahnt(West Frisian)|VEE-nahnt(West Frisian)
column12: Medieval Dutch form of Wijnand, Frisian variant of Winand and South African form of Winand.Known bearers of this name include the retired South African rugby player Wynand Claassen (b. 1951), the South African darts player Wynand Havenga (b. 1965) and the South African rugby union player Wynand Olivier (b. 1983).

column5: wie-NAHN-dah(Medieval Dutch, Dutch)|vie-NAHN-dah(Medieval Dutch, Dutch)|wee-NAHN-dah(West Frisian)|vee-NAHN-dah(West Frisian)
column12: Medieval Dutch form of Wijnanda, Frisian variant of Winanda and South African form of Winanda.
Allegedly a Southern USA feminization of the Welsh name Llewellyn.
Transferred use of the surname Wyndham.
Alternate transcription of Burmese ဝိုင်း (see Waing).
Feminine form of Wyn using the popular name suffix elle.

Used by S. Alice Callahan for the heroine of 'Wynema: A Child of the Forest' (1891), the first novel written by a Native American woman. Callahan was one-sixteenth Muscogee (Creek), but it is unknown if this name was commonly used in the Creek tribe or if she invented it for use in her book.The name is also used by Native Americans belonging to the following nations: Caddo, Modoc, and Omaha.
Variant of Wynette or a combination of Wyn and Etta.

Allegedly derived from the rune ᚹ (equivalent to Old English Ƿ (wynn) and Gothic � (winja)). The rune is associated with the words joy and bliss, probably because the name of the rune is ultimately derived from Proto-Germanic *wunjō "joy, delight".

Wynkyn de Worde (originally Jan van Wynkyn) was William Caxton's journeyman, after whose death he became the first printer to set up his shop in Fleet Street, "which was for centuries perhaps the world's most famous centre of printing." It was used in the popular children's poem Wynken, Blynken, and Nod (Dutch Lullaby) (1889).
Alternate transcription of Burmese ဝင်း (see Win).

Means "gift of joy" in Old English, from the mostly-poetic word wynn "joy, delight, bliss" combined with gifu, an alternative form of giefu "gift, present".Keeping in mind that spelling was much looser in Anglo-Saxon times, it seems that ġiefu was mainly used for the vocabulary word, while ġifu was preferred for given names.
Derived from the Old English elements wynn "joy" and helm "helmet, protection".
Derived from the Old English elements wynn "joy" and here "army".
Derived from Old English elements wynn "joy" and hild "battle"
Variant of Winnie or a feminine diminutive of Wynn.
Latinized form of the Old English name Wynngifu.
Derived from the Old English elements wynn "joy" and sige "victory".
Variant of Winter, the spelling influenced by that of Wynn.
Derived from Old English elements wynn "joy" and þryþ "strength"
Derived from wynn "joy, delight" and wulf "wolf". The Wulfwynn is the same but in the reverse order.
Older form of Wijntje. This name was found among Dutch colonists in America in the 1600s and 1700s.
Older form of Wijntje. This name was found among Dutch colonists in America in the 1600s and 1700s.
Variant of Winton. Two jazz musicians bear this name, Wynton Marsalis and Wynton Kelly.

Cornish form of Breton Gwenole. St Wynwallow's Church, the parish church of Landewednack in Cornwall, England, is dedicated to Saint Gwenole or Winwaloe. Built of local serpentine stone, it is the most southerly church in mainland Britain and the church in which the last sermon in the Cornish language was preached, in 1674.
Medieval Hungarian and Medieval Ukrainian cognate of Viola.
Possibly from the American state name Wyoming.
Meaning unknown. Notable bearer of the name is Wyomia Tyus (1945—).
From the US state of Wyoming.
Possibly derived from the state of Wyoming in the United States.
Alternate spelling of Wyatt, or possibly Wyot.
Possibly a combination of the phonetic element wy and Ouida.
The name is derived from the the name of the rivers Afon Wyre in Wales and Wyre in Lancashire. It means "winding river". It is bourne by the BBC journalist Wyre Davies.
Derived from the Slavic name elements wysze "higher" and niega "delight".
Feminine Polish name derived from wysze meaning "higher" and sław meaning "glory, fame".
Transferred use of the surname Wythe.

The first element of this name is derived from Polish wzorowy "exemplary, model", which is in turn derived from Polish wzór "example, model". Also compare Croatian uzoran and Czech vzorný, both of which also mean "exemplary, model". The second element is derived from Slavic slav "glory".
From Sino-Vietnamese 賒 (xa) meaning "distant, far" or 車 (xa) meaning "vehicle".
From Sino-Vietnamese 麝香 (xạ hương) meaning "musk" or "thyme".
Portuguese form of Shadreck. It is mostly used in Mozambique.
Created from the name Adrian by adding an initial letter X.

This name was devised by South African entrepreneur Elon Musk and Canadian musician Claire "Grimes" Boucher for their son, born in 2020. The name was originally X Æ A-12, but was changed to X Æ A-Xii because California law does not allow the use of numbers in names. According to Grimes: - The X is the unknown value, typically seen in mathematics;- The Æ is the 'Elven spelling' of AI, the acronym for "artificial intelligence" and also the word for "love, affection" in several languages (i.e., Japanese 愛 (ai) and Chinese 爱 (ài));- The A-Xii is from the Lockheed aircraft A-12, the precursor of SR-17, which is said to be their 'favorite aircraft'. The A in A-12 also stands for "Archangel", from the song title of the same name made by British musician Burial, which Grimes describes as 'her favorite'.
Derived from Uzbek xafif meaning "fine, light"
Name of the daughter of the vizier who tells stories to the king at the beginning of ‘One Thousand and One Nights’
Possibly from Teochew 屎 (xái) meaning "residue of smoked tobacco or opium".

Variant of Sainte. This name was borne by Xainte Dupont (1595-1680), an early settler of New France, the wife of settler Zacharie Cloutier (1590-1677), and an ancestress to the Cloutier family of Quebec.
Possibly an invented name. It was borne by contestant Xairexis García on the Spanish-language talent show La Voz Kids.
Variant of the Tatar name Häkimcan.
Derived from Nahuatl xalli "sand" combined with either icuilolli "painting, piece of writing" or cuilol "a design, a decoration".
Azerbaijani and Uygur form of Khaliq.
From the name of mount Xalo in the town of Cerceda, Spain.
Means "sweet" in Somali. It is the name of a Somali dessert.
From Sino-Vietnamese 侵 (xâm) meaning "to invade, encroach".
Xamaniqinqu is a benevolent Maya god and the brother of the hostile triad of Yantho, Usukan, and Uyitzin.
Somali form of Hamid 1 or Hamid 2.
From Sino-Vietnamese 縝 (xân) meaning "detailed, fine, careful".

Short form of Alexandra, Alexander, Xanthe and other names containing xan. A known bearer is American actress and director Alexandra 'Xan' Cassavetes (1965-), the daughter of actor-director John Cassavetes and actress Gena Rowlands.
From the word xana, a type of fairy in Asturian mythology who are said to live in pure rivers and fountains. It may derive from the Roman mythological name Diana.

From the name of the summer capital of the 13th-century Mongol ruler Kublai Khan, located in Inner Mongolia, China. It is an anglicized form of Chinese 上都 (Shangdu), derived from 上 (shàng) meaning "above, upper" and 都 (dū) meaning "city".
Variant of Xander. This is the name of one of the housemates on the cartoon Drawn Together.
Elaboration of Xandra or short form of Alexandrea.
Xandrie is the name of a fiction character, played by Adelaide Clemens, in a 2010 Australian film called "Wasted on the Young."
From the Shipibo xane, referring to a species of small green bird, and the genitive suffix -n.
From a non-Sino-Vietnamese reading of Chinese 青 (thanh) meaning "blue, green".
Tatar and Bashkir form of Hanifa.
Means "khans, rulers, leaders" in Azerbaijani, from the plural form of xan (see kaan).
Possibly based on Zanna or Xandra.
From Uyghur خان meaning "ruler, leader" combined with قىز meaning "girl".

column5: ksan-TEH-na(Canarian Spanish, Guanche Mythology)|san-TEH-na(Canarian Spanish, Guanche Mythology)
column12: From Guanche *šan-əḍănay, meaning "twin recipient". In Guanche mythology, she was the mother of all humans.
Modern elaborated form of Xanthe. It coincides with the name of a yellow organic heterocyclic compound; xanthene dyes tend to be fluorescent and brilliant, yellow to pink to bluish-red.
Possibly an elaboration on Xanthe, used in Mark Z. Danielewski's 'The Familiar' series.

Derived from Greek ξανθος (xanthos) meaning "yellow" or "fair hair". This was used by the Greek playwright Aristophanes in works including 'The Frogs'; all of the characters named Xanthias are slaves.
French form of Xanthippos via its latinized form Xanthippus.
Latinized form of Xanthippos. A known bearer of this name was Xanthippus of Carthage, a Spartan mercenary general from the 3rd century BC.
Derived from Ancient Greek ξανθός (xanthos) meaning "yellow, blond, fair-haired".
Latinized form of Xanthios. This is the name of a minor character from Greek mythology as well as of a 3rd-century saint who was one of the 33 martyrs of Melitene.

Derived from Ancient Greek ξανθός (xanthos) meaning "yellow" or "blond, fair hair" (see Xanthe). This name is sometimes included as one of the Nereids of Greek myth (the fifty daughters of Nereus by Doris).

Feminine form of Xanti.It also coincides with xantiana, a latinised adjective derived from the Hungarian surname Xántus that is found in the binomial names of some flowering plants, notably Clarkia xantiana and Chaenactis xantiana.
Catalan form of Xanthippos via its latinized form Xanthippus.
Portuguese form of Xanthippos via its latinized form Xanthippus.

Latinate form of Xanthippe. Saint Xantippa or Xanthippe and her sister Saint Polyxena were Spanish martyrs of the 1st century. The apocryphal Acts of Xanthippe and Polyxena is a 3rd- or 4th-century account of their lives.
Maybe derived from the originally Hungarian surname Xántus.
Mir Xanzad was a military commander and ruler of the Soran Emirate in the late 16th or early 17th century. The castle that she had built and resided in bears the same name.
From Sino-Vietnamese 巧 (xảo) meaning "skillful, cunning, crafty".

Xaphan is the name of a fictional character depicted from later Christian demonology and occult literature. Xaphan was most famously detailed in the 19th-century 'Dictionnaire Infernal' by Collin de Plancy. In the story, Xaphan was a fallen angel of the second rank who joined Lucifer's rebellion. The legend states that Xaphan proposed setting Heaven on fire before all the fallen angels were cast into the abyss.
Derived from Persian خاقانی (khaghani). Khan (or khagan) is a historic Turkic and Mongolic title to refer to a king. Khaqani Shirvani (1126-1199) was the pen name of a major Persian poet.
Diminutive of Xaqueline, variant of Zackie/Zachie.

Invented name in the same fashion as Yaretzi and Nayeli. Despite popular belief on the Internet, it was coined at most in the late 20th century and it is not related to any goddess or princess in Otomi folklore.
Meaning uncertain, possibly an elaborated form of Xaria.
Meaning uncertain, possibly modelled on names like Marielys or Karielys.
Alternate transcription of Greek Χάρης or Χάρις (see Charis).
This is the name of one of the Thirteen and later king of Qarth in George R. R. Martin's Song of Ice and Fire.
Possibly in part from Arabic خاص (khāṣṣ) meaning "special, particular, distinguished".
From Uygur خاسىيەت meaning "character, trait", from Arabic خَاصِّيَّة (ḵāṣṣiyya).
From Persian خطائی (khatā'i) meaning "the Cathayan". Khata'i was the pen name of Shah Ismail I, who wrote poetry in the Azerbaijani language.
Probably a short form of Xavier.
Dutch and Flemish form of Xaverius as well as an English variant of Xavier.
Czech and Dutch feminine form of Xavier.
Latinized form of Xavier. In Indonesia, the name is often paired with Fransiskos or Fransiskus, in honour of the Spanish saint Francis Xavier (1506-1552).
Possibly a feminine form of Xavian or an elaboration of Xavia.
Vietnamese form of Xavier. This is usually used in combination with Phanxicô to honor Saint Francis Xavier.

This name is possibly a combination of Xavier with a Hebrew name ending in -iel, such as Gabriel. However, given the fact that this name has been around in the Spanish-speaking world since at least the 18th century, it could also be an independent name of its own (in which case its etymology is unknown), as combining names in that manner generally seems to be a fairly modern phenomenon in the Spanish-speaking world.A known bearer of this name was the Asturian (Spanish) writer Xaviel Vilareyo (1967-2015).
Languedocian and Gascon form of Xavier.
Languedocian and Gascon feminine form of Xavièr and Provençal feminine form of Xavier.
Formed from Xavier and the on suffix found in such names as Davion, Javion, Trevion and Tavion.
Variant of Xavier, influenced by Saviour.
Modern, Polonised form of Xavier (see Ksawery).
Means "victory" in Lao, ultimately from Sanskrit जय (jaya).
Possibly a variant of Zaya and Xaia.
From the Arabic حياة (hayat) meaning life and Persian بانو (banu) meaning "lady".
Tatar and Bashkir form of Haidar.
One of the main antagonists in Michael Ende's fantasy novel The Neverending Story (1979).
From Lao ໄຊ (xay) meaning "victory" and ຄຳ (kham) meaning "gold".
Variant of Zaylee. 12 girls in the USA were given the name Xaylee in 2021 according to the USA Social Security Administration.
From Lao ໄຊ (xay) meaning "victory" and ປະເສີດ (paseuth) meaning "excellent, precious, superb".
Derived from Uzbek xayr meaning "blessing" or "charity" and gul meaning "rose, flower".
Variant of Khayrullo used in Uzbekistan.
From Lao ໄຊ (xay) meaning "victory" and ສະຫວັນ (savanh) meaning "heaven, paradise".
From Lao ໄຊ (xay) "victory", ສົມ (som) "priest", and ພອນ (phone) "good blessing".
Derived from the Adyghe зечэ (zeche) meaning "breeder, trainer" and хьэ (kh'e) meaning "dog".

The exact etymology of Xbaquiyalo is not definitively established. Some interpretations suggest connections to concepts like "Little and Gory Bone" or "Little and Gory Kernel," possibly linking her to themes of death and the underworld.Xbaquiyalo is a figure in the Popol Vuh, the sacred narrative of the Kʼicheʼ Maya people. She is the wife of Hun Hunahpu, one of the "first twins," and the mother of the Monkey Twins, Hun Batz and Hun Chouen. These twins are known as the patron deities of the arts, including music, writing, and sculpture.Xbaquiyalo's role in the narrative is brief; she dies shortly after childbirth and is not mentioned further in the text.
From Xcaret, a Mayan place name meaning "small inlet" or "little bay".
From ancient mixtec, a mexican language
Means "to move out of the way" in Vietnamese.
Means "waning sun" or "waning moon" in Vietnamese.

The name XEAN has the same meaning with the name SEAN. The first letter "S" was just replaced with letter "X".Xean has the same meaning with the name SEAN.It is derived from an Irish name SEÁN (Anglicized to SEAN) meaning "YAHWEH (The LORD) is gracious", God is gracious, God's gracious gift.
Means "born" or "produce, give rise to" in Hmong. More likely in names it is derived from the Hmong form of the Chinese 心 (xin) meaning "heart".
This name comes from a character from Kingdom Hearts Birth by Sleep and also has some short appearances in Kingdom Hearts 2.

Name used by the Lummi people of northwest Washington state for the Transformer, a being that appears in the mythologies of many indigenous peoples who inhabited the Pacific Northwest Coast. This legendary figure (or figures) is also known as Xáays in Squamish and Xa:ls in Halkomelem.
Means "a spring of water" in Yucatec Maya.
Probably related to Nahuatl xeloa "to divide, to distribute". This was the name of a giant in Aztec mythology, one of seven survivors of the great flood.
Dutch variant of Sem, influenced by the popularity of X- starting names.
Aragonese and Galician form of Gema.
The name of a gargoyle demon in the 'Ruby Red' trilogy by Kerstin Gier.The name spilled over to real life use in Germany.
Variant of Zen. This name was used by American actors Tisha Campbell and Duane Martin for their son born 2001.
Transferred use of the surname, which comes from 'xenos' meaning "stranger, foreigner" and the suffix '-akis'.
Derived from Ancient Greek ξένος (xenos) meaning "foreign, strange" as well as "foreigner, guest" combined with ἀνδρός (andros) meaning "of a man".

Derived from Greek ξένος (xenos) meaning "foreign, strange" as well as "foreigner, guest" combined with either the Greek noun ἀρχός (archos) meaning "master, leader" or the Greek noun ἀρχή (arche) meaning "origin, source".
Latinized form of Xenarchos. A notable bearer of this name was Xenarchus of Seleucia (1st century BC), a Greek Peripatetic philosopher and grammarian.
Name of various villages in Galicia, like the parish of Xende (Lama, Pontevedra). The toponyms are hypotesized to ultimately come from some Germanic forename.
Slovak, French and Hungarian form of Xenia.
Both a Galician borrowing of Xenia and a short form of Euxenia used as a given name in its own right.
The Catalan writer Eugeni d'Ors has used this name as a pen name. (See Xenius and Xènia.)
Latinized form of Greek Ξένιος (Xenios), a masculine form of Xenia.

Perhaps a variant of Zeno or maybe a Latinized form of Xenon.A notable male bearer was a a Swiss rower and Olympic gold medallist: Xeno Müller. He's Born on August 7th 1972.Recently used first in 2017 with 7 baby boys born with this name.

Derived from Greek ξένος (xenos) meaning "foreign, strange" as well as "foreigner, guest" combined with either the Greek noun χαρά (chara) meaning "joy, delight, happiness" or the Greek noun χάρις (charis) meaning "grace, kindness" (see Chares).
Derived from Greek ξένος (xenos) meaning "foreign, strange" as well as "foreigner, guest" combined with the Greek noun χάρις (charis) meaning "grace, kindness".
Latinized form of Xenokleia. In Greek mythology, this is the name of a priestess and oracle of the temple of Apollo at Delphi.
Variant latinization of Xenokleia, because its proper (and most common) latinized form is Xenoclea.
Variant latinization of Xenokleidas, because its proper latinized form is Xenoclidas.This is one of the names under which the Corinthian commander Xenokleidas (5th century BC) is known.
Latinized form of Xenodike. This is the name of several characters in Greek mythology, one of which is a Cretan princess.
Derived from Greek ξένος (xenos) meaning "foreign, strange" as well as "foreigner, guest" combined with the Greek noun δίκη (dike) meaning "justice, judgement" as well as "custom, usage".
Masculine form of Xenodike. This was the name of an Olympic victor from 400 BC.
Derived from Greek ξένος (xenos) meaning "foreign, strange" as well as "foreigner, guest" combined with the Greek noun δῶρον (doron) meaning "gift".
Latinized form of Xenodoros. This was the name of a Greek architect from the 4th century BC.
Galician and Portuguese form of Xenophanes.
Catalan and Romanian form of Xenophon.
Galician and Portuguese form of Xenophon.
Feminine form of Xenokles. In Greek mythology, this name belonged to a Delphic priestess who was consulted by Herakles.

Aeolic and Doric Greek form of Xenokleides, because it contains ίδας (idas), which is the Aeolic and Doric Greek form of the patronymic suffix ἴδης (ides).This was the name of a Corinthian commander who participated in the Peloponnesian War (431–404 BC). He is better known under the latinized forms of his name, including those of its Attic Greek form Xenokleides.
Means "son of Xenokles" in Greek, derived from the name Xenokles combined with the patronymic suffix ἴδης (ides).This was the name of an Athenian poet from the 4th century BC.
Derived from Ancient Greek ξένος (xenos) meaning "foreign, strange" as well as "foreigner, guest" combined with πατήρ (pater) meaning "father" (genitive πατρός).

It is widely used as a place name (like Xingfu Road) and is a common name for boys, signifying a blessed life.

Xiwangmu is one of the oldest and most important goddesses in Chinese mythology, with evidence of her cult dating back to the Shang Dynasty (c.1600 - 1046 BCE). She is said to reside in the west on Mount Kunlun, accompanied by sacred animals. Early texts depict her as a fearsome goddess with disheveled hair, tiger’s teeth, a leopard’s tail and the ability to control five plagues, but in later Chinese history she became a benevolent matriarch who conferred immortality and ruled over all female immortals.Her name is commonly translated as "Queen Mother of the West".

The exact etymology of Xmucane is not definitively established. Some interpretations suggest connections to concepts like "burial" or "earth pit" in old Kʼicheʼ, possibly linking her to themes of the earth and the underworld. However, these interpretations are speculative and not universally accepted. Xmucane is a central figure in the Popol Vuh, the sacred narrative of the Kʼicheʼ Maya people. She is revered as the divine grandmother, embodying wisdom, creation, and guidance.In the creation myth, Xmucane, along with her counterpart Xpiyacoc, attempts to create humanity. After unsuccessful attempts using mud and wood, they succeed by forming humans from maize dough, highlighting maize's sacred significance in Maya culture. Xmucane also plays a pivotal role in the upbringing of the Hero Twins, Hunahpu and Xbalanque, guiding them through their challenges and adventures.

Yalavaç is the "authorized conveyer of the divine or sovereign mandate." Etymologically, it is built upon the ancient Turkic verb root *yala- ("to command, to send a message, to charge with a mission"), combined with the native agent suffix -vaç to denote a functional, high-level envoy.The common colonial-era attempt to tie Yalavaç to Persian administrative suffixes is inherently flawed because it misidentifies the word's structural anatomy. The etymological anchor is not a Persian suffix, but the pure Turkic head-root *yala-. This root is completely absent from the Persian lexicon, yet it stands firmly at the center of Old Turkic administrative terminology. Because the word's foundation is entirely Turkic, looking for a Persian origin in the tail-end is a linguistic non-sequitur. Furthermore, Yalavaç appears natively in Manichaean Uyghur texts long before the era of intensive Persian-Turkic linguistic synthesis, proving it is an organic, indigenous construct meaning "the one who bears the flame of the message."The most prominent bearer of this title, Mahmud Yalavaç, was an Urgench Turk who weaponized the sophisticated Uyghur bureaucratic infrastructure to manage the complex tax systems of the Mongol Empire. Remembered as the "architect of nomadic administration," he was the pragmatic genius who translated the raw will of the steppe khans into structured imperial law, serving as the ultimate bridge of early Eurasian statecraft.

From the Chinese 焱 (yàn) meaning "flames" and 露 (lù) meaning "dew".
From the Chinese 滟 (yàn) meaning "overflowing, billowing" and 鸾 (luán), a mythological bird.
From the Chinese 燕 (yàn) meaning "swallow (bird)" and 纶 (lún) meaning "green silk thread".

column3: 艳梅, etc.(Chinese)|艷梅, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 艳 (yàn) meaning "beautiful, gorgeous" combined with 梅 (méi) meaning "plum, apricot". This name can be formed from other combinations of characters as well.
From the Chinese 琰 (yǎn) meaning "jewel, gem, glitter of gems" and 淼 (miǎo) meaning "wide expanse of water".

column3: 艳敏, etc.(Chinese)|艷敏, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 艳 (yàn) meaning "beautiful, gorgeous" combined with 敏 (mǐn) meaning "quick, clever, sharp". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 彦明, 燕鸣, 燕明, 衍明, 岩明, 琰铭, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 彦 (yàn) meaning "elegant, handsome, learned", 燕 (yàn) meaning "swallow (bird)", 衍 (yán) meaning "overflow, spill over", or 岩 (yán) meaning "cliff, rocks" combined with 明 (míng) meaning "bright, light, clear" or 鸣 (míng) "sing, call, cry". Other hanzi combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 滟墨, 彦茉, 儼默, 彥謨, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From the Chinese 滟 (yàn) meaning "overflowing, billowing" or 彦 (yàn) meaning "elegant" and 墨 (mò) meaning "ink" or 茉 (mò) meaning "white jasmine".
Place name; a rural suburb on the outskirts of Melbourne in Victoria, Australia. Its name is from a local language and means "walk about, travel, journey, roam".

French borrowing of Breton Yanna 2. Yanne Charbonneau (aka Vianne Rocher) is the main character of the book The Lollipop Shoes by Joanne Harris, sequel of Chocolat.
Variant of Yanelis mainly used in Venezuela.

From Chinese 燕 (yàn) meaning "swallow (bird)" combined with 妮 (ní) meaning "maid; little girl". This name is also used as a translation for German Jenny, especially Johanna "Jenny" Bertha Julie von Westphalen. Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From Chinese 延 (yán) meaning "stretch, prolong" combined with 年 (nián) meaning "year". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 雁宁, etc.(Chinese)|雁寧, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 雁 (yàn) meaning "wild goose" combined with 宁 (níng) meaning "peaceful, tranquil". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Used by Eloise Jarvis McGraw in her 1997 Newberry Honor book "The Moorchild". It is borne by the protagonist's step-father.

From the Chinese 燕 (yàn) meaning "swallow (bird)" and 祺 (qí) meaning "good luck, good fortune".
From the Chinese 燕 (yàn) meaning "swallow (bird)" and 勤 (qín) meaning "industrious, diligent, attentive".

column12: From Chinese 彥 (yàn) meaning "elegant, handsome, learned", 艷 (yàn) meaning "beautiful, gorgeous", or 燕 (yàn) meaning "swallow (bird)" combined with 卿 (qīng) meaning "minister, high officer, noble", 清 (qīng) meaning "clear, pure, clean", or 青 (qīng) meaning "blue, green, young". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

column12: From Chinese 艳 (yàn) meaning "beautiful, gorgeous", 硯 (yàn) meaning "inkstone" or 晏 (yàn) meaning "late, peaceful, quiet, tranquil" combined with 秋 (qiū) meaning "autumn" or 球 (qiú) meaning "ball, sphere, orb". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
From 雁 (yàn) meaning "wild goose" and 全 (quán) meaning "pure jade".
From the Chinese 嫣 (yān) meaning "charming, fascinating" and 燃 (rán) meaning "light fire, ignite".
From the Chinese 妍 (yán) meaning "beautiful, handsome" and 娆 (ráo) meaning "graceful, charming, fascinating".
From the Chinese 燕 (yàn) meaning "swallow (bird)" and 仁 (rén) meaning "humaneness, benevolence, kindness".
From the Chinese 琰 (yǎn) meaning "jewel, gem, glitter of gems" and 荣 (róng) meaning "glory, honour, prosper".

Modern Spanish and Caribbean name, predominantly used in Cuba. It is a contemporary phonetic hybrid that emerged during the late 20th-century Caribbean naming wave (often called the "Generación Y" phenomenon), where parents creatively invented names starting with the letter 'Y'. Linguistically, it adapts traditional European elements into a modern Hispanic framework, combining the Slavic and Dutch root Jan (a derivative of John, meaning "God is gracious") with a Germanic diminutive suffix similar to Hansel.
From the Chinese 燕 (yàn) meaning "swallow (bird)" and 善 (shàn) meaning "good, virtuous, kind".
From the Chinese 燕 (yàn) meaning "swallow (bird)" and 绍 (shào) meaning "continue, join".

From 艳 (yàn) meaning "bright, gaudy" and 淑 (shū) meaning "limpid, clear, pure".
From the Chinese 炎 (yán) meaning "flame, blaze" and 霜 (shuāng) meaning "frost".
From the Chinese 燕 (yàn) meaning "swallow (bird)" and 水 (shuǐ) meaning "water".

From the Chinese h嫣 (yān) meaning "fascinating, charming" and 稣 (sū) meaning "revive, rise again".
Derived from the Persian جان‎ (jan) meaning "soul" and сылу (sylu) meaning "beautiful".
Meaning uncertain. Most likely a hostile god to humanity and one of the Mayan gods of earthquakes. A part of the Yantho triad along with Usukan.

Possibly from Sanskrit यान्ति (yānti) meaning "they go, they pass by", ultimately from याति (yāti) meaning "to go, to move". Alternately it could be taken from the sound yanti present in many Indonesian names of Indian origin, such as Damayanti or Jayanti.
From the name of the month of January (Januari in Indonesian), usually used as a given name for a boy born in January.
Ukrainian or Ukrainianised form of Janusz.
From Russian январь (yanvar) "January", making it a cognate of Januaria. (Cf. Oktyabrina, Noyabrina.)
From the Chinese 燕 (yàn) meaning "swallow (bird)" and 娃 (wá) meaning "doll, pretty girl".

column12: From Chinese 彦 (yàn) meaning "elegant, handsome, learned" or 妍 (yán) meaning "beautiful" combined with 玮 (wěi) meaning "fine jade, rare, precious" or 威 (wēi) meaning "power, pomp". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

column12: From Chinese 延 (yán) meaning "stretch, prolong", 严 (yán) meaning "strict, rigid, severe, intense", 妍 (yán) meaning "beautiful" or 燕 (yàn) meaning "swallow (bird)" combined with 文 (wén) meaning "literature, culture, writing" or 雯 (wén) meaning "cloud patterns". From the Chinese 妍 (yán) meaning "beautiful, handsome" and 妩 (wǔ) meaning "charming, enchanting".
From the Chinese 燕 (yàn) meaning "swallow (bird)" or 琰 (yǎn) meaning "jewel, gem, glitter of gems" and 曦 (xī) meaning "sunlight, sunshine, early dawn" or 夕 (xī) meaning "evening, night, dusk".
From Chinese 艳 (yàn) meaning "beautiful, gorgeous" or 雁 (yàn) meaning "wild goose" combined 霞 (xiá) meaning "rosy clouds, mist". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

From the Chinese 燕 (yàn) meaning "swallow (bird)" or 妍 (yán) meaning "beautiful, handsome" and 馨 (xīn) meaning "fragrant, aromatic" or "distant fragrance" or 心 (xīn) meaning "heart, mind, soul".
From the Chinese 雁 (yàn) meaning "wild goose" and 煦 (xù) meaning "kind, gentle, gracious".
From the Chinese 炎 (yán) meaning "flame, blaze" and 璇 (xuán) meaning "beautiful star, jade".
From the Chinese 燕 (yàn) meaning "swallow (bird)" or 琰 (yǎn) meaning "jewel, gem, glitter of gems" and 勋 (xūn) meaning "meritorious deeds, merits" or 洵 (xún) meaning "true, real, truly".
Named from the Kingdom of Yany in Gambia, a diminutive of Yanimarew.

column3: 燕燕, 炎炎, 妍妍, 雁雁, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 燕 (yàn) meaning "swallow (bird)", 炎 (yán) meaning "flaming, blazing, burning, red", 妍 (yán) meaning "beautiful, handsome" or 雁 (yàn) meaning "wild goose" all combined with themselves. Other character combinations can form this name as well.
From the Chinese 焰 (yàn) meaning "flame, blaze, glowing" and 瑶 (yáo) meaning "precious jade".
From the Chinese 琰 (yǎn) meaning "jewel, gem, glitter of gems" and 怡 (yí) meaning "happy, joyful, harmony, joy".
From the Chinese 炎 (yán) meaning "flame, blaze" or 滟 (yàn) meaning "overflowing, billowing" and 滢 (yíng) meaning "clean, pure water; lucid, glossy".
From the Chinese 燕 (yàn) meaning "swallow (bird)" and 优 (yōu) meaning "superior, excellent".

column3: 琰媛, 嫣鸢, 燕媛, 雁媛(Chinese)
column12: From the Chinese 琰 (yǎn) meaning "jewel, gem, glitter of gems", 嫣 (yān) meaning "charming, fascinating", 燕 (yàn) meaning "swallow (bird)" or 雁 (yàn) meaning "wild goose" and 媛 (yuàn) meaning "beauty, beautiful woman" or 鸢 (yuān) meaning "kite (bird)".
From the Chinese 滟 (yàn) meaning "overflowing, billowing" or 焱 (yàn) meaning "flames" and 月 (yuè) meaning "moon" or 悦 (yuè) meaning "pleased, contented".
The name frequently breaks down into characters meaning "strict" or "serious" (严, Yan) and "correct" or "upright" (正, Zheng), reflecting historical familial virtues of integrity and discipline.
From the Chinese 彦 (yàn) meaning "elegant" or 燕 (yàn) meaning "swallow (bird)" and 蓁 (zhēn) meaning "abundant, luxuriant vegetation" or 珍 (zhēn) meaning "precious, valuable, rare".
From the Chinese 燕 (yàn) meaning "swallow (bird)" and 智 (zhì) meaning "wisdom, knowledge, intelligence".
Uncertain etymology, possibly derived from the Mongolian feminine suffix маа (maa) and an unknown first element. Also compare Yanzhima.

Alternative name or epithet of the Queen Mother of the West, which translates to "Golden Mother of the Nacre Lake" or "Golden Mother of the Mother-of-Pearl Lake".
Means "to make war cries", from Nahuatl yoatl "war, warfare; combatant" and choca "to cry, weep; to bleat, roar, growl".
Means "war woman, warrior woman" in Nahuatl, from yaotl "combatant; war, battle" and cihuatl "woman".
Means "war kite, combative kite", derived from Nahuatl yao- "war, combat" and cuixtli "kite (bird of prey)".

column3: 耀华, etc.(Chinese)|耀華, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 耀 (yào) meaning "shine, sparkle, ray, radiance" combined with 华 (huá) meaning "splendid, illustrious, flowery, Chinese". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
From the Chinese 瑶 (yáo) meaning "precious jade" and 欢 (huān) meaning "joyous, merry".

column3: 耀辉, etc.(Chinese)|耀輝, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 耀 (yào) meaning "shine, sparkle, ray, radiance" combined with 辉 (huī) meaning "brightness". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

From a combination of the characters 瑶 (yao, meaning "beautiful jade") and 姬 (ji, meaning "princess; noble woman"). Yaoji is "the goddess of Wushan", a mountain in southern China. Some sources say that she was a daughter of the Flame Emperor, while later ones incorporate her into the Daoist religion by making her a daughter of Xiwangmu.She is most well-known from two poems, The Ode of Gaotang and The Ode of the Divine Maiden, both of which are attributed to the late Warring States poet Song Yu (c. 298 – 263 BCE). Both poems have her encountering a king of the Chu state, but while she invites the king to cavort with her in the former, she rejects the king in the latter.
From the Chinese 瑶 (yáo) meaning "precious jade" and 瑾 (jǐn) meaning "brilliance of gems, fine jade".
From the Chinese 姚 (yáo) meaning "handsome, elegant" and 晶 (jīng) meaning "crystal, clear, bright, radiant".
From the Chinese 谣 (yáo) meaning "folksong, ballad" and 玲 (líng) meaning "tinkling of jade".

From the Chinese 瑶 (yáo) meaning "precious jade" and 清 (qīng) meaning "clean, pure, clear".
From the Chinese 耀 (yào) meaning "shine, sparkle, dazzle, glory" and 蕊 (ruǐ) meaning "unopened flowers, flower bud".
From the name of a river in central Nicaragua, hence the heavy concentration of the name's usage in that country.
From the Chinese 谣 (yáo) meaning "folksong, ballad" and 纱 (shā) meaning "gauze, thin silk".

column12: From Chinese 耀 (yào) meaning "shine, sparkle, ray, radiance" combined with 胜 (shèng) meaning "victory, success" or 生 (shēng) meaning "living, fresh". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
From the Chinese characters 瑶 (yáo) meaning "precious jade" and 霜 (shuāng) meaning "frost; crystallized".
More commonly used variant of Yaosca.
From the Chinese 瑶 (yáo) meaning "precious jade" and 松 (sōng) meaning "pine, fir".
From Thai เยาว์ (yao) a prefix meaning "young, youthful" and ธิดา (thida) meaning "daughter".
Means "scorching of war" or "destruction of war" in Nahuatl.

From the Chinese 瑶 (yáo) meaning "precious jade" and 星 (xīng) meaning "star, planet, point of light".

From the Chinese 瑶 (yáo) meaning "precious jade" and 勋 (xūn) meaning "meritorious deeds, merits".

From the Chinese 瑶 (yáo) meaning "precious jade" and 煜 (yù) meaning "bright, shining, brilliant".
From the Chinese 姚 (yáo) meaning "handsome, elegant" and 玥 (yuè) meaning "mythological pearl".
From the Chinese 瑶 (yáo) meaning "precious jade" and 珍 (zhēn) meaning "precious, valuable, rare".
From the Chinese 谣 (yáo) meaning "sing, folksong, ballad" and 筝 (zhēng) meaning "zheng zither", "kite".
From the Chinese 瑶 (yáo) meaning "precious jade" and 智 (zhì) meaning "wisdom, knowledge, intelligence".

Alternate transcription of Arabic يعقوب (see Yaqub).
From Bashkir яҡшы (yaqšï) meaning "good" and feminine name element бикә (bikä).
Variant of Jacqueline in use in Latin America. It is especially popular in Cuba.
Meaning uncertain, possibly related to Nahuatl yaoquiza "to go to war". Alternatively, may be related to Yaquin.
Possibly derived from Nahuatl yaqui "departed, gone, having left for a place".
Variant of Yakisha or Yakeisha, a combination of the phonetic element ya with the name Keisha.
Transcription of Bashkir and Uyghur form of Yaqub.
Refers to a specific kind of cow in Dinka.
Italian form and variant transcription of Yaara.

Alternate transcription of Arabic يارا (see Yara 1).

Khanty and Mansi form of Gerasim.
Derived from yarash meaning "reconciliation" and gul meaning "flower, rose".

Meaning uncertain, perhaps an elaboration of Yara 1 or Yara 2 using the same suffix as Lizeth. Also compare Yaretzi, Yaritza.The name Yarazetd is borne by both the wife and daughter of Venezuelan politician and four-star general Vladimir Padrino López (1963-).
Traditionally a surname, although not a common one.
Transferred use of the surname Yarde.
From the Kurdish yar meaning "mistress" and dil meaning "heart".
Transferred use of the surname Yardley.

Allegedly derived from a Taíno word meaning "small gold jewelry", for example necklaces of gold.-------------------------------------Spanish name derived from hebrew "yarib" meaning "to strive/fight." Famous bearer is is Jerubbaal(Fights with Baal) also known as Gideon.
Variant of Yarielis, itself a feminine variation of Yariel.

Derives from the Ugaritic yariḫ ("moon"). Name borne by a moon god worshipped in the Amorite and Ugaritic pantheons, and later as part of the Phoenician and Punic pantheons following the collapse of Ugarit. He was regarded as the husband of Nikkal, as attested in the myth "The Marriage of Nikkhal and Yarikh". His Mesopotamian equivalent was Sin.
Yarilo is a Slavic god of vegetation, fertility and spring.
Combination of Yari and Mar, perhaps modelled on Marimar and Larimar.
Masculine and feminine variant of Yaron.
Variant of Irina, perhaps influenced by the Slavic element yaru meaning "energetic".
Combination of Yaris and the popular element -bel.

Perhaps a variant of Yaritza. It is borne by Yarishna Ayala (1991-), a Puerto Rican bodybuilder and fitness model on Instagram. This name was given to 18 girls born in the United States in 2018, and to 28 girls born in the United States in 2019.
Combination of Yaris and Leidis, present mostly in Cuba.
Elaboration of Yaris with the popular suffix -leth (cf. Yamileth, Yanisleth).
Variant of Yaritzel, which is a variant form of Yaritza (perhaps influenced by Itzel and Alitzel).
Means "rival" or "he will fight" in Hebrew.

From Persian یار (yār) meaning "friend, companion" and the given name Muhammet.
Archaic variant of Ierofey. The spelling might have been influenced by Slavic names that contain the Slavic element yaru meaning "fierce, energetic", such as Yaroslav.
French form of Yaroslav, one of the given names of Jacques Jean Yaroslaw Marie, Duke of Orléans (1941-)

The name of a Polabian god of war, often identified with the Roman god Mars.Scholars connect the root jar- with the Proto-Slavic adjective *jarъ(jь) "vigorous, strong" or alternatively with *jarъ "vernal", and thus be connected to the Slavic deity of vegetation Jarylo.In the second part there is supposed to be a suffix -vit meaning "lord, ruler, hero". The suffix has been linked to the word *vitati "to invite, to wish health".The deity is also known as Jarovit and Gerovit.
Means "child" in Yoruba, Nago and Kanga, spoken in Northern and Western Africa.
Means "deep water" in Darug. Yarramundi was a famous 18th/19th century Indigenous leader from the western Sydney area; many of his descendants still live in the area.
Transferred use of the surname Yarrio.
Transferred use of the surname Yarrow, and/or from the word for the flowering plant (Achillea millefolium).

Yasur is a first name and a last name that refers to some types of birds that live near the sea.1. The family Procellariidae is a group of seabirds that comprises the fulmarine petrels, the gadfly petrels, the prions, and the shearwaters. This family is part of the bird order Procellariiformes (or tubenoses), which also includes the albatrosses, the storm petrels, and the diving petrels.2. Puffinus is a genus of seabirds in the order Procellariiformes. It comprises about 20 small to medium-sized shearwaters. Two other shearwater genera are named: Calonectris, which comprises three or four large shearwaters, and Ardenna with another seven species (formerly often included within Puffinus).Yasur is also the name of a military helicopter, which is knows as "The CH-53 Sea Stallion" in English.

A profoundly traditional Turkic name meaning "God bestowed a child" or "a child is given." It is formed by joining the Old Turkic root yav / yavru / yavrık (offspring, child, new generation) with the past tense conjugation of the verb ber- / bir- "to give" (birdi). Symbolically, it stands for deep gratitude, divine gift, and lineage survival. Rooted deeply in Tengrism, it was traditionally bestowed by grateful families who had waited a very long time for a child (mirroring the precise theological logic of names like Tengriverdi, Kutverdi, or Ayverdi).

She was born somewhere in Númenor. She had two siblings (brothers), the younger being Axantur and the older being Oromendil. Her uncle Amandil would take the Sceptre as Tar-Amandil, third King of Númenor. Nothing else is known of her life, including whether she married and had children.

column12: From Sino-Korean 藝 (ye) meaning "art, talent, craft" or 叡 (ye) meaning "shrewd, astute, clever, keen" combined with 娜 (na) meaning "elegant, graceful, delicate". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

Yendembe means ‘he is free’ and is the childhood name of Lonkundo in the Nkundo mythology complex. It also means “Take No Orders”.

This is the name of a town in northeastern Ghana. A famous bearer is Yendi Phillips, she is a Jamaican TV Host, model and beauty queen who the winner of the Miss Jamaica World 2007 beauty pageant, as well as the Miss Jamaica Universe 2010 pageant.

This name is most likely a combination of two given names, such as Yesenia and Daniel (or an other Hebrew name that ends in -iel). Names like these are often formed from the names of the bearer's parents, since it is fairly common in Middle America and South America for parents to give their children a combination of their own names. The names Elián and Josmar are good examples of this. Last but not least, it should be noted that in some cases, this name can also be a variant spelling of Jeniel. Also compare Yenuel.A known bearer of this name is Yeniel Bermúdez (b. 1985), a Cuban soccer player.

Yennenga is a legendary princess, and is considered to be the mother of the Mossi people. Her son Ouedraogo was the founder of the Mossi Kingdoms.

Alternate transcription of Greek Γενοβέφα (Genovefa), the Greek form of Geneviève via Italian Genoveffa.

column3: 여정(Korean Hangul)|旅程, 璵正, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 旅程 (yeojeong) meaning "itinerary, journey". Alternatively, it could come from 璵 (yeo) meaning "beautiful jade" combined with 正 (jeong) meaning "right, proper, correct". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
From Sino-Korean 麗 "beautiful, magnificent, elegant" and 珍 "precious, valuable, rare". A famous bearer is Australian fashion designer Yeojin Bae.

Meaning unknown. This was the personal name of Jungjong (1488-1544), king of Joseon from 1506-1544.

column3: 예온(Korean Hangul)|藝穩, 譽穩, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 藝 (ye) meaning "art, talent, craft" or 譽 (ye) meaning "fame, reputation" combined with 穩 (on) meaning "peaceful, serene". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.
Meaning unknown. This was the personal name of Seonjo (1552-1608), fourteenth king of Joseon.

column3: 연아(Korean Hangul)|娟雅, 妍雅, 娟娥, 妍娥, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 娟 (yeon) or 妍 (yeon) both meaning "beautiful" combined with 雅 (a) meaning "elegant, graceful, refined" or 娥 (a) meaning "good, beautiful". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well. A famous bearer is the retired South Korean figure skater Kim Yeon-a (1990-).

column3: 영아(Korean Hangul)|英雅, 永雅, 英娥, 永娥, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 英 (yeong) meaning "flower, petal, brave, hero" or 永 (yeong), meaning "long, deep, forever" combined with 雅 (a) meaning "elegant, graceful, refined" or 娥 (a) meaning "good, beautiful". Other hanja combinations are possible.
From Sino-Korean 永 "long, perpetual, eternal, forever" and 培 "bank up with dirt; cultivate".

column3: 영빈(Korean Hangul)|英斌, 榮斌, 永斌, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From From Sino-Korean 英 (yeong) meaning "flower, petal, brave, hero" or 榮 (yeong) meaning "glory, honour, flourish, prosper" or 永 (yeong), meaning "perpetual, eternal" combined with 斌 (bin) meaning "refined". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 영복(Korean Hangul)|英福, 永福, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 英 (yeong) meaning "flower, petal, brave, hero" or 永 (yeong), meaning "long, deep, forever" combined with 福 (bok) meaning "fourtune, blessing, luck". Other hanja combinations are possible.

column3: 영찬(Korean Hangul)|永燦, 英讚, 泳贊, 映璨, 暎讚, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Combination of a yeong hanja, like 永 meaning "long, lengthy," 英 meaning "floral decoration; excellent, outstanding," 泳 meaning "swim," 映 or 暎, both meaning "shine, reflection," and a chan hanja, such as 燦 meaning "shine; sparkle," 讚 meaning "praise; support," 贊 meaning "help; bright; praise" or 璨 meaning "beautiful gem."
From 英 (yeong) "petal, flower, leaf; brave, a hero" and 昌 "light of sun; good, proper".
From Sino-Korean 靈 (yeong) meaning "spirit, soul, deity" and 大 (dae) meaning "large, big".

column3: 영은(Korean Hangul)|英恩, 榮恩, 永恩, 英銀, 榮銀, 永銀, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From From Sino-Korean 英 (yeong) meaning "flower, petal, brave, hero" or 榮 (yeong) meaning "glory, honour, flourish, prosper" or 永 (yeong), meaning "perpetual, eternal" combined with 恩 (eun) meaning "kindness, mercy, charity" or 銀 (eun) meaning "silver, money". From 淵 "gulf, abyss, deep", 涓 "brook, stream; select; pure" or 延 "delay, postpone, defer" (yeon) and 近 "near, close" or 根 "root; foundation".

column3: 영광(Korean Hangul)|永光, 英光, 榮光, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Combination of a yeong hanja, like 永 meaning "long, lengthy," 英 meaning "floral decoration; excellent, outstanding" or 榮 meaning "prosperity, glory," and a gwang hanja, e.g. 光 meaning "light."
From Sino-Korean 榮 (yeong) meaning "glory, honor; flourish, prosper" combined with 均 (gyun) meaning "equal, even, fair".

column3: 영하(Korean Hangul)|映河, 映夏, 榮河, 榮夏, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 映 (yeong) meaning "to reflect, shine, mirror, illuminate" or 榮 (yeong) meaning "glory, honor, flourish, prosper" combined with 河 (ha) meaning "river, stream" or 夏 (ha) meaning "summer, grand, great". Other Hanja combinations are possible.
From Sino-Korean 年 (yeon) meaning "year" and 鶴 (hak) meaning "crane (bird)".

column3: 영훈(Korean Hangul)|英勛, 榮勛, 永勛, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From From Sino-Korean 英 (yeong) meaning "flower, petal, brave, hero" or 榮 (yeong) meaning "glory, honour, flourish, prosper" or 永 (yeong), meaning "perpetual, eternal" combined with 勛 (hun) meaning "meritorious deed, rank". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 영화(Korean Hangul)|永和, 靈和, 榮和, 永火, 靈火, 榮火, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 永 (yeong) meaning "eternal, forever" or 靈 (yeong) meaning "soul, spirit, deity" or 榮 (yeong) meaning "glory, honour, prosper", combined with 和 (hwa) meaning "harmony, peace" or 火 (hwa) meaning "fire". Other hanja combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 영현(Korean Hangul)|英賢, 榮賢, 瑛賢, 英顯, 榮顯, 瑛顯, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: Fron Sino-Korean 英 (yeong) meaning "flower, petal, brave, hero" or 榮 (yeong) meaning "glory, honour, flourish, prosper" or 瑛 (yeong) meaning "jade" combined with 賢 (hyeon) meaning "virtuous, worthy, wise" or 顯 (hyeon) meaning "manifest, clear". column3: 영일(Korean Hangul)|英一, 榮一, 永一, etc.(Korean Hanja)

Composed of the endearing Kazakh term Yerke ("cherished," "spoiled in a loving way," "darling of the family") and Ay ("Moon"). It translates to "The Cherished Moon" or "The Beloved Moon." This name captures a profound emotional aesthetic, it is not merely about beauty, but about the specific, tender affection a family holds for a child who is their source of light and pride. The name is a modern Turkish feminine given name derived from the combination of the Turkic elements yer meaning "place, earth, soil, land" and su meaning "water, river, life-fluid." It is a direct reference to the sacred primordial entity Yersu (Old Turkic (Orkhon): 𐰘𐰯𐰼:𐰾𐰆𐰥 (YER SUB)), the personification of the sacred landscape, homeland, and natural order in Turkic mythology and Tengrism.In the ancient spiritual cosmos of the Altai, Orkhon, and Steppe peoples, Yersu is not a singular anthropomorphic goddess, but a collective divine essence; the spiritual unity of the homeland's soil, mountains, rivers, and trees. Belonging to the middle realm (the world of humans), the Yersu spirits represent the physical and spiritual anchor of the Turkic soul. In the Orkhon Inscriptions, the protective deities of the state are explicitly invoked alongside Gök Tengri as "Ötüken’in Kutsal Yer-Subu" (The Sacred Earth-Water of Ötüken), highlighting their role as the ultimate guardians of national independence, tribal sovereignty, and ecological balance.Unlike the specialized deities of agrarian societies, Yersu is an animistic and ecological collective representing the living pulse of the geography itself. It is the spiritual consciousness of the nomadic horizon; the unseen protectors residing in the peaks of sacred mountains like Khan Tengri or Altay, and the depths of untamed rivers. In Siberian traditions, violating nature (polluting a spring or cutting an ancient tree) was seen as a direct offense against the Yersu, as they are the life-sustaining fabric of the forest and the steppe, acting as the bridge between human morality and cosmic harmony.For the family, this name carries the weight of the sacred homeland. It symbolizes a child who possesses an "Unshakable Soul"; a spirit as grounded and nurturing as the protective mountains of Ötüken, yet as fluid and adaptive as the great rivers of Central Asia. It suggests a daughter who does not merely occupy a space, but sanctifies it; a personality that carries the stabilizing force of the land, possessing the innate wisdom to bring stability, fertility, and peace to her surroundings. To bear this name is to be the "Sacred Sanctuary." It bestows a legacy of moral nobility, suggesting a life defined by deep roots that defy storm winds and a grace that flows like boundless, life-giving waters. She is the "Guardian of the Source," representing a beauty that is organic, enduring, and protective; a presence that, like the Earth-Water of the ancestors, whispers resilience into the passing ages.

column3: 怡瑶, 忆谣, 旖谣(Chinese)

From Chinese 宜 (yí) meaning "suitable, proper" combined with 瑜 (yú) meaning "fine jade" or "lustre of jade". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 怡缘, 宜缘, 怡缘(Chinese)
column12: Derived from the Chinese 怡 (yí) meaning "happy, joyful" or "harmony, pleasure, be glad" or 宜 (yí) meaning "suitable, right, proper" and 缘 (yuán) meaning "hem, margin" or "reason, cause, fate"

column3: 怡悦, 依悦, 懿月(Chinese)

From the Chinese 宜 (yí) meaning "suitable, right, proper" and 云 (yún) meaning "clouds".

From the Chinese 仪 (yí) meaning "ceremony, rites, gift, admire" and 哲 (zhé) meaning "wise, sage".

Invented by Finnish poet Eino Leino (1878-1926) for the main character of his poem Helkavirsiä I. Perhaps derived from Finnish ylevä "sublime" or from the prefix ylä- "superior, upper, high, higher". It's been used as a diminutive of Yrjö in parts of Finland.

Yll is the name of a Martian in the story Ylla in the Martian Chronicles written by Ray Bradbury.

The name was most likely invented for the character of a little girl in the German film "Wickie und die starken Männer", released in 2009. It was probably based on the Scandinavian name Ylva meaning "she-wolf". It quickly caught on in Germany as a Nordic sounding given name and has enjoyed some popularity in the Netherlands as well, spelled Ilvy. It is most likely a modern German invention, but has been used rarely as a given name in Scandinavian countries as well.
Variant of Imani. Ymania Brown (1963-2025) was a Samoan LGBTQ rights activist and lawyer.

Possibly an Old English name in which the second element is mære "famous". Saint Ymar was a 9th-century Benedictine monk at Reculver Abbey in Kent, England, who was killed by marauding Danes. Alternatively, may be a relation to Ímar.
Possibly derived from Livonian im "miracle" and and "gift".

Old English form of Emma and Irma, from Germanic element irmin "whole" or "great". Queen Emma of Normandy (wife of Æthelred the Unready and Cnut) is referred to as "Ymma" in the 1017 entry of the Manuscript F of the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle.
Yndiara Asp is a Brazilian skateboarder who participated in the Olympic Games, Tokyo 2021.

Old Norse combination of Ing and vár "spring".

Possibly a variant of Yngvi. According to Gesta Danorum, Yngwin was a king in Götaland, who was a close friend to one of the Danish kings named Halfdan.
From Sino-Vietnamese 鷾鴯 (ý nhi) meaning "swallow (bird)".
Means "delicately or subtly meaningful", from Sino-Vietnamese 意 (ý) meaning "wish, desire, meaning" and 蕊 (nhị) meaning "stamen, pistil".
Uncertain etymology, possibly derived from the feminine suffix -ynja, which is added to nouns to indicate a female individual.

Feminine form of Ynyr (and, as such, the Welsh cognate of Honora).

Used as a female name in modern Hebrew, Yodfat is a variant of the Hebrew name Yotvat, which is derived of the Hebrew root TOV, meaning good. Yotvat was a walled Jewish town in the north-west Galilee from as early as the 3-4 centuries BC. Later, the Romans, who ruled the land, altered the pronunciation to Yodfat.During the First Jewish-Roman war, Yodfat withstood a 47-day seige in the year 67AD. Following this revolt Yodfat was rebuilt and the town kept its Jewish culture and life.
Derived from Uzbek yodgor meaning "remembrance, monument".

From the Korean word 요정 (Yo-Jeong), which comes from Sino-Korean 妖精. The character 妖 (Yo (妖)) means "Supernatural." The character 精 (Jeong (정)) means "Spirit." This name can also be spelled with the Hanja 謠 meaning "Song," 曜 meaning "Radiant," 姚 meaning "Pretty," 僥 meaning "Luckily," or 瑤 meaning "Precious stone," for Yo (요), and 貞 meaning "Virtue" or 晶 meaning "Crystal; Diamond" or "Glittering" for Jeong (정).

column3: 偉正, 偉政, 頼正, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 偉 (yori) meaning "admirable" and 雅 (masa) meaning "elegant, graceful". Other kanji combinations can be used.

Name that was given during the Hēan Period, to a Court Noble, "藤原 頼通" FUJIWARANOYORIMICHI, married to "隆姫女王" TAKAHIME the Japanese Princess Takahime. The Kanji Character "頼" meaning "Rely" with the Kanji Character "通" meaning "Street".
From 頼 (yori) meaning "trust, rely" and 光 (mitsu) meaning "light, radiance". Other kanji combinations can be used.

Name that was given during the Kamakura Period to "源 頼朝" MINAMOTONOYORIMOTO who was the Founder and the First Shōgun of the Kamakura Shogunate of Japan. His Buddhist Name was "武皇嘯原大禅門" BUKŌSHŌGENDAIZENMON. He was married to "北条 政子" HŌJŌ MASAKO, a Political Leader.

Name that was given during the Hēan Period, to a Court Noble, "藤原 頼宗" FUJIWARANOYORIMUNE, married to "源倫子" MINAMOTONORINSHI the Japanese Empress Rinshi. The Kanji Character "頼" meaning "Rely" with the Kanji Character "宗" meaning "Religion", "Sect".

column3: 頼宣, 頼信, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 依 (yori) meaning "to depend on" and 宣 (nobu) meaning "announce". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: よりのり(Japanese Hiragana)|頼徳, 頼升, 頼則, 頼憲, 頼範, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 頼 (yori) meaning "to rely" and 徳 (nori) meaning "virtue". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: よりお(Japanese Hiragana)|ヨリオ(Japanese Katakana)|頼夫, 頼雄, 頼男, 頼郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 頼 (yori) meaning "depend, rely" combined with 夫 (o) meaning "man, husband", 雄 (o) meaning "hero, manly", 男 (o) meaning "male" or 郎 (o) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 順敬, 頼敬, 飛由, 尚和, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 順 (yori, jun, nao) meaning "obey, submit, order, occasion, docile, turn, right" or 頼 (yori) meaning "trust, request" combined with 敬 (kei, taka, kyo) meaning "respect, honor, reverence, awe" or 飛 (taka, hi) meaning "flight, to fly, overhead". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From 頼 (yori) meaning "to rely" and 藤 (to) meaning "wisteria". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 頼朝, 依智, 尚朋, 順友, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 頼 (yori) meaning "to rely" or 和 (yori) meaning "harmony, Japanese style, peace, soften, Japan" combined with 朝 (tomo) meaning "morning" or 朋 (tomo) meaning "friend". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 和禎, 由禎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 和 (yori) meaning "peace, harmony, tranquility" or 由 (yori) meaning "reason, cause" combined with 次 (tsugu) meaning "next, order, sequence, below", or 亜 (tsugu) meaning “second, Asia, sub-”. Other kanji combinations can be used.

Derived from the Uzbek yorliq meaning "order, decree" and boy meaning "rich, wealthy".
Variant spelling of the Finnish name Jorma.In Germany, there is a snack food chain named YORMA'S after its founder Yorma Eberl.
Invented name, probably based on the sounds found in other names such as Jordan and Norman.
Derived from the Uzbek yor meaning "friend" and murod meaning "aim, wish, desire".

Derived from the Uzbek yor meaning "friend" and nazar meaning "look, glance".

column3: よろこび(Japanese Hiragana)|喜, 慶, 悦, 歓, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 喜び (yorokobi) meaning "joy". Other spellings are possible.
Derived from Uzbek yorqin which can mean "bright, vivid", "clear", or "lucky, fortunate, happy"; and oy meaning "moon".
Derived from the Uzbek yor meaning "friend" and quvvat meaning "strength, force, power, might, energy".
Derived from the Uzbek yor meaning "friend" and said meaning "fortunate".

Yorsch is also the main protagonist in two independent series of children's books, firstly 'Der letzte Elf' "The last Elf" by Silvana de Mari (appeared in a notable publishing house), secondly the Yorsch series by Christoph Schellenberg (self published).
Derived from the Uzbek yor meaning "friend" and soat meaning "time, minute".

It could be derived from the Yoruba word Ori Obba "the Head King". This is the name of a West African ethnic group mainly inhabits parts of Nigeria, Benin, and Togo. Yoruba Richen (1972- ) is an American film director, screenwriter and producer.
From Japanese 夜 (yoru) meaning "night" and 一 meaning "one".Yoruichi Shihoin is a character from the 'Bleach' anime and manga series.

column3: 夜子(Japanese Kanji)|ヨル子(Kanji/Katakana)|よるこ(Japanese Hiragana)|ヨルコ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name is used as 夜子 with 夜 (ya, yo, yoru) meaning "evening, night" and 子 (shi, su, tsu, ko, -ko, -ne) meaning "child, sign of the rat (1st sign of the Chinese zodiac)." Alternatively, it can be used as ヨル子 with ヨル, the phonetic characters representing Yoru, and 子.One fictional bearer of this name is Yoruko Shinomiya (四宮 夜子) in the computer game Coμ - Kuroi Ryū to Yasashii Ōkoku (コミュ - 黒い竜と優しい王国 -).This name is extremely rare. According to data gathered from phonebooks, only 4 people (presumably women) have 夜子 as their name and only 1 has ヨル子 as their name.
From Japanese 夜 (yoru) meaning "night" combined with 月 (tsuki) meaning "moon". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Derived from the Uzbek yor meaning "friend" and the given name Yusuf.

Korean form of Joseph.One bearer of this name is footballer Park Yo-seb (1980-), who was part of the squad for the 2004 AFC Asian Cup.

column3: 陽青, 陽精, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 陽 (yo) meaning "light, sun, male" and 青 (sei) meaning "blue, green". Other kanji combinations can be used.妖精 (yosei) is an unrelated word that means 'fairy'.
an elaboration of Josel combined with the diminutive medieval German suffix mann
From Sino-Korean 耀 "shine, sparkle, dazzle; glory" and 燮 "harmonize, blend; adjust".
Indonesian form of Joseph, more often used by Christians.
Famous bearer: Mexican goalkeeper Yosgart Gutiérrez.

Khanty and Mansi variant and diminutive of Yoshchkigi.
