column3: 恵吾, 好亜, 禎亜, 芳亜, 善開, 義空, 由愛, 美亜, 美空, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 恵 (yoshi) meaning "favour, benefit", 好 (yoshi) meaning "fond, pleasing, like something", 禎 (yoshi) meaning "happiness, blessed, good fortune, auspicious", 芳 (yoshi) meaning "perfume, balmy, favorable, fragrant", 善 (yoshi) meaning "virtuous, good, goodness", 義 (yoshi) meaning "righteous", 由 (yoshi) meaning "cause, reason" or 美 (yoshi) meaning "beautiful" combined with 吾 (a) meaning "I, me", 亜 (a) meaning "second, Asia", 開 (a) meaning "open, unfold, unseal", 空 (a) meaning "sky" or 愛 (a) meaning "love, affection". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 宜親, 宜悠, 美親, 義親, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 宜 (yoshi) meaning "good, best regards" combined with 親 (chika) meaning "parent, elder" or 悠 (chika) meaning "permanence".
From Yoshie combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child."This name is very rarely used.

column3: 吉文, 喜文, 佳文, 孝文, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 吉 (yoshi) meaning "good luck", 喜 (yoshi) meaning "rejoice", 佳 (yoshi) meaning "beautiful, good" or 孝 (yoshi) meaning "filial piety" combined with 文 (fumi) meaning "writing". Other kanji combinations are possible as well.

column3: 義治, 良治, 善治, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|よしはる(Japanese Hiragana)|ヨシハル(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 義 (yoshi) meaning "justice, righteousness", 良 (yoshi) meaning "good, virtuous, respectable" or 善 (yoshi) meaning "good, virtuous" combined with 治 (haru) meaning "govern, administer". This name can be formed from other combinations of kanji as well.

column3: 与志偉, 由栄, 美偉, 良日出, 吉英, 喜英, 芳秀, 祥秀, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 祥 (yoshi) meaning "auspiciousness, good omen, happiness", 美 (yoshi) meaning "beautiful", or 由 (yoshi) meaning "reason, cause" combined with 栄 (hide) meaning "glory, honour, prosperous, flourishing, luxuriant, lush" or 偉 (hide) meaning "admirable". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: よしひこ(Japanese Hiragana)|ヨシヒコ(Japanese Katakana)|賀彦, 栄勉, 允比古, 令彦, 亮勉, 慶比古, 養彦, 葦勉, 縦比古, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 縦 (yoshi) meaning "at will, height, length", 葦 or 芦 (yoshi) meaning "bulrush, common reed, Phragmites australis", 愛 (yoshi) meaning "love, affection", 因 (yoshi) meaning "factor, reason, cause", 資 (yoshi) meaning "capital, funds, resources, materials, property", or 惟 (yoshi) meaning "think, reflect, consider, however, but" combined with 彦 (hiko) meaning "boy, prince". Other kanji combinations are also possible.
From Japanese 吉 (yoshi) meaning "good luck" combined with 姫 (hime) meaning "princess". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: よし ひら(Japanese Hiragana)|ヨシ ヒラ(Japanese Katakana)|芳平, 好衡, 義平, 美衡, 由平, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 能 (yoshi) meaning "ability, talent, skill", 悦 (yoshi) meaning "joy, pleased", 禎 (yoshi) meaning "lucky, auspicious, good omen", 慶 (yoshi) meaning "jubilation", 善 (yoshi) meaning "virtue, goodness", or 嘉 (yoshi) meaning "auspicious" combined with 平 (hira) meaning "peace, flat, even". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 義弘, 吉弘, 善弘, 芳弘, 善博, 良博, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|よしひろ(Japanese Hiragana)|ヨシヒロ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 義 (yoshi) meaning "justice, righteousness", 吉 (yoshi) meaning "good luck", 善 (yoshi) meaning "good, virtuous", 芳 (yoshi) meaning "fragrant, virtuous, beautiful" or 良 (yoshi) meaning "good, virtuous, respectable" combined with 弘 (hiro) meaning "enlarge, expand, great" or 博 (hiro) meaning "command, esteem". This name can be formed from other combinations of kanji as well.

column3: よしひさ(Japanese Hiragana)|ヨシヒサ(Japanese Katakana)|可常, 善久, 嘉寿, 貴契, 義恒, 吉弥, 慶尚, 芳彌, 良恆, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 可 (yoshi) meaning "passable, to accept, to permit, can do, able" combined with 常 (hisa) meaning "unchanging, eternal, ordinary". Other kanji combinations are also possible.Famous bearers are Yoshihisa Hirano (1971-), a professional Japanese baseball player.

column3: 能等, 宜人, 薫仁, 欣壱, 淑一, 禎侍, 祥等, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From the Japanese 宜 (yoshi) meaning "good, naturally, best regards" combined with 人 (hito) meaning "person". Other kanji combinations are usable.

column3: 嘉一, 由一, 明市, 芳市, 吉壱, 慶壱, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 佳 (yoshi) meaning "excellent" combined with 一 (ichi) meaning "one". Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.
From Japanese 義 (yoshi) meaning "righteous", 一 (ichi) meaning "one" combined with 郎 (rou) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 喜家, 義家, 能家, 良家, 憙家, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 喜 (yoshi) meaning "rejoice" combined with 家 (ie) meaning "house". Other kanji combinations are possible.A famous bearer is Yoshiie Tachibana, a former Japanese baseball player.

column3: よしじ(Japanese Hiragana)|ヨシジ(Japanese Katakana)|芳児, 佳二, 吉司, 益治, 喜次, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 益 (yoshi) meaning "advantage, benefit, gain, profit" or 義 (yoshi) meaning "righteous" combined with 二 (ji) meaning "two". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 嘉二郎, 佳次郎, 喜次郎, 義治郎, 吉治郎, 慶次郎, 善二郎, 美治郎, 芳二郎, 良治郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 嘉 (yoshi) meaning "praise, auspicious", 二 (ji) meaning "two" combined with 郎 (rou) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: ヨシカ(Japanese Katakana)|よしか(Japanese Hiragana)|芳花, 悦香, 良加, 美佳, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 悦 (yoshi) meaning "pleased, joy" and 加 (ka) meaning "increased, add". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 義景, 義影, 吉景, 吉影, 佳景, 佳影, 良景, 良影, 好景, 好影, 美景, 美影(Japanese Kanji)|よしかげ(Japanese Hiragana)|ヨシカゲ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name can combine 義 (gi, yoshi) meaning "morality, righteousness, justice, honour," 吉 (kichi, kitsu, yoshi) meaning "good luck," 佳 (ka, yoshi) meaning "beautiful, excellent, good," 良 (ryou, (-)yo.i, (-)i.i, yoshi) or 好 (kou, i.i, kono.mu, su.ku, yo.i, yoshi), both meaning "good," or 美 (bi, mi, utsuku.shii, yoshi) meaning "beauty" with 景 (kei, kage) or 影 (ei, kage), both meaning "shadow, figure."One bearer of this name was Sengoku Period daimyō Asakura Yoshikage (朝倉 義景) (1533–1573), who ruled a part of Echizen Province (present-day northern Fukui Prefecture). His conflicts with Oda Nobunaga led to the his death and destruction of his clan and its castle, Ichijōdani Castle.This name is rarely given to boys, if given at all.

column3: 義兼, 義懐, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 義 (yoshi) meaning "righteous" combined with 兼 (kane) meaning "concurrently, in addition" or 懐 (kane) meaning "feelings". Other combinations of kanji characters are also possible.Famous bearer of this name is Japanese astronomer Yoshikane Mizuno.

From Japanese 能 (yoshi) meaning "ability, talent, skill" combined with 活 (katsu) meaning "life". Other kanji combinations are possible.Famous bearers of this name is Japanese footballer Yoshikatsu Kawaguchi (Yoshi Kawaguchi), Japanese actor and voice actor Yoshikatsu Fujiki and Japanese politician Yoshikatsu Nakayama.

column3: 義和, 義一, 良和, 良一, 善和, 善一, 芳和, 芳一, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|よしかず(Japanese Hiragana)|ヨシカズ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 義 (yoshi) meaning "justice, righteousness", 良 (yoshi) meaning "good, virtuous, respectable", 善 (yoshi) meaning "good, virtuous", 芳 (yoshi) meaning "fragrant, virtuous, beautiful" combined with 和 (kazu) meaning "harmony, peace" or 一 (kazu) meaning "one". This name can be formed from other combinations of kanji as well.

column3: 義樹, 芳生, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 佳 (yoshi) meaning "good" and 貴 (ki) meaning "value, valuable". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 義君, 芳公, 好君, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 義 (yoshi) meaning "righteous" and 君 (kimi) meaning "lord, noble". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 佳潔, 能清, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 恭 (yoshi) meaning "respectful" and 潔 (kiyo) meaning "pure". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 吉邦, 啓公仁, 嘉芳, 佳好, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 啓 (yoshi) meaning "to say, to open, to disclose" and 邦 (kuni) meaning "home country (Japan)". Other kanji combinations are possible.

From Japanese 吉 (yoshi) meaning "good luck", 義 (yoshi) meaning "righteous", or 良 (yoshi) meaning "good, virtuous, respectable", combined with 真 (ma) meaning “real, genuine, true”, 麻 (ma) meaning “flax”, 満 (ma) meaning “full”, 馬 (ma) meaning “horse”, and 間 (ma) meaning “among, between”. Other kanji combinations are also possible.

column3: 良麿, 芳麿, 嘉麿, 吉丸, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|よしまろ(Japanese Hiragana)|ヨシマロ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 良 (yoshi) meaning "good, virtuous, respectable", 芳 (yoshi) meaning "fragrant, virtuous, beautiful", 嘉 (yoshi) meaning "excellent, good, auspicious" or 吉 (yoshi) meaning "good luck" combined with the affectionate suffix 麿 (maro) or 丸 (maro) meaning "circle, round, whole". Other kanji combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 悦将, 喜政, 喜昌, 悦正, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 悦 (yoshi) meaning "ecstasy" combined with 将 (masa) meaning "commander, leader, general". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 義松, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|よしまつ(Japanese Hiragana)|ヨシマツ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From 義 (yoshi) meaning "righteous" combined with 松 (matsu) meaning "pine tree, fir tree". Other kanji combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 義通, 良通, 祥倫, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 義 (yoshi) meaning "righteousness, morality, justice" and 通 (michi) meaning "way, road, path". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 吉宗, 義宗, 良宗, 慶宗, 芳宗, 美宗(Japanese Kanji)|よしむね(Japanese Hiragana)|ヨシムネ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name can be used to combine 吉 (kichi, kitsu, yoshi) meaning "good luck," 義 (gi, yoshi) meaning "morality, righteousness, justice, honour," 良 (ryou, (-)yo.i, (-)i.i, yoshi) meaning "good," 慶 (kei, yoroko.bu, yoshi) meaning "joy, delight, rejoicing, congratulation," 芳 (hou, kanba.shii, yoshi) meaning "perfume, fragrance" or 美 (bi, mi, utsuku.shii, yoshi) meaning "beauty" with 宗 (shuu, sou, mune) meaning "principle, aim."One noted bearer of this name was shōgun Tokugawa Yoshimune (徳川 吉宗) (1684-1751), considered among the best of the Tokugawa shōguns.

column3: 善奈, 喜奈, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 善 (yoshi) meaning "good, virtuous, charitable, kind" combined with 奈 (na) meaning "apple tree". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 善心, 義央, 義仲, 由仲, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 善 (yoshi) meaning "good, virtuous, charitable, kind", 義 (yoshi) meaning "righteous" or 由 (yoshi) meaning "cause, reason" combined with 心 (naka) meaning "heart, mind, soul", 央 (naka) meaning "centre, middle" or 仲 (naka) meaning "relationship, terms". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: ヨシナオ(Japanese Katakana)|よしなお(Japanese Hiragana)|嘉直, 義直, 孝尚⁠, 敬尚, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 敬 (yoshi) meaning "respect, honor, reverence" or 孝 (yoshi) meaning "filial piety" combined with 尚 (nao) meaning "still, as always, in addition". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 義也, 吉成, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 吉 (yoshi) meaning "lucky, good" and 成 (nari) meaning "completed".

column3: 吉音, 義音, 吉子, 義子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: This name could be made of 吉 (yoshi) meaning "fortune, good luck", 義 (yoshi) meaning "righteous", or 芳 (yoshi) meaning "fragrance" combined with 根 (kon, ne, -ne) meaning "head (pimple), radical, root," 音 (in, on, -non, oto, ne) meaning "sound, noise," 子 (shi, su, tsu, ko, -ko, ne) meaning "child, sign of the rat (1st sign of the Chinese zodiac)" and 眠 (min, nemu.i, nemu.ru, ne) meaning "die, sleep(y)".If spelled with 子 at the end, it could be read as Yoshiko.

column3: 吉野, 吉乃, 芳野, 芳乃, 好野, 好乃, 良野, 良乃, 美野, 美乃, 佳野, 佳乃, 嘉野, 嘉乃, 由野, 由乃(Japanese Kanji)|よしの(Japanese Hiragana)|ヨシノ(Japanese Katakana)

column3: 由伸, 栄伸, 佳伸, 吉伸, 圭伸, 義伸, 能信, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 由 (yoshi) meaning "cause, reason", 栄 (yoshi) meaning "glory, honor", 佳 (yoshi) meaning "beautiful, good", 吉 (yoshi) meaning "good luck", 圭 (yoshi) meaning "jade pointed at top" or 義 (yoshi) meaning "righteous" combined with 伸 (nobu) meaning "extend, stretch". Other kanji combinations are possible as well.

column3: 義典, 義徳, 義憲, 義紀, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|よしのり(Japanese Hiragana)|ヨシノリ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 義 (yoshi) meaning "justice, righteousness" combined with 典 (nori) meaning "rule, ceremony", 徳 (nori) meaning "virtue", 憲 (nori) meaning "law" or 紀 (nori) meaning "record, chronicle". This name can be formed from other combinations of kanji as well.

column3: 佳乃介, 佳之介, 嘉之輔, 義之介, 慶之助, 芳之介, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 佳 (yoshi) meaning "beautiful, good", 乃 (no), a possessive particle, combined with 介 (suke) meaning "shell, shellfish". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 能臣, 悦臣, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 能 (yoshi) meaning "ability, talent, skill", 悦 (yoshi) meaning "joy, pleased", 禎 (yoshi) meaning "lucky, auspicious, good omen", 慶 (yoshi) meaning "jubilation", 善 (yoshi) meaning "virtue, goodness", or 嘉 (yoshi) meaning "auspicious" combined with 臣 (omi) meaning "one who serves a lord; a vassal, subject". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: よしさだ(Japanese Hiragana)|ヨシサダ(Japanese Katakana)|悦定, 能禎, 嘉貞, 祥質, 善成, 喜定, 慶貞, 美定, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column3: 与志作, 良咲, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 良 (yoshi) meaning "good" combined with 咲 (saku) meaning "blossom, bloom". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 吉繁(Japanese Kanji)|よししげ(Japanese Hiragana)|ヨシシゲ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 吉 (yoshi) meaning "good luck" and 繁 (shige) meaning "flourishing, luxuriant". Other kanji can be used.

column3: 佳典, 嘉介, 佳亮, 嘉輔, 賀祐, 喜亮, 吉助, 欣祐, 好甫, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column3: よした(Japanese Hiragana)|ヨシタ(Japanese Katakana)|義汰, 喜矯, 因他, 善長, 嘉長, 良発, 賀経, 縦多, 葦妥, 芦太, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|योषिता(Hindi, Marathi)

column3: 義格, 芳忠, 好匡, 良肇, 由美, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 好 (yoshi) meaning "like, fondness" or 由 (yoshi) meaning "cause, reason" combined with 格 (tada) meaning "rank, grade, status" or 肇 (tada) meaning "to start, to begin". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 由多加, 与志隆, 嘉登, 能嵩, 祥任, 欣敬, 薫昂, 慶誠, 禎孝, 仁尚, 淑高, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

Other kanji combinations can be used.
From Japanese 好 meaning "good, fine, best" and 剛 "hard, tough, strong" or 義 meaning "right conduct, morality" and 岳 meaning "mountain peak".

column3: 義太郎, 芳太郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 義 (yoshi) meaning "right conduct, righteousness, justice, morality", 太 (ta) meaning "thick, big" combined with 郎 (rou) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 純光, 純照, 欣映, 能輝, 益輝, 令輝, 佳輝, 惟映, 令映, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 令 (yoshi) meaning "order, decree, command", 純 (yoshi) meaning "pure, innocent", 欣 (yoshi) meaning "joyful, rejoice", 益 (yoshi) meaning "advantage, profit, gain, benefit" or 惟 (yoshi) meaning "think, consider, reflect" and 映 (teru) meaning "shine, reflect, project, glow". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: よしと(Japanese Hiragana)|義人, 吉人, 良人, 善斗, 由人, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column3: 良時, 慶時, 吉時(Japanese Kanji)|よしとき(Japanese Hiragana)

column3: 佳知, 喜知, 嘉知, 慶知, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 佳 (yoshi) meaning "beautiful, good", 喜 (yoshi) meaning "rejoice", 嘉 (yoshi) meaning "auspicious, praise" or 慶 (yoshi) meaning "jubilation" combined with 知 (tomo) meaning "wisdom". Other kanji combinations are possible as well.

column3: 孝年, 敬利, 成智, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 禎次, 令禎, 好嗣, 義二, 吉亞, 美亜, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column3: ヨシヤ(Japanese Katakana)|よしや(Japanese Hiragana)|嘉哉, 佳夜, 栄彌, 善弥, 恵八, 四志耶, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column3: 義安, 吉泰, 吉安, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column3: 吉代, 吉世, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 吉 (yoshi, kichi, kitsu) meaning "joy, good luck, congratulations", combined with 代 (yo) meaning "generation".

column3: よしゆき(Japanese Hiragana)|ヨシユキ(Japanese Katakana)|義幸, 吉幸, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column3: 吉三, 好三, 佳三, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

(よつばと! in Japanese).This name is rarely given to girls, if given at all.

Used as a female name in modern Hebrew, Yotvat is derived of the Hebrew root TOV, meaning good. Yotvat was a walled Jewish town in the north-west Galilee from as early as the 3-4 centuries BC. Later, the Romans, who ruled the land, altered the pronunciation to Yodfat.During the First Jewish-Roman war, Yodfat withstood a 47-day seige in the year 67AD. Following this revolt Yodfat was rebuilt and the town kept its Jewish culture and life.Yotvat is also the Ancient Hebrew name of Tiran island, a Red Sea island within the maritime borders of Saudi Arabia that was administered by Egypt in the recent past.

From the name used in the Eastern Orthodox Church for the festival of Candlemas or Purification (February 2), which commemorates the meeting of the infant Jesus and his mother with Simeon and Anna in the temple. It literally means "meeting" from Late Greek Ὑπαπάντη (Hypapantê), derived from ὑπαπαντάω (hypapantaô) "to meet, encounter". The Meeting of the Lord is one of the twelve Great Feasts in the Eastern Orthodox liturgical calendar.
Variant of Ibe, a Frisian name of uncertain etymology.
Medieval variant of Hippolyta, recorded in 16th-century French-speaking Switzerland.

A name meaning "patience" in Greek. This was the name that Helen Dragaš, the wife of Byzantine Emperor Manuel II Palaiologos, took when she became a nun at the Monastery of Lady Martha. Two of her eight children became emperors: John VIII and Constantine XI, that latter of whom was the legendary final Byzantine emperor. Alternate spellings include Ipomoni and Hypomone. Today, she is venerated as a saint in the Eastern Orthodox Church. Her name is sometimes translated to Patience.
From the name of the town and municipality in Belgium's West Flanders province (see Ieper), the name first used and peaked during the Battles of Ypres in 1914 and 1915.

Borne by a 7th-century Scottish saint who was a disciple of Saint Ternan and a bishop to the Picts.

Gallicized form of Latin Aredius via Occitan Iriès. This was the name of a 6th-century Catholic saint born at Limoges, France, also known as Saint Aredius, who served for a time in the court of the Franks and then founded the monastery of Atane in Limousin. The monastery and also the surrounding village of Saint-Yrieux were named in his honor.
Feminine form of Yrjan and Yrjar as well as a variant of Irja as well as a derivation from Old Norse yrja "drizzling rain".

The name of a giant and father of Olwen in the Mabinogion, a collection of eleven prose stories collated from medieval Welsh manuscripts.The origin of his name is disputed; one theory suggests that it might be derived from Welsh ysbaddu "to castrate", while other scholars suspect a derivation from Welsh ysbyddad "hawthorn".

A warrior in the service of King Arthur who was the son of King Fflergant of Armorica. He is thought by many scholars to be equal to Duke Alan Fyrgan (1084-1112). Alan married William the Conqueror’s daughter.

Of debated origin and meaning, the name seems to have been coined by Paul Claudel for a character in his 1906 play Partage de midi (The Break of Noon in English). The inspiration behind this name is unclear, although it has been speculated that Claudel may have based it on the (originally masculine) name Isée or on Isèu, itself a form of Yseult. Another theory suggests a derivation from the name of the Shinto Ise Shrine in Japan (which Claudel himself renders in one of his later works phonetically as Ysé), while yet another theory proposes a derivation from Ancient Greek ἴσος (ísos) "equal", as both religion and equality are motifs in Partage de midi.
Derived from Cornish ysel "modest". This is a recently coined Cornish name.
Medieval Silesian German variant of Isentrud.

It also appears in the medieval French Roman de Thèbes in which case it is an Old French form of Ismene.

Diminutive of Yitzhak, using the Yiddish diminutive suffix tzik. It was sometimes Anglicized as Izzy.

From Chinese 玉 (yù) meaning “jade” and 帝 (dì) meaning “emperor”. In Daoist mythology, Yudi is the supreme ruler of the cosmos who has authority over heaven, earth and hell. He rules with the help of an extensive divine bureaucracy that is headquartered in the sky but extends its jurisdiction to all parts of the natural world. He is most well-known from his appearance in the classic Chinese novel Journey to the West, where he is forced to deal with the increasingly rebellious Monkey King Sun Wukong. He is also known as Yu-huang (玉皇) and Yu-huang Dadi (玉皇大帝).

This name is most likely a combination of two given names, such as Yudith and Daniel (or an other Hebrew name that ends in -iel). Names like these are often formed from the names of the bearer's parents, since it is fairly common in Middle America and South America for parents to give their children a combination of their own names. The names Elián and Josmar are good examples of this.

Meaning unknown. It may possibly be a variant form of Yadier or is otherwise related to it.I first found the name in a number of articles about a June 2015 plane crash in the Colombian jungle, in which it was the name of one of the survivors. Later on, I also found numerous (adult) bearers of the name on Facebook.

column12: From Chinese 玉 (yù) meaning "jade, precious stone, gem", 钰 (yù) meaning "treasure, solid metal", or 育 (yù) meaning "raise, rear, nourish" combined with 琴 (qín) meaning "zither, lute", 芹 (qín) meaning "celery", or 钦 (qīn) meaning "respect, admire". This name can be formed from other character combinations as well.

column3: 玉清, 玉青, 玉卿, 昱清, 育青, 语晴, 宇清, 雨晴, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 玉 (yù) meaning "jade, precious stone, gem", 昱 (yù) meaning "sunlight, sunshine, brightness", 育 (yù) meaning "rear, nourish, nurture", 语 (yǔ) meaning "language, speech", 宇 (yǔ) meaning "house, eaves, universe" or 雨 (yǔ) meaning "rain" combined with 清 (qīng) meaning "clear, pure, clean", 青 (qīng) meaning "blue, green, young", 卿 (qīng) meaning "minister, noble, officer" or 晴 (qíng) meaning "clear weather". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
From the Chinese 煜 (yù) meaning "bright, shining" or 雨 (yǔ) meaning "rain" and 琼 (qióng) meaning "jade, rare, precious, elegant".

column3: 玉秋, 雨秋, 昱秋(Chinese)
column12: From the Chinese 玉 (yù) meaning "jade", 雨 (yǔ) meaning "rain" or 昱 (yù) meaning "bright light, sunlight" and 秋 (qiū) meaning "autumn".
From Korean Yur meaning cloud or YurMeaning allow consent, as well as other Korean Characters that are pronounced in similar way.

column3: 유라(Korean Hangul)|由路, 維羅, etc.(Korean Hanja)
column12: From Sino-Korean 由 (yu) meaning "cause, reason, from" or 維 (yu) meaning "to tie, fasten, maintain" and 路 (ra) meaning "road, path, journey" or 羅 (ra) meaning "net, silk". Other hanja combinations are also possible.

column3: 妤然, 钰然, 钰燃(Chinese)
column12: From the Chinese 妤 (yú) meaning "beautiful, handsome" or 钰 (yù) meaning "rare treasure" and 然 (rán) meaning "yes, certainly, pledge, promise" or 燃 (rán) meaning "light fire, ignite".

column3: 幽霊(Japanese Kanji)|ゆうれい(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: The name consists of two kanji, 幽 (yū), meaning "faint" or "dim" and 霊 (rei), meaning "soul" or "spirit".

column3: 玉仁, 育仁, 毓仁, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 玉 (yù) meaning "jade, precious stone, gem", 育 (yù) meaning "raise, bring up, rear" or 毓 (yù) meaning "foster, nurture" combined with 仁 (rén) meaning "compassionate". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

From Sino-Korean 琉璃 meaning "glass", or from 俞 (yu) "consent, approve" or 宥 (yu) "forgive, pardon, indulge" combined with 利 (ri) "gains, advantage, profit, merit". Other hanja combinations are possible.

column3: ユリア(Japanese Katakana)|優里亜, 百合愛, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 優 (yuu) meaning "gentleness, lithe, superior", 里 (ri) meaning "village" and 亜 (a) meaning "second, Asia" or 百合 (yuri) meaning "lily" and 愛 (a) meaning "love". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 百合芽, 由利女, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column3: ゆりみ(Japanese Hiragana)|ユリミ(Japanese Katakana)|由利実, 百合実, 百合美, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 由 (yu) meaning "cause, reason", 利 (ri) meaning "benefit; advantage" combined with 実 (mi) meaning "reality, truth, fruit". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 友琳, 結鈴, 柚凛, 由琳, 湯鈴, 優凛, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column3: ゆりな(Japanese Hiragana)|ゆり奈(Kanji/Hiragana)|結梨菜, 結利那, 結梨渚, 結璃奈, 結李奈, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 結 (yu) meaning "tie, fasten, join, organize", 梨 (ri) meaning "pear" combined with 菜 (na) meaning "vegetable, greens". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: ゆり音(Kanji/Hiragana)|結鈴音, 百合子, 祐梨音, 揺音, 尭音, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 結 (yu) meaning "tie, fasten, join, organize", 鈴 (ri) meaning "bell, chime" combined with 音 (ne) meaning "sound". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: ユリノ(Japanese Katakana)|ゆりの(Japanese Hiragana)|ゆり乃(Kanji/Hiragana)|結莉乃, 由梨乃, 佑里乃, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 結 (yu) meaning "tie, bind", 莉 (ri) meaning "jasmine", and 乃 (no) a possessive particle. Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 百合之介, 百合之助, 百合之輔(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 百合 (yuri) meaning "lily", 之 (no) meaning "of, this", and 介 (suke) meaning "help, mediate, aid, rescue". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: ゆりお(Japanese Hiragana)|ユリオ(Japanese Katakana)|百合男, 百合夫, 百合郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 百合 (yuri) meaning "lily" combined with 男 (o) meaning "male". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: ユリリ(Japanese Katakana)|優理々, 悠理々, 優李梨, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 優 (yu) meaning "gentleness, lithe, superior", 李 (ri) meaning "plum" and 梨 (ri) meaning "pear". Other kanji combinations are possible.

From Thai ยุทธ (yuttha) meaning "war, battle" and ชัย (chai) meaning "victory".
From Thai ยุทธ (yuttha) meaning "war, battle, conflict" and จักร (chak) meaning "wheel, circle, chakra".

column3: ยุทธศักดิ์(Thai)
column12: From Thai ยุทธ (yuttha) meaning "war, battle" and ศักดิ์ (sak) meaning "power".

column3: ยุทธศาสตร์(Thai)
杏優杏, 結愛, 結空, 優亜, 優綾, 優羽愛, 優明, 優有, 友愛, 悠亜, 有杏, 由阿, 由愛, 祐愛, 裕亜, 夕愛, 侑愛, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 杏 (yu) meaning "apricot", 結 (yuu) meaning "tie, bind, contract, join, organize, do up hair, fasten", 優 (yuu, yu) meaning "tenderness, excel, surpass, actor, superiority, gentleness", 友 (yuu) meaning "friend", 悠 (yuu) meaning "permanence, distant, long time, leisure", 有 (yuu) meaning "exist", 由 (yuu) meaning "wherefore, a reason", 祐 (yuu) meaning "help", 裕 (yuu) meaning "abundant, rich", 夕 (yuu) meaning "evening" or 侑 (yuu) meaning "urge to eat", 優 (u) meaning "tenderness, excel, surpass, actor, superiority, gentleness" or 羽 (u) meaning "feathers" combined with 杏 (a) meaning "apricot", 愛 (a) meaning "love, affection", 空 (a) meaning "sky", 亜 (a) meaning "second, Asia", 綾 (a) meaning "design, figured cloth, twill", 明 (a) meaning "bright, light", 有 (a) meaning "exist" or 阿 (a) meaning "flatter, fawn upon, corner, nook, recess". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 優吾, 勇吾, 裕吾, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 優 (yuu) meaning "excellence, superiority, gentleness", 勇 (yuu) meaning "brave" or 裕 (yuu) meaning "abundant" combined with 吾 (go) meaning "I (pronoun), me". Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.

column3: 優羽, 有羽, 優波, 湧波, 夕波, 侑葉, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 優 (yuu) meaning "excellence, gentleness" combined with 羽 (ha) meaning "plumes, feathers". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: ゆうひ(Japanese Hiragana)|夕飛, 雄飛, 夕日, 優陽, 優羽妃, 百愛灯, 結灯, 悠日, 由有陽, 夕姫, 侑陽, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 夕日 (yuuhi) meaning "evening, setting sun" or from 優 (yuu) meaning "kindness, gentleness, lithe, superior" combined with 陽 (hi) meaning "light, sun, male". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 勇星, 勇歩, 有帆, 有歩, 由帆, 由歩, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 勇 (yuu) meaning "brave", 有 (yuu) meaning "exist" or 由 (yuu) meaning "cause, reason" combined with 星 (ho) meaning "star", 歩 (ho) meaning "walk" or 帆 (ho) meaning "sail". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 祐一, 裕一, 雄一, 悠一, 友一, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|ゆういち(Japanese Hiragana)|ユウイチ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Alternate transcription of Japanese Kanji 祐一 or 裕一 or 雄一 or 悠一 or 友一 (see Yūichi).

column3: 優一郎, 雄一郎, 裕一郎, 祐一郎(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 優 (yuu) meaning "gentleness, lithe, superior", 一 (ichi) meaning "one" combined with 郎 (rou) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations are possible as well.Famous bearers are Yuichiro Ando, Japanese-American painter and Yuichiro Miura, Japanese mountain climber.

column3: 雄司郎, 雄二郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
ゆうかた(Japanese Hiragana)|夕方, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 夕方 (yuukata) meaning "early evening". Other kanji combinations are usable.

column3: 勇健, 有健, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 勇 (yuu) meaning "brave" or 有 (yuu) meaning "exist" combined with 健 (ken) meaning "healthy, strong". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 勇吉, 佑吉, 優吉, 友吉, 悠吉, 有吉, 裕佶, 遊吉, 融吉, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 勇 (yuu) meaning "brave" combined with 吉 (kichi) meaning "good luck". Other kanji combinations are possible.A famous deceased bearer is Yukichi Chuganji, a Japanese supercentenarian and "... was recognised by Guinness World Records as the oldest man... " in Japan until his death at age 114 years 189 days and a living bearer is Yukichi Amano, a Japanese columnist, founder and chief editor of monthly magazine Kokoku Hihyo.

From Japanese 侑 (yuu) meaning "help, assist, repay kindness" combined with 広 (kou) meaning "vast, wide". Other kanji combinations are possible.Famous bearer of this name is Nippon Professional Baseball outfielder Yuukou Minamimura.

column3: 勇久, 悠久, 祐久, 雄久, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 勇 (yuu) meaning "brave", 悠 (yuu) meaning "permanence", 祐 (yuu) meaning "divine intervention, protection" or 雄 (yuu) meaning "hero, manly" combined with 久 (kyuu) meaning "long time". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 弓, 由美, 友美, 夕美, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column12: The Okinawan name for ‘sea hibiscus’. Also known as the Ryukyuan form of Yuna and Yūna.

column3: ゆうの(Japanese Hiragana)|ユウノ(Japanese Katakana)|由乃, 柚乃, 有乃, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 柚 (yuu) meaning "citron", 由 (yuu) meaning "cause, reason" or 有 (yuu) meaning "exist" combined with 乃 (no), a possessive particle. Other combinations of kanji characters can also form this name.

column3: ゆうら(Japanese Hiragana)|夕空, 優空, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 夕 (yuu) meaning "evening" or 優 (yuu) meaning "gentleness, lithe, superior" combined with 空 (ra) meaning "sky". Other kanji combinations are also possible.

column3: 尤郎, 佑郎, 勇郎, 祐郎, 雄郎, 雄朗, 雄老, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 尤 (yuu) meaning "especially, particularly", 佑 (yuu) meaning "assist, help, protect", 勇 (yuu) meaning "brave", 祐 (yuu) meaning "divine intervention, protection" or 雄 (yuu) meaning "hero, manly" combined with 郎 (rou) meaning "son", 朗 (rou) meaning "bright, clear" or 老 (rou) meaning "old age, an elderly person, the aged, the elderly". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 勇亮, 友綾, 裕亮, 雄亮, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 勇 (yuu) meaning "brave", 友 (yuu) meaning "friend", 裕 (yuu) meaning "abundant, rich, plentiful" or 雄 (yuu) meaning "hero, manly" combined with 亮 (ryou) meaning "clear" or 綾 (ryou) meaning "thin type of silk fabric resembling satin, damask silk". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: ゆうせい(Japanese Hiragana)|ユウセイ(Japanese Katakana)|侑征, 邑惺, 優生, 夕誠, 友声, 悠世, 雄成, 祐政, 裕勢, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 湧 (yuu) meaning "to spring up from below" combined with 星 (sei) meaning "star, dot". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 勇七, 勇志智, 友七, 祐七, 雄七, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 勇 (yuu) meaning "brave" combined with 七 (shichi) meaning "seven". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 勇七郎, 祐七郎, 雄七郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 勇 (yuu) meaning "courage", 七 (shichi) meaning "seven" combined with 郎 (rou) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations can be possible.

column3: 勇心, 優心, 優真, 友伸, 宥信, 有真, 祐伸, 雄進, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 勇 (yuu) meaning "brave" combined with 心 (shin) meaning "heart, mind, soul". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 勇四郎, 祐四郎, 郁四郎, 優四郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 勇 (yuu) meaning "brave", 祐 (yuu) meaning "divine intervention, protection", 郁 (yuu) meaning "fragrance, perfume" or 優 (yuu) meaning "gentleness, lithe, superior", 四 (shi) meaning "four" combined with 郎 (rou) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 祐俊, 有, 宥俊, 祐舜, 雄舜, 又春, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 祐 (yuu) meaning "to protect" combined with 俊 (shun) meaning "excellence". Other combinations of kanji are possible.
From Japanese 勇 (yuu) meaning "brave" combined with 諦 (tai) meaning "truth, clarity, abandon, give up". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Japanese 祐 (yuu) meaning "divine intervention, protection", 太 (ta) meaning "thick, big" combined with 郎 (rou) meaning "son". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 優也, 雄也, 勇也, 祐也, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|ゆうや(Japanese Hiragana)|ユウヤ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: Alternate transcription of Japanese Kanji 優也 or 雄也 or 勇也 or 祐也 (see Yūya).

column3: ゆうゆ(Japanese Hiragana)|結佑, 結有由, 優結, 優唯, 優有, 悠優, 夕夢, 侑由, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 結 (yuu) meaning "tie, fasten, join, organize" combined with 佑 (yu) meaning "to assist; to help; to protect". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 有山, 遊山, 雄山, 友山, 勇山, 熊山, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 有 (yuu) meaning "exist" combined with 山 (zan) meaning "mountain". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Derived from Sanskrit yuvā (युवा) meaning "youth, young."
Alternate transcription of Thai ยุวดี (see Yuwadi).
Diminutive of Yuval or a combination of the name Yuval and the name Li 2, then the meaning will be "my stream, my brook" in Hebrew.
Means "stream of light", a combination of the names Yuval and Or.
Khanty and Mansi form of Ivan.
From a title meaning "heir apparent, crown prince" from Sanskrit युवन् (yuvan) meaning "young" combined with राज (rāja) meaning "king".
Derived from Sanskrit युवराज्ञी (yuvarajni) meaning "crown princess", making it a feminine form of Yuvraj. Also compare Rajni and Rani.
Derived from Sanskrit युवश (yuvaśa) meaning "young, youthful".
Russian form of Iuvenalis (see Juvenal) via its variant form Iuvenalius.
Elaboration of Vielka with the prefix Yu-, used mainly in Nicaragua.
Derived from the Uzbek yuvosh meaning "gentle" and boy meaning "rich, wealthy".

column3: 宥羽, 結判, 優分, 融, 夕和, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 結 (yu) meaning "tie, fasten, join, organize" combined with 和 (wa) meaning "peace, harmony". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Alternate transcription of Thai ยุวดี (see Yuwadi).
Means "young woman, girl" in Thai, ultimately from Sanskrit युवती (yuvatī).
From 結 (yu) meaning "to bind, to tie", 和 (wa) meaning "peace, harmony", and 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations can be used.
From the Chinese 钰 (yù) meaning "rare treasure" and 湾 (wān) meaning "bay, cove".
From Chinese 余 (yú) meaning "surplus" combined with 望 (wàng) meaning "gaze, hope". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 宇威, 宇卫, 玉伟, 雨微, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 宇 (yǔ) meaning "house, eaves, universe", 玉 (yù) meaning "jade, precious stone, gem" or 雨 (yǔ) meaning "rain" combined with 威 (wēi) meaning "power, pomp", 卫 (wèi) meaning "guard, protect", 伟 (wěi) meaning "great, robust, extraordinary" or 微 (wēi) meaning "small". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
From the Chinese 榆 (yú) meaning "elm tree" and 雯 (wén) meaning "cloud patterns".
From Javanese yuwana meaning "healthy, well, safe, blessed", ultimately from Sanskrit युवन् (yuvan).

column3: 羽霞, 雨霞, 昱霞, 雨夏, 钰夏(Chinese)
column12: From the Chinese 羽 (yǔ) meaning "feather, wing", 雨 (yǔ) meaning "rain", 昱 (yù) meaning "bright light, sunlight, dazzling" or 钰 (yù) meaning "rare treasure" and 霞 (xiá) meaning "rosy clouds" or 夏 (xià) meaning "summer".

column3: 钰仙, 煜仙, 愉娴, 誉娴, 玉仙(Chinese)
column12: From the Chinese 钰 (yù) meaning "rare treasure", 煜 (yù) meaning "bright, shining, brilliant", 愉 (yú) meaning "cheerful, happy", 誉 (yù) meaning "fame, reputation, praise" or 玉 (yù) meaning "jade" and 仙 (xiān) meaning "transcendent, immortal" or 娴 (xián) meaning "elegant, refined".

column3: 玉祥, 玉香, 宇翔, 羽翔, 禹襄, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 玉 (yù) meaning "jade, precious stone, gem", 宇 (yǔ) meaning "house, eaves, universe", 羽 (yǔ) meaning "feather" or 禹 (yǔ) referring to Yu the Great, a legendary Chinese emperor, combined with 祥 (xiáng) meaning "good luck, good omen", 香 (xiāng) meaning "fragrant", 翔 (xiáng) meaning "soar, glide" or 襄 (xiāng) meaning "help, raise, assist". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 昱晓, 玉孝, etc.(Chinese)|昱曉, 玉孝, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 昱 (yù) meaning "bright light, sunlight" or 玉 (yù) meaning "jade, precious stone, gem" combined with 晓 (xiǎo) meaning "dawn, morning" or 孝 (xiào) meaning "filial piety, obedience". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
From the Chinese 妤 (yú) meaning "beautiful, handsome" and 谢 (xiè) meaning "thank".
From the Chinese 玉 (yù) meaning "jade" and 杏 (xìng) meaning "apricot, almond".
From the Chinese 钰 (yù) meaning "rare treasure" and 秀 (xiù) meaning "beautiful, elegant, excellent, luxuriant, refined".

column3: 玉绪, 玉旭, 雨旭, 宇旭, 雨徐, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 玉 (yù) meaning "jade, precious stone, gem", 雨 (yǔ) meaning "rain" or 宇 (yǔ) meaning "house, eaves, universe" combined with 绪 (xù) meaning "thread", 旭 (xù) meaning "dawn, rising sun" or 徐 (xú) meaning "slowly, calmly, composed, dignified". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
From the Chinese 玉 (yù) meaning "jade" or 雨 (yǔ) meaning "rain" and 珣 (xún), the name of a kind of jade or 寻 (xún) meaning "seek, search, look for".

column3: 優也, 雄也, 勇也, 祐也, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|ゆうや(Japanese Hiragana)|ユウヤ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 優 (yū) meaning "excellence, superiority, gentleness", 雄 (yū) meaning "hero, male, manly", 勇 (yū) meaning "brave" or 祐 (yū) meaning "divine intervention, protection" combined with 也 (ya) meaning "to be". Other kanji combinations can form this name as well.
Derived from the Japanese kanji 勇 (yu) meaning "courage" combined with 也 (ya) meaning "to be".Other kanji combinations are also possibile.

column3: 結也子, 友哉子, 友弥子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 結 (yu) meaning "tie, bind, contract, join, organize, do up hair, fasten" or 友 (yu) meaning "friend", 也 (ya) meaning "also", 哉 (ya), an exclamation or 弥 (ya) meaning "all the more, increasingly" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". This name can be formed of different kanji characters as well.

column3: 玉琰, 玉滟, 雨燕, 雨雁, 雨滟, 钰琰, 钰燕, 裕燕(Chinese)
column12: From the Chinese 玉 (yù) meaning "jade" or 雨 (yǔ) meaning "rain" or 钰 (yù) meaning "rare treasure" or 裕 (yù) meaning "abundant; rich; plentiful, fertile" and 琰 (yǎn) meaning "jewel, gem", "glitter of gems", 滟 (yàn) meaning "billowing, overflowing", 燕 (yàn) meaning "swallow (bird)" or 雁 (yàn) meaning "wild goose".Other hanzi combinations are also possibile.

column3: 钰杳, 钰窈, 誉谣, 羽谣, 雨姚(Chinese)
column12: From the Chinese 钰 (yù) meaning "rare treasure", 誉 (yù) meaning "fame, reputation, praise", 羽 (yǔ) meaning "feather, wing" or 雨 (yǔ) meaning "rain" and 杳 (yǎo) meaning "obscure, dark, mysterious", 窈 (yǎo) meaning "obscure, secluded", 谣 (yáo) meaning "folksong, ballad" or 姚 (yáo) meaning "handsome, elegant".

column3: 玉叶, 玉烨, 玉夜, 玉业, 煜叶, 煜烨, 煜夜, 煜业, 芋叶, 芋烨, 芋夜, 芋业, 萸叶, 萸烨, 萸夜, 萸业, 雨叶, 雨烨, 雨夜, 雨业, 羽叶, 羽烨, 羽夜, 羽业, 宇叶, 宇烨, 宇夜, 宇业, etc.(Chinese)|玉葉, 玉燁, 玉夜, 玉業, 煜葉, 煜燁, 煜夜, 煜業, 芋葉, 芋燁, 芋夜, 芋業, 萸葉, 萸燁, 萸夜, 萸業, 雨葉, 雨燁, 雨夜, 雨業, 羽葉, 羽燁, 羽夜, 羽業, 宇葉, 宇燁, 宇夜, 宇業, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 玉 (yù) meaning "jade, precious stone, gem", 煜 (yù) meaning "brilliant, glorious", 芋 (yù) meaning "taro, tuber", 萸 (yú) meaning "dogwood, cornelian cherry", 雨 (yǔ) meaning "rain", 羽 (yǔ) meaning "feather", or 宇 (yǔ) meaning "house, eaves, universe" combined with 叶 or 葉 (yè) both meaning "leaf", 烨 or 燁 (yè) both meaning "glorious, bright, splendid", 夜 (yè) meaning "night", or 业 or 業 (yè) both meaning "business, trade, merits, achievements". Other characters combinations are also possible.

column3: 玉懿, 玉意, 钰漪, 钰宜, 雨漪(Chinese)
column12: From the Chinese 玉 (yù) meaning "jade", 雨 (yǔ) meaning "rain" or 钰 (yù) meaning "rare treasure" and 懿 (yì) meaning "virtuous, admirable", 意 (yì) meaning "thought, idea", 漪 (yī) meaning "ripples, swirling", or 宜 (yí) meaning "appropriate, fitting, suitable".
From the Chinese 钰 (yù) meaning "rare treasure" and 银 (yín) meaning "silver" or "money, wealth" or 殷 (yīn) meaning "many, great, abundant, flourishing".

column3: 結々, 優々, 友々, 柚々, 由々, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 結 (yu) meaning "tie, fasten, join, organize", 優 (yu) meaning "gentleness, lithe, superior", 友 (yu) meaning "friend", 柚 (yu) meaning "grapefruit, pomelo, citrus fruit" or 由 (yu) meaning "cause, reason" combined with 々, a phonetic character indicting a duplication of the beginning kanji. Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 钰源, 钰瑗, 玉园, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From the Chinese 钰 (yù) meaning "rare treasure" or 玉 (yù) meaning "jade" and 瑗 (yuàn) meaning "jade ring" or 园 (yuán) meaning "garden, park, orchard".

From the Chinese 玉 (yù) meaning "jade" or 钰 (yù) meaning "rare treasure" and 玥 (yuè) meaning "mythological magical pearl, mysterious gem", 悦 (yuè) meaning "pleased, contented" or 越 (yuè) meaning "go beyond, exceed".

column3: ユユカ(Japanese Katakana)|ゆゆか(Japanese Hiragana)|結々花, 柚々香, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 結 (yu) meaning "tie, fasten, join, organize" or 柚 (yu) meaning "grapefruit, pomelo, citrus fruit" duplicated and combined with 花 (ka) meaning "flower" or 香 (ka) meaning "fragrance". Other kanji combinations can form this name.

column3: ゆゆき(Japanese Hiragana)|ユユキ(Japanese Katakana)|優雪, 由幸, 遊々喜, 友々紀, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 優 (yu) meaning "gentleness, lithe, superior" or 遊 (yu) meaning "to play" with 喜 (ki) meaning "joy", 紀 (ki) meaning "chronicle" or 貴 (ki) meaning "valuable" and then combined with 々, a phonetic character indicting a duplication of the beginning kanji. Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: ユユコ(Japanese Katakana)|ゆゆこ(Japanese Hiragana)|ゆゆ子(Kanji/Hiragana)|結由子, 由友子, 祐々子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 結 (yu) meaning "tie, fasten, join, organize", 優 (yu) meaning "gentleness, lithe, superior" or 由 (yu) meaning "cause, reason" duplicated using 々, and then combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.Famous bearer is Yuyuko Takemiya (1978-), who is a Japanese writer of light novels.

column3: 钰韫, 钰云, 雨芸(Chinese)
column12: From the Chinese 钰 (yù) meaning "rare treasure" or 雨 (yǔ) meaning "rain" and 芸 (yún) meaning "rue" or "art, ability, talent, craft", 韫 (yùn) meaning "hide, conceal" or 云 (yún) meaning "clouds".

Means "wanting to fight, eager for battle" in Sanskrit, the desiderative form of युध् (yudh) meaning "war, battle, fight". In the Hindu epic the Mahabharata Yuyutsu is a Kaurava prince, the son of Dhritarashtra and a concubine woman. During the Kurukshetra War he defects to the side of the Pandavas.

column3: 雄三郎, 友三郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)

column12: From Chinese 玉瓒 (yùzàn) meaning "ceremonial ladle made of jade". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From the name of a type of shrub or small tree that bears fragrant white or cream-coloured flowers (scientific name Murraya paniculata).
Yuz(柚)meaning yuzu shortened for adding ari. Ari(有)meaning exist.
From Chinese 毓 (yù) meaning "to bring up" and 嶂 (zhàng) meaning "mountain range" or 玉 (yù) meaning "jade, precious stone, gem" and 章 (zhāng) meaning "chapter".
From Chinese 宇 (yǔ) meaning "the universe" combined with 哲 (zhé) meaning "philosophy". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From the Chinese 雨 (yǔ) meaning "rain" and 筝 (zhēng) meaning "zheng zither", "kite".
From the Chinese 玉 (yù) meaning "jade" and 枝 (zhī) meaning "branches" or 雨 (yǔ) meaning "rain" and 智 (zhì) meaning "wisdom, knowledge, intelligence".

column3: 玉珠, 愉竹, 裕竹, 雨竹, 愉珠, 裕珠, 雨珠, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From 愉 (yú) meaning "happy, pleasent, delightful" or 裕 (yù) meaning "abundant, rich, plentiful" or 雨 (yǔ) meaning "rain" combined with 竹 (zhú) meaning "bamboo" or 珠 (zhū) meaning "pearl". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Derived from the Dena'ina Athabaskan root Yuq'. Means "Clear sky".

column3: 祐二, 雄二, 右二, 有二, 優司, 裕治, 勇治, 雄次, 祐志, 裕士, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|ゆうじ(Japanese Hiragana)|ユウジ(Japanese Katakana)

column12: Derived from the Uzbek yuz meaning "hundred" and jon meaning "spirit, soul".

column3: 雄三, 雄蔵, 有三, 有造, 祐三, 祐造, 裕三, 勇蔵, 優蔵(Japanese Kanji)

column12: Derived from the Uzbek yuz meaning "hundred" and toy meaning "colt".

column3: 柚, 柚子, 柚寿, 柚朱, 由子, 由寿, 由珠, 有珠, 優珠, 優寿, 友珠(Japanese Kanji)|ゆず(Japanese Hiragana)|ユズ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: This name can be used as 柚 or 柚子 with 柚 (jiku, yu, yuu, yuzu) meaning "citron" and 子 (shi, su, tsu, ko, ne) meaning "child, sign of the rat (1st sign of Chinese zodiac)."This name can also be used as 柚寿, 柚朱, 由子, 由寿, 由珠, 有珠, 優珠, 優寿 or 友珠 with 寿 (shuu, ju, su, kotobuki, kotobo.ku) meaning "congratulations, longevity, one's natural life", 朱 (shu, ake, su) meaning "bloody, cinnabar, red, scarlet, vermillion", 由 (yu, yui, yuu, yoshi, yo.ru) meaning "a reason, wherefore", 珠 (shu, tama, su) meaning "gem, jewel, pearl", 有 (u, yuu, a.ru, yu) meaning "exist, happen, have, occur, possess", 優 (u, yuu, sugu.reru, masa.ru, yasa.shii, yu) meaning "actor, excel, gentleness, superiority, surpass, tenderness" and 友 (yuu, tomo, yu) meaning "friend."Yuzu (柚 & 柚子), as a word, is the name of a type of citrus fruit.
From Japanese 柚 (yuzu) meaning "grapefruit, pomelo, citrus fruit" combined with 江 (e) meaning "creek, bay". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: ユズハ(Japanese Katakana)|柚葉, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 柚 (yuzu) meaning "citrus, citron" and 葉 (ha) meaning "leaf". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 柚帆, 柚穂, 柚歩, etc.(Japanese Kanji)|ゆずほ(Japanese Hiragana)|ユズホ(Japanese Katakana)
column12: From Japanese 柚 (yuzu) meaning "grapefruit, pomelo, citrus fruit" combined with 帆 (ho) meaning "sail", 穂 (ho) meaning "grain" or 歩 (ho) meaning "walk, step". Other combinations of kanji can form this name as well.

column3: 柚伽, 柚佳, 柚夏, 柚歌, 柚花, 柚華, 柚圭, 柚香(Japanese Kanji)|ゆずか(Japanese Hiragana)
column12: From Japanese 柚 (yuzu) meaning "grapefruit, pomelo, citrus fruit" combined with 伽 (ka) meaning "nursing or taking care of a person", 佳 (ka) meaning "beautiful, good", 夏 (ka) meaning "summer", 歌 (ka) meaning "song, poetry", 花 (ka) or 華 (ka) which both mean "flower", 圭 (ka) meaning "jade pointed at top" or 香 (ka) meaning "fragrance".Other kanji combinations are also possible.

column3: 優月子, 柚子, 柚木, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 優 (yu) meaning "gentleness, lithe, superior", 月 (zu) meaning "moon" or 柚 (yuzu) meaning "grapefruit, pomelo, citrus fruit" combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child" or 木 (ko) meaning "tree". Other kanji combinations are possible.
From Japanese 雄 (yu) meaning "hero, manly", 図 (zu) meaning "map, drawing, plan, extraordinary, audacious" combined with 馬 (ma) meaning "horse". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: ゆずみ(Japanese Hiragana)|ユズミ(Japanese Katakana)|柚美, 柚実, 友寿美, 柚心, 由寿美, 夕純, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 柚 (yuzu) meaning "grapefruit, pomelo, citrus fruit" combined with 美 (mi) meaning "beautiful" or 実 (mi) meaning "fruit". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: ゆずな(Japanese Hiragana)|柚奈, 柚子奈, 柚菜, 優津奈, 由寿奈, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 柚 (yuzu) meaning "grapefruit, pomelo, citrus fruit" combined with 奈 (na) meaning "apple tree". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 柚音, 柚子音, 柚寧, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 柚 (yuzu) meaning "grapefruit, pomelo, citrus fruit" combined with 音 (ne) meaning "sound". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: ゆずの(Japanese Hiragana)|柚乃, 由子乃, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 柚 (yuzu) meaning "citron" combined with 乃 (no), a possessive particle. Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: 譲子, 柚里子, 柚李子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 譲 (yuzuri) meaning "allow, permit, concede, yield" and 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 柚人, 柚斗, 柚翔, 柚都, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 柚 (yuzu) meaning "grapefruit, pomelo, citrus fruit" combined with 人 (to) meaning "person", 斗 (to), which refers to a Chinese constellation, 翔 (to) meaning "soar, fly" or 都 (to) meaning "metropolis, capital, all, everything". Other kanji combinations are possible.

column3: ゆずゆ(Japanese Hiragana)|ゆず柚(Kanji/Hiragana)|柚結, 柚子憂, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 柚 (yuzu) meaning "citrus" and 憂 (yu) meaning "excellence, superiority, gentleness". Other kanji combinations are possible.As a word, 柚子湯 (yuzuyu) refers to a yuzu bath, a bathing tradition for the winter solstice in Japan.

It is most probable that it is the feminine form of the name Yvain. Though, it is commonly thought of as a combination of Yvonne and Elaine.The name is most popularly recognized as the name of the fallen star in Neil Gaiman's novella 'Stardust'.

Variant spelling of Ivanka. In some cases, the name might be a combination of Yvonne or Yvette with Bianca, as these names used to be very popular in the Netherlands (the former primarily in the 1960s and the latter two chiefly in the 1970s).
Variant of Evangeline, possibly influenced by Yvette.
French diminutive of Yves and Judeo-Anglo-Norman diminutive of Yvo.
Transferred use of the surname Yvenson. A famous bearer of this name is Yvenson Bernard (1984-) a former professional Canadian football running back.
Ivetka, it is endearment of the name Yvette
Gallicized form of Breton Yvig, a diminutive of Yves.
Diminutive of Yvonne and Yvette, and sometimes used as a variant of Evie.
Possibly a contraction of Yvette and Rose.

Possibly means either "Ireland" or "the Atlantic Ocean" (which lies in the direction of Ireland from Wales), both meanings derived from Proto-Celtic *ɸīweriyū meaning "earth, soil". This was the name of a parent of Brân in Welsh mythology, either being a variant name of Llŷr (which means "the sea") or the name of his wife.

Perhaps from the Old English elements íw "yew tree" (see īwaz) and wig "war". Ywi (or Iwig) was an Anglo-Saxon saint venerated in the English county of Wiltshire in the Middle Ages, where his relics were enshrined (at the county town, Wilton, near Salisbury). According to legends, he was a Benedictine monk of Lindisfarne Abbey in the Kingdom of Northumbria, and was ordained a deacon by Saint Cuthbert. He died a hermit in Brittany.
Character from the Disney movie, "The Emperors New Groove."
Possibly a much-mangled form of Ismeria via its variants Ismérie and Ismaria.
Variant transcription of Arabic زاهرة (see Zaahira).
The meaning of the name Zaaidh is "Abundance" or "Plentiful" or "Growing"
Means "one who increases in growth and goodness" in Arabic.
Form of Zakir used especially in South Africa.
Variant of Zaldastan influenced by the Georgian name Zaal
Form of Zaal with the nominative suffix, used in Georgian when the name is written stand-alone.

Derived from the Hebrew noun זועה (zewa'a) or זעוה (za'awa) meaning "a trembling", from the verb זוע (zua') meaning "to tremble, to quake". In the Old Testament this is the name of a grandson of Seir.
Means "Zababa desired", deriving from the Akkadian element eršu ("(of a thing) demanded , desired").
Means "gift", from the Hebrew verb זָבַד (zavaḏ) "to give". This is the name of seven men in the Old Testament.
Means "flame (as of a candle)" in Persian.
Of unknown meaning. This is the name of the father of Baruch, who "earnesty repaired" part of the Jerusalem wall.
Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the Tribe of Judah, was the father of Carmi and the grandfather of Achan, according to Joshua 7:1. He was present at the Battle of Jericho.
Form of Zabdiel used in the Latin Old Testament.
Variant of Zabdi, which is a masculine name in the Old Testament (belonging to four men) - essentially a contracted form of Zebadiah.
Konkani form of Elizabeth, borrowed from Portuguese Isabel and used by Konkani Catholics.
Walloon form of Isabelle. The name coincides with Walloon zabele "bluethroat (bird)".
Galician short form of Elisabete and Walloon form of Élisabeth.
Means "gazelle" in Arabic, this is also the name of a star.

Old Arabic name, possibly related to the modern Arabic noun زَبِيبَة (zabība) meaning "raisin". This was the name of an 8th-century BC queen of Qedar, an ancient Arab nomadic tribe. She was a vassal of the Assyrian king Tiglath-Pileser III.
Swahili name meaning "grapes" which comes originally from Arabic word zabīb meaning 'raisins', given to five girls in the US in 2023
Alternate transcription of Dhabihullah. A known bearer of this name is the Afghan politician Zabihullah Mojaddidy (b. 1946).

From a blend of the Russian noun собака (sobaka) "dog" and the verb забивать (zabivat') "to strike". This name was used for the 2018 FIFA World Cup official mascot, Zabivaka the Wolf, designed by 22-year-old student designer Ekaterina Bocharova.

Diminutive of Isabelle. French actress and director Zabou Breitman (born Isabelle Breitman, but professionally known as Zabou) brought some attention to the name: while historically it was strictly used as a vernacular diminutive, in recent years it has seen some usage as a given name in its own right.
Possibly a blend of Zabrina and Reannon.
Possibly a combination of Zabrina and Briana.Also compare Zipriana, which has been found spelled as Zibriana in a handful of cases.
Probably an invented name, possibly a variant of Sabriel or a blend of similar names such as Zane 1 and Gabriel.
Variant of Sabrina. A notable bearer of this name is the American actress Zabryna Guevara (b. 1972).
This name is used for a a fictional saber-toothed tiger in Marvel Comics.
Zabud, meaning “endowed.” The son of Nathan, a priest and friend of King Solomon, according to 1 Kings 4:5.
Derived from Nahuatl zacatl "grass, hay, straw".
Probably derived from zacatl "grass, hay" and huehue "elder, old man".
Possibly derived from zacatl "grass, hay, straw" and the suffix -catl.
Variant and feminine form of Zachary.
Zaccur of the house of Reuben was the father of Shammua, a scout sent to Canaan prior to the crossing of the Jordan River according to Numbers 13:4.
Means "God remembers" from Hebrew element זָכַר (zakhar) meaning "to remember" and אֵל ('el) meaning "God".It could be also used as a combination of Zachary and Michael.
A known bearer is Zacharati Chatzi-Babis, who died in 1838. One of her daughters was Manto Mavrogenous, a Greek princess active in the Greek War of Independence.
Greek feminine form of Zacharias. This coincides with the Greek vocabulary word ζαχαρένια (zacharenia) meaning "sugary", from ζάχαρη (zachari) "sugar, sucrose".
The form of Zacharias used in Czech Bible translations.
Derived from Caló zaché "happy; blessed". Used as a Caló equivalent of Felix.
Swedish and medieval English form of Zacchaeus, as well as a German variant of Zachäus.
The Angel of Memory in all three of the main Abrahamic faiths.
Modern spelling of Zakariyya or Zekeriya influenced by some English forms of that name.
Derived from Polish zacny "noble, respectable, upright" combined with Slavic slav "glory".
Feminine form of Zacynthus. This name was very rarely used in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, mainly in Britain.
Variant of Zadok. A famous bearer of the name was Congressman Zadock Pratt (1790-1871), a member of the U.S. House of Representatives from New York.
Most likely derived from Persian یزدان (yazdân) meaning "god, divinity, angel". Zadeni (also transcribed as Zaden) was a pagan god of fruitfulness and the harvest in pre-Christian Georgian mythology.

Derived from the Lithuanian verb žadėti meaning "to promise" combined with old Lithuanian gailas, which usually means "strong, potent" but has also been found to mean "sharp, jagged" as well as "angry, fierce, violent" and "miserable, sorrowful, remorseful". Also compare the modern Lithuanian noun galia meaning "power, might, force".
Variant of Sadie. A known bearer of this name is British author Zadie Smith (1975-), who was born Sadie Smith.

The first element of this name is derived from the Lithuanian verb žadėti meaning "to promise". The second element is either derived from Lithuanian mantus meaning "intelligent" (see Daumantas) or from Lithuanian manta meaning "property, estate" as well as "wealth, riches, fortune".
Derived from the Lithuanian verb žadėti meaning "to promise" combined with the Lithuanian verb minėti meaning "to celebrate" as well as "to remember, to commemorate".
Derived from an old Hungarian word for "violent".
Created from the name Adrian by adding an initial letter Z.
Derived from the Lithuanian verb žadėti meaning "to promise" combined with the old Lithuanian noun vaina meaning "cause, reason" as well as "fault".
Derived from the Lithuanian verb žadėti meaning "to promise" combined with Baltic vil meaning "hope" (see Viltautas).
Derived from the Lithuanian verb žadėti meaning "to promise" combined with Baltic vyd meaning "to see" (see Vytautas). Also compare other names that end in -vydas, such as Alvydas and Tautvydas.
Variant of Zayden. Zadyn was given to 27 boys in 2014 according to the SSA.
Alternate transcription of Arabic زعيم (see Zaim).
Bengali variant of Zayn or alternate spelling of Zain.
Variant of Zaylee. Zaelee was given to 8 girls in 2017 according to the SSA.

Zaelna is a unique feminine name of Angolan origin, symbolizing kindness and humility.It represents a woman who, for forty years, never disrespected her husband — a modelof virtue, strength, and dignity.
A recently created name, formed using the popular phonetic elements zay and lyn, possibly modelled on similar names such as Kaylyn, Braelyn and Shaelyn. Also compare Zaylee and Zayla.

A traditional Japanese masculine name suffix, historically acting as a title for a "palace guard" or "gatekeeper". It became a common, prestigious ending for samurai given names during the Edo period, signaling a historical or, today, quaint tone.Derived from saemon-no-jo, a title for a guard of the left gate of the palace.
German Yiddish diminutive of Sarah, first recorded between the late 1300s and early 1400s.
Means "victory of God" from Arabic ظَفَر (ẓafar) meaning "success, victory" combined with Allah.
Derived from the Uzbek zafar meaning "victory" and xo'ja meaning "master".
From Greek ζαφείρι (zafeíri), derived via Italian from Ancient Greek σάπφειρος (sáppheiros) (see Sapphire) through Latin (compare Zafeiro).
From Greek ζαφείρι (zafeíri), derived via Italian from Ancient Greek σάπφειρος (sáppheiros) (see Sapphire) through Latin (compare Zafeiris).
Feminine form of Zafeiris, using the diminutive suffix -ούλα (-oula).
Masculine form of Zaffira, the name coincides with Italian zaffiro "sapphire".
Means "winner, victor, victorious, triumphant" in Arabic, a derivative of ظفر (ẓafira) meaning "to be successful, to be victorious".
From Greek ζαφείρι ή σαπφειρός meaning "sapphire".
Spanish feminine name derived from the word zafiro meaning "sapphire". This is a modern coinage.
Bengali form of Jafar or Zafar.

Etymology uncertain.It could be the feminine form of an Arabic name that sounds like Zafrin or a variant of Zeferina. The name can also be created by Stephenie Meyer for her book 'Breaking Dawn' (2008) where the character is an Indigenous American woman from Pantanal wetlands, Amazon, South America so there is a possibility that is actually an Indigenous name.

In The Lesser Key of Solomon, this is the name of a Great King and President of Hell, commanding over thirty-three legions of demons. Zagan is depicted as a griffin-winged bull that turns into a man after a while.

An invented name, probably based on the sounds found in names such as Zane, Zayden, Sage and Gage. The name Zage was given to 6 boys born in the United States in 2017 according to the U.S. Social Security Administration.

From Arabic زُغْلُول (zuḡlūl) which is both a noun meaning "a young infant, boy" and an adjective meaning "young and active, quick". In Egyptian Arabic it also means "squab, young dove". In Egypt it is occasionally used as a given name, but is more commonly a surname (see Zaghloul).
Alternate transcription of Arabic زَغْلُول (see Zaghloul).
Russian form of Zaahir 1 or Zaahir 2, used particularly in Bashkortostan and Dagestan.

The name of an American candy bar made with coconut and peanut butter, presumably composed of zag (from the word zig-zag) and nut. This name was used by American physician Hunter 'Patch' Adams (1945-) for his son Atomic Zagnut 'Zag' Adams.
Derived from Serbo-Croatian загорје (zagorye) meaning "up behind the mountains, plains". It may also designate an inhabitant of Hrvatsko Zagorje, an area of Croatia.
Italian and Spanish form of Zagreus.
Catalan and Portuguese form of Zagreus.

An obscure chthonic god sometimes identified with the Orphic Dionysos. Uncertain etymology; possibly derived from Ancient Greek ζάγρη (zagre) meaning "hole in the ground, pit for catching animals", giving the hypothetical word ζαγρεύς (zagreus) "hunter of live animals". The word ζάγρη may have also meant "barefoot". Alternatively, it could derive from ζα (za) meaning "very" or "through" combined with either αγρεύς (agreus) meaning "hunter" or ἀγρός (agros) meaning "field, land", though this is likely folk etymology.

Means "clear; pure" in Hebrew from the root צ־ח־ח‎ (ts-kh-kh). It also means "bright; shine" in Arabic.A famous bearer is Dame Zaha Hadid (1950-2016) an Iraqi–British architect. She was the first woman to receive the Pritzker Architecture Prize, in 2004. She received the UK's most prestigious architectural award, the Stirling Prize, in 2010 and 2011. In 2012, she was made a Dame by Elizabeth II for services to architecture, and in February, 2016, the month preceding her death, she became the first and only woman to be awarded the Royal Gold Medal from the Royal Institute of British Architects.
Means "loathing" in Hebrew. Zaham was the son of Rehoboam and grandson of Solomon.
Possibly derived from Arabic زهر (zahara) meaning "to shine, to bloom" or ظهر (ẓahara) meaning "to be visible, to be clear".
Alternate transcription of Greek Ζαχαρίας (see Zacharias).

Derived from Hebrew זָכַר (zakhar) meaning "to remember" and אֵל ('el) meaning "God". In Judeo-Christian legend, Zachariel or Zakhariel is another name of the angel Zerachiel, one of the primary angels who leads souls to judgement. In the Book of Enoch he is listed as one of the seven archangels. An Angel of Healing, he is also the presiding angel of the sun, prince of ministering angels (those who watch over mortals), and the angel of children, particularly children of parents who have sinned (and are therefore at risk of falling into sin as adults themselves). He is said to have dominion over the earth.Zahariel El'Zurias is a character in Warhammer's Horus Heresy series.
Elaboration or variant of Zahara. Famous bearer is Zaharira Harifai, Israeli actress.
Alternate transcription of Arabic زاهد (see Zahid), as well as the Persian and Bengali form.
Means "sagacious, acute, clever, ingenious" in Urdu, ultimately from Arabic ذهين (dhahīn).
Possibly means "shining" or "brilliant". May also be an alternative spelling of Zahira or a feminine form of Zaheer.

column3: ظہیر الدین(Shahmukhi, Urdu)|ਜ਼ਹੀਰੁੱਦੀਨ(Gurmukhi)|زہیردین(Balochi)|ظهير الدين(Sindhi-Arabic)|ज़हीरुद्दीन(Hindi, Kashmiri Devanagari)|ظَہیٖرُ الدیٖن(Kashmiri Arabic)

column12: Means "he who owns ten thousands of horses". Zahhak was an evil emperor in Persian Mythology who was revolted against by the blacksmith Kaveh.
Alternate transcription of Arabic زاهية (see Zahia), as well as the usual Malay form.
Alternate transcription of Arabic زاهدة (see Zahida), as well as the usual Malay and Indonesian form.
Alternate transcription of Arabic ظهيرة or زاهرة (see Zahira), as well as the Malay form.
Means "helper of the faith" or "defender of the faith", derived from Arabic ظهير (ẓahir) meaning "helper, assistant" combined with الدين (ad-dīn) "the faith, the religion".
Tatar, Turkish, and Uygur form of Zahid.
Transferred use of the surname Zahn.
Derived from Arabic ظهور (zuhur) meaning "rise, emergence, appearance".
Anglicized form of Indo-Persian name derived from Arabic.
Alternate transcription of Arabic زهراء (see Zahra 1).
Means "flower of the religion" from Arabic زهر (zahr) meaning "flowers, blooms, blossoms" combined with دين (dīn) meaning "religion, faith".
Variant of Zahra or a diminutive of Fatimazahrae
From Arabic زَهْر (zahr) meaning "flowers, blossoms" or the related word زَهَرَ (zahara) meaning "to shine".
Alternate transcription of Arabic زهر الدين (see Zahr ad-Din) chiefly used in Algeria.

Etymology unknown. In Mandaeism, a Gnostic religion, Zahreil is the daughter of Qin and mother of the creator of the material universe. She is believed to dwell in the bed of pregnant women, ensuring the safety of infants before and after birth.
Variant of Zahra and feminine variant of Zahr, meaning “blossom” or “beauty” in Arabic
Uzbek form of Zahra or Zahrah.
Alternate transcription of Arabic زهر الدين (see Zahr ad-Din), as well as the Indonesian and Malay form.
Means "laughs frequently", and by extension "happy", in Arabic.
Possibly a variant of Zaya or Izaiah.
Means "beauty" in Pashto and "ornament" in Urdu ultimately from Persian زیب zib.
Derived from the Lithuanian noun žaibas meaning "lightning".

Gallicized form of Zaida. Zaïda was a 12th-century saint who, along with her siblings Saint Ahmed, a Cistercian monk, and Saint Zoraïda, lived in Valencia, Spain. Having converted from Islam to Christianity, all three bore witness to their faith until they were martyred. The emir had Ahmed put to death, nailed to a tree, while the two sisters were beheaded.
Arabic alternate transcription of Zaida as well as the Malay and Indonesian form.
Alternate transcription of Arabic زيدان (see Zaydan).
Variant of Zaiden. Zaidenn was given to 5 boys in 2018 according to the SSA.

Means "my increase", from Arabic زاد (zada) meaning "to increase" (see Zayd). It may also come from the name of 8th-century Muslim leader Zaid bin Ali, whose unsuccessful revolt against the Umayyad Caliphate led to the formation of the Zaidiyyah sect of Shia Islam.
Possibly an invented name combining the phonetic elements zy or zay and ʾel.
Derived from 再 (zài) meaning "again, twice" and 芬 (fēn) meaning "fragrance, aroma, perfume".This transcription could also represent other combinations of hanzi.
This was the name of Zaifeng, Prince Chun (1883-1851), younger brother of Zaitian and father of Puyi.
Derived from Latvian zaigot "to glisten, to glimmer".

Possibly an invented name from another name, but coincides with the Hanyu Pinyin reading of Mandarin 再見 "goodbye, see you later" or 再建 "to rebuild, to reconstruct". A famous bearer of this name is Filipino actor and dancer Zaijian Godsick Lara Jaranilla (2001-).
Japanese masculine name derived from 在 (zai) "be at, consist in", 二 (ji) "two" and #郎 (rou) "son".
From Japanese 在 (zai) meaning "exist, stay" and 賢 (ken) meaning "wise, smart". Other Kanji combinations are possible.
Malay and Indonesian variant of Jilani.
Alternate transcription of زعيم (see Zaim), chiefly used in Northern Africa.
Arabic alternate transcription of Zaima as well as the Malay and Indonesian form.
Alternate transcription of Arabic زينة (see Zayna), as well as a Malay and Indonesian variant.
Alternate transcription of Arabic زينب (see Zaynab).
Malay and Indonesian form of Zainul.
Malay and Indonesian form of Zayn al-Abidin.
Malay and Indonesian variant of Zaynab.
Alternate transcription of Arabic زينب (see Zaynab) chiefly used in Northern Africa (using French-influenced orthography).
Alternate transcription of Arabic زينب (see Zaynab).
Means "my beauty" or "my decoration" from Arabic زين (zayn) meaning "beauty" or "ornament, decoration".
Indonesian and Malay form of Zayn ad-Din.

First part of compound Arabic names beginning with زين ال (Zayn al) meaning "adornment of the" or "beauty of the" (such as زين ال (Zayn al-ʿAbidīn) meaning "adornment of the worshippers" or زين الدين (Zayn ad-Dīn) meaning "beauty of the faith").
Appears in medieval legends of the knight-errant Amadis, perhaps related to Zaïre or a place name mentioned in the Old Testament (2 Kings 8:21), Za'ir meaning "little".
Zaïre means the river that never swallows in Kikongo
Masculine form of Zaira as well as inspired by Zaire.
Diminutive of Zaira, not used as a given name in its own right.
This was the personal name of the Guangxu Emperor (1871-1908), the second-to-last emperor of the Qing Dynasty.
Maghrebi transcription of Zaitun influenced by French orthography.
Alternate transcription of Arabic زيتون (see Zaytun), as well as the usual Malay and Indonesian form. It is sometimes used as a masculine name in Indonesia.
Means "olive" in Swahili, ultimately from Arabic زيتون (zaytūn).
Rhyming variant of Gaius used in the 1968 film 'Planet of the Apes'.
Zaiva is Arabic/Muslim Girl name and meaning of this name is "Strong Mind".
Origin and meaning unknown. Possibly related to the Albanian and Hungarian surname Zaja.
Means "mind, intelligence" in Azerbaijani, ultimately from Arabic ذكاء (ḏakā').
Armenian and Mordvin form of Zakhar (see Zachariah).
Alternate transcription of Arabic زكريا (see Zakariyya).
Alternate transcription of Zakariyya chiefly used in Morocco.

This first name is predominantly found in South America, although it is not very common there: one is much more likely to encounter the name as a surname there instead. Because of that, it is possible that the bearers' parents were inspired to give their sons the surname as a first name, just like it is done in English-speaking countries these days. The surname is derived from the Spanish word zarco meaning "light blue" (ultimately from Andalusian Arabic zárqaʼ, which in turn is derived from Arabic ʼazraq "blue"), which is in reference to the eye colour of the surname's original bearer. However, given the fact that the word zarco is still in use in modern Spanish, it is also possible that in the case of some bearers, their parents deliberately named them after the colour (instead of after the surname). It ultimately doesn't matter either way, as the etymology is the same in both scenarios.

Zariadres was an Orontid ruler of Sophene in the early 2nd century BC. According to Strabo, he was a general of the Seleucid ruler Antiochus III who was made ruler of Sophene, although most scholars believe that he was a member of the Orontid dynasty, which ruled Armenia and Sophene. After the Seleucids were defeated by the Romans in 190 BC, Zariadres and his ally Artaxias I of Greater Armenia (possibly also Zariadres' son) revolted against the Seleucids, became independent kings and expanded their territories.The name is generally believed to derive from Old Iranian roots: "Zarya" is possibly related to the Avestan zara- meaning "gold" or "bright", and "-dres" is possibly from dara- (as in Darius), meaning "to hold" or "to possess".

Lithuanian goddess of the earth, her name deriving from Lithuanian žemė "earth".Žemyna was first documented in the form Źęmîną by Martynas Mažvydas in his Latin introduction to Catechismusa Prasty Szadei (1547). Even though the spelling of her name kept slightly changing, over the centuries many historians, ranging from Mikalojus Daukša, Daniel Klein, Jan Łasicki, Matthäus Prätorius, Philipp Ruhig to Jakob Brodowski, corroborated her existence in the Baltic pantheon and her functions.Modern-day academics agree that Žemyna was a mother goddess personifying the fertile earth and nourishing all life on earth, human, plant, and animal. When Christianity started to gain ground in Lithuania, her cult became influenced by the cult of the Virgin Mary."Prätorius described a ritual, called žemyneliauti, performed at major celebrations (e.g. weddings) or agricultural works (e.g. harvest). The head of the household would drink a cup of beer, but first he would spill some of the drink on the ground and say a short prayer. Then he would kill a rooster or a hen, which would be cooked and eaten by the entire family. Each family member would receive a loaf of bread and say prayers, blessings, and greetings. The bones and other scraps would be sacrificed to the goddess (burned or buried). Other recorded rites included burying bread baked from last crops of prior harvest in a field before new sowing and sacrifice of black piglet. People would also kiss the earth saying a short prayer thanking Žemyna for all her gifts and acknowledging that one day they will return to her."

From the Chinese 增 (zēng) meaning "increase, add to" and 媛 (yuàn) meaning "beauty, beautiful woman".
Diminutive of Zenobia, Zenona and Zenaida.
From Japanese 銭 (zeni) meaning "money", and 婆 (ba) "old woman, grandmother". This is the name of a witch in Hayao Miyazaki's animated film 'Spirited Away' (2001).
Combination of Zé and Nilda or else a variant of Zeneide.

From Middle English senith, from cinit, from Old French cenit and/or Latin cenit, a transliteration of Arabic سمت (samt, "direction, path") which is in itself a weak abbreviation of سمت الرأس (samt ar-ra's, "direction of the head").In modern English, zenith means "the highest point or state; peak" and in astronomy, refers to "the point in the sky vertically above a given position or observer" or "the highest point in the sky reached by a celestial body."In the English-speaking world, this name has been in occasional use from the late 19th century onwards.

Overall, Zenitsu can mean "goodness" or "run fast", but "善ぜん"("zen") and "逸いつ"("itsu") can mean different things individually. "善ぜん"("zen") often has good meanings like "goodness", "right thing" or "improve", while "逸いつ"("itsu") has both good and bad meanings. The good meaning are “run fast” or “have an outstanding talent.” The bad meanings are “lose a chance”, “deviate from the standard” or "let something escape".Zenitsu is the name of one of the main characters in Demon Slayer/Kimetsu no Yaiba.
Hypocoristic form of Zejneb or Zenobia.The name can also be a misspelling of Ženja without the hachek on the first letter.

column3: 泉二, 泉時, 泉司, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 泉 (zen) meaning "natural spring, wellspring" or 善 (zen) meaning "good, virtue" combined with 時 (ji) meaning "time, moment, chance, occasion" or 二 (ji) meaning "two". Other kanji character combinations can be used.

column3: 泉二郎, 善時郎, 泉司郎, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 泉 (zen) meaning "natural spring, wellspring" or 善 (zen) meaning "good, virtue" combined with 時 (ji) meaning "time, moment, chance, occasion" or 二 (ji) meaning "two", and then combined with 郎 (rō) meaning "son".

ゼンキ(Japanese Katakana)|前記, 善希, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 善 (zen) meaning "virtue, good, goodness" and 生 (ki) meaning "living". Other combinations of kanji can form this name as well.

column3: 然吉, 善吉, 禅吉, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 善 (zen) meaning "good" and 吉 (kichi) meaning "fortune, luck." Other kanji combinations can be used.

column3: 善子, 然子, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From Japanese 善 (zen) meaning "good, virtuous, charitable, kind" or 然 (zen), a suffix after nouns to express likeness combined with 子 (ko) meaning "child". Other kanji combinations are possible.
