Diminutive of Zenobia and variant of Zanna, a diminutive of Suzanna, and feminine form of Senne/Senna, diminutives of Sebastian.
Zenni is a Muslim Girl Name. Zenni name meaning is Imagen. It has multiple Islamic meaning.
Name of a Cornish village derived from the local saint, St Senara. In current use.
Serbian and Croatian form of Zenobia.Also used as a German and Dutch transliteration of the Russian name Zenobiya.
Spanish, Portuguese, and Italian masculine form of Zenobia.
Latinized form of Zenobios. Saint Zenobius was a 5th-century bishop of Florence and one of the city's patron saints.
Polish and Kashubian form of Zenobios.
Azerbaijani and Russian form of Zenobia.
Archaic variant of Zenobia, prevalent in Cornwall and Devon as well as in the southern states of the US.
Italian, Spanish and Portuguese form of Zenodorus.
Means "gift of Zeus", derived from Greek Ζηνός (Zenos) meaning "of Zeus" and δωρον (doron) meaning "gift".
Latinized form of Zenodoros. This name was borne by an ancient Greek mathematician from the 2nd century BC.
Means "given by Zeus", derived from Greek Ζηνός (Zenos) meaning "of Zeus" and δοτός (dotos) meaning "given, granted".
Means "glory of Zeus", derived from Greek Ζηνός (Zenos) meaning "of Zeus" and κλέος (kleos) meaning "glory".
Means "manifestation of Zeus", derived from Ancient Greek Ζηνός (Zenos) meaning "of Zeus" and φανής (phanes) meaning "appearing".
The name of a woman in 'A genuine account of the life and transactions of H. ap D. Price ... Written by himself' (1752).

Invented by Paul Mowatt and Marina Ogilvy, the daughter of Princess Alexandra of Kent, for their daughter born 1990, allegedly inspired by the American novel Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance (1974; see also Zen) and Eno, the surname of English musician Brian Eno (1948-). Perhaps this was combined with a Russian diminutive suffix (such as in Anouska) to reflect her descent from Tsar Alexander of Russia, through Marina Ogilvy's grandmother, Princess Marina of Greece and Denmark.

From the kanji 善 (zen) meaning “good” and 保 (ho) meaning “protection”.Notable person with this name is Zenpo Shimabukuro (島袋 善保) (1943-), the current head of the Shorin-Ryu Seibukan karate system and the son of its founder, Zenryo Shimabukuro (具袋 善良) (1908-1969).

column3: 善助, 前記, etc.(Japanese Kanji)
column12: From 前 (zen) meaning "in front of, before" and 記 (suke) meaning "mark, describe, statement, inscription, mention, the Kojiki". Other kanji combinations can be used.
From Japanese 善 (zen) meaning "virtue, goodness" or 禅 (zen) meaning "dhyana, zen" combined with 太 (ta) meaning "big, great, fat". Other Kanji combinations are possible.

column3: ゼンタロウ(Japanese Katakana)|ぜんたろう(Japanese Hiragana)

column12: Means "she will do for herself" in Xhosa.

From Xhosa uzenzile meaning "you brought this on yourself". This was the first name of the South African singer and civil rights activist Miriam Makeba (1932-2008), full name Zenzile Miriam Makeba. Her mother had a difficult labour and delivery, and Miriam's grandmother, who attended the birth, often muttered uzenzile to Miriam's mother during her recovery.
It is from the Kanji characters "禅" (zen) meaning "ritual" and "僧" (sō) meaning "monk".
It is a variant transcription of Zenzō.
Old High German variant of Proto-Germanic *Tīwaz (compare Tyr and Cisa).
Likely an invented name, based off rhyming names such as Leola.
Likely an 18th and 19th-century elaboration of the (very) rare feminine name Zéolie with the then-popular feminine name suffix -ide.
Possibly related to Zoila or an erroneous form of Zoélie.
A name coined by the English poet Alexander Pope, appearing in his poem "Epistle to Miss Blount" (1715).
Perhaps a modern feminine form of Zephaniah inspired by Stephani and Tiffani.
Means 'Yahweh is in the clouds' originating from Hebrew in accordance to Zeph or Zeph...
The name might mean "one born on Sabbath", but more probably is a modification of the ethnic Zephathi (Zephathite), from Zarephathi (Zarephathite).
Anglicized form of Ceferino. In the English-speaking world, the Venerable Ceferino Namuncurá (1886-1905) is sometimes known as Zepherin.
Short form of Joséphine. This is the name of a minor character in Victor Hugo's novel Les Misérables (1862).
Variant of Zéphyrin (see Zephyrinus). Though it was a popular French name in the 19th and early 20th centuries, its usage is mainly confined to various French-speaking African nations today.
This is the name of one of the sons of Eliphaz listed in the Bible.

Variant of Ziphion. Means "hidden" in Hebrew. In the apocryphal Book of Enoch this was the name of an angel sent by the archangel Gabriel, along with the angel Ithuriel, to find the location of Satan after his fall.
Likely a combination of Zephyrine and Stefanie.
Variant of Sophronia, perhaps altered by association with Zéphyrine.
Likely a diminutive and feminine form of Zephaniah.
From Zephyranthes, the name of a genus of flowering plants in the Amaryllis family, derived from the name of the Greek god Zephyros and Greek ἄνθος (anthos) meaning "flower, blossom".

Derived from Ancient Greek ζεφύριος (zephyrios) meaning "of the West, west wind, westerly". This may have been an epithet of the Greek goddess Aphrodite, as there was a temple dedicated to her at Cape Zephyrion.
Variant of Zephyrus, the Greek god of the west wind.
Possibly an Armenian form of Zephyr.
Feminine variant of Zeppelin using the suffix lyn.

Transferred use of the name of the Zeppelin airships; from the surname of Count Ferdinand von Zeppelin (1838-1917), a German aeronautical pioneer, designer and manufacturer of airships. Modern usage of the name may also be inspired by the English rock band Led Zeppelin (formed 1968).

column3: 泽清, etc.(Chinese)|澤清, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 泽 (zé) meaning "moist, grace, brilliance" and 清 (qīng) meaning "blue, green, young", as well as other character combinations that can form this name.
Possibly a form of Zahra 1 or Zahra 2.
Lamanite commander at Sidon battle (c. 74 BC).
From the Hebrew name זרחיה (Zerachyah) meaning "Yahweh has risen, brightness of the Lord", from the verb זרח (zarah), "dawning, shining" and יה (yah), referring to the Hebrew God.
The main protagonist in the children's book 'Zeralda's Ogre' by Tomi Unger.

column4: French (Quebec, Rare, Archaic)|French (Belgian, Rare, Archaic)|French (Rare, Archaic)

column12: Derived from Kurdish zêr meaning "gold" and av meaning "water".
Feminine name possibly invented by Molière for his play Les Fourberies de Scapin.

Munpa Zerdan-"Radiant Black Darkness" "Rays of Darkness" was formed by Medbum Nagpo (Infinite Black Non Being) in an egg of darkess (mun pa ‘i sgong nga); is the king of Non-existence/oblivion and wants to annihilate/emtpy existence; made wife from his own shadow; their grandchildren are demons. From Tibetan Bon Religion.
Possibly from the Persian زرافشان Zar-afshân meaning meaning "spreader of gold".

Variant of Serilda. It was regionally popular in the Midwestern and Southern United States in the 19th century, borne by the Kentuckian mother of Jesse James, outlaw, as well as her husband's niece, whom Jesse later married. Another known bearer was American suffragist Zerelda G. Wallace (1817-1901).
Unknown origin, possibly a variant of a last name.
Alteration of Jeremiah with a z.
Transferred use of the surname Zeren.
Derived from Kurdish zêr meaning "gold" and gula meaning "rose".
In the Bible, one of the six musical sons of the poet Jeduthun. Identical to Izri.
Famously borne by St. ZerJacob, missionary of Ethiopia.
Possibly a variant of Zerline. This is the title of a 1955 song by American R&B duo Gene & Billy (singers Gene Ford and Billy Boyd), about a woman named Zerlene.

The name of a character in Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart's opera 'Don Giovanni' (1787), to an Italian libretto by Lorenzo Da Ponte, which was based on the legend of Don Juan.It is not entirely clear where Mozart found this name: either he (thought he) invented it (possibly based on the Italian surname Zerla) or he adopted and adapted the old Yiddish name Zerline and Zerlina.Zerline and Zerlina themselves are elaborated forms and diminutives of the Yiddish names Zerle and Zaerle, all of which have first been recorded, in the German-speaking world, between the late 1300s and early 1500s. They have been occasionally used up until the late 1800s and early 1900s, although their later uses might have been inspired by the opera.
French form and German and Yiddish variant of Zerlina.This name was also used on a character in Daniel Auber's opera Fra Diavolo (1830).

(Slovak) variant transcription of Chernobog. Zernebog is a Slavic deity, about whom much has been speculated but little can be said definitively. The name may also be given as Crnobog, Czernobóg, Černobog, Црнобог or Chernobog; these are all romanizations of the Russian Чернобог, meaning black god. The only historical sources, which are Christian ones, interpret him as a dark, accursed god, but it is questionable how important (or evil) he was really considered to be by ancient Slavs.The name is attested only among West Slavic tribes of the 12th century, hence it is speculated that he was not a very important or very old deity.
From Persian زر (zar) meaning "gold" and نگار (negār) meaning "beloved, sweetheart; painting, picture".

Derived from the Italian zero itself from Medieval Latin zèphyrum, Arabic صفر (ṣifr) and Sanskrit शून्य (śūnyá), ultimately meaning "empty".In Japan the same sound and meaning was given to the kanji 零 (rei), probably after the contact with Western cultures. Zero has been used for some manga and anime characters.
Variant of Zerubbabel (or its Hellenized form Zorobabel).
From Japanese 零 (zero) meaning "zero" combined with 音 (ne) meaning "sound". Other kanji combinations are possible.

Zeror, son of Bechorath, of the tribe of Benjamin, was the great-grandfather of King Saul and of his commander Abner. According to Saul, his family was the least of the tribe of Benjamin. (1 Samuel 9)
From Japanese 零 (zero) meaning "zero" combined with 夜 (yo) meaning "night". Other kanji combinations are possible.
Means "golden, yellow" or "daffodil, jonquil, narcissus" in Turkish, ultimately from Persian زرین (zarrin).
Means "daffodil crown, narcissus crown, golden crown" in Turkish.
Modern coinage derived from Basque zeru "sky; heavens; heaven".

Possibly means "conceived and born in Babylon" from a contraction of either Assyrian-Babylonian Zəru Bābel "seed of Babylon" or Hebrew זְרוּעַ בָּבֶל (Zərua‘ Bāvel) "the one sown of Babylon". In the Old Testament Zerubbabel led the first group of Jews out of captivity in Babylon in the first year of the Persian king Cyrus.
German form of the Biblical name Zeruiah
Hebrew form of Zeruiah. This is borne by Israeli novelist Zeruya Shalev (1959-).
Feminine variant of Zyren or Zyron

column3: 泽仕, etc.(Chinese)|澤仕, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 泽 (zé) meaning "moist, marsh, grace, brilliance" combined with 仕 (shì) meaning "to hold an official post, to be an official". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Greek diminutive of Georgia. Also compare Zorzeta.
From 泽 (zé) meaning "pool, pond" and 涛 (tāo) meaning "billows, large waves".
Hungarian male name, of possible Slavic origin, from zet ''son-in-law''.

Possibly derived from Ancient Greek ζητέω (zeteo) meaning "to seek, look for, inquire; to strive for, desire, wish". In Greek myth, Zetes and his twin brother Calais were sons of Boreas, the god of the north wind, and members of the Argonauts.
According to Hitchcock's Bible Names Dictionary, means "he that examines or beholds". In the Bible, this is the name one of the seven eunuchs of Ahasuerus in the Book of Esther.
Means "ours" or "belongs to us" in both Xhosa and Zulu within the Nguni language group. Notable South African name bearers include actor Zethu Dlomo and orchestral musician Zethu Mashika.

Latinized form of the Greek name Ζῆθος (Zêthos), a derivative of the verb ζάω (zaô) "to live". In Greek legend Zethus and his twin brother Amphion were sons of Zeus by Antiope. They are important characters in one of the two founding myths of the city of Thebes, as the builders of the city walls. This was also the name of a 3rd-century Neoplatonist philosopher and friend of Plotinus.
Means "to the day" in Mandarin Chinese. This is the posthumous name of Wu Zhao, the sole female ruler of the Chinese Empire.
Diminutive of the composed name José António, formed by combining Zé and Tó.
Short form of names ending in -zetta, -cetta and -setta.
Short form of names ending in -zette, such as Suzette or Lizette.
Diminutive of Rosetta, Izetta, Lizette, Suzette and other names containing a similar sound.
Alternate transcription of Tigrinya ዘውዲ (see Zewdi).

Derived from Ancient Greek ζεῦξις (zeuxis) meaning "a yoking together" (which comes from ζεύγνυμι (zeugnymi) "to yoke, saddle a beast of burden; to join, link together; to join in wedlock") and δᾶμος (damos), the Doric Greek form of δῆμος (demos) "the people".
Feminine form of Zeuxippos. This was the name of several Greek mythological figures.
Means "desultor, someone who can leap from one horse or chariot to another", from Greek ζεύγνυμι (zeugnumi) meaning "to yoke, saddle; to join, link together" and ἵππος (hippos) meaning "horse".
Latinized form of Zeuxippos. This was the name of several characters in Greek mythology, including a son of Apollo by the nymph Syllis.
Means "to yoke together" or "to bridge", ultimately derived from Greek ζεύγνυμι (zeugnymi) meaning "to yoke, saddle; to join, link together".
Derived from Ancient Greek ζεύγνυμι (zeugnumi) meaning "to yoke, join together, join in wedlock" and θεά (thea) meaning "goddess".
Derived from Ancient Greek ζεύγνυμι (zeugnumi) meaning "to yoke, bridle, join together, join in wedlock". In Greek mythology, Zeuxo was one of the Oceanids, possibly associated with marriage.
Derived from zevar, the name of a decoration sewn in colourful silk thread on traditional Uzbek footwear called mahsi.
Diminutive of the composed names José Vítor or José Vicente, formed by combining Tó and Vi.
Variant of Zeven, possibly influenced by Kevin.
Form of Zeus in various Slavic, Caucasian, Siberian and Central Asian languages.
Means "weapon, armament, firearm" or "tool, instrument" in Mongolian.

Zewditu is an Amharic word meaning "the Crown". Although it was sometimes erroneously Anglicized as Judith, it's not a cognate.Zewditu (born Askala Maryam; 29 April 1876 – 2 April 1930) was the Empress of Ethiopia from 1916 to 1930.
From 则 (zé) meaning "rule, law, regulation" and 文 (wén) meaning "mark, pattern, design".
German transcription of Zvi. It was recorded in medieval German-speaking countries but became very rare in modern times.

column3: 泽炫, 泽铉, 泽绚, etc.(Chinese)|澤炫, 澤鉉, 澤絢, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From 澤 (zé) meaning "moist, marsh, grace, brilliance" combined with 炫 (xuàn) meaning "shine, glitter" or 鉉 (xuàn) referring to a device used to lift a ritual tripod cauldron or 绚 (xuàn) meaning "brilliant fabric design, kimono design". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

column3: ဇေယျ, ဇေယျာ(Burmese)
column12: Means "victory" in Burmese, ultimately from Sanskrit जय (jaya).
Alternate transcription of Arabic زياد (see Ziyad).

column3: ဇေယျ, ဇေယျာ(Burmese)
column12: Alternate transcription of Burmese ဇေယျ/ဇေယျာ (see Zeya).
Possibly an Azerbaijani form of Ziba 1.

Means "grandfather" in Yiddish.This is a so-called amuletic name which was given to a child who was ill, or one whose parents had lost children before. It was chosen in the hope that the child would live to be a grandfather.
From the first part of Zeynalabdin.
Alternate transcription of Arabic زينب‎‎ (see Zaynab).
Turkish form of Zainul, used as a short form of Zeynel Abidin.
Possibly from Arabic zayn which means "beauty".
From Arabic زين (zayn) meaning "beauty" and فلك (falak) meaning "sky, firmament".
Means "flower, blossom" in Chechen, ultimately from Mongolian цэцэг (tsetseg) via Turkish çiçek.
Meaning unknown, perhaps a misinterpretation of the French name Suzette. This name is not used in French, though, as it is a crude word for female genitalia.
Basque and Milanese Lombard form of Cecilia.
Meaning unknown. This is the name of the main character of the fairy tale La gatta Cenerentola, an early version of Cinderella written by Giambattista Basile.
From Chinese 泽 (zé) meaning "moist, marsh, grace, brilliance" and 宗 (zōng) meaning "lineage, ancestry", or other character combinations.
Likely an invented name. This is the name of Charles Manson's son.
Derived from Albanian zgjim "awakening" as well as from Albanian zgjim, an archaic term meaning "knowledge, education".

From Chinese 吒 (zhà) meaning "shout, roar; scold", in addition to other hanzi that are pronounced similarly. This name is sometimes inspired by 哪吒 (pinyin: Nézhā), a protection deity in Taoism, Buddhism, and Chinese folk religion.
Means "small stone" in Mongolian, from жаахан (jaakhan) meaning "small, a bit" and чулуу (chuluu) meaning "stone".

Ukrainian non-canonical name meaning "welcomed, desired, wished for", derived as a contracted patriciple of verb zhadaty (жадати) - "to want, to wish for, to desire, to demand, to wish something to somebody, to crave". There were 159 cossacks of this name in 1649 Zaporozhian Army register. It may have been used as translation of Desiderius.
Indonesian and Malay form of Zafir.
From Chinese 斋 (zhāi) meaning "fast, vegetarian diet; room". Other hanzi are possible but rare for this name.
Means “goodness, kindness, good deeds” in Kyrgyz.
Kazakh and Kyrgyz form of Yakub.
Kurdish form of Zhaleh and Azerbaijani variant transcription of Jalə.
Alternate transcription of Persian ژاله (see Zhaleh).
Possibly a variant transcriptions of Arabic adjective خالي jali meaning "empty, free, open" in Arabic.

Kazakh form of Janpolad. It could also be that the name has a slightly different etymology, in which case it is derived from the Arabic adjective جميل (jamil) meaning "beautiful, handsome, good" (see Jamil) combined with the Persian noun پولاد (polad) meaning "steel". It is identical to the Kazakh word жамбыл (jambyl) meaning "citadel, fortress".
Kazakh and Kyrgyz form of Jamila.

column3: Жан(Bulgarian, Macedonian, Ukrainian)|湛, 霑, 瞻, 展, 战, 占, 詹, etc.(Chinese)
column12: Bulgarian, Macedonian, and Ukrainian form of Žan.
Georgian form of the French name Jeanne. It is also used as a short form of Zhaneta in Georgia.
Maybe a rare variant of Shanade.
Invented name based on Shanae or Janae.
From жан (zhan) meaning "soul, life" (of Persian origin) and Arabic نار (nār) meaning "fire" combined with beg meaning "chieftan, master".
Either derived from Kazakh жанат (zhanat) meaning "raccoon" (figuratively meaning "large eyes") or Arabic جنة (jannah) meaning "paradise, garden".
From Kazakh жан (zhan) meaning "soul" combined with the Turkic military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".
From Kazakh жан (zhan) meaning "soul" and болат (bolat) meaning "steel".
From Kyrgyz жан (zhan) meaning "soul" and болот (bolot) meaning "steel".
From жан (jān) meaning "soul, life" combined with бота (bota) "camel calf, colt" in Kazakh
Means "rich in rain" in Kazakh, derived from жаңбыр (zhanbyr) "rain" and бай (bay) "rich, wealthy".
From the Chinese 湛 (zhàn) meaning "deep, profound" or "clear, tranquil, placid" and 嫦 (cháng), the name of a moon goddess.
From Kazakh жан (zhan) meaning "soul" and дәулет (daulet) meaning "contentment, wealth, fortune".
Variant of Zander. According to the SSA, Zhander was given to 5 boys in 2018.

Combination of the Chinese character 占 (see Zhan) and 堆 (see Dui).Other characters combinations are also possible.A famous bearer is Ciren Zhandui, a Chinese cross-country skier who competed at 2022 Winter Olympics.
Variant of Zane 1. This was the name of the Silver Ranger in the TV series 'Power Rangers in Space'.
From Kazakh жан (zhan) meaning "soul" and ел (el) meaning "people, country".
Albanian, Belarusian, Macedonian, Bulgarian, and Ukrainian form of Jeannette.

column3: 章, 璋, 彰, 张, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 章 (zhāng) meaning "chapter; seal, official stamp", in addition to other hanzi that are pronounced similarly.
Combination of the name Zhangir and the Turkic title khan meaning "ruler, leader".
From Chinese 樟 (zhāng) meaning "camphor tree" combined with 柯 (kē) meaning "stalk or branch; axe-handle, helve". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 章龙, 张龙, etc.(Chinese)|章龍, 張龍, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 章 (zhāng) meaning "chapter" or 张 (zhāng) meaning "stretch, extend" combined with 龙 (lóng) meaning "dragon". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
From the Chinese 璋 (zhāng) meaning "jade ornament" and 玫 (méi) meaning "rose".
From the Chinese 长 (zhǎng) meaning "long, lasting" or "excel, be good at" and 巧 (qiǎo) meaning "artful, skillful, clever".

column3: 樟煜, 璋豫, 长宇, 长雨, etc.(Chinese)|樟煜, 璋豫, 長宇, 長雨, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 樟 (zhāng) meaning "camphor tree" or 长 (zhǎng) meaning "to grow, to develop" combined with 煜 (yù) meaning "brilliant, glorious", 豫 (yù) meaning "relaxed, comfortable, carefree, happy", 宇 (yǔ) meaning "house, eaves, universe" or 雨 (yǔ) meaning "rain". Other character combinations are also possible.
Derived from Kazakh жан (zhan) meaning "soul" and the Turkish military title beg meaning "chieftain, master" or Kazakh бекем (bekem) meaning "firm, strong, steady".
Derived from Kazakh жан (zhan) meaning "soul", ultimately from Persian.
From Chinese 占 (zhān) meaning "to divine, to foretell" combined with 金 (jīn) meaning "metal" or "gold", as well as other hanzi combinations that can form this name.
From the Chinese 湛 (zhàn) meaning "deep, profound" or "clear, tranquil, placid" and 娟 (juān) meaning "beautiful, graceful".

column3: 展乐, etc.(Chinese)|展樂, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 展 (zhǎn) meaning "to open up, to spread out, to unfold, to unfurl" combined with 乐 (lè) meaning "happy, glad". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From 展 (zhan) meaning "to open, to unfold" and 玲 (ling) meaning "a jade sound".
From the Chinese 湛 (zhàn) meaning "deep, profound" or "clear, tranquil, placid" and 妹 (mèi) meaning "younger sister" or 梅 (méi) meaning "plum".

column3: 中愉, 忠愉, 仲愉, 中玉, 忠玉, 仲玉, 中雨, 忠雨, 仲雨, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 中 (zhōng) meaning "middle" or 忠 (zhōng) meaning "loyalty, devotion" or 仲 (zhòng) meaning "middle, second" combined with 愉 (yú) meaning "pleasant, delightful" or 玉 (yù) meaning "jade, precious stone, gem" or 雨 (yǔ) meaning "rain". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
From the Chinese 忠 (zhōng) meaning "loyalty, devotion" and 珠 (zhū) meaning "bead, pearl, precious stone".
Means "flowers" in Arabic, the plural form of زهْرة (zahra) (chiefly Morrocan and Algerian).

Taken from the French surname Jaurès, which was most famously borne by French Socialist Jean Jaurès (1859-1914). This name was created by Communist parents who were eager to reject traditional names.A notable bearer is Zhores Alferov (1930-), a Soviet Russian physicist.
Armenian, Bulgarian, Ukrainian and Georgian form of Georges.
Armenian and Bulgarian form of Georgette.
Derived from Ancient Greek ἰῶτα (iota) meaning "jot, a small amount" through palatalization of the word in Georgian.Also see the Georgian name Joto, which comes from the same root.
Derived from Central Kurdish ژوان‎ (jwan) meaning “tryst”.
Derived from Persian گوهر (gowhar) meaning "jewel, gem, pearl", as well as a variant transcription of the masculine name Dzhokhar (of the same etymological origin).
Russian and Armenian variant of Josef.
Russian and Ukrainian form of Josephine.
Means "little duck" in Potawatomi. This was the name of a chief of the St. Joseph and Elkhart Potawatomi.

column3: 铸, 朱, 竺, 柷, 洙, 珠, 翥, 助, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 朱 (zhū) meaning "vermilion red; cinnabar", in addition to other hanzi that are pronounced similarly.
From Chinese 拽 (zhuài) meaning "drag, pull", in addition to other hanzi that are pronounced similarly.

column3: 专, 譔, 瑑, 颛, 篆, 转, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 专 (zhuān) meaning "concentrated, devoted; speciality", in addition to other hanzi that are pronounced similarly.
From Chinese 庄 (zhuāng) meaning "village; solemn, serious", in addition to other hanzi that are pronounced similarly.

From Chinese 颛 (zhuān) meaning "good, honest, simple" and 顼 (xū) meaning "grieved, anxious". In Chinese mythology, Zhuanxu is the grandson of the Yellow Emperor (Xuanyuan) and one of the Five Emperors, sage-kings who ruled in the early days of Chinese civilization. He fought and won a war against Gonggong, instituted laws and calendrical systems, and commanded the gods Chong and Li to cut the connections between Heaven and Earth, thus ending the era of widespread shamanism. After his death, he became deified as the Black Emperor of the North. A cryptic passage in the Shanhaijing (山海经) or Classic of Mountains and Seas implies that his spirit might have gone on to inhabit the bodies of fish. He is also known as Gaoyang (高阳) or Qianhuang (乾荒).
From the Chinese 竹 (zhú) meaning "bamboo, flute" and 冰 (bīng) meaning "ice".
From the Chinese 竹 (zhú) meaning "bamboo, flute" and 纯 (chún) meaning "pure, clean, simple" or 春 (chūn) meaning "spring".
From the Chinese 竹 (zhú) meaning "bamboo, flute" and 翠 (cuì) meaning "green" or "kingfisher".
From 茱 (zhū) the Chinese name for Zanthoxylum ailanthoides and 迪 (dí) meaning "to englighten, to guide".
From the Chinese 竹 (zhú) meaning "bamboo, flute" and 芳 (fāng) meaning "fragrant".

From the characters 烛 (zhú, meaning "shining, torch-like") and 光 (guāng, meaning "light"). This is the name of a goddess mentioned in the Shanhaijing (山海经). Along with her sister, Xiaoming, she is a daughter of the Emperor Shun (Chonghua) by his wife Dengbi. The two of them live in a marsh next to the Yellow River, where their spirits illuminate the surrounding land in a hundred-league radius.
From the Chinese 竹 (zhú) meaning "bamboo, flute" and 晗 (hán) meaning "pre-dawn".
From the Chinese 竹 (zhú) meaning "bamboo, flute" and 晖 (huī) meaning "sunshine" or "light, bright, radiant".
From Chinese 骓 (zhuī) meaning "piebald horse", in addition to other hanzi that are pronounced similarly.
From the Chinese 隹 (zhuī) meaning "bird" and 嘉 (jiā) meaning "good, fine, excellent, auspicious".
From the Chinese 隹 (zhuī) meaning "bird" and 诺 (nuò) meaning "promise".
From the Chinese 隹 (zhuī) meaning "bird" and 荃 (quán) meaning "aromatic herb".
From the Chinese 隹 (zhuī) meaning "bird" and 笑 (xiào) meaning "smile, laugh".
From the Chinese 隹 (zhuī) meaning "bird" and 欣 (xīn) meaning "happy, joyous, delighted".
From the Chinese 隹 (zhuī) meaning "bird" and 燕 (yàn) meaning "swallow (bird)".
From the Chinese 隹 (zhuī) meaning "bird" and 烨 (yè) meaning "bright, glorious, splendid, firelight".
From the Chinese 隹 (zhuī) meaning "bird" and 嬴 (yíng) meaning "to win".
Alternate transcription of Kazakh Жұлдызай (see Zhuldyzay).

From Kazakh жұлдыз (zhuldyz) meaning "star" and ай (ay) meaning "moon". The name can be used as a reference to the crescent moon and star symbol originating with ancient Turkic and Central Asian celestial mythologies (often associated with the goddess Umay) which was later adopted by the Ottoman Empire and became widely associated with the Islamic faith. Compare Uyghur Yultuzay and Turkish Yıldızay.
From the Chinese 竹 (zhú) meaning "bamboo, flute" and 蕾 (lěi) meaning "bud, unopened flower".
From the Chinese 竹 (zhú) meaning "bamboo, flute" and 莉 (lì) meaning "white jasmine".
From Kazakh жұма (zhuma) or Kyrgyz жума (zhuma) meaning "Friday" (of Arabic origin) combined with бай (bay) meaning "rich, wealthy".
From Kazakh жұма (juma) meaning "Friday" (of Arabic origin) combined with the Turkish military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".
From Kyrgyz жума (zhuma) meaning "friday, week" (from Arabic جمعة (jumuʕa)), combined with Persian بی‌بی‌ (bibi) meaning "madam, lady, matron".
From Kazakh жұма (zhuma) meaning "Friday" (of Arabic origin) combined with the name Ali 1.

From Kazakh жұма (zhuma) or Kyrgyz жума (zhuma) meaning "Friday" (both of Arabic origin) and Kazakh and Kyrgyz гүл (gul) meaning "flower". It is only used as a feminine name in Kazakhstan while it is unisex in Kyrgyzstan.
From Kazakh жұма (zhuma) meaning "Friday" (of Arabic origin) combined with the Turkic title khan meaning "leader, ruler".
Derived from Kazakh жұма (zhuma) meaning "Friday" (of Arabic origin) combined with қыз (qyz) meaning "girl".
From Kyrgyz жума (zhuma) meaning "friday" (of Arabic origin) and the given name Ali 1.

column3: 竹梅, 竹玫, 珠玫, 祝妹(Chinese)
column12: From the Chinese 竹 (zhú) meaning "bamboo, flute", 珠 (zhū) meaning "bead, pearl, precious stone" or 祝 (zhù) meaning "pray for happiness and blessings" and 梅 (méi) meaning "plum", 玫 (méi) meaning "rose" or 妹 (mèi) meaning "younger sister".
From the Chinese 竹 (zhú) meaning "bamboo, flute" and 萌 (méng) meaning "bud, sprout".
From the Chinese 珠 (zhū) meaning "bead, pearl, gem" and 淼 (miǎo) meaning "wide expanse of water".
From the Chinese 竹 (zhú) meaning "bamboo, flute" and 敏 (mǐn) meaning "agile, nimble, fast" or "clever".
From Chinese 竹 (zhú) meaning "bamboo" combined with 明 (míng) meaning "bright, light, clear". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From Chinese 准 (zhǔn) meaning "level; accurate; equal", in addition to other characters that are pronounced similarly.
From the Chinese 竹 (zhú) meaning "bamboo, flute" and 宁 (níng) meaning "calm, peaceful, tranquil".
From the given name Zhunis combined with the Turkic military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".
From Chinese 准 (jun) meaning "approve, permit" combined with 翼 (yì) meaning "the wing of a bird". Other character combinations are possible.
From Chinese 卓 (zhuó) meaning "tall, lofty, outstanding", 茁 (zhuó) meaning "sprout, flourish" or other hanzi that are pronounced similarly.
From Chinese 卓 (zhuó) meaning "tall, lofty, outstanding" combined with 成 (chéng) meaning "completed, finished, succeeded". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
From Chinese 卓 (zhuó) meaning "outstanding" or 倬 (zhuō) meaning "large, grand, attractive" combined with 凡 (fán) meaning "ordinary". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From Chinese 卓 (zhuō) meaning "outstanding, brilliant" combined with 恆 (héng) meaning "constant, persistent", as well as other character combinations that can form this name.

column3: 卓华, 灼华, etc.(Chinese)|卓華, 灼華, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 卓 (zhuó) meaning "tall, lofty, outstanding" or 灼 (zhuó) meaning "bright, shining, luminous" combined with 华 (huá) meaning "splendid, illustrious, flowery, Chinese". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 卓慧, 卓辉, etc.(Chinese)|卓慧, 卓輝, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 卓 (zhuó) meaning "tall, lofty, outstanding" combined with 慧 (huì) meaning "bright, intelligent" or 辉 (huī) meaning "brightness". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
From the Chinese 卓 (zhuō) meaning "profound, brilliant" and 娈 (luán) meaning "lovely, beautiful, docile".

column3: 卓明, 灼明, 焯明, 茁鸣, etc.(Chinese)|卓明, 灼明, 焯明, 茁鳴, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 卓 (zhuó) meaning "tall, lofty, outstanding", 灼 (zhuó) meaning "bright, shining, luminous", 焯 (zhuō) meaning "bright, clear" or 茁 (zhuó) meaning "sprout, flourish" combined with 明 (míng) meaning "bright, light, clear" or 鸣 (míng) meaning "cry, call, make a sound, voice". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
From the Chinese 卓 (zhuō) meaning "profound, brilliant" and 朋 (péng) meaning "friend".
From the Chinese 卓 (zhuō) meaning "profound, brilliant, lofty" and 琼 (qióng) meaning "jade, rare, precious, elegant".
From the Chinese 卓 (zhuō) meaning "profound, brilliant" and 彤 (tóng) meaning "red, vermillion".
From the Chinese 卓 (zhuō) meaning "profound, brilliant" and 娃 (wá) meaning "doll, baby, pretty girl".

column3: 卓璇, 卓轩, etc.(Chinese)|卓璇, 卓軒, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 卓 (zhuó) meaning "tall, oustanding" combined with 璇 (xuán) meaning "fine jade" or 轩 (xuān) meaning "high, lofty".

From Chinese 卓 (zhuó) meaning "tall, lofty, outstanding" or 琢 (zhuó) meaning "carve, cut (jade or gemstone)" combined with 妍 (yán) meaning "beautiful" or 言 (yán) meaning "say, speak, words, language". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
From the Chinese 倬 (zhuō) meaning "noticeable, clear, distinct" and 瑛 (yīng) meaning "luster of gems, crystal".
From the Chinese 卓 (zhuō) meaning "profound, brilliant, lofty" and 月 (yuè) meaning "moon".
From the Chinese 竹 (zhú) meaning "bamboo, flute" and 茜 (qiàn) meaning "madder" or "reeds".
From the Chinese 竹 (zhú) meaning "bamboo, flute" and 情 (qíng) meaning "sentiment, affection, emotion" or 清 (qīng) meaning "clear, pure, clean, peaceful".
From Chinese 朱 (zhū) meaning "vermilion red, cinnabar" and 雀 (què) meaning "sparrow". This is the Chinese name of the Vermilion Bird, associated with the south and the summer season.

From Chinese 祝 (zhù) meaning “to pray” and 融 (róng) meaning “to fuse, harmonize”. This is the name of the Chinese god of fire who oversees the south and the season of summer. He is described as a figure with the face of a human and the body of a beast, riding on two dragons. Zhurong is known for his clash with the water god Gonggong, which famously led to the goddess Nüwa patching up the sky. He is also regarded as the ancestor of the Chu people.
From the Chinese 竹 (zhú) meaning "bamboo, flute" and 桑 (sāng) meaning "mulberry tree".
From Chinese character 渚 (zhǔ) meaning "shore, islet, sandbank" combined with 砂 (shā) meaning "sand". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
From the Chinese 竹 (zhú) meaning "bamboo, flute" and 珊 (shān) meaning "coral".
Combination of the given name Zhusip and the Turkish military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".
From the Chinese 竹 (zhú) meaning "bamboo, flute" and 婷 (tíng) meaning "pretty, attractive, graceful".
From the Chinese 竹 (zhú) meaning "bamboo, flute" and 薇 (wēi), a type of fern.
From the Chinese 竹 (zhú) meaning "bamboo, flute" and 溪 (xī) meaning "mountain stream".
From the Chinese 竹 (zhú) meaning "bamboo, flute" or 朱 (zhū) meaning "bright red, vermilion" and 霞 (xiá) meaning "rosy clouds".
From the Chinese 竹 (zhú) meaning "bamboo, flute" and 仙 (xiān) meaning "transcendent, immortal".
From the Chinese 竹 (zhú) meaning "bamboo, flute" or 祝 (zhù) meaning "pray for happiness or blessings" and 馨 (xīn) meaning "fragrant, aromatic" or "distant fragrance".
From the Chinese 竹 (zhú) meaning "bamboo, flute" and 燕 (yàn) meaning "swallow (bird)".
From the Chinese 竹 (zhú) meaning "bamboo, flute" and 漪 (yī) meaning "ripples, swirling".
From the Chinese 珠 (zhū) meaning "bead, pearl, precious stone" and 银 (yín) meaning "silver, wealth".
From the Chinese 珠 (zhū) meaning "bead, pearl, precious stone" and 玉 (yù) meaning "jade".
From the Chinese 竹 (zhú) meaning "bamboo, flute" and 园 (yuán) meaning "garden, park, orchard" or 媛 (yuàn) meaning "beauty, beautiful woman".
From the Chinese 竹 (zhú) meaning "bamboo, flute" and 云 (yún) meaning "clouds".

According to Georgian sources, this name is derived from a (presumably archaic) Georgian word that means "blinking". However, there is a Russian source that states that the name is a Georgian form of Julia. Last but not least, there is also an English source that says that at least in modern Georgian, ჟუჟუნა (zhuzhuna) is a regular word that means "sun shower" (as in, a rain shower that occurs while the sun is shining).
From Kyrgyz жылдыз (zhyldyz) meaning "star" combined with the Turkic military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".
From Kyrgyz жылдыз (zhyldyz) meaning "star" and кан (kan) meaning "blood".
Derived from жыл (zhyl) meaning "year" and келд (keld) meaning "arrived".
From Kyrgyz жыргал (zhyrgal) meaning "happiness" and the Turkish military title beg meaning "chieftain, master".
From Ukrainian життя (zhyttya), meaning "life", and мир (myr), meaning "peace". This was the name of a Kyivan knyaz, whom the city and region Zhytomyr was named after.

column3: 紫, 姿, 子, 梓, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 紫 (zĭ) meaning "purple", 姿 (zī) meaning "appearance, gesture, presence, posture", 子 (zǐ) meaning "child", or 梓 (zǐ) meaning "catalpa tree". Other hanzi with similar pronunciations are also possible.

Possibly means "sweat, swelling" in Hebrew. Hebrew name of a man mentioned in the Old Testament, 1 Chronicles 5:13, in a genealogical list. This 'has been used as a first name in Britain since the 1960s, but is likely to be mistaken for a girl's name' (Dunkling & Gosling, 1986). It was used for the central character in the film 'Wristcutters: A Love Story' (2006), which was based on a short story by Israeli writer Etgar Keret (1967-).

column3: 子爱, 子艾, 梓艾, etc.(Chinese)|子愛, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" or 梓 (zǐ) meaning "catalpa tree" combined with 爱 (ài) meaning "love, affection" or 艾 (ài) meaning "sagebrush, wormwood". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" or 梓 (zǐ) meaning "catalpa tree" combined with 安 (ān) meaning "peace, quiet". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Perhaps a variant of Xiana. This name is borne by Malaysian pop singer Ziana Zain (1968-), in whose case it is a short form of Roziana (her real name being Siti Roziana binti Zain).
Form Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 昂 (áng) meaning "raise, lift". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Short form of Jozias. But in other words, you could also say that it is a variant spelling of Sias.There have also been a few cases where Zias is a contracted form of Zacharias.
From the first part of compound Arabic names beginning with ضياء ال (diya al) meaning "splendour of the" (such as Ziya ad-Din).
Multi-part Perso-Arabic-origin name, consisting of the elements Zia and Karim.
Means "brilliance of the moon, splendour of the moon" in Arabic.
From the first part of the Arabic phrase ضياء الرحمن (dhiyāʾ ar-raḥmān) meaning "splendour of the merciful".
From the Arabic phrase ضياء الرحمن (dhiyāʾ ar-raḥmān) meaning "splendour of the merciful".
Short form of Žibuoklė and its diminutives, such as Žibutė.
Means "ostrich nest" or "hatching place" in Arabic. This is the traditional name of the star Zeta Eridani in the constellation Eridanus.

column3: 子宝, etc.(Chinese)|子寶, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 宝 (bǎo) meaning "treasure, jewel, precious, rare". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
The Hivite son of Seir the Horite.
From the Hebrew word צִבְיָה (Tzivyah) meaning "gazelle" or "doe". In the Hebrew Bible, Zibia is the wife of King Ahaziah and the mother of King Joash.
From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 博 (bó) meaning "wide, extensive, gamble". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Derived from the Caló word ciborí meaning "miraculous". Ziboris is used as the Caló form of Milagros.

Derived from the Lithuanian noun žibuoklė meaning "liverleaf, liverwort" (as in, the flower). In turn, the flower may ultimately have derived its name from the Lithuanian verb žibėti meaning "to glint" as well as "to shine, to sparkle".
Diminutive of Žibuoklė, since this name contains the feminine diminutive suffix -utė.
From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 辰 (chén) meaning "stars, dragon of the Chinese zodiac". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 子成, 梓成, 子诚, 梓诚, 子程, 梓程, etc.(Chinese)|子成, 梓成, 子誠, 梓誠, 子程, 梓程, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" or 梓 (zǐ) meaning "catalpa" combined with 成 (chéng) meaning "completed, finished, succeeded" or 诚 (chéng) meaning "sincere, honest, truth" or 程 (chéng) meaning "rule, order, regulations". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
Nickname (stage name?) of soccer coach and footballer Arthur Antunes Coimbra.
Alternate transcription of Arabic زيدان (see Zaydan).
Alternate transcription of Arabic زيدان (see Zaydan) chiefly used in North Africa.
From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" or 紫 (zǐ) meaning "purple" combined with 蝶 (dié) meaning "butterfly". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Variant of Zedekiah. The name of a character mentioned in chapter 10 of Nehemiah.
Norman and Picard form of Isidore.
Variant of Sidsel, common in 17th century Denmark.

From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning “son” combined with 都 (dū) meaning “capital city”, “head” or “beautiful”. This is a name that appears in the song The Mountain has Fusu Trees (山有扶苏) featured in the Classic of Poetry (诗经). Within the song, it is used to refer to an ideal beautiful man the female narrator is waiting for. Other hanzi combinations are possible.

Likely means "first" in one of the Senufo languages, as the name is traditionally given to the first-born son.Known bearers of this name include the Ivorian soccer players Zié Diabaté (b. 1989) and Zié Ouattara (b. 2000).
Alternate transcription of Arabic زياد (see Ziyad) chiefly used in Tunisia.
Derived from the Lithuanian noun žiedas meaning "blossom, flower" as well as "ring, collar".
Derived from either Latvian zieds "blossom, bloom; flower" or from Latvian ziedēt "to blossom, to flower". This name was recorded in Latvia in the late Middle Ages.
Derived from either Latvian zieds "blossom; flower" or from Latvian ziedēt "to blossom, to bloom, to flower".
Combination of Žiedė and the suffix -ūne.
Derived from Lithuanian žiezdrà "sand; earth; spark". In Lithuanian mythology, this was the name of the personification of the planet Mars, one of the daughters of Saulė.

Meaning unknown. 'Livro del cavallero Cifar' (later written Zifar) is the earliest fictional adventure tale in prose in the Spanish language. It was written around 1300, probably by a cleric of Toledo, Ferrand Martínez.

column3: 子菲, 子飞, etc.(Chinese)|子飛, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 飞 (fēi) meaning "to fly" or 菲 (fēi) meaning "luxuriant, lush". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 子枫, 子丰, 梓枫, 紫枫, etc.(Chinese)|子楓, 子豐, 梓楓, 紫楓, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child", 梓 (zǐ) meaning "catalpa tree", or 紫 (zǐ) meaning "purple" combined with 枫 (fēng) meaning "maple" or 丰 (fēng) meaning "luxuriant, lush, bountiful". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Short form of Ziggy. In the case of American motivational speaker and self-help author Hilary Hinton 'Zig' Ziglar (1926-2012), it was a short form of his surname (see Ziglar).
From Chinese 子 (zǐ), meaning "son; person " or "ancient title of respect for a learned or virtuous man", combined with 歌 (gē) meaning "song; sing". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From the Karachay-Balkar зыгыт (zıgıt) meaning "sprout, shoot".
Short form of Zigmantas, which is the Lithuanian form of Sigmund.

Lithuanian form of Zsigmond, which is the Hungarian form of Sigmund. This name is not currently in use in Lithuania and most likely never has been: it is purely a lithuanized form of a foreign (in this case Hungarian) name, as in Lithuania foreign names tend to be lithuanized in order to make them easier to understand and pronounce to Lithuanian speakers.

This is a name originating in the Hararian language of Eastern Ethiopia. With the root "mazagna” (to dawn), it has several possible meanings, including ”she who is of the dawn,” "she who is first/at the beginning,” and ”she who shines like the dawn."
In the case of missing Houston, Texas man Ziguaros Kokoriss (born 1924), his name appears to be an altered form of Latvian Zigurds.

column3: 子荷, 子和, 子鹤, etc.(Chinese)|子鶴, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 荷 (hé) meaning "lotus, water lily", 和 (hé) meaning "harmony, peace", or 鹤 (hè) meaning "crane (bird)". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Combination of Zi, Hong, and Fan.

Means "he warned me" in Mandaic, a derivative of ࡆࡄࡓ (zhr) meaning "to warn". In Mandaean tradition this is the name of an uthra (a celestial being) who is the main subject of the text the Zihrun Raza Kasia. He often appears in a pair with the uthra Zhir.

column3: 子环, 子欢, etc.(Chinese)|子環, 子歡, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 环 (huán) meaning "circle, ring" or 欢 (huān) meaning "happy, pleased". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 子惠, 子恢, 资惠, etc.(Chinese)|子惠, 子恢, 資惠, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" or 资 (zī) meaning "money, wealth, goods, resources, to provide, to support" combined with 惠 (huì) meaning "favour, benefit" or 恢 (huī) meaning "extensive, vast, to restore, to recover". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 佳 (jiā) meaning "good, auspicious, beautiful". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 建 (jiàn) "build, establish" or 健 (jiàn) "strong, healthy". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 江 (jiāng) meaning "river, Yangtze". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 子杰, etc.(Chinese)|子傑, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 杰 (jié) meaning "heroic, outstanding". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 京 (jīng) meaning "capital city" or 晶 (jīng) meaning "clear, crystal". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 菊 (jú) meaning "chrysanthemum". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 子娟, 梓娟, 紫娟, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child", 梓 (zǐ) meaning "catalpa tree", or 紫 (zǐ) meaning "purple" combined with 娟 (juān) meaning "beautiful, graceful". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 子俊, 子君, 子骏, 子军, etc.(Chinese)|子駿, 子軍, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 俊 (jùn) meaning "talented, handsome", 骏 (jùn) meaning "good horse, fast", 君 (jūn) meaning "king, ruler", or 军 (jūn) meaning "army". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 愷 (kǎi) meaning "joyful, contented". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Means "We are blessed with girls" in Xhosa.
Diminutive of masculine names that contain the Slavic element živŭ meaning "alive, living", such as Živojin and Živorad.
Means "my remembrance, my recollection" from Arabic ذكر (dhikr) meaning "remembrance, recollection".
From Chinese 梓 (zǐ) meaning "catalpa tree" combined with 坤 (kūn) meaning "earth, female". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Possibly derived from Arabic زلال (zulāl) meaning "pure, clear (of water)", compare Zülal, Zilol and Zelal.

column3: 紫兰, etc.(Chinese)|紫蘭, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 紫 (zǐ) meaning "purple" combined with 兰 (lán) meaning "orchid, elegant". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

Possibly from a surname of an anglicized form of Armenian Զիլճյան (Zilčyan) meaning "cymbal-maker". This was the name of Zaijian Godsick Lara Jaranilla and Zymic Demigod Lara Jaranilla's brother, Zildjian Godweevil Lara Jaranilla.
Directly taken from Latvian zīle "acorn; titmouse".
From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 雷 (léi) meaning "thunder" or 蕾 (lěi) meaning "bud". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Another variation for Sanskrit name "Jhilika" which means Sunlight, the strong light of sun.
From the Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" and 琳 (lín) meaning "beautiful jade". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Variant transcription of Zillethai.This transcription is used in the Revised Standard Version of the Bible.

The name is comprised of two parts. The first, צלל (salal), can have one of two meanings: "to ring" or "to be dark". It is also associated with צל (sel), meaning "shadow". The second, י (yod), has multiple purposes. It can make the word possessive, make it an adjective, or it can be an abbreviation of Yahweh. The most supported combined meaning of the name is "Shadow of Yahweh".In the Bible, there are two people named Zillethai. The first, in 1 Chronicles 8:20, is a descendant of Benjamin. He is the son of Shimei and brother of Jakim, Zikri, Zabdi, Elienai, and Eliel. The second, in 1 Chronicles 12:20, is one of the men of Manasseh who deflected to David while in Ziklag.
From the word zillion, coined in the 1940s to refer to an unspecified large number, itself a blend of the letter Z and million.
Possibly a combination of the phonetic sound zilly and the common name suffix ana. As a given name, it might be taken from the name of a videogame character.
Variant of Zilmar. Alternatively, it may be derived from Persian zilmat "dark, darkness".
Variant of Solimar or Celimar or possibly formed from azul and mar, in which case it would literally mean "blue sea".
Derived from the Uzbek zilol meaning "crystal-clear, limpid" and boy meaning "rich, wealthy".

column3: 子龍, 子龙, 子隆, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 龍 or 龙 (lóng) meaning "dragon" or 隆 (lóng) meaning "prosperous, abundant". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
Variant transcription of Zillethai.This transcription is used in The Darby Translation, Jubilee Bible 2000, King James Version, The Webster Bible, and Wycliffe Bible.
Derived from Chinese Zi and Lu.

column3: 子鸾, etc.(Chinese)|子鸞, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 鸾 (luán) referring to a "mythological bird." Other hanzi combinations are possible.

Derived from either the old Lithuanian noun žilvis meaning "child, offspring" as well as "offshoot, sprout", or from old Lithuanian želvys meaning "unripe, immature, young". In Lithuanian folklore and popular culture, Žilvinas is the name of the husband of the titular character of the folk tale Eglė žalčių karalienė, which translates to English as Eglė, the Queen of Serpents.
Derived from the Lithuanian noun žilvitis meaning "osier, (basket) willow", which is ultimately derived from the old Lithuanian noun žilvis meaning "child, offspring" as well as "offshoot, sprout".
Means "radiant, clarity, illumination" from Arabic ضِيَاء‎ (ḍiyāʾ) meaning "splendour, light, glow" (see Ziya).
From an Arabic word meaning "robe, garment" and also "preparation for a journey".

Zimbo is the name of a Tarzan influenced titular character in the eponymous Zimbo Trilogy (1958-66) of Bollywood films by John Cawas and the Wadia Brothers, although the character first appeared 2 decades earlier, in Toofani Tarzan (1937).
From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 梅 (méi) meaning "plum, apricot (Prunus mume)" or 美 (měi) meaning "beautiful". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 子铭, 子鳴, 子明, 紫明, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child, offspring" or 紫 (zǐ) meaning "purple, violet" combined with 铭 (míng) meaning "inscribe, engrave", 鳴 (míng) meaning "to cry (of birds, animals, or insects)", or 明 (míng) meaning "bright, light", as well as other character combinations.
From the Hebrew זִמָּה meaning "wickedness, lewdness". In the Bible, he is the son of Shimei and father of Joah.
Feminine form of either Zimri or Zimran. In the Netherlands, a known bearer of this name is the model and journalist Zimra Geurts (b. 1991).
A character mentioned in the works of JRR Tolkien. The name is of unknown etymology.

Meaning uncertain. Some sources say that the name means "musical" or "musician" and is ultimately derived from Hebrew zimrah meaning "melody, song (in praise of God)". If this is true, then the name is etymologically related to Zimri. Other sources say that this name is derived from Hebrew zemer meaning "mountain sheep" or "mountain goat".In the Hebrew Bible, Zimran is the name of the first son of Abraham and his wife Keturah.

Means "jewel daughter" in Adûnaic, from Adûnaic zimra, "jewel" and phel, which probably means "daughter". Zimraphel is a translation of the Quenya name Míriel. In The Silmarillion (1977) by J. R. R. Tolkien, Ar-Zimraphel (Queen Zimraphel) was Míriel's Adûnaic royal name.
From Burmese သဇင် (thazin) meaning "orchid".
Alternate transcription of Arabic زينب (see Zaynab).
From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child, offspring, descendant" combined with 男 (nán) meaning "man, male", as well as other hanzi combinations.
Derived from Arabic نَار (nār) meaning "fire, flame, light".

Classical Persian name meaning "jewel among women", from Persian زینت (zinat) "jewel, ornament" (compare Zinat) and Arabic النِّسَاء (an-nisāʔ) "women" (compare Nisa). This name was borne by Zinat un-Nisa (1643-1721), a daughter of the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb and patron of the arts.
Possibly from the Kurdish zin meaning "saddle".
Alternate transcription of Arabic زين الدين (see Zayn ad-Din) chiefly used in North Africa.
Diminutive of Agostinu and its variants.
Alternate transcription of Arabic زين العابدين (see Zayn al-Abidin) chiefly used in North Africa.
Possibly an elaboration of Zina by way of combining it with the name suffix -etta.
Tuscan form of Ginevra. This name was used by Giovanni Boccaccio for a character in his The Decameron (written between 1348 and 1353).
Means "cloudy, misty" or "early morning" in Hakha Chin.
Likely a short form of names ending in -zinha such as Mariazinha and Florazinha.
Means "they (the girls) are beautiful" in Zulu.
Georgian diminutive of Zina and Zinaida.

column3: 子宁, 梓宁, 紫宁, etc.(Chinese)|子寧, 梓寧, 紫寧, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child", 梓 (zǐ) meaning "catalpa tree", or 紫 (zǐ) meaning "purple" combined with 宁 (níng) meaning "peaceful, calm, serene". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Croatian variant of Zrinka, or a diminutive of names ending in -zina.
A diminutive of names ending in -zino.
Estonian transcription of Russian Зиновий (see Zinoviy).
Latvian and Lithuanian form of Zenobia.
Modern Greek transcription of Zenobios. This was borne by Zinovios Valvis (1800-1886), a Greek politician who served two terms as Prime Minister of Greece, in 1863 and 1864.
Derived from Latvian zinte "magic, charms, witchcraft".
Means "to know the people", derived from the Lithuanian verb žinoti meaning "to know" combined with Baltic tauta meaning "people, nation" (see Vytautas).
The name of a minor Hittite goddess of Hattian origin, whose name means "granddaughter". She was part of a triple deity with her mother Mezulla and the sun goddess of Arinna.

column3: 子诺, 梓诺, etc.(Chinese)|子諾, 梓諾, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" or 梓 (zǐ) meaning "catalpa tree" combined with 诺 (nuò) meaning "to promise, to approve". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Vilamovian form of Zofia and Zośka.
Feminine form of Zion combining Zion and the popular suffix -ira.

Means "place of daneworts", from Basque zihaurri meaning "danewort, dwarf elder" and the suffix -tza, which indicates a place abundant in something. This is the name of a collegiate church dedicated to the Virgin Mary on the Way of St. James in Bizkaia.
Means "born to meet wealth" in Ijaw.
Younger form of Zigpert, traditionally found in central Grisons.
Maybe a Romani form of Joseph.The name is borne by two Gypsi musicians, the guitarrist Zipflo Reinhard and the violinist and actor Zipflo Weinrich.
In I Chronicles 4:16, Ziphah is mentioned as a son of Jehaleleel, a descendant of Judah.
From Hebrew tsiphion "watchman, lookout", ultimately derived from Hebrew tsaphah "to look out, to keep watch." In the bible, Ziphion was the name of a son of Gad.
Alternate transcription of Hebrew ציפי (see Tzipi).

column3: 子飘, etc.(Chinese)|子飄, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 飘 (piāo) meaning "to float in the air, to flutter, to waft". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 平 (píng) meaning "level, even, peaceful". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

Of uncertain origin, but possibly using the Luwian feminine suffix -wiya ("woman"). Name borne by a sister of the Hittite king Tudhaliya I. Her name is mentioned in a ritual to protect her brother from witchcraft that she allegedly carried out in an attempt to curse him.
Spanish form of Zipporah. Also compare Séfora.
Variant of Zipporah, recorded in medieval Frankfurt, Germany.
Dutch, German, Judeo-Anglo-Norman and Italian form of Zipporah.

column3: 子柒, 子竒, 子齐, 子期, 子琪, 梓淇, 自齐, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child", 梓 (zǐ) meaning "catalpa (a type of plant)" or 自 (zì, zí) meaning "self, oneself" combined with 柒 (qī) meaning "seven", 竒 (qí) meaning "odd, unusual, strange", 齐 (qí) meaning "even, level, uniform", 期 (qī, qí) meaning "time period, stage", 琪 (qí) meaning "fine jade" or 淇 (qí), the name of a river in Henan province. Other character combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 子千, 子谦, etc.(Chinese)|子千, 子謙, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 千 (qiān) meaning "thousand" or 谦 (qiān) meaning "humble, modest". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 子桥, etc.(Chinese)|子橋, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 桥 (qiáo) meaning "bridge". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 琴 (qín) meaning "zither, lute". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 子晴, 子青, 子清, 子庆, etc.(Chinese)|子慶, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 晴 (qíng) meaning "clear weather", 庆 (qìng) meaning "congratulate, celebrate, celebration", 青 (qīng) meaning "blue, green, young", or 清 (qīng) meaning "clear, pure, clean". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 紫琼, 子琼, etc.(Chinese)|紫瓊, 子瓊, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 紫 (zǐ) meaning "purple" or 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 琼 (qióng) meaning "fine jade (particularly red jade)". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Derived from Uzbek zira meaning "cumin" and gul meaning "flower, rose".
Means "person whom one dare not attack" in Cicassian.
From Chinese 自然 (zìrán) meaning "nature, natural". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
Derived from Uzbek zira meaning "cumin" and oy meaning "moon".
Zirnitra (or Zir) is Wendish God of sorcery.
Derived from Persian and Ottoman Turkish زراعت (zirâ’at) meaning “farming, agriculture, cultivation” combined with the Turkic title khan meaning “leader, ruler”.
Friulian and Ladinian form of Girolamo.
Of unknown meaning.Ziroli Winterstein was a German gypsi guitarrist.

column3: 子荣, 子容, etc.(Chinese)|子榮, 子容, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 荣 (róng) meaning "glory, honour, flourish, prosper" or 容 (róng) meaning "appearance, form". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

Meaning unknown. This is the name of the protagonist of the fairy tale "Princess Camion" by Mademoiselle de Lubert. Zirphil is a young prince who is given a doll named Camion, who is really an enchanted princess, to be his wife.

Feminine form of Zirphil. This name is borne by one of the title characters of the French fairy tale "Acajou et Zirphile". Zirphile is the name of a vain princess. When her head is cut off, her beloved prince Acajou travels to the moon to find it.
Germanised form of the name Circe.The name is mostly used for the mythological figure. It is rarely, if ever, used as a given name.

column3: 子赛, 梓赛, etc.(Chinese)|子賽, 梓賽, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" or 梓 (zǐ) meaning "catalpa tree" combined with 赛 (sài) meaning "to have a contest, to compete". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From Chinese 梓 (zǐ) meaning "catalpa tree" or 紫 (zǐ) meaning "purple" combined with 桑 (sāng) meaning "mulberry". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 子善, 子山, 子杉, 子珊, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 善 (shàn) meaning "good, virtuous", 山 (shān) meaning "mountain, hill, peak", 杉 (shān) meaning "pine, fir", or 珊 (shān) meaning "coral". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 子舒, 子淑, 子述, 子叔, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 紫 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 淑 (shū) meaning "good, pure, virtuous, charming" or 舒 (shū) meaning "open up, unfold, comfortable, easy". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 爽 (shuǎng) meaning "bright, clear; frank, straightforward". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 水 (shuǐ) meaning "water". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From Ancient Greek ζήσει (zesei) meaning "he will live", itself from the verb ζάω (zao) "to live" (the source also of ζωή (zoe) "life").
Means "sweet kid" in Yiddish, derived from Süsskind.
From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 松 (sōng) meaning "pine tree, fir tree". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Alternate transcription of Greek Ζήσης (see Zisis).
Variant of Ziusudra. A Sumerian priest-king during the great flood.

column3: 子桃, 梓桃, 子韬, 梓韬, etc.(Chinese)|子韜, 梓韜, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" or 梓 (zǐ) meaning "catalpa tree" combined with 桃 (táo) meaning "peach", 涛 (tāo) meaning "large waves", or 韬 (tāo) meaning "sheath, bowcase". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Diminutive of Zita 1. Nowadays this is a word for 'spinster' and no longer a name.
From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 田 (tián) meaning "field" or 天 (tiān) meaning "sky, heaven". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 迢 (tiáo) meaning "far away, distant" or 窕 (tiǎo) meaning "gentle and graceful". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Means "red bird" from Lakota ziŋtkála "bird" and šá "red". This name was adopted by a Yankton Dakota writer and political activist, birth name Gertrude Simmons (1876-1938).

Means "to live in peace", derived from Proto-Slavic žiti "to live" combined with Slavic mir "peace". In other words, this name is more or less the Croatian and Serbian cognate of the Polish name Życiomierz.

column3: 子桐, 子通, 梓桐, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" or 梓 (zǐ) meaning "catalpa" (a type of plant) combined with 桐 (tóng) meaning "paulownia" (a type of plant) or 通 (tōng) meaning "pass through, travel". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

Meaning, "life of long days." The name of a king listed in the Sumerian king list; listed as the last king of Sumer prior to the deluge and subsequently recorded as the hero of the Sumerian flood epic. He is mentioned in other Sumerian epic literature as well, and in Akkadian and Greek stories.
Derived from the Slavic word живъ (zhivu) meaning "living".
Means "know what the father wants" in Shona.
"Know each other". Meant for relatives to keep in touch.
Means "adornment" in Azerbaijani, ultimately from Persian زیور (zivar).
Combination of the names Ziv and El means "brightness of God" in Hebrew.

Zivena was the goddess of life, love and fertility in Slavic mythology, also recorded as Živa.In Slovakia, she was closely associated with Praboh, "the chief god".Her name is said to derive from an old word meaning "alive".
Combination of the name Ziv and the letters יה (ya) which are part of the name of God.

Of uncertain origin and meaning. One theory derives this name from Lithuanian žygiuoti "to move; to march" and viltis "hope", while other scholars believe this name to be a much-mangled form of Zizili, the name of an obscure fertility goddess of whom nothing else is known. Should the name indeed be derived from Zizili, then its meaning would be lost.
Derived from the elements živ, meaning "alive, living, vivacious" and ljub meaning "love" or "loved".
Derived from the Serbian živ, meaning "alive, living, vivacious".
From Chinese 紫 (zǐ) meaning "purple, violet" combined with 娃 (wá) meaning "doll, pretty girl". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 子婉, 子菀, 子琬, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 婉 (wǎn) meaning "gentle, meek", 菀 (wǎn) meaning "aster (Aster tataricus)", or 琬 (wǎn) meaning "fine jade". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 文 (wén) meaning "literature, culture, writing". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 子西, 紫曦, 紫溪, etc.(Chinese)
column12: This name was created by L. Frank Baum, who used it as the name of the titular character in his book 'Queen Zixi of Ix' (1905).
From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 霞 (xiá) meaning "rosy clouds, mist" or 夏 (xià) meaning "summer, great, grand". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 子贤, etc.(Chinese)|子賢, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 贤 (xián) meaning "virtuous, worthy, wise". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 翔 (xiáng) meaning "soar, glide" or 祥 (xiáng) meaning "good luck, good omen". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 子孝, 子晓, etc.(Chinese)|子曉, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 孝 (xiào) meaning "filial piety, obedience" or 晓 (xiǎo) meaning "dawn, morning". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 新 (xīn) meaning "fresh, new". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 子兴, etc.(Chinese)|子興, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 兴 (xīng) meaning "rise, prosper". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 秀 (xiù) meaning "luxuriant, beautiful, elegant, outstanding". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 旭 (xù) meaning "rising sun". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 子学, 子雪, etc.(Chinese)|子學, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 学 (xué) meaning "study, learning, school" or 雪 (xuě) meaning "snow". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 子荀, 子迅, 子薰, 子勋, etc.(Chinese)|子勛, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 荀 (xún) meaning "plant, ancient state", 迅 (xùn) meaning "fast, sudden", 勋 (xūn) meaning "meritorious deed, rank", or 薫 (xūn) referring to a "medicinal herb". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Means "Allah increases" from the Arabic زيادة (ziyadat) and combined with الله (Allah)
From Arabic ضياء (ḍiyāʾ) meaning "light, glow" combined with دين (dīn) meaning "reigion"
Means "feast, banquet" in Azerbaijani, ultimately from Arabic ضيافة (ḍiyāfa).

column3: زين(Arabic)|জিয়ান(Bengali)|زیاں(Urdu)|झियान(Hindi)|子研, 子妍, 子燕, etc.(Chinese)
紫阳, 子洋, 子揚, etc.(Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 紫 (zǐ) meaning "purple, violet" or 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 阳 (yáng) meaning "light, sun, male", 洋 (yáng) meaning "ocean" or 揚 (yáng) meaning "lift, raise, praise, acclaim". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 子瑶, etc.(Chinese)|子瑤, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 瑶 (yáo) meaning "precious jade". Other hanzi combinations are possible.
Alternate transcription of Pashto زيار (see Ziar).
Composed of the name Ziya and the Arabic word din "religion, faith".
Arabic alternate transcription of Ziya al-Din as well as the Indian form.
Probably the Avar form of Ziya al-Din.

column3: 子怡, 子仪, 子义, 子艺, 子翼, etc.(Chinese)|子怡, 子儀, 子義, 子藝, 子翼, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 怡 (yí) meaning "joy, harmony", 仪 (yí) meaning "ceremony, rites", 义 (yì) meaning "justice, righteousness", 艺 (yì) meaning "art, talent, craft" or 翼 (yì) meaning "wing". Other character combinations can form this name as well.

column3: 子银, 子胤, 子音, 子荫, etc.(Chinese)|子銀 子蔭, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child" combined with 银 (yín) meaning "silver, money", 胤 (yìn) meaning "heir, successor", 音 (yīn) meaning "sound, tone" or 荫 (yīn) meaning "shade, shelter, protect". Other hanzi combinations are possible.

column3: 子英, 紫莹, 资颖, 自应, etc.(Chinese)|子英, 紫瑩, 資穎, 自應, etc.(Traditional Chinese)
column12: From Chinese 子 (zǐ) meaning "child", 紫 (zǐ) meaning "catalpa tree", 资 (zī) meaning "money, wealth, goods, resources, to provide, to support" or 自 (zì) meaning "self, oneself, one's own" combined with 英 (yīng) meaning "flower, petal, brave, hero", 莹 (yíng) meaning "lustrous, jade", 颖 (yǐng) meaning "clever, grain tip" or 应 (yīng) meaning "agree, consent to". Other character combinations can form this name as well.
Derived from the Uzbek ziyo meaning "divine light" or "enlightenment" and the given name Ali 1.
Either the Uzbek form of Ziyad or from Persian زیاد (ziyad) meaning "more, a lot"
Means "more, numerous, abundant" derived from Persian زیاد (ziyâd) meaning "much, a lot, many".

Zoram has five plausible etymologies, though only the first etymology given below is attested in an ancient Semitic source (see below). The first three of the five are only slightly different from each other: "The Rock is the (divine) kinsman," "Rock of the people," and "Their Rock." These three plausible etymologies will be discussed in that order, with the first discussion supplying most of the basic information. In the first of the five etymologies, the only etymology with an attested ancient Semitic instance, the first part of Zoram is the Hebrew word ṣûr, meaning "rock, cliff face," but is used metaphorically for the God of Israel, as in 2 Samuel 22:47, "The Lord liveth; and blessed be my rock ṣûr; and exalted be the God of the rock ṣû] of my salvation." The vocable ṣûr also appears in several biblical personal names, such as Zur ṣûr "Rock" (Numbers 25:15), Zuriel, ṣûrî-ʾēl "El (God) is my rock" (Numbers 3:35).The second part of Zoram could come from the common Semitic vocable ʿām, meaning "father's brother," "(divine) kinsman," and "people." The vocable ʿām is qutie common in ancient Semitic name giving. As an element in Hebrew names, there is no question that it is a theophoric element, appearing in names such as Jekameam, yĕqam-ʿām (1 Chronicles 23:19). In addition to appearing as the final element, it also can be found at the beginning of names, e.g., Amminadab, ʿammî-nādāb (Numbers 1:7), "my father's brother is generous."

From Arabic زبدة (zubdat) meaning "butter, cream, extract" and نساء (nisāʾ)meaning "women".
Means "someone who touches the sky" in Dogri and Kashmiri.
Alternate transcription of Urdu زبیدہ (see Zubaida).
Avar form of Zubaida also used by Nigerian Muslims.
Alternate transcription of Urdu زبیر (see Zubair).
From the name of a Basque province, also called Xiberoa
Malay and Indonesian form of Zubair.
From Serbian жубор (žubor) meaning "rushing sound of water", "burble".
From 祖 (zǔ) meaning "ancestor, forebear" and 儿 (ér) meaning "child, baby".
A latinised form of Sweer under the influence of the Biblical name Ahasuerus.
Means "spreading light" from Arabic ضوء (ḍawʼ) meaning "light" combined with Persian‎ فشان (feshan), the present stem of فشاندن (feshandan) "to scatter, to disperse". Also compare Zarafshan.
Means "good luck" or "good fortune" in Dagbani.
Derived from Arabic ضُحَى (ḍaḥḥā) meaning "sacrifice, immolate" or "morning, forenoon".
Means "piece of gold, golden" in Arabic.
Feminine name derived from Basque zuhaitz "tree", ultimately from Old Basque zur "wood" and haritz "oak" (formerly a generic term for "tree").
Arabic variant and Turkish form of Zohal.
Alternate transcription of Arabic زهير (see Zuhair).
Probably an invented name, perhaps an elaboration of Suhaila or Sujey using the English name suffix lyn. This is borne by Zuheilyn Clemente (2000-), a Honduran model and beauty pageant titleholder.
Combined from the names Zühre and Naz.

From the name of 7th-century Islamic jurist and scholar Ibn Shihab az-Zuhri, whose name was derived from the Banu Zuhrah clan. It can also be derived from Indonesian and Malay zuhur meaning "midday, noon", ultimately from Arabic ظهر (ẓuhr), given to boys born around noon during the midday prayer (Dhuhr).

Means "flowers" in Arabic, a plural form of زهْرة (zahra). Known bearers of this name include Zuhur Dixon (1933-2021), an Iraqi poet, and Zuhur Wanasi (1936-), an Algerian author and politician known for her powerful short stories and for her role as one of the first women in Algerian government.
Basque equivalent of Prudencia and Prudence.
From Chinese 醉 (zuì) meaning "be addicted to, indulge in; drunk, intoxicated", in addition to other hanzi that are pronounced similarly.
Caló form of Martha, possibly from Romani zhulyi, "lady, woman". Alternatively, it could be derived from Caló zujenia, meaning "flower".
Zuki is of Japanese origin and means "Moon".

Fictional name apparently meant to be from Chinese 蘇 (sū) meaning "to regain consciousness" or 祖 (zǔ) meaning "ancestor, forefather" combined with 科 (kē) meaning "sort, class" or 寇 (kòu) meaning "bandit, robber". This is the name of a main character in the television series 'Avatar: The Last Airbender'.
First part of compound Arabic names beginning with ذو ال (Dhū al) meaning "possessor of the, owner of the" (such as Dhu al-Kifl or Dhu al-Qarnayn).

Means "brilliant" in Tigrinya.Zula is a small town in central Eritrea. It is situated near the head of Annesley Bay, on the Red Sea coast. Four kilometers away is the archeological site of Adulis, which was an emporium and the port of Axum.
Malay and Indonesian variant of Zulaykha.
Form of Zulaykha used in several languages.
Arabic alternate transcription of Zulaykha as well as the form used in several languages.
From Arabic زلال (zulāl) meaning "pure, clear (of water)".
Either a diminutive of Zulaykha or Zuleykhan or a combination of Arabic ذُو (ḏū) meaning "possessor, owner of" and Turkic ай (ay) meaning "moon".
Spanish, Portuguese and Italian form of Zuleika.
Name of an African American character in Nella Larsen's 1929 novel Passing.
Azerbaijani and Tatar form of Zulaykha. Used in the novel "Zuleykha opens her eyes" by Guzel Yakhina.
Means "closeness, nearness, proximity" in Arabic, also referring to a period of time marking the commencement of either day or night. It is sometimes used as a masculine name in Indonesia.
From Arabic ذو الفضل (dhū al-faḍl) meaning "possessor of generosity", derived from ذو (dhū) meaning "possessor, holder, master" and فضل (faḍl) meaning "grace, generosity".
From Arabic ذو الفهم (dhū al-fahm) meaning "holder of understanding", derived from ذو (dhū) meaning "possessor, holder, master" and فهم (fahm) meaning "understanding, comprehension".
Indonesian and Malay variant of Zulfiqar.
Combination of Zulfikar and Persian شاه (shāh) meaning "king".
From Arabic ذو الفكر (dhū al-fikr) meaning "possessor of thought", derived from ذو (dhū) meaning "possessor, holder, master" and فكر (fikr) meaning "thinking, thought, idea".
From Persian زلف (zolf) meaning "tress" and نگار (negār) meaning "beloved, sweetheart; painting, picture".
Combination of Zulfiqar and Arabic دين (dīn) meaning "religion, faith, belief".
Uzbek and Tajik form of Zulfiqar.
Derived from Arabic ذُو (ḏū) meaning "possessor (of), owner (of)" combined with Hadi.
Uzbek feminine name derived from the name of the twelfth month of the Islamic lunar calendar, the month of Hajj.

Basically means "possessing the ability to charm or intoxicate", derived from Arabic ذو (dhu) meaning "possessor, owner" combined with Persian خمار (humar) meaning "intoxicating" or "giving pleasure".
Tajik and Uzbek form of Zulhumar.
Means "possessor of beauty, possessor of goodness" from Arabic ذو ال (dhu al) meaning "possessor of the, owner of the" and حسن (husn) meaning "beauty, goodness".
One of the 23 states of Venezuela. Zulia can also be used as a variant to the name Julia.
Possibly a combination of Zuli and Julie.
Invented name, likely inspired by names such as Zulema and Julieth.
Possibly a Karachay-Balkar form of Zuleikha.
Means "one who is blessed with graciousness".
Combination of the given names Zuli or Zulema with the suffix -mar, present in other names such as Gladimar, Yulimar and Lilimar.
Malay and Indonesian form of Dhu al-Qarnayn.
Means "possessor of goodness" from Arabic ذو ال (dhu al) meaning "possessor of the, goodness of the" combined with خير (khayr) meaning "goodness, good".
Malay and Indonesian form of Dhu al-Kifl.
Malay and Indonesian variant of Dhu al-Kifl.
Malay and Indonesian variant of Dhu al-Kifl.
In the case of the Argentine actress Zully Moreno (1920-1999), it was a diminutive of Zulema.
Derived from Uzbek zulmat meaning "pitch darkness".
A character in "Erewhon" by Samuel Butler.
Urdu and Malay form of Dhu al-Qarnayn.
The name Zuly is a Puerto-Rican name from my friend. Also a variant of the name Julie with a french accent!
Means "abundance" in Chumashan. This is the name of a beach in Malibu, California, after which Gwen Stefani and Gavin Rossdale's son was named.
Derived from Basque zuma meaning "wicker". It is also the name of a town in Gipuzkoa, Basque Country.
From Uyghur زۇمرەت meaning "emerald", from Persian زمرد (zomorrod).
Variant form of Zümre or Zümrüt.
From Arabic زُمُرُّد (zumurrud) meaning "emerald", also used as an alternate transcription of Azerbaijani Zümrüd.
Variant of Zümra directly from the Turkish word zümrüt meaning "emerald".
Derived from Arabic zumurrud, ultimately from Persian zumrud, "emerald".
